title: After Discovering a Cyber-Security Problem, Services are Racing to Upgrade Their Computer Systems
author: editor
excerpt: Organisations and corporations are still trying to upgrade their systems after cyber-security holes were discovered in PHP, a popular programming language. Websites worldwide went offline on Wednesday and Thursday after PHP developers disclosed “critical vulnerabilities” in the back-end language, which has powered online development for decades. Researchers warned that the “severe” faults might expose millions of sites that use it to potential hackers if not patched, prompting the UK government to take some sites offline as a precaution. So yet, no successful attempts have been reported, but experts believe any impact may take weeks or months to become apparent. Downing Street stated on Thursday that “some” limited government services “may be offline” while security measures were being implemented. The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable,” said technology minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra in the House of Lords. She explained that this “largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied”. title: A Famous Shark That was Escorted out of the South Korea Canal Declined to go out to Sea
author: editor
excerpt: After being led out of a canal on Wednesday, a well-known dusky shark from South Korea is still hanging around. When the shark, known as Bukangi, was seen swimming in a canal in the southeast port city of Busan last month, it caused an unexpected stir. Rescuers used big nets for weeks in an unsuccessful attempt to return it to the open sea. Authorities announced on Thursday that they had strengthened obstacles to stop Bukangi from going back. However, it has not yet ventured out into the open ocean and has been continually returning to the waterway’s entrance. In Busan, opinions on the shark’s rescue were divided; some believed it should remain, while others thought it would be best for it to leave. It took more than eight hours for rescue personnel to carefully steer the three-meter-long (10-foot) shark toward open water in a port during a livestreamed operation on Wednesday. At the park with a view of the canal, hundreds of devoted spectators gathered to cheer and bid the shark farewell. However, Bukangi apparently broke through an official barrier on Thursday morning and swam back into the canal. Bukangi was imprisoned for a while in the canal between two layers of nets. title: Stablecoin Payments Could be Made by AI Agents as Early as 2027
author: editor
excerpt: As autonomous systems increasingly perform purchases and financial transactions on behalf of users, artificial intelligence agents may play a significant role in the adoption of stablecoins as early as 2027, according to digital asset executives at the ADGM Global Media Forum. According to Andrej Majcen, co-founder and group CEO of Bitcoin Suisse, the quick advancement of AI may lead to the emergence of a new class of economic players that can conduct transactions with little assistance from humans.”I anticipate that the proliferation of AI agents will occur in 2027,” Majcen stated. He clarified that AI agents will require quicker and more effective payment methods as they grow more autonomous. Majcen anticipates that these systems will progressively favour stablecoins and other digital assets because to their programmability and efficiency, even though they could still accept conventional payment methods like credit cards. Digital assets known as stablecoins are made to have a comparatively steady value, typically by being connected to a conventional currency like the US dollar. Within the next three to five years, AI bots may start communicating directly with one another, according to Edward Hong, Senior Executive Officer of Hashed Global Management and Chief Platform Officer and Partner of Hashed. He clarified that because these computers might autonomously make purchases, access data, and pay for computer services, there would be a need for quick, programmable payment infrastructure that could facilitate international transactions. title: On the Basis of Energy Security, the UK Permits the Long-Delayed Jackdaw Gas Field
author: editor
excerpt: LONDON: The Jackdaw North Sea gas field was cleared by Britain on Wednesday, concluding years of legal and political fighting as the Labour administration tries to strike a balance between energy security concerns and climate aspirations. According to Energy Minister Miatta Fahnbulleh, the project will start supplying gas by the end of this month, which will assist reduce energy bills that have increased due to the Iran War. US President Donald Trump has frequently urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to increase North Sea drilling due to the impact of rising energy prices on people and businesses, which has negatively impacted Britain’s economy. The government described Jackdaw as “a source of national strength” during a time of global turmoil, claiming it would increase local gas production by roughly 6% at peak output and run for up to 11 years. According to Reuters calculations based on official statistics, Jackdaw would supply slightly less than 4% of Britain’s daily petrol demand at its anticipated peak production of 40,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Burnham stated, “It’s right that we look responsibly at maximising the existing energy reserves we have in Britain that could help at a time when people are really struggling.” Also Read: As Tech Tensions with China Persist, the US Prohibits the Government From Using DeepSeek AI Russia Claims it is Prepared to Start Peace Negotiations With the US and Ukraine

title: Why do Speculations of Kim Jong Un’s Death Keep Resurfacing When North Korea Releases Pictures of Him?
author: editor
excerpt: Kim Jong Un, who is said to have died from a brain bleed, has shown up in North Korean state media looking astonishingly well. The 42-year-old tyrant is shown touring a clothes-and-footwear exhibition, which the state daily Rodong Sinmun described, with his daughter. The pictures surfaced just hours after a Chinese dissident living in the United States made an unsupported claim that Kim had died after being sent to a Beijing hospital in a coma. This kind of speculation has nearly become commonplace for those who keep a close eye on North Korea. Facts are often hard to confirm in one of the world’s most secretive states, which encourages conjecture. Wanjun Xie, who claims to be the chairman of the Chinese Democratic Party that Chinese authorities have outlawed, is the source of this most recent allegation. In the past, he has made unsubstantiated claims, such as including speculation about the death of Chinese leader Xi Jinping. According to Xie, Kim had a serious brain hemorrhage and was sent to Beijing because North Korea lacked the medical resources to care for him. He asserted that Kim’s death was later concealed by the authorities and that his body had been covertly repatriated to North Korea. title: Patients with Thalassaemia in the UAE now Have More Options Thanks to Gene Therapy
author: editor
excerpt: With the help of advanced gene therapy, Yas Clinic and the Abu Dhabi Stem Cells Center (ADSCC) have shown encouraging results in treating thalassaemia. Fahad, a 43-year-old patient, is no longer dependent on frequent blood transfusions to manage his condition. Fahad had transfusion-dependent thalassaemia for a long time; in order to keep his haemoglobin levels steady, he needed blood transfusions every three to four weeks. His general health and quality of life were affected by a number of long-term transfusion-related problems, such as iron overload and the requirement for regular iron chelation therapy, in addition to the continuous burden of treatment. Fahad was referred to Yas Clinic and ADSCC about a year and a half ago, when both organisations were attempting to bring cutting-edge gene therapy therapies to the United Arab Emirates. One of the most important developments in the treatment of inherited blood disorders is gene therapy, which may provide a long-term solution for individuals who might not have access to a suitable donor for bone marrow transplantation. Fahad was determined to be a good candidate for gene therapy after thorough medical evaluations, intensive testing, and thorough interdisciplinary assessments. His course of treatment coincided with national initiatives, backed by the UAE’s government and Department of Health, to bring this cutting-edge therapy to the country, opening up new avenues for patients to receive cutting-edge care nearer to their homes. Fahad’s own stem cells were harvested for the procedure, genetically altered, and then reinfused after preparatory therapy. The method, which is comparable to an autologous transplant, uses the patient’s own genetically altered cells to treat the disease’s root cause. title: After Protests Turn into “Apocalyptic” Chaos, Marseille Prepares for Further Turmoil
author: editor
excerpt: After the weekend’s chaos, thunder and lightning have erupted around Marseille, illuminating the boarded-up doors and damaged windows of hundreds of shops that were destroyed when protests turned violent. Chaos swept around France on Saturday, with some of the worst violence occurring in the country’s second city. More than 500 businesses were damaged, and most of them were plundered, according to local business leaders. For his coworkers, the weekend had been an “apocalyptic” misery, a police union boss told the BBC. 118 officers more than a tenth of the total were hurt. Children make up 25% of the 101 arrests made in the port city so far. However, on Monday, police, not protesters, were most visible on the city’s streets. To prevent a third day in a row of chaos, police banned protests and gatherings for eight hours. It appeared to be effective, as evidenced by the largest concentrated gathering we saw a group of weather-beaten visitors lumbering along the quayside. However, starting Tuesday night, some areas of the city will implement an overnight curfew for children. Additionally, a midnight curfew implemented in several areas of Paris on Monday has been extended. title: After Being Struck by a Car in What Appeared to be an Attack, an Australian MP Suffered Grave Injuries
author: editor
excerpt: After being struck by a car in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese claims may have been a premeditated attack, Australian MP Helen Haines is seriously ill in a Melbourne hospital. On Monday afternoon, the 65-year-old independent MP was attacked outside her constituency office in Wangaratta, Victoria. A 43-year-old man from the neighbouring town of Tarrawingee was apprehended at the site by a bystander, and according to the police, a knife was discovered inside the vehicle. Although they do not think there is a “continuous threat to the community,” police are looking into if it was a “intentional act.” Albanese stated that “there is no place for violence in a democracy” in response to shock and dismay expressed by political leaders. Albanese acknowledged that Australia’s political climate has been getting hotter, but he said it was too early to determine the motivation behind what had occurred. Tony Burke, his minister of home affairs, supported that claim with data indicating that the number of allegations of intimidating or harassing behaviour directed at politicians had increased from 951 to 1,067 during the previous 12 months. At 15:35 (04:35 GMT), Haines was struck by a white Toyota Landcruiser outside her Wangaratta office on Murphy Street, according to the police. title: As Tech Tensions with China Persist, the US Prohibits the Government From Using DeepSeek AI
author: editor
excerpt: The US has mandated that DeepSeek, a Chinese company, remove all artificial intelligence (AI) technology from the majority of government systems. All civilian government entities are prohibited from using DeepSeek or any technology developed using its AI models by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). DeepSeek has been viewed as a disruptive factor in the continuing AI technology race because it is a potent AI model that is open source, which means it is free to access and less expensive to utilise. The White House has blasted Chinese AI companies this year, although the DHS notification did not specify the precise security issues with DeepSeek. We have reached out to DeepSeek, the Chinese embassy in Washington, DC, and the DHS for comment. Although the prohibition went into place at the end of July, the DHS made the directive public on Monday. The Department of the Treasury, the Department of State, and the Department of Justice are among the civilian agencies covered by the directive. Department of Defence agencies are not included, though. The prohibition comes after American companies and the Trump administration criticised Chinese AI. title: India Arrests ‘Cockroach’ Party Leader Ahead of Protest
author: editor
excerpt: Police in Delhi detained the originator of India’s “cockroach” movement, Abhijeet Dipke, and a few others as they sought to stop a protest calling for the resignation of the country’s election chief. Despite the massive security presence, hundreds congregated in Connaught Place, one of the capital’s busiest commercial districts, waving Indian flags and screaming slogans. Police cordoned off Central Park where the demonstration was to be held and deployed thousands of police and paramilitary forces to prevent the gathering. The Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has accused India’s Election Commission of altering voter records to suit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP. They both reject the charge. The group has organised a number of protests in Delhi in recent weeks, with police arresting its leaders and supporters on more than one occasion. Security was also tight for Friday’s protest, although the police response was less heavy-handed than the widespread crackdown last weekend. The cops visited the house where Dipke was staying hours before the protest. In a live Instagram video, he questioned the officers who had come to warn him against staging the march if it was illegal to wave the Indian flag. title: Dubai Home Healthcare Services Climb 22.7% in the First Half of 2026
author: editor
excerpt: Home care services in Dubai expanded faster than any other element of the health industry in the first half of 2026, with the number of licensed facilities increasing by 22.7% to 249, up from 203 in the same period last year. The significant increase, disclosed in a recent Dubai Health Authority (DHA) study, indicates a shift in how the emirate delivers care, with more patients receiving treatment at home rather than in a hospital or clinic. The report revealed widespread growth in the sector. The number of licensed health institutions in Dubai increased by 7% to 5,931 in the first half of 2026, compared to 5,541 in the same time of 2025. Licensed health professionals numbered 70,566, up 6.5% from 66,277. Other categories have also grown. The number of pharmacies increased 6.8% to 1,794. Complementary and alternative medicine centers increased by 8.1%, from 99 to 107. Medical complexes and optical centers increased by 9.9 percent, to 1,903 from 1,731 in the first half of 2025. Dr. Alawi Alsheikh-Ali, Director General of the Dubai Health Authority, commented on the report, stating that the expansion reflects the improvement of the emirate’s healthcare system and its capacity to meet community demands.The continued growth of Dubai’s health sector reflects the evolution of the emirate’s healthcare system and its ability to meet the needs of the community. author: editor

According to the sources, the authorities were still attempting to shed light on “the reasons and circumstances” that led to the relocation. title: Adam Rumanek on Building a YouTube Content Engine Through Licensing, Localization, and Rights Strategy
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: To Adam Rumanek, Founder and CEO of Aux Mode, YouTube is not just a video library. For him, it is a portfolio of various assets that can be programmed, localized, licensed, protected, and monetized in different ways. An effective YouTube strategy is not about finding one video that goes viral. It’s about getting even more commercial value from the content you already have while making smarter decisions about what to acquire next. For media companies, producers, and rights holders, this means they need to bring content strategy and licensing strategy much closer together. Stop Thinking in Videos. Start Thinking in Assets. A complete video may appear to be a single piece of content to benefit from, but it can become several things. Long episode content can anchor a playlist. Chosen scenes can become short clips. Old content can be resurfaced once audience interest picks up again. The catalog could be based on genres, cast, themes, seasons, or recurring viewing habits. The same underlying asset can also be adapted for audiences in other languages. Simply, ask: How many useful opportunities are already inside the assets we have? This also makes planning easier. Content pillars, playlists, release schedules, thumbnails, titles, descriptions, and audience data are no longer separate optimization processes. The Catalog Can Tell You What to License Next Licensing is treated as a negotiation problem. What does the title cost? Which territories are available? How long are the rights? What does the agreement allow you? Those questions are also still important, but YouTube has another layer of evidence. Adam Rumanek has put weight on using analytics for evaluating potential acquisitions through signals, which can include watch time, revenue, average view duration, search traffic, returning viewers, etc. If numerous titles that feature a particular celebrity consistently are being watched more than other comparable titles, that pattern is worth investigating. If one genre is producing fewer views but way more revenue, raw view counts are probably hiding its commercial value. If particular territories are continuously generating unbalanced revenue, they are also deserving of closer attention. The point here is absolutely not to assume that yesterday’s winner will also become tomorrow’s winner. Previous performance can be distorted and changed by thumbnails, promotion, seasonality, competition, or temporary cultural moments, etc. Instead, the data you find should help more in identifying repeatable characteristics. A licensing team that is aware of what their audience is already watching holds a stronger starting point when they’re deciding what to acquire. One Library, More Markets: The Localization Layer Localization is a hidden vault, especially when the stuff has already been produced. In an English catalogue, dubbing videos into Spanish and Portuguese produces more audiences without having to make entirely new content. AI dubbing helps the economics because the marginal cost of making another language version can be significantly lower than traditional voice production. Adam Rumanek suggests using AI dubbing. Take existing libraries and expand their potential instead of just constantly creating new material. It’s also easier since YouTube now supports both automatic dubbing for creators and manually uploaded different-language audio. If one company has produced 500 relevant English videos, the opportunity is not to create another 500 videos. It is to see which of those 500 deserve localization. Which markets justify dedicated channels, and which titles should remain concentrated on a single channel with multiple audio tracks? This is an entire portfolio design. The Real Work Begins After the Upload The problem that results from increased distribution is increased opportunities for content to be stolen, contested, or mismanaged. Here comes the necessity for license management to work side by side with programming. YouTube has the Content ID feature, which can recognize any matching audio or visual material and enable the matched video to be monetized, monitored, or blocked based on the rights holder’s decision. These decisions can even change according to the region. For licensed content, this is really important. A rights agreement can not end with the question of where a video may get published. It also needs to consider who is controlling the Content ID asset, how claims are handled, which territories are covered, what happens when rights expire, and how revenue is reconciled. Adam Rumanek’s insights in this area highlight a mostly overlooked reality that rights management is a significant part of monetization. Video monetization from your own channel could be an option. Similarly, the same video being used somewhere else without permission could also be an option for rights management, as long as there is proper ownership and licensing of the property. Adam Rumanek’s View: Build More Value From What You Already Own Good YouTube strategy should focus on extracting value from every asset possible. This also means having a better release schedule, a long-form title made into several formats, complementary titles licensed after a clear audience pattern, an existing catalog dubbed into new languages, or tighter rights management once the content has left the channel. To Adam Rumanek, this approach is what separates maintaining a YouTube channel from building a YouTube content business. title: In November, US President Trump will Travel to the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit
author: editor
excerpt: Next month, US President Donald Trump will go to Manila to attend the 2026 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Meetings. Claire Castro, a spokesperson for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., confirmed the scheduled visit on Wednesday but did not offer any other information. Prior to his journey to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, the White House had previously announced that Trump would be visiting the Philippines. The APEC Summit in China is set for November 18–19, while the ASEAN Summit is set for November 15–17. For the ASEAN conference, Marcos has designated November 16–18 as special non-working days in the National Capital Region. Marcos and Trump last had a face-to-face meeting at the White House in July of last year to talk about trade, defence cooperation, and bilateral relations. On July 23 of this year, they spoke over the phone about regional security issues, particularly the South China Sea, as well as economic developments. In November 2017, Trump made his first trip to the Philippines as president during his first term. There, he met former President Rodrigo Duterte in Manila and attended the ASEAN 50th anniversary banquet. Renato Reyes Jr., president of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan, a left-wing, multi-sectoral political alliance in the Philippines, wrote on Facebook on Wednesday that “Trump’s image and effigy will burn in the streets of Manila the moment he steps foot on Philippine soil. The chief imperialist and fascist will get the fiery welcome he deserves. No red carpet welcome, only red banners of protest for the warmonger who plunged the world deeper in crisis.”Trump would face protests for escalating the global crisis through his assault on Iran, just as he did during his previous trip to the Philippines, Reyes continued. title: The Head of the Philippine Central Bank Thinks That Asia Needs to Prevent Another Financial Disaster
author: editor
excerpt: The director of the Philippine central bank stated on Wednesday that Asian nations need to remember what transpired during the region’s financial crisis in the late 1990s and take precautions to prevent such shocks from happening again. Eli Remolona, governor of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, stated in an IMF panel on the outlook for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) that massive capital inflows into regional economies prior to the start of the Asian financial crisis in 1997 led the World Bank to refer to it as the “East Asian miracle,”Asia saw an influx of investment, but since it wasn’t truly a miracle, there was a crisis. I believe we need to remind ourselves of that. That kind of crisis is something we need to prevent,” he stated. “We have not really been making a lot of effort looking at that kind of crisis.” The director of the IMF’s Asia and Pacific Department, Krishna Srinivasan, refuted the viewpoint during the panel discussion, claiming that the organization has made strides in evaluating financial vulnerabilities and potential spillovers among each economy.We’ve taken the situation seriously, and we’ve worked on a framework to discuss how nations should handle erratic capital flows in terms of things like whether to interfere in foreign exchange markets, among other things,” Srinivasan stated. author: editor

title: Six Flags Closes Nine Coasters Following a “Gruesome” Rider Death Fall
author: editor
excerpt: Following the death of a rider who allegedly fell off a ride at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday, the theme park chain is temporarily closing nine more coasters at six of its locations. Local media accounts state that a passenger fell or was thrown from the 200-foot, 70-mph Goliath coaster, though the death’s specifics have not yet been formally confirmed. Witnesses told Atlanta NBC station 11Alive of a “gruesome scene” in which the rider repeatedly struck the coaster while falling. According to one ride, the falling man was even caught in a souvenir photo that was immediately taken and sold in the gift shop. The witness stated, “He was in our pictures.” “He hit the car three times after falling.” Police say several other riders were hurt as well. According to two riders, personnel checked their safety belts in accordance with practice before the ride began. In a statement, a Six Flags representative told the Associated Press, “We have temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks out of an abundance of caution.” “One of our top priorities continues to be the safety of our guests and team members.” Following the incident, riders are seen being escorted off Goliath in the video below. Nine other coasters, including Goliath at Magic Mountain in Valencia, California; Nitro at Six Flags Great Adventure in New Jersey; and Orion and Diamondback at Kings Island in Ohio, have been temporarily closed. These rides resemble the Goliath in the Georgia park. The announcement comes after two riders had brain haemorrhages and numerous other riders reported severe problems, leading Six Flags Magic Mountain to permanently close its well-liked X2 ride last month. Due to the ride, three people have sued Six Flags and the coaster’s manufacturer. title: Banking Watchdogs Ratchet up AI Examination as Stability Concerns Increase, Sources Say
author: editor
excerpt: Banking authorities are accelerating efforts to manage rising AI risks, according to six people familiar with the situation, with some citing the possibility of bank cyberattacks or rogue agents that could damage global financial stability. The regulatory review reflects a growing realisation that breakthroughs in frontier AI may require costly cyber recovery, greater reliance on external technology suppliers, and, in some jurisdictions, clearer regulatory guidance, according to sources. Three top US regulators, including the Federal Reserve, are questioning banks about their use of advanced artificial intelligence models, according to two sources, adding to previous scrutiny. Three of the participants questioned whether they use Chinese-developed technology, AI agents in cyber defence, and whether they can control more autonomous systems. Supervisors in Europe, including the Bank of England and the European Central Bank, are pressuring banks to improve recovery plans, concerned that rapid advances in artificial intelligence may cause serious harm and disruption in financial markets sooner than previously thought, according to three people familiar with their thinking. A senior executive at a major European bank expressed concern about the possibility for significant harm to banking and financial markets within the next six months. title: Russia, Iran, and AI Pose a Threat to the UK, According to the Head of MI5
author: editor
excerpt: According to the chief of the intelligence agency, MI5 is investing more resources than it did during the Cold War to combat state threats. According to Sir Ken McCallum, threats from foreign adversaries have increased fourfold over the past ten years, with Russia emerging as “aggressor number one” and increased aggression by Iran-affiliated groups against military installations and Jewish sites. The head of MI5 claimed that Russia was using hybrid warfare while AI was “supercharging the cyber-security contest between attackers and defenders” during an annual lecture in London. Additionally, he added that MI5 has “caught terrorists seeking to exploit Al,” particularly by integrating the technology with drones, and warned of growing dangers from “extreme right-wing terrorism.” According to him, extremist organisations employing AI to create new and old bioweapons pose the greatest threat from their misuse. He did point out that efforts to combat state threats and terrorism were now “pretty much of equal scale,” which he called a “huge shift” in recent years. Sir Ken stated that while Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has made “minimal and horrifically costly” progress, it has refrained from engaging in “conventional conflict” with NATO and is instead attempting to unnerve European nations. The words “hybrid warfare” and “hybrid attacks” are ambiguous and typically refer to non-military tactics, such as cyberattacks, sabotage, or disinformation, that are intended to put pressure on and destabilise an enemy. title: The Former Top Commander in Kyiv Tells the BBC That Russia’s Offensive Capabilities are Broken
author: editor
excerpt: In an interview with the BBC, Ukraine’s previous commander-in-chief said that by killing so many Russian soldiers, Ukraine had “broken Russia’s ability to advance” and stabilised the front line. In an exclusive interview, Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi made the remarks for the first time since being abruptly removed from his position in the summer. In response to his dismissal, he disagreed with some who said he was too “old school” to lead Ukraine’s new, technologically sophisticated troops. Additionally, he refuted claims made by soldiers who had fought under him in the past, who told the BBC that they were commanded to hold their positions despite being nearly surrounded by Russians, resulting in significant casualties. According to Syrskyi, Moscow’s total combat losses were six times greater than those of Ukraine. “If you count only dead, then it’s up to 11 times,” he said. The death toll is not publicly disclosed by either Russia or Ukraine. Although it cannot be confirmed, the Ukrainian military claims to have inflicted record losses on Russian soldiers in September of this year. Since beginning its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Russia is thought to have lost almost 500,000 men, according to UK intelligence chiefs. According to the US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies, Ukraine may have lost as many as 150,000 soldiers by June 2026. He claims that the current standoff at the front is caused by this disparity in the death toll, technological advancements, and a policy of striking weak locations in Russia’s lines while restricting their advances in other areas. title: Trump is Getting More and More Negative Feedback About His Plans to Buy Diesel from Russia
author: editor
excerpt: As the war in Iran continues to affect energy prices around the world, US President Donald Trump is facing more and more criticism over his plans to buy diesel from Russia. Trump said on Friday that Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to send 300,000 tonnes of diesel right away “to the American and global marketplace.” This would be the first of several shipments. That’s true even though he signed a bill just a few weeks ago that lets the US put new sanctions and tariffs on countries that buy oil and gas from Russia. Some Republicans and Democrats in Congress have said this move is wrong because they think the deal breaks US law. Trump said that Russia would send an extra one million tonnes of diesel after the first 300,000 tonnes. In November, Russia would send another 500,000 tonnes. The next shipment would be three million tonnes, sent “within a short period”, depending on the state of its refineries, which Ukraine has attacked during the war between the two countries. My top priority is lower prices for all Americans, but especially for our great farmers, ranchers, and truckers,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. title: Healey Must Pay £35 Billion. Think Tank: Budgetary Challenge to Fulfilll Spending Commitments
author: editor
excerpt: An respected think group has cautioned that Chancellor John Healey must find £35 billion to achieve defence commitments in his first Budget without reducing public spending. According to the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS), the government would require a “top-up” of billions of pounds if it hopes to increase health spending and defence spending to 3% of national revenue by 2030 without putting pressure on other departments. Healey will have to decide between cutting expenditure, raising taxes, or doing both, according to the IFS, since higher inflation brought on by the Iran conflict may reduce the amount of money the government intended to spend on public services. The Treasury declined to comment. As borrowing costs increase, the government is under increasing pressure to demonstrate to the financial markets that it has a firm grip on finances. Healey must present “credible” spending plans in the budget, which is scheduled for October 28, according to the IFS.The chancellor cannot choose a “steady-as-she-goes” budget, according to Helen Miller, director of IFS.Maintaining the inherited tax and expenditure plans would mean letting inflation throw departments’ spending projections off track. title: The BBC Discovers That Abramovich Faked Documents to Avoid Paying Taxes on his Wealth
author: editor
excerpt: According to BBC Panorama, the largest accounting firm in the world assisted in fabricating paperwork to conceal Roman Abramovich’s fortune and avoid paying taxes. Superyachts, residences, and private aircraft valued at $672 million (£508 million) disappeared from Abramovich’s business accounts due to accounting approved by Deloitte in Cyprus. Additionally, it seems that Deloitte offered advice on a plan to use document fraud to avoid paying a significant tax bill on the oligarch’s wealth. Financial services lawyer Barrister Andrew Mitchell KC stated that the scheme was “straightforward” tax evasion and “it couldn’t be more blatant” based on Panorama’s evidence. Roman Abramovich disputes that he concealed his wealth or avoided paying taxes, according to his attorneys. They claimed it was acceptable to depend on expert counsel and that Panorama offered no proof that he was aware of, approved, or directed the falsification of any document. “Acts in compliance with applicable laws” is how Deloitte Cyprus put it.The results are being made public after the Bureau of Investigative Journalism and BBC Panorama conducted a collaborative investigation. Roman Abramovich was the most well-known Russian tycoon in the UK for almost twenty years. He was welcomed to London, where he purchased Chelsea Football Club in 2003 and provided funding for the team’s most prosperous era. However, the UK government sanctioned him as an associate of President Vladimir Putin during Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, forcing him to sell the club. Simmons later reported that a man died of carbon monoxide poisoning after running a generator in an improperly ventilated garage. Four more persons from the same house were brought to the hospital. title: Leaders of the “Cockroach Gang are Among Hundreds Detained During a Protest in Delhi
author: editor
excerpt: Delhi police detained hundreds of demonstrators during the latest protest by the Gen-Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which is demanding election reforms. The group said its founder, Abhijeet Dipke, who started the action in May after India’s Chief Justice compared some unemployed young people to “cockroaches,” was detained along with other organisers immediately after arriving in Delhi. Tens of thousands of security personnel were mobilised, and highways were closed in preparation for the demonstration, which the CJP maintained would take place. The Delhi Police have not commented on the detentions, but have refused permission for the protest to take place in Jantar Mantar, a landmark in the Indian capital. The group, which is not registered as a political party in India, is demanding electoral reforms just months before critical state elections. It has also called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar after claims of voter list manipulation, which the Election Commission has denied. Under Kumar’s chairmanship, India’s election commission undertook a massive exercise to update electoral rolls nationwide, claiming it was a standard effort to remove dead, duplicate, or disqualified voters. However, in many jurisdictions, the process has drawn controversy, with tens of thousands of registrants claiming they were wrongfully purged. title: A Four-Day Outdoor Lifestyle Festival is Scheduled to Commence in Dubai on January 14
author: editor
excerpt: Dubai will host a new four-day outdoor festival featuring over 50 activities, 200 brands, 50 clubs and communities, and motoring, camping, adventure activities, food, and family entertainment. The event is being organised in response to the growing number of residents seeking outdoor activities during the cooler winter months. The Motor, Outdoor & Camping Festival (MOC27) will be held at The Sevens Stadium Grounds from January 14 to January 17, 2027, spanning more than 350,000 square meters. The event is expected to include over 200 brands, 50 clubs and communities, and more than 50 activities. As part of the DSF Auto Season, the festival is organised to capitalise on the UAE’s growing outdoor culture by bringing together activities that are often spread across multiple events. “MOC was never intended to be a mere car show or desert party.” Organised around the organisations and communities that live outdoors every day, the festival is designed for fathers, mothers, sons, and daughters. Justyn Cánovas, CEO & Senior Partner of MOC27 and JBCM Event Architects, stated, “We have not fulfilled our obligations if visitors merely observe and stroll.” Dedicated areas will be available for visitors who are interested in motoring, hiking, cycling, adventure sports, and other outdoor activities, while families can explore camping and outdoor equipment. title: JD Vance Expresses Scepticism Regarding the Firing Squad Execution and Declares that He will Not Observe it
author: editor
excerpt: The Pentagon’s efforts to simulcast a firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter have been called into question by US Vice-President JD Vance. Vance expressed uncertainty regarding the likelihood of the event occurring as intended during an interview with reporters, stating, “I am uncertain that that will actually transpire.” He further stated, “I will not be watching it if it is broadcast live.” Vance characterised the actions of former US Army major Nidal Hasan as “the most severe terrorist attack on American soil since 9/11. In 2009, Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood, injuring an additional 32. His firing squad execution would be the first military execution in over 60 years. The Pentagon announced earlier this week that it would execute Hasan by firing squad, the first such execution since the conclusion of World War Two. Subsequently, on Thursday, US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth declared that the execution would be broadcast live to the public.”People must comprehend that these actions have severe repercussions,” stated Hegseth. The BBC has questioned the White House on whether Trump endorses the plans. title: US Unveils Sanctions on ICC in Move that Court Condemns as Attack on the Rule of Law
author: editor
excerpt: The Trump administration has announced sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), accelerating its efforts to “dismantle” what it considers a “rogue” institution. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the restrictions, which include a ban on US firms conducting dealings with the ICC, were meant to “defend US sovereignty” and accused the court of attempting to prosecute Americans. The ICC described the measures as an assault on the rule of law and the pillars of the international legal order. The announcement came just hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay received the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her work to promote peace and international justice. The US has already sanctioned 17 of the ICC’s judges and executives, but this step targets the court as an institution, threatening its ability to operate financially. However, the US has allowed a six-month grace period before some of the latest penalties take effect, letting member states keep paying for its operations, a move Washington says is meant to give countries time to find a “solution to address” US concerns. title: Are You Ready for the Midterms? Trump Wants to Lower the Price of Petrol. Will it Work?
author: editor
excerpt: Since the US-Israel confrontation with Iran started in February, the price of petrol and diesel has more than doubled, impacting transportation companies, farmers, and all American drivers. US President Donald Trump has made a number of remarks and statements targeted at lowering fuel prices in the run-up to the crucial midterm elections. Trump on Friday announced an agreement with President Vladimir Putin for the rapid delivery of Russian diesel to the US and international markets, only weeks before Americans cast their ballots. Over 300,000 tonnes were sent immediately, 500,000 tonnes in November, and an additional million tonnes “immediately thereafter,”according to him. According to him, diesel prices “will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST in the US and worldwide. Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority.” Depending on the state of its refineries, he continued, an additional 3 million tonnes of Russian diesel would be delivered “within a short period” after. The election is taking place as the population is deeply concerned about rising prices for food, fuel, and other necessities. Republicans competing in November are being burdened by voters who have linked the issue to Trump and his party. title: Top 10 Innovative Leaders Redefining Success
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Success in business rarely follows one fixed path. Some leaders build their reputation by questioning familiar ways of working. Others find new opportunities in difficult markets, introduce fresh ideas to established industries, or take a different approach to challenges that others have accepted as normal. The Top 10 Innovative Leaders featured in this article represent different industries, backgrounds, and experiences. What connects them is the way they approach their work. They look for better answers, stay open to change, and understand that progress often starts with asking a different question. For these Top 10 Innovative Leaders, success is about more than growth or financial results. It can be seen in the businesses they build, the people they influence, the ideas they bring forward, and the standards they set within their fields. Their journeys show why innovative leadership continues to matter in a business environment that is constantly changing. Top 10 Innovative Leaders—Revolutionary Minds Below are the Top 10 Innovative Leaders Redefining Success, each bringing a distinct perspective to their industry. From established sectors to newer fields, these leaders are finding their own ways to create value, solve problems, and build lasting businesses. The stories of these Top 10 Innovative Leaders also show that innovation does not have to mean something completely new. Sometimes, it is about improving an existing idea, approaching a familiar challenge differently, or having the confidence to take an untested path. Ken Thompson | Connecting Global Industry with Innovative Manufacturing Behind every successful industrial project is a network of people and businesses working to find the right components, technologies, and expertise. For Ken Thompson, the challenge of connecting manufacturers with the customers who need their solutions became the foundation for KT Technical Solutions (KTTS), a U.S.-based manufacturers’ sales representative firm serving industrial and technology markets worldwide. Thompson founded KTTS after recognizing the need for a more responsive, technically focused approach to manufacturers’ representation. His customer-first philosophy, summed up in the words “We do whatever it takes,” has shaped the company’s work, particularly when customers need help sourcing hard-to-find components or finding practical solutions to keep critical projects moving. Under his leadership, KTTS has expanded across a broad range of sectors, including electronics, automation, energy storage, robotics, industrial equipment, precision instruments, and advanced manufacturing. The company connects customers with technologies and services that include printed circuit boards, cable assemblies, lithium battery technologies, precision machining, sheet metal fabrication, castings, molding, and engineering support. This breadth allows KTTS to help businesses navigate complex sourcing, manufacturing, and supply chain challenges. Rather than focusing on a single product category, the firm brings together manufacturers and customers across different technical fields, helping them identify suitable solutions for their project needs. Integrity, technical expertise, and long-term partnerships remain central to the company’s approach. Today, KTTS is among the largest independent manufacturers’ sales representative firms in the United States, linking innovative technologies with opportunities across global markets. As KTTS continues to connect manufacturers with customers across industries and markets, its work remains rooted in a practical belief: the right technical solution can help keep business moving. Through its broad network, industry knowledge, and commitment to responsive service, the company aims to make complex sourcing challenges easier to navigate and help innovative manufacturers reach new opportunities worldwide. LinkedIn | Company LinkedIn | Company Website A New Route to the Screen: Bonnie Bruderer’s BINGE Movies + TV A finished film is a major achievement, but for many independent creators, completing the project is only the beginning. Finding a route to viewers, securing distribution, and earning revenue can be just as demanding as making the work itself. Bonnie Bruderer encountered that challenge through her own experience in television, and it became the starting point for BINGE Movies + TV, the streaming and distribution company she founded. Bruderer began producing her own television show in New York City in late 2014. The experience gave her a close look at the creative side of the industry, but it also brought a practical question into focus: how could creators get their work in front of an audience beyond the traditional television system? As streaming grew, she saw an opportunity to help independent producers navigate a changing distribution landscape. Today, BINGE Movies + TV works with filmmakers and content owners to distribute films, series, documentaries, and other programming. Its streaming app is one part of the business, while its wider distribution and licensing work helps place projects on other streaming outlets. The company continues to seek placements across platforms and expand the reach of the content it represents. For Bruderer, the work is not simply about getting a title onto a single service. Different projects have different audiences and commercial possibilities, so the route to market may vary. BINGE Movies + TV considers each project individually and looks at a range of options, including major streaming services, niche platforms, cable, and even DVD distribution where it makes sense. The aim is to find a practical path for the particular film or programme, rather than treating one outlet as the only meaningful destination. That approach responds to a common difficulty for independent creators: visibility does not automatically lead to a distribution deal or reliable income. A project may attract attention at festivals and still struggle to reach a wider audience. BINGE Movies + TV’s distribution services are intended to help creators move beyond that bottleneck by handling outreach and pitching to potential licensing partners. Its public materials also emphasize that creators retain ownership of their work, while the company helps them pursue distribution opportunities. The business has also developed a model that connects its own streaming service with the wider licensing market. Content partners can earn through different routes, including revenue from distribution on partner platforms. BINGE Movies + TV’s published agreement outlines quarterly reporting and payment of a share of net proceeds from platform revenue, while its distribution information describes a revenue-sharing option for branded channels. These arrangements place monetization alongside distribution as part of the service offered to content owners.

A New Route to the Screen: Bonnie Bruderer’s BINGE Movies + TV

A finished film is a major achievement, but for many independent creators, completing the project is only the beginning. Finding a route to viewers, securing distribution, and earning revenue can be just as demanding as making the work itself. Bonnie Bruderer encountered that challenge through her own experience in television, and it became the starting point for BINGE Movies + TV, the streaming and distribution company she founded.

Bruderer began producing her own television show in New York City in late 2014. The experience gave her a close look at the creative side of the industry, but it also brought a practical question into focus: how could creators get their work in front of an audience beyond the traditional television system? As streaming grew, she saw an opportunity to help independent producers navigate a changing distribution landscape.

Today, BINGE Movies + TV works with filmmakers and content owners to distribute films, series, documentaries, and other programming. Its streaming app is one part of the business, while its wider distribution and licensing work helps place projects on other streaming outlets. The company continues to seek placements across platforms and expand the reach of the content it represents.

For Bruderer, the work is not simply about getting a title onto a single service. Different projects have different audiences and commercial possibilities, so the route to market may vary. BINGE Movies + TV considers each project individually and looks at a range of options, including major streaming services, niche platforms, cable, and even DVD distribution where it makes sense. The aim is to find a practical path for the particular film or programme, rather than treating one outlet as the only meaningful destination.

That approach responds to a common difficulty for independent creators: visibility does not automatically lead to a distribution deal or reliable income. A project may attract attention at festivals and still struggle to reach a wider audience. BINGE Movies + TV’s distribution services are intended to help creators move beyond that bottleneck by handling outreach and pitching to potential licensing partners. Its public materials also emphasize that creators retain ownership of their work, while the company helps them pursue distribution opportunities.

The business has also developed a model that connects its own streaming service with the wider licensing market. Content partners can earn through different routes, including revenue from distribution on partner platforms. BINGE Movies + TV’s published agreement outlines quarterly reporting and payment of a share of net proceeds from platform revenue, while its distribution information describes a revenue-sharing option for branded channels. These arrangements place monetization alongside distribution as part of the service offered to content owners.

Bruderer’s role has involved building the relationships and operational capacity needed to make that model work. The company has to assess projects, understand where they might fit, coordinate submissions, and maintain connections with platforms and licensing partners. BINGE Movies + TV has a team with experience across different parts of the entertainment business, including cinema and content licensing. That mix of expertise helps the company evaluate opportunities beyond its own streaming app.

BINGE Movies + TV is also focused on growing its direct subscription audience. Bruderer has identified subscriber growth as a key priority and discussed testing different marketing approaches to reach viewers. The company’s subscription model is closely tied to its creator-focused positioning: as the subscriber base expands, a portion of subscription revenue is shared with creators.

After more than a decade in the streaming and distribution business, Bruderer’s work reflects a shift in how independent content can find its audience. BINGE Movies + TV is not only building a place for viewers to watch films and shows; it is also working across the distribution process that can help those projects travel further. For independent filmmakers, that means another potential route from a completed project to a wider market, with distribution and earning opportunities considered together.

Jean-Pierre Cubizolle from Impact2Scale Calls for Anticipatory, Convergent Governance to Advance the UN Sustainable Development Goals

With a career spanning international consulting, corporate leadership, and board-level responsibilities, Jean-Pierre Cubizolle is the Founder and President of CHC Corporate Horizon Consulting, which specializes in dental support services, occupational health, performance and risk management, and emotional intelligence. Since 2025, he has served as a Partner and Board Member of Impact2Scale. From 2020 to 2024, he was regularly invited to speak at Horasis conferences.

His professional experience includes leadership positions across consulting, human resources, and healthcare. From 1992 to 2010, he founded and chaired CCT Management Group SA, a European consulting firm focused on organizational efficiency, performance management, risk management, skills development, and executive compensation. The group operated through subsidiaries in Switzerland, France, Italy, Spain, Luxembourg, Dubai and Egypt. In 2010, it merged with hkp/// Group, where Jean-Pierre served as Senior Partner and Director until 2013.

Earlier in his career, he was Corporate Director of International Human Resources at Motorola Inc. in Chicago from 1979 to 1985, before helping to establish TPF&C Continental Europe. He later co-founded Edenweiss Group SA, serving as Director and CEO from 2013 to 2016.

In early 2026, Jean-Pierre Cubizolle co-authored The Legacy of All with Olivier Ferrari, Founder and CEO of Amberstone Finance SA. This book provides a broader reflection on sustainable development, collective responsibility, and the legacy passed on to future generations.

Jean-Pierre is now developing these reflections through a forthcoming White Paper proposing a model of “anticipatory and convergent governance” for the Sustainable Development Goals. Building on the experience of the first decade of the UN 2030 Agenda, the paper will explore how governance mechanisms could evolve to translate shared commitments into more coherent, measurable and sustainable outcomes.

He argues that, more than a decade after the UN 2030 Agenda established 17 Goals, 169 targets and more than 230 indicators, the central challenge is no longer simply to define additional goals, but to strengthen the governance mechanisms required to transform commitments into measurable results.

Jean-Pierre notes that the global context has shifted markedly since 2015. Armed conflicts, rising geopolitical tensions, persistent poverty, ecosystem degradation, pressure on planetary boundaries, and declining trust in multilateral institutions all point to the same conclusion: ambitious goals alone are not enough without governance that can translate them into effective action.

Two complementary principles should guide this evolution:

Convergent governance: creating the conditions for international organizations, States, businesses, civil society, academia, and citizens to retain their own responsibilities, competencies, and autonomy, while aligning their decisions and actions toward a shared vision and measurable collective outcomes.

Anticipatory governance: developing permanent vigilance capable of identifying situations that may generate future risks, assessing their probable trajectories, and acting early enough to keep those risks under control before they reach critical or irreversible levels.

Jean-Pierre further suggests that international institutions should evolve to better integrate strategic foresight, early warning, mediation, operational coordination, and accountability. This reflection also extends to the governance of the United Nations Security Council, including its composition, decision-making processes, and the implementation of its decisions, to strengthen its contribution to SDG 16 on Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions and, more broadly, to the objectives of the UN 2030 Agenda.

“The SDGs should be regarded not only as a set of objectives, but as the expression of a shared global responsibility. Their success will depend less on the adoption of new goals than on our capacity to anticipate emerging challenges, make autonomous actors converge around a shared vision, and transform that vision into coherent, measurable and collective outcomes.”

Jean-Pierre Cubizolle, President, Corporate Horizon Consulting

Jean-Pierre describes the end of this decade as an important window for reflection. The approaching succession of the UN Secretary-General, changes in political leadership across many Member States and the 2030 deadline are converging at a time when the international community is already considering what should follow the current UN Agenda. Together, these developments provide an opportunity for collective reflection on the future of the SDGs, their governance and the international institutions involved in their implementation.

Jean-Pierre also highlights the role of new tools in supporting this evolution. Artificial intelligence can help analyze complex data, detect emerging risks, and simulate scenarios to support SDG monitoring and decision-making.

He finally emphasizes the importance of giving micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) a more structured role in delivering the Goals. MSMEs account for around 90% of businesses worldwide, generate 60–70% of global employment and contribute approximately 50% of global GDP. MSMEs offer an exceptional capacity to translate the SDGs from international commitments into millions of concrete decisions and actions throughout the global economy.

The book “The Legacy of All” is available on request. The white paper will be available in November 2026.

Krzysztof Dziarmaga | Bringing Digital Intelligence to Maritime Operations

A ship’s condition is often assessed through inspections, reports, and the experience of the people responsible for keeping it running. But as maritime operations become more complex, technology creates new ways to monitor vessels and make decisions using timely information. For Krzysztof Dziarmaga, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Smart Nautilus Ltd, the opportunity lies in connecting practical maritime knowledge with digital tools that can make operations more efficient, transparent, and sustainable.

Krzysztof is a maritime technology leader whose work spans digital transformation, subsea operations, remote inspection technologies, and the development of solutions for the maritime industry. Throughout his career, spanning roles from seafarer to Technical Superintendent, he maintained a strong interest in emerging technologies. After founding his own company, he focused on helping shipowners, operators, and other maritime stakeholders leverage data and technology to enhance vessel efficiency, ensure regulatory compliance, and optimize asset management.

As CTO and Co-founder of Smart Nautilus, Krzysztof leads the company’s technology strategy, product development, and innovation roadmap. Its solutions bring together technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), underwater robotics, environmental monitoring, AI-driven analytics, digital reporting, and real-time decision-support tools. The aim is to give vessel operators clearer, more continuous insight into their assets, supporting a shift from periodic inspections towards proactive, data-informed management.

A significant part of his work involves remotely operated vehicle (ROV) technologies and underwater inspection systems. These tools can support hull inspections, asset integrity assessments, and condition-based maintenance. Krzysztof’s areas of expertise include monitoring vessel hull conditions, inspecting propellers and rudders, assessing biofouling, managing marine growth, and using digital survey reports to help operators understand the condition of their vessels.

Biofouling has been a particular focus. Marine growth on a vessel’s hull can affect fuel consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, performance, and regulatory compliance. Krzysztof has helped develop technology-based approaches that support ongoing monitoring, earlier detection, and better-informed maintenance decisions. Through Smart Nautilus’ digital ecosystem, operators can gain a clearer picture of hull conditions, plan maintenance, and respond to evolving international requirements related to biofouling management.

His work also reflects the growing role of environmental responsibility in maritime operations. By connecting inspection data, monitoring systems, and digital reporting, technology can help operators understand the effects of their decisions and identify opportunities to improve how vessels are maintained and managed. For Krzysztof, these capabilities are part of a wider shift towards safer and more sustainable operations.

Beyond product and technology development, he has worked to build partnerships across Europe, Australia, New Zealand, the US, and other maritime regions. He supports collaboration among technology providers, vessel operators, regulators, research institutions, and service organizations, recognizing that practical solutions often require expertise from across the industry. These partnerships have been involved in areas such as environmental monitoring, maritime digitalization, smart inspections, asset integrity, and intelligent reporting.

Krzysztof’s approach brings operational experience and emerging digital capabilities together. His focus is on turning complex information into useful insights for people responsible for vessels and marine assets. As the maritime sector continues to adopt automation and real-time intelligence, he remains committed to developing tools that support greater operational transparency and help stakeholders make informed decisions.

Through his role at Smart Nautilus, Krzysztof continues to contribute to the development of intelligent shipping and marine asset management, with an emphasis on connecting technology to the everyday needs of maritime operations.

Prof. Dr. Joseph Peebles | A Journey Built on Persistence, Purpose and Global Ambition

Success rarely arrives in a straight line. For some people, it is built through years of steady progress, while for others, the journey is marked by unexpected turns, challenges, and opportunities that gradually shape the person they become. For Sir, Prof. Dr. Joseph Peebles, President and CEO of Peebco Energy Group, persistence has remained a central part of that journey.

His recent achievement adds another milestone to an already extensive list of professional and academic accomplishments. Prof. Dr. Peebles has taken part in his second major international business and intellectual competition, competing on a global stage alongside some of the strongest participants in the field. The achievement reflects his continued interest in business, leadership, and intellectual development.

His journey has included recognition from a number of organisations and institutions over the years. On June 13, 2021, Dr. Peebles was among the recipients of the Catholic Man of the Year recognition within the St. Louis Catholic Archdiocese. The recognition marked one of several milestones that would follow in the years ahead.

Education has also remained an important part of his development. On June 25, 2024, he graduated from Harvard University’s two-year H-BAP Leadership Program. Later that year, on September 4, he was accepted into Seton Hall Law School for International Business Compliance and Regulations.

His professional and institutional affiliations continued to grow. On November 10, 2024, Dr. Peebles was inducted into The Royal Society of St. George, followed by his appointment to the United Nations Association on November 26. On January 21, 2025, he was accepted into the American Bar Association.

The academic side of his journey reached another milestone on August 22, 2025, when Dr. Peebles earned his PhD in International Trade & Finance. He later earned a Professorship in International Literature on February 15, 2026, adding another dimension to his academic pursuits.

Alongside these achievements, his work has also received international recognition. On May 19, 2021, Prof. Dr. Joseph Peebles, PhD received an international nomination for an International Peace Ambassador.

The year 2026 brought several significant moments. On May 21, Prof. Dr. Peebles won first place in an international business competition, receiving recognition as the Global Business Innovation & Sustainability Leader of the Year. The achievement placed his work in business and sustainability on an international platform.

Just over a month later, on June 29, 2026, he received the Business Leadership & Excellence Award for Top International Chairman & Chief Executive Officer. On August 31, 2026, he was also awarded an international certificate recognising him among the Global Business Icons to Follow in 2026.

For Dr. Peebles, however, these milestones appear to represent more than a collection of titles and awards. His own reflections place greater emphasis on the resilience required to keep moving forward when the path becomes difficult.

“Over time, hard work does pay off,” Sir Joseph states. “Yes, there will be bumps in the road along the way. There will be failures to launch, and there will be detours within the journey.”

That understanding of perseverance forms an important part of his outlook. He points to versatility, adaptability, and the determination to remain engaged in the competition as qualities that help people navigate difficult periods.

His ambitions also extend beyond personal achievement. Through his work, he says his journey has always been connected to providing for both the planet and the greater good of its inhabitants. That broader purpose gives his business and leadership journey another layer, linking professional ambition with a desire to contribute to something beyond the individual.

The road ahead will undoubtedly bring its own challenges, but Dr. Peebles’ story so far is one of continued movement. From education and professional development to international recognition and business competition, each milestone has added another chapter to his career.

Perhaps the philosophy that best captures his outlook comes from the French saying he uses at the end of his reflection: “Après la pluie, le beau temps”, or, after the rain, the good weather comes. For Dr. Peebles, it is a reminder that difficult periods do not have to define the destination.

Geoffrey Spooner | Turning Field Experience into the Future of Building Intelligence

What if the people who spend years fixing buildings are the ones best placed to rethink how those buildings are understood?

For Geo Spooner, Founder and CEO of CoreTherm Aerial, the answer began long before the idea of a technology company. Nearly three decades spent working across construction, facilities, property operations, and the built environment gave him a close view of how buildings are actually built, operated, repaired, and maintained. His experience was shaped by construction sites, rooftops, mechanical rooms, and job trailers, not by Silicon Valley or a laboratory.

That background became the foundation for a different kind of entrepreneurial journey.

Geo is FAA Part 107 certified and a licensed thermographer, bringing together practical experience with technical knowledge of the built environment. Over the years, he began noticing that some of the biggest opportunities were often hidden inside problems that an industry had simply become accustomed to accepting.

That realization led to CoreTherm Aerial.

The company was founded around a straightforward but ambitious idea: physical assets should have an engineering memory. Buildings produce vast amounts of information throughout their lifetimes, but much of that information remains scattered across photographs, reports, spreadsheets, service records, and the knowledge of individual people.

Geo sees an opportunity to change that.

CoreTherm combines radiometric thermal data, engineering intelligence, and artificial intelligence to create a deeper understanding of how physical assets change over time. The goal is not simply to collect more information, but to make that information useful to owners and operators before small problems turn into expensive capital events.

For someone who spent much of his career seeing these challenges firsthand, the idea is deeply connected to his own experience. Technology, in this case, is not being developed simply because it is new. It is being developed because Geo has seen a real problem from the ground level and believes there is a better way to address it.

But CoreTherm is only one part of his story.

His path to entrepreneurship has included mistakes, risks, failures, and rebuilding. There have been chapters he is proud of and others that brought lessons that no classroom could have provided. Rather than separating those experiences from his leadership journey, Geo sees them as part of what shaped the way he operates today.

That perspective has given him a practical view of leadership. He believes conviction matters, but so does speed. Accountability matters, but so does the willingness to challenge familiar ways of doing things. For him, entrepreneurship is not about accepting that something has always been done a certain way. It is about having the courage to ask whether it still needs to be done that way.

This mindset is particularly important in an industry where many processes have developed over decades. Buildings are long-term assets, and decisions made today can affect their performance and costs for years. Bringing better information into those decisions could change how owners think about maintenance, repairs, and capital planning.

At 47, Geo does not see himself as someone reaching the end of an entrepreneurial journey. Quite the opposite.

“I’m 47 years old, and I genuinely believe I am just getting started.”

That statement captures much of what defines his approach. He is not interested in building another company simply for the sake of calling it successful. His ambition is larger: to build something that can change the way an entire industry thinks about its physical assets.

Perhaps the most revealing part of his story is that he does not consider knowing everything to be his greatest strength. His advantage, he believes, came from something much simpler: curiosity.

“My greatest advantage was never that I knew everything.

It was that I was never afraid to ask why everyone else accepted it.”

That question sits at the heart of Geo Spooner’s journey. From construction sites and rooftops to building CoreTherm Aerial, his career has been shaped by looking closely at problems that others may have learned to overlook. Now, he is bringing that same mindset to the intersection of thermal data, engineering, and AI, with the ambition of helping the built environment become more intelligent, more proactive, and better prepared for what comes next.

Yves Marc Ouffoue | Building Africa’s Next Private Aviation Network

In private aviation, the journey begins long before an aircraft takes off. Finding the right aircraft, matching it to a client’s needs, coordinating with operators, and navigating the realities of different African markets all require experience and strong relationships. Yves Marc Ouffoue, known as Marc, has built nearly 15 years of that experience across the African aviation industry, and today he is using it to build a stronger network for private jet brokerage on the continent.

An Ivorian aviation entrepreneur and private jet brokerage expert, Marc has developed his expertise entirely within the African market. His career has involved working closely with operators across passenger aviation, cargo logistics, and specialised aviation support missions, including military-related operations in selected African countries.

That experience has given Marc a close view of how the African aviation market works and where there is room to improve the way private aviation services are connected and delivered. At 37, he is now taking that experience into entrepreneurship with a focus on strengthening the role of African brokers.

One of his key ventures is The Black Jet Brokers (BJB), a pan-African network created exclusively for jet brokers based on the continent. The idea behind BJB is to bring together the knowledge, connections, and reach of African brokers and turn them into a stronger collective force.

Marc’s vision is centred on supporting the growing mobility needs of Africa’s elite and institutional stakeholders. By creating a more connected brokerage community, he aims to help brokers improve service standards, respond more efficiently, and handle high-level travel requirements with greater ease.

The initiative also reflects his belief that African brokers should have a stronger role in shaping the continent’s private aviation market. Rather than relying entirely on networks outside Africa, BJB is designed around the people and businesses already operating within the continent.

Marc is also leading Empty Legs Africa, an initiative focused on promoting and monetising empty-leg flights across, to, and from Africa. These flights create an opportunity to make use of aircraft that would otherwise travel without passengers, potentially opening new revenue opportunities for both brokers and operators.

For Marc, the initiative is about finding value in an existing part of private aviation while improving access to aviation solutions across the continent. It adds another dimension to his work, connecting commercial opportunity with a more efficient use of available aircraft capacity.

Both ventures come from the same underlying idea: Africa’s private aviation industry has significant potential, but that potential can be strengthened through better connections, stronger local networks, and a deeper understanding of the continent’s unique requirements.

As he continues developing The Black Jet Brokers and Empty Legs Africa, his focus remains firmly on Africa. His ambition is to empower the continent’s brokers, create new opportunities for operators, and contribute to a private aviation ecosystem that is better connected and better equipped to serve the people and institutions driving Africa’s growth.

For Yves Marc Ouffoue, the future of private aviation in Africa is not simply about more aircraft in the sky. It is about building the relationships and networks on the ground that make those journeys possible.
