Hanan Al-Shayeb | Leading Fintech Growth Across Markets

The financial world has evolved during the past two decades. Payments have moved online, digital banking has increased, and new types of financial technology have opened up previously inaccessible markets. Hanan Al-Shayeb has spent more than 25 years navigating these shifts, founding companies and directing teams in fintech, payments, digital assets, e-commerce, and regulated financial services.

As a C-level executive, Hanan has worked across MENA, Europe, Africa, and other international markets. Her experience combines business growth with the practical side of running financial services businesses, including regulation, partnerships, market expansion, and day-to-day execution.

Today, she serves as the DFSA-authorised CEO/SEO of Altery, where she brings together commercial goals and strong governance. Her experience in regulated financial services has given her a clear understanding of the care and responsibility required when building businesses in complex markets.

Before Altery, Hanan held senior leadership roles at companies including Paytiko, Bybit, OPay, JollyPay, Souq.com, and Bayt.com. Across these roles, she has led international teams, entered new markets, developed partnerships, and helped businesses achieve double- and triple-digit growth.

Her work covers a wide part of the financial technology sector, from payments and digital banking to cross-border financial solutions, acquiring and issuing, and digital asset infrastructure.

What stands out in Hanan’s career is her focus on turning plans into results. Growth, in her view, is not simply about having a good idea. It also requires the right people, strong partnerships, careful planning, and the ability to execute.

That approach has helped her build payment ecosystems and lead businesses through periods of change. Working across different regions has also given her experience with markets that have their own customers, regulations, business cultures, and challenges.

Her career has earned recognition through several awards, including Women Rising in Fintech – UAE 2025, Excellence in Women’s Leadership – FinTech 2026, and Visionary Fintech & Payments CEO of the Year – 2026.

Beyond her executive roles, Hanan is involved with organisations supporting women and the wider fintech community. She is a member of the MENA Fintech Association, WOMENCHOICE.ORG, and the Dubai Business Women Council (DBWC). She also gives back through mentorship as a Mentor at Ignyte.

Hanan believes that generating possibilities for individuals and businesses is intimately related to leadership. Her expertise in a variety of sectors and geographical areas has given her insight into the potential for significant change when technology, sound strategy, and capable leadership are combined.

Today, she continues to focus on fintech and the future of financial services. She continues to work on building responsible, adaptable and sustainable businesses that can grow from MENA to international markets.

Her journey is a career built around change. In a world of constant change, Hanan Alshayeb is determined to help shape what’s next in financial services through growth, innovation and hands-on leadership.

The Top 10 Innovative Leaders featured here come from different backgrounds, but their stories share a common thread. They have been willing to question the usual approach and create their own definition of success.

Their journeys remind us that progress does not always come from following a proven path. Sometimes, it starts with the decision to take a different one.

title: Equinor Warns That if Oil and Gas Fields are Not Approved, it May Cease Investing in the UK

title: Residents of a Kibbutz Devastated by Hamas-Led Attacks on October 7 Struggle to Rebuild
author: editor
excerpt: In the empty dining room of Kibbutz Nir Oz, which was once the vibrant center of a close-knit, 400-person Israeli settlement devastated by the Hamas-led onslaught on October 7, 2023, roosting birds now coo among the ceiling tiles.We used to visit and dine together. Dalit Ram Aharon, who is taking me around with her husband, Achi, recalls, “There were lots of activities here, also holidays to celebrate.” A startling reminder of what happened to the missing residents may be found by the glass entrance doors, which are peppered with gunshot holes. Following the attacks three years ago, stickers were placed on each household’s postbox: red ones show those who were slain, and black ones show those who were taken hostage. “”Kidnapped or murdered, that’s one out of four of us,” adds Dalit. “including infants and young children.” Residents of the kibbutz, which is located just a mile (1.6 km) from the Gaza border and was among the worst-hit areas, are going through another difficult period of reflection as Israel commemorates the third anniversary of its bloodiest day ever. At the Siman Tov family’s nearby burned-out home, where a wind chime hangs at the entrance, time seems to stop still. Tamar and Yonatan are pictured with their three kids: their two-year-old son, Omer, and their five-year-old twin girls, Shahar and Arbel. The parents were shot through the door of their bomb shelter, which was not intended to withstand gunfire but rather rockets fired from Gaza. title: After a Boy’s Hand was Blown off During Student Protests, France Stopped Using Stun Grenades
author: editor
excerpt: Following the blowing off of a 15-year-old’s hand earlier this week, France has halted the deployment of stun grenades to quell the nationwide student protests. According to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, he had asked for a delay until the details of Monday’s incident in Lens were “clarified” after officials and demonstrators gave differing stories. Over 500 schools were either completely or partially closed on Wednesday as the disruption persisted. Following complaints from various groups about police employing excessive force against youths, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has supported the police reaction. He denied that security officers had “orders to confront” the youths in a speech to the country on Wednesday nite. He stated that by the end of October, the government would provide a package of ideas, including building renovations to increase the number of teachers available, after looking into the demands made by students. He did not provide any more information. The alleged “anger of young people does not come from nowhere,” he stated. According to Education Minister Édouard Geffray, 24 schools have been “set alight or vandalised” to the point that they will be closed for several weeks, impacting 30,000 students. title: On October 7, Manila Celebrates Palestinian Heritage Day with a Demonstration and art Exhibit
author: editor
excerpt: In honour of Palestinian Heritage Day, an art exhibition debuted in the Philippines this week. The University of the Philippines (UP)-College of Fine Arts (CFA) Art Gallery features a variety of images, crafts, and devotional items that depict the Palestinian way of life. The month-long exhibition, “Palestine: Living Heritage, Enduring Steadfastness,” was opened by UP President Angelo Jimenez and Palestinian ambassador to the Philippines Mounir Anastas. It provides visitors with a direct connection to the country’s ongoing cultural traditions. Images of Gaza’s historical landmarks before and after they were destroyed by Israeli occupation forces are contrasted with pictures of ancient sites throughout the West Bank. The exhibit’s first docent, Ambassador Anastas, described traditional Palestinian arts, including devotional objects, painting, and needlework. He thanked the CFA, the institution, and its Office of International Linkages for their dedication to international solidarity, education, and cultural preservation. The exhibit, according to CFA, offers evidence of a culture’s lasting beauty and vitality in the face of the deliberate destruction of Palestinian identity, communal memory, history, and territory. The exhibition, according to the top fine arts institution in the Philippines, presents “Palestinian visual culture to testify to the catastrophic loss of a people’s physical and cultural memory alongside the genocide happening across the Gaza Strip today.” The display spreads the message of solidarity and the need for social justice by highlighting both concrete and intangible cultural assets throughout this crisis, according to the institution. title: MPs From the Indian Opposition Were Arrested in Protest Against the Election Chief
author: editor
excerpt: Several opposition MPs were arrested by Delhi police when they attempted to march and demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner due to a contentious change to the voter roll. Rahul Gandhi, the main opposition leader, his sister Priyanka, and other Members of Parliament were compelled to board a police bus. After being freed soon after, they started a sit-in close to the Election Commission headquarters and continued their march. It is the most recent development in an expanding dispute over a national voter roll change. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has been accused by opposition parties of supervising a procedure that could help Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Both the BJP and the Election Commission have denied this accusation. “Some of the MPs tried to take some other roads to the Election Commission building.” Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Manjeet Sheoran told the BBC, “We have officers stationed at multiple points, from where the protesters were picked up in buses and taken to different police stations.” The number of MPs held was not disclosed by the police. 237 MPs from various parties took part in the march, according to the opposition. Only four days had passed since the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical organization supported by Generation Z, held protests in Delhi and Mumbai and called for the resignation of the CEC. The group has called for more protests on October 10 and has referred to those demonstrations as the start of a national campaign. The Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is at the heart of the dispute. title: How China’s Imports Caused a Hazardous Addiction in India
author: editor
excerpt: Enter an Indian toy store and, in addition to finding a child’s new favourite toy, you can learn more about the country’s struggle for improved commercial ties with its big neighbour, China. India increased tariffs on imported toys from 20% to 60% and finally to 70% six years ago in an effort to discourage local production and prevent inferior toys from entering its market. Retailers were furious, claiming that domestic companies could never compete with products manufactured abroad. However, the combination of stricter quality control requirements and increased customs fees was effective. Indian toy exports increased from approximately $129 million to $200 million during the same period, while imports decreased by a third from nearly $300 million (£227 million) in 2020 to $100 million this year. Additionally, the nation was able to significantly lessen its reliance on China, which controlled 70% of the regional toy market. In India’s usually fruitless attempts to correct an increasingly uneven trading relationship with its larger neighbor—which some experts claim is currently among the most asymmetric in the world—the industry stands out as a rare exception. Its trade deficit with Beijing has only increased, from $44 billion in 2020 to an astounding $112 billion this year, despite the fact that diplomatic relations between the two nations completely collapsed after the Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and Delhi announced a number of anti-dumping duties and a ban on Chinese apps like Tik Tok.Kevin Zongzhe Li, a Washington-based Fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis, told the BBC that while political, security, and investment ties were at their lowest point, India’s economic reliance on China continued to grow. title: Trump Appoints a Top Spy to Lead a New AI Taskforce
author: editor
excerpt: The director of national intelligence has been appointed by US President Donald Trump to lead a new taskforce on artificial intelligence. title: Ahead Of the Midterm Elections, the US Labour Market is Sharply Slowing Down
author: editor
excerpt: Employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, marking a significant downturn in the US labour market prior to the midterm elections. According to data from the Bureau of Labour Statistics (BLS), headcounts in key industries, including tech and retail, barely changed despite a sharp decline in hiring since August. Meanwhile, the unemployment rate rose slightly from 4.1% in August to 4.2% in September. According to experts, the numbers indicate a slowing US economy, which reduces the likelihood that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in the future. According to updated BLS data for the month, 29,000 jobs were created in September compared to 133,000 in August. Although job growth has been a “rollercoaster” this year, George Brown, senior economist at Schroders, said a single disappointing report is unlikely to signal a long-term collapse. The lower number was “not disastrous,” according to Bradley Saunders, North America economist at Capital Economics, who also noted that changes in temporary visa policies and a decline in government jobs negatively affected overall growth. The statistics revealed conflict between “goods producing sectors that support the AI boom” and service businesses feeling the impact of changes brought about by the technology, according to Jeffrey Roach, chief economist at LPL Financial. title: Japan Increases Permanent Residency Fees by 20 Times
author: editor
excerpt: Japan has increased payments for foreigners seeking permanent residency by 20 times, to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955). Applicants for permanent residency must also meet stringent income, pension, and Japanese language requirements. Long lineups formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants rushed to avoid the cost increases, with Tokyo’s main immigration agency reporting wait times of more than seven hours. The fee increases are part of a series of adjustments to Japan’s immigration policy implemented by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in an effort to regulate the country’s fast rising foreign population. In July, Japan implemented a five-fold rise in visa costs for all foreigners, the country’s first in 50 years. Authorities stated that this was done to “reflect inflation and exchange rate fluctuations”. Although immigration remains politically contentious and regulated in Japan, the country’s ageing population is increasingly reliant on foreign labour to fill labour shortages. Japan’s foreign resident population topped 4.12 million at the end of 2025, a 9.5% increase over the previous year. However, this has heightened concerns about immigration and social change. Takaichi has made managing immigration one of her top goals since taking office in October of last year. title: Following Demonstrations Over the Removal of an 87-year-Old Woman From Her Flat, Spain Banned Evictions
author: editor
excerpt: Following protests over the nation’s housing crisis, which were triggered by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her Madrid home last week, Spain’s coalition government has approved new housing measures. The plans, which include a prohibition on evictions until 2030, were discussed by ministers on Tuesday. More than five million individuals would benefit from the measures, according to Health Minister Mał García, while opposition leader Míriam Nogueras claimed that “small landlords out in the cold” were left out of the deal. Although the government intends to hold the vote as soon as this Friday, the plans, presented as two decrees, take effect immediately but must be approved by Congress within a month. In addition to lacking a majority in parliament, Pedro Sánchez’s leftist coalition administration has struggled to persuade right-leaning parties to accept earlier directives. Right-leaning parties vetoed a decree intended to roll over rental contracts in April. According to García of the Sumar alliance, additional measures decided upon on Tuesday included prohibiting investment firms from purchasing real estate, tightening regulations on short-term and room rentals, and extending contracts until 2028. title: Lindsay Clancy Shows up in Court while her Attorney Attempts to Have The Murder Case Dropped
author: editor
excerpt: For the first time since her murder trial collapsed earlier this month, Lindsay Clancy, the American mother charged with killing her three children, has made an appearance in court. Prosecutors claimed the state had “met its burden” in establishing her guilt, despite her defence team’s Tuesday argument that the judge should dismiss her case. Although Clancy, 36, does not dispute killing her three children in 2023, her defence team contends that she was experiencing acute postpartum psychosis at the time. The killings, according to the prosecution, were deliberate. Whether she will be put on trial again is yet unknown. Judge William Sullivan said a hearing on November 2 will address several issues, including the request to dismiss the case. Kevin Reddington, Clancy’s attorney, filed a motion on Tuesday asking for her to be declared not guilty under Rule 25, a Massachusetts statute that stipulates that a defendant shall be found not guilty if the prosecution fails to provide a strong case. Reddington also presented a fresh defence, claiming there was insufficient proof that Clancy had murdered her kids. title: What Is the Difference Between Debt Collection, Litigation and Enforcement in Saudi Arabia?
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: When a business is owed money, it may hear several legal terms used during the recovery process, including debt collection, litigation, and enforcement. These terms are connected, but they do not mean the same thing. Understanding the difference can help businesses identify what stage they are dealing with and avoid taking the wrong approach when trying to recover an outstanding amount. In simple terms, debt collection focuses on recovering an outstanding debt, litigation concerns resolving a legal dispute through the courts, and enforcement concerns executing an enforceable judgment or instrument. The appropriate step depends on the circumstances of the individual matter. What Is Debt Collection? Debt collection generally refers to efforts to recover money that remains unpaid. For a business, this may involve an overdue invoice, an unpaid commercial account, or another outstanding financial obligation. The first stage may involve reviewing the agreement and supporting documents, contacting the debtor, requesting payment, and attempting to resolve the matter without immediately escalating it into a formal legal dispute. The exact approach depends on the contractual relationship, the amount involved, the available documentation, and the reason for non-payment. Debt collection is therefore not necessarily the same as going to court. A business may be able to resolve an unpaid account through communication or an agreed payment arrangement without commencing litigation. When Does Debt Collection Become More Complicated? An unpaid amount becomes more complicated when the debtor disputes the obligation or refuses to resolve the matter despite repeated requests. For example, a customer may claim that: The invoice is incorrect The goods or services were not delivered as agreed The work was incomplete The agreed price was different The payment has already been made The contract does not require the amount being claimed In these circumstances, the business should examine the underlying agreement and evidence rather than treating the matter as a simple overdue payment. The distinction between an undisputed debt and a genuine commercial dispute can influence what happens next. What Is Litigation? Litigation is the process of resolving a legal dispute through court proceedings. A business may consider litigation when there is a dispute that cannot be resolved through other appropriate means and a formal legal determination is required. Commercial litigation can involve disagreements concerning contracts, payments, obligations, or other business relationships. The preparation for litigation can require careful review of: Contracts Invoices Correspondence Transaction records Delivery or performance documents Payment records Other evidence relevant to the dispute The precise requirements depend on the nature of the case. Litigation should therefore not be viewed simply as another name for debt collection. A debt may be undisputed, while litigation generally becomes relevant when a legal dispute requires formal resolution. Businesses dealing with a developing commercial dispute can consider the available litigation services in Saudi Arabia based on the circumstances of the matter. What Is Enforcement? Enforcement is different again. If a party has obtained an enforceable judgment or another enforceable instrument, the issue may move from establishing or resolving the claim to taking steps to execute the enforceable obligation. This distinction is particularly important for businesses that have already succeeded in obtaining a judgment. Winning a dispute and actually obtaining payment are not necessarily the same stage. The enforcement process is concerned with giving effect to an enforceable obligation in accordance with the applicable legal procedures. Businesses seeking to understand this stage can review enforcement services in Saudi Arabia for more information about the relevant legal service. Debt Collection vs. Litigation vs. Enforcement The easiest way to understand the difference is to consider the main question at each stage. Stage Main Question Debt collection How can the outstanding amount be recovered? Litigation Does a legal dispute need to be formally resolved? Enforcement How can an enforceable judgment or instrument be executed? These stages may sometimes connect, but they should not automatically be treated as one process. For example, a business may have an unpaid invoice but no dispute. The initial issue may therefore concern debt recovery. If the debtor challenges the underlying obligation and the matter cannot be resolved, litigation may become relevant. If the business subsequently obtains an enforceable judgment, the focus may then move to enforcement. Does Every Unpaid Debt Require Litigation? No. An overdue payment does not automatically mean that court proceedings are necessary. Before considering litigation, a business should understand why payment has not been made and whether the issue can be resolved through appropriate communication or other available recovery steps. The decision should take into account the amount involved, the contractual position, the available evidence, and the debtor’s response. Unnecessary escalation can create additional cost, time, and commercial disruption. At the same time, delaying action indefinitely can also create problems, particularly where the business has repeatedly attempted to recover an amount without success. Does Winning a Case Automatically Mean the Money Has Been Recovered? Not necessarily. A judgment establishes an enforceable legal outcome, but the business may still need to take the appropriate enforcement steps to pursue the amount awarded. This is why businesses should understand the difference between resolving a dispute and enforcing the resulting obligation. The legal strategy should consider the entire situation rather than focusing only on the initial dispute. What Should a Business Review Before Choosing the Next Step? Before deciding whether to pursue collection, litigation, or enforcement, a business should organize the facts and documents surrounding the matter. Important considerations may include: 1. Organize contracts, invoices, correspondence, delivery records, payment records, and other relevant documents. 4. Has a judgment already been obtained? If an enforceable judgment or instrument already exists, the issue may be different from an initial unpaid invoice. 5. What outcome does the business need? Does Winning a Case Automatically Mean the Money Has Been Recovered?

Not necessarily.

A judgment establishes an enforceable legal outcome, but the business may still need to take the appropriate enforcement steps to pursue the amount awarded.

This is why businesses should understand the difference between resolving a dispute and enforcing the resulting obligation.

The legal strategy should consider the entire situation rather than focusing only on the initial dispute.

What Should a Business Review Before Choosing the Next Step?

Before deciding whether to pursue collection, litigation, or enforcement, a business should organize the facts and documents surrounding the matter.

Important considerations may include:

1. Is the amount actually due?

Review the contract, invoice, payment terms, and relevant transaction records.

2. Does the debtor dispute the amount?

Identify whether there is a genuine disagreement concerning the contract, goods, services, or payment.

3. What evidence is available?

Organize contracts, invoices, correspondence, delivery records, payment records, and other relevant documents.

4. Has a judgment already been obtained?

If an enforceable judgment or instrument already exists, the issue may be different from an initial unpaid invoice.

5. What outcome does the business need?

The appropriate legal step should reflect the actual problem the business is trying to resolve.

Why Understanding the Difference Matters

Confusing debt collection, litigation, and enforcement can lead to unrealistic expectations.

For example, a business with an overdue invoice may assume that immediately starting court proceedings is always the best option. In another situation, a business may have already obtained a judgment but focus on the original dispute instead of understanding the enforcement stage.

A clearer understanding of the stages allows businesses to assess their position more logically.

It also helps them communicate more effectively with legal advisers and prepare the documents needed for the relevant process.

Consider a company that supplied goods to another business under a written commercial agreement.

The customer receives the goods but does not pay the final invoice.

The supplier first reviews the agreement and invoice and contacts the customer regarding the outstanding amount.

If the customer accepts that the amount is owed and agrees to pay, the matter may remain at the debt-collection stage.

If the customer instead claims that the goods did not meet the contractual requirements and refuses payment, the matter may become a commercial dispute requiring further assessment.

If the dispute proceeds to court and the supplier obtains an enforceable judgment, the focus may then shift to enforcement.

The example demonstrates why the three terms should not be treated as interchangeable.

How Can Businesses Prepare for Debt Disputes?

Good preparation starts before a payment problem occurs.

Businesses should maintain clear commercial agreements, accurate invoices, transaction records, and written communications.

When a payment becomes overdue, records should be organized promptly rather than only after the matter has escalated.

A clear documentary record can help a business understand its position and determine what further action may be appropriate.

Final Thoughts

Debt collection, litigation, and enforcement are connected but distinct parts of dealing with unpaid commercial obligations and legal disputes.

Debt collection focuses on recovering an outstanding amount. Litigation concerns the formal resolution of a legal dispute. Enforcement concerns the execution of an enforceable judgment or instrument.

The correct approach depends on the facts, documentation, contractual relationship, and current legal position.

Businesses should therefore assess where the matter actually stands before deciding what action to take.

title: In a World First, a Rogue OpenAI Agent “Infiltrated” an Australian Government Website
author: editor
excerpt: In what experts claim is the first instance of its sort in history, a rogue OpenAI bot gained access to private information on an Australian government website in June. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated in New York on Wednesday, local time, that the agent “infiltrated” a statistics portal that held “non-sensitive” data from Medicare, Australia’s universal healthcare program. He told OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that there would be “legal consequences” for taking “too long” to reveal the breach during a “very frank discussion” with Altman. OpenAI claimed to have discovered the breach only in August when examining “misaligned model activity” and sent an email on September 10 to an Australian government agency’s general inbox. The email was forwarded to Australia’s cybersecurity center five days later by that government agency, Services Australia, before the prime minister and a government minister were informed. Albanese claimed that when he spoke with Altman, he expressed “Australia’s extreme concern about this incident” and expressed his “disappointment” that the business had waited months to disclose the breach and “the nature of the way” it did so. According to the Australian leader, Altman had admitted that OpenAI had “issues with protocols.” Albanese stated that the nation’s cybersecurity agency would conduct a “forensic investigation” to see whether additional government systems were impacted. title: Trump’s White House Media ban is Temporarily Overturned by a Judge
author: editor
excerpt: Three news organisations that the president excluded from the White House last week have been ordered by a federal judge to have their access restored right away. The judge declared that the prohibition “likely violated their constitutional due process rights” and ordered the restoration of access for CNN, MS NOW, and Politico for a period of 14 days. On Thursday morning, some of the publications’ correspondents claimed to have been turned away. After their reporters were refused admission last weekend, the three media outlets filed a lawsuit. In court, the administration defended the action, accusing the media of disseminating misleading information and endangering national security. Early on Thursday morning, it was unclear if all of the outlets’ reporters would be allowed to return to the White House. CNN said that while some of its reporters were let in, others were turned away. A Politico reporter claimed they were turned away, while MS Now reported that another reporter was also barred from entering. The president’s attorneys may pursue more legal action, and the White House has not yet commented on the decision. CNN, Politico, and MS NOW were “likely to succeed” in proving the White House had not used “adequate due process” while enforcing the ban, according to Judge Timothy Kelly. He also questioned the Trump administration’s claims that national security considerations drove the prohibitions, pointing out that the president had not mentioned this in his initial proclamation. title: Trump Claims he Would Support an Export Restriction on Fuel
author: editor
excerpt: In an effort to lower petrol prices for drivers, US President Donald Trump has stated that he would support plans to stop US diesel exports. His remarks come as US diesel prices surge to all-time highs and Republican lawmakers put pressure on the president to limit exports ahead of the midterm elections in November. Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Trump proposed that lowering overall gas prices might also be achieved by maintaining local supply within the US.That’s what I’ve also demanded. Let’s not send out the diesel, I said. We produce a lot of diesel. Regular car petrol might be slightly impacted by that’, he stated. Officials were evaluating “whether a full or partial ban would work” without interfering with refinery operations, according to US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. According to figures from the American Automobile Association, national average diesel prices reached a new high of $6.50 (£4.87) per gallon on Tuesday. Pump prices are under pressure since the Middle East conflict has limited the world’s oil supply. Ahead of the pivotal midterm elections on November 3rd, the rise in diesel prices has created political urgency. A number of Republicans are pressuring the government to limit the fuel’s export in order to relieve voters’ financial burden. title: In Response to Russian Threats, Lithuania is Prepared to “Fight Back” but has Evacuation Preparations, the PM told the BBC
author: editor
excerpt: The prime minister of Lithuania told the BBC that although his nation has prepared for evacuation in response to Russian threats, they “will not surrender” in the event of an assault. Lithuanians feel “constantly threatened” by Russia, according to Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius, who told Newsnight that this is partly due to drones breaching the country’s airspace. He warned Newsnight if his country was invaded, “we will fight back… we will engage”. But he added there were plans for a “variety of scenarios” and provided an example of moving elderly citizens out of cities “smoothly” and avoiding traffic congestion. The Russian outpost of Kaliningrad has a land border with Lithuania, a member of NATO. It is estimated that thousands of NATO soldiers, including German and American personnel, are based in the Baltic state. Although the US is now assessing its deployments in Europe, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda stated on Tuesday that a new US army rotation was on its way to his country. title: 15 Men are Found Guilty by a Sri Lankan Court of the Devastating Easter Sunday Explosions
author: editor
excerpt: 15 men who were accused of planning the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings that killed 270 people and injured over 500 were found guilty by Sri Lanka’s High Court. Naufer Moulavi, who authorities claimed was the mastermind behind the suicide attacks, was among those convicted. Nine other men were found not guilty. The coordinated explosions at three upscale hotels and three churches were the bloodiest in Sri Lanka since the country’s civil conflict ended in 2009. Among the dead were forty-five foreigners. The explosions claimed the lives of every bomber that carried out the attacks. The 25 individuals indicted were members of Sri Lanka’s Muslim minority, and investigators have already attributed the attacks to Islamist extremists. In detention, one person passed away. Before sentencing, the court session was adjourned. Two prison buses transported the accused, who had been charged with over 23,000 offences, to the High Court in the capital city of Colombo while handcuffed in pairs. Sri Lankans, many of whom were minors, made up the majority of those slain. Celebrity chef Shantha Mayadunne and her daughter, a young family of five, at least eight employees from the hotels targeted, and five members of the same family from Negombo, in western Sri Lanka, were among them. excerpt: A court has heard that a former police officer’s “jealous infatuation” with his ex drove him to use his work gun to murder a Sydney couple. title: India’s Corporate Crown Prepares for Change Amid Boardroom Mutiny
author: editor
excerpt: This week, the board of Tata Sons, one of India’s oldest conglomerates and owner of renowned British brands such as Jaguar Land Rover and Tetley Tea, defied its largest shareholder, Tata Trusts, by reappointing N Chandrasekaran as chairman and backing the holding company’s public listing. Tata Trusts, which owns 66% of Tata Sons, termed the decision “illegal” under its articles of association and opposed the listing, paving the way for prolonged turmoil and possibly a protracted judicial drama at Bombay House, the company’s 158-year-old headquarters. The Tatas, who are no strangers to boardroom disputes, are now facing a cloud of uncertainty on numerous levels. The resolution to reappoint Chandrasekharan, while accepted by the board, may be lost at the company’s Annual General Meeting because Tata Trusts is expected to vote against it, casting doubt on his future. According to reports, the meeting must take place by December 31. The previous meeting was adjourned due to a lack of quorum, but no new date has been scheduled.The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) of Tata Sons’ Board, which reappointed him, has no authority to make this choice. They can only give recommendations. Furthermore, their action violates the company’s governance rule, which requires executives to retire from active duties at age 65. title: In a Security Test, Google’s Gemini AI Compromised Three Businesses
author: editor
excerpt: During a test of its cyber-security capabilities, Google’s AI model Gemini broke into three businesses on its own, according to the firm, in what is believed to be the first instance of it doing so. A Google representative told the BBC that Gemini discovered “public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test” and that “the model stopped” in each case. The breaches occurred in May, and the impacted companies were notified. This follows increased public scrutiny of the pace of AI development, with some tech corporations advocating a pause because they worry about the technology’s potential harm to humanity. However, not all businesses or experts concur. The Wall Street Journal was the first to report on the breaches, which happened in May when an independent cyber-security assessment business called Irregular was conducting a test. Irregular said in a statement to the BBC on Saturday that, as part of its investigation, it notified Google and all impacted companies in July. All known problems on our end were fixed and resolved weeks ago thanks to Irregular’s prompt action,” it continued. title: Following Reports of An Air Raid in the Saudi Capital, Smoke was Visible Close to The Airport
author: editor
excerpt: Hours after air raid alarms were issued in the Saudi capital, a column of black smoke was observed close to Riyadh’s international airport. For the first time since a recent escalation in the fight with Iran-backed Houthi insurgents in neighbouring Yemen, locals were warned and advised to remain indoors. Since then, there have been several reported explosions in the city and significant issues at King Khalid International Airport; FlightRadar24, a tracking website, has reported lengthy delays and cancellations. According to one story, a fuel tank close to the airport may have been set on fire. Saudi authorities have not made an official statement. Firefighters were spotted attempting to put out the flames of a burned-out fuel tank owned by the national oil and gas corporation Aramco, according to an AFP journalist. Before giving the all-clear on Saturday morning, the Saudi Civil Defence had issued phone alerts over the night warning of possible danger in Riyadh and nearby areas. On condition of anonymity, locals told AFP that following the alarms, they heard what sounded like a volley of explosions reverberating throughout the city. title: What Will US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Talk in Washington Next Week?
author: editor
excerpt: US President Donald Trump will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping next week for the second time this year, as the two leaders seek stability in a relationship strained by issues ranging from trade to Taiwan and Iran to global concerns about artificial intelligence. Xi arrives for his first White House visit in a decade, leading an economy on course to produce a $1 trillion trade surplus for the second consecutive year. Trump, entrenched in the Iran war and with dismal support ratings, is seeking for trade victories to brag about to Americans fed up with rising prices. Markets will look for signals of an extension of the tariff truce, which was announced following a Trump-Xi summit in South Korea last October and is slated to expire on November 10. That agreement halted a trade war in which the world’s two largest economies threatened global supply lines with tariffs that exceeded 100 percent. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that the countries will make “some ‌announcements on agriculture and non-tariff barriers” this month. Traders will be looking for progress on an agreed mutual tariff reduction covering $30 billion in goods, which China could easily take by cutting duties on US agricultural imports. US officials say they have continued to press China to rectify its noncompliance with last year’s accord, while Beijing has sought additional tariff relief. author: editor

content:
Choosing a law firm in Saudi Arabia is an important decision, particularly when the matter involves a business dispute, company formation, debt recovery, inheritance, contracts, enforcement, or another issue governed by Saudi law. The right legal partner should do more than simply provide legal documents or represent you in court. They should understand your specific situation, the applicable Saudi legal framework, and the practical outcome you are trying to achieve.

There is no single law firm that is the right choice for every client. The appropriate firm depends on your legal issue, industry, location, budget, urgency, and whether you need local representation, commercial advice, or cross-border support. This guide explains the key factors to consider when comparing law firms in Saudi Arabia.

What Makes a Good Law Firm in Saudi Arabia?

A strong law firm should combine relevant legal knowledge with practical experience and professional standards. Before hiring a lawyer, consider the following:

  • Relevant practice-area experience: The firm should regularly handle matters similar to yours.
  • Knowledge of Saudi law: Local legal knowledge is particularly important when dealing with Saudi courts, regulators, contracts, or enforcement procedures.
  • Qualified lawyers: Verify that the lawyers representing you are properly licensed where required.
  • Clear communication: You should understand the legal position, available options, risks, and expected process.
  • Transparent fees: The scope of work and fee arrangements should be clearly explained before engagement.
  • Appropriate resources: Complex corporate or cross-border matters may require a broader team and international coordination.
  • Confidentiality and professionalism: Legal matters often involve commercially or personally sensitive information.

The Saudi Ministry of Justice provides services to search for licensed lawyers and verify the validity of lawyer licenses. This is an important step when assessing a legal professional in the Kingdom.

How Should You Evaluate Law Firms in Saudi Arabia?

Instead of choosing a firm simply because it appears high in a Google search or describes itself as the “best law firm in Saudi Arabia,” look at evidence that is relevant to your matter.

1. Check the Firm’s Practice Areas

Start by identifying exactly what legal help you need.

For example, a business dealing with a shareholder dispute may need corporate and commercial lawyers with litigation experience. A creditor trying to recover an unpaid commercial debt may need a firm that understands both debt collection and enforcement.

If you are comparing the services available from a Saudi law firm, review its legal services in Saudi Arabia to see whether its capabilities match the type of assistance you require.

Similarly, a foreign investor entering Saudi Arabia may need support with company formation, contracts, regulatory compliance, and ongoing corporate matters.

The firm’s practice areas should therefore match your legal requirements rather than simply being broad.

2. Consider Saudi Legal and Court Experience

Saudi Arabia has its own legal framework, regulatory procedures, and judicial processes. Local knowledge can therefore be particularly important when your matter involves Saudi authorities or courts.

The Saudi Bar Association maintains a directory of licensed lawyers, while the Ministry of Justice provides lawyer-related licensing and verification services. Checking professional credentials is a useful part of your due diligence.

3. Look at Experience Relevant to Your Matter

Years of experience can be useful, but the more important question is whether that experience is relevant.

For example:

Your legal need What to look for
Business formation Corporate and regulatory experience
Commercial dispute Litigation and dispute-resolution experience
Unpaid debt Debt recovery and enforcement capability
Contract issue Commercial contract expertise
Inheritance Estate and inheritance experience
Foreign investment Saudi regulatory and cross-border knowledge
Court enforcement Experience with Saudi enforcement procedures
Notarization Proper document preparation and authentication support

A firm’s ability to handle the particular type of legal problem is often more important than its overall size.

Comparing Law Firms: What Should You Look At?

Legal directories can provide another reference point when comparing firms. For example, Legal 500 evaluates firms across Saudi practice areas including commercial and corporate law, dispute resolution, banking and finance, projects and energy, real estate, and TMT.

This distinction matters.

A firm recognized for major corporate transactions may not be the ideal choice for an individual inheritance matter. Similarly, a firm with strong dispute-resolution credentials may be more appropriate for litigation than a firm whose primary focus is transactional work.

Therefore, use rankings and directories as one source of information, not as the only factor in your decision.

What Legal Services Can a Law Firm in Saudi Arabia Provide?

Depending on its structure and areas of practice, a Saudi law firm may provide services such as:

  • Corporate and commercial legal advice
  • Company formation and restructuring
  • Contract drafting and review
  • Litigation and court representation
  • Commercial dispute resolution
  • Debt collection and recovery
  • Enforcement of judgments
  • Regulatory and compliance advice
  • Notary and document-related services
  • Inheritance and asset management
  • Support for foreign investors and international businesses

For example, AlKhorayef Law Firm’s current service offering covers litigation and court representation, corporate and commercial advisory, contract documentation, enforcement, debt collection, notary and attestation, asset and inheritance management, and regulatory compliance.

Why AlKhorayef Law Firm May Be Suitable for Certain Clients

AlKhorayef Law Firm is a Riyadh-based Saudi law firm serving individuals, businesses, and international entities operating in the Kingdom. Its website describes a practice built around Saudi legal knowledge, litigation, corporate and commercial advisory, enforcement, debt recovery, inheritance matters, and legal consultancy.

Its suitability depends on the client’s requirements.

For businesses involved in commercial disputes, the firm’s litigation practice covers matters including contract disputes, partnership and shareholder disputes, financial claims, and representation before Saudi courts. Clients can review the firm’s litigation and court representation services when assessing whether this area matches their needs.

For creditors, its debt collection services in Saudi Arabia cover demand notices, negotiation, court representation, and recovery-related procedures.

For matters involving judgment execution, clients can also review the firm’s enforcement services in Saudi Arabia, which focus on enforcing court judgments, recovering debts, contract enforcement, and execution procedures.

For individuals and families, its asset and inheritance management services address estate and inheritance-related legal matters.

This makes the firm potentially relevant when a client needs several connected legal services rather than assistance with only one isolated document.

Choosing a Law Firm for a Business

Businesses should look beyond the immediate legal problem and consider whether the firm can support future requirements.

A company entering Saudi Arabia, for example, may initially need assistance with incorporation and regulatory requirements. Later, it may need contract drafting, employment advice, corporate governance, dispute resolution, debt recovery, or enforcement.

A law firm with relevant corporate and commercial capabilities can provide continuity as the business develops.

For foreign investors, local legal knowledge is especially important. Saudi market-entry requirements can involve multiple authorities and regulatory considerations, making early legal planning valuable. Businesses planning to enter the Kingdom can also review this guide on how to set up a company in Saudi Arabia.

Foreign investors should also understand potential compliance risks before beginning operations. AlKhorayef’s guide to common legal mistakes foreign investors make in Saudi Arabia covers issues such as licensing, contracts, tax compliance, employment requirements, and dispute-resolution planning.

Choosing a Law Firm for Individuals

Individuals should first identify the specific legal issue and then select a lawyer with relevant experience.

For example, inheritance matters require different expertise from commercial litigation. Similarly, a person involved in a contractual dispute may need a lawyer experienced in civil or commercial claims rather than a general legal consultant.

Ask the firm:

  1. Have you handled matters similar to mine?
  2. Who will actually handle my case?
  3. What documents do you need?
  4. What are the major legal risks?
  5. What are the possible stages of the matter?
  6. How will fees be calculated?
  7. How will I receive updates?

Clear answers to these questions can help you make a more informed decision.

Choosing a Law Firm for International Clients

International businesses and foreign investors often need more than knowledge of Saudi law. They may also require communication in English, document coordination, cross-border recovery, regulatory support, or coordination with lawyers in another jurisdiction.

The right firm should be able to explain Saudi requirements clearly to international clients and identify where local legal procedures interact with international transactions.

For cross-border disputes, enforcement can be particularly important. Businesses with foreign judgments or arbitral awards can also review AlKhorayef’s guide on enforcing a foreign court judgment in Saudi Arabia to understand the issues that may arise in cross-border enforcement.

Questions to Ask Before Hiring a Saudi Law Firm

Before formally engaging a firm, ask for clarity on:

  • The lawyer responsible for your matter
  • Relevant experience and practice area
  • Scope of legal services
  • Expected stages of the case
  • Key risks and potential complications
  • Communication arrangements
  • Fee structure
  • Required documentation
  • Whether additional specialists or foreign counsel may be required

Avoid selecting a lawyer solely on price. The cheapest option may not provide the experience or resources required for a complex legal matter.

Final Thoughts

The right law firm in Saudi Arabia is not necessarily the largest firm, the most expensive firm, or the firm described as “the best.” It is the firm whose legal expertise, experience, resources, communication, and approach match your particular needs.

For individuals, businesses, investors, and international clients, the decision should be based on practice-area expertise, Saudi legal knowledge, professional credentials, relevant experience, transparent communication, and the firm’s ability to handle the matter from start to finish.

Before making a decision, compare several suitable options, verify professional credentials, understand the scope of work, and choose legal counsel based on the nature and complexity of your matter.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the top law firms in Saudi Arabia?

There is no single official list that establishes the top law firm in Saudi Arabia for every legal matter. Legal directories such as Legal 500 evaluate firms across specific practice areas, while client requirements vary by industry and case type. The appropriate firm should therefore be selected based on relevant expertise, experience, credentials, and the nature of the legal matter.

What is the best law firm in Saudi Arabia?

There is no universally applicable “best” law firm. A firm that is highly suitable for corporate transactions may not be the best choice for litigation, debt recovery, inheritance, or enforcement. The better approach is to compare firms according to their relevant practice-area experience, Saudi legal expertise, professional credentials, communication, and ability to meet your specific requirements.

How do I choose a law firm in Saudi Arabia?

Start by identifying the type of legal assistance you need. Then compare firms based on relevant experience, practice areas, licensed lawyers, communication, fees, and resources. You can also verify lawyer licensing through Saudi Ministry of Justice services and the Saudi Bar Association’s licensed-lawyer directory.

What legal services do law firms in Saudi Arabia provide?

Depending on the firm, services may include corporate and commercial advice, contracts, litigation, dispute resolution, debt collection, enforcement, regulatory compliance, notary services, inheritance and asset management, and support for foreign investors. Always confirm that the specific firm handles the practice area relevant to your matter.

How much does a lawyer or law firm cost in Saudi Arabia?

Legal fees vary depending on the type, complexity, value, urgency, and duration of the matter. Corporate transactions and complex litigation may require substantially more work than a straightforward consultation or document review. Before engagement, ask the firm to clearly explain the scope of work, fee structure, and any additional costs.

Do I need a Saudi lawyer for legal matters in Saudi Arabia?

For matters requiring representation before Saudi courts, it is important to work with a lawyer who is properly licensed to practise in the Kingdom. The Ministry of Justice provides services for searching licensed lawyers and verifying lawyer-license validity.

title: Interest Rates in the US Increased for the First Time in Three Years
author: editor
excerpt: In an effort to halt increasing prices, US interest rates have been hiked for the first time in almost three years and may be raised even more. Higher interest rates can result in better returns on investments, but they also make borrowing more costly for those looking to get credit cards, loans, and mortgages. In a press conference on Wednesday after the ruling, Warsh stated that although there was “an attitude of optimism” among Fed leaders, inflation was still an issue. The Fed aims to manage inflation at 2% or less, just as many other central banks. US inflation has exceeded the goal “for more than five years,” according to Warsh. Due to rising wholesale oil prices since the beginning of the US-Israel war with Iran, fuel prices have skyrocketed, making affordability one of the main concerns of American voters. Numerous goods and services have become more expensive as a result. title: Following a US House Decision, India is Threatened with a 100% Tax on Russian Oil
author: editor
excerpt: One of the largest oil importers in the world, India, has benefited from Russia’s war-related disruption of the world’s oil markets for the past four years. Following the invasion of Ukraine, Russian crude was diverted from western markets to Indian refineries, frequently at alluring discounts. The deal has reduced the price of one of India’s largest imports and provided a plentiful supply of oil for its refiners. This deal is now posing a geopolitical concern. On Wednesday, the US House of Representatives passed a bill granting President Donald Trump extensive authority to impose sanctions on Russia and tariffs of up to 100% on nations that purchase Russian gas and oil. Trump will now have the opportunity to sign it into law. Due to their significant purchases of Russian oil, China and India are among the most vulnerable. According to the think tank Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), between December 2022 and August 2026, China accounted for half of Russia’s crude exports, followed by India at 37%, Turkey at 5%, and the EU at 5%. According to the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), a Delhi-based think tank, Russia delivered $40.8 billion, or 30.3%, of India’s $134.7 billion total crude import bill in fiscal 2026. Over half of India’s imports in July came from Russian crude. title: A Backlash Against Data Centers is Another Challenge to the AI Juggernaut
author: editor
excerpt: There is an unnerving low hum coming from data centers, where tens of thousands of chips perform trillions of operations each second to help drive the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. These chips fuel the text, photos, and videos produced by advanced AI models’ queries. Their computations, which are essentially the turning on and off of minuscule silicon transistors that comprise a chip, are actually silent. However, as with all computers, practically every watt of the enormous electricity need to run this operation is lost as heat, and the sound you hear is the slow buzz of thousands of fans needed to keep the heat from frying the server racks. Depending on the facility’s size, you may hear the thrum of transformers in substations that channel energy. In the United States, opposition to data centers is particularly visible on the political left. Democratic Senator Bernie Sanders has advocated for a freeze on all new development. “People are looking around worried about how quickly the technology is moving, how little control they have over it, how will data centers impact their community in terms of electric rates and water utilisation,” he said to me. title: EU President Backs proposal for Canada to Become ‘Associate Partner’
author: editor
excerpt: The European Commission’s president has endorsed suggestions for Canada to become the EU’s first “associate member”. Ursula von der Leyen told the European Parliament on Wednesday that she intended to work on “opening the door” to Canada, which would entail closer relations in a variety of crucial industries. Last week, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke of forming a “unique alliance” with the EU. Trade talks between Canada and the United States ended last month, prompting a slew of new tariffs. Trump’s constant mention of becoming Canada the “51st state” has further fuelled tensions between the North American rivals. title: Trump Attacks the Supreme Court After Judges Overturn Limitations on Mail-in Ballots
author: editor
excerpt: In a blow to the White House, the US Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump’s proposal to limit mail-in voting prior to the midterm elections in November. The US Postal Service (USPS) was temporarily prevented from implementing new restrictions for postal ballots by a federal judge’s injunction, which the court upheld. Trump described the ruling as a setback for his political party. “Republicans just got another bad decision from the United States Supreme Court,” the president posted on Truth Social. In reaction, a legal organization stated that the ruling will stop the USPS from “sowing chaos in our elections.” It seems unlikely that the decision will be the last word on the subject. Conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh concurred with the decision but hinted that, if the case proceeds, he might eventually decide in Trump’s favour. In March, Trump signed an executive order directing the USPS to distribute votes only to voters on lists of citizens, claiming the regulations would prevent electoral fraud. The action was challenged in court on the grounds that it infringed upon states’ constitutional rights to hold elections. Election officials from the District of Columbia and 24 Democratic-led states cautioned that the suggested modifications were not yet ready to be put into effect and might make it more difficult for voters to cast ballots. According to Trump, the US possesses “virtually unlimited” supplies of munitions, and any information to the contrary is “fake news”. However, the independent watchdog claimed that “strategic inventory shortfalls” resulted from US spending over $22 billion on weapons between February and June. The shortages in the US have been described as serious in earlier estimations. In order to stop oncoming Iranian attacks, US forces have spent enormous amounts of money on air and missile defences as well as long-range ground attack systems throughout the conflict. According to a late July estimate from the Center for Strategic and International Studies, or CSIS, stockpiles of some interceptors, such the Patriot missile and Terminal High Altitude Area Defence, or THAAD, were severely reduced, sometimes by more than half. title: Denmark Claims That a Military Helicopter was Flamed by a Russian Cruiser
author: editor
excerpt: While tracking the Russian battleship in the Baltic Sea, Denmark has accused it of firing two emergency lights at one of its helicopters. The incident occurred during a “routine” surveillance operation on Monday, according to the Danish government, which has summoned the Russian ambassador. The Russian action was described as “reckless” and intended to “intimidate and divide” by Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen. Despite accusing Danish helicopters of making “dangerous manoeuvres” close to Russian vessels, Russia declared it will “thoroughly investigate” the incident. The latest security concern on the alliance’s eastern frontier, where tensions are still high due to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, occurred the same day that NATO soldiers shot down a drone over Lithuania. The Danish military released the following statement about the Baltic Sea incident: “One of the air force’s Fennec helicopters was today fired at with flares during a routine photographic operation of a Russian frigate, which was located in international waters off Gedser.” The statement further stated that one of the two flares shot at the chopper passed near it. The act was deemed “completely unacceptable” by the Danish foreign ministry. title: After Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey Withdrew, the London Musical was Scrapped
author: editor
excerpt: Due to the withdrawal of A-listers Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey, the planned London reprise of Sunday in the Park With George has been scrapped. Next year, the Wicked stars were scheduled to reconvene on stage in the Stephen Sondheim production at the Barbican. As part of her desire to step back from the spotlight following the conclusion of her Eternal Sunshine Tour, Grande announced last month that she was leaving the musical. Bailey also announced his withdrawal from the show earlier this month. The musical will no longer be performed in 2027, according to a Monday announcement from production company Empire Street Productions, which had previously stated it would proceed as scheduled. “The planned 2027 production of Sunday in the Park with George at the Barbican will no longer proceed as scheduled,” the company announced in a statement.In order to deliver the production in 2028, Empire Street Productions will hold onto the rights. In due course, further information will be revealed. The original musical was written by American composer Sondheim and playwright James Lapine, and it made its Broadway debut in 1984. The French painter Georges Seurat’s A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte, in which a fictionalised version of the artist is consumed by his work, served as the inspiration for Sunday in the Park with George. title: Shortly After Boris Johnson and High-Ranking European Officials Depart the Station, Russia Strikes a Ukrainian Train
author: editor
excerpt: Shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and senior European security officials had passed through, a Russian drone struck a train close to the Ukraine-Poland border. The strike at Yahodyn, which struck the train’s engine, resulted in no recorded injuries. According to Ukrainian authorities, every passenger had been evacuated. On their way back from a conference in Kyiv, Johnson and other European national security advisors, including Jonathan Powell of the UK, had travelled along the same route on a different train. Ukraine’s state railway firm Ukrzaliznytsia stated that the drone’s target “could have been the diplomatic train” in contrast to Russia’s defence ministry’s claim that it had attacked “railway infrastructure” in western Ukraine. The chair of the Warsaw Security Forum, Professor Katarzyna Pisarska, told the BBC that she was in the same carriage as Johnson and Powell and that the attack occurred roughly half an hour after their train entered Poland. The diplomatic train “had left the station earlier than expected because of the timetable change… due to constant threats of Russian strikes,” according to a statement from Ukrzaliznytsia, the railway authority of Ukraine. Additionally, it claimed that a Russian jet-propelled drone had issued an evacuation order for passengers aboard the struck train “just 15 minutes” prior to the attack. title: After a Deadly Crash, Amazon Stops Working with a Transportation Company
author: editor

Major companies like Amazon and DHL use 21 Air, an all-cargo airline. After taking off from San Juan, Puerto Rico’s Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport, the cargo airliner, a Boeing 767-300, crashed in Miami. The plane skidded to a stop after overshooting the runway and colliding with neighbouring cars. author: editor

The Riksdag election in Sweden is open to almost eight million voters. title: According to UAE Experts, AI Might Have the Correct Solution Yet Still Fail in Practical Scenarios
author: editor
excerpt: Daniil Orel noticed anything odd in the kids’ code while he was judging a national AI Olympiad in Kazakhstan. Some remarks appeared to be instructions or text produced by a huge language model rather than notes written by a contestant. After a while, he was unsure of whose work he was evaluating. “As a human judge, I realised at one point that I could no longer be absolutely certain whether I was evaluating a student’s own work or code generated with the assistance of a language model,” Orel remarked. This ambiguity turned into a research issue. It also highlights a more significant issue that AI researchers are increasingly facing: once people start depending on a system, it may deliver the correct response, write useful code, or score highly on a benchmark, but it may still fail in significant ways. Different approaches to the topic are being taken by three incoming PhD candidates at Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence in Abu Dhabi. Orel is researching the security and dependability of code produced by AI. Ali Aljaberi, an Emirati researcher, is investigating vulnerabilities brought about by AI-assisted software development. Amna Alhammadi, another Emirati, is transitioning from machine learning to human-computer interaction in order to investigate if technically sound AI systems are truly beneficial, intelligible, and suitable for the people they serve. title: Saudi Arabia Closes a Vital Oil Pipeline Following an Iraqi Drone Strike
author: editor
excerpt: As the Middle East crisis intensifies, Saudi Arabia has shut down a vital oil pipeline after drones fired from Iraq targeted it. After acknowledging that one of its provinces bordering Iran was the source of the drone attack on its neighbor’s East-West pipeline, Iraq announced it had sacked a military officer and opened an investigation. Saudi Arabia has already accused an Iraqi militia supported by Iran of attacking its oil infrastructure. The greatest exporter of crude oil in the world, Saudi Arabia, has been able to avoid the Strait of Hormuz thanks to the 1,200 km (745 mile) pipeline. As the US-Iran war enters its seventh month, the incident coincides with a significant advance by the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, increasing pressure on international oil transportation lanes. A day after the Houthis took over the whole Red Sea coast, Yemen’s government troops, supported by Saudi Arabia, reported on Friday that they had attacked Houthi fighters in the vital coastal city of Mokha. As satellite photos of the area showed smoke and charred ground, Riyadh announced on Friday that it had closed the pipeline as a precaution. According to the foreign ministry, the incident caused some damage and injuries, which were still being evaluated. According to news agency Reuters, which cited ship tracking firms and analysts, the Saudi pipeline has been transporting 4% to 5% of the world’s oil supply. title: As Modi Welcomes Putin and Xi in Delhi, the Trump Shadow Hovers Huge over Brics
author: editor
excerpt: There will be discussions on a variety of topics with leaders from 11 Brics countries, including host India, China, Russia, Brazil, South Africa, the United Arab Emirates, and Iran. Saudi Arabia has been invited. Few, however, will have as much of an influence as President Trump’s initiatives. Global energy markets have become unstable due to the conflict in Iran and the constant threat of White House tariffs, which are aimed at both US allies and enemies. This has frequently left the world economy uncertain about the future. The leaders of Brics are gathering against this backdrop. However, it is unlikely that the group would come up with a consensus statement that publicly criticises the US or outlines a coordinated plan to oppose the geopolitics and policies of President Trump. This is partially due to the intense disagreement within Brics on the extent to which it should confront Washington.Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, told the BBC that “India cannot afford to have a joint statement that rails against Washington.” He anticipates that any criticism of US policy will be “vague and indirect” in order to represent the stark differences in the interests of the larger group. The geopolitical circumstances within the Brics are likely to make it challenging for the organization to take a more assertive stance against President Trump, despite pressure from Russia and Iran. India, which is supposedly nearing the end of a trade agreement with the United States, won’t want to make a remark that would anger the White House. China might also be concerned about being perceived as targeting Washington through Brics. title: Some Republicans Discreetly Wonder who will Follow Trump as he Dominates the Convention
author: editor
excerpt: In an attempt to improve their chances of winning the midterm, Republicans flocked to Dallas this week in the hopes that President Donald Trump’s unusual convention would invigorate supporters in advance of the November election. Many departed the event, which supporters had advertized in advance as a “Trump-a-palooza” political celebration, equally concerned about the party’s prospects in 2026 and uncertain about the Republicans’ post-presidential future. During his keynote speech on Thursday nite, Vice-President JD Vance, who is considered a strong candidate to succeed Trump, gave his party a preview of its possible future.Vance addressed the gathering, saying, “We have to take care of business this November.”After that, we’ll worry about what happens next.” Chants of “48”—a reference to Trump’s successor, who would become the 48th US president if they win in 2028—interrupted his address at one point. Vance waved the chant away after letting it linger for a moment. Party activists disagreed during the course of the two-day event on the appropriateness of hosting a midterm convention with a president whose support ratings are at an all-time low, as well as the public’s dissatisfaction with the war with Iran and the economy. title: Diesel Prices Surpass $6 per Gallon but US Inflation Remains Stable
author: editor
excerpt: According to official data, prices in the US increased by 3.4% in the year ending in August due to rising petrol prices driving up living expenses. The Bureau of Labour Statistics (BLS) reports that total inflation remained steady from July. It comes ahead of the Federal Reserve’s most recent interest rate decision, which is expected to be raised next week in an effort to curb the rate of price increases. A gallon of diesel set a new all-time high of more than $6 on average on Friday, underscoring the increasing pressure on US household budgets, particularly at the petrol pump. Due to supply delays brought on by the US-Iran war, the price of petroleum has increased globally. Due to recent escalations in the conflict, the benchmark Brent crude oil price is currently above $100 per barrel. Higher oil prices can increase the cost of transportation in addition to immediately raising costs at the pump. The cost of living may increase as a result of these expenses being passed on to consumers in the form of higher prices for food and other necessities. According to the BLS, petrol prices increased by 3.9% just last month, making up more than one-third of total inflation. Additionally, wages are not keeping up with the growing cost of living; according to separate data, actual average hourly earnings decreased by 0.3% during the previous year. Given the present inflation picture, the robust job market, and President Donald Trump’s statement that he does not believe oil prices would decline until the war with Iran finishes, which he anticipates happening after November’s elections, there are growing expectations that interest rates will be raised. title: The First Foldable iPhone, Priced at £1,999, is a Major Risk for Apple’s new CEO
author: editor
excerpt: The first significant iPhone design shift in nearly 20 years has occurred with the release of Apple’s most costly iPhone to ever, a foldable handheld that costs at least £1,999. John Ternus, who succeeded long-time CEO Tim Cook this month, is taking a risk with the iPhone Duo. Apple is somewhat late to the foldable phone market, trailing behind companies like China’s Huawei and South Korea’s Samsung. “Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together,” Ternus said to a crowd at Apple’s California headquarters. He asserted that Apple’s device “redefine[s] the experience of using a foldable phone.” Prices in the US range from $1,999 to $3,200. After serving for many years as a senior executive in Apple’s hardware group, Ternus was actively involved in its development, which took eight years. It resembles a smaller iPad when unfurled and a larger iPhone when folded. “It’s completely new and yet remarkably familiar,” Ternus remarked. It is about the same size as your passport and is easy to operate with one hand. However, the product is up against well-established rivals. title: A Cargo Ship Fire in Eastern China Claimed 25 Death
author: editor
excerpt: Chinese state television CCTV reports that a fire on a foreign-flagged cargo ship parked at a port in eastern China has killed twenty-five persons. According to CCTV, 17 of the 42 passengers were evacuated, and five of them are in stable condition at the hospital. At approximately 11:15 local time (03:15 GMT), the fire broke out as the ship was being maintained at a shipyard in the city of Qingdao. CCTV shows that it was removed a little more than three hours later. According to tracking site MarineTraffic, photos issued by official media identified the ship as the Ocean Melody, a Liberian-flagged carrier measuring 190 meters (623 feet) in length that arrived in Qingdao on August 31. Qingdao is one of the busiest ports in the world and a significant trading hub. What started the fire is unknown. Thick smoke was billowing from the ship, but he did not hear an explosion, an eyewitness told the AFP news agency. Premier Li Qiang emphasised the need to “prevent secondary disasters” while the nation’s leader, Xi Jinping, earlier called for “all-out” search and rescue operations. title: Compensation And Air Traffic Chaos: Shutdown Cost us More than £1,000
author: editor
excerpt: It should have been Catie and Phil Allen’s first vacation in two and a half years. Rather, they are at home begging for unpaid refunds. The four-hour closure of the UK’s air traffic control system on Tuesday confused thousands of travellers, including the couple. This suggests their trip to Slovenia has been cancelled, and although British Airways reimbursed them for their travel, they expect to pay £1,300 out of pocket for unused lodging and activities. After issues at UK airports, it’s not the first time and it won’t be the last—that travellers are left on a wing and a prayer. Here’s how their situation connects to others and the reasons behind their severe setback. aboard Tuesday, Catie, 30, and Phil, 34, were seated aboard a British Airways flight to Ljubljana that never got off. Airlines are required to send passengers to their destination as soon as feasible at no additional expense in the event of a flight cancellation, even if it is with a competitor airline. Alternatively, travellers can request a refund, which should be provided for flights delayed by more than five hours.
