title: After Duplicates Were Discovered in the Database, Spain Reduced the Estimate of Minors in Ceuta
author: editor
excerpt: After finding duplicate entries in their databases, Spanish police scaled down the number of minors registered in Ceuta following the large-scale arrival of Moroccan migrants last month. The Interior Ministry claims that several processes involving the same child were documented as distinct cases, increasing the total number. Since the large-scale Moroccan immigration on July 30 and up to 9:00 that morning, police reported on August 18 that they had found, recognized, and placed 2,168 kids in the care of the Ceuta authorities. After the records were examined, the number is currently approximately 1,500. Minors under Ceuta’s child protection services prior to July 30th are also included in the total. The number may increase after ongoing identification processes are finished, according to the Interior Ministry. For the time being, the kids stay in Ceuta while officials explore other options, such as moving them to other parts of Spain because the city lacks the capacity to receive them or, in certain situations, sending them back to their home countries. Children and teenagers from nations like Sudan and Chad, which are both impacted by humanitarian crises and conflict, are among them. Some may be eligible for international protection, according to Save the Children. The group has also drawn attention to the unique vulnerability of women and girls, who may be at risk for things like forced marriage, sexual assault, and human trafficking. title: Why a Significant Automobile Recall in China has Affected Tesla
author: editor
excerpt: Over the past week, hidden car door handles and the streamlined styles frequently seen on electric cars (EVs) have gained attention. That came after China declared the largest automobile recall in its history, affecting over four million vehicles, the majority of which were Teslas. The recall coincides with new rules in China mandating that automobiles have a mechanical release on both the inside and outside of their doors. This kind of nickname is now widely used worldwide thanks to Elon Musk’s massive electric vehicle company. However, several cases have raised concerns that this design could make doors difficult to open in an emergency. Approximately 60% of the top 100 best-selling new energy vehicles in China, including EVs and hybrids, have hidden door handles. “Even I often find it difficult to locate the switch to open the door from the inside of an unfamiliar vehicle,” Shanghai-based car industry analyst Stephen Dyer of consultancy AlixPartners told the BBC, adding that although the minimalist design gives cars a “sleek look and reduces wind drag,” it can be confusing to use. Beyond their practicality, however, the handles have been accused of putting drivers’ and passengers’ lives in jeopardy. According to Lyu Chen, an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University, electronically driven door handles grew popular in the business but caused “real safety concerns” when doors failed to open quickly, delaying rescue efforts following accidents. A door handle may appear straightforward, but in the moments following a collision, it becomes crucial for safety, according to Chen. After two tragic collisions involving its SU7 vehicle in 2025, in which suspected electrical failures allegedly locked occupants inside, Chinese automaker Xiaomi came under heavy criticism. title: Qatar Calls on Tehran to Reopen Hormuz and Says Officials are Working Every Day to Renew US-Iran Negotiations
author: editor
excerpt: According to a spokesperson for Qatar’s Foreign Ministry on Tuesday, the two countries are still working to relaunch talks between the US and Iran, with officials meeting with the parties every day to discuss potential paths forward. Majed Al-Ansari told reporters in Doha, “Our officials are on the phone on a daily basis trying to workshop ideas, workshop ways of getting back to the negotiations.” Al-Ansari stated that Qatar remained committed to finding a diplomatic solution to the ongoing conflict between the two sides, but he did not elaborate on the options under discussion. “Reaching a diplomatic solution through talks was always our priority,” he stated. “We are urging the parties to participate fully in the negotiations and mediation, which are being led by Pakistan, Qatar, and other regional players.” He went on to call talks “the only way out of this crisis” and exhorted both parties to act honourably. Since the battle began in late February, Qatar and Pakistan have served as the two principal intermediaries between the United States and Iran. Al-Ansari’s remarks followed a visit to Tehran by Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, who met with top Iranian officials in an attempt to ease tensions in the region and restart discussions. title: As the Ceuta Situation Persists, Spain Will Update its Asylum Laws to Conform to EU Regulations
author: editor
excerpt: As it tries to manage the political consequences from the Ceuta crisis, which saw 80,000 people enter the Spanish city illegally from Morocco in a single day in July, the Spanish government is set to introduce a draft bill to amend immigration and asylum regulations. In response to demands from hardline nations, Madrid stated that the goal is to “bring Spanish legislation into line with the European Pact on Migration and Asylum,” which went into effect this summer and makes it simpler to deny asylum requests and expedite expulsions. At first, Spain had rejected a significant portion of the legislation, claiming that a more all-encompassing and compassionate approach to migration would be more advantageous. Although Spanish sources maintain that the new system will guaranty fundamental rights, in reality, aligning with the EU will result in tougher penalties. The time coincides with the ongoing Ceuta migrant crisis, which draws attention to Madrid’s management of irregular migration and its efforts to regularize up to 500,000 migrants who are living and working in Spain without proper documentation. Approximately 5,000 people, including an estimated 2,000 minors, are still in the Spanish enclave, but the great majority of the 80,000 individuals who crossed the border illegally have returned to Morocco. Unaccompanied kids are a particularly delicate issue as Madrid tries to strike a compromise between stringent legal standards and its obligations to Brussels and Ceuta’s regional authorities to deport anyone who entered unlawfully. author: editor
excerpt: More than two years after he allegedly stole a denim jacket from a store at the airport shopping centre, Singapore has charged a British man with theft. When a retail clerk at Singapore’s Changi Airport saw a blue denim jacket stolen from a display mannequin on the evening of August 14, 2024, the police were notified of the theft. On camera, a guy was seen taking the jacket, which was estimated to be worth S$350 ($275; £202), off the mannequin and walking out of the store without paying. The individual had left Singapore by the time the authorities were able to identify him. The 26-year-old was accused on Tuesday after being detained at the airport on August 15 while travelling. “The police take a serious stance of shop theft and will deal firmly with offenders in accordance with the law.”The Singapore Police Force stated in a statement on Monday that criminals shouldn’t think they can avoid detection by just departing Singapore after committing a crime. A 50-year-old Polish lady who had stolen two bottles of perfume from retail establishments inside one of the airport’s terminals on June 11 of this year was also arrested, according to the police statement. title: China Criticizes the “illegal” New US Sanctions Against Iran and its Trading Partners
author: editor
excerpt: Following the US announcement that it would expand economic sanctions against Iran and its trading partners, including Beijing, China has pledged to defend its interests. China is adamantly against what it refers to as “illegal unilateral sanctions” and will take “all necessary measures” to protect its rights, according to Lin Jian, a spokeswoman for the foreign ministry. This followed the announcement of the new restrictions by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday, who threatened to isolate any country that partnered financially with Iran. Despite a decrease in trade due to the US blockade of Iran’s ports, China remains the largest customer of Iranian oil. Lin stated: “Cooperation between China and Iran has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be interfered with or disrupted.” Bessent called the proposed sanctions “the single greatest financial offensive ever” against Iran and warned companies and banks that if they didn’t sever relations with Iran, they would also be subject to isolation. He stated that US President Donald Trump will be calling international leaders “with specific requests to cease their interactions with the regime” but declined to mention any particular countries. But Bessent clarified that “no one was above the reach of US sanctions” in response to a query concerning Chinese institutions. title: As the Coalition of the Willing Convenes in Kyiv, The UK will Provide Ukraine With SCALP Missile Plans
author: editor
excerpt: Following Britain’s agreement to supply information on UK-made components of the Franco-British weapon, Ukraine has taken a step closer to manufacturing SCALP cruise missiles domestically. After months of talks between Kyiv and Paris on local manufacture and licensing, the decision makes it possible for the missiles to be assembled in Ukraine. The action should improve Ukraine’s defensive capabilities, according to Luke Pollard, the UK’s Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry.The missiles have already been employed by Ukraine against Russian military targets and infrastructure, including defence industrial sites and command posts both inside Russia and on occupied Ukrainian territory. In 2023, the UK was the first nation to supply Ukraine with long-range cruise missiles. Three years later, the technology transfer represents a another change in Western assistance, as countries shift from providing completed weapons to assisting Ukraine in producing its own advanced systems. title: In an Effort to Isolate Iran, The US Treasury Secretary Initiates “Operation Economic Outcast
author: editor
excerpt: In an effort to cut off Tehran’s financial lifelines during the ongoing conflict, Washington is initiating what it has dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast” against Iran.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described a new, “unprecedented campaign” against Iran and its “enablers” in a press conference on Monday. He called it an “economic onslaught” with the goal of isolating the Iranian regime.”Every node, facilitator, and network that Iran has used to smuggle oil and avoid sanctions has been mapped by Treasury,” he stated. “Beginning today, the actions of Treasury and other agencies will tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue that funds the IRGC and the evil Iranian regime. He went on, “Any organisation that aids in money laundering on behalf of Iran will be eliminated from the US dollar system.” He also mentioned that US President Donald Trump was reaching out to certain international leaders to ask them to cease their cooperation with Iran. The Treasury Department declared on Monday that it had “issued determinations against five critical sectors digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping that the Iranian regime uses to try to prop up its failing economy.” Bessent stated that Iran now has “a very clear choice” going forward. Total worldwide seclusion and a survival economy, or a return to normalcy with a chance to reintegrate into the world economy. title: The UK’s Missile Offer Might Benefit Ukraine, but Zelensky Doesn’t Really Need Them
author: editor
excerpt: Following a similar action by France, the UK will give Ukraine the blueprints for its British-French designed Storm Shadow cruise missiles, enabling Ukraine to manufacture the weapon at home. The action sends a crucial message that some Western countries are prepared to share their knowledge and know how to support Ukraine’s self-defense. However, this won’t significantly change how the battle plays out on its own. Both France and Britain have already sent Kyiv Storm Shadow and Scalp missiles. They have previously been deployed to attack Russian military objectives. The weapons are pricey, costing about £1 million each, and they are not brand-new, having been created in the 1990s. They were constructed in peacetime at comparatively low rates—in the hundreds, not the thousands—and depend on intricate international supply lines. Ukraine might have trouble sourcing parts even with the blueprints. Making the cruise missile themselves could take months or even years. It is actually impossible to win a war by imitating Western weapons manufacturing in times of peace. Even NATO countries are now aware of this. Britain and many of its allies have a tendency to produce expensive, highly sophisticated missiles in small quantities, which would quickly run out in any protracted confrontation. In a 2021 NATO scenario, the UK military ran out of essential weapons in a matter of days, according to Gen. Ben Hodges, the former commander of the US Army in Europe. The UK military is no longer purchasing Storm Shadow missiles for itself, which is evidence of the recent shift in perspective. title: El Niño Will Reduce the Number of Ships Using the Panama Canal
author: editor
excerpt: Due to El Niño’s low rainfall, the operator of the Panama Canal will reduce the amount of ships using the vital route. The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) informed shipping companies on Thursday that starting September 15, 32 vessels per day will be able to sail through it, down from the current 36. Global weather systems are impacted by El Niño, a trend of recurrent sea surface warming. This year is predicted to be especially powerful, with climate change intensifying its effects. The war in Iran has significantly reduced the number of ships travelling through the vital Strait of Hormuz, already causing major disruptions to the maritime industry. According to the ACP, the actions were taken to protect water supplies for human use and maintain service dependability. It further stated that further action was required “to support the long-term sustainability of transit operations” even though the rainy season had already begun in Central America and some water-saving measures had already been implemented in the canal. The new policies will be implemented gradually starting on September 3. The Panama Canal significantly shortens the time and distance ships must travel between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. title: US Borrowing Prices Increase as Attempts to Lower Rates Don’t Last
author: editor
excerpt: Despite the government’s declaration that it will step in to try to reduce long-term borrowing costs, they increased once more in the United States. The Treasury Department announced earlier this week that it will repurchase additional debt in an effort to reduce interest rates set by investors on international bond markets, which are the primary source of funding for governments and large enterprises. After the intervention, rates, or yields as they are known, decreased over the course of 30 years, but they have now increased once more. The US government’s unexpected action, according to economists, was short-lived because worries remain about borrowing levels as the country’s debt surpasses $40 trillion. The interest rate on 30-year bonds increased to about 5.27% on Friday. To raise funds for expenditures, governments and businesses sell bonds, which are basically IOUs, in exchange for interest. Yields are bond interest rates. If inflation is strong or is predicted to rise in the future, bond investors usually want larger returns, or yields. The Treasury Department’s announcement of its “support” caused yields to plummet earlier this week, from an almost two-decade high of 5.34% to 5.18%. title: Tiananmen Protestors in Hong Kong Were Found Guilty in a National Security Trial
author: editor
excerpt: According to the city’s contentious national security ordinance, two Hong Kong activists who planned yearly vigils to remember the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown were found guilty of encouraging others to overthrow state power. After being found guilty under the China-introduced law, Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, might get a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. A later date is anticipated for sentencing. Albert Ho, a 74-year-old defendant, entered a guilty plea in January. A statement released on Friday stated that Lee and Chow “incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power.” In May, Chow informed the court that the law was being tried. One of the few locations in China where people could congregate to commemorate the tragic crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators in 1989 was Hong Kong. Citing Covid-19 regulations, authorities outlawed these events in 2020, but they have never been held again. This year also marked the official implementation of the national security statute, which outlaws a wider variety of actions of dissent. Even indirect allusions to the 1989 crackdown are prohibited in mainland China. title: After Doubling in Ten Years, the US National Debt now Stands at $40 Trillion
author: editor
excerpt: According to Treasury statistics, the US national debt has more than doubled in ten years to reach a historic $40 trillion (£29.4 trillion). The increase is a result of years of excessive expenditure under both the Biden and Trump administrations, as well as increased interest payments that have gradually increased the amount. The national debt was slightly less than $20 trillion in 2016. By the conclusion of fiscal year 2026, the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) predicted that total borrowing would amount to $39.6 trillion. Concerns about how quickly the government’s borrowing needs are expanding and what that means for future interest costs have intensified due to the faster-than-expected growth. According to the CBO, the US is very close to its $41.1 trillion debt maximum, and by 2036, debt is expected to reach over $64 trillion. Consumers have had to deal with rising interest rates and inflation as the federal government spends more to pay for its budget shortfalls. As of August 18, the $40.05 trillion represents all outstanding Treasury bonds, bills, and notes and highlights the extent of US borrowing under two administrations. Under international criticism, Israel delayed plans to construct in E1 for decades. Many of Israeli friends and Palestinians felt that this would be a severe setback to hopes for a two-state solution, effectively dividing the West Bank. title: AI to Assist Aircraft in Avoiding “Sky Graffiti That Contributes to Climate Change
author: editor
excerpt: Everybody has seen the white lines that follow airplanes in the sky as they looked up. Scientists have been attempting to figure out how to prevent contrails, which are icy clouds that contribute to climate change. In order to determine whether AI can be helpful, a £5 million UK project will anticipate where warming contrails are likely to occur and direct aircraft to avoid certain locations. The Shanwick Oceanic airspace in the eastern half of the North Atlantic corridor, which is responsible for about 5% of global contrail warming, will be the main emphasis. Google, the UK government, the Met Office, National Air Traffic Services (NATS), an air traffic control company, and researchers from Imperial College London and the University of Cambridge collaborate on the 30-month Operation Blue Skies initiative. Contrails, sometimes referred to as vapour trails, are formed when cold air at high altitudes combines with hot aircraft engine exhaust to form ice crystals. Many of them vanish quickly, but in extremely cold and humid weather, they can linger and spread, creating clouds that trap heat that would otherwise escape the Earth. Google’s technical head for the project, Dr. Paul Hodgson, told the BBC’s Tech Life show that his five-year-old calls the white lines “sky graffiti” in a more colourful way. title: Global Borrowing Costs Reached New Highs on oil, AI, And Hyperinflation
author: editor
excerpt: Long-term borrowing prices in some of the world’s largest economies have reached new highs due to fears about inflation, government debt levels, and spending on artificial intelligence (AI). On Tuesday, the interest rate on US borrowing over 30 years rose to 5.33%, the most since June 2007, while UK long-term debt reached 5.85%. Similar moves occurred in Germany and Japan. Bond interest rates, a sort of debt, are known as yields, and they can have a direct impact on the borrowing prices that customers pay for mortgages, car loans, and credit cards. Rising oil prices are the primary driver of the recent increase in bond yields, as investors fear inflation will jump again. If this occurs, central banks may decide to hike interest rates to control inflation. A barrel of Brent crude, the global standard for oil prices, reached $90 on Tuesday as concerns over the Middle East war rose. The recent rise followed President Donald Trump’s threat to strike Oman, a US ally, if it “gets in the way” of discussions with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Police advised the public to “conduct investigations and establish the facts of the case” and “not to speculate on the incident or its circumstances”. According to the Israeli military, “to protect the residents” was the goal. According to international law, all settlements are prohibited. Two of the three homes in Qusra occupied by the besieged families—the Hassan and Abu Ridi families—were ordered to evacuate on Thursday, they told the BBC. Those who were ordered to leave, they claimed, have subsequently relocated to the third residence. title: Incheon Airport in South Korea is Now the Busiest Airport in the World for International Travel
author: editor
excerpt: According to new data, Incheon, South Korea, is now the busiest airport in the world for international passenger traffic for the first time. According to preliminary figures from the Airports Council International, Incheon International Airport, the primary entry point to South Korea, handled 38.4 million foreign travellers during the first half of this year. With 37.79 million passengers, London Heathrow Airport came in second, followed by Changi Airport in Singapore with 34.53 million. Due in part to the dispute between the United States and Iran, passengers from Middle Eastern aviation hubs were diverted to Incheon’s airport. Based on full-year statistics, Dubai International Airport was ranked second in both 2024 and 2025; this time, it is predicted to be outside of the top five. Incheon was placed 12th and 13th, respectively, while London’s Heathrow airport was ranked fifth in 2024 and seventh in 2025. title: The Nobel Peace Prize Winner Tells the BBC That Putin can no Longer Claim Triumph in Ukraine
author: editor
excerpt: The hallways inside Novaya Gazeta’s Moscow offices are quiet. The feeling of emptiness is unbearable. Over thirty years ago, Muratov, sixty-four, co-founded Novaya Gazeta. That is three times greater than it was in the USSR during the brutal KGB era. title: Spotify Will Remove AI-Generated Artists From Recommendations and Add a Label for Them
author: editor
excerpt: A new feature from Spotify will indicate whether an artist was produced by artificial intelligence (AI). According to the streaming service, listeners will be alerted whether a “artist’s identity may be AI-generated and does not represent a real person” by the AI Persona emblem, which will display on some profiles starting in mid-September. According to Spotify, the modifications are being made to provide users with “more transparency” over what they’re hearing. It happened after some music lovers made it “clear” to the streamer that they dislike seeing profiles that appear to be created by AI. Artists and audiences have long been concerned about music produced by artificial intelligence. According to musician Alex Winn, the upcoming feature is a “really good thing” (BBC Newsbeat).Guitarist Winn of the North East band Swindled adds, “It almost separates the people who have created music properly from the people just using AI.” The musician believes that “AI can’t really do that” and that people want to “connect emotionally with music.” Additionally, the 19-year-old claims that having the AI label will enable individuals to make educated decisions about their listening preferences. He also thinks that it will help level the playing field by directing consumers to other artists.No matter what, musicians are struggling to compete, especially with certain AI bands taking over,” he claims. Leon Keenan, a music enthusiast, believes that explicitly marking AI music is a “really good” idea, but he disagrees that it should be entirely removed off Spotify.The 20-year-old continues, “I really dislike AI music; it’s awful. Music is about passion.” Also Read: Todd Blanche, Trump’s Former Attorney, was just Barely Approved as US Attorney General Watchdog Discovers That Doge Exaggerated Claims to have Saved Americans $110 Billion

title: 36 Hours After the Colombian Earthquake, a Woman was Rescued From the Rubble
author: editor
excerpt: After the 7.4-magnitude earthquake that rocked western Colombia, a 32-year-old lady was retrieved alive after being buried in debris for 36 hours. After a ten-hour rescue effort, Daniela Largo was extracted from under a collapsed building in the city of Pereira. She had been buried beneath four concrete slabs, but firefighters eventually found her by digging a tunnel beneath them. Official statistics show that the earthquake has killed at least 188 people, while hundreds more are still unaccounted for. According to data from the Association of Colombian Capital Cities (Asocapitales), Pereira, a city in the coffee-growing area of Colombia, has 79 confirmed deaths, the second-highest number behind Cali, which has 95. Largo’s mother told the AFP news agency that someone in the area had heard her daughter scream for assistance from under the debris. With the use of a tiny camera, emergency personnel were able to find Largo once they got to the scene. However, four large concrete slabs were obstructing the path, making her rescue more difficult. title: Trump’s Dramatic Plane Exchange Raises Personal Concerns About the Iran War
author: editor
excerpt: “He got me before I got him. They made two attempts. I got him first, tho. In a phone call with ABC correspondent Jonathan Karl the day after he began the US military assault against Iran in February, President Donald Trump made this statement. The Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and several senior Iranian leaders had just been killed in an Israeli airstrike that was approved and coordinated by the United States. Trump directly linked the attack to threats and purported plots the Iranians had made against him in the past. In the six months of conflict that have followed, Trump has refrained from making similar statements, although Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has expressed a similar opinion.He stated in March that an unidentified Iranian who he claimed oversaw an assassination unit had been killed in US strikes. “Iran attempted to kill President Trump, and President Trump got the last laugh,” he said. These remarks allude to the intimate nature of this conflict and the president’s and his security team’s worries about the threat Iran continues to represent to his safety. title: The Founder’s Path: How Nils Ehle Turned Corporate Frustration Into a Human-First AI Practice
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Some founders start a company because they spot a gap in the market. Nils Ehle started his because he got tired of watching good technology get wasted inside organizations that weren’t ready for it. Today, as Founder & CEO of Change Orange, Nils Ehle runs one of the more distinctive AI transformation practices in Europe, one built less on software and more on people, patience, and a refusal to treat AI as a shortcut. From Corporate Ladder to Founder’s Path Nils Ehle didn’t set out to be an entrepreneur in the traditional sense. His early career ran through Accenture and then E.ON, the energy giant, where he cut his teeth in IT transformation before moving closer to the operational side of the business. “The core problem back then was that technology was treated as an IT domain,” Nils Ehle recalls. “It rarely delivered what the business actually needed.” That frustration became fuel. In 2012, Nils Ehle was handed the freedom to build an international transformation unit spanning 12 country markets, reporting straight to the board. From there, he helped stitch together a cross-company innovation hub in Germany’s Ruhr Valley, pulling roughly 80 organizations into one ecosystem, corporates, startups, universities, public bodies, and even direct competitors of his own employer. The goal was simple: match the right solutions to the right problems and help companies adapt their culture along the way. By 2015, that instinct to build something of his own had grown too strong to ignore. Nils Ehle founded Change Orange as a side project focused on customer-centric redesign. It has since become his full-time calling, now dedicated entirely to helping organizations turn AI hype into measurable business value, without losing the human plot along the way. What Nils Ehle actually delivers stretches well past a diagnosis. His engagements typically start with AI strategy development, but run through full end-to-end AI business transformation, business model and operating model redesign, workforce capability building, and the change management work needed to make any of it hold. “Assessing where a company stands is only the starting point,” Nils Ehle says. “The real work is walking through the whole journey with a founder, from strategy to the operating model to the people doing the work every day.” Why Founders Should Stay Uncomfortable Ask Nils Ehle how he decides which opportunities to pursue, and he won’t talk about market sizing or funding rounds. “You have to refuse to get stuck on the skills and projects you’ve already done,” he says. “AI is the current layer to embrace, and it’s fundamentally a business skill, not a technology topic.” For Nils Ehle, the engagements worth taking are the ones with a genuine spark in them, a client who wants to build something real rather than simply cut costs. “If you want to stay relevant, you cannot stay in your comfort zone, not as a founder, not as a company,” he says. “Comfort is where reinvention quietly dies.” Building Core Strength Instead of Chasing Use Cases Many entrepreneurs building in the AI space fall into the same trap: leading with flashy use cases instead of foundational capability. Nils Ehle sees this constantly in the clients who come to him after a failed pilot. “AI business transformation is not a use-case sport. It’s a capability-building exercise,” he says. That thinking shaped Change Orange’s six-dimensional AI Business Maturity Model, covering data, technology infrastructure, organization and process design, team skills, strategic alignment, and leadership culture. Only two of those six dimensions are actually about AI. “It’s like someone who only trains their biceps at the gym,” Nils Ehle explains. “Impressive to look at, useless the moment something unexpected happens. You need a strong back, strong legs, a strong core.” A Founder’s Take on Leadership Running a growing practice has sharpened Nils Ehle’s views on what leadership actually requires in an AI-saturated world. He points to an image he returns to often: the elephant, whose heart weighs roughly five times more than its brain, compared to humans, where the ratio is reversed. “Most modern leadership is built on that imbalance, heavy on analysis, light on heart,” he says. “The founders and leaders I see succeeding are the ones who deliberately shift toward heart-based leadership.” He’s equally direct about vulnerability at the top. “You do not have to have all the answers,” Nils Ehle says. “The leaders I see thriving are willing to stand in front of their teams and say, I don’t know yet, let’s figure this out together.” The Product Behind the Practice Alongside consulting, Nils Ehle has been building AI Use Case Engine with network partners, a real-time system that breaks a company down into its core business capabilities, then proposes and prioritizes AI and automation use cases benchmarked against real-world examples. “We deliberately run it alongside human experience and intuition that AI alone can’t provide,” he says, describing it as pairing narrow artificial intelligence with what he calls general human intuitive intelligence. Listen to what your heart is telling you,” he says. “But feeling right has to come from a place of service, not ego. When you act from ego, you optimize for status. content:
Some founders start a company because they spot a gap in the market. Nils Ehle started his because he got tired of watching good technology get wasted inside organizations that weren’t ready for it. Today, as Founder & CEO of Change Orange, Nils Ehle runs one of the more distinctive AI transformation practices in Europe, one built less on software and more on people, patience, and a refusal to treat AI as a shortcut.

From Corporate Ladder to Founder’s Path

Nils Ehle didn’t set out to be an entrepreneur in the traditional sense. His early career ran through Accenture and then E.ON, the energy giant, where he cut his teeth in IT transformation before moving closer to the operational side of the business. “The core problem back then was that technology was treated as an IT domain,” Nils Ehle recalls. “It rarely delivered what the business actually needed.”

That frustration became fuel. In 2012, Nils Ehle was handed the freedom to build an international transformation unit spanning 12 country markets, reporting straight to the board. From there, he helped stitch together a cross-company innovation hub in Germany’s Ruhr Valley, pulling roughly 80 organizations into one ecosystem, corporates, startups, universities, public bodies, and even direct competitors of his own employer. The goal was simple: match the right solutions to the right problems and help companies adapt their culture along the way.

By 2015, that instinct to build something of his own had grown too strong to ignore. Nils Ehle founded Change Orange as a side project focused on customer-centric redesign. It has since become his full-time calling, now dedicated entirely to helping organizations turn AI hype into measurable business value, without losing the human plot along the way.

What Nils Ehle actually delivers stretches well past a diagnosis. His engagements typically start with AI strategy development, but run through full end-to-end AI business transformation, business model and operating model redesign, workforce capability building, and the change management work needed to make any of it hold. “Assessing where a company stands is only the starting point,” Nils Ehle says. “The real work is walking through the whole journey with a founder, from strategy to the operating model to the people doing the work every day.”

Why Founders Should Stay Uncomfortable

Ask Nils Ehle how he decides which opportunities to pursue, and he won’t talk about market sizing or funding rounds. “You have to refuse to get stuck on the skills and projects you’ve already done,” he says. “AI is the current layer to embrace, and it’s fundamentally a business skill, not a technology topic.”

For Nils Ehle, the engagements worth taking are the ones with a genuine spark in them, a client who wants to build something real rather than simply cut costs. “If you want to stay relevant, you cannot stay in your comfort zone, not as a founder, not as a company,” he says. “Comfort is where reinvention quietly dies.”

Building Core Strength Instead of Chasing Use Cases

Many entrepreneurs building in the AI space fall into the same trap: leading with flashy use cases instead of foundational capability. Nils Ehle sees this constantly in the clients who come to him after a failed pilot. “AI business transformation is not a use-case sport. It’s a capability-building exercise,” he says.

That thinking shaped Change Orange’s six-dimensional AI Business Maturity Model, covering data, technology infrastructure, organization and process design, team skills, strategic alignment, and leadership culture. Only two of those six dimensions are actually about AI. “It’s like someone who only trains their biceps at the gym,” Nils Ehle explains. “Impressive to look at, useless the moment something unexpected happens. You need a strong back, strong legs, a strong core.”

A Founder’s Take on Leadership

Running a growing practice has sharpened Nils Ehle’s views on what leadership actually requires in an AI-saturated world. He points to an image he returns to often: the elephant, whose heart weighs roughly five times more than its brain, compared to humans, where the ratio is reversed. “Most modern leadership is built on that imbalance, heavy on analysis, light on heart,” he says. “The founders and leaders I see succeeding are the ones who deliberately shift toward heart-based leadership.”

He’s equally direct about vulnerability at the top. “You do not have to have all the answers,” Nils Ehle says. “The leaders I see thriving are willing to stand in front of their teams and say, I don’t know yet, let’s figure this out together.”

The Product Behind the Practice

Alongside consulting, Nils Ehle has been building AI Use Case Engine with network partners, a real-time system that breaks a company down into its core business capabilities, then proposes and prioritizes AI and automation use cases benchmarked against real-world examples. “We deliberately run it alongside human experience and intuition that AI alone can’t provide,” he says, describing it as pairing narrow artificial intelligence with what he calls general human intuitive intelligence.

Advice for Founders Building Anything Right Now

Asked what advice shaped his own founder’s path, Nils Ehle doesn’t reach for a productivity hack. “Don’t follow a career path, follow your path. Listen to what your heart is telling you,” he says. “But feeling right has to come from a place of service, not ego. When you act from ego, you optimize for status. When you act from service, you optimize for impact.”

He adds a shorter list underneath that: be yourself, be honest, have fun at work, and don’t try to solve problems alone. “And be fearless,” he says. “Being fearless doesn’t mean never feeling fear. It means refusing to let fear be the deciding factor.”

Staying Grounded While Building

For all the talk of AI and business models, Nils Ehle is unusually candid about what keeps him functional as a founder: going analog. He plays the handpan, runs, does physical work, and spends time in nature with his family. “Those moments aren’t breaks from work, they’re part of how the work happens,” he says. “New ideas rarely arrive when you’re staring at the problem. They arrive when you’ve stepped away.”

He describes his approach to balance less as a goal and more as a practice of letting go. “When you operate from a controlling stance, you live from ego, and you spend enormous energy fighting reality,” Nils Ehle says. “Once you live differently, balance stops being something you achieve. It becomes something you are.”

Nils Ehle speaks regularly on leadership in the age of AI and building organizations for AI readiness. He can be followed on LinkedIn, X, YouTube, and TikTok, and more on his work is available at www.changeorange.com

title: The Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange Saw Rapid Expansion in the First Half of 2026
author: editor
excerpt: In the first half of 2026, the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX) Group advanced a more comprehensive, highly accessible, and globally connected investment platform for issuers and investors, further solidifying the fundamentals of Abu Dhabi’s capital markets. The ADX’s performance in the first half of 2026 is indicative of the ongoing development of Abu Dhabi’s market ecosystem, which is bolstered by measures to increase investor involvement across asset classes and regions, new product offerings, improved market connection, and infrastructure upgrades. These advancements strengthen the ADX’s status as a reliable entry point for international capital and its support of Abu Dhabi’s long-term economic goal. The ADX started H1 2026 in a strong operational position during a time of increased geopolitical unpredictability in the area. This advancement was aided by significant improvements to the market infrastructure, such as the Core Platform Upgrade, the introduction of AD Clear and AD CSD as new subsidiaries, and the incorporation of hybrid cloud capabilities. Resilience strategies, such as enhanced short-selling procedures, upgraded circuit breaker floors, and round-the-clock operational preparedness, maintained continuous market operation and settlement integrity. The ADX showed resilience in comparison to regional conditions, maintained orderly market operations, and remained stable under pressure. This performance is a reflection of the thoughtful infrastructure design of the ADX and the success of the strategies put in place to improve the market’s capacity to withstand volatility and bounce back quickly. “The ADX’s focus remains on building a deeper, more liquid, and more internationally connected market that supports Abu Dhabi’s role as an open, leading, and preferred global economy,” stated Abdulla Salem Alnuaimi, Group Chief Executive Officer of the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (ADX) Group. title: According to Accounts, Trump hid in a Catering Truck During a Covert Jet Exchange Due to the Iran Threat
author: editor

According to the Washington Post, the US president boarded Air Force One in front of media cameras before being driven by a food truck to a military aircraft. Some White House employes and journalists on board were unaware that he had been sneaked out. The US had identified a credible Iranian threat to launch a missile against the aircraft, officials informed CBS News, the BBC’s US partner. The covert swap has not been verified by the White House. At the talks in Ankara, Trump had already declared himself Iran’s “number one target.” The covert move was made the day after Washington and Tehran failed to reach an agreement to end the conflict, prompting the US to resume military operations against Iran. Trump declared he would depart on the ancient Air Force One “for old time’s sake” after arriving in Turkey on a more recent Boeing 747-8 that Qatar had donated. He was seen boarding the presidential aircraft at the airport in Ankara on July 8. title: Following a Salmonella Outbreak, Taylor Farms Recalled Jalapeño Products
author: editor
excerpt: Following a salmonella infection, food manufacturer Taylor Farms is recalling a large portion of its fresh goods that contain jalapeño peppers. The agricultural behemoth announced that it will recall about 20 items, including sandwiches and dips, from stores like Walmart, Target, and Whole Foods. The company claimed to have produced 40% of all salad kits sold in the US last year. The business announced that it was discontinuing the items in 26 US states but claimed it was unaware of any diseases associated with them. This comes after thousands of people were impacted by an outbreak of cyclospora, a parasite that causes severe diarrhea, which was recently connected to some lettuce from Taylor Farms. The company’s pepper supplier, Coast Citrus Distributors, withdrew its own fresh jalapeno due to salmonella concerns, which prompted the jalapeño recall. Taylor Farms stated that it “is no longer sourcing products from this farmer and will be filling orders from alternative suppliers” after identifying a producer in Sinaloa, Mexico, as the cause of the outbreak. Customers should throw away any recalled goods right away and refrain from using them. It further stated, “Refunds are available at the location of purchase. title: July Temperatures in the World’s Oceans Reached Record Highs
author: editor
excerpt: According to the EU’s climate monitoring service, increasing El Niño conditions in the Pacific contributed to the world’s waters reaching their highest recorded temperatures in July. Last month, the average sea surface temperature (SST) outside of the world’s polar regions—between 60 degrees north and 60 degrees south—was 20.96C, surpassing the previous record of 20.89C, which was established in 2023. According to the Copernicus Climate Change Service, last month’s temperatures were 1.47C higher than the projected pre-industrial average, making it the joint second-warmest July on record worldwide. In the meantime, June and July were the hottest months in Western Europe’s history, and the region’s severe wildfires were fueled by persistently hot and dry weather. In other news, the UK is expected to see its fifth heatwave of the year this week as ongoing dry weather puts more strain on water resources and may result in the formal declaration of drought in more locations. Sea surface temperatures in the Atlantic and western Mediterranean regions of Europe hit all-time highs in July, causing widespread, intense, and severe marine heatwaves. In the tropical Pacific, where El Niño conditions are forming and are expected to intensify in the upcoming months, sea temperatures remained abnormally high. excerpt: There’s a difference between being in charge and actually leading, and most people can tell within minutes which one they’re dealing with. The leaders on this list fall firmly into the second category. They didn’t just occupy positions of influence; they used them to build something that held up long after the initial buzz wore off. A policy that actually worked years later. A company culture that outlived its founder’s tenure. A community program that kept running long after the cameras left. That’s what we’re after here, not the flashiest names, but the ones whose fingerprints are still visible on the world today. This roundup of the top 10 global leaders looks past the headlines to the work that actually held up. Inside the List of Top Leaders Making a Mark This list brings together the top 10 global leaders from different corners of the world, working across sectors as varied as their approaches. A quick look at what they’ve built and why it’s still standing. 1. Merissa Boey | Building a Smarter Way to Discover Technology & Software Solutions “Software and technology solutions should be accessible, transparent, and easy to navigate for businesses of every size.” That belief sits at the heart of everything Merissa Boey is building. As the Founder and CEO of SICONICA, Merissa is working towards making software and technology solutions easier to discover for businesses, professionals, developers, students, creators, and technology enthusiasts. In a world where software platforms, AI solutions, cloud technologies, and cybersecurity products continue to grow at a rapid pace, she saw the need for a place where people could discover, compare, and connect with the right solutions more easily. For Merissa, the idea behind SICONICA came from observing how complex the software and technology landscape had become. As more businesses embraced digital transformation, identifying the right software and technology solutions became increasingly challenging. SICONICA was created to bridge that gap by bringing technology providers and users together on one global platform. More than a technology discovery platform, SICONICA is designed to connect software companies, technology innovators, business leaders, and digital transformation experts. Through executive interviews, industry insights, product showcases, technology news, and global event coverage, the platform aims to educate, inspire, and connect the worldwide technology community. Merissa’s entrepreneurial journey has been centred on innovation, operational excellence, and business growth. Having led international teams and expanded operations across Australia and Asia, she has focused on building businesses while embracing emerging technologies that continue to change how organisations operate. As SICONICA prepares for its global launch, the platform is expanding its presence across Australia and Asia, with plans to continue growing internationally. For Merissa, the vision extends beyond creating a place to discover software and technology. She wants to build a trusted destination where organisations can confidently explore solutions that support their future growth. Throughout that journey, one principle has remained unchanged. “Software and technology solutions should be accessible, transparent, and easy to navigate for businesses of every size.” It is this belief that continues to guide Merissa Boey as she leads SICONICA and works towards helping innovative software and technology companies gain the global visibility they deserve. 3. Shairose Gulamani | Helping Leaders Turn Pressure into Their Greatest Strength

“Pressure doesn’t break leaders. It reveals them.”

Pressure is often treated as something to avoid, overcome, or simply endure. For Shairose Gulamani, it is something to understand and channel. Through a career spanning executive coaching, education, entrepreneurship, governance, and community leadership, she has developed a clear conviction: the true measure of a leader is not simply how much pressure they can withstand, but how intentionally and effectively they respond when it arrives.

That conviction led her to found PressurePoint: Channeling Pressure into Power Inc., where she works with executives, senior leaders, and organisations to strengthen their capacity to lead when the stakes are high. Instead of viewing resilience as simply pushing through adversity, Shairose helps leaders develop the self-awareness, emotional regulation, strategic clarity, and decision-making skills needed to perform under pressure without sacrificing their well-being.

Her perspective is grounded in both professional expertise and lived experience. Her career has taken her across education, entrepreneurship, governance, and community service, giving her first-hand insight into the complex realities leaders face. Before founding PressurePoint, she co-founded and helped build Vovito Cafés and Vovito Wholesale. These ventures deepened her understanding of business growth, operational responsibility, uncertainty, and the weight of making decisions that affect employees, customers, and communities.

Shairose’s understanding of resilience began much earlier. Born in Uganda, she came to Canada with her family after they were forced to leave their home country and rebuild their lives. That experience shaped her belief that even profound uncertainty can cultivate adaptability, courage, and the confidence to begin again.

Today, she brings these perspectives together in her work with organisations and leadership teams. Drawing on neuroscience, leadership psychology, and practical executive experience, she helps leaders navigate change, make sound decisions, and create sustainable high performance. At the heart of her approach is a powerful principle: before leaders can respond effectively to what is happening around them, they must understand what is happening within them.

Her growing influence has earned external recognition. She has also received the President’s Volunteer Service Award at the Gold level for her commitment to volunteer service.

Across her coaching, entrepreneurship, governance, writing, and community work, one purpose remains constant: helping people lead with greater clarity, intention, and humanity.

For Shairose, leadership is not about eliminating pressure or waiting for uncertainty to pass. It is about developing the inner capacity to meet difficult moments with clarity, courage, and purpose. Through PressurePoint, she helps leaders move beyond merely enduring pressure and learn to transform it into focused, meaningful action.

Those experiences taught her the value of understanding people, recognising where they thrive, and appreciating that the right opportunity is about more than matching a résumé to a role.

That perspective became the foundation of AAA Global. Rather than measuring success by how quickly a position is filled, Augusta believes the best outcomes come from taking the time to understand both clients and candidates. In markets where many of the strongest professionals are not actively looking for a new role, she believes trust, relationships, and patience make all the difference.

The same philosophy shapes the way her team works. Each consultant at AAA Global focuses on a single market, allowing them to develop specialist knowledge and build lasting relationships within their area of expertise. Augusta has also fostered a culture that values collaboration, continuous learning, and maintaining high standards, creating an environment where the team grows together while delivering consistent results.

Over the years, this approach has helped AAA Global become a trusted recruitment partner for leading hedge funds and financial institutions around the world. Rather than relying on volume, the firm’s reputation has been built through consistency, reliability, and long-term relationships.

Across these initiatives, his work centres on economic cooperation, territorial development, investment, and sustainable partnerships.

The idea behind AKAL grew from a simple observation. Countries have their own resources, traditions, industries, and expertise, yet many struggle to gain international visibility while preserving what makes them unique. Rather than creating a single standard for every market, AKAL was designed as a platform where participating countries can present their own strengths while remaining connected through a shared international network coordinated from Geneva.

This approach has led to territorial initiatives such as SEN-AKAL in Senegal and AKAL-IVOIRE in Côte d’Ivoire. While each reflects the identity of its own country, they are part of a broader framework that encourages cooperation, knowledge sharing, and economic exchange.

Through AKAL INVEST, Otmane also supports investment initiatives that encourage the development of local industries, strengthen partnerships, and create opportunities for long-term economic growth. Alongside this work, he has placed importance on education by encouraging collaboration between universities, researchers, and international development projects. His aim is to create opportunities where academic knowledge can contribute to practical solutions.

Geneva remains at the centre of this vision, serving as the meeting point where governments, entrepreneurs, institutions, NGOs, investors, and international partners can come together to explore new opportunities for collaboration.

Much of Otmane’s work brings together economic development, international cooperation, territorial branding, and sustainable development. It is guided by the belief that countries do not need to lose their identity to participate in global opportunities. Instead, they can strengthen what already makes them unique while working alongside others.

His philosophy, “From Local to Global – Ubuntu,” reflects that perspective. For Otmane Yassine, cooperation is built not by making countries the same, but by creating opportunities that allow each one to grow while preserving its own identity.

7. Kristin Bone | Choosing the Work That Matters Most

“Some people spend their careers following a single path. Kristin Bone built hers by saying yes to the work that mattered, even when it didn’t fit neatly into a title.”

That decision has taken her into places most people never experience. One day she’s leading a nursing team inside a psychiatric unit. Another day she’s on a film set helping bring an independent production to life. While the settings couldn’t be more different, Kristin sees a common thread running through all of them: people, pressure, and the responsibility that comes with both.

For more than a decade, Kristin has worked as a registered nurse and nursing supervisor in psychiatric units, correctional facilities, emergency departments, rehabilitation centres, and long-term care settings. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she stepped into travel nursing, moving between hospitals across the United States to support facilities facing severe staffing shortages. It was demanding work, but it also shaped the way she thinks about leadership, resilience, and showing up when people need you most.

Her academic background reflects that balance between healthcare and leadership. Kristin earned a Bachelor of Science in Nursing from Washburn University before completing an MBA at the University of Saint Mary, bringing together clinical knowledge with a broader understanding of organisations and the systems that support them.

Outside healthcare, Kristin found another way to tell stories. As an actress and independent film producer, she works with Cinemaddict Films and Gaimchang3r Entertainment. Among the projects closest to her is Pony, a film exploring mental health, the fentanyl crisis, family, and female motorsports. The film is complete and is currently being submitted to film festivals around the world. A world premiere is in the works, but a date has not yet been set. Follow the Pony Movie Instagram page for updates and to learn how to support the film.

That same willingness to step into unfamiliar spaces has also shaped her work beyond nursing and film. Kristin serves on the Advisory Council for the Customer Experience Certificate Program at Seton Hall University’s Stillman School of Business and is a Global Advisory Board Member of the Fortuna Business Council.

Recognition has followed along the way. In 2025, she was named Transformational Leader of the Year by White Page International and honoured at the House of Lords in London. She has also been recognised among the Global 200 Women Power Leaders, the Brainz 500 Global list, received a CREA Global Award, and contributed as an Executive Contributor to Brainz Magazine.

Looking back, Kristin doesn’t describe her career as carefully planned. Instead, it has been shaped by opportunities to make a difference, whether that meant caring for patients, producing stories that reflect real life, or contributing to conversations about leadership and mental health. Across every role, one thing has remained constant: a willingness to step forward when the work matters most.

8. Nayan Patel | Leading with Values, Purpose, and People

“A vision may start with one person, but it truly comes to life through teamwork.”

That belief has guided Nayan Patel throughout nearly three decades in the automotive manufacturing industry. Over 28 years, he has worked in Tier 1 manufacturing environments, partnering with leadership teams to strengthen operations while keeping people, culture, and accountability at the centre of every decision.

Nayan’s career has been shaped by operational leadership and organisational development. Working in director-level leadership roles within Piston Group, he has contributed to building operational discipline, supporting workforce engagement, and helping organisations align their long-term objectives with day-to-day execution. His experience also includes collaborating across supplier operations, strengthening executive communication, and encouraging cross-functional teamwork in complex manufacturing environments.

Alongside his operational expertise, Nayan has played a role in developing organisational culture and core values that support business growth. Rather than viewing culture as a separate initiative, he believes it should be reflected in the way leaders communicate, make decisions, and work with their teams.

Today, as a Certified FocalPoint Business & Executive Advisor, Nayan works with business leaders on operational leadership, organisational effectiveness, strategic growth, and leadership alignment. His approach combines years of manufacturing experience with practical business advisory, helping organisations strengthen performance while creating workplaces where people can contribute with confidence.

His professional background is supported by qualifications that include Six Sigma Black Belt, OSHA General Industry Trainer, and a degree from Lawrence Technological University. Together, they reflect his commitment to continuous learning and operational excellence.

Beyond his professional experience, Nayan is guided by a set of personal values that influence the way he leads and advises others. He believes in the importance of self-belief, lifelong learning, empowerment, integrity, diversity, and teamwork. For him, leadership is not about individual recognition but about creating an environment where others can grow, make informed decisions, and work towards shared goals.

Reflecting on his own journey, Nayan believes he found his purpose by leading with sincerity and authenticity. Inspired by the resilience and determination associated with Motown, he continues to encourage leaders to build organisations where strong values and ethical leadership remain at the heart of every decision.

Today, Nayan continues to support organizations facing complex operational challenges, helping leadership teams strengthen alignment, improve organizational effectiveness, and build cultures that support long-term success.

9. Simmone L. Bowe | Helping Leaders Build Stronger People and Stronger Organizations

“Real transformation begins with people.” That belief has shaped Simmone L. Bowe’s work as she helps organisations strengthen leadership, improve performance, and build healthier workplace cultures.

Over the years, Simmone has worked with small, medium, and large organisations, supporting leaders as they navigate change, develop their teams, and create environments where people can perform at their best. Her experience spans leadership development, cultural transformation, talent strategy, and executive coaching, bringing together practical business solutions with a people-first approach.

As the founder and lead consultant of Limitless Life, Simmone partners with organisations looking to strengthen leadership capability and organisational effectiveness. Her work includes facilitating executive retreats, helping leadership teams define their vision and strategy, designing leadership development programmes, and coaching executives as they grow into more effective leaders.

Culture has become another important focus of her work. Rather than addressing workplace challenges at the surface level, Simmone works with organisations to understand the factors influencing engagement, retention, morale, and performance. From there, she supports leaders in developing practical strategies that improve processes, strengthen collaboration, and create cultures aligned with an organisation’s long-term direction.

Alongside her consulting work, Simmone is also an accomplished speaker, certified corporate trainer, HR strategist, and personal development coach. Her career has included work as a consultant, leadership advisor, men’s empowerment advocate, educator, mentor, newspaper columnist, author, singer, and radio and television host. Each experience has contributed to her perspective on leadership and the role it plays in helping people realise their potential. Currently she is working as a Human Resources Director at Royal Caribbean Group Bahamas.

Her contributions have also been recognised beyond the workplace. Simmone was named one of the Caribbean Women to Watch in 2018 and was honoured as Mentor of the Year by Project Bahamas in 2022. She is also the author of seven books.

Academically, Simmone holds a BA in English, an MSc in Career and Human Resource Development, along with numerous professional certifications. Having worked across both the public and private sectors, she continues to bring together leadership, strategy, and personal development in ways that help organisations grow while empowering the people within them.

Today, through Limitless Life, Simmone continues to work with leaders who want to build organisations where performance and people develop together, believing that lasting success begins with investing in those who make it possible.

10. Sridhar Kuppa | Helping Businesses Make Better Financial Decisions

“Finance should do more than explain what happened. It should help leaders make better decisions about what happens next.”

For Sridhar Kuppa, finance has never been just about reporting numbers or closing the books. Throughout a career spanning more than 25 years, he has worked with founders, executives, and growing businesses, helping them use financial information as a tool for better decision-making. Whether in public accounting, corporate finance, consulting, or strategic advisory, his focus has remained the same: turning financial complexity into practical insight that supports sustainable growth.

Sridhar’s professional journey began with Ernst & Young (EY) India, where he spent more than seven years in the Assurance practice. The experience gave him a strong grounding in financial reporting, governance, and audit while exposing him to the demands of large-scale business operations. During his time at EY, he received the EY Sparkle Award in recognition of his integrity and ethical leadership and contributed to a major IPO engagement.

As his career progressed, Sridhar took on finance leadership roles with organisations including Aurobindo Pharma, Amneal Pharmaceuticals, and Solomon Edwards. Across these roles, he worked on financial reporting, transaction advisory, ERP implementations, financial planning, cash flow management, and finance transformation. The variety of these experiences gave him a practical understanding of the financial decisions businesses face as they grow, evolve, and adapt to changing markets.

Today, Sridhar is the Co-Founder of Huntward Advisors, where he partners with founders, CEOs, and finance leaders to build finance functions that support better business decisions. His work spans CFO advisory, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), cash flow forecasting, outsourced finance and accounting, and decision support. Rather than viewing finance as a function focused solely on reporting, he helps leadership teams use financial information to plan ahead, manage uncertainty, and make informed strategic choices.

His professional experience is complemented by qualifications earned across both India and the United States. Sridhar is a Chartered Accountant (India) and a Certified Public Accountant (USA). He also holds an MBA from NYU Stern School of Business, a Master’s degree in Accounting from the University of Phoenix, and a Bachelor of Commerce from Osmania University, combining technical financial expertise with a broader understanding of business strategy.

In 2026, Sridhar was recognised at the Founders 2.0 Conference in Las Vegas, where he also participated in discussions on leadership, entrepreneurship, and experiential learning. After building much of his career in the United States, he relocated to India to establish and lead Huntward Advisors’ offshore operations, bringing together global financial experience with scalable delivery for growing businesses.

For Sridhar, the most meaningful part of finance isn’t found in spreadsheets or reports. It’s in helping leaders make confident decisions, prepare for what’s ahead, and build businesses that can grow with purpose. That belief continues to guide his work as he supports organisations looking to turn financial insight into lasting business value.

LinkedIn | Huntward Advisors

Conclusion

If there’s one thing these top 10 global leaders prove, it’s that impact rarely happens overnight. It’s built slowly, tested repeatedly, and often goes unnoticed until much later, when someone finally looks back and realizes how much actually changed. None of them took the easy route. All of them left something behind that’s bigger than their own name. And in a world obsessed with instant results, that kind of staying power is worth paying attention to.

title: Todd Blanche, Trump’s Former Attorney, was just Barely Approved as US Attorney General
author: editor
excerpt: Todd Blanche, a former personal attorney for US President Donald Trump, was narrowly confirmed as the country’s highest law enforcement official, the attorney general. The vote ends a protracted impasse over Blanche, who has been acting attorney general since April, between the Trump administration and Senate Republicans. Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski, two Republicans, joined all Democrats in opposing Blanche’s candidacy, but Blanche secured confirmation in a 50-49 vote overnight. Given the years of animosity between the Louisiana Republican and Trump, Senator Bill Cassidy cast the decisive vote, which was widely monitored in Washington. Blanche declared that he was “deeply honored by the trust and confidence President Trump has placed in me” following the vote. Blache’s role in setting up Trump’s $1.8 billion (£1.3 billion) “anti-weaponization” fund and his management of the release of information pertaining to Jeffrey Epstein had drawn criticism from several Republican lawmakers. Murkowski and other critics feared that the fund, which was intended to compensate people who said they had been persecuted by the government, would instead go to people who had been charged with taking part in the 2021 attack on Congress on January 6. After receiving backlash from Republican senators during his confirmation hearings, Blanche finally promised to withdraw the cash. title: Watchdog Discovers That Doge Exaggerated Claims to have Saved Americans $110 Billion
author: editor
excerpt: A watchdog has discovered that some of the estimations made by Doge, the organization tasked with cutting US government spending, that it saved billions of dollars are “incorrect or lack supporting evidence”. Doge’s assertions regarding its so-called “Wall of Receipts”—which claimed savings of $110 billion (£82 billion) across contracts, grants, and leases—were thoroughly examined in a study published on Thursday by the Government Accountability Office (GAO).The openness and dependability of these reported savings are limited by a number of concerns, according to the research. When contacted for comment, a White House official stated that the administration informed the GAO that all staff members were required to take ethics training and adhere to financial disclosure regulations. The Department of Government Efficiency, or Doge, was not a recognized government agency. It shuttered last month after opening at the beginning of President Trump’s second term. Its Wall of Receipts served as an online display of its alleged taxpayer savings. The wealthy CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, Elon Musk, who formerly headed Doge until leaving in May 2025, first pledged to save up to $2 trillion annually by eliminating government programs and downsizing federal positions, among other cost-saving initiatives. Doge’s website claims to have saved an estimated $214 billion, although even by Doge’s own estimations, it failed to meet that target.The transparency and dependability of these purported savings are limited by a number of concerns, despite Doge providing some information regarding estimated savings, according to the GAO report. title: Unexpected Decline in US Employment Last Month as the Summer Continues to be Slow
author: editor
excerpt: According to official data, the US economy is producing fewer jobs than anticipated, and the summer job market is doing worse than previously believed. Despite economists’ predictions of growth, there was an unexpected loss of 23,000 jobs last month, primarily due to reductions in local government education and retail positions. Additionally, the Bureau of Labor Statistics revised down the number of jobs created in May and June by 103,000, indicating a poor summer for job creation. Despite strong inflation, analysts suggested the most recent data would lessen pressure on the Federal Reserve, the US central bank, to hike interest rates next month. Expectations of an increase in interest rates have “scaled back” since last month’s decision, according to Nancy Vanden Houten, lead economist at Oxford Economics. Following the announcement of the most recent employment data, US stock markets opened higher on Friday due to the possibility that any rate hikes could be avoided due to the poor data. title: A Thai Student Shoots Fire at Home and at School, Killing Seven People
author: editor
excerpt: A 14-year-old boy opened fire at his house and school on the suburbs of Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, leaving at least seven dead and twenty-three injured. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul told reporters that the gunman, a pupil at the Debsirin School in Nonthaburi, killed his grandparents and five teachers before ending his own life. According to Anutin, the assailant had “more than 30 bullets left” when he turned the gun on himself. According to police, nine of the injured individuals are still in severe condition. The second school shooting in Thailand this year has increased pressure on the government to take stronger gun control measures. The active gunfire started just after 10:00 local time (03:00 GMT), and police were called to the location. Reporters were informed by National Police Chief Gen. Kittiratt Phanphet that forensic investigators had discovered that the gunman’s rounds were quite precise, with multiple of them striking critical areas of the body. According to the prime minister, the attack had “clear steps and clear goals” and was “well prepared”. The BBC was informed by a female seventh-grader who was still wearing her school uniform that she was in front of her instructor when the woman was shot. title: Meta is The Latest Company to Allege its AI Hacked Another Company
author: editor
excerpt: Meta, Facebook’s parent company, is the latest tech business to admit one of its AI models managed to connect to the internet and hack into another organisation’s systems during testing. Meta said the incident happened during a review by an independent organization. It is the fourth recent instance of its kind acknowledged by AI companies. Cybersecurity worries and calls for stronger controls and more thorough testing have been fueled by similar breaches from OpenAI and Anthropic models. A Meta representative told the BBC it was examining the attack, which it said was triggered by a “misconfiguration” by its independent tester. It also said the incidence was comparable to what had been reported at other organizations in the past. Meta stated the security testing were undertaken by Irregular, the same AI security provider that tested Anthropic’s AI model that had breached three other companies’ systems. The Meta incident is the very same evaluation-environment issue already disclosed by Anthropic last week,” an Irregular spokeswoman said. The firm’s representative told the BBC Irregular is working on a paper on how to execute cyber-security testing involving AI agents securely. Meta said the incident happened during a review by an independent organization. It is the fourth recent instance of its kind acknowledged by AI companies. Cybersecurity worries and calls for stronger controls and more thorough testing have been fueled by similar breaches from OpenAI and Anthropic models.

A Meta representative told the BBC it was examining the attack, which it said was triggered by a “misconfiguration” by its independent tester. It also said the incidence was comparable to what had been reported at other organizations in the past.

Meta stated the security testing were undertaken by Irregular, the same AI security provider that tested Anthropic’s AI model that had breached three other companies’ systems.

The Meta incident is the very same evaluation-environment issue already disclosed by Anthropic last week,” an Irregular spokeswoman said. The firm’s representative told the BBC Irregular is working on a paper on how to execute cyber-security testing involving AI agents securely.

title: No One is Safe from Russia’s New Black Sea Strikes on Odesa
author: editor
excerpt: My mate, my crane operator, died just five metres from me… The driver stayed in the cab. He died, too. Svitlana Halchenko winces at the memory of the Russian ballistic missile which exploded at work in Odesa, killing her colleagues. Svitlana is a shift manager at the city’s biggest port, at the warehouse. Despite her injuries – bits of shrapnel still lodged in her leg and back, she walks with a limp Svitlana is determined to keep working. Her normally busy workplace is mostly quiet. Russia is intensifying its efforts to strangle Ukraine’s trade connections to the outside world by shelling the entire Black Sea coast of the country. The evidence is everywhere, from destroyed port infrastructure to ships that are wallowing with burned bridges and containers still smoldering. That is especially true as far as the eye can see, where the approaches to Ukraine’s once-bustling ports of Odesa, Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi are all but empty of ships. Svitlana keeps a brave smile on her face during our conversation, but her pain is obvious. Her fingers twist a tissue as she attempts to keep control and she looks into the distance as tears start to fill up behind her glasses.
