content:
Every enterprise today has access to more information than ever before. Reports arrive instantly, dashboards refresh in real time, and executives can monitor nearly every business metric with a few clicks. Yet despite this abundance of information, many important business decisions are still delayed, debated, or driven by experience instead of structured analysis.

Technology has made it easier to collect data. It has not necessarily made organizations better at acting on it.

That challenge sits at the center of Abhijit Singh’s work.

As Founder and CEO of Seven Billion Analytics, he works with organizations across manufacturing, FMCG, supply chain, healthcare, and agri-food to help them move beyond reporting toward systems that actively support operational decisions. Rather than treating analytics as the final destination, his focus is on making data useful at the exact moment decisions need to be made.

In this conversation, Abhijit shares why many organizations continue to struggle despite significant investments in analytics, how enterprises should identify meaningful opportunities for automation, why trust is essential before technology can scale, and why the future of enterprise operations depends as much on decision design as it does on intelligent systems.

Key Takeaways

  • Business value comes from improving decisions, not simply producing more reports.
  • Organizations should identify high-impact business decisions before selecting technology.
  • Production deployment requires far more effort than building a successful model.
  • Explainability and governance should be designed from the beginning.
  • Voice-based enterprise systems can serve operational users who rarely interact with traditional applications.
  • The most successful enterprise systems combine automation with appropriate human oversight.
  • Organizations should measure success through business outcomes and decision confidence rather than technical metrics alone.

Q1. Organizations have invested heavily in analytics over the last decade. Why do so many still struggle to improve business decisions?

One of the biggest misconceptions is that more data automatically leads to better decisions. In reality, most enterprises already possess enormous amounts of operational data. The challenge is rarely data availability.

The challenge is deciding what to do with that information.

Many organizations have excellent reporting systems and sophisticated dashboards, but when critical operational decisions need to be made—whether it’s production planning, inventory allocation, procurement, or distribution—people often revert to manual judgment because the system doesn’t help them make the actual decision.

That is where the real opportunity exists.

The objective shouldn’t simply be to visualize information better. It should be to reduce uncertainty around important business decisions so leaders can act faster and with greater confidence.

Ultimately, organizations don’t create value from dashboards. They create value from making better decisions consistently.

Expert Insight: Throughout the conversation, Abhijit returns to one consistent idea: analytics becomes valuable only when it improves operational decision-making rather than simply reporting business performance.

Q2. When companies begin exploring enterprise AI, where do you believe they should actually start?

Most organizations start by discussing technology.

They ask which models they should use, which platform they should buy, or which latest innovation they should experiment with.

Those are important conversations, but they usually happen too early.

The better starting point is identifying a business decision that has measurable impact. It should be a decision that happens frequently, carries meaningful business risk when it’s wrong, and currently depends on fragmented or inconsistent information.

Once that decision is clearly defined, technology becomes much easier to evaluate because every technical choice can be measured against a business outcome.

Without that clarity, projects often become technology demonstrations instead of operational improvements.

The goal is never to implement technology for its own sake.

The goal is to improve the quality, consistency, and speed of business decisions.

Expert Insight: Rather than beginning with software or models, Abhijit recommends beginning with a business decision that can produce measurable operational improvement.

Q3. Many AI initiatives perform well during pilots but struggle once they reach production. Why does that happen?

Building a working model is only one part of the journey.

In many cases, it is actually the easiest part.

The much larger challenge begins after that.

Production systems have to integrate with existing business processes, work alongside legacy applications, gain the trust of operational teams, and continue performing reliably under real business conditions.

That requires engineering, governance, change management, and continuous monitoring.

Organizations frequently underestimate this phase because successful demonstrations create the impression that deployment will be straightforward.

In practice, production success depends on much more than model performance.

If people don’t trust the recommendations, or if the system doesn’t integrate naturally into existing workflows, even highly accurate models may never influence business decisions.

That’s why production readiness should be treated as a core objective from the beginning rather than something addressed after a successful pilot.

Q4. You often talk about “decision intelligence.” How is that different from traditional analytics?

Traditional analytics helps organizations understand what has happened or what is happening. It gives leaders visibility into business performance through reports, dashboards, and metrics.

Decision intelligence takes the next step.

Instead of stopping at insights, it focuses on helping people decide what action to take next.

For example, a dashboard may show that inventory levels are increasing. That information is useful, but someone still has to decide whether production should change, whether purchasing should slow down, or whether distribution plans need adjustment.

Our goal is to reduce that gap between information and action.

Technology should support the decision itself, not just display the numbers behind it.

When organizations improve the quality of their decisions, they naturally improve business performance.

Expert Insight: Abhijit’s approach is simple: reports explain the business, while decision intelligence helps improve the business by supporting better operational decisions.

Q5. As more organizations rely on AI, how important are trust and explainability?

They are essential.

No organization should deploy a system that people cannot understand or confidently use.

Business leaders need to know who owns the system, how decisions are reviewed, and what happens when the system produces an unexpected recommendation.

These questions should be answered before deployment, not after.

Explainability is equally important.

When people understand why a recommendation has been made, they are much more likely to trust it and use it during daily operations.

That is especially important for decisions involving production, supply chain planning, procurement, and other operational processes where the cost of a wrong decision can be significant.

Governance should never be treated as an additional feature.

It should be part of the system from the beginning because trust is built through good design.

Expert Insight: Trust is created through ownership, governance, and explainability. These are foundational elements of enterprise systems rather than optional additions.

Q6. Your company has invested in voice technology through VaaniOS. What business challenge does it solve?

Many enterprise solutions are designed for people who regularly use mobile apps or digital platforms.

However, large parts of India’s supply chain operate very differently.

Distributors, retailers, field teams, and many participants across emerging markets often communicate through phone calls in their preferred regional language.

VaaniOS was built for those users.

The platform combines Indian-language speech recognition, neural voice synthesis, and conversational reasoning so users can complete business tasks through natural voice conversations.

One example is supporting distributor order capture.

Another is managing healthcare front-desk interactions.

A deployment that stands out is an agri-distributor in Haryana, where farmers place orders in Haryanvi. The system manages those conversations while allowing human review whenever an interaction requires escalation.

That demonstrates an important principle.

Technology should adapt to how people already work instead of expecting people to completely change their behavior.

Expert Insight: VaaniOS focuses on making enterprise technology accessible through voice for users who may never rely on traditional mobile applications.

Q7. Do you believe enterprises should move toward complete automation?

I believe automation should be practical.

Not every decision should be handled entirely by machines, and not every decision requires constant human involvement.

The most effective approach is finding the right balance.

Routine decisions that follow well-defined business rules can often be handled automatically.

More complex situations, unusual exceptions, or high-impact decisions should be reviewed by people.

That combination allows organizations to improve speed without losing accountability.

For this approach to succeed, organizations first need clearly defined decision processes.

If the decision itself has never been properly structured, there is nothing reliable for automation to execute.

Automation works best when it strengthens good decision-making rather than replacing it.

Expert Insight: Abhijit believes enterprise automation should combine operational efficiency with human judgment, allowing routine work to be automated while exceptional situations continue to receive appropriate human oversight.

Q8. How do you measure whether an enterprise AI project has truly been successful?

Many organizations focus first on technical metrics like model accuracy. Those numbers are important, but they don’t tell the complete story.

The bigger question is whether the system helps people make better business decisions.

If a planning team can make decisions with greater confidence, if operational teams trust the recommendations, and if business outcomes improve, then the project has delivered real value.

One example that stays with me is when the supply chain head of a leading ready-to-eat food company said they could confidently explain and defend their production plan instead of relying on instinct.

That moment represented something much bigger than an accuracy score.

Technology should improve the quality of judgment, not simply generate predictions.

Business success comes when people trust the system enough to use it in their everyday decisions.

Expert Insight: Technical performance matters, but long-term success is measured by stronger business decisions, greater confidence, and meaningful operational outcomes.

Q9. What advice would you give to business leaders who want to begin their AI journey today?

Keep the first step simple.

Don’t begin with a large transformation programme or a long strategy document.

Start by identifying one business decision that happens regularly, has a meaningful business impact, and can be measured clearly.

Solve that problem well.

When teams see measurable improvements from one successful implementation, confidence grows across the organization. Future initiatives become much easier because people have already experienced the value.

Trying to transform everything at once usually creates unnecessary complexity.

Building momentum through one successful business problem creates a much stronger foundation for long-term adoption.

Technology should always support business priorities, not become the priority itself.

Expert Insight: Starting with one measurable business problem creates faster results, stronger internal confidence, and a clearer path for future transformation.

Q10. Looking ahead, what is your long-term vision for Seven Billion Analytics?

Our vision has remained consistent from the beginning.

We want to help organizations become better at making important business decisions.

Whether that involves manufacturing, supply chains, food systems, healthcare, or other operational environments, the objective is the same—to help organizations make decisions faster, with greater confidence, and under uncertainty.

We do not see ourselves as a company that simply builds dashboards or delivers technology projects.

Our focus is helping enterprises strengthen the decision-making process itself.

If the organizations we work with are consistently making better decisions because of the systems we build, then we have achieved what we set out to do.

That is the impact we want to create over the long term.

Expert Insight: Abhijit’s long-term vision is centred on improving how organizations make decisions, ensuring technology becomes a practical tool for better business outcomes rather than an end in itself.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1. What does Seven Billion Analytics do?

Seven Billion Analytics works with organizations across FMCG, manufacturing, supply chain, healthcare, and agri-food to build systems that help improve business decisions. The focus is on closing the gap between data and operational decision-making rather than simply delivering reports or dashboards.

Q2. Why do many enterprise AI projects struggle after the pilot stage?

Many projects underestimate the work required for production deployment. Successful implementation requires integration with existing systems, operational trust, governance, and reliable day-to-day performance—not just an accurate model.

Q3. What is decision intelligence?

Decision intelligence focuses on helping organizations make better business decisions. Instead of only presenting information, it supports choosing the most appropriate action based on available data.

Q4. Why is explainability important?

Business users need to understand why a recommendation has been made before relying on it for important operational decisions. Explainability builds confidence and supports responsible deployment.

Q5. What is VaaniOS?

VaaniOS is a voice platform designed for supply chain participants who primarily communicate through phone calls in Indian regional languages. It supports business interactions such as distributor order capture and healthcare front-desk operations while allowing human review when needed.

Q6. Should every enterprise decision be fully automated?

No. Routine decisions can often be automated, while complex or exceptional situations should continue to involve human oversight. A balanced approach provides both efficiency and accountability.

Q7. What is the best starting point for organizations exploring AI?

Begin with one clearly defined business decision that occurs frequently, has measurable business impact, and currently depends on unstructured or inconsistent decision-making. Solve that problem first before expanding to larger initiatives.

title: Due to the “Tank Day” Incident, Police Raid the Starbucks Korea Headquarters
author: editor
excerpt: Due to allegations of slander about a contentious advertising campaign, South Korean police visited Starbucks’ national headquarters. In honor of the anniversary of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising, in which hundreds are thought to have been slain by military forces, Starbucks Korea created a coffee tumbler campaign named “Tank Day” in May. The campaign prompted a widespread boycott movement since many believed the “tank” was a reference to vehicles used to crush pro-democracy demonstrators. Civic organizations filed a criminal complaint against Starbucks, demanding that the authorities look into the firm for defaming victims of the military dictatorship. Starbucks swiftly retracted the statement, claiming it was inadvertent. After conducting an internal inquiry into the campaign, Shinsegae Group, which runs Starbucks in Korea, declared that the error was inadvertent. It further stated that neither the higher management nor the team responsible for organizing the promotion saw the connection to the historical incident. Starbucks locations nationwide shuttered for half a day in June so that employees could attend history classes. Shinsegae expressed regret for the “inappropriate marketing” and said that Starbucks sales in South Korea, one of the company’s biggest markets, had significantly decreased as a result of the Tank Day issue. title: Why it’s Contentious for Trump Media to Sell Quick Access to Popular Social Media Postings
author: editor
excerpt: Financial traders are among the most attentive listeners when Donald Trump speaks. Teams of traders and a variety of automatic computer systems keep an eye on the US president’s remarks to execute deals in a matter of seconds since anything he says can affect markets, from trade battles to military conflicts. These days, Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG) intends to charge for information that moves the market on its Truth Social platform. title: Analysts Say the Threat to Oil Tankers in the Middle East is The Biggest Since the Start of the Iran War
author: editor
excerpt: Experts say the threat to ships carrying oil in the Middle East has reached its peak since the Iran conflict began, following a series of strikes on another vital route in the region. The warning follows a series of attacks on vessels in the Red Sea, an alternate channel used by some tankers since Iran sealed the Strait of Hormuz. Iran rejected conversations with the US to reopen the strait, but stated that it is negotiating with Oman to secure the maritime passage.In terms of the threat to petroleum commerce, we’re in the worst situation we’ve been in since the crisis began,” said Matthew Wright, an analyst with ship tracking service Kpler. According to Kpler, the number of ships transiting through the Strait of Hormuz was only eight on Sunday and 11 on Saturday, down from more than 100 every day before the war. Prior to the conflict, almost 20% of the world’s oil and gas went through the strait. The temporary peace agreement with the United States reached in early June caused numbers to rise again, but the restart of strikes between the two countries about a month later drastically curtailed travel. author: editor
excerpt: Two Republican senators who had vowed to oppose Todd Blanche’s confirmation as the next US attorney general have suddenly stated that they are willing to lend their support. We are pleased that the Department of Justice has issued a formal order terminating the anti-weaponization fund,” the two remaining senators, Thom Tillis and John Cornyn, said in a joint statement. title: No Dogs Left Behind Transparency: Following Every Rescue From Day One to a Forever Home
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: When people support an animal rescue organization, they want to know where their donations go and how rescued animals are cared for after they are saved. This is one reason transparency has become such an important topic in animal welfare. For No Dogs Left Behind, transparency is not simply a policy. It is part of the rescue process itself. From the moment a dog is rescued to the day it enters a forever home, supporters are often able to follow the journey through updates, rescue footage, rehabilitation stories, and adoption milestones. This commitment to transparency helps people better understand what rescue truly involves and the resources required to help animals recover from severe cruelty and neglect. Why Transparency Matters in Animal Rescue Animal rescue is often much more complicated than people realize. Many rescued dogs require: Emergency intervention Veterinary treatment Long-term rehabilitation Sanctuary care Adoption preparation International transportation Without transparency, it can be difficult for supporters to understand the work taking place behind the scenes. No Dogs Left Behind believes supporters should have the opportunity to see how rescued animals progress through each stage of recovery. This helps build trust while also highlighting the reality of large-scale rescue operations. Rescue Begins Before the Cameras Stop Rolling Many people first discover No Dogs Left Behind through rescue videos shared online. These videos often document difficult situations involving: Slaughter trucks Dog trafficking operations Wet markets Illegal holding facilities Slaughterhouses While the rescue itself is dramatic, it is only the beginning of the story. Once dogs are removed from danger, a much longer process begins. Many animals arrive frightened, injured, sick, malnourished, or severely traumatized. Helping them recover requires months of dedicated care. No Dogs Left Behind Never Pays for Dogs One of the most important aspects of the organization’s rescue philosophy is that No Dogs Left Behind does not buy dogs from traffickers or slaughterhouses. The organization works alongside local activists, government authorities, and law enforcement agencies to help confiscate animals from dangerous situations. This distinction matters because purchasing animals can unintentionally create financial incentives for trafficking networks. Instead, No Dogs Left Behind focuses on rescue efforts that prioritize animal welfare while supporting responsible intervention practices. Many rescue operations documented by the organization clearly show authorities working alongside rescue teams to secure animals without any exchange of money. The First Days After Rescue The first few days after a rescue are often the most critical. Many dogs require immediate medical evaluations to determine their condition and identify urgent health concerns. Veterinary teams may need to address: Dehydration Infections Injuries Parasites Malnutrition Respiratory illnesses Skin conditions For some dogs, these treatments can mean the difference between life and death. Supporters often receive updates that help them understand the challenges individual dogs face during this stage of recovery. Rehabilitation Takes Time Physical recovery is only one part of the healing process. Many rescued dogs have experienced severe trauma. Some are fearful of human interaction. Others have never lived in a safe environment. No Dogs Left Behind invests significant time and resources into helping dogs rebuild confidence and learn to trust people again. Rehabilitation may include: Socialization Behavioral support Structured care routines Safe housing Daily interaction with caregivers Each dog recovers at a different pace. Some adjust quickly, while others require months of patience and support. Jeffrey Beri and the Commitment to Accountability Jeffrey Beri, founder of No Dogs Left Behind, has long emphasized the importance of showing supporters what happens after a rescue. Many people see rescue footage online, but fewer understand the extensive care required after animals are removed from dangerous situations. By documenting rescue missions, treatment plans, rehabilitation progress, and adoption stories, the organization provides a clear picture of the work involved in helping dogs recover. Jeffrey Beri’s direct involvement in rescue efforts also allows supporters to witness many aspects of the process firsthand. His presence alongside rescue teams, local activists, volunteers, and government officials has become a key part of the organization’s commitment to accountability and transparency. Preparing Dogs for Adoption Before a dog can be adopted, several important steps must take place. Depending on the individual dog, this process may include: Medical clearance Vaccinations Behavioral assessments Socialization programs Travel preparation Adoption matching The goal is to ensure that each dog is physically and emotionally ready for life with a permanent family. No Dogs Left Behind continues supporting dogs throughout this process until they are safely placed in loving homes. From Rescue to Forever Home One of the most rewarding aspects of transparency is seeing the transformation that occurs over time. Dogs that once arrived frightened, injured, and struggling to survive often become healthy, confident companions living with families who love them. These success stories demonstrate the impact of rescue, rehabilitation, and ongoing care. They also help supporters understand how their contributions directly affect the lives of rescued animals. Every adoption represents the completion of a journey that began with a rescue and ended with a second chance. Transparency Supports the Mission Transparency is not only about sharing information. It is about helping people understand the reality of rescue work. No Dogs Left Behind continues to fight against cruelty, support efforts to end the dog meat trade, and advocate for stronger animal welfare protections worldwide. By documenting each stage of the rescue process, the organization allows supporters to see how dogs move from crisis situations to safe and loving homes. That visibility helps build trust and strengthens the connection between the organization and the community that supports its mission. Final Thoughts Transparency plays an important role in everything No Dogs Left Behind does. From confiscation and rescue operations to medical treatment, rehabilitation, adoption, and forever homes, the organization works to ensure supporters can understand and follow the journey of rescued animals. Every dog’s story is different, but the mission remains the same: provide safety, healing, and hope for animals that have experienced extraordinary hardship. For supporters, that transparency offers confidence that every rescue is about more than saving a life
content:
When people support an animal rescue organization, they want to know where their donations go and how rescued animals are cared for after they are saved.

This is one reason transparency has become such an important topic in animal welfare.

For No Dogs Left Behind, transparency is not simply a policy. It is part of the rescue process itself.

From the moment a dog is rescued to the day it enters a forever home, supporters are often able to follow the journey through updates, rescue footage, rehabilitation stories, and adoption milestones.

This commitment to transparency helps people better understand what rescue truly involves and the resources required to help animals recover from severe cruelty and neglect.

Why Transparency Matters in Animal Rescue

Animal rescue is often much more complicated than people realize.

Many rescued dogs require:

  • Emergency intervention
  • Veterinary treatment
  • Long-term rehabilitation
  • Sanctuary care
  • Adoption preparation
  • International transportation

Without transparency, it can be difficult for supporters to understand the work taking place behind the scenes.

No Dogs Left Behind believes supporters should have the opportunity to see how rescued animals progress through each stage of recovery.

This helps build trust while also highlighting the reality of large-scale rescue operations.

Rescue Begins Before the Cameras Stop Rolling

Many people first discover No Dogs Left Behind through rescue videos shared online.

These videos often document difficult situations involving:

  • Slaughter trucks
  • Dog trafficking operations
  • Wet markets
  • Illegal holding facilities
  • Slaughterhouses

While the rescue itself is dramatic, it is only the beginning of the story.

Once dogs are removed from danger, a much longer process begins.

Many animals arrive frightened, injured, sick, malnourished, or severely traumatized.

Helping them recover requires months of dedicated care.

No Dogs Left Behind Never Pays for Dogs

One of the most important aspects of the organization’s rescue philosophy is that No Dogs Left Behind does not buy dogs from traffickers or slaughterhouses.

The organization works alongside local activists, government authorities, and law enforcement agencies to help confiscate animals from dangerous situations.

This distinction matters because purchasing animals can unintentionally create financial incentives for trafficking networks.

Instead, No Dogs Left Behind focuses on rescue efforts that prioritize animal welfare while supporting responsible intervention practices.

Many rescue operations documented by the organization clearly show authorities working alongside rescue teams to secure animals without any exchange of money.

The First Days After Rescue

The first few days after a rescue are often the most critical.

Many dogs require immediate medical evaluations to determine their condition and identify urgent health concerns.

Veterinary teams may need to address:

  • Dehydration
  • Infections
  • Injuries
  • Parasites
  • Malnutrition
  • Respiratory illnesses
  • Skin conditions

For some dogs, these treatments can mean the difference between life and death.

Supporters often receive updates that help them understand the challenges individual dogs face during this stage of recovery.

Rehabilitation Takes Time

Physical recovery is only one part of the healing process.

Many rescued dogs have experienced severe trauma.

Some are fearful of human interaction.

Others have never lived in a safe environment.

No Dogs Left Behind invests significant time and resources into helping dogs rebuild confidence and learn to trust people again.

Rehabilitation may include:

  • Socialization
  • Behavioral support
  • Structured care routines
  • Safe housing
  • Daily interaction with caregivers

Each dog recovers at a different pace.

Some adjust quickly, while others require months of patience and support.

Jeffrey Beri and the Commitment to Accountability

Jeffrey Beri, founder of No Dogs Left Behind, has long emphasized the importance of showing supporters what happens after a rescue.

Many people see rescue footage online, but fewer understand the extensive care required after animals are removed from dangerous situations.

By documenting rescue missions, treatment plans, rehabilitation progress, and adoption stories, the organization provides a clear picture of the work involved in helping dogs recover.

Jeffrey Beri’s direct involvement in rescue efforts also allows supporters to witness many aspects of the process firsthand.

His presence alongside rescue teams, local activists, volunteers, and government officials has become a key part of the organization’s commitment to accountability and transparency.

Preparing Dogs for Adoption

Before a dog can be adopted, several important steps must take place.

Depending on the individual dog, this process may include:

  • Medical clearance
  • Vaccinations
  • Behavioral assessments
  • Socialization programs
  • Travel preparation
  • Adoption matching

The goal is to ensure that each dog is physically and emotionally ready for life with a permanent family.

No Dogs Left Behind continues supporting dogs throughout this process until they are safely placed in loving homes.

From Rescue to Forever Home

One of the most rewarding aspects of transparency is seeing the transformation that occurs over time.

Dogs that once arrived frightened, injured, and struggling to survive often become healthy, confident companions living with families who love them.

These success stories demonstrate the impact of rescue, rehabilitation, and ongoing care.

They also help supporters understand how their contributions directly affect the lives of rescued animals.

Every adoption represents the completion of a journey that began with a rescue and ended with a second chance.

Transparency Supports the Mission

Transparency is not only about sharing information.

It is about helping people understand the reality of rescue work.

No Dogs Left Behind continues to fight against cruelty, support efforts to end the dog meat trade, and advocate for stronger animal welfare protections worldwide.

By documenting each stage of the rescue process, the organization allows supporters to see how dogs move from crisis situations to safe and loving homes.

That visibility helps build trust and strengthens the connection between the organization and the community that supports its mission.

Final Thoughts

Transparency plays an important role in everything No Dogs Left Behind does.

From confiscation and rescue operations to medical treatment, rehabilitation, adoption, and forever homes, the organization works to ensure supporters can understand and follow the journey of rescued animals.

Every dog’s story is different, but the mission remains the same: provide safety, healing, and hope for animals that have experienced extraordinary hardship.

For supporters, that transparency offers confidence that every rescue is about more than saving a life in the moment. It is about creating a future where that life can truly thrive.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does transparency mean at No Dogs Left Behind?

Transparency means documenting and sharing the rescue journey from confiscation and medical treatment to rehabilitation, adoption, and placement in a forever home.

Does No Dogs Left Behind buy dogs from traffickers?

No. The organization works alongside government authorities, law enforcement agencies, and local partners to help confiscate dogs rather than purchasing them.

Why do rescued dogs need rehabilitation?

Many rescued dogs have experienced trauma, neglect, illness, or abuse and require time, medical care, and behavioral support before they are ready for adoption.

Who is Jeffrey Beri?

Jeffrey Beri is the founder of No Dogs Left Behind and is known for working directly with rescue teams, activists, volunteers, and authorities during rescue missions.

What happens after a dog is rescued?

Rescued dogs receive medical treatment, rehabilitation, nutritional support, sanctuary care, adoption preparation, and ongoing assistance until they are placed in loving homes.

title: If Hamas’ Disarming Proposal Succeeds, it Might be the First Real Step Toward Putting an End to the Conflict in Gaza
author: editor
excerpt: For the first time, Hamas has agreed to the Board of Peace’s plan to fully disarm Gaza after months of intense negotiations. The plan calls for the inventory and storage of its remaining heavy weapons under Palestinian supervision, which may eliminate the biggest barrier to the Trump-backed peace strategy for Gaza. The action was taken shortly after Hamas held elections to choose its new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, who is located in Gaza. Driven by the dire humanitarian circumstances that more than two million Palestinians in Gaza face, Palestinian officials participating in the negotiations believe the new leadership was ready to make what they call the most significant political choice in Hamas’s history. The BBC was informed by a senior Hamas official and member of the movement’s negotiating team that the negotiations were “long and extremely difficult” and that Hamas insisted on the phrase “inventorying and storing weapons” under Palestinian supervision instead of giving them to Israel. Whether the agreement will be completely executed or whether all parties will keep their end of the bargain is still too early to say. However, if it succeeds, it might be the first real step toward putting an end to a nearly three-year-long conflict and paving the way for a more comprehensive political process. title: Due to the Iran War, Shell’s Revenues Treble as Oil Prices Climb
author: editor
excerpt: Due to higher oil prices brought on by the Iran war, Shell’s profits for the second quarter of this year more than doubled. For the April–June period, the oil major reported profits of $9.84 billion (£7.37 billion), up from $4.26 billion at the same time last year. Due to significant disruptions to the world’s oil and LNG supplies via the Strait of Hormuz, the price of crude has increased since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran. However, the battle has also caused significant fluctuations in energy prices, which has helped Shell’s trading business. The company’s “operational performance enabled very strong results during another quarter of severe disruption in global energy markets,” according to Shell CEO Wael Sawan. When combined with its $6.92 billion in profits for the first three months of the year, this indicates that Shell’s first-half earnings have increased by 70%. Due in part to speculating on fluctuations in oil prices, Shell and other energy behemoths like BP and Norway’s Equinor have enjoyed enormous profits this year. The price of Brent crude, the world standard for oil prices, was about $73 per barrel prior to the start of the conflict. title: Amal and Clooney Flee Their French Residence Due to Wildfires
author: editor
excerpt: Amidst the devastating wildfires in the south of France, George and Amal Clooney have fled their house. Earlier last week, actor Clooney, his wife, a human rights attorney, and their two kids departed their Brignoles home. author: editor

title: New Chinese Humanoid Robots are Prohibited by the Trump Administration
author: editor
excerpt: Due to “unacceptable risks” to the country’s security, the Trump administration declared on Tuesday that new humanoid robots manufactured abroad will not be allowed to be imported into the United States. This move covers advanced robots, such as humanoid and four-legged machines. China, which is competing with the US in the development of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI), produces a large number of them. Additionally, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) prohibited the import of power inverters, which are used in solar panels and data centers and which it claimed could endanger the US economy. Beijing has always opposed the US’s “politicizing” of economic disputes and sanctions based on “groundless pretexts,” according to the Chinese embassy in Washington. According to FCC chairman Brendan Carr, the organization is contributing “to secure America’s critical supply chains.” The products have been added to the FCC’s Covered List, which is a list of products and services that are thought to pose a threat to US national security. The restriction only affects newly manufactured advanced robotic devices and power inverters made in other countries; it does not stop the import or sale of any products that have already been approved by the FCC. title: Why Small Businesses Should Hire an AI Digital Marketing Agency in 2026
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Small business owners have always had to do more with less. Limited budgets, limited time, and usually one or two people wearing the marketing hat alongside five other jobs. That’s exactly why the shift toward AI-driven marketing matters more for small businesses than it does for big brands with entire departments to throw at a problem. A few years ago, the kind of data analysis and targeting precision available today required a specialist team. Now it’s built into the tools an AI digital marketing agency uses as standard practice. That’s a real shift in what’s accessible to a business running on a modest monthly budget. The Budget Problem Small Businesses Actually Face Most small businesses can’t afford to waste money figuring out what works through trial and error. A $2,000 monthly ad budget doesn’t leave much room for a slow three-week testing cycle before you know if a campaign is working. This is where the gap between traditional and AI-assisted marketing shows up most clearly. Traditional campaigns often need weeks of data before a human team can confidently say what’s working. AI-driven tools can flag early performance signals within days, sometimes less, letting an agency shift budget away from underperforming ads before too much money is wasted on them. For a business without room to burn cash on guesswork, that speed translates directly into savings. Targeting That Doesn’t Waste Impressions on the Wrong People Broad targeting — age range, general location, general interest categories — was standard for years because it was the best tool available. It still works, but it’s inefficient. You end up paying to show ads to a lot of people who were never going to buy anything from you. An AI marketing agency typically builds more specific audience profiles using behavioral signals: recent searches, site visits, engagement with similar businesses. A local bakery, for example, doesn’t need to reach everyone within a 10-mile radius. They need to reach people who’ve recently searched for catering, custom cakes, or local dessert options. That precision keeps cost per lead lower, which matters a lot more when your budget is tight. Content That’s Backed by Actual Search Demand Small businesses often struggle with content because it’s time-consuming and the return isn’t always obvious. Writing blog posts or social content without knowing if anyone is actually searching for that topic is a gamble most small teams can’t afford to keep making. AI research tools change that by showing what people are actually searching for before any content gets written. This doesn’t replace good writing — a person still needs to shape the message so it actually connects with readers — but it means the topics chosen have a real chance of getting found, instead of being a guess. Reporting That Actually Makes Sense One of the more frustrating parts of working with a traditional agency, especially for a first-time client, is getting a report full of numbers with no clear connection to actual business results. Impressions and click-through rates don’t mean much if you can’t tell whether they led to paying customers. Agencies using AI-driven reporting tools can usually connect specific campaigns to actual revenue outcomes — which keyword, which ad, which email brought in a sale. For a small business owner trying to decide where next month’s budget should go, that clarity makes the decision a lot easier. What Changes When You Switch to an AI-Driven Agency Business owners who’ve made this switch usually notice a few consistent changes within the first couple of months: Faster answers. Instead of waiting for a monthly report to find out if something worked, updates come sooner and adjustments happen in real time. Lower wasted spend. Budget shifts toward what’s converting instead of sitting in an underperforming campaign for weeks. More specific targeting. Ads reach people who are actually likely to buy, not just people who technically fit a broad demographic. Clearer priorities. Content and campaign decisions are based on actual demand data instead of guesswork. None of this requires an enterprise-level budget. Most of these tools are already built into standard advertising and marketing platforms — the difference is in how an agency uses them. Questions to Ask Before Switching Agencies If you’re a small business owner considering a change, a few direct questions can save you from a disappointing decision: How quickly will I know if a campaign isn’t working? Can you explain how your targeting is different from standard demographic targeting? How does your reporting connect to actual sales, not just clicks? Who reviews content or campaign decisions before they go live? A good agency will answer these clearly and with specifics. Vague answers usually mean the “AI” branding is more marketing language than an actual process. Is It Worth the Switch? For most small businesses already spending money on digital ads or content, the answer is generally yes — not because AI is trendy, but because faster testing and sharper targeting tend to save money that would otherwise go toward slow trial and error. The size of the benefit depends on your current setup. A business still relying on broad, untargeted campaigns will likely see the biggest difference. The goal isn’t to chase every new tool that comes out. It’s finding an agency that uses a handful of proven ones well, paired with people who know how to read the data and make smart calls with it. title: Maps of Devastating European Wildfires and Their Response
author: editor
excerpt: Over 300,000 people have been forced to flee their homes as wildfires rage throughout France and Spain. While officials in Madrid, the capital of Spain, claim that the fires are the worst the region has ever seen, France has witnessed its worst in twenty years. It comes after a scorching summer that saw temperatures climb above 40C (104F) in several parts of Europe due to heatwaves. Authorities believe that several wildfires in the areas outside of Madrid have burned an area greater than Madrid itself, totaling around 297 square miles (770 square kilometers). Over 200,000 people have been displaced from their homes in Gironde, the region surrounding Bordeaux, which is the most severely hit in France. In less than four days, the fire has burned over 162 square miles (420 square kilometers), an area around four times the size of Paris. The fire has expanded quickly, tearing across fields and forests in France’s renowned wine region. The distance from Bordeaux’s south is now only nine miles (15 km). Numerous important military and industrial locations in the region, such as those involved in the production of French ballistic missiles, rocket motors, and hazardous chemical processing, have also been put in danger by the fires. Large tracts of burned, scorched ground may be seen on satellite photography above Gironde, with smoke moving eastward inland. content:
A travel ban is the single most effective debt enforcement tool in the Kingdom, and the most feared. It is enforced at every exit point — airports, land borders, and seaports — so a person subject to one simply cannot leave until the matter is resolved.

This guide explains how a debt-related travel ban actually works, how to check whether one exists against you, how to get it lifted, and — if you are the creditor — how it becomes available to you.

We have written it for both sides, because both sides usually misunderstand the same three things.

Misunderstanding 1: The Bank Did Not Ban You. The Court Did.

This trips up almost everyone.

For a civil financial travel ban, the issuing authority is always the court. The bank or creditor is the petitioner — the party that asked. The court issues the order, and it is registered through the Ministry of Interior system.

Why this matters practically: if you call the bank demanding they “remove the ban,” you are calling the wrong party. The bank can confirm the debt is settled, but only the court can lift the order. Knowing the sequence saves weeks.

The typical sequence runs:

  1. The creditor files an enforcement case at the Execution Court.
  2. The court issues its decision.
  3. The creditor petitions for a travel ban as an enforcement measure.
  4. The court registers the ban through the Ministry of Interior system.

Misunderstanding 2: It Does Not Expire

An immigration or administrative restriction — an unpaid fine, a visa violation — clears once the underlying fee is settled.

A civil court financial travel ban has no automatic expiry date. It remains active until the underlying debt is fully paid or resolved through a court-approved arrangement. Waiting does not help. Time does not run it out.

This is precisely why it works as an enforcement tool, and why our enforcement services treat it as one of the most reliable routes to actual payment.

Misunderstanding 3: You May Not Be Told

Many people discover a ban at the airport, not before it.

Discovering it at the border is materially worse than discovering it at home. A person stopped at departure may be held while the creditor is notified and the enforcement process takes over. Resolving from that position is harder, more expensive, and considerably more stressful than resolving it in advance.

If you have any unresolved debt in the Kingdom, check before you book.

How to Check Your Travel Ban Status

There are two official channels, and you should use both, because they show different things.

Absher — the broad check.

  1. Log in at absher.sa with your National ID or Iqama number.
  2. Go to My Services → Queries → Generalization Report Query.
  3. Submit.

The report shows whether a restriction exists. Where a ban is present, the reason is generally shown. Note what Absher will tell you: it shows a court restriction, not a “bank restriction” — again, because the court is the issuer.

Najiz — the specific check.

Absher tells you a ban exists. Najiz (najiz.sa) tells you which case caused it. The case record shows the case number, the plaintiff — that is your creditor — and the claim amount.

You need this detail before you can do anything, because you cannot negotiate with a creditor you have not identified.

For workers whose restriction may arise from an employment matter rather than a debt, labour-related status and Huroob reports are checked through the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development channels, the Absher portal, or the Muqeem platform.

How to Get a Debt Travel Ban Lifted

A ban is generally lifted where the underlying obligation is resolved. Recognised routes include:

Pay the debt. The obvious route, with one very useful wrinkle covered below.

Deposit the sum with the court. Where the debtor deposits the amount with the court as a deposit, the prohibition decision may be lifted.

Settle with the creditor. Negotiate a settlement, payment plan, or restructuring directly with the identified creditor, then apply to the court for lifting on the creditor’s confirmation that the debt is resolved or secured.

Court-approved instalments or a bank guarantee. Where full payment is genuinely not possible, these arrangements can unlock the position.

Withdrawal of the original claim. If a decision is issued to withdraw the original lawsuit, the ban falls away with it.

Then apply formally. The Ministry of Justice provides an online service allowing an enforcement debtor to apply for the lifting of a travel ban restriction, accessible through the Najiz portal. This is the formal pathway once the underlying matter is resolved.

The Frozen Account Trap — And the Way Out

Here is the situation that traps people, and the solution most do not know exists.

The Execution Court often freezes the debtor’s bank accounts and imposes the travel ban together. The debtor then reasons: I cannot pay the debt, because the account I would pay from is frozen. Deadlock.

It is not a deadlock. The Ministry of Justice provides a SADAD invoice service for enforcement debtors through the Najiz portal. It generates a SADAD payment reference, letting the debt be paid through any Saudi bank’s platform, ATM, or payment terminal — without needing access to the frozen account.

Two further points that matter for people outside the Kingdom:

  • The service is accessible using a National ID or Iqama number, and does not require Absher access or a Saudi mobile number.
  • For former residents who have lost Absher access — often because a deactivated SIM means the OTP no longer works — a Saudi lawyer holding a power of attorney can generate the SADAD invoice through Najiz on the debtor’s behalf. See our guide on how to issue a power of attorney.

Do Not Book Flights Until You Have Verified Removal

Lifting is not always instant across every system. After the debt is resolved:

  1. Take the settlement documents to the court that issued the ban and obtain clearance.
  2. Allow processing time for the removal to reflect across systems.
  3. Re-check Absher and Najiz before booking.

Keep the documentation. Where a ban existed and was lifted, the Najiz record will show the resolved status — and a printed record is often required later by foreign visa authorities who encountered the earlier restriction in their own systems.

Exceptions

There are narrow exceptions. Where a person subject to a ban becomes seriously ill and must travel outside the Kingdom for treatment, travel may be permitted on the issuance of a report from the Ministry of Health.

If You Are the Creditor

Everything above is the reason a travel ban is worth pursuing.

Unlike a judgment that sits unenforced, a travel ban directly affects the debtor’s daily life and has no expiry. It is frequently what converts a paper right into payment. Combined with account freezing and asset seizure, it is the core of practical recovery in the Kingdom.

We pursue these measures for businesses, banks, and financial institutions as part of our debt collection services in Saudi Arabia, covering local and cross-border recovery through our TCM Group partnership across 120+ countries. For company-to-company claims see our B2B debt collection service. If your debtor gave you a cheque that bounced, you are in an even stronger position — see our guide to a bounced cheque in Saudi Arabia.

Whichever Side You Are On

If you are a debtor, act before you are stopped at a border. If you are a creditor, understand that this measure exists and is available to you.

Either way, identify the case on Najiz first — everything else follows from knowing the case number and the parties. You can view our full range of legal services in Saudi Arabia, or if you are still comparing firms, read our guide to the top 10 law firms in Saudi Arabia.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Who Issues A Travel Ban For Debt In Saudi Arabia?

The court issues it. For civil financial travel bans the creditor or bank is only the petitioner — the party that applies — while the Execution Court makes the order, which is then registered through the Ministry of Interior system. This is why a bank cannot lift a ban on its own.

2. Does A Debt Travel Ban In Saudi Arabia Expire?

No. A civil court financial travel ban has no automatic expiry date and remains active until the underlying debt is fully paid or resolved through a court-approved arrangement. This differs from an administrative immigration restriction, which clears once the outstanding fee or violation is settled.

3. How Do I Check If I Have A Travel Ban In Saudi Arabia?

Use both official channels. On Absher, log in with your National ID or Iqama and run My Services → Queries → Generalization Report Query for the broad check. Then use the Najiz portal to identify the specific case, which shows the case number, the plaintiff, and the claim amount.

4. How Do I Lift A Travel Ban For Debt?

Resolve the underlying obligation — by paying, depositing the sum with the court, agreeing a settlement or court-approved instalment plan, or providing a bank guarantee — then apply through the Ministry of Justice enforcement debtor service on the Najiz portal for the ban to be lifted. A ban also falls away if the original claim is withdrawn.

5. Can I Pay The Debt If My Bank Account Is Frozen?

Yes. The Ministry of Justice provides a SADAD invoice service for enforcement debtors through the Najiz portal, generating a payment reference that can be settled at any Saudi bank platform, ATM, or payment terminal without using the frozen account. It is accessible with a National ID or Iqama number.

6. Can Someone Outside Saudi Arabia Resolve A Travel Ban?

Yes. The Najiz portal can be accessed with a National ID or Iqama number, and where a former resident has lost Absher access because a deactivated SIM no longer receives the OTP, a Saudi lawyer holding a power of attorney can act on their behalf, including generating the SADAD invoice.

7. What Happens If I Try To Travel With An Active Ban?

Travel bans are enforced at airports, land borders, and seaports. A person stopped at departure may be held while the creditor is notified and enforcement proceeds. Resolving the matter from that position is significantly harder and more costly than checking and resolving it in advance.

8. Is There Any Exception To A Travel Ban?

There are narrow exceptions. Where a person subject to a ban becomes seriously ill and needs treatment outside the Kingdom, travel may be permitted on the issuance of a report from the Ministry of Health.

title: The Third Drone in Three Days is Shot Down by Romanian Military
author: editor
excerpt: Romanian President Nicușor Dan has declared that Romanian soldiers have shot down a third drone in just three days, adding to the nation’s history of drone-related events. Dan stated in a social media post that at around 10:13 a.m. on Sunday, an F-16 fighter jet from the Romanian air force had intercepted a drone over Romanian territorial seas. According to reports, the incident happened near the Ukrainian border in the Sulina–Chilia region of the Danube Delta.Dan wrote on X, I would like to congratulate the Romanian pilots and ground crews on their professionalism, bravery, and efficiency in carrying out their missions.” An F-16 shot down another unmanned aerial object on Saturday morning, around 10 kilometers west of the eastern Romanian village of Sfěu Gheorghe, according to Romanian authorities. The drone was “safely shot down in an unpopulated area near the border,” according to a statement released by the Romanian Defense Ministry on Saturday, after two jets scrambled to locate and intercept the target. Around 11 a.m. on Friday, a Romanian F-16 shot down a third drone. According to Romanian officials, the drone that was caught on Friday was identified by the Romanian Prosecutor General’s Office as being of the Shahed kind, which was employed by Russian forces in their conflict with Ukraine. title: Where are the Highest Earners in France Heading, and Why are They Leaving?
author: editor
excerpt: Is France expelling a large number of its wealthy? According to the most recent Henley & Partners Wealth Migration Report, 800 millionaires left France in 2025. The wealthiest appear to be leaving the country, at first glance. For comparison, the UBS Global Wealth Report states that 2.4 million people in France still have a net worth of more than €1 million. Although France’s quality of life and joie de vivre continue to make it a desirable place for the wealthy to reside, there is a general trend—albeit little at the moment—that some of the country’s wealthiest citizens are relocating and, more crucially, bringing their capital with them. According to the French Institute for Research on Public Administration and Politics (iFRAP), each millionaire who left the country last year took with them an average of €5 million in personal assets, or about €4 billion. Economists note that even a relatively small number of high-net-worth individuals can have an outsized economic impact because they frequently own businesses, fund investments, and generate significant tax revenues, even though the number of departing millionaires represents only a small portion of France’s wealthy population. author: editor

author: editor

title: The EU Fined Google €890 Million for Preferring its Own Apps Over Rivals
author: editor
excerpt: The EU penalized Google €890 million (£759 million) for allegedly abusing its dominance by preferring its own apps and services over those of competitors. It is the first major action taken against the digital behemoth under the EU’s Digital Markets Act (DMA), a historic regulation aimed at limiting the influence of the world’s largest tech giants. The Commission argued that Google’s practices restricted consumer choice and gave its own services an unfair advantage over competitors. The corporation criticized the decision, claiming the EU’s restrictions could harm services used by millions of European customers. To comply, we must remove real-time Search features that Europeans value, such as instant pricing and direct availability for hotels, flights, and restaurants, as well as dismantle Google Play safety protections,” said Kent Walker, Google’s president of global affairs. EU authorities rejected that claim, stating that the measures are necessary to prevent dominating platforms from undercutting competitors. Google received a total punishment for two distinct DMA violations. The European Commission imposed a €460 million penalty after discovering that Google favored its own services for helping people book flights and hotels over competitors in search results. title: Tankers Conduct fast U-Turns Following Houthi Shipping Threat
author: editor
excerpt: At least seven oil tankers have made U-turns near Yemen since the Iran-linked Houthi group declared a “maritime embargo” against Saudi Arabia on Monday, according to ship-tracking data. All of the ships were on their way to or from Saudi ports when the embargo was declared, and they changed course abruptly. Nearly 15% of world sea traffic passes through the Red Sea, which connects the Mediterranean and Gulf of Aden via two choke points: the Suez Canal in Egypt and the Bab al-Mandab Strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa. The Red Sea has been a crucial conduit for Saudi oil exports since the US-Israeli conflict with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, drastically restricting the flow of oil and gas from the Gulf. This has played a “major role in relieving pressure on global markets,” and if the Houthis continue to restrict trade, “prices will rise,” according to Rosemary Kelanic of the US-based Defence Priorities think tank. According to maritime intelligence firm Kpler, 20 vessels entered the Red Sea the day before the Houthis launched their blockade, while 22 withdrew via the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. title: Despite Argentina’s World Cup Defeat, Thousands Welcome Home the Team Without Messi
author: editor
excerpt: Following their World Cup final defeat to Spain, the Argentine football team returned home without star Lionel Messi, but thousands of supporters braved the cold and rain on Monday to give them a euphoric welcome. Four years after millions celebrated their team’s tournament victory in 2022, it was not the homecoming Argentines had dreamed for, but new scenes of ecstatic anarchy filled the street as they danced, sung, and let off fireworks to thank the players. The legendary team captain Messi was not seen getting off the plane in pictures shown on local television, and the Argentine Football Association (AFA) had previously announced that some team members would not be traveling. A military band and a crimson carpet greeted coach Lionel Scaloni and the team. After that, they got on a bus and waved to ecstatic fans as they went. “Argentines will celebrate anyway,” said housewife Marga Ledezma, despite not winning a second consecutive championship. The 36-year-old hailed Messi for “all the years he made us happy,” encouraging him to continue playing for Argentina but acknowledging that it would be challenging given his advanced age of 39. Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in a match that has drawn criticism from the international media due to the Albiceleste’s numerous fouls and acts of poor sportsmanship. Despite Argentina’s World Cup defeat, thousands welcome home the team without Messi. On Monday, the Argentine Football Association (AFA) training camp in Ezeiza, Buenos Aires Province, is approached by a bus carrying the Argentina national football team. AFP “I think they criticize us because we know what it’s like to suffer, that we get up, we fall down again, and we keep going,” said Ledezma. In view of the ongoing conflict between the two nations over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands, many supporters emphasized that Argentina’s 2-1 victory against England in the semifinals was the true triumph. title: If the Hormuz Attacks Continue, the US “Will Target Iran’s Bridges and Power Plants
author: editor
excerpt: In the event that Iranian forces attack a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, President Donald Trump has threatened to destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant. In a post on Truth Social, he stated that potential targets would include those “located next to, or in,” Tehran, the country’s capital. Any attack on shipping in the crucial waterway, “whether it be by missile, rocket, drone, or any other device or weapon,” would result in a military response. His ultimatum comes after Tehran warned the US not to target its nuclear facilities after the US launched strikes on Iran for the eleventh night in a row. The strikes were “designed to continue degrading Iran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping” in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US Central Command (Centcom). Tehran, the country’s capital, had its air defenses activated, according to Iranian state media. Additionally, there have been reports of explosions in the southern city of Bushehr, which is home to Iran’s sole nuclear power facility, the northwest city of Tabriz, and the southeast ports of Chabahar and Konarak. A ceasefire between Iran and the United States was reached in April, but fighting broke out again this week as both nations fought for control of the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway. According to Centcom, US forces have targeted Iranian military logistics infrastructure, aircraft hangars, drone storage facilities, maritime capabilities, and military operations centers. Additionally, it claimed that during the previous three months, Iran had attacked “more than 30 commercial vessels” traveling through the Strait of Hormuz.It stated that the channel was still “open for commercial vessel transit” and that the unjustified attacks had compromised freedom of navigation and put hundreds of innocent seamen in danger. title: As Trump Announces 50% Tariffs on Canada, Carney is Considering “all Options
author: editor
excerpt: In retribution for what he described as “unequal treatment” of US autos, dairy products, and alcohol, US President Donald Trump has levied a 50% duty on a variety of commodities imported from Canada. The target list includes both industrial products like cement and common consumer goods like wine and hockey sticks. However, a number of important exports—such as electricity, potash, vital minerals, and fish will be spared. title: Following Israel’s Withdrawal, the Lebanese Army Claims its Troops are Moving into a “Pilot Zone
author: editor
excerpt: According to Lebanon’s army, its soldiers have started moving to a “pilot zone” in the country’s south after Israeli forces withdrew as part of a deal mediated by the United States last month. Units entered the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh in the Nabatieh district on Tuesday morning, according to a statement from the army command. The pilot zone proposal, which calls for the disarmament of the Iran-backed organization and the withdrawal of Israeli troops from a tiny portion of the region they have seized during their fight with Hezbollah, was confirmed by Israel’s military on Monday night. It takes place before US President Donald Trump and his Lebanese counterpart, Joseph Aoun, meet in Washington. Aoun is anticipated to exert pressure on Trump to force Israel to leave the remainder of southern Lebanon and to help the Lebanese army seize complete control of regions controlled by Hezbollah. In accordance with the Trilateral Framework agreement between Israel, Lebanon, and the US, the US State Department declared on Monday afternoon that “pilot zone operations” had started in Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh and two additional Lebanese villages, Froun and Srifa. It claimed that talks between Israeli and Lebanese delegates in Rome last week directly led to the “milestone.” The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) will “adjust its force posture in one of the pilot areas” to enable the Lebanese army to fulfill its mission while simultaneously “safeguarding the security of IDF soldiers and preserving its right to self-defence and to remove threats,” an Israeli military official confirmed later on Monday. title: The EU Fined AliExpress a Record €550 Million for Permitting the Sale of illicit Goods
author: editor
excerpt: The EU penalized the massive Chinese online retailer AliExpress a record €550 million (£467 million) for permitting the sale of illicit goods such dangerous toys and counterfeit clothing. AliExpress has failed to “diligently assess” the risk of illicit, dangerous, or counterfeit items on its platform, according to the European Commission. According to EU tech director Henna Virkkunen, “the spread of fake clothes, dangerous toys, hazardous cosmetics, and other illegal and harmful products is not an inevitable cost of online shopping; it is a failure by AliExpress to comply with its obligations.” AliExpress declared that the fine was “disproportionate” and that it would file an appeal. AliExpress’s detection systems “did not work properly,” according to the two-year inquiry, with many illicit products going unreported and others that were discovered remaining on the website for several weeks. The European Commission also discovered that the business failed to adequately penalize vendors who sold illicit goods. Its product conformity tests could also be “easily circumvented. With 193 million users in Europe, AliExpress, owned by the Chinese tech giant Alibaba, has more consumers than Shein or Temu, two other Chinese online merchants. author: editor
excerpt: In defiance of a police ban, thousands of members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led protest movement seeking employment and education reforms, attempted to march on parliament to demand the resignation of India’s education minister. title: Ryanair’s Earnings Decline as the War in Iran Deters Travelers and Raises Fuel Prices
author: editor
excerpt: The Middle East conflict has caused jet fuel prices to increase and passengers to be reluctant to book flights, which has resulted in a dramatic decline in Ryanair’s profitability. Between April and June, the Irish airline’s pre-tax profits fell 34% to €593 million (£503 million), although revenues remained unchanged as the carrier was compelled to lower tickets in order to boost demand. Additionally, Ryanair stated that because of “consumer hesitancy” around air travel, it anticipates summer fares to be marginally lower than they were last year. Since the US and Israel began attacking Iran in February, the cost of fueling an aircraft has increased dramatically. Although Ryanair claimed to have “hedged” or made agreements for the majority of future fuel expenses, those not covered by these agreements had more than doubled. Following a weekend of intensive gunfire between the US and Iran, crude oil prices reached $90 (£67) per barrel for the first time in a month on Monday before marginally declining. The Strait of Hormuz, a vital gateway for the world’s supply of gas and oil, is completely closed. Oil and energy prices saw a brief reprieve last month due to an interim ceasefire agreement, but they surged once more when talks broke down and hostilities restarted. The airline cautioned that its annual results will be “highly sensitive” to external factors such as the expansion of the Middle East and Ukraine conflicts and the cost of unhedged jet fuel. title: Deadly Ukrainian Strikes Target Russian Online Retail Warehouses
author: editor
excerpt: According to Russian officials, Ukrainian drones attacked two warehouses owned by Russia’s largest online store, Wildberries, resulting in eight fatalities and sixty-two injuries. A warehouse in the city of Tambov, some 295 miles (475 km) southeast of Moscow, resulted in seven fatalities and 25 injuries. At another Wildberries facility near Elektrostal in the Moscow area, there was one fatality and thirty-seven injuries. According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, “major logistics facilities” that were utilized to “supply sanctioned components for drone production and navigation equipment” were hit by the assaults. Additionally, he said, Ukraine has attacked targets in the Black Sea, the Sea of Azov, and Russian-annexed Crimea. Images from one of the warehouse strikes showed dozens of workers fleeing into a parking lot while flames and massive plumes of black smoke rose from a large logistics building. Some films show injured and scared employees trying to escape while the explosions continue, suggesting that the attacks began at night. Another video seems to show a warehouse’s walls collapsing as flames consume them. According to Zelensky, “Russian strikes on our civilian infrastructure and on our cities and communities” were the reason behind Ukraine’s actions. 14 people were killed in Russian assaults throughout Ukraine overnight and into Wednesday. Many people refer to wildberries as the Russian version of Amazon. title: China “Firmly Opposes” British Steel’s Nationalization by the UK
author: editor
excerpt: China’s Ministry of Commerce issued a statement on Friday denouncing the UK’s decision to nationalize British Steel, stating that it “firmly opposes and is strongly dissatisfied with the British government’s decision” and cautioning that the action had undermined Chinese companies’ confidence in investing in the UK. The British government declared on Thursday that it will take control of the losing business in order to preserve jobs and a “vital national capability.” After Jingye contemplated shutting down the plant’s blast furnaces, the UK government assumed operational control of British Steel’s Scunthorpe operations in 2025. However, the government’s power to decide the company’s future was limited because the Chinese group continued to own it. British Steel has been losing money for years prior to its purchase by Jingye, according to a statement released by China’s Ministry of Commerce on Friday. Jingye made a significant investment in the business after the acquisition, which allowed it to continue operating and maintain employment. The ministry charged that the UK was using national security as an excuse to seize control of and nationalize the business while ignoring Jingye’s contribution to the British economy and society. title: Tamás Sulyok, the President of Hungary, Signs a Constitutional Change That Terminates his Own Term
author: editor
excerpt: The seventeenth amendment to Hungary’s Fundamental Law has been signed by Tamás Sulyok, ending his own term as the republic’s president. The head of state called the constitutional modification that forced his resignation “unprecedented and shameful” in a Facebook speech.This amendment ends the current President of the Republic’s tenure in office with a single sentence. That sentence adds to the list of coerced Gordian-knot solutions that will go down in history as serious and disgraceful instances of political power abuse, he said. The statute that forced him to leave was harshly criticized by the departing head of state, who described it as an unprecedented restriction on the right to vote and an open assault on the independence of institutions and the rule of law. He signed the amendment after realizing that it would be illegal to refuse to do so. “My signature is the final seal of my presidential obligations and of my full and unconditional respect for the institution of the presidency,” he said. It indicates that I have never broken Hungary’s Fundamental Law and have always complied with it. However, it will also serve as enduring evidence that the fundamental principles of a democratic society—the separation of powers, democracy, and the rule of law—have been subverted for the sake of power. The power that modified the constitution has sole responsibility for this decision, the leaving Sulyok stated. title: Trump Media Plans to sell Speedier Access to Major Market-Moving Social Media Posts
author: editor
excerpt: On Thursday, US President Donald Trump’s media organization, Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), announced plans to develop a subscription service that will provide financial institutions with real-time access to posts from various high-ranking Truth Social accounts. Trump is Truth Social’s most well-known user and the majority shareholder in its publicly traded parent business. It is now his preferred forum for making significant announcements, but selling high-speed access raises new issues about Trump’s ability to monetize the presidency. TMTG did not specify whose accounts will be featured or confirm whether Trump’s posts would be included of the service. However, the business branded the service’s content as the platform’s “most market-moving Truths” and stated that “markets already move on Truth Social posts”. It also did not specify whether subscribers would receive posts before they appeared publicly on Truth Social. The solution, according to the company, will transmit posts to clients “in milliseconds”, eliminating the need for manual monitoring. TMTG stated that the new service, Truth API, will give a direct, machine-readable feed to high-frequency and algorithmic trading firms that rely on obtaining market-moving information as rapidly as possible. title: Chip Giant TSMC Promises to Increase US Production by an Additional $100 Billion
author: editor
excerpt: As it increases its production in the US, Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC plans to invest an additional $100 billion (£74 billion) in Arizona. TSMC is now the most valuable firm in Asia thanks to the high demand for its semiconductors. title: Public Ownership of British Steel to Safeguard Vital” UK Supplies
author: editor
excerpt: The government claimed that taking British Steel into public control would preserve “a vital national capability” and jobs. In recent years, uncertainty has plagued the future of the steelworks, which support numerous other businesses in north Lincolnshire and employ about 2,700 people in Scunthorpe. Although British Steel was still owned by China’s Jingye Group, the UK government had taken over its activities in Scunthorpe last year, which limited the government’s authority to determine its future course of action. Nationalization keeps the blast furnaces operating while buying the government time and granting it the authority and freedom to determine the plant’s future. In the end, the government is unlikely to want to continue running a company that costs it more than a million pounds per day. The Scunthorpe steelworks were costing the government almost £1.3 million per day, according to a report published in March by the National Audit Office. The nationalization followed the passage of legislation by Parliament on Wednesday that permitted the government to take public ownership of the steel industry in situations where it satisfied a public interest test. Jingye, which earlier said it was losing £700,000 per day, is requesting compensation for nationalization. Jingye has not responded to the announcement made on Thursday, according to the BBC.
