title: China’s Economic Growth Drastically Declines, Falling Short of Expectations
author: editor
excerpt: Between the beginning of April and the end of June, China’s economic growth drastically slowed as the country’s robust exports were overshadowed by poor domestic demand and the impact of the Iran War on oil prices. According to official GDP data, the second-largest economy in the world expanded by 4.3% in the second quarter, falling short of Beijing’s yearly goal and following a 5% increase in the first. It occurs one day after independent data revealed that China’s exports increased by 27% in June over the same month last year. China’s growth objective was lowered to a range of 4.5% to 5% in March, its lowest goal for economic expansion since 1991. According to some observers, this change has allowed Beijing to admit the country’s pre-existing economic weakness. As China was coming out of its severe Covid-19 limitations, the announcement reflects the lowest quarterly expansion since the end of 2022 and the first complete quarter of GDP statistics since the commencement of the Iran conflict on February 28.In a statement that accompanied the data, China’s National Bureau of Statistics stated, “There are more external instability and uncertainty factors.” It also pointed out that the domestic economy’s robust supply and weak demand were out of balance. Beijing’s domestic economic problems, such as a protracted decline in the real estate market and low consumer expenditure, were brought to light by separate data that was made public on Wednesday. title: A Bill Allowing Assisted Dying for Certain Terminally ill Adults is Passed by the French Parliament
author: editor
excerpt: On Wednesday, French lawmakers approved a bill granting certain terminally ill persons the right to assisted suicide under stringent guidelines. With 291 votes in favor and 241 against, the lower house supported the legislation. The measure still has to be reviewed by the nation’s highest constitutional authority. With its enactment, France becomes one of eleven nations with assisted dying legislation, each with its own set of regulations. One of the main promises of French President Emmanuel Macron’s second five-year term was the law, which he referred to as “the French model for end-of-life care.” There was only one way to address a deeply sensitive problem that touches on life, pain, and dignity: listening, talking, and debating. Many French citizens have visited neighboring nations where euthanasia and assisted suicide are permitted. The main feature of the bill is medically assisted suicide, which permits qualified individuals to obtain and, under certain restrictions, self-administer fatal medicine. A doctor or nurse would only be able to help individuals who were physically incapable of doing so. Patients who wish to terminate their lives must be French nationals or lawful residents of France and be at least eighteen years old. title: Trump Claims That ICE Should Carry out Traffic Stops Following Shootings, Seemingly Going Against New Policy
author: editor
excerpt: In apparent defiance of a new regulation banning the practice, US President Donald Trump stated that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) should carry out traffic stops in the wake of recent deadly shootings. ICE is “doing a GREAT job, one that has to be done,” Trump posted on his social media platform early on Wednesday. We must be strong, tough, and smart and we CANNOT give up one of ICE’s most important and effective Crime Fighting tools, THE TRAFFIC STOP!” Trump declares in an attempt to deport criminals he claims were allowed entry into the nation during the previous Democratic administration. Following two fatal shootings by ICE officers, ICE banned the use of traffic stops to apprehend immigrants on Tuesday, according to media sources. Spark Behind the Vision Entrepreneur Mirror: Could you tell us about your professional journey and what inspired you to develop the True Story Method? Gergana Valcheva: My journey began in Bulgaria, but the life and career I have today were built across borders. I moved to the Netherlands immediately after high school, at eighteen, to study International Business and Management with a major in marketing. It was a defining step. I had to build a new life, learn to navigate a different culture, and discover who I was away from everything familiar. I later spent a year in Canada, where I further specialised in marketing and consumer behaviour. That experience deepened my fascination with why people make certain decisions, what creates trust, and why some messages stay with us while others disappear. Over the past fifteen years, I have worked across international marketing, consumer electronics, technology, e-commerce, engineering, professional services, and personal brands. My experience covers both B2C and B2B marketing, including brand positioning, product marketing, social media strategy, paid advertising, content, influencer collaborations, campaign development, events, and business growth. I have built European brand channels and online communities from zero, including growing a Facebook community beyond 60,000 followers and establishing Instagram and LinkedIn presences from the ground up. I have also organised and managed brand participation at major international events such as IFA Berlin, including press activity that welcomed around 300 journalists in a single day, as well as exclusive lounge events designed to create closer experiences between brands, media, partners, and audiences. Entrepreneur Mirror: You often speak about the Human + AI era. How do you see the relationship between technology and human clarity shaping the future of marketing and brand building?

But AI does not remove the need for human clarity. It increases it.

When a person does not understand their positioning, values, audience, or voice, AI can simply help them produce confusion more efficiently. It may create content that looks professional but does not build recognition, trust, or meaningful demand.

This will also change what audiences value. As synthetic content becomes more common, people will become more sensitive to generic language, manufactured expertise, and communication without real experience behind it. Trust will increasingly come from specificity: original thinking, honest perspective, evidence of practice, and a recognisable human voice.

For founders and personal brands, the question is no longer only, “How can I use AI to create more?” It is, “What should I create, what truth should it carry, and how can AI help me deliver that value more effectively?”

Technology can extend our capabilities. It should not replace our responsibility to think.

My vision for the Human + AI era is not less technology. It is better-directed technology, guided by clearer humans.

Entrepreneur Mirror: Yi Jing-based wisdom plays an important role in your work. Could you share how it influences your approach to decision-making, timing, leadership, and personal brand development?

Gergana Valcheva: Yi Jing, also known as the I Ching or Book of Changes, is rooted in a principle that is both ancient and highly relevant today: change is constant, but change is not always random.

Through my training in Shuyi Culture International and my work with the Asia Yi Jing Cultural Exchange Association, I have learned to approach ancient wisdom as a practical system for self-understanding and better decision-making – not as a replacement for personal responsibility, professional expertise, or action.

I hold a Professional Certification as a Certified Consultant (Chinese Philosophy). For me, this is not a separate identity from my marketing work. It adds depth to how I understand people, timing, leadership, and the choices behind a personal or business direction.

The first dimension is character understanding. People do not all lead, communicate, decide, or build businesses in the same way. When we understand our natural strengths, behavioural patterns, and blind spots, we can make choices that are more aligned with who we really are.

The second is timing. In business and life, a good decision taken at the wrong moment can create unnecessary resistance. Yi Jing wisdom teaches us to observe cycles, recognise periods for initiation, development, adjustment, or consolidation, and act with greater awareness.

The third is leadership. Leadership is not only directing others. It is knowing when to move, when to listen, when to adapt, and when ego is interfering with clarity. Wisdom-led leadership combines conviction with responsiveness.

For personal branding, this becomes especially valuable. Many people build a brand around who they think they should become. I help them understand what is already present: their character, patterns, strengths, purpose, and the lessons their life has prepared them to share.

My stage name, Xiya Wan 万夕雅, represents this wisdom-led dimension of my work, while Gergana Valcheva carries my personal and professional journey. They are not two separate identities. Together, they represent the bridge I am building between modern strategy and timeless wisdom.

Shuyi Culture’s ancient wisdom framework does not tell us to sit and wait for life to happen. It helps us understand ourselves and the conditions around us so that we can participate in change more wisely.

“Shuyi Culture Yi Jing-based wisdom helps us understand ourselves and the conditions around us so that we can participate in change more wisely.”

Xiya Wan, Certified Consultant in Chinese Philosophy and founder of True Story Method

Envisioning the Future

Entrepreneur Mirror: What major changes do you foresee in marketing, social media, and brand positioning over the next few years?

Gergana Valcheva: I believe we are moving from an attention economy toward a trust economy.

Attention will remain important, but it will become easier and cheaper to generate artificial attention through AI, automation, paid distribution, and high-volume content. The more crowded the digital environment becomes, the less attention alone will tell us about real authority or value.

Trust will become the more meaningful differentiator.

First, generic content will lose effectiveness. AI can already reproduce standard advice, polished captions, and familiar formats. Brands will need stronger points of view, better evidence, and more original intellectual property.

Second, personal brands will become increasingly important, even within traditional companies. People want to understand the humans behind the business: how they think, what they believe, and whether their actions match their message.

Third, search behaviour will continue moving beyond traditional search engines. People are already discovering experts, products, and answers through AI-generated summaries, social search, videos, podcasts, and community recommendations. This makes AEO, answer engine optimization, an important extension of SEO. Brands must become easy for both people and machines to understand.

Fourth, social media success will become less dependent on follower size and more dependent on relevance, depth, and conversion. A smaller audience with genuine trust can create more impact than a large but passive following.

Finally, positioning will move from broad claims toward clear category ownership. “I help everyone grow” will become weaker. The brands that stand out will connect a specific audience, problem, method, and perspective in a memorable way.

The future belongs to brands that can answer four questions clearly:
Who are you?
Who are you for?
What do you understand differently?
Why should people trust you?

Tools will continue changing. Those questions will not.

“We are moving from an attention economy toward a trust economy.”

Building Meaningful Visibility with Purpose

Entrepreneur Mirror: What advice would you give to founders, entrepreneurs, and purpose-driven businesses looking to create meaningful visibility and long-term impact?

Gergana Valcheva: Do not begin by asking, “What should I post?”

Start by asking: What do I want to be known for? Whose problem am I uniquely equipped to solve? What truth can I communicate consistently for the next several years?

Meaningful visibility is not the same as being seen everywhere. It is being recognised for something valuable by the right people.

My first advice is to build clarity before volume. Define your positioning, audience, promise, perspective, and proof before increasing content production.

Second, connect strategy with service. The strongest marketing is not built around what you want to say about yourself. It is built around what your audience needs to understand, feel, or do in order to move forward.

Third, create evidence. Share the thinking behind your work, practical examples, lessons, processes, and outcomes. People trust what they can understand and verify.

Fourth, build owned assets. Social media is valuable, but platforms change. Your website, email list, methodology, searchable articles, workshops, and intellectual property give your brand stability beyond algorithms.

Fifth, use AI deliberately. Let it support research, organisation, ideation, and execution, but do not delegate your identity, judgment, or relationship with your audience.

Finally, be patient enough to build trust and courageous enough to remain distinct.

I built my own international life and career step by step – from leaving Bulgaria at eighteen, to studying, and working abroad to building brands across markets, and now creating my own method and body of work. There was no single shortcut. What created progress was the willingness to keep learning, adapt without losing myself, and turn each experience into something useful for others.

Long-term impact is rarely one viral moment. It is the compound effect of clarity, consistency, service, and trust.

“Meaningful visibility is not being seen everywhere. It is being recognised for something valuable by the right people.”

What’s Next for the True Story Method

Entrepreneur Mirror: Looking ahead, what are your plans and aspirations for your work and the impact you hope to create?

Gergana Valcheva: My next chapter is about turning the True Story Method into a complete ecosystem that supports people at different stages of their growth.

At the strategic level, I will continue working directly with founders, professionals, personal brands, and purpose-driven businesses through one-to-one consulting focused on positioning, brand clarity, social media, paid marketing, content, and practical execution. My approach is to meet people where they are – whether they need strategic direction, hands-on implementation support, or a bridge between the two.

I am also developing educational offers that make this knowledge more accessible. These include AI Freedom, Instagram Mastery, Custom Xiya AI for social media content creation, and other practical digital resources that help people use AI and social media with more clarity, confidence, and independence.

Through Shuyi Culture International and the Asia Yi Jing Cultural Exchange Association, I am also sharing experiences such as the Self-Discovery workshop and ‘Orchestration of Life’ program. These help people understand their strengths, patterns, timing, relationships, and direction through a grounded application of Yi Jing-based wisdom.

My intention is to make this wisdom more accessible to people in Europe and internationally, while communicating it in a practical way – showing how ancient principles can support modern decisions, self-mastery, leadership, relationships, and business without becoming vague or disconnected from real life.

Over time, I see True Story Method developing into a recognised body of intellectual property: a methodology, educational platform, consultancy, digital-product ecosystem, and community built around one central belief: the strongest growth begins when strategy aligns with self-truth.

I want to help people understand themselves before the world defines them, use technology without becoming dependent on it, and build brands and businesses that reflect both who they are and the value they are capable of creating.

My goal is not only to help people become more visible. It is to help them become more clear, more capable, and more intentional – so that when visibility comes, it has something meaningful to reveal.

“The strongest growth begins when strategy aligns with self-truth.”

title: In a Slander Action, a Singaporean Court Ordered Bloomberg to Reimburse Ministers $356,000
author: editor
excerpt: Two ministers who sued Bloomberg and one of its reporters for defamation over an article mentioning their real estate dealings were awarded S$460,000 ($356,000; £266,000) by a Singaporean court. The ministers K Shanmugam and Tan See Leng filed a lawsuit against Bloomberg and reporter Low De Wei last year over a 2024 article that made reference to their real estate transactions. According to Bloomberg, it used them as examples of a larger trend and did not suggest any illegality. The judge concluded that, taken as a whole, the article suggested misconduct by the ministers because it also referred to money laundering and concealment. The chief editor of Bloomberg News, John Micklethwait, stated that the publication was “very disappointed by this ruling but we will of course respect it” in a statement.We contended during the trial that our reporting was truthful and beneficial to the public interest, and we still think the ministers have given a very strained interpretation to what is a good story,” he stated. The article “Singapore Mansion Deals Are Increasingly Shrouded in Secrecy” examined the methods used by some affluent Singaporean buyers to conceal their purchases of Good Class Bungalows, a class of multimillion-dollar mansions in Singapore, including the use of shell corporations that conceal their identities. title: US Inflation is Being Reduced by Gas Costs, But Will This Trend Continue?
author: editor
excerpt: The cost of energy and gasoline decreased last month, which helped to reduce inflation in the US. However, given the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, it is unclear if this improvement will endure. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that prices increased 3.5% in the year ending in June, compared to 4.2% in May, a greater decline than analysts had anticipated. The price of a barrel of Brent crude, the world standard, increased by $10 in only one day to reach $87 as a result of further US military strikes on Iran this week. The Federal Reserve has “no tolerance to persistently elevated inflation,” according to Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh. In his first hearing before the House Financial Services Committee on Tuesday, he assured Congress that he was dedicated to “restoring price stability” following the impact of the Middle East crisis on prices.”Inflation is a decision,” he asserted. We monetary policymakers need to choose lower prices and that’s the commitment my colleagues have made. According to analysts, inflation may increase in the upcoming months, which might lead the Fed to determine whether to raise or maintain interest rates at their current level. title: Donations to The Bill Gates Charity are Stopped by Billionaire Warren Buffett
author: editor
excerpt: A few weeks after Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates revealed his connections to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, billionaire investor Warren Buffett ceased contributing to Gates’ philanthropic foundation. In 2006, Buffett made a “irrevocable” pledge to donate shares of his company, Berkshire Hathaway, to the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation “throughout my lifetime.” However, the Gates Foundation was excluded from the list of companies that will get stock valued at billions of dollars on Thursday. Instead, the stock will be divided among four Buffett family-affiliated foundations. The 95-year-old stated that he will spend the next eight years selling off his remaining shares.Naturally, mortality is unpredictable,” Buffett remarked. “But my remaining shares will be donated to the four foundations one way or the other by 31 December, 2034.” When materials from the US Department of Justice were made public in January, it became clear that Gates was connected to Epstein. In his comments on his donations, Buffett did not specifically name Gates or Epstein. title: History was Made With the SpaceX IPO. Has it lost Steam after a Month?
author: editor
excerpt: In SpaceX’s first month as a publicly traded business, investor sentiment has fluctuated between celebration and apparent anxiety. There was a frenzy among investors on June 12 when shares in the company, which Elon Musk co-founded and oversaw, were first made available for purchase on the public stock market. The price of the company’s shares soared up to $150 on the first day, reaching $176 before ending at $160.95, despite the company’s decision to price them at $135 each. It made SpaceX the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history. Its shares increased even further the next week, reaching an intraday high of $225, which meant that its total market worth had eclipsed that of Microsoft and Amazon.Any business that Elon Musk touches generates excitement, according to Keith Snyder, an analyst at the investment research firm CFRA. “But this was also the first time people felt like they were able to invest in something that was being marketed as an AI play.” Willy Lee, an investor at Neosteller, a company that helps individual investors invest in private firms, concurred that artificial intelligence (AI) was a major factor in the excitement around the IPO. title: 51 People are Killed in Bangladesh Due to Flash Floods and Heavy Rainfall
author: editor
excerpt: In recent days, Bangladesh’s torrential rains has harmed over a million people and killed at least 51. Flash floods and landslides have devastated much of the nation, including the capital city of Dhaka, causing thousands of people to lose their homes. Cox’s Bazar, which has a sizable Rohingya refugee community, has seen more than half of the deaths to date. When floodwaters surged through the district’s school last week, a teacher and many pupils perished. Bangladesh is a low-lying nation with several rivers. During its yearly monsoon season, it frequently experiences heavy rain and flooding. However, experts caution that rainfall has increased in frequency and intensity due to climate change. Authorities issued warnings about floods and landslides, evacuated people in high-risk locations, and postponed student exams as the heavy rain, which started more than a week ago, got worse in recent days. There are currently thousands of people residing in government shelters. As of Sunday, authorities reported that the rain had impacted over a million people. Cox’s Bazar has accounted for 28 of the 51 deaths that have been documented thus far. Over a million Rohingya, who make up the largest refugee community in the world, live in the region. title: As Tensions Over the Strait of Hormuz Increase, the US And Iran Trade Fire
author: editor
excerpt: As a dispute over control of the Strait of Hormuz threatens to sabotage diplomatic efforts to end their war, the US and Iran have exchanged another round of attacks. In an effort to make it more difficult for Iranian forces to strike commercial ships in the vital Gulf waterway, the US military claimed to have struck dozens of targets overnight. Two people were killed, according to Iranian media. The Revolutionary Guards of Iran later claimed to have assaulted US military installations in Kuwait, Jordan, Bahrain, and Oman, where officials claimed to have intercepted projectiles. Iran declared it has closed the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. However, the US maintained that traffic was flowing and that it was not under Iranian control. According to information from the website MarineTraffic, a few ships seemed to be passing through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday even though traffic was still prohibited. The tentative agreement that the United States and Iran struck in June to terminate their four-month confrontation and reopen the strait—through which around 20% of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) typically pass has come under scrutiny due to the increasing attacks. Due to the resumed hostilities, the price of crude oil increased by more than 2% on Monday. title: US Pays $3m to Victims of Mysterious ‘Havana Syndrome’ Revealed by Spies
author: editor
excerpt: The US government has compensated victims of the enigmatic neurological disorder known as “Havana Syndrome,” which has been reported by spies, diplomats, and their families, for almost $3 million (£2.2 million). In connection with the disease, which CIA operatives stationed in the Cuban capital initially reported ten years ago, the reimbursements are the first to be provided to US agency employees. Since then, “anomalous health incidents” have been recorded by American employees stationed abroad, especially in China. A low hum, clicks, squeals, and “grinding metal” have all been reported by sufferers, while others have experienced severe pressure on the skull, lightheadedness, and nausea. The US Department of Defense announced the compensation, which was paid out in accordance with the Havana Act, which was passed into law in 2021, and stated that it will continue to give “the care of affected personnel” top priority. For many years, there has been a lot of conjecture about what causes Havana Syndrome and who is to blame. Some have suggested that microwaves are the cause of the illness, which has led to additional conjecture that a foreign force may have attacked US employees and their dependents abroad using a sonar weapon. title: Will American Children Benefit from Trump Accounts?
author: editor
excerpt: The Wall Street opening bell was ringed in the Oval Office this week to commemorate the debut of Trump Accounts, a new savings program designed to encourage investing among American youth. However, some are skeptical that the project will live up to the expectations and succeed in providing new generations with a stake in the so-called American dream. All US children under 18 can now open savings accounts, and kids born between 2025 and 2028 are eligible to start saving with a $1,000 contribution. Ahead of the midterm elections in November, the cost of living is still a significant concern. However, tax experts warned the BBC that the plan is too convoluted and that lower-income households may lose out. Anyone under the age of 18 who has a valid Social Security number can open an account named after the president, and these accounts are available countrywide. The app is easy for parents to download. Up to $5,000 can be contributed annually by families, friends, and employers for each child, who can access the money once they turn 18. The funds must, by law, be placed in an inexpensive index fund intended for long-term growth. However, withdrawals made before age 59½ are subject to taxes and a potential 10% penalty, even though the money grows tax-free. content:

title: EU Nations Strive to Prevent a Catastrophic Modification of the Russian Oil Price Cap
author: editor
excerpt: As nations rush to prevent a politically disastrous update to the price restriction on Russian oil, the European Union has entered the final round of discussions to find an agreement on a new round of penalties against Moscow. In order to stay 15% below the average market price, the cap, which is now set at $44.10 a barrel, must be automatically modified every six months. The date of the next review is July 15. The revision is likely to push the cap much higher, probably to $58 per barrel, given that Russian oil prices skyrocketed following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. This would give the Kremlin breathing room at a time when its economy is under increasing strain and Ukraine is gaining momentum on the battlefield. The European Commission has suggested postponing the review until January of the following year in order to maintain the cap at $44.10 a barrel since they find this scenario intolerable.Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen told Euronews, “We need to have as strict sanctions as we can, including the price cap.” “We are not in a situation where we are stepping down or in any way loosening our pressure on Russia.” However, three nations with strong maritime services—Malta, Cyprus, and Greece in particular—have questioned the delay. title: As Shares Soar in a Big US IPO, Chip Giant SK Hynix Raises $26.5 Billion
author: editor
excerpt: In its New York share offering, South Korean computer chip manufacturer SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion (£19.8 billion), making it the largest foreign company listing in US history. The business, a major supplier to Nvidia, a major manufacturer of AI chips, announced on Thursday that it had sold 177.9 million US depositary shares for $149 apiece. On Friday, the shares’ first day of trading on the Nasdaq saw a 17% increase. The surge in demand for AI chips helped SK Hynix’s market value surpass $1 trillion in its native nation in May. Together with Samsung Electronics, its share price has more than tripled in South Korea this year, contributing to a more than 70% increase in the benchmark Kospi index over the same period. SK Hynix is one of the top producers of memory chips worldwide. The hundreds of billions being invested on AI have significantly boosted the sector. In recent months, shares of competitors Micron and Samsung Electronics have more than doubled. The launch follows the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) announcement this week that a global surge in AI infrastructure spending is helping protect tech-heavy economies such as South Korea from the growth-stifling consequences of the Middle East conflict. title: The Most Recent Test of EU Unity is a Trade Boycott on Israeli Settlements
author: editor
excerpt: The next test of EU unity on Israel is expected to be a possible trade restriction on Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory. An options document outlining a complete or partial trade ban on Israeli settlements was distributed by the European Commission on Wednesday and will be debated at the foreign affairs ministers’ meeting on Monday. In addition to needing an export license for items from the settlements and raising tariffs to make them unaffordable, the prohibition is just one of the alternatives available. At a ministerial conference last month, twenty member states asked the Commission to outline the alternatives for trade restrictions on the settlements, which are prohibited by international law. This request was reaffirmed in the conclusions of the most recent European Council summit. Even though they anticipate splits to emerge in the upcoming talks, a number of member states have welcomed the fact that the file is finally moving while EU capitals continue to analyze the choices now formally on the table.On condition of anonymity, an EU ambassador informed Euronews that there is no agreement on this. “But we are already happy that it is there.” One of the most contentious issues in the bloc is still Israel. While Germany and the Czech Republic have been more circumspect, afraid of upsetting Israel, France and Sweden have publicly advocated for trade restrictions with the settlements. title: Platner’s Unsuccessful Campaign Reveals Divisions That Could Undermine Democrats’ Chances of Winning the Senate
author: editor
excerpt: Graham Platner’s quick ascent from relative obscurity to the Democratic nominee in this year’s most important US Senate race has now come to a disastrous end. On Wednesday night, the oysterman and former Marine who defeated a well-liked governor and established a grassroots network of over 15,000 supporters in Maine declared he was quitting his campaign. Just over 48 hours after Politico published an article detailing an ex-girlfriend’s claims that an inebriated Platner had broken into her home without permission in 2021 and sexually attacked her, the revelation was revealed through a recorded video shared on social media. He has refuted the accusation.In his 11-minute video marking the end of his campaign, Platner stated, “We went toe to toe with one of the most entrenched political systems in the history of the world, and we won.” “And now they are not going to let us have it, not if it’s me.” Platner was selected by his party to challenge five-term Senator Susan Collins, the only Republican in Congress representing a state that Democrats won in the 2024 presidential election. Platner had been supported by liberal mainstays like Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders and Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren. This election has become critical for Democrats. They must protect all of their seats and flip four Republican-held ones in order to win the Senate in November’s midterm elections. Many people believe that Maine is a target that must be won. Their hopes are now in danger of being severely damaged by Platner’s departure. Additionally, it is re-exposing divisions between the party’s moderates and left wing, which could jeopardize their success both this year and in the 2028 presidential contest. title: To Please France and Italy, the EU Has Narrowed its Ban on Russian Soldiers
author: editor
excerpt: Following opposition from France and Italy, the European Union is debating a more limited version of its plan to prohibit the issuance of visas to Russian military veterans and soldiers, restricting the measure to short-stay visas and those who directly participated in the combat in Ukraine. Given that Russia mandates military conscription for all male citizens between the ages of 18 and 30, who must spend a year in the armed forces, France and Italy had previously questioned the measure’s viability. Additionally, the exemptions have been expanded. Only those who could demonstrate they were dissidents or defectors from the Russian army would be eligible for an exemption under the initial proposal. Additionally, the most recent version permits admission or passage for international commitments, national interest, or humanitarian grounds. For these exceptions, the visa would only be valid in the EU nation that issued it, therefore the holder would not be able to travel to another member state without that nation’s permission. Since the restriction would put a heavy administrative burden on consular services that must conduct case-by-case evaluations, practical questions are still expected to come up during the ambassadors’ meeting on Wednesday. The Commission has promised to change its guidelines on granting visas to Russian applicants and amend the necessary supporting documentation in order to allay these worries. 5. Inaas Abdalla’s Vision on Building Ethical Beauty Products

The beauty industry has rapidly evolved over the last few years, with innovative products getting launched every few months. But leaders like Inaas Abdalla did not enter the field by launching a product, rather, she started with the ingredient list and worked backwards from there. Often called Inaas, which is more Arabic, but her actual Latin name being Inês, is someone who does not hop into every trend when it comes to skincare, she believes in building products that genuinely work. 

With an MBA in Business Administration and Management Operations from Oneday, in partnership with Woolf University, she was instilled with the strategic vision required in building successful ventures. Additionally, as a Skin Masterclass Certified and Licensed Skincare Consultant™ trained under Cigdem Kemal Yilmaz, Chemical Engineer, Skincare Formulator, and founder of the globally award-winning Skin Masterclass PRO programme, Inaas learned to read INCI ingredient lists the way a formulator does: not for claims, but for molecular function, efficacy, and anything that undermines long-term skin health. That professional rigour became the standard she has never lowered.

Her first brand, InêSKN, was a reflection of Inaas’ expertise as a professional consultant and a strong academic foundation. As she realised a market gap between genuine skincare and real-life requirements, Inaas decided to build InêSKN to fill that gap. From analyzing the formulations to assessing the right ingredient concentrations, she did everything from scratch. In 2022, Inaas launched Inês Cosmetics, a brand built around premium, sustainable DIY cluster lash extensions that allow women to achieve salon-quality results at home. 

Eventually, her latest development is YIP, the AI-powered, founder-first community Inaas launched in January 2026, and leads today as its Executive Director. With two vocational qualifications, one from Mindvalley, and another from Google both completed in 2023, helped her learn more about AI and machine learning. Built for entrepreneurs who want to think clearly, build systematically, and grow with intention, YIP is an extension of the philosophy that runs through her brands: rigour over trend, substance over noise.

Inaas has also spoken on the WOHA Women of Heart Awards stage as part of the We Go Black event, and continues to build her voice as a trusted educator across Instagram and Facebook, where her educational content cuts through the marketing confusion that defines so much of the beauty industry.

Her exceptional contributions have earned Inaas several recognitions, including the title of Leader in Ethical Cosmetics and Expert in Skin Health by the Women of Heart Awards in May 2026. She is even a nominee for awards in this field in Dubai and London, while being a sponsor of Women Of Hearts Awards, and has received the UAE Stories Awards for 2026 for Inês Cosmetics. These recognitions are a reflection of how her work is not just here for the trends, it is here to make a difference.

Looking ahead, Inaas Abdalla will keep working across her roles with a consistent belief: that real beauty is built on knowledge, integrity, and the courage to hold a higher standard.

7. Mario N. Rimbano | Engineering Reliability for Generations through RECANATI Europe

A pioneering force and innovator in the field of HDPE pipe fittings, Mario N. Rimbano’s leadership is dedicated to development of polyethylene infrastructure systems. With a leadership approach which is rarely found in today’s dynamic business world, he brings hands-on experience of more than 45 years in the field. A Master’s degree in Engineering earned through on-the-job training, rather than at traditional universities, instilled in him the skills and expertise, shaping Mario into the leader he is today. He even has 39 industrial patents, alongside devoting his time to research and development.

As the Founder and CEO of RECANATI Europe, Mario has built one of the leading manufacturers of advanced connection systems for polyethylene water and gas networks. Found in Italy, and active across Europe, Africa, the Middle East and the US, RECANATI Europe produces accessories not only in HDPE, but also in steel, to meet all plant engineering requirements. For more than four decades of its existence, the company’s mission has remained clear: to make critical infrastructure safer, more reliable, and capable of serving future generations.

Specialised in the development and manufacturing of transition fittings, manifolds and accessories for liquid and gaseous distribution networks for the Utilities and Energy industries, RECANATI Europe aims at environmental sustainability, and is continuously committed to corporate social responsibility.

Mario reflects, “Polyethylene has become one of the most important materials for modern water and gas distribution networks due to its durability, flexibility and resistance to corrosion. Yet experience has shown that the greatest risks rarely originate from the pipe itself. The real challenge lies in the connection between different materials. This is where RECANATI Europe has built its expertise.” 

Through continuous research, field experience and engineering development, RECANATI Europe has created innovative solutions designed to improve the safety, reliability and long-term performance of water and gas infrastructures operating under the most demanding conditions. Today, utilities, contractors and infrastructure operators in more than 40 countries rely on RECANATI Europe technologies to reduce water losses, increase network reliability, minimize maintenance costs and protect strategic assets that communities depend on every day.

With a simple philosophy: the pipe is rarely the problem; the connection is where engineering makes the difference, RECANATI Europe has been actively reshaping practical experience into innovative solutions, from Italy to the world. Under the efficient leadership of Mario, the company continues to challenge conventional approaches and promote engineering solutions designed to withstand time rather than simply satisfy today’s requirements.

For RECANATI Europe, innovation is not about creating something new for the sake of novelty; it is about creating solutions that future generations will never have to worry about.

8. Jacques Christopher Lomani on Building Digital Models Made for Africa’s Needs

In today’s digital age, when every industry is being reshaped by technological advancements, Jacques Christopher Lomani is creating digital models designed specifically to meet the needs of Africa. He states, “Africa does not need to copy digital models built elsewhere. It needs technology designed around its own realities, its own constraints, and its own ambitions.” 

As an entrepreneur, digital transformation strategist, and technology builder, he is dedicated to developing practical digital infrastructure for businesses, institutions, and communities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and throughout Africa. With a career at the intersection of artificial intelligence, software development, business productivity, and digital inclusion, he has built ventures that are designed for the region. 

As the Founder of Infinity Group Solutions, a Congolese digital services company, he aligned his vision of helping organizations modernize their operations through custom-built technology. Jacques shares, “Through the company, we develop web applications, mobile applications, professional websites, business platforms, automation tools, AI-powered solutions, and digital transformation strategies for companies and institutions operating in the DRC.” 

Behind building Infinity Group Solutions, lies a clear observation of Jacques: many organizations in the DRC and across Africa still rely on manual, paper-based, fragmented, or outdated processes, resulting in reduced productivity, slow decision-making, increased operational costs, and limited ability of companies to scale. Jacques believes that digital tools are not only a matter of convenience, but a driver of economic productivity. By helping companies move from archaic processes to structured digital systems, Infinity Group Solutions aims to increase efficiency, strengthen competitiveness, and contribute to the broader economic development of Africa.

The company’s services span custom software development, web and mobile development, process automation, AI integration, HR and internal management platforms, digital advisory, and tailored business applications. Having worked on a wide range of projects, from platforms for business management and logistics to HR tools, medical platforms, and more, its approach is not to impose generic technology, but to understand the reality of each organization and build tools adapted to its operational needs.

Jacques has also worked on the democratization of Artificial Intelligence in the DRC. In 2023, following the global rise of generative AI tools, he launched the first Congolese-built AI chatbot initiative designed specifically to make artificial intelligence accessible to users in the Democratic Republic of Congo. At the time, global AI tools were not accessible to Congolese users. This is what led Jacques to develop his own AI chatbot, as he did not want people from Congo to be left behind in a world where AI can be a true competitive advantage. 

Rather than presenting the initiative as the creation of a foundational AI model, Jacques positioned it as a practical and locally adapted AI access platform. The chatbot named “Jacques” adapted the user experience to local realities. One of its adaptations was the integration of Congolese mobile money systems such as M-Pesa, Orange Money, and Airtel Money, making premium AI tools accessible to users without international bank cards. The initiative also included a free version, reflecting his broader belief that artificial intelligence should not be limited only to users with high purchasing power.

For Jacques, this platform was not just a technology experiment; it was a statement about digital inclusion. His ambition was to ensure that the DRC would not be left behind in the global AI transformation. By building a locally accessible AI chatbot, he wanted to give students, professionals, entrepreneurs, and organizations in Congo a way to experience and use AI tools in their daily work.

In 2026, Jacques expanded his entrepreneurial journey into digital health through OpenAfya, a health-tech venture formally launched in June 2026. OpenAfya is building a digital health ecosystem designed for African realities, starting with the Democratic Republic of Congo. The venture combines two complementary pillars: a digital health platform, and a connected medical device designed to enrich remote consultations.

The word “Afya” means “health” in Swahili, one of Africa’s most widely spoken languages. The name reflects OpenAfya’s ambition to build a health solution that is both technologically modern and culturally connected to the continent. The platform allows patients to search for doctors by specialty, location, or health facility, book appointments online, receive reminders, access teleconsultations, and centralize their medical history.

On the provider side, the platform helps doctors, hospitals, clinics, and reception teams manage appointments, patient flows, consultations, agendas, and certain operational data. The long-term ambition is to connect patients, doctors, hospitals, pharmacies, insurers, and companies into a single digital ecosystem. Jacques sees this as a necessary step because access to care does not depend only on the existence of doctors. It also depends on information, orientation, availability, coordination, payment, insurance coverage, pharmacy access, and reliable medical data.

The second pillar of OpenAfya is a connected medical device: a portable kit capable of collecting useful patient data remotely. The device is designed to capture indicators such as blood pressure, temperature, oxygen saturation, heart and lung sounds through a connected stethoscope, and medical images of areas such as the throat, ears, skin, or eyes through an integrated camera. The objective is not to replace doctors, but to give them better information earlier through teleconsultation, even when the patient is not physically present.

Jacques believes that telemedicine in Africa cannot be limited to a simple video call where the patient describes symptoms without a clinical context. In many cases, doctors need concrete data to assess urgency, guide decisions, prioritize patients, and improve the quality of care. OpenAfya therefore aims to make remote consultations more useful, more structured, and more medically relevant.

This dual approach, combining a digital health platform with a connected medical device, is what makes OpenAfya distinctive. Many digital health initiatives focus either on appointment booking or on teleconsultation, while others focus only on medical hardware. OpenAfya’s ambition is to combine both: a platform to organize access to care, and a device to make remote medical assessment more meaningful.

The health-tech project, originally recognized under the name MAVIMPY and now being launched as OpenAfya, won the top award at the Innovation and Startup Investment Forum in May 2026, which contributed to Jacques Lomani’s participation at VivaTech 2026, held from June 17 to June 20. Jacques was even selected among the top 10 finalists at the Innovation and Startup Investment Forum 2026, further reinforcing his position as an emerging technology entrepreneur working on solutions adapted to African markets.

His academic and professional background also shaped his approach to technology and entrepreneurship. Jacques graduated with a Master’s degree in Economics from the Toulouse School of Economics in 2022, after receiving two excellence scholarships. During his studies, he was selected as a representative of the 2022 Master’s cohort and delivered a speech at graduation. He also gained academic experience by teaching Economics to about 100 undergraduate students. These experiences helped him develop a strong analytical foundation, a structured understanding of economic systems, and a practical approach to business problem-solving.

Beyond entrepreneurship, Jacques has participated in public discussions, media appearances, and radio programs related to technology, artificial intelligence, and Africa’s digital future. His broader message is that African countries should not only consume foreign technologies, but also build tools adapted to their own economic, social, and institutional realities.

Across his two ventures, Jacques’s work is guided by a common conviction: technology must solve real problems. For Infinity Group Solutions, this means helping businesses become more productive and competitive through digital tools. For OpenAfya, it means making healthcare access more structured, more intelligent, and more useful for both patients and medical professionals.

From Jacques’ perspective, 2026 is a pivotal year. Through Infinity Group Solutions, he aims to strengthen the digital transformation of companies and institutions in the DRC. Through OpenAfya, he aims to contribute to a more connected, efficient, and accessible healthcare system. These ventures are a reflection of his long-term ambition to help build African technology infrastructure that is not copied from other markets, but designed from the ground up for African needs.

Jacques’s leadership philosophy is built around practical impact. He believes technology should be judged not by how impressive it sounds, but by how clearly it solves real operational problems, improves productivity, and gives people better access to essential services. By combining ambition with realism, he is interested in innovation, but not innovation disconnected from the ground.

For Jacques, the best digital products are those that understand local constraints: how people pay, how institutions operate, how companies manage their workflows, how patients search for care, and how professionals make decisions under pressure.

title: A Landslide Strikes a Bangladeshi Girls’ School, Killing Eight People
author: editor
excerpt: A landslide struck a girls’ school inside a refugee camp in Bangladesh, killing seven students and a teacher. On Wednesday afternoon, mud and debris buried the Islamic study center in the coastal city of Cox’s Bazar, prompting a desperate search and rescue operation. The number of people inside the school is unknown. The country has been pummeled by monsoon rains since Sunday, with many deadly landslides recorded in Cox’s Bazar. The largest refugee camp in the world is home to over a million Rohingya who escaped a violent military crackdown in Myanmar. According to Mohammed Mizanur Rahman, the Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner, eight of the 13 persons rescued from the muck that swallowed their school hut perished.A local district officer named Panna Akhter informed BBC Bangla that some of them are seven, eight, eleven, or twelve years old. For treatment, the other five kids were brought to the hospital. At least eight Rohingya refugees, including five children, have been killed by additional landslides since Sunday, according to earlier reports from officials. During an army operation in Myanmar in 2017, thousands of Rohingya, one of the country’s numerous ethnic minorities, were slaughtered, and over 700,000 fled to neighboring Bangladesh. The government of Myanmar, a country with a majority of Buddhists, denies citizenship to the minority, which is mainly Muslim. In Bangladesh, many people live in substandard housing made of bamboo and tarpaulin on steep hillsides. Authorities are warning of more landslides and floods and relocating residents in high-risk regions as more rain is predicted over the next few days. title: Fuel Shortages in Russia Hurt, But will Putin Shift Course in the Conflict with Ukraine?
author: editor
excerpt: You only need to drive around Moscow for a day to get a feel of the fuel crisis that Russia is currently experiencing. There was a line of vehicles and trucks at practically every gas station we went by. There were long and short lines, as well as static and steadily moving lines. If there was no line, the garage was closed and had completely ran out of fuel. Recall that this is Moscow, the populous, affluent capital that attracts a large portion of Russia’s abundant resources. Even here, the authorities are unable to guarantee that there is sufficient gasoline and diesel to keep Muscovites on the road. However, there was more frustration than anger in the lines. According to Yekaterina, there was “panic because everybody thinks there will be no oil” and she was “not happy.” However, she stated that “we just need to reorganise the oil distribution” and that everything would be fine. Elmar claimed that the situation was “very bad” and that as fuel supplies ran low, prices were rising. “You are wasting hours to fill up,” he replied. “At the moment I am planning a trip to Dagestan but I don’t know if I should drive there or not because there are so many problems with petrol.” I questioned him about who was at fault. In our country, you can’t say what is to blame and who is to blame,” he remarked, grinning knowingly. Most Russians believe they are not allowed to publicly criticize the president or even the Kremlin. In a nation that extracts a lot of oil, Valery thought it seemed odd to have to wait in line. He placed equal culpability for Ukrainian rockets and Russia’s lack of readiness. “I have no desire to get used to queues,” he replied. “I hope the situation will change soon and won’t be continued.” Also Read: Officials Report that an Incident in Pakistan Killed Nine Police Officers Meta is Ordered by India to Take Down Advertisements that Encourage Child Sexual Abuse

I questioned him about who was at fault. In our country, you can’t say what is to blame and who is to blame,” he remarked, grinning knowingly. title: Egypt Wants World Cup Officials Expelled
author: editor
excerpt: The EFA said it has filed a protest with football’s world governing body, requesting a probe into “double standards” in officiating during the game in Atlanta. With Egypt leading 1-0 in the second half, the video assistant referee (VAR) disallowed a goal by Mostafa Zico after Egypt midfielder Marwan Attia was penalized for stomping on Lisandro Martinez’s foot at the commencement of the action. content:
When people first hear about No Dogs Left Behind, they often search online to learn more about the organization and understand how it operates.

One of the most common questions people ask is:

“Is No Dogs Left Behind legit?”

This is a reasonable question. Before donating, volunteering, fostering, or adopting a rescue dog, people want to understand the organization’s mission, rescue process, and overall impact.

The answer starts with understanding what No Dogs Left Behind actually does and why its work is different from many traditional animal rescue organizations.

What Is No Dogs Left Behind?

No Dogs Left Behind is an international animal welfare organization dedicated to rescuing dogs from some of the most dangerous and heartbreaking situations imaginable.

The organization is widely recognized for its work helping dogs rescued from:

  • Dog trafficking operations
  • Slaughter trucks
  • Illegal dog meat trade networks
  • Wet markets
  • Slaughter facilities
  • Severe neglect and abuse cases

Unlike many rescue organizations that focus only on shelter placement, No Dogs Left Behind remains involved throughout the entire journey of a rescued dog.

From the moment a dog is saved until it reaches a forever home, the organization continues to provide care, treatment, and support.

Fighting to End the Dog Meat Trade

A major part of the No Dogs Left Behind mission is working to help end the dog meat trade.

The organization works alongside local activists, volunteers, government officials, and law enforcement agencies to intervene in situations where dogs are being trafficked or held in cruel conditions.

One fact that is often misunderstood is that No Dogs Left Behind does not buy dogs from traffickers.

The organization has consistently maintained that it does not pay traders, traffickers, or slaughterhouses for animals.

Instead, rescue efforts focus on working with authorities to legally confiscate dogs and remove them from dangerous situations.

Many of the organization’s rescue videos show operations where local authorities and rescue teams work together to secure the safety of animals while addressing the conditions in which they were being held.

This approach reflects a commitment to protecting animals without creating financial incentives for the people responsible for their suffering.

Jeffrey Beri’s Role in Rescue Operations

When discussing No Dogs Left Behind, it is impossible not to mention Jeffrey Beri.

Jeffrey Beri is the founder of No Dogs Left Behind and has become known for his direct involvement in rescue missions.

Rather than managing operations from a distance, he frequently works alongside rescue teams, local activists, volunteers, and government officials during field operations.

Many supporters first discover the organization through rescue footage that shows Jeffrey Beri participating in efforts to save dogs from trafficking operations and slaughter facilities.

His commitment to being physically present during rescue missions reflects the organization’s hands-on approach to animal welfare.

For many supporters, this level of involvement demonstrates a genuine dedication to helping animals in crisis.

Transparency Throughout the Rescue Process

One of the strongest indicators of a legitimate rescue organization is transparency.

No Dogs Left Behind regularly documents the journey of rescued dogs from the day they are saved through every stage of recovery.

This often includes updates on:

  • Rescue operations
  • Veterinary treatment
  • Medical recovery
  • Rehabilitation
  • Shelter care
  • Adoption preparation
  • Forever home placements

Many dogs rescued from trafficking networks and slaughter facilities arrive with serious medical conditions or emotional trauma.

The rehabilitation process can take weeks or even months depending on the dog’s condition.

By sharing these updates, the organization allows supporters to follow the progress of individual dogs and better understand the resources required to help them recover.

Why Rehabilitation Is Just as Important as Rescue

Saving a dog is only the first step.

Many rescued dogs need extensive care before they are physically and emotionally ready for adoption.

No Dogs Left Behind invests significant time and resources into helping these animals heal.

This may include:

  • Emergency surgeries
  • Vaccinations
  • Treatment for infections
  • Nutritional support
  • Behavioral rehabilitation
  • Long-term sanctuary care

The goal is not simply to remove dogs from danger but to prepare them for healthy, successful lives with loving families.

A Mission That Extends Beyond Rescue

While rescue work remains at the heart of the organization, No Dogs Left Behind also advocates for broader animal welfare improvements.

The organization supports awareness campaigns and works toward stronger protections for animals through education, advocacy, and collaboration with local communities.

Their long-term vision is a world where animals are protected by meaningful welfare standards and where cruelty is no longer accepted or ignored.

Why People Continue to Support No Dogs Left Behind

Supporters are often drawn to the organization because of its direct rescue work, transparency, and commitment to helping dogs throughout their entire recovery journey.

Many people appreciate seeing how rescued dogs transform from frightened and vulnerable animals into healthy companions living safely in permanent homes.

The organization’s focus on rescue, rehabilitation, adoption, and advocacy has helped build a community of supporters who share the goal of creating a better future for animals.

Final Thoughts

If you are asking, “Is No Dogs Left Behind legit?” it is important to look beyond headlines and understand the work involved in every rescue.

No Dogs Left Behind is dedicated to rescuing dogs from trafficking operations, slaughter trucks, wet markets, and slaughter facilities while advocating for stronger animal welfare protections around the world.

The organization works with local authorities and rescue partners to help dogs in crisis, provides ongoing medical care and rehabilitation, and supports them until they find loving forever homes.

At its core, the mission is simple: protect vulnerable animals, fight cruelty, and give every rescued dog the opportunity to live a safe and happy life.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is No Dogs Left Behind a registered nonprofit organization?

Yes. No Dogs Left Behind operates as a registered nonprofit organization dedicated to animal rescue, rehabilitation, and welfare advocacy.

Does No Dogs Left Behind buy dogs from traffickers?

No. The organization does not purchase dogs from traffickers, traders, or slaughterhouses. Rescue efforts focus on working alongside local authorities and law enforcement agencies to help confiscate dogs from dangerous situations.

Who is Jeffrey Beri?

Jeffrey Beri is the founder of No Dogs Left Behind and is known for participating directly in rescue missions alongside rescue teams, volunteers, activists, and government officials.

What happens to dogs after they are rescued?

Rescued dogs receive medical treatment, rehabilitation, nutrition, shelter, and adoption support before being placed with suitable families whenever possible.

What is the mission of No Dogs Left Behind?

The organization’s mission is to rescue vulnerable dogs, help end the dog meat trade, support global animal welfare efforts, and ensure rescued animals have the opportunity to live safe and healthy lives.

author: editor
excerpt: A local government official informed BBC Urdu that an ambush by gunmen in Pakistan’s southwest Balochistan region had left at least nine police personnel dead and numerous missing. As part of a “clearance operation” in Ziarat, security personnel murdered 15 members of the Pakistani Taliban (TPP), according to Balochistan officials. According to officials, they were protecting the Mangi Dam construction site, which is being built to help Quetta, the capital of Balochistan, overcome its water scarcity. author: editor
excerpt: A dispute has erupted in Germany after the coalition government announced revisions to sick-leave laws that require Germans to send a doctor’s letter to their employers on the first day of their illness. Workers will no longer be able to receive the notice via phone, which was implemented in response to the Covid-19 pandemic.”The number of sick days in Germany is excessive, remarked Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Under existing guidelines, a certificate is only required if a person is unable to work for more than three days – that is, on the fourth day – however employers may request the sick note earlier. Merz’s CDU and SPD alliance reached an agreement on the measures.”This is a difficult decision,” the chancellor explained. “But we can no longer afford this competitive disadvantage caused by long periods of absence from work. Merz stated that the government will not allow “exorbitant amounts of sick leave in the wake of the outbreak. Germany was “returning to the arrangements we had before the coronavirus pandemic,” he told ARD TV on Thursday night. title: Google Must Pay a €4.1 Billion Punishment for Using Android to ‘Block’ Competition
author: editor
excerpt: Europe’s top court has ordered that Google must pay a €4.1 billion (£3.5 billion) fine for using its Android mobile operating system to hinder competitors. The European Commission originally imposed a €4.3 billion (then £3.9 billion) fine in 2018, which was reduced to €4.1 billion in 2022. The tech giant’s appeal has now been dismissed. This is the largest punishment the Commission has ever issued on Google. A Google spokeswoman stated that the decision “fails to recognise” the company’s enormous investment in keeping Android open, interoperable, and free.In any case, we updated our agreements to comply with the initial ruling in 2018, and we remain committed to continuous innovation and openness for our users, partners, and developers,” they added. When the fine was first announced in 2018, it was claimed that Google had acted illegally in three ways. It was noted that Google’s version of Android did not prevent users from downloading other web browsers or using other search engines. In reaction to the original fine, Google CEO Sundar Pichai wrote in a blog post that the decision “rejects the business model that supports Android, which has created more choice for everyone, not less. The European Commission has initiated many cases against Google and its parent firm, Alphabet. title: Poland’s Prime Minister Warns of Critical Months Ahead in The Face of Russian Threat
author: editor
excerpt: Poland’s prime minister has said the country is preparing for “various” scenarios and that the coming months could be “critical” concerning the threat from Russia. Donald Tusk was responding to media reports that Moscow was planning an armed “provocation” in Poland to test Nato’s resolve, citing US intelligence. “I don’t mean to scare anyone but the coming months may truly be critical, also due to the changing nature of the war. These concerns are particularly palpable in the Baltic states,” Tusk told reporters on Friday. Polish news outlet Onet reported that sources close to President Karol Nawrocki had said the US had issued several warnings to Warsaw about a plot to attack the country. The White House and US State Department did not respond to the BBC’s requests for comment. Under the purported plans, also published by the Telegraph in the UK on Friday, Polish infrastructure could be targeted by missiles or drones, or soldiers could be sent into the Nato state. The reports suggest the aim would be to place pressure on Ukraine’s western allies to suspend aid to the country as it continues to fight against Russia’s full-scale invasion, launched in 2022. Asked about the reports, Tusk said: “Let’s not be afraid, we are preparing for various situations, but we cannot ignore them. We are aware of the threats, also thanks to information from our allies”. title: A Venezuelan Earthquake Survivor Was Rescued Alive After Eight Days
author: editor
excerpt: A guy was rescued alive after being buried for eight days in the wreckage of a building in Venezuela that collapsed following twin earthquakes. More than 100 hours after finding Hernán Gil under 140 tonnes of rubble, emergency workers were able to liberate him. A Chilean firefighter had previously described the rescue effort as “without a doubt the most complex and technically difficult that I’ve had to tackle.” Almost 2,300 people are documented to have killed in the earthquakes that slammed Venezuela on June 24th, while tens of thousands are still missing. Allan Madrigal, a paramedic with the Costa Rican Red Cross, informed reporters at the scene that Gil had “emerged just perfect” from his trauma. Madrigal, the rescuer, heard Gil’s weak calls for aid emerging from the rubble on Sunday.things was an emotional moment,” he recounted, noting that at first, he had not trusted his own ears and had asked a coworker to clarify that he “wasn’t just dreaming things.” From that point forward, rescuers rushed to extract the security guy. Gil had been working in a small concrete booth in the bottom of the parking lot next to the Galerias Playa Grande mall in Catia La Mar when the twin quakes struck. The booth shielded him from the 140 tons of rubble that fell around and on top of him.”He has told us that he doesn’t even have a crushed nail,” claimed another Costa Rican Red Cross worker soon before Gil was rescued from the rubble. title: Ryanair Warned of ‘Queue Pandemonium’ With The New EU Border Arrangement
author: editor
excerpt: Ryanair and Berlin Airport’s CEO have warned of serious disruptions to summer travel due to the new digital EU border check system. Ryanair warned that families will experience “queue chaos” and urged governments to postpone the system until after the summer holiday period. According to Berlin Airport’s Aletta von Massenbach, non-EU nationals are having to line for up to two hours under the new method, and the situation is “not bearable over the summer”. Under the EU’s Entry-Exit System (EES), visitors from outside the bloc must submit biometric information while entering most European nations, which is then checked when they leave. The European Commission (EC) says it is open to provide additional assistance. Von Massenback told the BBC’s Today programme that waiting periods at one terminal in Berlin, where Ryanair and Wizz Air operate, can last “an hour to two hours”. Neal McMahon, Ryanair’s senior operations officer, stated, “Passengers and families should not be used as guinea pigs for a half-baked passport control system that risks creating long queues, missed flights, and unnecessary stress at airports this summer. The airline reported substantial difficulties at airports including Tenerife South, Palma, Alicante, Malaga, Milan Bergamo, Krakow, and Paris Beauvais. title: World Cup Surge Stalls as US Hospitality Jobs Decrease in June
author: editor
excerpt: A World Cup job boom in the United States has failed to materialize, with employment in restaurants, pubs, and hotels declining in June. Analysts predicted the event, held jointly by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, would result in a surge in leisure and hospitality jobs. However, the sector lost 61,000 jobs last month, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported on Thursday.Overall employment in the United States increased by 57,000 in June, less than predicted, while the unemployment rate fell slightly to 4.2%. The BLS had reported early signs of an employment boom in May, with bars and restaurants hiring to preparation for the World Cup. Goldman Sachs analysts predicted that the competition will raise employment by approximately 40,000 jobs in June. However, despite reports of traveling football fans drinking their way out of pubs around the United States, growth slowed in June. ING’s chief US economist, James Knightley, said Thursday’s results showed a “real area of weakness” in leisure and hospitality. title: Australia Takes Amazon to Court on Alleged Discriminatory Subscriber Contracts
author: editor
excerpt: Australia’s consumer watchdog has sued Amazon, claiming the tech giant placed advertising in Prime Video using allegedly unfair contract conditions. Amazon has infringed consumer protection law by entering into unfair contracts with over one million annual members between November 2023 and August 2025, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) claimed.Consumers who wished to avoid adverts had no choice but to pay more to keep the service they had signed up for in the first place,” ACCC chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb said. An Amazon representative said the business was “looking at the case filed by the ACCC in detail”.“We have worked closely with the ACCC during its investigation and remain focused on delivering the best experience for our Australian customers,” she added. Prime Video was a commercial-free streaming offering available for over a decade as part of Amazon’s popular Prime subscription, sold as an upgrade on top of its main delivery service. Prime launched in Australia in 2018. It started rolling out advertising in the service globally in early 2024.When Amazon started adding advertisements to Prime Video that year, it told users in Australia they’d have to pay an extra fee each month to keep the program ad-free, raising the monthly price to 12.99 Australian dollars. title: Trump has Suffered Significant Setbacks from the US Supreme Court While Gaining More Authority
author: editor
excerpt: President Donald Trump’s reaction to the Supreme Court’s decision against him regarding birthright citizenship was muted by his own standards. Before endorsing legislation that would reestablish his proposed restrictions on the long-standing legal concept that anybody born in the country is a US citizen, Obama declared Tuesday’s ruling to be “too bad for our country”. However, there is little likelihood that Congress will take action on that. Any attempt in the US Senate would very definitely be thwarted by Democrats, and even if such a bill were passed, it’s not obvious how it would pass constitutional scrutiny. Although this ruling was a setback for Trump, it ends a term on the Supreme Court that has largely followed a recent pattern. The president has won a number of significant triumphs thanks to its conservative majority, which was solidified throughout his first term. It has systematically increased presidential authority and protected Trump and all subsequent presidents from legal action. However, a few conservatives joined forces with the three liberal justices of the court to clearly restrict several of Trump’s most ambitious trade, immigration, and law enforcement policies issues that have been core to his political identity for more than ten years. title: U.S. Court Backs Birthright Nationality in a Major Blow to Trump
author: editor

Chief Justice John Roberts declared 6-3 that children born in the US “to parents unlawfully or temporarily present” are “citizens at birth” under the 14th Amendment. President Trump had attempted to curtail that right via executive order, contending that children of undocumented immigrants and of some temporary visitors were not “subject to the jurisdiction thereof,” and hence not eligible for birthright citizenship. We don’t need a long, complicated constitutional amendment,” he remarked. “Congress should begin work TODAY to end costly and very unfair to our country birthright citizenship.The U.S. has given citizenship to anybody born in the country since 1868. That right is enshrined in the 14th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution and supported by subsequent U.S. Supreme Court decisions. title: Manhunt After Bomb Attack Injures Ukrainian Tycoon in Monaco
author: editor
excerpt: French police are hunting a suspect after a parcel bomb exploded at a private building in Monaco, injuring wealthy Ukrainian businessman Vadym Yermolaiev and two others. Two of the injured are in a severe condition in hospital in the French city of Nice, Monaco public prosecutor Stéphane Thibault told AFP, adding that a woman was the most gravely hurt. He said police were seeking one man and the event on Monday evening was being regarded as attempted murder, not as a terrorist act. Ukraine’s foreign ministry said its embassy in France was in contact with authorities in Monaco and working to officially identify those allegedly injured in the bomb. Monaco’s government said the blast was caused by a parcel bomb, and its head Christophe Mirmand told AFP news agency the explosive device looked to contain bolts and pellets. title: India’s Highest Share Sales are a Story of a Nation Tied to its Phones
author: editor
excerpt: India’s major stock exchange and its top telecoms company will both list by the end of this year in what experts say might be milestone offerings for the country’s capital markets. Billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries’ digital arm Jio Platforms and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) – the world’s largest derivatives exchange and one of the top three equity exchanges by trade volume – filed draft papers for their initial public offerings just days apart last month. The market is likely to hoover up roughly $4bn (£3.02bn) from Jio at an estimated valuation of $120-160bn, while NSE’s issuance is expected to sell 6% of shares for $3.3bn, valuing the bourse at $57bn. Beyond the sheer size of the offerings could push India’s overall market capitalization higher by several notches – investors are keenly watching the listings as they reflect the sweeping changes in the way Indians have come to live, consume, invest and transact in the last decade,” Yatin Singh, CEO – Investment Banking at Emkay Global, told the BBC. These are one-off businesses which aren’t built often. “NSE is a direct proxy for the ‘financialization’ of Indian household savings in mutual funds and stocks. Jio is the story of a company that single-handedly ushered in a digital revolution and became a driving factor for several new-age Indian businesses,” said Singh. title: 9,000 Jobs Will be Eliminated by British American Tobacco
author: editor
excerpt: As part of a significant cost-cutting initiative, British American Tobacco (BAT) plans to lay off over a fifth of its global staff. The massive tobacco company, which produces Dunhill and Lucky Strike cigarettes, is exporting 3,500 jobs and eliminating 5,500. It stated that the US was unaffected but did not specify where the cuts would occur. Earlier this year, BAT had stated that it intended to make reductions in order to become “more digital and AI-focused”. Sales of traditional cigarettes are declining as more smokers turn to nicotine packs and vapes. In an effort to spur growth, BAT is concentrating on smoking substitutes like its Velo nicotine packs and Vuse vapes, but its sales and profit margins have been weak recently. Currently, the corporation has roughly 47,000 employees worldwide. By 2028, the cost reductions are anticipated to save roughly £600 million annually. The cost of living has also affected sales in the US, its largest market, as smokers switch to less expensive brands.Launches of innovative products, such as vapes, have been delayed by American regulators’ strict licensing requirements. According to BAT, this has increased the flow of illicit Chinese goods, which has hurt its market share and revenues.
