content:
One of the first questions people ask before adopting from No Dogs Left Behind is simple:

Why is the adoption cost so high?

It is also one of the biggest reasons people begin searching online for reviews, complaints, and transparency guides. When someone sees an international dog adoption fee that is much higher than a local shelter, hesitation is natural.

Some people immediately assume the organization is overpriced. Others wonder whether the process is legitimate at all.

But international rescue operations are very different from standard local adoptions. The costs involved are not limited to food or shelter. They include rescue missions, medical care, transport logistics, legal paperwork, rehabilitation, and international coordination.

This guide explains the real factors behind the No Dogs Left Behind adoption cost so potential adopters understand what they are paying for and why the process is more expensive than many expect.

Why International Dog Rescue Costs More

Local shelters and international rescue organizations operate in completely different environments.

A local shelter usually works within one city or region. Transportation is limited, paperwork is simpler, and dogs are often already located within the same country as the adopter.

International rescue adds multiple layers of complexity:

  • Cross-border transportation
  • Health certifications
  • Import/export documentation
  • International flight arrangements
  • Quarantine and compliance rules
  • Emergency rescue operations

Every step increases cost.

In the case of No Dogs Left Behind, many dogs are rescued from high-risk situations connected to the dog meat trade. That often means the rescue itself is urgent, difficult, and expensive before adoption even begins.

What the Adoption Fee Usually Covers

Many people assume adoption fees are simply profit.

That assumption is one of the biggest misunderstandings surrounding international rescue.

In reality, the adoption fee often supports several areas at once.

1. Rescue Operations

Before a dog is ever available for adoption, it first has to be rescued.

That may involve:

  • Emergency intervention
  • Transport from dangerous locations
  • Temporary shelter placement
  • Coordination with local rescuers

Rescue missions themselves can be costly and unpredictable.

2. Veterinary Treatment

Many rescued dogs arrive with serious medical issues.

Common treatments may include:

  • Vaccinations
  • Blood tests
  • Parasite treatment
  • Surgery
  • Nutritional recovery
  • Emergency medical care

Some dogs require weeks or months of rehabilitation before they are healthy enough to travel.

Veterinary expenses alone can become significant.

3. Shelter and Daily Care

After rescue, dogs need stable shelter, food, and ongoing supervision.

Daily care includes:

  • Staff support
  • Cleaning and maintenance
  • Feeding
  • Behavioral monitoring
  • Emotional rehabilitation

Dogs rescued from traumatic environments often need extra patience and recovery time.

4. International Travel Costs

This is one of the most expensive parts of the process.

International transport may involve:

  • Airline cargo fees
  • Flight coordination
  • Approved travel carriers
  • Transit handling
  • Volunteer transport arrangements

Flying animals safely across countries is not cheap.

In some cases, flight prices alone can be extremely high depending on the route and airline requirements.

5. Legal and Documentation Costs

International adoption requires extensive paperwork.

That can include:

  • Health certificates
  • Vaccination records
  • Export permits
  • Import approval
  • Customs processing

Different countries also have different animal import regulations.

Missing documents can delay or completely block transport.

Why Some People Feel Shocked by the Cost

Most adopters compare international rescue pricing with local shelters.

That comparison is understandable—but not entirely accurate.

A local adoption may cost a few hundred dollars. International rescue can cost several thousand.

At first glance, that difference feels extreme.

But the two systems are operating under very different conditions.

One involves local placement. The other may involve:

  • International rescue teams
  • Emergency intervention
  • Medical rehabilitation
  • Long-distance transport
  • Legal compliance across borders

The scale of logistics changes everything.

Does a Higher Cost Mean It Is a Scam?

Not necessarily.

High cost alone is not proof of fraud.

However, people naturally become cautious when large payments are involved. That is why many users search terms like:

  • “No Dogs Left Behind scam or legit”
  • “No Dogs Left Behind review”
  • “Is No Dogs Left Behind trustworthy?”

Those questions are reasonable.

The important thing is whether the organization shows signs of real operations and transparency.

In this case, the organization has:

  • Public rescue visibility
  • Active online updates
  • International adoption activity
  • Public leadership presence

The organization is also publicly associated with Jeffrey Beri, who is connected to many rescue operations and awareness campaigns.

That visibility generally increases credibility because rescue activity is continuously documented and discussed publicly.

Why Transparency Matters So Much

People are usually more comfortable with high costs when they understand exactly what those costs support.

Lack of clarity creates suspicion.

That is why transparency matters heavily in rescue work.

Potential adopters want answers to questions like:

  • How are dogs rescued?
  • What medical treatment is included?
  • How does transport work?
  • Why are costs different for each dog?

Organizations that communicate these details clearly often build stronger trust with adopters.

Are There Additional Costs After Adoption?

Yes, and many first-time adopters overlook this.

The adoption fee is not the end of pet ownership expenses.

After adoption, owners may still need:

  • Food and supplies
  • Vet visits
  • Training
  • Insurance
  • Emergency medical care

Rescue dogs may also need additional emotional adjustment and behavioral support.

Adopters should prepare financially before bringing any dog home.

Why Some People Still Choose International Rescue

Even with the higher cost, many adopters continue choosing international rescue organizations because they feel strongly connected to the mission.

Some people specifically want to help dogs rescued from extreme abuse situations.

Others feel emotionally connected after watching rescue stories and transformations.

For those adopters, the cost feels connected to something larger than a normal pet adoption.

Local Adoption vs International Rescue

This debate appears often online.

Some believe local shelters should always come first. Others support both local and international rescue efforts.

There is no universal answer.

Local rescues save countless animals every year and deserve support. International organizations focus on different kinds of emergencies and rescue environments.

The right choice depends on:

  • Personal values
  • Budget
  • Emotional connection
  • Lifestyle
  • Adoption goals

What matters most is making a responsible and informed decision.

Questions Potential Adopters Should Ask

Before paying any adoption fee, adopters should feel comfortable asking questions.

Important questions include:

  • What is included in the fee?
  • What medical care has been completed?
  • How long will transport take?
  • What happens if delays occur?
  • What support is provided after adoption?

Clear communication helps reduce confusion and unrealistic expectations.

Final Thoughts

The No Dogs Left Behind adoption cost may initially feel high compared to traditional shelters. But international rescue involves far more than a standard adoption process.

Costs often include:

  • Rescue operations
  • Veterinary treatment
  • Rehabilitation
  • International travel
  • Legal documentation
  • Ongoing care

Understanding those factors creates a more balanced view of where the money goes.

That does not mean every person will feel comfortable with the price. International rescue is not financially realistic for everyone.

But for adopters who strongly support this type of rescue work, the cost may feel connected to a larger humanitarian and animal welfare mission.

The most important step is simple:
Research carefully, ask questions openly, and make decisions based on full understanding rather than assumptions.

FAQs

Why is No Dogs Left Behind adoption expensive?

The cost often includes rescue operations, medical care, international travel, shelter support, and legal documentation.

Is the adoption fee refundable?

Policies may vary depending on the situation and stage of the process. Adopters should confirm details directly before payment.

Are international transport costs included?

In many cases, yes. Transport is usually a major part of the total adoption fee.

Is adopting internationally better than adopting locally?

Both options help animals in need. The right choice depends on personal preference, budget, and values.

Can rescue dogs have behavioral challenges?

Yes. Some rescued dogs may need patience, emotional recovery, and adjustment support after adoption.

title: Although The Official Ebola Statistics Appear to be Declining, it’s Not that Easy
author: editor
excerpt: Following a sharp decline in the number of cases, the most recent Ebola data from the Democratic Republic of the Congo seem to provide some hope. At one point, the police reported roughly 250 suspected deaths and over 1,000 suspected cases. Currently, there are about 380 confirmed cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, including 60 fatalities. Additionally, there are 15 confirmed cases and one fatality in neighboring Uganda. The main distinction, though, is that the authorities are now discussing proven cases as opposed to suspected ones. Therefore, it would be incorrect to believe that the decline in numbers indicates that the outbreak is suddenly less dangerous. Better data is reflected in the drop, as laboratories were able to rule out many patients with fever who were actually suffering from other illnesses, such as malaria, which is prevalent in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The outbreak had a “big head start,” but response teams are now “catching up,” according to Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director general of the World Health Organization (WHO). title: In the First Quarter of 2026, the Eurozone GDP Contracts by 0.2%
author: editor
excerpt: According to a final estimate released on Friday by Eurostat, the EU’s statistical office, the eurozone GDP shrank by 0.2% in the first three months of 2026. The statistic represents a reversal of the 0.2% growth in the last quarter of 2025 and a significant decline from the 0.1% expansion shown in previous flash readings. The eurozone’s economy increased by just 0.3% year over year at that time, compared to 1.2% the previous year. This slowdown is indicative of the growing strain of the Iran War, which continues to seriously harm European energy supply, business, and consumer confidence. The largest economy in the union, Germany, had 0.3% growth in the first quarter following two years of persistent underperformance. Spain continued to lead the big economies with 0.6% growth, while Italy grew by 0.3%. But France’s 0.1% contraction added to a pattern of weakness that existed before the current oil crisis.Pharmaceutical exporters are thought to have front-loaded shipments to the US ahead of tariff deadlines, inflating Irish output and, consequently, data for the entire eurozone. This is largely responsible for the first quarter decline. title: SpaceX is Targeting the Largest ever Stock Market Debut and Believes it is Worth $1.75tn
author: editor
excerpt: Elon Musk’s rocket company SpaceX has revealed a proposed share price ahead of a potential listing that would be the biggest first public offering ever. SpaceX claimed in a filing outlining plans for its initial public offering (IPO) that its shares should trade at $135 (£100) each, lifting its own valuation of the corporation to almost $1.75tn. It is rare to put a price tag on a stock listing this long in advance and the figure is a considerable increase from SpaceX’s prior valuation of $1.25tn earlier this year. The disclosure does not guarantee that its shares will sell at the suggested price, which will ultimately be selected by buyers. Price may increase or decrease. SpaceX, which makes space exploration rockets and equipment but also owns xAI and Starlink, announced its expected share price more than a week before its public debut a step that is unusual. Companies usually only announce the price they wish to sell their shares at the day before they begin trading on the open market. SpaceX is due to begin trading on the Nasdaq stock index on 12 June, making their price estimate one of, if not the earliest price projections in stock market history. title: British teen Approved by Russia Over his Exposé on Suspected Moscow-Backed Crypto Laundering
author: editor
excerpt: A 17-year-old British boy’s whistleblowing on a purported Russian-backed money laundering network has reached the Kremlin and landed him on a new list of sanctioned individuals. Russia’s Foreign Ministry sanctioned Alexander Browder on Wednesday over what it called “defamatory speculations and false information”. The adolescent will now be prohibited from entering Russia, along with four other British nationals. Browder’s research, “Confronting the Illicit-Finance Hydra in Crypto Markets: Protecting Retail Investors and Disrupting Hostile Government Exploitation,” was published in March by the Henry Jackson Society think tank. In it, Browder exposed alleged illicit crypto laundering operations, stating that some $350 billion had been laundered by numerous regimes like Russia, Iran and North Korea. A Ruble-backed stablecoin a sort of digital currency designed to keep a stable value by pegging to fiat currencies — known as A7A5 was “one of the most prevalent issues facing the West” in the fight against laundering, he claimed. The UK Foreign Office believes Russia has been using tokens like A7A5 to try to dodge western sanctions and assist fund its military by moving money through crypto exchanges. In May, the British government issued a raft of fines against individuals associated with the network behind A7A5, which it said claimed to have moved more than $90 billion last year. title: US Secretary of State: Marco Rubio: Greenland Belongs to Denmark ‘for Now
author: editor
excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has rekindled the US’s long standing interest in Greenland. During a hearing Wednesday before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Congresswoman Sarah McBride asked him if he was “aware that Greenland is indeed part of Denmark.” Speculation over Greenland has been rampant since the return of US President Donald Trump to the White House, with the president constantly insisting that Washington needs to acquire the Danish territory to boost national defence. Trump has also warned China or Russia could capture the island if the US does not intervene. The administration has been talking to both Greenland and Denmark about using the island for “collective defence” and missile defence, Rubio told the committee on Wednesday. WE are in those discussions presently. “I think we’re in a good place on it,” Rubio added. At the height of the Cold War, the US was said to have maintained 17 military sites and over 10,000 personnel stationed on Greenland. The island has just one base, the Pituffik Space Base, the northernmost base of the US Department of Defense. 5. Catherine Tondelli | Global Entrepreneur, Corporate Meeting and Event Strategist, and Champion for Women’s Empowerment

Catherine Tondelli is a successful business owner and international leader. For over 30 years, she has helped companies grow in advertising, publishing, hotels, events and business communications. As the Founder and CEO of Meeting Angels, a Rome-based boutique agency specializing in venue sourcing, meeting and event strategy, Catherine helps international corporations, associations, and organizations across the US, Europe, the UK, and the Middle East optimize their operations, save time and money in their meeting and event planning and maximize their visibility. 

Her agency is proudly woman-certified through WEConnect International, featuring an all-women team dedicated to being a true “guardian angel” for clients from venue finding, contract negotiation to a flawless execution.

“True leadership isn’t just about delegation; it’s about working side by side, encouraging individuality, and lifting others as you grow.”

Beyond her agency, Catherine is a deeply committed institutional leader. She serves as the President of the Professional Women’s Association (PWA) of Rome, where she leads an eight-person board and a thriving community of over 150 members, an organization she successfully led with her board to grow by triple in numbers. Through target initiatives in mentorship, networking, workshops and education, she aims to support women at every stage of their professional development. 

Her global activism is supported by her role as G100 Italy Country Chair for Hospitality and Tourism, where she promotes women’s leadership worldwide.

Catherine grew up believing that financial independence is the best form of empowerment. She sees entrepreneurship as the most dependable path to economic freedom for women. This core belief comes from her mother, who worked until she was 85 and is her greatest inspiration. In practice, Catherine leads with empathy and a mindset for change. She focuses on active listening and creating environments where everyone has the chance to thrive.\

Her journey from San Diego to Rome, with an important stop in London, is described in her memoir, Three Coins in the Fountain (available on Amazon). The book highlights the humor and resilience needed to navigate those significant cultural shifts. Today, whether she is consulting for global executives, mentoring students, playing music, or caring for stray cats, Catherine approaches life with genuine optimism. For her, every unexpected turn is just another
opportunity to step up, inspire, and make a real impact.

6. Founder & Chairman – EFG-HUB Technologies

He is a Cameroonian entrepreneur, business strategist, and visionary founder of EFG-HUB Technologies, a global ecosystem connecting Africa, the Gulf, and international markets through technology, trade, logistics, media, and innovation.

With more than 15 years of experience across Africa, Europe, and the Middle East, he has dedicated his work to helping African businesses, entrepreneurs, and young innovators access global opportunities through digital transformation and cross-border collaboration.

Under his leadership, EFG-HUB Technologies has expanded into a multi-division ecosystem covering B2B trade, corporate services, logistics, AI & cybersecurity, media, branding, and professional training.

Through EFG Vision, the media and branding division of the ecosystem, Ambe also promotes African entrepreneurship, innovation, and digital storytelling through podcasts, branding solutions, and global media engagement.

Driven by a strong belief in ethical leadership, innovation, and youth empowerment, Ambe Fidelis Ndang continues to advocate for sustainable business growth, digital inclusion, and Africa’s integration into the future global economy.

“Connecting Africa to the Future Through Innovation, Trade & Technology.”

7. Natanya Wachtel | Behavioral Science-Powered Marketing, Healthcare Strategist, and Advocate for Purpose-Driven Wellness

Natanya Wachtel is a behavioral psychology-based healthcare leader and show host who changes how people approach mental health and personal wellness. For over 20 years, she has combined consumer psychology and data analytics to help wellness and healthcare brands connect with people more authentically.

As the founder of New Solutions Network, Natanya leads a specialized collective of companies that, in part, uses behavioral science to design compassionate, effective commercialization strategies, health education programs, and media. Founded in 2008, the network has grown into a multi-division ecosystem spanning behavioral science consulting, media production, wellness innovation, life sciences, and ethical technology. On the consulting side, it advises Fortune 500 companies and mission-driven organizations on how people actually think, decide, and change.

Its media division, The Natanya Experience, produces original programming including Psych + Hip Hop and Game Mindset — that carries mental health conversations into high-pressure worlds like sports, entertainment, and law enforcement. Its wellness arm builds the tools to match: identity-mapping frameworks, applications, and immersive technology for the nervous system’s conventional systems are slow to reach. The throughline across every division is a single conviction, that people do their best work, and their best healing, when they are met as whole human beings rather than the version that fits the org chart.

Her network partners exclusively with organizations that prioritize health and public benefit, ethical innovation, and community support over corporate profit.

“I don’t teach the way out from a mountaintop. I teach it from inside the climb, because that is the only place I have ever stood.” 

Natanya is deeply involved in building modern mental health tools. She was the co-founder of evrmore.io, an empathy-driven artificial intelligence platform designed to help young people build emotional resilience and navigate social challenges. Starting in June 2026, she will host the Hear Me Now! podcast, filmed at the United Nations in partnership with Montessori Model United Nations (MMUN).

Natanya grew up traveling the world alongside her mother, an immigrant who became a global corporate executive. Witnessing severe wealth and healthcare disparities at a young age inspired her lifelong commitment to giving back. Today, she translates that commitment into direct community action. She has donated numerous university scholarships and served as Board Chair for Women Who Create, a New York City nonprofit that mentors and provides scholarships to young women of color.

Her professional standing is matched by a personal resilience that few of her peers have been tested by. A mother of five and a young widow who later remarried, Natanya has rebuilt her life and her company not once but twice. In 2015, a spinal injury left her temporarily paralyzed and bedridden for a year; she relearned how to walk and rebuilt her health and her business from the ground up. A decade later, in 2025, she fell from a former product partner’s stage at an industry event, sustaining a traumatic brain injury, a broken arm, and months in a neck brace. She rebuilt a brain, a voice, and a company at the same time — choosing meditation, non-invasive neurostimulation, and integrative protocols over the multiple surgeries she was advised to have, and exceeding every recovery marker her doctors set.

That lived experience is not a sidebar to her work; it is the operating system beneath it. Building a company devoted to human flourishing while privately fighting her way back from collapse forced a reckoning most wellness leaders never face: what it means to sell healing while still doing the work yourself. It is the reason New Solutions Network is built for real nervous systems shaped under pressure, not for ideal conditions that almost no one actually has.

Her work has been recognized widely. She serves on the Fast Company and Harvard Business Review Executive Boards, has been featured in Forbes, Psychology Today, TEDx, and across more than thirty-five publications, and has received the Marquis Who’s Who Humanitarian Award, the HEaL Brilliance in Healthcare honor, a World’s Leaders Magazine cover, and recognition on the INNOVATE100 and Dreamers & Doers Women to Watch lists. She writes openly about leadership, identity, and healing for outlets including Fast Company. Whether she is advising healthtech founders, mentoring the next generation, or rebuilding herself again, Natanya leads with radical honesty, proof that the most durable leadership is forged, not credentialed.

“Women in law do not ask for permission. They build, transform, and lead with excellence.” 

Dr. Karen Figueiredo is a lawyer who believes the legal system should protect real people. She started her own firm, Karen Figueiredo Advocacia, to defend social rights and assist everyday citizens. Karen focuses on Social Security Law, helping people with retirement planning, disability claims, and public pensions. She is known for combining strong legal skills with kindness, ensuring her clients achieve financial security and peace of mind.

Beyond her office, Karen is a committed leader in the legal community. She made history by becoming the first woman elected and then re-elected to preside over the 35th subsection of OABRJ. During her leadership, she worked to support local lawyers, ensuring that professionals outside the big cities felt valued, connected, and heard.

Today, she helps shape the future of her profession through several key roles. She serves as the Vice Director of Social Security Affairs for OAB/RJ and collaborates directly with the National Social Security Law Commission. She is also an active member of the Brazilian Association of Women in Legal Careers, where she advocates for fellow female professionals.

For Karen, traditional legal values and modern thinking go hand in hand. She respects the foundations of law but understands that today’s world needs quick problem-solving and clear communication. She does not let old workplace barriers hold her back. Instead, she uses her position to open doors for other women, mentoring the next generation of lawyers and demonstrating that true leadership involves lifting others as you grow.

9. Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu | A Thoughtful Approach to Care, Research, and Human Connection 

Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu has built a career that reflects both discipline and curiosity. Trained as a family physician, she completed her medical studies at the University of Iași in Romania and later pursued research in family medicine at Maastricht University in the Netherlands. Early on, she showed a clear interest in understanding not just disease, but the many factors that shape a person’s health.

Over the years, her work has taken her far beyond the clinic. She has presented her research at more than 140 international conferences and has published over 60 articles in well-regarded medical journals. Her role within the academic community is equally active. She is a member of the Academy for Professionalism in Healthcare, contributes to The Journal of Patient Experience as part of its editorial review board, and serves as an Associate Editor for Primera Scientific Publication. These roles reflect her ongoing commitment to improving both medical knowledge and patient care.

One of the most defining aspects of her journey is her decision to build a private practice based on a medical home model. For more than a decade, she has worked directly with patients in their own environments. This shift has allowed her to observe details that are often missed in traditional consultations. Daily routines, family dynamics, access to resources, and even subtle patterns of communication all play a role. Through this approach, she has gained a deeper understanding of how health is influenced by more than just clinical symptoms.

Dr. Bistriceanu often speaks about the importance of communication. In her view, the way people interact can shape both mental and physical well-being. Simple qualities such as respect, honesty, and kindness are not abstract ideals. They are practical elements that affect how people feel and function. She believes that no one exists in isolation, and that everyday exchanges, whether personal or professional, leave a lasting impact on health.

Her approach to medicine also focuses on looking beneath the surface. Rather than treating isolated symptoms, she works to understand the root of imbalance. This perspective often leads to better outcomes, not only in terms of treatment but also in patient satisfaction and long-term stability. It is a method that requires patience, attention, and a willingness to listen.

Alongside her medical and academic work, Dr. Bistriceanu is also a published poet. She has authored seven volumes, offering a different lens through which she explores human experience. This creative side adds another layer to her work, one that values reflection as much as precision.

In many ways, her journey brings together science and sensitivity. She continues to contribute to healthcare with a steady focus on people, not just processes. Her work serves as a reminder that good medicine is not only about knowledge, but also about understanding the lives behind each patient.

10. Günter Loibl on Reshaping Music Production and Distribution

Leaders like Günter Loibl are shaping the music industry with their passion for music and new technologies. As a founder and CEO of multiple successful music business companies, his vision is to bridge music production, digital distribution, and emerging audio technologies.

Starting his entrepreneurial endeavours with Rebeat, Günter established it as a physical distribution for CDs and DVDs. Eventually, adapting to technological advancements, he founded Rebeat Digital, contributing his part to the rise of digital music. Currently, Rebeat Digital has become a leading name in the field, with its in-house developed Music Enterprise Software (MES) at the core. From digital music distribution to sales analyses, the MES integrates everything into a single system, empowering easy music distribution from around the globe. 

Additionally, Loibl bought the majority of Preiser Records in 2013, one of Austria’s oldest and most established classic labels, which currently comprises over 30,000 titles. Moreover, he is the co-founder of Legitary, built along with Nermina Mumic, a PhD graduate from the Technical University of Vienna. The startup’s mission is clear: to improve transparency in music streaming data for stores, labels, and artists while reducing errors and preventing fraud in royalty accounting. The venture even won the MIDEM Lab award in Cannes in 2019, reflecting the recognition it earned in the music startup industry. 

With a strong vision to promote vinyl culture, Loibl co-founded the Vinyl Alliance, a global organisation that strengthens the vinyl record business. His contribution to bringing innovative solutions in the field of music has resulted in Loibl building a Dolby Atmos recording studio at Rebeat’s headquarters. Envisioning to channel his passion for music in the right direction, Loibl reflects, “I have recently returned more actively to hands-on recording and mixing, releasing several records with Viennese pop-rapper Syko.” 

Known for building artist-focused platforms, Loibl launched Gimme Beat, and Yeebra in 2025, a next-generation physical music distribution platform designed for independent artists and smaller labels. By making production and distribution easily accessible to all, he empowers artists to reach a wide audience without the need for traditional labels.

Aligning his passion for music with his business endeavours, Günter Loibl is reimagining music through innovation and artist-centred developments.

title: Germany is Unable to Win UN Security Council Seat
author: editor
excerpt: Germany on Wednesday failed to secure a seat on the UN Security Council for the first time, with Portugal and Austria winning more votes for the two Western European seats available from 2027. The UN Security Council has 15 members, five permanent – the United States, Russia, China, France and the United Kingdom – and 10 elected for staggered two-year periods, the seats allotted for different world regions. The General Assembly, voting by secret ballot, elected Portugal and Austria to the European seats, with 134 and 131 votes, respectively. Germany, which has previously served six terms, got 104. Germany is a member of the G7, Europe’s biggest economy and seen as the continent’s political and security anchor. Zimbabwe was the only contender for an African member and was elected with 182 votes. Trinidad and Tobago, which similarly faced no opposition, won the seat for the Latin American and Caribbean group with 181 votes. A second round to select between the Philippines and Kyrgyzstan for the Asia seat was under way on Wednesday. The five elected countries will replace Pakistan, Somalia, Greece, Denmark and Panama, commencing 1 January 2027. title: Hackers Duped Instagram’s AI Chatbot Into Giving Access to other People’s Accounts
author: editor
excerpt: Instagram claims it has fixed an issue in which hackers tricked its AI assistance tool into allowing them access to other users’ accounts. According to assertions made in photos and videos shared on social media, Instagram’s AI chatbot has enabled users to “hijack” accounts. Hackers can change passwords for other accounts by simulating their location and instructing AI to alter the corresponding emails.This problem has been rectified, and we are securing affected accounts,” Meta spokesperson Andy Stone told subscribers in a statement on X. In response to another post on X, Stone stated that suggestions the vulnerability was exploited to break into the accounts of international leaders were “completely false. According to tech news outlet 404media, posts exposing the vulnerability coincided with “a series of high-profile Instagram account takeovers,” including a verified account used by Barack Obama during his time in the White House. Prior to its recovery, the former US president’s account was said to have posted pro-Iran messages. It’s unknown how many Instagram accounts were impacted by the purported exploit. title: Canada Formally Requests Extension of the North American Free Trade Agreement.
author: editor
excerpt: As the July deadline to renegotiate the North American Free Trade Agreement with the United States and Mexico, known as the USMCA, approaches, Canada has formally requested its renewal. In Tuesday’s notice of renewal, Canada-US trade minister Dominic LeBlanc proposed that the pact be extended for another 16 years, calling it “highly beneficial” to all three countries. It comes as LeBlanc is in Washington to meet with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. Greer has completed the most recent round of official bilateral talks with Mexico, but negotiations with Canada have stalled, with the two countries appearing to disagree on sector-specific tariffs and vehicle production. Prime Minister Mark Carney has stated publicly that he wants sector-specific levies on Canadian steel, aluminum, cars, and timber eliminated or reduced, while Greer has suggested that Canada may be forced to accept some kind of US tariffs. Meanwhile, the United States has identified a number of trade irritants with Canada, including most Canadian provinces’ decision to remove American liquor from shelves in response to tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump. It also wants more access to Canadian markets for American businesses, particularly dairy, where Canada controls production quotas and imports to support local farmers. title: Israel Bombs Southern Lebanon, But the Fragile Truce with Hezbollah Looks to Hold

Lebanon stated that under an agreement made late Monday by US President Donald Trump, Israeli forces would not strike the capital in exchange for Hezbollah refraining from striking Israel. It came after Iran said Israeli involvement in Lebanon jeopardised efforts to settle its war with the US. Following the cease-fire statement, the Israeli military stated that it had intercepted two rockets fired into northern Israel. Hezbollah claimed to have struck Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, where officials confirmed fatal Israeli attacks. Lebanon stated that under an agreement made late Monday by US President Donald Trump, Israeli forces would not strike the capital in exchange for Hezbollah refraining from striking Israel. It came after Iran said Israeli involvement in Lebanon jeopardised efforts to settle its war with the US.

Following the cease-fire statement, the Israeli military stated that it had intercepted two rockets fired into northern Israel. Hezbollah claimed to have struck Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, where officials confirmed fatal Israeli attacks.

The Lebanese health ministry reportedly reported that four persons were killed and 127 injured after Israeli air raids damaged structures near the Jabal Amel hospital in Tyre on Monday afternoon. Thirty-nine hospital staff members were injured, with four in critical condition.
What remained outside the hospital on Tuesday was complete wreckage.

Concrete and twisted metal were scattered throughout the region. The beeping of wrecked cars and the crackle of felled electrical wires resonated through streets that were otherwise dead silent.

title: Anthropic, a Leading AI Company, has Announced its Intention to list on the US Stock Market
author: editor
excerpt: Anthropic, a global leader in artificial intelligence, has announced plans to become a publicly traded company in the United States. The company behind the popular chatbot Claude announced on Monday that it had submitted confidential documentation to the US Securities and Exchange Commission to conduct an initial public offering (IPO) this year. The company has stated that the price and number of shares to be offered have not yet been determined, but individuals will be able to purchase and trade shares in the firm on the stock market once it becomes public. The stock market plans of Anthropic, in conjunction with those of Elon Musk’s SpaceX, will likely serve as a test to determine whether investor appetite aligns with the escalating valuations of AI firms. Anthropic, which was established five years ago by chief executive Dario Amodei and a small group of other executives, recently secured funding from private investors, valuing the company at over $965 billion (£717 billion). Although the valuation was based on the assumption of future growth, it placed Anthropic ahead of OpenAI, which was most recently valued at $852 billion by private investors. After working for several years at OpenAI, the company’s chief executive, Dario Amodei, founded Anthropic. He left the company after an argument with its chief executive, Sam Altman. title: Japan’s Defense Minister Criticizes China’s “Huge Arsenal While Denying Militarism
author: editor
excerpt: Beijing’s accusation that Japan was practicing a “new militarism” has been refuted by Japan’s defense minister, who has criticized China for its military build-up and lack of openness. According to Shinjiro Koizumi, the world community’s “serious concern” was China and its “huge arsenal” of weapons. On the final day of a defense forum in Singapore, he made some of Tokyo’s sharpest comments to date in reaction to China’s persistent criticism of Japan’s military build-up under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Tensions between the two nations have long existed as a result of Japan’s invasion of China during World War Two. Jiang Bin, a spokesman for China’s national defense ministry, issued a warning last week that “the grey rhino of a remilitarized Japan is gathering speed” and urged the international community to “work together to contain Japan’s neo-militarism” one day prior to the start of the Singapore summit. Japan’s defense budget has been rising gradually, and for the past 12 years, it has established spending records. The country is getting closer to its goal of allocating 2% of its GDP to the military with its most recent budget, approved by the cabinet in December and totalling more than 9 trillion yen ($57 billion; £42 billion). The Japanese administration has repeatedly stated that it merely wants to strengthen its defenses and is not seeking conflict. title: A Dissident Who left China in a Rubber Boat is Detained by South Korea
author: editor
excerpt: After spending hours at sea, a Chinese dissident who left his nation in a rubber boat was arrested in South Korea. Human rights campaigner and former police officer Dong Guangping was discovered on Monday night in Korean waters. The BBC was informed by South Korea’s coast guard that Dong’s case will be referred to prosecutors and that he is being investigated for possible immigration breaches. The 68-year-old has been imprisoned multiple times in China due to his activism, which included participating in events honoring the crackdown at Tiananmen Square. Dong had fled China at least three times before, but each time he was returned. Mao Ning, a spokesperson for China’s foreign affairs ministry, said she was unaware of the event on Monday. Canada-based activist Sheng Xue claimed on X that she had spoken to Dong after he arrived in South Korea. Dong had left Weifang, a city in the central Shandong province, aboard an engine-powered rubber boat. He had informed her that by the time he arrived in the waters outside Taean, a county on the western coast of South Korea, he was “fainting” from tiredness after spending more than thirty hours at sea. According to the South Korean coast guard, they were able to save him after a fishing boat reported seeing Dong. author: editor
excerpt: Following a major film workers’ union’s request that its members refrain from working with Bollywood actor Ranveer Singh due to his alleged abrupt departure from the upcoming film Don 3, fans of Singh are reacting with disbelief. title: The Rudest Chalk Figure in the UK is Given a Glow-up to Prevent it From Fading in the Rain
author: editor
excerpt: Cut into a hillside close to the Dorset village of Cerne Abbas, the 55-meter chalk figure depicts a club-wielding, nude man whose silhouette has become one of the most instantly identifiable historical icons in the United Kingdom. However, the site’s owner and manager, the National Trust, claims that it is becoming more difficult to maintain the Giant’s prominence on the hillside due to shifting weather patterns. This week, volunteers and employees of the National Trust will apply tons of fresh chalk to the statue in order to restore his outline’s sharp whiteness. Luke Dawson, a National Trust ranger who assists with site maintenance, claims that while mild, moist weather allow algae to grow more readily, heavy winter rains are washing chalk from the slope more quickly. According to him, the Giant’s outline has been undergoing “a dulling effect” due to the wetter weather, making it less prominent and greener in between maintenance tasks. When it comes to directly linking the changes to climate change at a particular location, the Trust is hesitant.”It’s one of these things we cannot really prove,” Dawson says. “It is more just observation of what we are seeing up there. title: After a Months-Long Outage, Iran’s Internet is Finally Coming Back Online
author: editor
excerpt: Iran’s first vice-president announced that internet connectivity had been restored after being taken off about three months ago.On Tuesday, Mohammad Reza Aref posted on X: “The first step toward free and regulated access to cyberspace has been taken.” Internet monitoring groups Netblocks and Kentik reported “partial” restoration about 13:00 GMT, with the latter warning that most networks remained offline. Following the US and Israeli attacks on February 28, the Iranian regime stopped internet connection. Officials said that the goal was to prevent spying, espionage, and cyber-attack. It is one of the world’s longest national internet shutdowns. A Tehran-based video creator informed the BBC that he was able to connect to the internet using his house WiFi on Tuesday. “The main point is that some of my income will be returned,” he stated. Isik Mater, research director of the global internet tracker, stated on Tuesday that access has not been restored globally, with some geographical difference. The speaker reported more filtering, including limits on messaging apps like WhatsApp, compared to a comparable blackout imposed in January amid the regime’s assault on anti-government rallies. This means that families may still have difficulty contacting loved ones for the time being. title: Ferrari Reveals The First Fully Electric Automobile
author: editor
excerpt: Ferrari has introduced its first all-electric vehicle, the $640,000 (£474,320) Luce. The new model, the Italian brand’s first five-seater, deviates from traditional Ferrari design and was built in partnership with the LoveFrom agency, founded by former Apple design leader Sir Jony Ive. Social media responses to the debut have ranged from “straight to the junkyard trash” to a “absolute masterclass in design”.Due to low demand and fierce competition from Chinese firms, supercar rivals such as Lamborghini and Porsche have cut back their electric vehicle plans. Benedetto Vigna, Ferrari’s CEO, stated in Rome that the Luce, which means “light” in Italian, took a half decade to build. Ferrari intends to launch an electric vehicle (EV) after earlier ruling it out, preferring to produce hybrid vehicles that run on both gasoline and electricity. The Luce has a Ferrari-made electric motor on each wheel, allowing it to reach 60 mph (96 km/h) in approximately 2.5 seconds. The company stated that all of the components are manufactured in-house, allowing the automobile to be fixed by the company for many years to come, preserving the Luce’s market value. On behalf of King Norodom Sihamoni, Hun Sen, the acting head of state of Cambodia, issued an order pardoning his political foe. In a video released in 2017, Sokha, the former head of the now-dissolved Cambodian National Rescue Party (CNRP), claimed to have gotten backing from pro-democracy organizations in the United States. Since his conviction for treason in 2023, he has been under house arrest. Human rights organizations have generally mocked the accusations as being politically driven. Hun Sen said on Facebook that Sokha had been “pardoned” and included a picture of the royal proclamation that he had signed. The pardon, according to his son Hun Manet, who succeeded his father as prime minister in 2023, is “one more step towards strengthening national unity”. It followed the denial of an appeal against Sokha’s sentencing last month. However, it did not involve lifting the politician’s five-year restriction from leaving Cambodia. “Hun Sen’s decision to pardon Kem Sokha after more than eight years in arbitrary detention partially reverses a grievous injustice, but it is deplorable that Sokha remains barred from participating in politics or leaving the country,” stated Elaine Pearson, Human Rights Watch’s Asia director. title: An Explosion at a Chinese Coal Mine Claimed at Least 82 Lives
author: editor
excerpt: According to officials, a coal mine explosion in northern China has left at least 82 people dead and two missing. After initially stating that at least 90 people had perished, rescue officials lowered the death toll in an update late on Saturday. The deadliest mining accident in China since 2009 occurred at the Liushenyu Coal Mine in Shanxi province due to a methane explosion. When the explosion occurred on Friday at 19:29 local time (11:29 GMT), 247 personnel were allegedly on duty. More than 100 individuals were reportedly saved, and hundreds of rescuers were dispatched to the scene. According to Chinese President Xi Jinping, every effort must be made to care for the wounded and find survivors. Later, the nation’s state council declared that a “rigorous” inquiry would be carried out and that those found guilty would face “severe punishment.” Officials expressed regret for the uncertainty around the death toll, claiming that the initial chaos caused an imprecise headcount and an inaccurate total. They said that 128 patients, including two in serious condition, were receiving treatment at hospitals. The building fell on itself at around 3am (7pm GMT Saturday), severely destroying a nearby hotel where two of the 26 people who were rescued had been staying, they added. Rescue efforts were ongoing, but Sajili cautioned that activities would grow increasingly difficult after nightfall. According to officials, the authorized permit called for a nine-story condo-hotel, but a swimming pool was being built on the tenth floor. title: Trump Plays Diplomatic, Threatening Cards in Iran Conflict
author: editor
excerpt: The US President started the week with a declaration that he was “about an hour away from making the decision” to resume attacks on Iran. title: Turkish Court Removes Leader of Largest Opposition Party
author: editor
excerpt: A court in Turkiye has nullified the 2023 leadership vote of the main opposition Republican People’s Party (CHP) in a severe escalation against the country’s struggling opposition. It is the latest in a series of attempts against the CHP, the oldest political fixture in Turkiye, which chalked up a stunning victory over President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling AK Party in the 2024 local elections and is on the rise in the polls. The verdict on Thursday invalidated the result of a leadership election that installed current party chief Ozgur Ozel, with the court appointing the party’s former chair, Kemal Kilicdaroglu, who lost the election to Ozel, as interim leader. The case was considered as a test of Turkiye’s fragile balance between democracy and more centralised power, and the verdict might push the opposition into further confusion and possibly infighting. It might also increase President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s chances of extending his more than two-decade-long control over the massive NATO member country and significant emerging market economy. The CHP said the decision was a “attempted coup” while the government claims it uses courts to target political opponents and says it restored Turks’ faith in the rule of law. The secular and centrist CHP, which has been polling roughly even with Erdogan’s Islamic-rooted and conservative ruling AK Party, has also faced an unprecedented judicial crackdown since 2024, with hundreds of its members and elected officials arrested under corruption charges that the party denies. title: Meta Settles US Social Media Addiction Suit with School System
author: editor
excerpt: Meta has settled a lawsuit with a US school district that sued the owner of Instagram over costs to deal with a mental health crisis purportedly created by the company’s social media platforms. The first was to be the Breathitt School District in the US state of Kentucky which had been planning to sue social media corporations to cover such expenditures. The school district settled the same lawsuit last week with three other defendants: TikTok, Snap Inc and Google’s YouTube.”We have settled this case amicably,” a Meta representative told Reuters on Thursday of the accord, which permits it to avoid mounting a defence at current trial, while similar cases remain due for trial in the near future. The Breathitt County School District case was selected to be a test case for more than a thousand U.S. school districts that have sued social media corporations. The school district accused the businesses of intentionally making their platforms addictive, resulting in consequences ranging from anxiety and sadness to self-harm. It was seeking $60m (£44.7m) in damages to pay to combat the effects of social media on students, and an abatement programme. The district also wants the corporations to change the allegedly addictive nature of their platforms. Animal welfare has become an important global concern, yet many regions still face serious challenges related to animal abuse, illegal trade, and lack of proper protection systems. In this context, organizations that operate beyond local boundaries play a crucial role.

No Dogs Left Behind NGO is one such organization that focuses on rescuing dogs from extreme conditions and creating pathways for long-term safety. Rather than working only at a local level, it addresses issues that exist across different countries.

This article explains how the NGO functions, what makes it different, and why its work is relevant today.

What Defines No Dogs Left Behind NGO

At its core, No Dogs Left Behind is a nonprofit organization dedicated to rescuing dogs that are at immediate risk. Its work is not limited to taking in stray animals but extends to intervening in situations where survival is uncertain.

The NGO operates with a structured approach that includes:

  • Identifying high-risk situations
  • Conducting rescue operations
  • Providing medical care
  • Supporting recovery and rehabilitation
  • Facilitating adoption

This complete cycle ensures that rescued dogs are not only saved but also given a real opportunity for a stable future.

A Broader Scope Than Traditional Shelters

To understand the role of this NGO, it is important to recognize how it differs from typical animal shelters.

Most shelters:

  • Operate within a city or region
  • Take in animals that are surrendered or found
  • Focus mainly on housing and adoption

In contrast, No Dogs Left Behind:

  • Works across borders
  • Responds to urgent rescue situations
  • Handles complex logistics
  • Focuses on high-risk cases

This broader scope allows the organization to address problems that local shelters may not be equipped to handle.

Rescue Model and Operational Approach

The NGO’s rescue model is built around quick response and coordination.

When a situation is identified, the organization works with local teams or partners to carry out the rescue. This may involve navigating difficult environments and ensuring the safety of both animals and rescuers.

Once rescued, dogs are moved into a controlled environment where their condition can be assessed.

This phase is critical because it determines the next steps in their recovery.

Rehabilitation as a Core Priority

Rescue alone is not enough. Many dogs require significant care before they can be adopted.

The NGO focuses on rehabilitation through:

  • Veterinary treatment for injuries and illness
  • Proper nutrition to restore health
  • Safe shelter to reduce stress
  • Behavioral support when needed

This process may take time, but it is essential for ensuring that the dogs are ready for a new environment.

A strong rehabilitation system increases the chances of successful adoption.

International Adoption Network

One of the defining features of No Dogs Left Behind NGO is its international adoption program.

Instead of limiting placements to a local area, the organization connects rescued dogs with families in different countries.

This expands opportunities and helps more dogs find homes.

The adoption process generally includes:

  • Health checks and vaccinations
  • Legal documentation
  • Travel arrangements
  • Careful matching between dog and adopter

This structured approach helps ensure that each adoption is stable and long term.

The Importance of Awareness

In addition to rescue and adoption, the NGO plays a role in raising awareness.

By sharing information about animal cruelty and rescue efforts, it helps people understand issues that may not be widely discussed.

Awareness contributes to:

  • Better understanding of animal welfare
  • Increased support for rescue efforts
  • More responsible pet ownership

This educational aspect is an important part of long-term change.

Challenges Faced by Global NGOs

 

Operating at an international level brings several challenges.

These include:

  • Differences in regulations between countries
  • Limited infrastructure in certain areas
  • High costs related to transportation and care
  • Urgent situations that require immediate action

Despite these challenges, organizations like No Dogs Left Behind continue their work because of the need for intervention in critical cases.

Why This NGO Matters

The importance of No Dogs Left Behind NGO lies in its ability to address problems that go beyond local boundaries.

Its work matters because it:

  • Helps animals in extreme situations
  • Builds connections across countries
  • Encourages global responsibility toward animal welfare
  • Supports long-term solutions through adoption and awareness

This combination of rescue, care, and education makes it a significant contributor to the broader animal welfare ecosystem.

Final Thoughts

No Dogs Left Behind NGO represents a structured and global approach to animal rescue. It focuses not only on saving lives but also on creating sustainable outcomes through rehabilitation and adoption.

For individuals interested in supporting meaningful animal welfare efforts, understanding how such organizations operate is essential.

By combining direct action with awareness, the NGO continues to play an important role in addressing animal cruelty on a global scale.

No Dogs Left Behind NGO is an international nonprofit focused on rescuing dogs from dangerous and abusive situations. It provides medical care, rehabilitation, and helps dogs find homes through adoption programs across different countries.

Unlike local shelters, the NGO operates internationally and focuses on high-risk rescue cases. It also manages complex logistics and works in areas where animal protection systems may be limited.

The organization identifies urgent situations and works with local teams to carry out rescues. After that, dogs are moved to safe environments for medical care and recovery.

Yes, it runs an international adoption program that connects rescued dogs with families worldwide. The process includes health checks, documentation, and safe transportation.

Awareness helps people understand animal welfare issues and encourages responsible behavior. It also helps build support for rescue operations and long-term change.

title: Police Said a Tesla Cybertruck Driver was Detained after Using Wade Mode” While Driving into a Lake
author: editor
excerpt: A guy in Texas has been taken into custody on suspicion of purposefully using the “wade mode” function of his Tesla Cybertruck by driving it into a lake. The car was abandoned by the driver and occupants after it took on water and became trapped, according to the Grapevine Police Department, which claimed its officers were summoned to Grapevine Lake in north Texas on Monday to retrieve the vehicle. According to Tesla’s online documentation, wade mode enables a Cybertruck “to enter and drive through bodies of water, such as rivers or creeks” at a maximum depth of 81.5 cm (32 inches). According to police, the driver was detained on suspicion of driving in a restricted area of the lake and of violating other water safety equipment regulations. The Grapevine Fire Department Water Rescue Team assisted police in the removal of the partially submerged vehicle from close to the lake’s south bank “The vehicle became disabled and took on water” after “the driver stated he intentionally drove into the lake to use the Cybertruck’s “Wade Mode” feature,” according to the police statement. excerpt: In an effort to defeat incumbent Senator John Cornyn in the Republican primary run-off on Tuesday, US President Donald Trump has endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. By endorsing Paxton, Trump is endorsing a politician from Texas who has been the president’s close buddy for a long time, but who also has a lot of political baggage. In a state with a long history of choosing Republicans, many Democrats view Paxton as the weaker of the two contenders and are excited about what they see as a chance to change a Senate seat. Cornyn’s fellow Senate Republicans, many of whom have worked with the Texan for decades and see him as a friend and partner, were shocked by Trump’s action. Paxton was referred to as “ethically challenged” by Senator Susan Collins of Maine. Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska expressed her “supremely disappointed” feelings. But Trump seems to have different tastes. A Texas lawmaker who has long been the president’s close supporter is receiving backing from the president. In his capacity as attorney general, he supported Trump’s attempts to reverse the 2020 presidential election results. title: At Least Eight People Have Been killed in a Collision Involving a Freight Train and a Bus in Bangkok
author: editor
excerpt: At least eight people have been killed and scores more have been injured as a result of a collision that occurred in Bangkok between a freight train and a public bus. The accident, according to officials from the police and rescue services, caused the fire that devoured the public bus on Saturday. During the incident, several automobiles in the vicinity were also struck, prompting the rescue and fire departments to respond to the scene. An investigation into the full reason of the collision is still ongoing, according to the authorities. title: Taiwan Maintains its Independence Despite Trump’s Warning
author: editor
excerpt: After US President Donald Trump warned Taiwan not to formally declare its independence from China, Taiwan has maintained that it is a sovereign, independent republic. Trump claimed he had “made no commitment either way” over the self-governing island, which China claims as part of its territory and has not ruled out capturing by force, following a two-day summit in Beijing. Trump also stated that he would soon decide whether to accept a $11 billion ($8 billion) package of weaponry to be sold to Taiwan following discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Although the US administration is legally required to give Taiwan a weapon for self-defense, it has often had to balance this commitment with preserving diplomatic ties with China. Lai Ching-te, the president of Taiwan, has previously said that as Taiwan already considers itself to be an independent state, it does not need to formally declare its independence. Taiwan’s status as “a sovereign, independent democratic country” was deemed “self-evident” by presidential spokesperson Karen Kuo on Saturday.She did, however, emphasize that Taiwan was dedicated to upholding the current state of affairs with China, in which Taiwan neither combines with China nor proclaims independence from it. title: Adanis From India Agree to pay $18 Million to Resolve a Civil Fraud Prosecution in the United States
author: editor
excerpt: In order to resolve a civil fraud action brought by the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Indian billionaire Gautam Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani have agreed to pay a total of $18 million in fines. The Adanis were accused by the FCC in 2024 of deceiving US investors about anti-bribery procedures while attempting to collect money through a bond offering and paying bribes to Indian officials for prominent renewable energy projects. Although a court must approve the planned deal, markets reacted favorably to the news, with shares of the Adani Group company surging on Friday. One of the biggest corporate empires in India, the Adani Group has holdings in the aviation and energy industries. In addition to prohibiting the Adanis from breaking important US anti-fraud statutes pertaining to investor deceit, securities fraud, and market manipulation in the future, the proposed deal does not acknowledge or refute the charges. The securities agency accused the Adanis in the 2024 lawsuit of raising $750 million, including about $175 million from US investors, while allegedly deceiving them about Adani Green Energy’s adherence to anti-bribery regulations. The accusations have been deemed “baseless” by the Adani Group. The 63-year-old Adani is among the richest persons in the world, with a net worth of $82 billion, according to Forbes. title: For The First Time in 70 years, Honda Experiences a Yearly Loss
author: editor
excerpt: Due to the failure of its investments in the electric vehicle (EV) market, Japanese automaker Honda experienced its first annual loss in 70 years. Honda reported a total operating loss of ¥423 billion ($2.68 billion: £1.99 billion) for the year ending in March 2026, indicating that demand for EVs has not been as robust as the business had anticipated. The company announced that it would source parts from China, where prices are lower, to reduce costs, and that it was abandoning some of its EV production targets. It said that changes in US policy, including as the removal of tax breaks for US consumers buying EVs and the application of tariffs, contributed to its losses. President Donald Trump eliminated tax incentives worth up to $7,500 (£5,500) for US consumers who bought new electric vehicles in September 2025. Even if the tariffs were lowered from 25% to 15% in 2025, his taxes on imported automobiles and auto parts also hurt revenues at a number of significant automakers. Since going public on the stock market in 1957, Honda has expanded to become the second-largest automaker in Japan. Its enormous size and heritage nature, according to analysts, make it challenging to swiftly adjust to sharp fluctuations in EV demand. Honda announced that it would now focus on expanding its profitable motorbike division, its financial services division, and its hybrid-vehicle production. title: Socialists Reject the EPP’s Attempt to Move EU-US Trade Negotiations Forward
author: editor
excerpt: The European People’s Party (EPP) and the Socialists and Democrats (S&D), the two biggest parties in the European Parliament, are at odds over the EU-US trade agreement after the most recent attempt to put it into effect failed last week. In an effort to refine the specifics of the agreement, the EPP has, in recent days, attempted to advance the next round of negotiations between the European Parliament and EU member states. However, according to persons acquainted with the situation who spoke to Euronews, Bernd Lange, the German Socialist MEP who leads the Trade Committee, rejected the request and insisted on preserving May 19 as the date for the next round of negotiations. In accordance with the agreement reached last summer in Turnberry between US President Donald Trump and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Trump has given the Europeans until July 4th to complete it, which would lower EU taxes on US exports to zero and cap US tariffs at 15%. MEPs generally anticipate a favorable resolution prior to Trump’s deadline, but the dispute over when the next negotiations will take place reveals varying opinions across political factions regarding the severity of the situation. In commercial aviation, two primary types of fuel are used. While Jet A is primarily used in North America, Jet A-1 is the worldwide standard for most overseas operations. The two are basically the same and are both types of kerosene. Jet A-1’s freezing point is lower than Jet A’s, though. This implies that it can be utilized more adaptably on long-distance and arctic journeys, according to Fox. Asia is the region most affected by the present energy crisis. Nearly 90% of the gas and oil that crossed the Strait of Hormuz last year was intended for the area. It is used by ordinary people to generate electricity, fuel their cars, and heat their homes. It is necessary for businesses to run a large manufacturing base in the area. South East Asia, in particular, is especially exposed to the blockade in the Persian Gulf. Over the past ten years, even oil-producing nations like Malaysia and Indonesia have progressively begun to produce less and import more. The kind of oil produced in the Middle East and the methods used by its nations to process it also contribute to the vulnerability.
