content:
In every industry, there exist pioneering leaders who make a difference with their bold vision and commitment to excellence. The global leaders featured in this article are a reminder that adding the right vision with execution can turn the tables. Their innovative solutions and thriving businesses are not just bridging market gaps, they are reshaping the way industries operate. 

Recognized for their visionary approach and resilience to bring a positive change, these global leaders are setting new industry standards. 

Top Global Leaders To Know

In the sections that follow, you will learn about the visionary global leaders of the current times who are leading transformation in their fields. With years of experience in their respective fields, these global leaders are turning challenges into milestones. With inspirational journeys, these global leaders are emerging as strong voices for countless.

1. Dr. Desziree Richardson | Redefining Empowerment Through Voice, Vision and Global Impact

“Empowerment is not a moment. It is a movement built through action, intention and unwavering belief.”

For Dr. Desziree Richardson, empowerment is not just a cause. It is a lifelong commitment to creating spaces where women are seen, heard and celebrated. As a global advocate for women’s rights and humanitarian progress, her work bridges purpose with impact, reaching communities across borders and cultures.

Her journey is rooted in a deep belief that true influence comes from uplifting others. Through her initiatives, Dr. Richardson has consistently created platforms that spotlight women who are driving change in their own communities. Her work goes beyond recognition. It fosters connection, leadership and a shared sense of possibility among women worldwide.

At the center of this vision is FACE OF WOHA (Women of Heart Awards), a global platform designed to honour resilience, leadership and innovation among women. More than an awards initiative, it serves as a powerful storytelling space. It is a place where voices are amplified, journeys are shared and inspiration travels far beyond the stage. Through this, she continues to build a global network of women who lead with purpose and passion.

What sets Dr. Richardson apart is her multidimensional approach to transformation. As a vibratory voice healer, she brings a unique dimension to personal development, using the power of sound and frequency to create experiences of calm, clarity and emotional release. Her voice, often described as deeply resonant and restorative, has become a tool for healing as much as it is for connection.

Alongside her advocacy and healing work, she has also stepped into the entrepreneurial space with ventures like Happy Mood Swagger, a brand that reflects her philosophy of confidence, self-expression and joy. Each initiative she builds carries a consistent thread. The intention is to inspire positivity while encouraging individuals to step into their most authentic selves.

Her influence extends into global humanitarian and leadership spaces as well. Through her involvement in diversity and inclusion initiatives and her role in international advocacy for child welfare, Dr. Richardson continues to champion causes that create meaningful, long-term change. Her work reflects a strong commitment to building a more inclusive and compassionate world.

Recognised globally for her contributions, including cultural honours that celebrate her role in fostering unity, Dr. Richardson stands as a symbol of purpose-driven leadership. Her journey is not defined by titles alone, but by the lives she continues to impact.

At its core, her message remains clear. Empowerment begins when individuals recognise their own voice and use it to create change not just for themselves, but for others.

LinkedIn | Instagram | Website

2. Brendon Bell | Building Conviction Capital Across Asia-Pacific and Africa

“Great investing is rarely about access alone. It is about conviction, timing, and the ability to see structural opportunity before the market names it.”

For Brendon Bell, capital is not simply deployed. It is directed with intent, shaped by pattern recognition, operating discipline, and a long view of where value is forming before it becomes obvious. As an investor, founder, and operator, Brendon has spent the last decade building a career defined by disciplined capital allocation, cross-market fluency, and a strong instinct for asymmetric opportunities across public and private markets.

Today, that experience informs his next chapter: a conviction-led venture platform designed to connect Asia-Pacific innovation with one of the world’s fastest-growing and most underserved markets, Africa.

Brendon’s path into venture capital has been shaped by both market experience and operating depth. Over the last ten years, he has built a personal investing track record averaging 22.5% per annum across global public markets, spanning Wall Street, London, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore, and the ASX. His investment approach has been grounded in disciplined position sizing, macro-aware sector rotation, options strategy, and a deliberate move into concentrated private opportunities.

That experience has given Brendon more than performance. It has given him a practical understanding of how capital moves across cycles, markets, and asset classes, and where opportunity tends to emerge before it becomes widely recognised.

This perspective has been reinforced by direct operating experience.

Brendon was an early backer of a private Australian fintech, supporting the business with both capital and strategic input as it scaled. That early conviction has since grown into an estimated 30x return on invested capital and remains one of the defining outcomes in his private market track record.

Alongside investing, Brendon is also the Founder and CEO of Gybe Sailing Charters, a premium experiential business operating across Sydney Harbour and Australia’s east coast. There, he has built a reputation for operational discipline, brand clarity, and turning a lifestyle-led business into a scalable, cash-generative platform.

Together, these experiences shape the investment philosophy behind his current venture strategy.

His focus is clear: concentrated, high-conviction capital deployed into category-defining founders building across fintech, wealthtech, proptech, and the broader productivity and automation stack, with a differentiated focus on the Asia, Australia, and Africa corridor.

For Brendon, this is not simply a geographic thesis. It is a structural one.

As digital infrastructure expands and demographic growth accelerates, some of the most compelling opportunities are emerging in markets where financial systems are being rebuilt, SME ecosystems are digitising quickly, and mobile-first infrastructure is transforming access and scale.

This is where Brendon sees a clear edge.

Through long-standing relationships, trusted partners, and years of exposure across Asian and African business networks, he brings founders more than capital. He offers access to markets and strategic corridors that remain overlooked by many traditional investors, but are increasingly shaping the next generation of high-growth economies.

From cross-border payments and embedded finance to SME credit infrastructure, agritech, and mobile-led financial systems, Brendon’s focus is on businesses solving structural problems in markets where adoption is rising fast and legacy systems remain open to reinvention.

What sets this approach apart is not just reach, but capital fluency.

Brendon’s experience across public equities, options, private markets, and multi-asset allocation has built a practical understanding of how liquidity, credit, and macro cycles shape value long before they become consensus. In a market where capital efficiency matters more than capital abundance, that perspective is increasingly valuable.

It is this combination of market discipline, operator instinct, and frontier-market access that defines his investment lens.

For Brendon, the opportunity is clear. The next era of venture will not be defined only by where capital has historically concentrated, but by where it can move with the greatest conviction next.

LinkedIn | Website 

3. Kelly Marie Mackinnon | From Potential to Precision in Business Growth

“Stay focused on yourself, your goals, and your vision; the rest will fall into place.”

For Kelly Marie Mackinnon, entrepreneurship is not just about building businesses. It is about building people, ideas, and long-term impact. With over 15 years of experience across industries, she has positioned herself as a driving force behind brands that aim to grow with clarity and purpose.

Based in Dubai since 2008, Kelly Marie is the Founder and CEO of KMM Dubai, a company that brings together business mentoring, events, and brand management under one strategic vision. Her work focuses on helping businesses move beyond potential and into execution, creating structures that support sustainable growth.

Through KMM Dubai, she has built a strong reputation in the events and promotions space, delivering large-scale, high-impact projects. The company’s portfolio includes globally recognised platforms such as The Amazing Race, Global Soccer Awards, Dubai World Cup, and Abu Dhabi Formula One. These collaborations reflect not only operational excellence but also an ability to navigate complex, high-visibility environments.

At the core of her work is mentorship. Kelly partners with entrepreneurs across different industries and growth stages, helping them align their vision with actionable strategies. Her approach is practical and results-driven, focused on turning ideas into structured, scalable businesses rather than short-term wins.

Beyond mentoring and events, she continues to expand her footprint as an investor. She is actively involved with Gym Clothing Co., a homegrown brand that combines performance, style, and accessibility. Her involvement reflects a strong belief in supporting emerging businesses that bring both innovation and value to the market.

Her growth mindset extends internationally as well. Kelly is currently leading the expansion of KMM Dubai into the UK, working with clients such as Caffe Monza while introducing business masterclasses designed to equip entrepreneurs with practical tools and insights.

Kelly’s journey is deeply personal. She has spoken about overcoming early life challenges that shaped her independence and resilience. These experiences continue to influence her perspective on success, reinforcing her belief that mindset plays a defining role in what individuals can achieve.

For her, success is not measured in milestones alone. It is reflected in the ability to create opportunities for others, to support growth, and to contribute to a larger ecosystem where businesses and individuals rise together.

Her philosophy remains clear. Stay focused, stay consistent, and build something that lasts.

LinkedIn | Website

4. Irina Lazar-Visu | Reimagining Professional Learning for a Changing World

“Professional training should not be a checkbox. It should be a catalyst for growth, clarity, and transformation.”

For Irina Lazar-Visu, professional education is not simply about acquiring new skills. It is about creating the conditions for people and businesses to evolve with confidence, relevance, and resilience. As Co-Founder and CEO of I-Grow, Irina is building a professional training ecosystem designed to make learning more accessible, practical, and aligned with the real needs of modern professionals and organisations.

Irina’s path to founding I-Grow is shaped by a career that bridges technical expertise, corporate leadership, and international governance. With an academic foundation in chemical engineering from the Polytechnic University in Bucharest, she later expanded her expertise through studies in banking, business administration, and executive leadership, earning qualifications from Spiru Haret University, the Romanian Banking Institute, and ESSEC Business School in France.

Over the course of 20 years in banking and financial services, including 15 years in risk management and controlling, Irina built a career at the intersection of governance, compliance, leadership, and operational excellence. From Credit Analyst and HR Manager to Director of Operational Risk and Permanent Controls, she held senior positions across Société Générale Group and Orange Bank – Orange Group in both Romania and France. Her work placed her at the center of decision-making, where she designed governance models, strengthened risk and compliance frameworks, and led multicultural teams across Europe, Russia and West Africa.

This experience shaped more than her expertise. It revealed a critical gap in how professional learning is often delivered.

Too often, training remains fragmented, generic, and disconnected from the realities professionals face in fast-changing business environments. Irina recognized that while organizations are investing in learning, many still struggle to access the right expertise, compare relevant programmes, and translate training into measurable impact. That insight became the foundation for I-Grow.

Launched in 2026, I-Grow was created with a clear mission: to make professional development more intelligent, more transparent, and more meaningful. I-Grow is built around two main pillars: a technical solution which is an aggregation, comparison and intermediation platform gathering and providing professional training offers existing on the French market and a human centered solution consisting in tailor-made training programs developed by freelance expert trainers.  As a professional training aggregation, comparison, and intermediation platform, I-Grow helps organizations and professionals identify the right learning opportunities, connect with trusted experts, and access training that is relevant, practical, and built for real business outcomes.

At its core, I-Grow is designed to simplify and strengthen the learning journey. By bringing together expert-led programs, curated learning pathways, and a more transparent approach to training discovery, the company aims to solve a growing challenge in professional education: not the lack of training, but the difficulty of finding the right training that creates lasting value.

For Irina, this is where the future of learning is headed.

She sees professional training evolving from static, one-size-fits-all instruction into a more dynamic and strategic business function. As industries transform under the pressure of digital acceleration, regulatory complexity, AI adoption, and global market shifts, learning must become more agile, personalized, and directly tied to business performance. The organizations that will lead in the future are those that treat learning not as an isolated HR initiative, but as a core lever of growth, adaptability, and competitive advantage.

This belief is central to I-Grow’s value proposition.

The company is built on the idea that effective training should do more than inform. It should enable better decisions, stronger leadership, sharper execution, and more resilient organizations. Through I-Grow, Irina and her co-founder Iouri Goloubtzoff aim to create a platform and training programs where learning is not reduced to content delivery but elevated into a strategic tool for transformation.

What distinguishes I-Grow is not only its model, but also the values it is built on.

Irina believes meaningful learning must be rooted in clarity, trust, and relevance. Training should be practical, not performative. It should empower people with tools they can apply, not just theories they can repeat. It should create space for reflection, challenge assumptions, and support long-term capability building rather than short-term knowledge transfer.

These same principles shape how I-Grow approaches partnerships and ways of working. The company promotes collaboration over hierarchy, curiosity over rigidity, and substance over surface. It is committed to building learning environments that are rigorous, human-centered, and grounded in real-world application. For Irina, professional growth happens best in spaces where expertise is shared generously, critical thinking is encouraged, and development is approached as a continuous process rather than a one-time intervention.

A recognized conference speaker and trusted advisor, Irina brings to this work a rare ability to translate complex regulatory and business realities into practical executive learning. Her strength lies not only in understanding systems, but in helping others navigate them with greater confidence and competence.

Through I-Grow, she is now channeling that experience into a larger mission: helping professionals learn better, helping organizations grow stronger, and helping education evolve into a more strategic force for business and human development.

For Irina, the goal is clear. Learning should not only keep pace with change. It should help shape what comes next.

LinkedIn | Website 

5. Ramzy Maher | Bringing Egypt’s Stories to the Modern World

Growing up surrounded by Egypt’s incredible history, Ramzy Maher has always known that the best way to see the country is through the stories it tells. Today, he uses his 50-year legacy at Emeco Travel and Gray Line Egypt to help the rest of the world discover those stories.

Ramzy acts as a bridge between Egypt’s ancient wonders and the modern digital world. He spends his days working with global travel platforms and tech companies to ensure that when someone dreams of visiting Egypt, they find high-quality, seamless, and unique experiences waiting for them.

He is especially most passionate about moving beyond standard sightseeing. Whether he is designing special trips for women or crafting deep tours for solo travelers, his goal is to make travel feel personal and premium. For Ramzy, it isn’t just about getting people to a destination; it’s about making sure Egypt stays connected, innovative, and unforgettable for every person who visits.

For Ramzy, this work is more than a job, it is a personal mission to share the authentic heart of his country. He keeps creating new opportunities for explorers by fusing his strong industry background with a modern, forward-thinking viewpoint, making sure that the enchantment of Bile and beyond is always just a few clicks away. 

LinkedIn | Website

6. Alf Hellström | Building Stronger Leaders, Teams, and Organizations

“Leadership is not tested when things are easy. It is revealed when pressure rises, the pace quickens, and people are asked to perform beyond the familiar.”

For Alf Hellström, leadership has never been a theoretical exercise. It has always been shaped in real environments, under real pressure, where behaviour matters more than intention and culture is defined by what people do, not what they say.

With a background as an officer, Alf developed an early understanding of leadership in its most practical form. He saw firsthand what happens when expectations rise, decisions carry weight, and teams are required to perform under pressure. That experience shaped his enduring interest in people, behaviour, and the conditions that allow teams to function at their best.

Today, as Founder of KEY Leadership & Transformation, Alf helps leaders, teams, and organisations strengthen leadership, build healthier cultures, and navigate transformation with greater clarity and trust.

His work is grounded in a simple belief: sustainable results are created by people, and people perform at their best when they experience meaning, clarity, and trust.

Rather than relying on fixed frameworks or one-size-fits-all models, Alf works from the understanding that every organisation is different. Every team carries its own dynamics. Every individual brings their own history, behaviours, and motivations. His role is to help organisations understand those patterns, work with them more effectively, and create the conditions for long-term growth.

His work is centred around three connected levels of transformation.

The Self focuses on helping leaders and employees better understand themselves, their behaviours, and the impact they have on others.

The Team focuses on building safe, high-performing teams with stronger trust, clearer expectations, and healthier ways of working together.

The Company focuses on shaping the structural and cultural behaviours where purpose, values, and direction become visible in everyday work.

Across industries ranging from manufacturing and energy to service-led and founder-driven businesses, Alf has worked with leaders through growth, change, and transformation. Whether the organisation is large or small, his core principle remains the same: lasting performance is built through human clarity, not organisational complexity.

What defines Alf’s work is not just his focus on leadership, but his focus on behaviour.

He believes transformation becomes meaningful only when it is lived in practice. Not in strategy decks. Not in leadership slogans. But in how people communicate, make decisions, handle pressure, and work together every day.

That is where culture is built. And that is where transformation succeeds or fails.

Alf is driven by helping people lead with greater self-awareness, helping teams perform with greater trust, and helping organisations turn intention into behaviour.

Outside of work, physical and mental training remain a central part of his life. He sees a clear connection between body, mind, and performance, and brings that same discipline into the way he approaches leadership, growth, and transformation.

LinkedIn | Website | Personal 

7. Peter Sundara Swamickannu | Leading with Purpose in Global Logistics

Peter Sundara Swamickannu is Medov Logistics’ Managing Director in Asia-Pacific. In simple words, he is in charge of ensuring that products arrive at their intended destination on time. 

Peter focuses on ensuring that these difficult journeys run smoothly and efficiently, whether he is working in the building and maintenance of massive cruise ships or delivering cargo over the ocean. He spends his days establishing teams capable of surviving whatever challenges the contemporary world throws at them, as well as looking for ways to expand the company with new technologies.

He has over 25 years of experience in the shipping and freight industry, so he has seen it all. He has led major advancements in the use of digital tools by organisations and managed massive budgets. The people and the idea are more significant than the ships or the numbers for Peter. He thinks that a company is only as strong as its employees, therefore he spends a lot of time teaching, mentoring, and helping the next generation of logistics experts find their footing. 

His experience has propelled him to the position of industry authority. He routinely speaks at large international conferences and shares what he has learned about staying adaptable in a fast changing world. He even helped create a leadership book to help others navigate difficult corporate environments.

When he is not managing global supply chains, he is most likely sharing his leadership and grit ideas, constantly looking for new ways to make the complex world of global trade a little more human and much more connected. 

LinkedIn 

8. Monsef Idrissi | Connecting the World of Sports Beyond the Field

“The future of sports will not be decided only on the field, but in how its ecosystems are connected, structured, and empowered.”

Monsef Idrissi believes that the future of sports happens where talent meets opportunity. Based in Madrid, Monsef is an entrepreneur working at the busy intersection of sports, law, and technology. As the founder of CarrerUp, he is building a digital home where athletes, clubs, agents, and fans can finally connect in one organized and high-performance space.

Monsef’s journey is inspired by one simple goal: making the sports world easier to navigate. While earning his Master’s in International Sports Law at the Real Madrid Graduate School, he saw firsthand how disorganized the industry could be. He decided to fix this by building a bridge that connects talent with global opportunities in a stable, professional way.

His work combines big dreams with real-world action. Whether he is improving the sports industry through CarrerUp or growing his coffee shop businesses, he stays focused on what is important. For Monsef, it is all about building companies that truly help people and create long-term success.

At the heart of what he does is the conviction that, while games are won on the pitch, the industry thrives through stronger links and greater administration. Monsef is committed to ensuring that the future generation of sports is more structured, transparent, and full of opportunities for all participants. 

LinkedIn | Website | Twitter | Instagram  

9. Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu | A Life Dedicated to Care, Knowledge, and Expression

For Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu, healthcare has never been limited to diagnosis or treatment. It has always been about understanding people. Her journey as a family physician reflects this belief. She focuses on the human side of medicine just as much as the clinical side.

She graduated from Iași University in Romania and later pursued family medicine research at Maastricht University. Over the years, she has built a strong presence in the medical field. She has delivered more than 137 international presentations and published over 60 articles in respected journals. Each contribution reflects her commitment to learning and sharing knowledge.

Dr. Bistriceanu is also closely involved in academic and professional circles. She is a member of the Academy for Professionalism in Healthcare. In addition, she serves on the Editorial Review Board for The Journal of Patient Experience and contributes to other medical publications. Her work as an Associate Editor with Primera Scientific Publication further highlights her role in shaping medical research.

One of her most distinctive contributions is her medical home model. Instead of limiting care to a clinic, she focuses on treating patients in their own environments. This allows her to observe factors that are often missed in traditional settings. She pays close attention to communication, family dynamics, and daily habits. According to her, these elements play a major role in overall health.

Beyond medicine, Dr. Bistriceanu has also built a name in the literary world. She has authored seven volumes of poetry. Her writing reflects a thoughtful and reflective mind, one that looks beyond science into emotion and experience.

Her work continues to influence both healthcare and research. She brings a clear message. To treat a person well, one must first understand the life they live.

LinkedIn

10. Dr. Karen Wendt | Guiding the Future of Sustainable Finance

Dr. Karen Wendt has spent her career at the point where finance meets long-term impact. She began in investment banking, working on acquisition strategies and project finance for leading institutions. Over time, her focus shifted. She moved toward sustainability, not as a trend, but as a necessary direction for the financial world.

Her work today reflects that shift. Dr. Wendt believes that real impact often comes from new ideas and new companies entering the market. To understand where finance is heading, she looks closely at areas like decentralized systems, tokenization, and new forms of asset ownership. For her, these are not distant concepts. They are already shaping how capital moves and how value is created.

With a PhD focused on impact investing and institutional clients, she combines research with real-world application. She also serves as President of SwissFinTechLadies, where she supports greater participation of women in finance and emerging financial systems. This is an area she speaks about often. She believes the future of finance must be inclusive, not limited.

As the CEO of Eccos Impact GmbH, Dr. Wendt works directly with investors and organizations. She helps them build strategies that align financial returns with measurable impact. Her work includes portfolio design, risk understanding, and the development of structured approaches to sustainable investment. She focuses on making these ideas practical and usable.

Beyond her advisory work, she is also an active voice in the field. She edits a Sustainable Finance science series, has written several books in both German and English, and regularly speaks at global forums. Her sessions are known for being clear and grounded, often linking complex ideas back to real decisions.

Dr. Karen Wendt continues to work with a clear sense of direction. She supports investors who want to do more than follow the market. She helps them understand where it is going and how to be part of that change.

Conclusion

The global leaders featured in this article are not just building successful ventures, they are pioneers of transformation in the current times. Their journey of dedication and relentless efforts is proof that with a strong vision, leaders can not only change industries, but they can also empower an entire generation.

title: Sir John Curtice: The Election Results Demonstrate the Fragmentation of UK Politics
author: editor
excerpt: The election results on Thursday have revealed the extreme fragmentation of British electoral politics. The English municipal elections were undoubtedly won by Reform UK. The party has secured the majority of seats and votes. In the end, the net gains will be considerably over 1,000. In the meantime, the party reported an average vote share of 25% in a sample of more than 500 council wards where the BBC gathered comprehensive voting data. This is not a very high percentage, but it is nevertheless sufficient to put Reform well ahead of its competitors. title: For The Second Consecutive Month, US Jobs data Exceeds Projections
author: editor
excerpt: Despite the economic consequences of the US-Israel conflict in Iran, businesses continued to hire, and in April the US economy added 115,000 jobs. The sum was nearly twice as much as economists had predicted, making the gain larger than anticipated. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) released the data, which also revealed that the jobless rate remained at 4.3%. Gas prices for American consumers have increased due to a global energy shock caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in reaction to US and Israeli operations on Iran. The most recent data follows months of significant swings in the number of jobs. In February, non-farm payrolls decreased by 156,000, but in March, they increased by 185,000. Expectations that the Federal Reserve will retain interest rates in an effort to control inflation were heightened by April’s strong job data. The number of jobs increased by 48,000 on average during the previous three months, according to revisions to the numbers for March and February. This is consistent with the so-called breakeven rate, which is the pace at which new hires can be hired. title: To What Extent Should We be Concerned About the Hantavirus?
author: editor
excerpt: Authorities said they are taking the hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship that is transporting people from all over the world very seriously. The ship sailed from Argentina a month ago, and three passengers have perished either on board or after traveling. For medical attention, four more people have been taken off the ship. A massive effort is underway to track down individuals who may have been exposed to the virus and who have already returned home via flights to the UK, South Africa, the Netherlands, the US, and Switzerland, among other nations. A Different Kind of Animal Rescue Organization

Most people are familiar with local shelters that take in stray or abandoned animals. No Dogs Left Behind operates very differently.

Their work focuses on dogs in extreme conditions, including:

  • Illegal transport situations
  • Severe neglect cases
  • High-risk environments where survival is uncertain

This type of rescue requires more than just shelter space. It involves coordination, planning, and the ability to respond quickly in urgent situations.

Because of this, their operations are more complex than typical rescue groups.

The rescue process is not a single step. It is a sequence of actions that must be carefully managed.

First, the organization identifies situations where dogs are in immediate danger. Then, they coordinate with local teams to intervene.

Once the dogs are rescued, the next phase begins. This includes:

  • Immediate medical assessment
  • Stabilization and treatment
  • Safe relocation

This process ensures that rescued dogs are not only removed from danger but also given a real chance to recover.

Rehabilitation: The Most Important Phase

Many rescued dogs have gone through trauma. Some are injured, while others are malnourished or fearful.

No Dogs Left Behind places strong emphasis on rehabilitation.

This includes:

  • Veterinary care
  • Proper nutrition
  • Safe and calm environments
  • Time for emotional recovery

Without this stage, adoption would not be successful. Rehabilitation is what turns a rescued animal into a healthy companion ready for a home.

Adoption Process Explained

One of the key questions people have in any No Dogs Left Behind review is about adoption.

The organization offers international adoption, which means dogs can be placed with families in different countries.

The process includes:

  • Health checks and vaccinations
  • Documentation and compliance
  • Travel coordination
  • Matching dogs with suitable adopters

This is not an instant process. It is structured to ensure that both the dog and the adopter are a good fit.

Adoption is not free, and this sometimes creates confusion.

However, the costs are not profit-based. They typically cover:

  • Medical care
  • Vaccinations
  • Transportation

title: Ted Turner, Media Entrepreneur Who Revolutionized Television News by Establishing CNN, Died at 87
author: editor

title: Massive Alaska Megatsunami was The Second Greatest Ever Recorded
author: editor
excerpt: According to geologists, a massive ‘megatsunami’ wave caused by the collapse of an Alaskan mountain into the sea is the second-largest ever recorded and serves as a reminder of the risks posed by melting glaciers. Last summer, a massive wave smashed through a secluded fjord in southeast Alaska, causing devastation. The event remained completely unnoticed at the time, but a new scientific research has revealed that it was caused by a major landslide. An astonishing 64 million cubic metres of granite – the equivalent of 24 Great Pyramids – landed in the ocean below. The sheer force of so much rock plunging into the fjord in under a minute created a massive wave nearly 500 metres high. According to the experts, only the timing – early in the morning – prevented tourist cruise ships from getting caught up in the disaster. Dr. Bretwood Higman, an Alaskan geologist who witnessed the destruction in Tracy Arm Fjord, described it as “a close call”.We know that there were folks who were almost in the wrong area,” he explained. ‘I’m scared that we won’t be as lucky in the future.” Also Read: Gaurav Sharma: Transforming Immigration With Vision, Strategy, And Trust Issam Mhanna: Turning Every Space Into A Timeless Experience

title: China Urges for The Reopening of the Strait ‘as Soon as Feasible’ in Iran Talks
author: editor
excerpt: In conversations with his Iranian counterpart, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi advocated for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz “as soon as possible”. The two met in Beijing on Wednesday, marking Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi’s first visit to China since the Iran conflict began. Wang Yi also informed Araqchi that securing a long-term truce was a “urgent priority” and that negotiations must continue. He went on to say that Beijing was ready to help de-escalate tensions. The meeting comes a week before US President Donald Trump’s encounter with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. The leaders are expected to discuss the Iran conflict and the reopening of the strait. According to official media, Wang Yi stated that China prioritizes securing a comprehensive ceasefire and opposes resuming hostilities.On the issue of the Strait, the world community is concerned about restoring regular and security passage across the Strait, and China expects that relevant parties would respond as quickly as possible to the strong appeal from the international community. Beijing, which has attempted to mediate while avoiding involvement in the issue, has repeatedly pushed the US and Iran to conduct talks, a stance Wang emphasized on Wednesday. title: People are Encouraged Not to Cancel Flights amid Gasoline Shortage Fears
author: editor
excerpt: Holidaymakers are being advised not to reschedule their travel plans owing to fears about jet fuel supplies, as there is presently no shortage in the UK and contingency procedures are in place. Airlines worldwide canceled 13,000 flights in May as jet fuel prices skyrocketed owing to the Middle East turmoil. However, this barely accounts for 1% of global flights, with flights into and out of the UK remaining mostly unaffected. According to Cirium, Munich and Istanbul were among the worst-hit destinations. The Department for Transport (DfT) stated that there is no need for anyone to adjust their travel plans.UK airlines purchase jet fuel in advance, and airports maintain stock to ensure resilience.If your flight is canceled, you have the legal right to a full refund or re-routing. We encourage travelers to verify with their airlines before traveling and to consult the FCDO travel advisory for the most recent changes. “You should also make sure you have adequate travel insurance,” the DfT stated. title: In an Indian State, a “Fun” Superstar Dazzles Competitors and Transforms Politics
author: editor
excerpt: In the state of Tamil Nadu, movie star-turned-politician C Joseph Vijay is about to make history.His political party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), nearly won the state election on Monday, defying all predictions and upending the status quo. Matinee idol MG Ramachandran, who split from the well-established Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) to form his own party and became chief minister in 1977, is being likened to Vijay’s remarkable ascent. Vijay has obstacles to overcome in order to attain the top rank, despite the fact that his success has thrilled fans and supporters. A party needs 118 seats in the 234-member Tamil Nadu assembly in order to establish a government. With 108 votes, Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) is 10 seats short of a majority. In order to clear the threshold and establish a claim to power, Vijay will therefore need to transition over the next days from being a crowd-puller to a coalition builder, engaging with smaller parties and independent lawmakers. Even yet, his achievement is a momentous political event in a state that has been choosing between the DMK and its competitor, the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), for decades. For some, politics and persona are equally important explanations.Vijay has a unique energy, according to social scientist Shiv Visvanathan. “He offers a sense of fun, confidence and an aura of competence rooted in individuality and that gives him a different kind of power.” Also Read: The US Disputes Iranian Claims That Rockets Hit a Warship In a Historic Deal with South Korea, the UAE and Qatar Seek a New Gulf-Asia Economic Corridor

title: Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini  | Transforming an Overlooked Industry Through Purpose and Leadership
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In this exclusive interview, Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reflects on her journey from chemical engineering to entrepreneurship, and how she built Emakheni Group into a purpose-led facilities management company. From navigating a male-dominated industry to transforming an overlooked sector, she shares how resilience, leadership, and vision continue to shape her path. From Engineering to Purpose To understand the foundation of her journey, we asked, “Could you share a bit about your early background, education, and the key experiences that shaped your career journey?” Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply -“I was raised by my grandparents in the rural village of eMpendle, near Pietermaritzburg, while my mother pursued a teaching qualification. My upbringing instilled resilience, discipline, and a deep respect for education, which was further strengthened through my boarding school experience. I went on to build a career in chemical engineering, working with organisations such as Sappi, Sasol, and Unilever. Despite the stability and prestige, I found myself searching for deeper purpose. In male-dominated industrial environments, I often felt unseen, which led me to reflect on where I could create more meaningful impact. That search led me to the cleaning industry, where I identified both a challenge and an opportunity — a workforce that was undervalued, yet full of untapped potential. This insight became the foundation of Emakheni. I founded the business in 2013, and the early years were extremely challenging. I had to learn how to navigate a competitive, compliance-driven industry while also developing business acumen and leadership under pressure. With the support of mentors and a clear sense of purpose, I was able to build a strong foundation for the business.” Building Emakheni To understand how this vision translated into reality, we asked, “How has your company evolved since its inception?” Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply -“Today, Emakheni Group is a 100% Black-owned, ISO 9001-certified facilities management company serving clients such as Unilever, SA Home Loans, and NCS Resins. We provide specialised industrial cleaning, including high-pressure, high-level, and chemical cleaning, alongside integrated hygiene, contract cleaning, pest control, and landscaping services. Backed by my technical background, we operate in environments where safety, compliance, and efficiency are critical. Our purpose, “Transforming Lives While Cleaning Excellently,” guides everything we do. We invest in training, promote from within, and integrate sustainability with social impact. Looking ahead, we are expanding beyond KwaZulu-Natal, with plans for national growth, AI-driven operational improvements, and the establishment of an NPO to further professionalise the sector.” Impact on the Ecosystem To explore the company’s broader role, we asked, “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?” “We contribute by creating employment opportunities in the communities where we operate, which is especially important in the current economic climate. We also contribute economically by being a compliant business and paying our taxes responsibly.” Defining Success in the Industry As the conversation shifted to industry insights, we asked, “What three qualities are critical for success in your industry?” “Resilience is essential, because this industry requires you to persist despite challenges. An inquisitive mindset is also important, as you need a strong desire to learn, understand your market, and identify how to bring value. Leadership is equally critical, particularly the ability to manage yourself and lead teams to consistently deliver results.” Adapting to Technology To see how the business is evolving with changing times, we asked, “How has your organisation adapted to technological changes?” Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply – “We are currently upgrading a number of our systems to improve efficiency across multiple sites. We have also integrated Artificial Intelligence into key processes to enhance operational performance and enable smarter service delivery.” Advice for the Next Generation Finally, looking ahead, we asked, “What advice would you give to someone entering this industry?” “You need a clear vision and a strong sense of purpose. You must have the desire and hunger to learn, and to understand both your industry and the clients you want to serve. Most importantly, you need to embody a spirit of excellence and be willing to go above and beyond expectations.” Connect with Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini on LinkedIn. Learn more about Emakheni Group and its work through their official channels. title: Bengal, One of India’s Most Difficult Political Frontiers, is Won by Modi’s BJP
author: editor
excerpt: The West Bengal state of India was the notable exception to Narendra Modi’s political progress for many years. His Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) defeated once-powerful regional rivals, surged over India’s Hindi-speaking heartland, and spread into the west and northeast. Bengal, however, continued to be obstinately resistant while being contentious and deeply rooted in a sense of cultural superiority. Because of this, the state election was very important. With a population of over 100 million, West Bengal has a larger electorate than Germany, making its election more akin to a national election for a government than a typical state election in India. The BJP’s victory there on Monday would be one of the biggest achievements of Modi’s twelve-year rule. It is the culmination of the party’s protracted advance into eastern India, not just the removal of a three-term incumbent.Author and writer Nilanjan Mukhopadhyay claims that the BJP’s victory in Bengal is significant because it is a land of potential that has long eluded its grasp. There was also a remarkable political upheaval in southern India on Monday. Actor-turned-politician Vijay and his nascent TVK party overthrew MK Stalin’s DMK government in Tamil Nadu, signaling the dramatic return of movie star politics to the state. The last Communist-led state government in India was overthrown when the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) defeated the Left Democratic Front (LDF) in Kerala after two terms in a row. The BJP and its allies managed to hold onto the federal territory of Puducherry, but they only managed to defy the wider anti-incumbent tide in Assam. title: No Dogs Left Behind NGO: A Global Effort to Protect Dogs from Cruelty
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In recent years, awareness around animal welfare has grown significantly, but many parts of the world still struggle with issues like illegal dog trafficking, abuse, and neglect. This is where organizations like No Dogs Left Behind NGO play a critical role. Unlike traditional shelters that operate locally, this organization focuses on rescuing dogs from extreme conditions across different countries. Their work is not just about saving animals; it is about creating a global movement that challenges cruelty and promotes compassion. If you are exploring animal rescue organizations or considering adoption or support, understanding how this NGO operates can give you valuable insight. What is No Dogs Left Behind NGO? No Dogs Left Behind is an international nonprofit organization dedicated to rescuing dogs from life-threatening situations and giving them a second chance. The NGO focuses on: Emergency rescue missions Medical rehabilitation Safe sheltering International adoption programs Their mission is centered around a powerful idea: Every dog deserves safety, care, and the opportunity to live a better life. This mission drives all their operations, from on-ground rescues to global awareness campaigns. How This NGO is Different from Local Shelters Many people assume all animal rescue organizations function in the same way. However, No Dogs Left Behind operates on a completely different level. Global Rescue Focus Instead of working in a single city or region, the NGO operates internationally, often in places where animal protection laws are limited or poorly enforced. High-Risk Operations Their rescue missions often involve dangerous environments, including illegal transport routes and areas where dogs face immediate harm. End-to-End Rescue Model They handle the entire process: Rescue Medical care Rehabilitation Adoption This full-cycle approach ensures that dogs are not just saved, but also successfully rehomed. Rescue Operations: The Core of Their Work The most important aspect of No Dogs Left Behind NGO is its rescue operations. These missions often include: Intervening in illegal dog transport cases Rescuing dogs from slaughterhouse environments Working with local activists and volunteers Providing immediate medical attention These are not routine rescues; they require coordination, funding, and quick decision-making. Because of this, the NGO operates in a space where both emotional commitment and logistical expertise are essential. Rehabilitation and Recovery After rescue, dogs are not immediately put up for adoption. Many of them require time to recover physically and emotionally. The NGO ensures proper rehabilitation through: Veterinary treatment Nutritional care Safe shelter environments Behavioral support This stage is critical because it prepares the dogs for a stable and healthy life in a new home. title: The US Disputes Iranian Claims That Rockets Hit a Warship
author: editor
excerpt: An Iranian media story that one of the US’s warships was hit by Iranian missiles while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz has been refuted by the US. Later, Centcom reported that two commerce ships flying the US flag had “successfully transited” through the strait. Iran’s military had already threatened to assault any foreign forces, especially the aggressive US army, if they crossed the Strait.A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Iran had fired a warning shot at the US vessel to stop it from entering the strait, although it’s unclear if any damage was done. Additionally, Iranian media said that on Monday, it stopped Israeli and American “enemy destroyers” from crossing the strait. US President Donald Trump had previously declared that the US will start attempting to liberate cargo ships that Iran had stuck on Monday. title: In a Historic Deal with South Korea, the UAE and Qatar Seek a New Gulf-Asia Economic Corridor
author: editor
excerpt: As part of a broader push by the Gulf states towards Asia, the United Arab Emirates inked a new trade agreement with South Korea the day after it left OPEC, lowering tariffs on the majority of traded goods, aiming to enhance trade and strengthen economic ties between the two nations. At a time when supply chains and broader geopolitical factors are altering international trade, the accord is South Korea’s first trade agreement with a nation in the Gulf Cooperation Council and the larger Middle East and North Africa region. To facilitate access to each other’s markets and promote trade and investment flows, the UAE and South Korea signed the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which eliminates or reduces tariffs on 91.2% of goods traded between the two nations. In 2025, non-oil commerce between South Korea and the United Arab Emirates reached $6.9 billion (about €6.3 billion), and officials anticipate continued development. According to Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, UAE Minister of Foreign Trade, the deal would boost collaboration in a number of industries, including technology, manufacturing, and logistics, and open up new prospects for exporters. title: Days After Accusing China of Canceling the Trip, The President of Taiwan travels to Eswatini
author: editor
excerpt: Days after his government announced that a trip had been canceled because China was pressuring African nations to prevent him from flying over their territory, Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te has landed in Eswatini. He stated that “days of careful arrangements by the diplomatic and national security teams” preceded his journey to Eswatini, Taiwan’s sole diplomatic ally in Africa, although he did not elaborate on how he got there. The visit was called a “stowaway-style escape farce” by China. Taiwan is seen by China as a part of its territory and is not entitled to state-to-state interactions. Pictures captured Lai passing a guard of honor and being greeted by Eswatini Prime Minister Russell Dlamini. According to its presidential office, Taiwan’s delegation also comprised National Security Council Advisor Alex Huang and Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung. Originally scheduled for April 22–26, the trip was intended to commemorate the 40th anniversary of King Mswati III of Eswatini’s ascension. It was put on hold after Taiwan claimed that, due to pressure from China, Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar had unilaterally canceled flight permits for Lai’s aircraft to pass through airspace under their control. title: New Proposals Allow Airlines to cancel Flights Ahead of Time Due to Fuel Shortages
author: editor
excerpt: If fuel shortages occur this summer, airlines will be able to cancel flights weeks in advance without sacrificing important takeoff and landing times at crowded airports. The government has created new backup plans to assist carriers prepare ahead of time and prevent passengers from being inconvenienced by last-minute cancellations. To save fuel, the plans would permit airlines to combine flights on routes with multiple trips to the same destination on the same day. This would allow passengers to switch from their original reservation to a similar one. author: editor

Cook, however, stated that the demand for the new Macbook Neo was “off the charts” on a call with financial analysts to review the company’s performance. title: Lawyers Claim That War Criminal Mladic is Near Death and are Pleading With the Judge to Release Him from Prison
author: editor
excerpt: Attorneys for convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic are waiting for a UN court to rule on their request to have him released from The Hague prison on the grounds that he is nearing the end of his life. In 2017, Mladic, 84, was sentenced to life in prison for crimes against humanity, war crimes, and genocide committed during the 1992–1995 hostilities in the former Yugoslavia. In 2021, the guy dubbed the “Butcher of Bosnia” had his sentence upheld on appeal. Mladic had previously been bedridden or in a wheelchair for a considerable amount of time, according to his attorneys’ comprehensive report to the court on Friday. However, they claimed that during a call with his son, he had a suspected stroke that nearly prevented him from speaking. The lawyers have demanded his urgent provisional or conditional transfer to a hospital or hospice where the Serbian language is spoken, claiming that two doctors had evaluated his condition as serious and that the “risk of imminent death is high”. It is evident that Mladic’s defense team wants him to go back home, and Serbian Justice Minister Nenad Vujic has stated that his country is willing to give the court assurances if they free him. An independent health examination was requested by Judge Graciela Gatti Santana, and the results were scheduled to be presented on Friday. In the 1990s, Mladic led Bosnian Serb forces against Bosniak (Bosnian Muslim) and Bosnian Croat armies. During this conflict, his troops massacred 8,000 men and boys at Srebrenica, engaged in “ethnic cleansing” in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and besieged Sarajevo, killing over 10,000 people. title: Matthieu Tebaus on AI, Advertising, and Locala’s Growth
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In this exclusive interview, we speak with Matthieu Tebaus, Senior Vice President Sales MENA at Locala, about the evolution of digital media, AI-led advertising, and how Locala is helping brands turn data into smarter omnichannel growth. With deep expertise across global markets and a sharp understanding of evolving consumer behavior, Matthieu Tebaus offers a clear perspective on what it takes to stay ahead in modern advertising. In this conversation, he shares how data, agility, and intelligent media strategies are shaping the future of brand growth across the MENA region. From Global Brands to AdTech Leadership “Could you share your early background, education, and key experiences that shaped your career journey?” “With over 20 years of experience at the forefront of the digital media industry, my journey has been shaped by a deep passion for technological evolution and brand performance. I began my career on the brand side, spending several foundational years at global powerhouses such as Nike, Chanel, and Decathlon. These roles gave me a client-first perspective and a rigorous understanding of how major international groups approach marketing ROI and consumer engagement. Driven by the rapid rise of advertising technology, I transitioned into the AdTech sector, where I have spent the last two decades building and scaling high-performance commercial operations. After leading French operations for several prominent British and American tech players, I joined Locala 11 years ago and have since played a key role in the company’s international expansion. Over the past decade, I have led commercial development across several major European markets, including France, Belgium, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the Nordics. For the past two years, I have had the privilege of leading Locala’s operations across the MENA region. The sculpture, which bears his signature, depicts a suited man going forward from a pedestal while holding a flag that conceals his face. The sculpture is situated among statues of Edward VII, Florence Nightingale, and the Crimean War memorial. Banksy’s agents told the BBC that the statue was installed in the early hours of Wednesday, before the artist shared a video of it on Instagram on Thursday afternoon. title: The US House Voted to Terminate the Government Closure over Immigration Operations
author: editor
excerpt: US senators have voted to fund the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), ending the 76-day partial government shutdown over the agency’s immigration enforcement efforts. Members of the US House of Representatives approved a Senate-passed bill by voice vote, restoring funding to much of DHS and ending the agency’s longest closure in history. Since February 14, the federal agency has been operating without normal finances, resulting in massive disruptions and hours-long wait times at airports around the United States. President Donald Trump supports the plan, which reopens DHS but does not provide fresh funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) or the US Border Patrol. The bill now goes to the president, who is likely to sign it quickly. The House’s thin Republican majority has regularly stagnated under Speaker Mike Johnson, with his own party embroiled in internal squabbles over a variety of urgent problems, including homeland security funding. The bipartisan package was unanimously adopted by the Senate a month ago, but it has stalled in the House. title: In an Instagram Post, Comey Surrenders to the Allegation of Threatening Trump’s Life
author: editor
excerpt: Former FBI Director James Comey surrendered to authorities on Wednesday to face charges that an image he briefly shared on social media threatened President Donald Trump’s life. It derives from Comey’s Instagram post, which featured an image of seashells on a seashore organized to say “86 47”. “Eighty-six” is a slang word for “get rid of,” and prosecutors say it incites violence against Trump, the 47th president. Comey denies any culpability, claiming he didn’t understand the figures and accusing the prosecution of political intent. This is the second time the Justice Department has filed criminal charges against Comey, Trump’s longstanding adversary. Comey did not speak during his brief appearance in a Virginia court, but his attorney told Reuters that the former director will argue the case was a spiteful prosecution or punishment for speaking out against Trump. During his second administration, President Trump has publicly suggested that Justice Department authorities investigate his political foes. The government has indicted individuals such as Comey and New York Attorney General Tish James, who brought fraud charges against the president. Attorney General Todd Blanche stated on Wednesday that the additional charges against Comey are “absolutely, positively not” politically motivated. title: ‘Unequivocal Evidence’: Europe’s Climate Disaster Impacts Food, Health, and Economic Growth
author: editor
excerpt: According to Copernicus’s most recent European State of the Climate assessment, very few regions in Europe would avoid rising temperatures in 2025, with at least 95% of the continent experiencing above-average conditions. Continuing its trend as the world’s fastest-warming continent, Europe faced new extremes in 2025, including 30°C heat in the Arctic Circle and 50 more ‘hot stress’ days in southern and eastern Spain, when temperatures felt like 32°C or higher. Türkiye recorded a blistering 50°C for the first time, while 85 percent of Greece had temperatures at or above 40°C, peaking at 44°C. Sub-Arctic Fennoscandia, which includes northern Norway, Sweden, and Finland, saw its longest and most severe heatwave on record in July, with temperatures peaking at 34.9°C. All that heat is pushing out the cold: the area of Europe that experiences winter days with freezing temperatures is shrinking, and it will be below average in 2025, according to a report released by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) of the World Meteorological Organization. Glaciers are melting at an alarming rate, extending a decades-long trend of ice loss throughout Europe. Iceland, in particular, experienced its second biggest ice loss on record. At the end of March, snow cover was 1.32 million square kilometers below average. To put things into perspective, that is nearly the combined size of Austria, France, Germany, Italy, and Switzerland. title: In Difficult Negotiations, the European Parliament Requests an Additional €200 Billion for the EU Budget
author: editor
excerpt: The European Parliament will propose an increase of over €200 billion in the next common EU budget, paving the way for contentious political debate over finances. The Parliament adopted its position with a huge majority of 370 votes in favor, 201 against, and 84 abstentions. EU countries are now expected to articulate their own positions before interinstitutional negotiations begin, which are expected to be challenging because the EU’s long-term budget must be approved by both the European Parliament and the 27 member states. When asked about negotiation strategies to convince EU member states to increase spending, President Roberta Metsola remarked, “Never underestimate the Parliament.” Political leaders have also vowed to oppose, claiming that Parliament would not just rubber-stamp the Council’s position. “Who thinks that this [budget] could be agreed in the Council and then imposed through phone calls does not know this Parliament,” said Iratxe García Pérez, president of the Socialists and Democrats group. Typically, the Parliament caves to budgetary pressure from member states. This time, however, numerous internal sources informed Euronews that a harsher attitude is expected. It is unwilling to accept budget cuts since the centrist majority is less than in earlier legislatures, when heads of government could impose their agenda. title: Italy Deports an Alleged Chinese Hacker to the US Accused of Espionage for Beijing During the COVID-19 Epidemic
author: editor
excerpt: Italy has extradited a Chinese hacker to the United States on espionage charges for his country’s government during the COVID-19 pandemic, police said Monday. He is suspected, along with associates, of leading a hacking gang known as “Hafnium” that was accused of infiltrating tens of thousands of Microsoft Exchange email servers by 2021. The hacker group allegedly “exploited computer flaws in Microsoft Exchange Server software” relating to e-mail conversations to “target a law firm and other entities.” The individual was seized at Milan’s Malpensa airport last July and is “suspected of acting for the Chinese government,” according to a police statement. The FBI accuses Xu Zewei of hacking US government agencies, research institutes, and universities involved in vaccine research in 2020 and 2021, during the peak of the pandemic, according to the statement. The police did not identify the individual, but said he was the former CEO of a big technology company in Shanghai. Italian police said the suspect was arrested on a Texas warrant, citing “excellent and well-established cooperation” with the FBI as a factor in the operation’s success. I am going through the most terrible time of my life; I am at risk of facing an unjust trial in the United States, as well as physical and psychological abuse. “Don’t extradite me,” Xu implored Judge Veronica Tallarida. Building efficient food processing systems today requires more than engineering expertise. It requires a deep understanding of ecosystems, operational realities, and global market dynamics. In this conversation, we interviewed Pranav Shah to gain insights into his journey, the evolution of global processing systems, and the principles that drive meaningful impact across the industry. With over two decades of experience across regions and technologies, he brings a perspective that combines technical depth with business insight and practical execution.

The Early Foundations

We began by asking, “Could you share a bit about your early background, education, and the key experiences that shaped your career journey?”

“My career began with a foundation in engineering and food processing, but what shaped me most was not just education, it was exposure to real systems and real people.

 

I completed my B.Tech in Dairy Technology from Anand, Gujarat, which gave me a strong grounding in dairy processing systems and the science behind large-scale food production, followed by an MBA from MSU, Vadodara. It is one of the few models in the world where technology, scale, and social impact work together seamlessly. Millions of farmers are connected, women are empowered, and value is created at every level. It teaches you very quickly that behind every processing line, there is a livelihood.

I later worked with Nestlé and GEA Group, and over the past two decades with SPX FLOW, now part of ITT Inc.

I have worked across Europe, Asia, China, and North America.

Living in Denmark for the last 14 years has refined my thinking. Europe sharpens your focus on sustainability and precision. Asia teaches speed and scale. North America pushes for performance and clear returns. If you can combine all three, you are in a good place.”

The Evolution of SPX FLOW

Continuing the discussion, we asked, “How has your company evolved since its inception?”

“SPX FLOW has evolved from being an equipment supplier to a global process solutions partner.

Today, we operate across complete processing ecosystems, from evaporation and spray drying to membrane filtration, UHT systems, and advanced fluid handling solutions. These systems are particularly critical in dairy and liquid food processing, where precision, hygiene, and consistency are non-negotiable.

Customers across the world are aligned on one expectation. Show me results. Lower energy use, less water consumption, higher uptime, and consistent product quality.

The evolution has been both technological and strategic. Automation, digital monitoring, and lifecycle services are now core. But equally important, we are much closer to customer operations. We are not just supplying equipment, we are part of how their plants perform every day.”

Contribution to the Ecosystem

Exploring the company’s broader impact, we asked, “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?”

“The impact of processing technologies is both local and global, and often interconnected.

In Europe, the focus is on sustainability and reducing carbon footprint. In Asia and Africa, the priority is improving food availability, extending shelf life, and minimizing supply chain losses.

In dairy processing especially, these technologies play a critical role in preserving quality, extending shelf life, and ensuring nutritional value reaches consumers efficiently.

There is also a strong flow of knowledge across markets. What works in one region often inspires solutions in another. That cross-learning is becoming one of the biggest advantages in this industry.

Alongside my core role, I stay engaged with global industry forums and advisory platforms. I am also registered as an independent director in India, and open to working with organizations that are looking to bring in a global perspective with practical execution experience.”

Qualities for Success

Shifting to leadership, we asked, “What three qualities do you believe are critical for success in your industry?”

  • Global mindset with local execution
    Strategy must travel well, but execution must fit the ground reality.
  • Operational credibility
    It helps if you have spent time where the noise, pressure, and reality exist, on the plant floor.
  • Clarity on value
    If a solution does not improve cost, quality, or efficiency, it will not survive long.

Innovation and Adaptation

Turning to technology, we asked, “How has your organization adapted to technological changes? Could you share a key innovation you’ve implemented?”

“The direction is clear. Integrated, data-driven, and resource-efficient processing.

Across technologies, whether UHT, evaporation, or drying, the focus is on reducing energy and water consumption while maintaining product integrity. Automation and digital tools are now embedded, enabling predictive maintenance and real-time monitoring.

There is also a subtle but important shift. Global standardization with local customization. The backbone is global, but the application is always tailored.

Innovation today is simple to define, but not easy to achieve. It must work on paper, and more importantly, it must work on a Monday morning in a real plant.”

Navigating Industry Challenges

As the conversation deepened, we asked, “How would you guide someone to navigate the key challenges you faced when establishing yourself in this industry?”

“Start where it matters. On the ground. Spend time in plants across different regions.

Build credibility through delivery. In this industry, people remember what worked, not what was presented.

Develop a cross-market lens early. The same challenge looks very different depending on geography.

Stay practical. This industry has little patience for theory without execution.

As I look ahead, I see increasing opportunities to contribute beyond operational roles, especially in advisory and board positions. Organizations looking for independent directors with global industry exposure and strong execution grounding are always welcome to reach out.”

Final Reflection

Before concluding, we asked Pranav to share a final thought.

“Food processing may look like stainless steel and pipelines from the outside. In reality, it is one of the most human industries in the world. When you improve a process, you are not just saving energy or improving yield, you are improving livelihoods across the value chain.”

title: Ukraine’s €90 Billion loan Approved by EU as Pipeline Turned on, Breaking Impasse
author: editor
excerpt: After months of negotiations, Ukraine has finally begun delivering Russian oil via a pipeline into Hungary and Slovakia. This ends the impasse over a €90bn (£78bn) loan, which is considered as critical EU aid for Kyiv. Officials reported that the loan and the 20th round of sanctions on Russia were both given preliminary clearance at a meeting of EU ambassadors in Brussels shortly after. The new deadline for approval is Thursday. After Ukraine reported that supplies had ground to a standstill due to damage caused by a Russian attack, Hungary’s Viktor Orbán invoked his veto power in February, even though the funding had already been agreed upon in December. Hours after the EU ambassadors started debating the loan, Ukrainian oil and government sources informed officials in Hungary and Slovakia that pumping had resumed. After Orbán insisted that oil flow resume before the loan could be disbursed, Ukraine confirmed on Tuesday that the repairs were complete. After 16 years in office, he was ousted as prime minister last Sunday in an election that cleared the air for the EU. Péter Magyar, the incoming leader of Hungary, has made improving relations between Budapest and Brussels a top priority. Speaking before the ambassadors’ meeting, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas emphasized that Ukraine desperately needs this funding and that it shows Russia cannot outlive Ukraine. title: Refunds for Trump Tariffs Start, but Customers Will Probably Miss Out
author: editor
excerpt: Refunds for billions of dollars in tariffs that the US Supreme Court overturned in February have started to be processed by the Trump administration. Companies can apply online to have repaid the money they were charged under the so-called “Liberation Day” tariffs, together with interest, as part of what will be the largest repayment program in history. About 330,000 importers may be able to get their money back after the US Court of International Trade ordered customs authorities to return the more than $160 billion (£121 billion) the government had collected in March. However, compensation is not anticipated for those particular consumers who were indirectly impacted by the levies through increased prices. The International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) taxes imposed by US President Donald Trump are the subject of the refunds.Judge Richard Eaton stated in March that “all importers of record whose entries were subject to IEEPA duties are entitled to the benefit” from the high court’s decision. When the portal opened in early April, almost 56,000 importers had finished the online application process for refunds, totaling $127 billion (£94 billion). title: As Iran Claims the Strait of Hormuz is Open” During the Ceasefire, Oil Prices Fall
author: editor
excerpt: Following Iran’s announcement that the Strait of Hormuz will be “completely open” to commercial ships for the duration of the ceasefire in the US-Israeli war, oil prices fell. Following the revelation, the price of a barrel of Brent crude dropped from above $98 to $88. A fifth of the world’s oil and liquified natural gas are normally transported via the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow stretch of water south of Iran. Although Iran’s announcement was hailed by US President Donald Trump, maritime organizations are still confirming it. “The passage for all commercial vessels through Strait of Hormuz is declared completely open for the remaining period of ceasefire,” stated Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The announcement sparked a global market rally, with the major US stock indices gaining in early trading. The Nasdaq and Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) increased by 1.3% and 1.9%, respectively, while the S&P 500 increased by 1.2%. In response to the news, shares in Europe also increased. London’s FTSE 100 finished the day up about 0.7%, while the Cac index in Paris and the Dax index in Frankfurt both closed about 2% higher. Since the US and Israel began military assaults in Iran in late February, the government has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. title: The Energy Boss says that Europe has Maybe Six Weeks of jet Fuel Left
author: editor
excerpt: The chairman of the International Energy Agency (IEA) has cautioned that Europe has “maybe six weeks of jet fuel left. According to a research released this week, stocks would hit a tipping point in June if Europe couldn’t replace at least half of its imports from the Middle East. In reaction to US and Israeli attacks, Iran has effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for jet fuel out of the Gulf, for more than six weeks, driving up prices and raising concerns about shortages. Fatih Birol, executive director of the IEA, warned AP that if supplies were still blocked, flights would soon be canceled. The IEA, which advises 32 member nations on energy supply and security, stated in its monthly oil market report that the Gulf region’s exports accounted for the majority of jet fuel supplied to the world market. Crude oil imports from the Middle East were crucial to refineries in other key exporting nations like China, India, and Korea. It stated that the crisis “has thrown a proverbial wrench into the inner workings of the aviation fuel markets” as a result. title: US Lawmakers Reject a Plan to Prevent Trump From Attacking Iran
author: editor
excerpt: Just one day after a similar resolution was blocked in the Senate, a Democratic-backed bill to limit President Donald Trump’s authority to wage war on Iran has once again failed in the House of Representatives. The House war powers resolution, which was narrowly defeated by a vote of 213-214, was mostly symbolic because, even if it had succeeded, it would have had little chance of overriding an anticipated veto from the president. In both chambers, the majority of Republicans opposed the resolution, but some members have hinted that they would change their minds if the battle continued past this month. Trump has given varying estimates for how long the war will go, most recently stating that it is “close to over.” The sole Republican to support the legislation in the House vote on Thursday was Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky, while the only Democrat to oppose it was Jared Golden of Maine. Ohio’s Warren Davidson, who had previously backed the Democrats’ bid in March, abstained by voting present. title: PepsiCo Regains Struggling Snackers with Cheaper Doritos and Lays
author: editor

Prior to the Super Bowl, Doritos, Lays (known as Walkers in the UK), Tostitos, and Cheetos were among the brands that had price reductions of up to 15%. After infuriating consumers in 2022 with a string of price increases in reaction to its own skyrocketing expenses, the business has been having trouble. On February 8, one of the most profitable days of the year for snack manufacturers, it announced its latest round of price reductions in an attempt to win back snackers. In early trade, PepsiCo’s stock increased by 2% in response to the findings.
