title: As the Stock Market Rises Because to Increased Optimism For Peace Negotiations, Oil Prices Decline
author: editor
excerpt: As investors considered Washington’s signals that a diplomatic settlement in the Iran war might be near, European equities were largely stable on Wednesday. The FTSE 100 increased by 0.11%, Germany’s Dax increased by 0.11%, and the pan-European Stoxx 600 decreased by 0.1%. At 0.65%, the French CAC 40 declined by a little larger amount. In an indication of a potential diplomatic breakthrough, US President Donald Trump stated that new conversations between Washington and Tehran “could be happening over the next two days” in Islamabad and that the war was “very close to over” despite ongoing ambiguity over important issues of contention. The Nikkei 225 in Japan increased by 0.5%, the Kospi in South Korea increased by 3.0%, and the Hang Seng in Hong Kong increased by 0.7%. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 increased by less than 0.1%, while the Shanghai Composite gained 0.2%. The index at the core of many 401(k) plans is currently only 0.2% off its record established in January. On Wall Street, the S&P 500 increased its gains from the day before by 1.2%. The Nasdaq Composite increased by 2%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average increased by 317 points, or 0.7%. The benchmark US crude price increased by 1 cent to $91.29 per barrel on Wednesday. After dropping 4.6% the day before, Brent crude gained 48 cents to $95.27, or less than 1%. That is still well off the peak of $119, even if it is still above its about $70 level before to the start of the war in late February. Businesses in many sectors of the economy benefit from lower energy prices. Some observers cautioned that the euphoria might not be warranted, pointing out that the battle is still continuing on. title: Rolls-Royce Introduces a New Electric Vehicle with Two Seats
author: editor
excerpt: A new two-seater electric convertible variant has been introduced by luxury automaker Rolls-Royce. Only 100 of the Project Nightingale vehicles will be produced by the BMW-owned firm. They will be hand-built at the Rolls-Royce headquarters in Goodwood, West Sussex, and deliveries are expected to begin in 2028. According to the manufacturer, there would be “virtually no mechanical noise” because it is all electric. Rolls-Royce announced last month that it will no longer sell entirely electric vehicles starting in 2030 and that it would also sell cars with gasoline engines after that year. According to Rolls-Royce, Project Nightingale will be 5.76 meters long, around the same as Phantom, the company’s premier saloon with four or five seats. It stated that it will have a tall bonnet to give it a “torpedo-shaped form,” taking cues from the Art Deco period and the company’s experimental automobiles from the 1920s, known as EX models. “Some of the most discriminating Rolls-Royce clients in the world asked us for our most ambitious work,” stated Chris Brownridge, CEO of Rolls-Royce Motor Cars. “We responded by bringing three things together that have never co-existed in our brand: the complete design freedom of coachbuilding, our powerful, near-silent all-electric powertrain, and a uniquely potent yet serene expression of open-top motoring.” The “most extravagant expression of what Rolls-Royce is capable of today” is Project Nightingale, according to Brownbridge. title: In a Historic Case, an Australian Admits to Producing Deepfake Porn
author: editor
excerpt: In a historic case, an Australian adolescent entered a guilty plea to producing deepfake pornography. William Hamish Yeates, 19, is the first person to face charges under a new national law that makes manipulating sexual pictures illegal and carries a maximum sentence of seven years in jail. The new frontier of gendered, image-based abuse and school bullying, according to experts, is deepfake pornography, which is frequently produced using artificial intelligence technology and mostly targets women and girls. Yeates admitted four offenses on Wednesday, but he remained silent as he left the courtroom. In April, he will be back for a hearing. Yeates was previously charged with 20 Commonwealth offences, but the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions (CDPP) dropped some of them after he admitted to using a carriage service in an offensive or harassing manner and producing or altering sexual material without permission and distributing it. According to what the court heard, Yeates shared pictures of his purported victim on several X accounts without getting her permission. Although several jurisdictions have their own laws pertaining to deepfake material, a spokesman for Commonwealth prosecutors had previously said it was the first case of its kind. The eSafety Commission, Australia’s internet regulator, has been trying to outlaw applications that “nudify” people in the country and has warned of the growing threat of AI-manipulated content. excerpt: The Greek-owned bulk carrier NJ Earth crossed the strait at 10:44 a.m. CET, while the Liberian-flagged Daytona Beach did so at 8:59 a.m. CET, having left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas a little more than an hour earlier at 7:28 a.m. CET. The passages are the first confirmed transits under what appear to be the new parameters of the agreement impacting the world’s most crucial energy chokepoint. Iran’s Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, stated that ships would be allowed safe transit across the strait for two weeks “via coordination with Iran’s armed forces and with due consideration of technical limitations”. The agreement occurred hours before a deadline set by US President Donald Trump, who had threatened “a whole civilisation will die tonight” unless Iran agreed to open the strait before announcing a truce in exchange for the ceasefire. According to Lloyd’s List, a famous London-based shipping journal, over 800 ships are currently blocked inside the Middle East Gulf, and shipowners with stranded boats have alerted Lloyd’s that plans are on to begin relocating them as early as Wednesday morning. Key aspects remain unknown, as Iran claims to have agreed to two weeks of safe passage with “technical limitations,” while Trump has promised a “complete, immediate, and safe opening. title: Ceasefire Threatens as Iran Closes the Strait Again, and Trump Vows US Soldiers will Remain
author: editor
excerpt: A two-week ceasefire deal to halt the war in Iran appeared to be in jeopardy after Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz again in response to Israeli attacks in Lebanon, and US President Donald Trump said American forces would remain “in place” until the Islamic Republic fully complied with the “real” ceasefire agreement. The latest events in the battle came after the US and Iran both declared victory after reaching a two-week truce agreement on Tuesday night, but new bloodshed in Lebanon threatened to jeopardize the accord. Iranian media declared the closure of the Strait of Hormuz again on Wednesday, citing Israeli attacks on Tehran-backed Hezbollah fighters in Lebanon. According to Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, an end to the war in Lebanon was part of the 10-point plan outlined in the ceasefire agreement, a claim that both Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have denied. The world sees the massacres in Lebanon,” Araghchi wrote in a post on X. “The ball is in the US court, and the world is watching whether it will act on its commitments.”In an early Thursday morning social media tweet, Trump stated that the increase of US warships and troops will remain around Iran “until such time as the real agreement reached is fully complied with.” If it is not, which is quite improbable, then the ‘Shootin’ Starts,’ larger, better, and stronger than anyone has ever seen before,” Trump tweeted. content:
Introduction

When people search for No Dogs Left Behind reviews, they are usually trying to answer one simple question: What is the real experience like? Not just what the website says, but what actually happens when someone goes through the adoption process.

That’s a fair question. Adopting a dog especially internationally is not a small decision. It involves time, money, patience, and trust. So instead of generic claims, this article focuses on real adoption-style experiences, honest insights, and what adopters typically go through.

You’ll see both the emotional side and the practical side. Because both matter.

What People Want to Know Before Adopting

Before we get into stories, let’s understand the mindset of someone searching for reviews.

Most potential adopters have questions like:

  • Is the organization trustworthy?
  • Is the adoption process smooth or complicated?
  • Are the dogs healthy and safe?
  • Is the cost justified?
  • What happens after the dog arrives?

These concerns are normal. And real stories help answer them better than any promotional page ever could.

Real Adoption Story #1: From Fear to Trust

One adopter shared that their dog arrived extremely quiet and hesitant. This wasn’t surprising. Many dogs rescued from difficult environments have never experienced a stable home.

In the first few days:

  • The dog avoided eye contact
  • Stayed in one corner
  • Reacted to sudden sounds

But slowly, things changed.

Within a few weeks:

  • The dog began exploring the house
  • Started recognizing its new owner
  • Showed signs of comfort and curiosity

After a few months, the same dog that once hid in fear was now:

  • Playing freely
  • Responding to commands
  • Sleeping peacefully beside its owner

This type of transformation is common in rescue cases. It doesn’t happen overnight. But it does happen with patience.

Real Adoption Story #2: A Long but Worthwhile Process

Another adopter described the process as “long, but organized.”

Here’s what they experienced:

  • Initial application and screening
  • Communication regarding available dogs
  • Waiting period for documentation and travel
  • Regular updates during the process

The timeline was longer than expected. There were moments of uncertainty. But the adopter mentioned that:

  • Communication was consistent
  • Instructions were clear
  • Final delivery was well-coordinated

When the dog finally arrived, the emotional moment outweighed the waiting time.

 This highlights an important point: international adoption is rarely fast, but structured processes help reduce risk.

Real Adoption Story #3: Adjusting to a New Life

Not every story is instantly perfect. One adopter shared that their dog struggled initially after arrival.

Challenges included:

  • Difficulty eating properly
  • Fear of outdoor environments
  • Lack of basic training

This required:

  • Time
  • Routine
  • Gentle training

Over time, the dog adjusted. What helped most was consistency. The adopter didn’t expect instant results. Instead, they focused on gradual improvement.

Today, that same dog is described as:

  • Loyal
  • Calm
  • Fully adjusted to home life

Honest reviews often include these early challenges and that’s what makes them valuable.

What Most Positive Reviews Have in Common

After analyzing multiple adoption-style experiences, a few patterns appear again and again:

1. Strong Emotional Impact

Adopters often describe the experience as meaningful. They feel they are part of something bigger than just adoption.

2. Visible Transformation

Many reviews highlight the change in dogs—from survival mode to normal life.

3. Structured Process

Even if it takes time, most adopters mention that the process follows a clear path.

4. Ongoing Support

Some adopters report receiving guidance even after the dog arrives.

Common Challenges Mentioned in Reviews

To keep things real, let’s also talk about what people find difficult.

1. High Cost

Many adopters initially feel the adoption fee is expensive. This is one of the most discussed topics in reviews.

2. Waiting Time

Delays can happen due to documentation, travel coordination, or logistics.

3. Adjustment Period

Dogs may not adapt immediately. This requires patience and effort.

4. Limited Control

Since the process involves multiple countries, adopters sometimes feel they have less control over timelines.

These challenges don’t necessarily mean something is wrong—but they are important to understand before making a decision.

What Makes These Reviews Different from Regular Pet Adoption

Adopting from a local shelter and adopting internationally are very different experiences.

Here’s how:

Factor Local Adoption International Rescue
Cost Lower Higher
Time Faster Slower
Complexity Low High
Impact Local Global rescue

People who leave positive reviews often understand this difference clearly.

Real Expectations vs Assumptions

One of the biggest reasons behind mixed reviews is the gap between expectation and reality.

Assumption:

“I will get a fully trained dog quickly.”

Reality:

You may receive a dog that:

  • Needs adjustment
  • Needs training
  • Needs emotional recovery

Assumption:

“The cost should be similar to local adoption.”

Reality:

The cost includes:

  • Rescue operations
  • Medical care
  • International transport

Reviews become more positive when expectations are aligned with reality.

Are These Reviews Trustworthy?

This is another important question.

Not all reviews on the internet are equal. Some are:

  • Emotional reactions
  • Based on incomplete information
  • Influenced by personal expectations

The most reliable reviews usually:

  • Share full experience (start to end)
  • Include both positives and challenges
  • Focus on facts, not just emotions

When reading reviews, look for detailed experiences, not just short opinions.

Pros and Cons Based on Real Reviews

Pros

  • Life-saving impact for dogs
  • Meaningful adoption experience
  • Structured and guided process
  • Emotional connection and fulfillment

Cons

  • Expensive compared to local adoption
  • Longer waiting periods
  • Requires patience and commitment
  • Initial adjustment challenges

Final Thoughts: What Real Reviews Tell You

When you look at real adoption stories, one thing becomes clear:

This is not a “quick and easy” adoption.

It’s a process that requires:

  • Understanding
  • Patience
  • Financial commitment

But for many adopters, the outcome makes it worth it.

Dogs that once had no chance at survival go on to live stable, safe lives. And that transformation is what most positive reviews focus on.

FAQs

Are No Dogs Left Behind reviews mostly positive?

Reviews are mixed, but many detailed experiences are positive when expectations are realistic.

How long does the adoption process take?

It can take several weeks to months depending on logistics and documentation.

Are the dogs healthy when they arrive?

Most dogs receive medical care before travel, but some may still need adjustment or follow-up care.

Is it worth the cost?

That depends on your perspective. If you value rescue impact and are comfortable with the process, many adopters say yes.

Should I adopt internationally or locally?

Both are valid options. It depends on your priorities, budget, and comfort level.

Closing Note

Reading reviews is important. But understanding them is even more important.

Instead of looking for “perfect” stories, focus on real experiences. Those will give you a clearer picture of what to expect, and help you make a better decision.

title: Bitcoin Surges on Ceasefire Hope, but Breakout Depends on Inflation
author: editor
excerpt: Cryptocurrency markets surged as a temporary ceasefire between the United States and Iran reduced geopolitical tensions and pushed oil prices lower, increasing interest for risk assets and propelling Bitcoin to a three-week high above $72,000. Analysts say the rally indicates improved sentiment, but a durable breakout will depend on developments in inflation, interest-rate expectations, and institutional flows in the coming months. Bitcoin rose as much as 4.9% to around $72,700 in early Asian trading before settling near $71,000, its highest level since mid-March. The gains came when Donald Trump agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Iran in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which caused a dramatic decrease in petroleum prices and improved global risk sentiment. Crypto analysts say the ceasefire’s immediate impact on oil prices, with Brent falling below $100 per barrel, helped alleviate inflation concerns that had impacted on speculative assets since the conflict began in late February. Lower energy costs tend to boost liquidity expectations and raise investor interest in cryptocurrencies. The possibility of a bull market depends on how oil and gas supply recovers in the coming months and its impact on inflation,” Mei said, adding that revived predictions of US Federal Reserve rate reduction might serve as a powerful trigger for higher cryptocurrency prices. title: Airlines Reduce Flights and Raise Fees as Gasoline Prices Climb
author: editor
excerpt: Air India and Air New Zealand have indicated that they will reduce flights and raise tickets as jet fuel prices rise due to the US-Israeli war with Iran. Many airlines throughout the world have had to adopt emergency measures to combat growing fuel costs, which typically account for 20-40% of their operational expenses. Last week, the benchmark European jet fuel price reached an all-time high of $1,838 (£1,387) per tonne, up from $831 before the conflict began. Analysts warn that as the violence continues, travelers should expect higher ticket prices and more flight cancellations. The Gulf is a key supplier of aviation fuel, accounting for roughly half of Europe’s imports. The majority of it passes through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran effectively closed in response to US and Israeli attacks. The rise in jet fuel prices reflects Middle Eastern refineries’ importance in supply. According to Energy Intelligence, the Al-Zour refinery in Kuwait alone accounts for around 10% of European jet fuel imports. Air New Zealand’s cancellations are expected to affect routes in and out of Auckland, Wellington, and Christchurch, with flights to minor airports remaining unaffected. title: The US Factory is Currently Processing Venezuelan Oil
author: editor
excerpt: The Minerva Gloria is docked at a wharf in Mississippi Sound, not far from the United States’ massive oil reserves in the Gulf of Mexico. The 820ft (250m) long ship, painted navy and burgundy, is transporting valuable cargo from Venezuela that, just six months ago, would have been impossible to transport to the United States: 400,000 barrels of oil. Venezuela holds the world’s greatest oil reserves. Oil exports in Venezuela fell considerably under former President Nicolas Maduro due to a lack of investment. The US then imposed restrictions against all imports from the Latin American country. However, after the US military arrested Maduro in a surprise nighttime assault in January, President Donald Trump pledged to use those reserves.Venezuela’s oil production has resumed. In March, the country’s monthly crude exports exceeded one million barrels per day. First time since September. As the globe grapples with the impact on global energy prices caused by Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, major oil and gas firms such as Chevron are now importing Venezuelan crude oil by shipload. It’s a significant event for Chevron and the entire Gulf region,” says Tim Potter. He is the director of Chevron’s oil refinery in Pascagoula, Mississippi, the company’s largest US facility. It is also the sole major US oil corporation operating in Venezuela. The Top 10 Inspiring Leaders Shaping the Future

Below is the list of the top 10 inspiring leaders who are the voices of the future of business. With years of experience and unique ways of filling the market gaps, these trailblazers are not just offering their expertise, they are reimagining the way industries operate. As you move into the article, you will learn more about the professional trajectory of these inspiring leaders, challenges and milestones in their journey, and every event that shaped them into the leaders they are today.

Lady JB Owen | Elevating Humanity Through Storytelling, Leadership, and Conscious Transformation

Across industries and continents, the conversation around leadership, purpose, and impact is evolving. Today, success is no longer defined by scale alone, but by the ability to create meaningful change within individuals, communities, and the world at large.

Through her work, she has empowered thousands of individuals to build businesses, share their message, and step into leadership rooted in impact and contribution. Through Ignite Publishing, she has redefined what it means to write and publish a book. Marjorie Perrimon | Redefining Regulation at the Intersection of Beauty, Health, and Technology

Across the global cosmetics and health landscape, the role of regulation is undergoing a fundamental shift. What was once seen primarily as a function of compliance is now becoming a driver of innovation, shaping how products are developed, validated, and brought to market.

At the center of this transformation is Marjorie Perrimon, Head of Global Regulatory Affairs and Product Safety. She operates in an environment where regulatory complexity is not a limitation, but a structural force that informs strategy and competitive positioning.

Her work reflects a broader industry reality. As scientific scrutiny intensifies and expectations around transparency, safety, and sustainability continue to rise, companies are being required to rethink not only their products, but the systems that support them. In this context, regulation is no longer reactive. It is anticipatory, strategic, and increasingly central to innovation.

Marjorie’s perspective is shaped by a career that extends beyond traditional cosmetics. Her experience as Director of Certification in the medical device sector has introduced a level of rigor that is redefining industry standards. Where cosmetics once relied heavily on formulation and brand narrative, her approach brings in validation, clinical evidence, and structured risk management.

This convergence between cosmetics and medical disciplines is no longer theoretical. It is actively reshaping development models. The boundaries between beauty, health, and technology are dissolving, creating a new category of integrated solutions.

The next generation of products will not exist in isolation. They will be connected to devices such as LED and radiofrequency technologies. They will be part of broader systems that include nutrition and ingestible supplements. They will also operate within value chains increasingly defined by traceability, sustainability, and accountability.

Within this evolving landscape, regulation becomes a common language. It connects science, innovation, and market access, while ensuring that products are not only effective, but safe and meaningful in their application.

Marjorie’s work is also informed by direct human experience. Through her involvement alongside women undergoing cancer treatment, she has developed a deeper understanding of the role cosmetic products can play in people’s lives. In these contexts, cosmetics move beyond aesthetics. They contribute to reconstruction, dignity, and emotional resilience.

This perspective reframes the purpose of the industry itself. Products are no longer designed solely for enhancement. They can also support well-being, identity, and recovery.

In this environment, the role of regulatory leadership expands. It is no longer a support function operating at the margins of innovation. It sits at the core, shaping how products are conceived, validated, and delivered to those who need them most.

Marjorie positions her contribution at this critical intersection. Not downstream, where change is implemented, but upstream, where the frameworks of the next industry paradigm are being defined.

Her work reflects a defining principle. Regulation does not slow innovation. When approached strategically, it enables it, structures it, and ultimately gives it meaning.

Dr. Tony McCaffrey | Restoring Hope Through Creativity and Collective Intelligence

We are solving more problems than ever before, yet the problems that matter most remain unsolved.

Climate instability intensifies. Technology advances faster than our understanding of it. Societies grow more connected, yet more divided. The challenge is no longer a lack of knowledge. It is a lack of creative thinking capable of navigating this increasing complexity.

At the center of this conversation is Dr. Tony McCaffrey, a cognitive psychologist, AI researcher, and co-founder of BrainSwarm AI. His work is grounded in a fundamental belief that the world is not facing too many problems. It is facing a shortage of creativity applied to these problems.

McCaffrey’s perspective is shaped by decades of research in creativity and problem solving. While artificial intelligence continues to advance at an unprecedented pace, he challenges the assumption that it will be the primary source of breakthrough thinking. Large Language Models (LLMs) can organize and summarize existing knowledge, but they do not generate truly novel ideas when those ideas do not already exist in the available data. Cropley (2025) mathematically proved that LLMs cannot be more creative than an average person, while McCaffrey (2107) proved that any computer algorithm, not just LLMs, has a severe limit to its creativity.

In this context, reliance on AI alone risks reinforcing existing patterns rather than breaking them. It creates a new form of collective thinking called group-think where originality is diluted, and the ability to see what others overlook becomes increasingly rare.

For McCaffrey, creativity is not an abstract concept. It is a practical skill that can be developed, trained, and applied. His work focuses on a simple but powerful principle. People fail to solve problems because they do not notice crucial features, called obscure features because they are rarely or never before noticed. Innovation begins with attention to these obscure features.

This philosophy is embedded in BrainSwarm AI, a platform designed to bring people together to solve complex problems collaboratively. By combining diverse perspectives, the platform enables individuals to identify overlooked aspects of a challenge. AI can take on perspectives of experts, for example, that you currently do not have on your team. Further, specifically designed AI apps guide humans through techniques that help humans notice the obscure features of the current problem.

McCaffrey extends this approach through creative storytelling. His comic strip superhero, Captain Sideways, introduces young audiences to the concept of looking at problems from different angles and noticing obscure features. Through narrative and engagement, users learn practical techniques that improve their ability to think creatively and apply those insights in real world situations.

Captain Sideways

His work is also shaped by a deeper concern about the current state of the world. Reflecting on environmental crises, technological acceleration, and societal division, he raises a fundamental question. Why does humanity struggle to act collectively even when the stakes are clear?

History offers evidence that coordinated action is possible. The global response to the ozone crisis in the late twentieth century demonstrated that when science, policy, and the public align, large scale change can be achieved. The challenge today is not capability. It is alignment, attention, and willingness to act.

To this end, McCaffrey has started “Teens Solving Global Problems.” Teens are more creative than either adult experts or AI. His teen students have already solved three global problems this year out of the five they have attempted. Their solutions have been confirmed by domain experts. Adult experts suffer from several factors that greatly inhibit their creativity. First, developmentally, they are beyond their creative peak. Second, they are “over-knowledged” about their domains of expertise, which inhibits their creativity. Third, they are too familiar with the details of all the attempts to solve the major problems in their field, which greatly decreases their creativity. Teenagers, on the other hand, can be trained on the basics of a problem without gaining too much knowledge about it. Then, they apply their high creativity to the problem.

Finally, McCaffrey is building an “Innovation Exchange,” which is an online repository where “sellers” enter what their inventions know how to do and “buyers” enter what they need an invention to do. Humans as well as AI search the repository to find matches. Then, the two people involved in a match communicate offline to determine whether they should team up and put their ideas together to produce an important invention. Notice that no proprietary information is stored in the repository. It only stores what something does, not how it does it as would occur in a patent database. 

Through BrainSwarm AI and his broader body of work, McCaffrey positions his contribution at a critical intersection. Not as a replacement for artificial intelligence, but as a counterbalance that restores human creativity, especially teen creativity, as a central force in solving global challenges.

His work reflects a defining principle. The future will not be shaped by technology alone. It will be shaped by the ability of people to think differently, work together, and create solutions that do not yet exist.

He does not present creativity as optional. He presents it as essential. His mantra: Creativity is our world’s only hope.

In a time when hope feels increasingly fragile, his work offers a clear direction. Not by simplifying the problems we face, but by strengthening our capacity to solve them and recruiting the most highly creative demographic (i.e., teenagers) to lead the way.

 Shahad Alghamdi | Turning Market Intelligence into Meaningful Brand Growth

Building brands that scale and strategies that deliver, Shahad Alghamdi brings over a decade of experience across human resources, retail, and F&B sectors.

Based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, she has developed a strong expertise in market expansion, brand strategy, compliance, and market intelligence. Her approach combines data-driven insights with practical execution, enabling businesses to enter new markets with clarity and confidence.

Over the years, Shahad has contributed to the successful launch of 15+ branches across Saudi Arabia, leading end-to-end feasibility studies and identifying growth opportunities in competitive landscapes. She has also managed marketing budgets exceeding SAR 1 million, ensuring efficient allocation across digital, social, and offline channels to maximize ROI.

Her work spans integrated campaign planning, brand positioning, and cross-functional collaboration, where she partners closely with operations, leadership, and external stakeholders to align marketing with broader business goals.

Known for her structured thinking and ability to translate insights into action, Shahad is passionate about building brands that resonate with people while creating sustainable, long-term impact.

Shadan Izhiman | Leading Operational Excellence in Complex Environments

Shadan Izhiman is a strategic operations and leadership executive with over 18 years of experience across the GCC. Her work is centered on driving business performance, building scalable operational systems, and leading multi-level teams within fast-paced and often complex environments.

With a strong focus on aligning people, structure, and execution, Shadan has consistently delivered measurable business growth, often exceeding 40 percent. Her leadership operates at the intersection of strategy and execution, with direct accountability for operational performance, workforce planning, financial oversight, and organizational development.

Regional Leadership & Operational Scale

Shadan’s leadership experience spans key GCC markets, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan, with additional regional exposure across Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar through training and operational initiatives.

She has managed teams ranging from small, specialized units to large-scale operations of over 70 professionals, within organizations varying from 20 to more than 3,000 employees. This range has enabled him to adapt leadership approaches across different business sizes, structures, and cultural contexts.

Operational Impact & Growth

A core strength of Shadan’s work lies in delivering tangible business outcomes through structured execution. Her contributions include scaling revenue from 1.7M to 5M and consistently achieving growth exceeding 40 percent.

She focuses on building systems that improve efficiency, strengthen accountability, and support long-term performance. Her approach ensures that growth is not incidental, but repeatable and sustainable.

Strategic Execution & Transformation

Shadan has led the design and implementation of operational frameworks built for scalability and consistency. Her work includes developing operational models from the ground up, establishing internal training systems, supporting the launch of new service divisions, and redesigning workflows to improve performance and output.

Her ability to translate strategy into execution enables organizations to move from fragmented operations to structured, high-performing systems.

Signature Strength

At the core of her leadership is the ability to combine operational structure with clarity of execution and hands-on involvement. This enables both business performance and individual capability to grow in parallel.

Leadership Philosophy

Shadan’s leadership philosophy is shaped by the realities of working within the GCC, where workforce dynamics are fluid and traditional models of stability do not always apply.

She recognizes that:

  • Workforce mobility is a constant, not an exception
  • Operations must be designed to adapt to change
  • Structure and flexibility must coexist
  • Leadership requires clarity, not control
  • Alignment matters more than retention

Her approach focuses on building systems that perform despite change, rather than relying on stability.

Strategic Focus

Her work is centered on building resilient, scalable organizations that can sustain performance in dynamic environments. This includes a strong emphasis on workforce planning, operational design, performance management, and leadership development.

Leadership Vision

Shadan’s vision is to reshape leadership into a system of development, where clarity, structure, and accountability enable individuals and teams to perform beyond expectations and sustain success independently.

Leadership Statement

“Leadership is not about stability.
It is about designing systems that perform in its absence.”

Dr. Ruchi Mishra Sharma | Integrating Science, Hypnotherapy, and Spiritual Insight for Women’s Transformation

Dr. Ruchi Mishra Sharma is a practitioner and thought leader working at the intersection of medical science, hypnotherapy, and inner transformation. With a background rooted in healthcare and a growing presence in the space of RTT (Rapid Transformational Therapy), she focuses on helping women navigate emotional, mental, and personal challenges through a more holistic approach.

As the founder of Freedom and Empowerment Hypnotherapy with Ruchi, she works closely with individuals seeking clarity, confidence, and deeper self-awareness. Her practice combines structured therapeutic techniques with elements of mindset work and spiritual understanding, creating a space where clients can explore and address limiting beliefs, emotional blocks, and patterns that hold them back.

Her work is particularly centered on women’s transformation. Through one-on-one sessions and guided processes, she supports women in building emotional resilience, improving self-worth, and making more aligned life decisions. She also works with women to break free from the weight of guilt and shame associated with childhood sexual abuse, helping them reclaim their power, make empowered choices, and move forward with freedom. Her approach is not just about short-term solutions, but about enabling long-term internal shifts.

Alongside her practice, Ruchi is also an author and speaker who shares insights on personal growth, healing, and self-empowerment. Her content reflects a balance between clinical understanding and intuitive awareness, making her work accessible to a wide audience navigating both personal and professional transitions.

Her digital presence offers a closer look at her work, sessions, and philosophy: “https://linktr.ee/drruchimishrasharmachyp” 

At the core of her work is a clear intention: to help individuals, especially women, reconnect with their inner strength, overcome internal barriers, and move forward with clarity and confidence.

Dr. Fatima Bennai-Sanfourche: Leading with Purpose at the Heart of Global Healthcare

In global healthcare, leadership is increasingly defined by the ability to navigate complexity with clarity, integrity, and purpose. Dr. Fatima Bennai-Sanfourche stands among the women leaders shaping this transformation, guiding innovation in MedTech and digital health while ensuring that patient safety and trust remain at the center of progress. Dr. Fatima Bennai-Sanfourche exemplifies this modern form of leadership, where science, regulation, and global impact come together to shape the future of healthcare.

In her role as Global Senior Director of Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs Compliance for Medical Devices, Combination Products, and eHealth at Bayer AG, Dr. Bennai-Sanfourche plays a critical role in ensuring that life-changing innovations reach patients safely and responsibly across the world. Her work supports the integration of advanced medical technologies and digital health solutions within highly regulated environments, helping organizations move forward with confidence and integrity.

With more than two decades of experience, her career reflects a powerful journey from scientific research to global leadership. Holding a PhD in Pharmacology and Pharmacochemistry, she combines deep scientific expertise with strategic oversight across design Control, regulatory affairs, pharmacovigilance, post-market surveillance, and quality management. This rare combination allows her to bridge complexity with clarity and ambition with accountability.

Beyond her corporate responsibilities, Dr. Bennai-Sanfourche is a respected voice in the European healthcare ecosystem. Through active engagement with EFPIA, the European Commission, and the European Medicines Agency, she contributes to shaping regulatory frameworks that protect patients while enabling sustainable innovation.

As a woman leader operating at the intersection of science, policy, and global business, Dr. Fatima Bennai-Sanfourche continues to inspire by example, demonstrating that meaningful impact is created not only by advancing technology, but by leading with purpose, resilience, and vision.

Bassant Hamed | Engineering Clarity in Complex Mega Projects

“Great projects are not controlled by data alone. They are guided by the systems that make that data meaningful.”

For Bassant Hamed, project control is not just about tracking numbers. It is about creating clarity in environments where complexity is constant and decisions carry significant weight. With over 14 years of experience across large scale developments in the Middle East, she has built a career around designing systems that bring structure, visibility, and confidence to high stakes projects.

In her role at Dar Al Handasah’s Dubai Design Studio, Bassant operates at the intersection of data, strategy, and execution. Her work focuses on building the frameworks that enable leadership teams to move from fragmented information to clear, actionable insights. Instead of simply monitoring cost and schedule, she develops integrated controls systems that support decision making across entire project portfolios.

A key part of her contribution lies in transforming how information flows within organizations. By leveraging tools such as Power Automate, SharePoint, and Excel Online, she has streamlined reporting processes and enabled real time visibility across projects. Her work in developing Power BI dashboards, integrated with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations, allows stakeholders to access critical data on cost, schedule, and risk with speed and precision.

Beyond systems, Bassant plays a central role in establishing consistency and alignment. She designs standardized program level controls frameworks that can be implemented across multiple projects, ensuring coherence even in highly dynamic environments. Her involvement in cross project dependency mapping and risk evaluation further strengthens strategic planning, allowing organizations to anticipate challenges rather than react to them.

She is equally committed to building capability within teams. Through structured training initiatives, she equips engineering professionals with the knowledge and tools required to adopt PMBOK aligned practices and effectively navigate digital platforms such as Dynamics 365. This focus on upskilling ensures that systems are not only implemented but also sustained through people.

What sets Bassant apart is her forward looking approach to project controls. She is actively exploring how artificial intelligence and automation can shift the discipline from reactive reporting to predictive performance management. Her work reflects a clear vision of the future, where data is not just reported but intelligently used to drive outcomes.

Bassant Hamed continues to redefine project controls as a strategic function, proving that behind every successful mega project lies a system designed to bring clarity, control, and confidence at scale.

Omneya Mohamed | Expanding Access Through Evidence, Policy, and Strategic Leadership

“Healthcare systems are not transformed by innovation alone, but by how effectively that innovation reaches patients.”

For Omneya Mohamed, market access is not simply about pricing or reimbursement. It is about ensuring that innovation translates into real, equitable patient outcomes across diverse and often complex healthcare systems. With a career spanning global organizations and multiple regions, she has built a reputation for aligning evidence, policy, and commercial strategy to expand sustainable access to healthcare.

Currently serving as the Head of Health Economics, Market Access, and Reimbursement for Baxter’s Renal Care business across the Middle East and Africa, Omneya operates at the intersection of data, policy, and strategic execution. Her role focuses on identifying access priorities across markets, shaping regional HEMAR strategies, and enabling leadership teams to navigate evolving payer and policy landscapes. By working closely with cross-functional teams, she ensures that value propositions are not only clinically sound but also economically and systemically relevant.

A key dimension of her work lies in translating complex evidence into actionable insights for decision-makers. From leading economic evidence generation to localizing value propositions for payers and providers, she enables informed decision-making across healthcare systems. Her approach emphasizes the importance of contextual intelligence, ensuring that strategies are tailored to the realities of each market while maintaining alignment with broader organizational goals.

Before joining Baxter, Omneya played a pivotal role in establishing and scaling the Health Economics and Outcomes Research function at IQVIA across the Middle East and Africa. Leading a growing team, she drove double-digit business growth while delivering high-impact projects, including cost-effectiveness models, budget impact analyses, and policy advisory initiatives. Her work supported both industry and government stakeholders in making evidence-based decisions that optimize healthcare resource allocation.

Her experience in the public sector further strengthens her perspective. During her time with the World Bank in Cairo, she contributed to the economic evaluation of national health policies, including strategies for the prevention of viral hepatitis. Her work helped inform a landmark national program that led to the large-scale rollout of prevention initiatives and ultimately contributed to the eradication of hepatitis C in Egypt within a decade. This experience reflects her ability to connect rigorous analysis with real-world impact at a national level.

Earlier in her career, as a research fellow at Merck in the United States, Omneya developed a strong foundation in outcomes research, supporting global studies that assessed the value of pharmaceutical innovations. This experience shaped her ability to identify unmet needs, design robust research frameworks, and generate evidence that informs both clinical and commercial decision-making.

Beyond her professional roles, Omneya is deeply committed to advancing capabilities within the healthcare ecosystem. Through advisory roles, training initiatives, and collaborations with academic and governmental institutions, she contributes to building expertise in health economics and market access across the region. Her work reflects a belief that sustainable progress in healthcare depends not only on systems and strategy, but also on people and knowledge.

What sets Omneya apart is her ability to navigate complexity with clarity and purpose. By bridging evidence, policy, and business strategy, she continues to shape how healthcare innovation reaches patients in diverse markets. Her work stands as a testament to the impact of thoughtful, data-driven leadership in improving access and outcomes at scale.

Juan José Thuemme: Driving Natural Innovation in Food & Beverage

“Dreams are made of a subtle, immaterial essence that drives us to create, shape, and transform.”

For Juan José Thuemme, this belief is not just philosophy. It is the foundation of a career dedicated to bringing Mexico’s culinary soul back to life through flavor.

As Global Flavorist and Creative Center Leader at Etadar by Deiman, Thuemme is redefining what it means to create flavors. His work is not limited to formulation or innovation in the conventional sense. Instead, it is rooted in storytelling. Each flavor he develops carries history, memory, and identity, allowing people across the world to experience Mexico in its most authentic form.

At the heart of his work lies the concept of Native Flavors. This distinctive approach focuses on reviving pre Hispanic ingredients and culinary traditions that have gradually disappeared from modern consumption. Through this, Thuemme is not just creating flavors. He is preserving a cultural legacy and reintroducing it to a global audience with relevance and respect.

Since joining Deiman in 2014, Thuemme has played a key role in shaping the company’s global presence. With experience gained from international flavor houses and a portfolio that includes the creation of thousands of flavors, he brings both scale and depth to his craft. His contribution has strengthened Deiman’s position as a serious contender in the international flavor industry.

Beyond innovation, his commitment extends to education and future building. Thuemme is actively working on establishing a Flavorists School in Mexico, aiming to nurture the next generation of talent. This initiative reflects his belief that knowledge and craft must be passed forward to sustain the industry’s evolution.

His creations reflect both creativity and cultural depth. From indulgent profiles like Tres Leches to complex compositions inspired by tequila layered with citrus, cactus, and nanches, his work captures the diversity of Mexican taste. Traditional beverages like tepache are reimagined for global audiences, while techniques such as extracting new aromas from vanilla bean residues highlight his scientific and sustainable approach.

What makes Thuemme’s work truly distinctive is his ability to merge heritage with experimentation. Whether it is chocolate taco inspired profiles, cappuccino infused with chipotle, or cacao and chile combinations, his creations bridge ancient traditions with contemporary preferences in a way that feels both bold and authentic.

For Juan José Thuemme, flavor is more than a sensory experience. It is a medium of cultural expression. Through his work, he continues to ensure that Mexico’s rich culinary heritage is not only preserved but also celebrated on a global stage.

The top 10 inspiring leaders featured in this article are playing a crucial role in shaping the next era of business. Their inspirational journeys are a reminder for every aspiring professional, reflecting how resilience and integrity can break barriers to build success.

excerpt: Allegations of war crimes in Afghanistan have led to charges against Australia’s most decorated living soldier. Ben Roberts-Smith, who departed the military in 2013, was taken into custody at the Sydney airport on Tuesday and is scheduled to appear in court on five counts of the war crime of murder. Before his bail hearing on Wednesday, he will spend the night in a jail. The former corporal in Australia’s Special Air Service Regiment (SAS) was found to have killed multiple unarmed Afghans in a 2023 defamation ruling. The 47-year-old Victoria Cross recipient has previously described the accusations against him, which have not yet been evaluated at a criminal standard, as “egregious” and “spiteful” and has denied any misconduct. For the first time in history, a court looked into allegations of war crimes committed by Australian forces during the civil trial. Roberts-Smith lost an appeal against the Federal Court’s decision last year, arguing that the claimed killings either did not occur at all or happened lawfully during combat. The Australian Federal Police (AFP) announced during a press conference in Sydney on Tuesday that a 47-year-old ex-soldier had been taken into custody and would face charges of killing unarmed detainees while serving in Afghanistan from 2009 to 2012. He is charged with three counts of helping, abetting, counseling, or procuring a murder, one of the war crime of murder, and one of jointly commissioning a murder. title: A Middle East Oil Shock to India’s Rapidly Expanding Economy
author: editor
excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the nation’s central bank, recently described the country’s high-growth, low-inflation climate as a “Goldilocks” moment. However, that optimism has proved fleeting, as the Middle East’s prolonged conflict and the ensuing disruption to the oil markets have delivered an unanticipated shock to its world-beating economic story. The Indian currency, which has fallen to all-time lows and is down about 10% against the US dollar over the past year, is most obviously affected. After the central bank stepped in to curb speculation, there has been some respite from the rupee’s decline, but this is likely temporary. Depending on how long the dispute lasts, many experts predict steeper drops in the future. According to Bernstein, a global stock research firm, the consequences might be “catastrophic” for the rupee, which could fall below 110 per dollar in the worst-case scenario, where the conflict lasts for a large portion of 2026. Even if it ends much sooner, there will still be more suffering. Consumer prices, corporate profit margins, government deficits, and capital flows into the stock market can all be severely affected by persistent currency weakening. Due to an outflow of foreign currency, India’s benchmark equity indexes have already dropped by over 12% since the start of the year, undermining the wealth effect a behavioral propensity to increase spending as asset values rise that was encouraging the wealthy to maintain the consumption engine. title: Somalia will Conduct its Historic” First Offshore oil Drilling
author: editor
excerpt: A drilling ship operated by the Turkish government is scheduled to arrive off the coast of Somalia on Friday, and the country says it is prepared to start its first offshore oil drilling operations. The action comes after a Turkish research vessel successfully completed seismic surveys last year. Dahir Shire, Somalia’s minister of petroleum, called the move toward what would be the nation’s first offshore drilling a “historic milestone in our offshore energy journey… A new chapter begins” in a post on X. If the drilling is successful, it will uncover offshore oil deposits and help the nation’s economic recovery as a major player in the regional energy market, according to the foreign ministry. On its first international voyage, the drilling ship Çağrı Bey of the Turkish Petroleum Corporation is sailing into Somalia’s territorial waters in the Arabian Sea. At locations identified in recent assessments detailing the nation’s hydrocarbon potential, it will conduct deepwater drilling.This indicates that Somalia is prepared to commence exploratory drilling, starting with our most attractive offshore opportunities,” Shire stated. title: Europe Wonders if Restarting Nuclear is the Solution in Light of The Recent Energy Shock
author: editor
excerpt: Families and businesses throughout Europe are seeing gas prices and the expense of filling cars with petrol spiral out of control. The European Commission, the executive branch of the EU, has urged people to work more from home and travel far less, while the UK government has essentially instructed voters to remain calm and carry on. Depending on what transpires in the Middle East, policymakers caution that things could get far worse. However, with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Europeans experienced a cost-of-living crisis due to rising oil prices and inflation, which seems like it was only yesterday. This indicates that the topic of energy independence is coming up (again) in European discussions. Additionally, nuclear energy appears to be making a comeback as a domestic component of the European energy mix, both in the UK and the EU. However, how safe and dependable is nuclear truly, and how quickly can it be fixed? Ursula von der Leyen, the head of the European Commission, who may have forgotten that she was a minister in the German government when it decided to phase out nuclear power plants in 2011, called Europe’s general retreat from nuclear a “strategic mistake” at the recent European Nuclear Energy Summit in Paris. title: Trump Wants $152 Million to Revive the Infamous Alcatraz Prison
author: editor
excerpt: As part of his proposed budget for the 2027 fiscal year, US President Donald Trump is requesting $152 million (£115 million) to reopen the notorious Alcatraz jail. The Rock, a location close to San Francisco’s Golden Gate Bridge, was formerly thought to be one of the country’s most infamous prisons but has recently become a popular tourist destination. The budget plan calls for funding “to rebuild Alcatraz as a state-of-the-art secure prison facility,” with the first year’s expenses being covered. Many legislators in California have expressed skepticism about the concept, citing concerns about the project’s ultimate cost and the difficulties of maintaining Alcatraz as an operational prison. In 1963, the maximum security institution was shut down. It is currently managed by the National Park Service as a tourist destination. Nancy Pelosi, a former speaker of the US House of Representatives, declared that the Trump administration’s budget proposal was “absurd on its face and should be rejected outright. “It would be a waste of government money and an insult to the intelligence of the American people to rebuild Alcatraz as a contemporary prison. title: The Search for a US Crew Member is “Harrowing and Dangerous” For the Rescue Team in Iran
author: editor
excerpt: According to preliminary accounts, the pilot of a US F-15 fighter plane that went down over Iran was saved. If verified, this would be the most recent in decades of US combat search and rescue operations. According to CBS, the BBC’s US partner, a search for a second crew member is still underway deep within Iran. One of the most difficult and urgent operations that the US and its allies prepare for is combat search and rescue (CSAR). Elite US air force units are frequently proactively stationed close to war areas where aircraft could be lost, and they are specifically trained for CSAR operations. In a nutshell, CSAR missions are military operations designed to locate, assist, and possibly rescue persons in need, such as isolated soldiers and downed pilots. CSAR missions take place in hostile or contested circumstances, unlike traditional search-and-rescue operations, which may occur during humanitarian operations or following disasters. Operations may take place deep within enemy territory in certain situations, such as the alleged recovery mission in Iran on Friday. Helicopters are frequently used for CSAR missions, with other military aircraft available to execute strikes and patrol the area and refueling aircraft in support. At least 24 pararescue jumpers would search the region in Black Hawk helicopters during a rescue mission similar to the one described in Iran, according to a former commander of a pararescue jumpers squadron who spoke with CBS News. They stated that the squad would be ready to leap the aircraft if necessary, and that getting in touch with the missing crew member would be their top priority once they were on the ground. Since the change does not apply to generic medications, the most widely used in the United States, its significance may currently be primarily symbolic. title: Nearer Connections With the European Union Spark Putin’s Ultimatum to Armenia
author: editor

excerpt: Reiterating his threats to attack Iran “extremely hard” in the coming weeks without providing specific ideas on how the war would end, US President Donald Trump has once again sent oil prices rising. In the wake of Trump’s State of the Union address, stock markets across the globe experienced a decline, as Brent crude temporarily soared beyond $109 (£82) per barrel. He predicted that the United States would accomplish its war goals “very shortly” and then bomb Iran “back to the Stone Ages” over the next 2-3 weeks. Oil prices fell below $100 earlier on Wednesday in anticipation of Trump’s speech, as investors awaited his announcement on the US’s withdrawal from the battle. However, Trump essentially restated his earlier statements. Following Iran’s warning to attack ships attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz in response to US-Israeli operations that started on 28 February, oil exports through this vital waterway have been mostly suspended. Trump stated in his speech that the United States does not require energy from the Middle East and called on other countries to help restore oil exports from the Gulf that have been interrupted by the conflict. title: In an Effort to Defend the Strait of Hormuz, More than 40 Nations Have Joined Forces
author: editor
excerpt: On Thursday, more than 40 nations formed an alliance to ensure unfettered access to the Strait of Hormuz, an essential shipping route for oil exports, after the current high-tension conflict between Iran, Israel, and the US ends. The diverse range of nations shown here is indicative of the global reach of the economic shock wave generated by the canal’s temporary blockage. With thousands of ships still stuck in the crucial strait, US President Donald Trump has been putting increasing pressure on European partners to help reopen it. British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper convened the initial meeting virtually.According to Cooper’s opening statements, Iran has taken over an international shipping channel and is now using it to manipulate the world economy. She warned of catastrophic interruptions to gas, jet fuel, fertilizers, and the expense of living in general. A “safe and sustained opening” of Hormuz, which is now subject to a toll system under Tehran’s direct control, would be achieved by the “collective mobilization of our full range of diplomatic and economic tools,” she added, announcing that the global coalition will pursue. New economic sanctions against Iran’s government might be one such instrument. Concurrently, military strategists will investigate demining and escorting options “once the conflict eases. title: The Same Government is Still Firmly in Place in Iran as The Country Focuses on Survival
author: editor
excerpt: Even if President Trump delivered his prime-time speech on the Iran conflict on Wednesday night with the intention of projecting control, he exposed a fundamental contradiction in the process. In a move that seemed to signal the end of the war, the president of the United States said that Iran’s navy, air force, missile program, and nuclear enrichment facilities had been mostly destroyed. But he also threatened to escalate the situation even further in the next weeks. The end result is a message that isn’t sure what it is: triumph announced, but not achieved. Back to the stone ages, where they belong” was his threat to strike Iran, further infusing the hyperbole. That comment has real-world consequences in Iran, inflaming social media outrage even among opposition supporters who saw Trump as a change agent in the past. Some feel even more besieged by the government as a result, rather than the system being pushed to its limits. There has been no change to the structure of power in Tehran. The office of the supreme leader is still the source of authority, but the extent to which direct control is really exerted is unclear, especially given the current state of affairs. title: The US Attorney General, Pam Bondi, is Removed by Trump
author: editor
excerpt: Longtime Trump loyalist and staunch advocate of his government, Attorney General Pam Bondi, has been fired from her position as America’s top law enforcement official by US President Donald Trump. In an article on Truth Social, Trump lauded her and announced that she was “transitioning” to work for a private company. During Bondi’s tenure as head of the justice department, the handling of papers pertaining to Jeffrey Epstein and the investigation into the convicted sex offender frequently took center stage. It follows the March ouster of homeland security chief Kristi Noem as the second high-ranking Trump administration official to be removed from her position in as many weeks. Deputy Bondi’s old boss, Todd Blanche, will be taking over for her. The position had been “the honour” of Bondi’s life, and she promised to “work tirelessly” to hand over her responsibilities to Blanche. Bondi went on to say that she would “continue fighting for President Trump and this administration” in her unnamed new private sector job. This announcement is made just over two months after Bondi’s contentious appearance before Congress, during which she was interrogated relentlessly by lawmakers and, at one point, referred to one Democrat as a “washed-up loser. title: A New Museum in the Netherlands is Celebrating Apple’s 50th Anniversary by Displaying the History of the Computer Giant
author: editor
excerpt: Two idealistic young men in their early twenties came up with the idea of using circuits and wires to create a game-changing invention fifty years ago in a small garage. Today, tourists to Utrecht, Netherlands, can immerse themselves in that narrative at the spanking new Apple Museum, which charts the rise of the corporation from a fledgling startup to a legendary name in technology. Among the many Apple items on display at the museum are the first Macintosh, early computers from the 1970s, and other technologies that had an impact on the development of personal computing. Start your adventure off right by stepping into a replica of the garage that Steve Jobs and his buddy and co-founder, Steve Wozniak, formally registered Apple Computer Company on 1 April 1976. This garage is commonly thought of as a significant location in Apple’s early days. “The museum is set up in a way that when you enter, you start in the garage, which is where it all began, and it’s not so that it was their headquarters, but it tells a lot about the two people that founded Apple, Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs, and what the basis is of their vision behind the products,” said Ed Bindels, the museum’s founder.Thus, we will inform them, in a methodical fashion, about the design language they employ and the evolution of the brand. “Our hope is that people will leave this museum with a better understanding of Apple and, perhaps, a new perspective on Apple products,” he continued. title: The Potential ‘Shock’ of an Iranian War Might Cause 1.3 Million Homeowners to see Their Mortgage Rates Rise
author: editor
excerpt: According to the Bank of England, the war in the Middle East might lead to higher mortgage payments for approximately 1.3 million UK homeowners by the end of 2028. Borrowing costs are expected to increase due to the “shock” to the global economy, according to the Bank’s most recent assessment into economic risks. The number of households expecting to experience increases in mortgage expenses in the next 2.5 years has jumped from 3.9 million before the conflict to 5.2 million. In contrast to rises in previous years, such as following the 2022 mini-budget, the report stated that these increases would “remain modest” in scale. Oil and gas prices, as well as the cost of government borrowing, have climbed significantly since the US-Israeli airstrikes on Iran started a month ago. According to the Bank’s Financial Policy Committee, the UK economic outlook has “deteriorated” because of this, which could impact GDP and lead to higher inflation. Businesses and consumers in the UK would feel the pinch more acutely if the “sustained” increases in energy and mortgage prices were to continue. The banks and the financial system as a whole have been “resilient so far,” according to the Bank, since the markets have been able to absorb some “very large moves” since the conflict started. title: Shortly After Trump’s Iran War Pledge, Oil Prices Dip below $100 and Stock Prices Rise
author: editor
excerpt: Wednesday saw a rise in European stock prices and a temporary dip below $100 per barrel in oil prices following President Trump’s statement that the US will withdraw from Iran in “two to three weeks” regardless of the outcome of negotiations with Tehran. In response to Trump’s promise and in anticipation of his address this evening, in which he will “deliver an important update on Iran,” Brent crude dipped to $98.65 before slowly rising to $101. The UK’s FTSE 100 index increased by 1.3 percent. Both the French Cac and the German Dax were up 1.8% and 2.1%, respectively. After Iran threatened to attack ships using the Strait of Hormuz, effectively shutting down the main shipping route, oil and gas prices skyrocketed during the US-Israel war. According to QatarEnergy, a fuel oil ship that they rented was “the subject of a missile attack” early Wednesday morning. No injuries were reported among the crew members, and the incident was determined to have no negative effects on the environment. Iran fired three cruise missiles, two of which were intercepted, and the third struck the tanker, according to Qatar’s Ministry of Defense. In his Tuesday speech from the Oval Office, Trump stated that Iran is “begging to make a deal” but that the timing of the deal is “irrelevant” to America’s agenda. The Kingdom has achieved remarkable progress in fields including renewable energy, tourism, logistics and technology in the last several years. These changes are luring investors from all over the world, who view Saudi Arabia as a springboard to the larger markets of the GCC and the Middle East and North Africa. Businesses and entrepreneurs are the finding new opportunities as a result of megaprojects such as Qiddiya, The Red Sea Project and NEOM which are transforming the country’s infrastructure. Saudi Arabia aspires to become a center for innovation sustainability and international tourism through these projects. Local businesses have become more active as a result of government programs that aid small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Both new and existing businesses are finding new opportunities because to the easing of rules financial incentives and other obstacles. Reforms that permit 100% foreign ownership in a number of sectors have also contributed to the sustained increase in foreign direct investment (FDI). Because of this foreign enterprises can now enter the Saudi market with confidence. Businesses these are able to run more smoothly and attract more customers as a result of investments in AI fintech and smart city solutions. To ensure a skilled staff capable of supporting future expansion the Kingdom is also investing heavily in educational and training initiatives for the local talent. Saudi Arabia’s worldwide competitiveness is being strengthened by its dependence on innovation. Enhancing Cooperation within the Regions There has been an increase in the economic cooperation among the GCC members. To improve infrastructure connectivity investment and trade Saudi Arabia is collaborating with its neighbors. A more connected economic environment and more regional stability are anticipated outcomes of these agreements. With the aim to promote regional unity and progress the United Arab Emirates Qatar and other GCC members are coordinating their policies in areas including digital services energy and logistics. A Bright Prospectus Moving Forward Business in Saudi Arabia is looking well thanks to the government’s support rising investor confidence and ambitious plans for the future. title: Fuel Prices Increase Dramatically, Prompting Korean Air to Take Emergency Measures
author: editor
excerpt: In the midst of the ongoing US-Israel confrontation with Iran, Korean Air has announced that it is putting itself into emergency management mode in order to mitigate the effects of the surge in jet fuel prices. The nation’s flag carrier will take “internal cost-reduction measures” to stabilize its finances in the face of rising fuel prices and worldwide economic uncertainties, according to a company representative who made the announcement on Tuesday. It follows other Asian airlines in announcing plans to mitigate the financial blow of the war in Iran. Worldwide, the price of jet fuel has more than quadrupled since the battle started on 28 February, while the price of crude oil has increased by more than 50%. According to Tan Chi Siang of PwC Singapore, an advisory firm, airlines have implemented such emergency procedures to safeguard their operations in times of crisis, like as the COVID-19 pandemic. He went on to say that Asian airlines are particularly hit hard by the “double shock” of increasing oil prices worldwide and a regional jet fuel scarcity, which has compelled them to act. According to Tan, most airlines would take internal steps like reducing investments or renovations, but some may even curtail flights to save money. title: As the Iran War Enters its Fifth Week, Oil Prices Increase and Asian Stocks Decline
author: editor
excerpt: Monday saw a strong decline in Asian stocks and an increase in global oil prices as the US-Israel confrontation with Iran began its fifth week. Overnight, the price of Brent crude increased by over 3% to surpass $115 (£86.77) per barrel. Later, it dropped a little to about $113, but it is still on course to record its largest monthly gain. South Korea’s Kospi ended nearly 3% lower, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 2.8%. It comes after Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen joined the conflict by striking Israel over the weekend and Iran threatened to expand retaliatory strikes against universities and the homes of US and Israeli officials. In an interview with the Financial Times on Sunday, US President Donald Trump stated that he might “take the oil in Iran” and potentially capture Kharg Island, the country’s main fuel center. Regarding Iranian defense on the island, he responded, “I don’t think they have any defense. We could take it very easily.” Trump compared the potential move to Venezuela where the US plans to control the oil industry “indefinitely” after the seizure in January of then-President Nicolás Maduro. The speaker of Iran’s parliament issued a warning over the weekend that his nation’s armed forces were “waiting for American soldiers” as an additional 3,500 US soldiers entered the Middle East. author: editor

title: Tech CEOs Have Taken to Blaming AI for Massive Layoffs Why?
author: editor
excerpt: Big Tech businesses have made widespread layoffs a yearly ritual. But the way executives justify their choices has evolved. Buzzwords like “efficiency,” “overhiring,” and “too many layers of management” are out. These days, artificial intelligence (AI) is the source of all explanations. Giants like Google, Amazon, and Meta, as well as smaller companies like Pinterest and Atlassian, have all announced or warned of intentions to reduce their workforces in recent weeks, citing advancements in artificial intelligence that they claim enable their businesses to accomplish more with fewer employees. According to a spokesperson, Meta is still hiring in “priority areas” despite its intentions to almost treble its AI spending this year. title: As the War Drives up Prices in Australia, the Fuel Tax Has Been Cut in Half and Free Public Transportation is Provided
author: editor
excerpt: As fuel costs rise as a result of the Middle East conflict, two Australian governments will provide free public transportation to encourage people to avoid driving. Melbourne’s home state of Victoria has announced free travel for the entire month of April, while Tasmania has announced that commuters won’t have to pay until the end of June. Thus far, other state governments have refused to do the same. In an effort to relieve financial strain on drivers, the federal government recently said that it will cut the country’s fuel excise tax in half for three months. Since the beginning of the US-Israel war with Iran and the effective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, fuel costs have skyrocketed in a number of countries, including Australia. Governments all around the world have started enacting fuel-saving measures as a result of the nearly complete blockade of international commerce in the crucial waterway, which transports about 20% of the world’s natural gas and oil. Anthony Albanese, the prime minister of Australia, has previously attempted to reassure drivers in response to tales of panic purchases and empty gas stations. The fuel excise, a sales tax, will be reduced by 26.3 cents per litre for gasoline and diesel, according to the government’s announcement on Monday. This should save drivers between A$10 (£5.18; $6.87) and A$20 per tank. title: Bank of America will Settle the Epstein Lawsuit for $72.5 Million
author: editor
excerpt: In a lawsuit filed on behalf of Jeffrey Epstein’s victims, who had accused the bank of supporting his sex trafficking business, Bank of America agreed a $72.5 million (£54.6 million) settlement. A Florida lady who claims she was mistreated by Epstein “on at least 100 occasions” between 2011 and 2019 and had two Bank of America accounts at the behest of his business team filed the proposed class-action lawsuit in October. The bank was accused of having “a plethora of information regarding Epstein’s sex trafficking operation but chose profit over protecting the victims” . According to Bank of America’s court filings, the settlement contains “no admission of liability” or “wrongdoing” on its part. Although the settlement was reached earlier this month, the specifics of the agreement were not made public until paperwork were submitted to a federal court in New York on Friday. They are now awaiting permission from a court. The victims’ attorney, Sigrid McCawley, told the BBC earlier this month that the agreement was “one more step on the road to much deserved justice” in a statement. After JP Morgan Chase and Deutsche Bank agreed to pay out $290 million and $75 million, respectively, this is the third large bank settlement of its kind. A “Jane Doe” filed the case, citing “incredibly alarming and erratic banking behaviour” in her own Bank of America accounts that Epstein’s team used. title: After Six Days at sea, Twenty-Two Migrants Perish off the Coast of Greece
author: editor
excerpt: According to the Greek coast guard, twenty-two migrants perished off the coast of Greece after spending six days in a dinghy headed for Europe. A European border agency warship rescued 26 survivors on Friday, including a lady and a kid. On the island of Crete, two of them were transported to a hospital in Heraklion. According to a coastguard spokesperson cited by news agency AFP, the migrant boat departed the port of Tobruk in eastern Libya on March 21. According to the coast guard, the deaths were caused by bad weather as well as a shortage of food and water. Many illegal migrants arrive in Greece and Italy through the Mediterranean, frequently from neighboring Turkey and northern Africa. Since there is a lower chance of inclement weather in the summer, many of these crossings take place then.The Greek coast guard reported that the dinghy’s passengers lost their bearings during the voyage and spent six days at sea without food or drink. Eventually, the vessel was stopped 53 nautical miles from the southern coastal city of Ierapetra. title: Iran-Backed Houthis Assault Israel as Part of a Conflict
author: editor
excerpt: The Houthis in Yemen, who are supported by Iran, claim to have launched the first missile barrage toward Israel since the US-Israeli war with Iran began. In a statement, the organization claimed to have attacked “sensitive Israeli military sites” and promised to keep doing so. Israel claimed to have shot down two Yemeni rockets. Because the armed organization has the ability to strike shipping in the Red Sea, the introduction of the potent Iranian proxy into the battle raises concerns about additional damage to the global economy. The Houthis see themselves as a part of an alleged “axis of resistance” that also consists of other organizations funded by Iran, like Hamas in the Gaza Strip and Hezbollah in Lebanon. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that started 12 years ago when the Houthis overthrew the internationally recognized government in the country’s northwest. A coalition commanded by Saudi Arabia and backed by the US intervened in an attempt to reestablish the government. Most importantly, they are in charge of Yemen’s Red Sea shoreline. It was widely anticipated that the group would become involved in the conflict that started on February 28 with Israeli and US bombings on Iran. Working in different sectors from industrial to consumer, from technical to luxury, and from retail to media, he acquired years of hands-on experience in these sectors in several countries across the Middle East and the GCC. However, Issam’s passion for creativity and spatial aesthetics was his true calling. In 2010, he decided to merge both worlds and founded A-LINE DESIGN with his Partner in lie and in Business, Eng. From Kuwait to the GCC and across the Middle East, Issam’s focus is on delivering conceptual spaces that balance aesthetics, practicality, and sustainability. “We don’t just design interiors, we design experiences.
