Working in different sectors from industrial to consumer, from technical to luxury, and from retail to media, he acquired years of hands-on experience in these sectors in several countries across the Middle East and the GCC.

However, Issam’s passion for creativity and spatial aesthetics was his true calling. In 2010, he decided to merge both worlds and founded A-LINE DESIGN with his Partner in lie and in Business, Eng. Aline Matar. He reflects, “The transition wasn’t sudden, it was strategic. I realized that interior design is not just about beauty; it’s about experience, branding, and functionality. My marketing background gave me a competitive edge in understanding clients’ needs and delivering spaces that truly connect with their vision.”

Core Philosophy behind A-LINE DESIGN

With a philosophy rooted in transforming concepts into functional realities, A-LINE DESIGN believes that every space tells a story. Whether residential or commercial, each project begins with understanding the client’s personality, goals, and lifestyle, ensuring to never miss even the tiniest detail. From Kuwait to the GCC and across the Middle East, Issam’s focus is on delivering conceptual spaces that balance aesthetics, practicality, and sustainability.

“We don’t just design interiors, we design experiences. Every detail, from layout planning to material selection, is carefully curated to ensure harmony and efficiency. Our goal is not only to meet expectations but to exceed them by creating timeless environments that leave lasting impressions,” Issam states.

Issam’s marketing background has significantly influenced his approach to interior design operations. Marketing instilled in him structure, planning, and measurable execution. In interior design, creativity must be supported by operational excellence. His experience in sales forecasting, budgeting, brand development, and market analysis allows Issam to manage projects with precision.

He comments, “At A-LINE DESIGN, I handle everything from client relationships and concept development to execution and delivery. I approach each project like a brand launch. There is research, strategy, positioning, and a final presentation. This operational discipline ensures projects stay within timeline and budget while maintaining high-quality standards. It also helps us market our services effectively and build long-term relationships with clients across the region.”

Standing Apart from the Competition

What sets A-LINE DESIGN apart is its holistic approach. While many studios focus only on design aesthetics, it is recognised for integrating strategy, operations, and branding into every project. Because of Issam’s background in Marketing Management, he has a strong understanding of commercial spaces not merely as physical areas, but as business tools.

He explains, “For retail or corporate clients, design must enhance customer experience and brand identity. For residential projects, it must reflect personality and comfort. We also emphasize end-to-end involvement from conceptualization to execution ensuring consistency and quality control.” A regional understanding of the GCC market gives the firm cultural sensitivity and adaptability, which is crucial in delivering impactful projects.

Embracing Lessons throughout the Journey

Over 16 years at A-LINE DESIGN, Issam has experienced several events that shaped his leadership approach. He believes the biggest lesson is that leadership requires balance between vision and discipline. Issam reflects, “Creativity inspires, but structure delivers results. As a Partner and Operations Manager, I learned that clear communication, accountability, and teamwork are essential. Every project involves architects, contractors, suppliers, and clients alignment is critical. I also learned the importance of adaptability. Markets evolve, design trends change, and client expectations grow.”

Issam strongly believes a leader must remain flexible while staying true to the company’s core values. “Empowering my team and fostering a collaborative environment has been key to sustaining growth and maintaining a strong reputation in the region,” he adds.

“Concept development begins with listening. I spend significant time understanding the client’s objectives, lifestyle, and long-term vision,” Issam states. Then, they conduct site analysis, research design trends, and explore functional requirements. Aligning with Issam’s belief that a strong concept must be both creative and practical, they create mood boards, 3D visualizations, and detailed plans to bring ideas to life before execution at A-LINE DESIGN. Leveraging Issam’s marketing experience, he even identifies how a space will be perceived especially for commercial projects where brand identity plays a major role. He mentions, “The concept stage is crucial because it sets the foundation for smooth execution and ensures alignment with the client’s expectations.”

title: As the Price of Petrol Rises Above 150p, the Asda CEO Denies Accusations of Profiteering
author: editor
excerpt: Asda’s CEO has denied allegations that merchants are leveraging skyrocketing oil prices to increase their own profits, following Friday’s little increase in petrol prices. For the first time in almost two years, the average price of a liter of petrol surpassed 150p, with diesel surpassing 177p, just one month after the US and Israel attacked Iran. Fuel costs are still rising as a result of the crisis, although they are still lower than they were following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, according to RAC data. Filling a normal family car with unleaded gasoline now costs over £82, £9.50 more than it did a month ago. At almost £97, a tank of diesel costs £19 more. Allan Leighton, executive chairman of Asda, responded to claims that forecourts had profited from the crisis by accusing ministers of “pointing the finger” at retailers. Additionally, he added that some areas’ fuel supply were being impacted by the violence, with a few pumps being shut down due to high demand. According to Leighton, Asda, the second-largest gasoline retailer in the UK, has not shuttered any forecourts due to the conflict and anticipates that any impacted gas stations will be operational until its next delivery.Our fuel volumes have increased considerably, and it is evident that demand has exceeded supply,” he stated. title: PM Assures Australians About Fuel Supplies in Response to Panic Purchasing
author: editor
excerpt: In response to stories of panic buying and gas stations running out of fuel since the beginning of the Iran conflict, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has attempted to reassure Australians that the nation’s fuel supply is still “secure” despite rising costs.The impact will increase with the length of this war. However, we are still taking steps to protect Australians from the worst of it,” Albanese told reporters on Friday. Reports of stranded truck drivers and other truckers have surfaced, and companies claim that growing expenses are hurting their bottom line. The government claims that shortages are the result of problems with distribution and demand rather than supply, which is still at the same level as it was prior to the start of the conflict.For the next few weeks, Australia’s supply of petrol and diesel and oil will be the same, if not higher, than it normally would be,” Energy Minister Chris Bowen said alongside Albanese. The BBC discovered a little, independent garage in Cairns, Queensland, that tells a very typical Australian tale. Unleaded gasoline has run out, and diesel is now 85% more expensive than it was prior to the commencement of the Iranian conflict. One in seven stores in Australia’s most populated state, New South Wales, claim to be out of at least one kind of fuel. Since the US and Israel attacked Iran and closed the Strait of Hormuz, Australia has seen sharp increases in oil prices. title: Out of Major Economies, the UK is Expected to Suffer the Most From the Iran War in Terms of Growth
author: editor
excerpt: According to a prominent global policy body, the UK is facing the most significant growth damage from the Iran war among the G20 major economies. The Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) forecasts 0.7% economic growth in the United Kingdom this year, down from 1.2% previously. Inflation is also expected to be greater than anticipated. The OECD has reduced projections for many of the world’s largest economies in response to the US-Israeli confrontation with Iran. A prolonged conflict could cause “significant energy shortages” around the world, it warned, while if the dramatic spike in fertilizer prices continues, agricultural yields will suffer and food prices will skyrocket the next year. Wholesale oil and gas prices have risen since the war began, owing to disruptions in supply caused by the effective closing of the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping channels, as well as damage to Middle Eastern oil and gas facilities. Experts warn that continued high energy prices will slow development, feed inflation, and make interest rate reduction less likely. The impacts are already being seen at the pump, with UK drivers seeing higher fuel and diesel prices, as well as heating oil consumers. title: Is the New York Cannabis Industry Truly Thriving?
author: editor
excerpt: Cannabis appears to be everywhere in New York, five years after it was legalized. However, business owners report that many legitimate businesses are struggling, owing partly to a growing grey market and the US cannabis industry’s confusing legal position. If you’ve lately been to New York, you’ve probably noticed something. Advertisements outside bodegas include vivid green flowers, higher-end dispensaries resembling coffee shops or electronics stores welcome consumers from all over the world, and, of course, there’s the scent, which appears to be omnipresent, prompting even US Open tennis players to complain. Weed is everywhere. From the outside, it appears to be a free-for-all, with skepticism coming from even those who broadly favor the legalization’s goals, such as minimizing harm and increasing tax revenue. Social media is awash with complaints (typical comments include “New York could not have screwed up legal weed any worse!”), and for years, the local press has been charting the growth of the “weed bodega” – often a corner business selling items of questionable origin. Weed usage has surged across the country, although studies show that the rate of use among young people has gradually decreased since the turn of the century. Things may have reached a boiling point lately when the New York Times, a former backer of legal marijuana, published an editorial headed “Marijuana Is Everywhere.” “That is a problem.” The newspaper now claims that “marijuana is causing more harm than predicted” and advocates for stricter regulations. Moscow is apparently giving drones and intelligence services to Tehran, a long-standing friend, to assist target American military assets in the Middle East. title: Elon Musk’s X Advertising Boycott Action was Dismissed by a US Judge
author: editor
excerpt: A US judge has dismissed Elon Musk’s X lawsuit, in which the company accused a collection of advertisers and other corporations of illegally boycotting its platform. Its parent corporation, X Corp, claimed in 2024 that companies such as food giants Unilever and Mars, renewable energy business Orsted, and the World Federation of Advertisers (WFA) conspired to deprive it of “billions of dollars” in advertising income. However, in Thursday’s verdict, US District Judge Jane Boyle stated that the corporation had failed to demonstrate any harm under federal competition regulations. The BBC has contacted X for comment. X Corp’s action, filed in a Texas court in 2024, stemmed from the platform’s fall in advertising revenue following Musk’s acquisition of Twitter in 2022. After purchasing the platform, the tech billionaire implemented significant modifications, including the reinstatement of controversial figures’ accounts and the relaxation of certain content restrictions. Within a year of Musk’s acquisition of X, advertising revenue had dropped by more than half, as some companies delayed or curtailed their promotions on the site. title: Meta and YouTube Found Responsible in Historic Social Media Addiction Trial
author: editor
excerpt: A Los Angeles jury awarded an unusual victory to a young teenager who sued Meta and YouTube for her childhood social media addiction. Jurors determined that Meta, which owns Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, and Google, the owner of YouTube, purposefully created addictive social media platforms that affected the 20-year-old’s mental health. author: editor
excerpt: Despite escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, old prices have entered a sharper-than-expected correction phase, falling below important technical levels. Senior market analyst Rania Gule of XS.com claims that dueling bullish and corrective forces are shaping the precious metals market’s impending decisive consolidation period. She also pointed out that if bond yields stay high and the dollar keeps strengthening, prices might drop to $3,800. She referred to this correction as a rebalancing period rather than the end of the larger bull cycle. title: Huel Acquired by Danone For €1 Billion
author: editor
excerpt: Danone is buying Huel, a British meal supplement manufacturer, for €1 billion (£864 million). Huel was founded in Buckinghamshire in 2014 and is most known for its shake powder, which it claims is a nutritionally balanced alternative for a regular meal. Its investors include actor Idris Elba and broadcaster Jonathan Ross. It has since expanded its product line to include ready meals, nutrition bars, and health drinks, all of which are plant-based. The company has already run into trouble with the UK advertising watchdog, which banned some of its advertisements for making “misleading” claims. According to the watchdog, one such advertisement made deceptive claims about the financial savings of replacing a regular diet with meal-replacement shakes. Huel (a mashup of “human and “fuel) goods are largely sold directly to consumers, with some sales coming from stores and supermarkets, but the Danone partnership will allow it to expand into new areas. The market for so-called complete nutrition products, aimed at busy, health-conscious customers, is estimated to be worth $5.9 billion (£4.4 billion). Some experts, however, have questioned the efficacy of substituting meals with nutritionally dense beverages. title: As the Iran War Causes an Oil Shock, the US Maintains Interest Rates
author: editor
excerpt: A surge in oil prices since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran has increased economic uncertainty and raised the possibility of inflation, the US central bank chose to keep interest rates unchanged once more. The Federal Reserve’s benchmark interest rate remained in the 3.5%–3.75% range, where it has been since December, following the largely anticipated decision. Policymakers have been acting cautiously despite demands from US President Donald Trump to reduce borrowing costs because they are dealing with a challenging mixture of rising prices and conflicting signals from the labor market. Expectations for a rate cut have been pushed back to the end of this year, according to analysts, because the war has made them even less likely to do so. When the Fed notices an increase in unemployment and wishes to stimulate the economy, it usually reduces borrowing prices. title: Cheap Weight-Loss Medications From India could Change the Global Battle Against Obesity
author: editor
excerpt: In theory, India might soon become much thinner. The Danish pharmaceutical company Novo Nordisk’s semaglutide patent, which powers the popular weight-loss medications Wegovy and Ozempic, expires on Friday. This will enable local pharmaceutical firms to produce more affordable versions or generics, sparking a flurry of competition that could cut costs by over half and quickly increase access for Indians and, eventually, those in other nations as well. The semaglutide market may potentially reach $1 billion domestically with the correct pricing and acceptance, according to investment bank Jefferies, which has dubbed it a possible “magic-pill moment” for India. Within months, analysts predict that about fifty branded generics of semaglutide will hit the market; this is a common occurrence in India’s extremely competitive pharmaceutical sector. About 30 branded versions of the diabetes medication sitagliptin emerged within a month of its 2022 patent expiration, and almost 100 within a year. The rise in weight-loss medications is driven by wealthy Indians. By 2030, the pharmaceutical sector in India, which is currently valued at roughly $60 billion, is predicted to double. A large portion of it is based on generics, a manufacturing powerhouse that currently creates the conditions for intense competition over semaglutide. This costly injection, which is currently mostly reserved for wealthy patients, may soon become much more widespread. These medications, which were once created to treat diabetes, are now being heralded as revolutionary weight loss tools that provide outcomes that few other therapies could equal. Semaglutide is a member of a class of medications called GLP-1 receptor agonists, which imitate a hormone that controls blood sugar and hunger. The medications cause patients to feel fuller sooner and remain fuller longer by increasing insulin release and delaying stomach emptying. They were first created to treat diabetes, but they are now among the most popular methods for losing weight worldwide. title: Iran increases the Minimum Wage by 60% When Household Budgets are Severely Damaged by Conflict and Sanctions
author: editor
excerpt: Iran’s minimum wage was raised by 60% on Monday, from 103 million rials (€67.5) to 166 million rials (€109), according to Labor Minister Ahmad Meydari. The action, which is intended to assist offset skyrocketing living expenses, comes months after economic hardship-driven protests, as well as in the midst of worsening conditions brought on by the continuous conflict between the US and Israel and increased sanctions. According to credible reports, the IRGC severely suppressed protests in Iran in early 2026, killing at least 36,000 people. According to reports, the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei ordered security personnel to “crush the protests by any means necessary” and approved the use of live fire against demonstrators. The Iranian government’s attempt to stabilize society is shown in the minimum wage rise, which is a direct response to pressure from labor organizations. Many workers covered by the Iranian Labour Law can no longer afford basic items due to the rial’s current exchange rate of about 1.35 million per US dollar. The IRGC package also includes a rise in family and kid allowances. This change will go into effect on March 20, the Persian New Year, which corresponds to the year 1405 in the Solar Hijri calendar. Iran and Afghanistan have been using the Persian calendar, a solar calendar, since 622 AD. author: editor
excerpt: S Jaishankar, the foreign minister of India, expressed optimism that negotiations with Iran will start to reduce maritime interruptions for the nation’s ships in the Strait of Hormuz.He told the Financial Times, “I am currently speaking with them, and my conversations have produced some results. However, he clarified that there was no “blanket arrangement” that would allow all Indian ships to navigate the crucial oil transportation canal. Two Indian-flagged gas tankers passed through the strait on Saturday after discussions progressed between Delhi and Tehran. Twenty-two Indian-flagged vessels are still waiting for clearance to pass through the channel. It also carries around half of the country’s liquefied natural gas imports and most of its liquefied petroleum gas shipments. title: The CEO of India’s IndiGo Airline Quits Months after a Crisis That led to the Cancellation of Several Flights
author: editor
excerpt: The CEO of India’s biggest airline, IndiGo, has stepped down. This comes months after a crisis that caused the airline to cancel thousands of flights. The airline acknowledged that Pieter Elbers had left right away, saying he did so for “personal reasons” but did not provide further information. The move comes after a lot of attention was paid to the situation last year when new pilot roster restrictions caused a lot of cancellations that left customers stuck all over India. IndiGo owns approximately two-thirds of India’s domestic aviation market, so problems with its operations are a big deal for the country’s rapidly rising air travel industry. The airline has about 440 planes and largely flies within the United States. It also flies to a few places in the Middle East, Europe, and Asia. It has been a big part of the quick growth of India’s aviation industry, which is one of the fastest-growing air travel industries in the world. IndiGo announced in a press release on Tuesday that Rahul Bhatia, one of the company’s co-founders, will run the airline until a new CEO is chosen. IndiGo canceled around 4,500 flights in December, which was the biggest disruption in the airline’s 20-year history. This left thousands of customers stuck at airports all throughout the country. title: Gas Supplies Are Disrupted by The War in Iran, Which Puts Pressure on Indian Businesses
author: editor
excerpt: Due to the disruption of gas supply caused by the US and Israel’s attack on Iran, Indian firms claim they are finding it difficult to maintain operations. Restaurant owners are struggling to keep their kitchens operating, while business owners in sectors such as fertilizers and ceramics say they cannot sustain their output and are threatening to close. Although India claims to have an adequate supply of gas, it has taken emergency action to guarantee that supplies reach home customers and other important users. The country meets half of its total gas demand through imports, much of which flows through the Strait of Hormuz – a tiny Gulf chokepoint – where commerce has virtually been blocked by retaliatory Iranian strikes. Millions of barrels of gas and oil have become trapped close to the Strait of Hormuz as a result of the confrontation, which is currently in its eleventh day. The small channel is used for about 40–50% of India’s imports of crude oil. Additionally, it transports about 80–85% of the nation’s shipments of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and 50–60% of its LNG imports. LPG, which is commonly used as cooking gas, is the main worry for restaurants, cafes, and millions of other eateries throughout India. India is the world’s second-largest importer of LPG, after China, with 80–85% of its yearly use coming from imports. Nearly majority of it originates from Gulf producers that cross the Strait of Hormuz, primarily from Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Kuwait. title: Jamil Siddique | Building Scalable Logistics Across Continents Through Leadership and Transformation
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In the world of global logistics, scale is complex. Borders shift. Markets evolve. Technology accelerates. But at the center of sustainable growth remains one constant — leadership. Over three decades, Jamil Siddique has built and transformed logistics businesses across the UK, South Korea, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Mekong region, and the Middle East. From managing some of the earliest fully automated warehouses in the 1990s to leading multi-country clusters with thousands of employees, his career reflects disciplined expansion, operational excellence, and people-first leadership. In this exclusive conversation, he reflects on the experiences that shaped him, the growth milestones that defined his journey, and the principles that continue to guide his leadership across regions. The Foundation: From Operations to Global Leadership We began by asking, “Can you share your early background and what shaped your career journey?” “My early background started in 3PL logistics operations, working through a number of operational roles and progressing through the management ladder. I spent ten years in confectionery logistics in the UK, including managing one of the world’s first fully automated warehouses in the 1990s.” Those formative years grounded him in operational discipline. But his journey did not remain linear. He transitioned into sales development, then moved into change management across multiple logistics centers in the UK. In 2002, he relocated to South Korea to project manage a national distribution center for Carrefour with Exel Logistics. Soon after, Indonesia became his first full P&L leadership role as General Manager, later Country Director, until DHL acquired Exel in 2006. Each move expanded both geographical scope and leadership responsibility. Scaling Across Asia Continuing the conversation, we asked, “What major growth milestones stand out in your journey?” “It was a great experience to see the other side of logistics and supply chain. Understanding production brings a different perspective to distribution.” After Indonesia, he moved to Singapore with IDS Logistics, serving in customer development, special projects, and eventually as Country Head. There, he managed what was then the largest fully automated logistics center in Asia and established a healthcare distribution center compliant with GDPMDS standards. He later joined HAVI Logistics, overseeing regional supply chain operations for McDonald’s across multi-temperature networks. content:
In the world of global logistics, scale is complex. Borders shift. Markets evolve. Technology accelerates. But at the center of sustainable growth remains one constant — leadership.

Over three decades, Jamil Siddique has built and transformed logistics businesses across the UK, South Korea, Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Mekong region, and the Middle East. From managing some of the earliest fully automated warehouses in the 1990s to leading multi-country clusters with thousands of employees, his career reflects disciplined expansion, operational excellence, and people-first leadership.

In this exclusive conversation, he reflects on the experiences that shaped him, the growth milestones that defined his journey, and the principles that continue to guide his leadership across regions.

The Foundation: From Operations to Global Leadership

We began by asking, “Can you share your early background and what shaped your career journey?”

“My early background started in 3PL logistics operations, working through a number of operational roles and progressing through the management ladder. I spent ten years in confectionery logistics in the UK, including managing one of the world’s first fully automated warehouses in the 1990s.”

Those formative years grounded him in operational discipline. But his journey did not remain linear.

He transitioned into sales development, then moved into change management across multiple logistics centers in the UK. In 2002, he relocated to South Korea to project manage a national distribution center for Carrefour with Exel Logistics.

Soon after, Indonesia became his first full P&L leadership role as General Manager, later Country Director, until DHL acquired Exel in 2006.

Each move expanded both geographical scope and leadership responsibility.

Scaling Across Asia

Continuing the conversation, we asked, “What major growth milestones stand out in your journey?”

“It was a great experience to see the other side of logistics and supply chain. Understanding production brings a different perspective to distribution.”

After Indonesia, he moved to Singapore with IDS Logistics, serving in customer development, special projects, and eventually as Country Head. There, he managed what was then the largest fully automated logistics center in Asia and established a healthcare distribution center compliant with GDPMDS standards.

He later joined HAVI Logistics, overseeing regional supply chain operations for McDonald’s across multi-temperature networks. During a year in Japan, he designed and specified a fully automated logistics center, further strengthening his expertise in high-efficiency distribution systems.

In 2014, he moved to ECCO in Thailand as Supply Chain Director. This shift to the manufacturing side broadened his understanding of production supply chains.

Building From Zero – Jamil Siddique

In 2016, he joined Kuehne & Nagel with a mandate to establish its contract logistics business from scratch.

“We started with zero. The first customer win was in healthcare retail. From there, we completed an acquisition of a local logistics company.”

By 2021, the operation had grown to 40,000 square meters of warehousing space, 300 full-time employees, and a 200-truck fleet.

Growth was not accidental. It was structured, relationship-driven, and built on disciplined execution.

He then moved to DB Schenker, leading the Mekong Cluster across Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam. The business encompassed over 20 logistics centers and 4,000 employees across sectors including hi-tech, FMCG, retail, industrial, and electronics.

In December 2023, he joined TALKE as Regional Director Middle East, later expanding responsibilities into Asia in early 2025. By October 2025, he also assumed the role of Acting Managing Director for Malaysia, accelerating growth within months.

His academic milestone came alongside his operational journey, completing an MBA in 2019.

Leadership Over Scale

Shifting to leadership philosophy, we asked, “How have you consistently grown teams and businesses?”

“I build people. Growth comes from solid, trusting relationships and good leadership.”

For him, leadership is not transactional. It is cultural. Teams grow when they feel empowered and aligned.

When asked about critical qualities for success in logistics, he emphasized three elements:

  • Authentic and clear leadership
  • Strong performance management through KPIs and metrics
  • A culture that values accountability

“Without people behind you, success is not possible.”

Sustainability and Technology

We then explored industry evolution. “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?”

“Sustainable logistics is key. We must incorporate sustainability into the culture of the team and continuously look for efficiencies.”

On technological change, his approach is pragmatic.

“Technology is key to successful growth. We must embrace technology that makes sense and is applicable to the needs of the business.”

For him, innovation is not about adopting trends. It is about implementing solutions that deliver measurable operational value.

Advice for Emerging Leaders

As the conversation concluded, we asked, “What guidance would you give someone entering this industry?”

“First understand the market. Then understand the customer. Know your own capabilities and gaps before establishing yourself.”

It is grounded advice.

In an industry defined by scale and speed, clarity of understanding often determines longevity.

Final Reflection

Jamil Siddique’s journey reflects more than geographic mobility. It reflects strategic mobility. From early automation in the UK to multi-country leadership in Asia and the Middle East, his career demonstrates that sustainable logistics growth is built on three pillars: operational expertise, technological pragmatism, and authentic leadership.

As global supply chains become more interconnected and sustainability becomes non-negotiable, leaders who combine transformation capability with people-centered management will define the next era of logistics. With decades of international experience and a proven ability to build and scale complex logistics operations, Jamil continues to engage with industry leaders and organizations exploring the next phase of supply chain transformation.

title: Oil Prices Rise Above $100 Per Barrel as the Iran Crisis Affects Supplies
author: editor
excerpt: On Monday, oil prices rose above $114 (approximately €98) per barrel for the first time since 2022 as the Iran war escalated, threatening Middle Eastern output and transportation. The price of a barrel of Brent crude, the international benchmark, surpassed $114 when trading reopened on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. That was a 23% increase from Friday’s closing price of $92.69. West Texas Intermediate, the light, sweet crude oil produced in the United States, was also trading at around $114 per barrel. That is 25% higher than Friday’s finish of $90.90. “The Iran conflict intensified over the weekend, and oil briefly rising above $115 per barrel triggered another bout of selling on financial markets,” Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said in a letter to Euronews. Risk appetite has gone as investors lock in profits on market segments that have performed well in recent months and years, such as Rolls-Royce and Lloyds shares, as well as gold. The precious metal was also driven down by a stronger US dollar, which makes gold more expensive for buyers in other currencies,” he explained. title: Anthropic Sues the US Government for Describing it as a Risk
author: editor
excerpt: Anthropic, an artificial intelligence (AI) business, has filed a first-of-its-kind lawsuit against the US government on claims that it is a “supply chain risk”. The AI firm’s CEO, Dario Amodei, and Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth have been openly feuding over the company’s unwillingness to grant the military unrestricted use of its AI technologies. The Pentagon replied by designating Anthropic as the first US company to be labeled a “supply chain risk,” but Anthropic said in a complaint filed on Monday against a number of US government departments that this was illegal and unprecedented. A spokesperson for the US Department of Defense declined to comment, citing a policy regarding pending litigation. Anthropic’s lawsuit claims that the Trump administration is penalizing the company for refusing to comply with the government’s ideological demands, a breach of its protected expression and an attempt to punish the company for not cooperating. These measures are unprecedented and unlawful. In its California complaint, Anthropic said that the constitution prohibits the government from using its immense power to punish a firm for its protected speech. title: G7 Will Take Necessary Steps to Help Energy Supplies
author: editor
excerpt: The G7 countries have declared they are ready to do what it takes to help the world’s energy supply after the US-Israel confrontation with Iran caused oil prices to rise. But the G7 finance ministers and the International Energy Agency (IEA) did not reach an agreement to release strategic crude stocks during their meeting. On Monday, the price of oil rose to almost $120 a barrel amid concerns about a long-term disruption to supplies. This caused stock markets around the world to collapse. Fatih Birol, chairman of the IEA, stated at the virtual conference that global oil markets “have deteriorated in recent days.” One of the options addressed was releasing oil from stocks. Birol added, “There are problems with getting oil through the Strait of Hormuz, and a lot of oil production has been cut back.” This is making the market far more risky and dangerous. IEA member countries presently have more than 1.2 billion barrels of public emergency oil stocks and are required by law to keep 600 million barrels of industry stocks. After the meeting, French finance minister Roland Lescure replied, “We’re not there yet,” when asked if emergency stocks would be released. It would be the first time since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 that reserves were released. title: The Magic of Career DNA: Why Your Weird Little Interests Matter
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Every career advice book will tell you to “find your passion”. That sounds nice. It also sounds simple. Pick one thing. Master it. Become successful. But if you look closely at the people who actually changed industries, built companies, or created new ideas, you’ll notice something strange. Their careers didn’t come from one passion. They came from many small curiosities. Little interests here and there. Random hobbies. Seemingly useless skills. Together, they form something I like to call the Magic of Career DNA. Your Career Is a Combination, Not a Single Skill Think of the world as a giant library of skills. Cooking. Architecture. Chemistry. Astrology. Calligraphy. Coding. Martial arts. Storytelling. Gardening. Rapping. There are thousands of them. But the real magic isn’t the skills themselves. It’s the combination of them. Just like DNA is a combination of genes that makes every human unique, your career is a combination of interests and abilities that no one else has in exactly the same way. The Leonardo Formula Take Leonardo da Vinci. He wasn’t just a painter. He was: An anatomist An engineer An architect A mathematician A philosopher A relentless observer of nature Individually, many people were painters. Many were engineers. But almost nobody was all of those things at once, with that specific level of proficiency. The collective of those abilities created the unique Magic of career DNA that made him Da Vinci. That combination produced masterpieces like the Mona Lisa and revolutionary sketches of flying machines centuries before airplanes existed. Leonardo’s genius wasn’t just talent. It was the intersection of his curiosities. The Steve Jobs Detour Then there’s Steve Jobs. When Jobs dropped out of college, he randomly started attending calligraphy classes. Not programming. Not engineering. Calligraphy. At the time, it looked completely useless. Years later, when building the first Macintosh computer at Apple, that strange little interest came back. Jobs insisted computers should have beautiful typography. Multiple fonts. Proper spacing. Elegant design. Today every laptop, phone, and website uses typography that traces back to that “useless” class. One small curiosity quietly rewrote the digital world. The Joe Rogan Puzzle Look at Joe Rogan. If you tried to predict his career from the beginning, it would look ridiculous. His background included: Stand-up comedy Acting Martial arts competition Curiosity about science and psychology Long-form conversations Individually, none of these guarantee success. But together they created the perfect formula for: UFC commentary One of the largest podcasts in the world His career DNA wasn’t linear. It was a strange puzzle that eventually fit together perfectly. The Secret Pattern When you examine innovators across industries, a pattern appears. They rarely specialize in one single path. Instead, they collect small curiosities along the way. A design class here. A hobby there. A random interest that seems irrelevant. At the time, these interests feel like distractions. Later, they become advantages. Because while millions of people might learn one skill, almost nobody has the same mixture of skills. And that mixture is where originality lives. The Myth of the Straight Career Path Modern career advice loves straight lines. Study accounting. Become an accountant. Study medicine. Become a doctor. But real life is messier. You might study engineering and fall in love with storytelling. You might work in finance and become fascinated with design. You might start in sports and discover broadcasting. Each little detour adds another gene to your career DNA. Why Random Interests Matter The world rewards rare combinations. Not just rare skills. A good architect is valuable. A good architect who understands psychology, storytelling, and technology becomes something much rarer. A developer who understands urban planning is useful. A developer who also understands macroeconomics, design, DJs, loves mixing music, breeds animals, loves art, races cars, and collects trains becomes a completely different kind of developer. The narrative becomes entirely different. The more diverse your skill stack becomes, the harder it is to replicate you. The Hidden Advantage of Curiosity Most people abandon curiosities because they don’t seem practical. Learning about typography feels pointless if you’re studying computers. Studying philosophy feels useless if you’re building a business. Taking martial arts seems irrelevant to broadcasting. Until suddenly… it isn’t. That small interest becomes the unexpected piece that makes everything else work. Your Career DNA Is Already Forming The most interesting part is this: You don’t consciously design your career DNA. It emerges naturally from the things that catch your attention. A book you read. A hobby you try. A topic you become obsessed with for six months. Each one adds another layer. Individually they look insignificant. Together they shape a career that no algorithm could design and no competitor could easily copy. The Real Career Strategy So perhaps the real strategy isn’t to obsess over one skill. Perhaps it’s to follow curiosity widely and seriously. Collect interests. Explore strange subjects. Learn things that seem unrelated. Because somewhere among those small curiosities is a combination that only you possess. And that combination — your Magic of Career DNA — might be the most valuable asset you’ll ever build. About the Author Hamzah Abu Zannad is the Co-Founder and Managing Director of Axiom Prime Real Estate Development. With over two decades of experience in Dubai’s property market, he has contributed to projects shaped by long-term strategy, disciplined execution, and sustainable growth. At Axiom Prime, he focuses on low-density, community-centered luxury developments inspired by Dutch living principles — prioritizing walkability, natural light, and human-scale design. The company’s flagship projects in Jumeirah Village Triangle and Jumeirah Garden City reflect his belief that real estate should be intentional, functional, and enduring — not merely impressive. With a steady, forward-looking view of Dubai’s evolution, Hamzah continues to play a thoughtful role in shaping the city’s evolving urban fabric. In its force majeure notice, Bapco Energies stated that its “group operations have been impacted by the ongoing regional conflict in the Middle East and the recent attack on its refinery complex. Force majeure is a legal principle that protects parties from liability when they fail to perform their obligations due to events beyond their control. title: Navigating Change in an Evolving Global Financial Landscape – Dina El Dalil
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In an era where global finance is evolving rapidly through sustainability imperatives and digital transformation, leadership requires more than financial expertise. It calls for strategic foresight, strong ethical grounding, and the ability to deal with diverse teams under shared goals. With extensive experience working in banking and cross border financing, alongside influential leaders and contributing to national development initiatives, this executive has developed a leadership philosophy shaped by mentorship, resilience, and long-term vision. Throughout her career, she has navigated complex organizational dynamics, cross-border negotiations, and shifting financial landscapes while maintaining a focus on integrity, collaboration, and sustainable growth. On women’s international day, Dina El Dalil shares the influences that shaped hercareer, the challenges that tested her communication and decision-making skills, and her perspective on how sustainability and digital innovation will redefine international finance in the years ahead. Influences That Shaped a Leadership Philosophy We began by asking, “Who has influenced your career the most, and what key lesson do you pass on to others?” “I’ve been fortunate to work alongside exceptional leaders throughout my career. Many of them were more than managers; they were true mentors, particularly during my involvement in national development initiatives. Their strategic vision and strong sense of responsibility toward broader economic impact deeply shaped my professional mindset. However, my greatest source of careerinspiration has always been my grandfather. Remarkably, he began one of the most successful chapters of his career after retiring at the age of 60. Watching him build, persevere, and thrive at a stage when many people consider slowing down profoundly influenced me. He taught me that ambition has no expiration date. Resilience and consistency, rather than speed or circumstance, are what truly drive long-term success.” Career Challenges Turning to leadership challenges, we asked, “Can you share a moment that tested your experience and communication skills?” “One of the most defining challenges I faced was managing a high-performing team where strong internal competition often led to recurring conflict. Addressing this situation required clear communication. content:
In an era where global finance is evolving rapidly through sustainability imperatives and digital transformation, leadership requires more than financial expertise. It calls for strategic foresight, strong ethical grounding, and the ability to deal with diverse teams under shared goals. With extensive experience working in banking and cross border financing, alongside influential leaders and contributing to national development initiatives, this executive has developed a leadership philosophy shaped by mentorship, resilience, and long-term vision.

Throughout her career, she has navigated complex organizational dynamics, cross-border negotiations, and shifting financial landscapes while maintaining a focus on integrity, collaboration, and sustainable growth. On women’s international day, Dina El Dalil shares the influences that shaped hercareer, the challenges that tested her communication and decision-making skills, and her perspective on how sustainability and digital innovation will redefine international finance in the years ahead.

Influences That Shaped a Leadership Philosophy

We began by asking, “Who has influenced your career the most, and what key lesson do you pass on to others?”

“I’ve been fortunate to work alongside exceptional leaders throughout my career. Many of them were more than managers; they were true mentors, particularly during my involvement in national development initiatives. Their strategic vision and strong sense of responsibility toward broader economic impact deeply shaped my professional mindset.

However, my greatest source of careerinspiration has always been my grandfather. Remarkably, he began one of the most successful chapters of his career after retiring at the age of 60. Watching him build, persevere, and thrive at a stage when many people consider slowing down profoundly influenced me.

He taught me that ambition has no expiration date. Resilience and consistency, rather than speed or circumstance, are what truly drive long-term success.”

Career Challenges

Turning to leadership challenges, we asked, “Can you share a moment that tested your experience and communication skills?”

“One of the most defining challenges I faced was managing a high-performing team where strong internal competition often led to recurring conflict. Addressing this situation required clear communication.

The turning point was to restructure individual KPIs to align directly with collective outcomes so that personal success is tied to team success. At the same time, we established clearer role boundaries to eliminate overlap and reduce friction. This strengthened accountability and improved collaboration.

Another constant challenge in leadership is balancing empathy with decisiveness. Empathy helps leaders understand individual concerns, maintain morale, and build loyalty. Integrity, however, requires making difficult decisions when necessary, while remaining transparent and fair for the greater good of the organization.”

The Future of International Finance

Looking ahead, we asked, “How will sustainability and digital transformation shape international finance over the next decade?”

“Sustainability and digital transformation will become decisive forces shaping the future of international finance. These shifts are redefining how capital is allocated, priced, and managed across global markets.

Sustainability is no longer simply a compliance requirement. It has become a core pillar of credit assessment. Financial institutions increasingly evaluate climate exposure, transition risks, and supply chain resilience when determining creditworthiness, pricing, and financing terms.

As a result, financial instruments such as green bonds, sustainability-linked loans, transition finance mechanisms, and carbon certificates are gaining significant traction. Financing structures are increasingly tied to measurable sustainability KPIs.

At the same time, digital transformation is reshaping the operational model of international finance. Digitalization enables faster cross-border transactions, more sophisticated risk analytics, improved compliance frameworks, and more personalized financial solutions.

To stay competitive, leaders must integrate sustainability and digitalization directly into their strategic planning. This includes investing in advanced data infrastructure and modernizing risk management frameworks. Institutions that act early will be better positioned to support sustainable growth while maintaining resilience in a rapidly evolving global financial environment.”

Building Trust Across Global Teams

As the conversation concluded, we asked, “How do you build trust across diverse global teams during high-stakes deals?”

“Trust begins with preparation, integrity, and unwavering dedication. In complex cross-border negotiations, credibility is established through deep technical knowledge and consistent delivery.

Equally important is transparency. Trust grows when there is alignment between what stakeholders say and what they do. In global environments where cultural differences and high financial stakes intersect, reputation becomes one of the most valuable assets.

Most importantly, I focus on creating genuine win-win outcomes. Successful deals are not about short-term advantage. They are about ensuring that all stakeholders feel heard, respected, and aligned around shared value.”

content:
In today’s times, women leaders are reshaping the global business landscape with bold visions and a strong voice to bring about change. With their participation in the highest level of decision-making and their setting of new industry insights, these women leaders are not just adapting to the evolving market, but are actively shaping the next era of business. 

From executing their vision to dedicatedly leveraging their expertise in driving impactful results, they are influential voices across industries. With strategic insights, problem-solving skills, and a passion to innovate, these women leaders are demonstrating what effective leadership looks like. 

The Top Women Leaders Shaping the Future of Business

Below is the list of top women leaders who are the driving force behind the growth and transformation across industries. Their journeys are a source of inspiration for generations of leaders to come. As you dive deep into the article, you will learn about their story, the challenges and opportunities in their career path, and how these leaders have established themselves in their current position. 

Komal Jajoo | Building Purpose-Driven Organizations and Transformative Education

Komal Jajoo is a purpose-driven entrepreneur, educator, and organizational leader whose work integrates consulting, governance, business strategy, and professional education. With over a decade of experience across the Middle East and Asia, she has built a strong international presence rooted in strategic leadership, people development, and operational excellence.

Co-founder and Managing Partner – AJMS Group

As Co-founder and Managing Partner of AJMS Group, Komal plays a pivotal role in shaping the group’s strategic direction and regional growth. She actively manages multiple offices across Dubai and leads the AJMS India operations, including the Jaipur office.

Under her leadership, the organization has strengthened governance frameworks, enhanced operational efficiency, and built high-performing multicultural teams across jurisdictions. She oversees human capital strategy, governance structures, and cross-border operations, ensuring alignment between people, processes, and long-term vision.

Today, she leads a team of over 100 professionals across regions, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous growth.

CEO and Co-founder – Hayford Integrated Training Institute

Komal is the CEO and Co-founder of Hayford Integrated Training Institute in the UAE. She established Hayford with a vision to bridge the gap between academic learning and practical industry application.

Under her leadership, Hayford has:

  • Secured key accreditations and strategic partnerships
  • Adopted technology-enabled learning models
  • Positioned itself as a future-ready platform for executive and professional development

Hayford has expanded its footprint beyond the UAE, with offices established in Qatar, Oman, and Kuwait, and is currently planning further expansion into Abu Dhabi. This regional growth reflects her commitment to delivering accessible, high-quality professional education across the GCC.

Leader – Fanar (Business & Company Setup Advisory Platform)

Komal also leads Fanar, a specialized business and company setup advisory platform. Fanar focuses on assisting entrepreneurs, investors, and corporations with company formation, business structuring, regulatory registrations, and strategic market entry solutions across the UAE and the broader region.

Through Fanar, she supports businesses in establishing compliant and scalable operations, contributing to economic growth and entrepreneurial development.

Recognition & International Acknowledgment

Komal’s contributions have received significant international recognition. She was honored as Outstanding Woman Entrepreneur in Education at the Economic Times Education Excellence Awards. She was featured on the cover of Conglomerate Magazine as UAE’s Iconic Woman Leader Driving Global Transformation.

She has been nominated for the Filmfare Most Influential Women Awards 2025 for Outstanding Contribution to Academic Excellence and was a nominee at the SHE Awards Dubai in the Corporate SHE Business Woman Entrepreneur category.

She has also been recognized as Exemplary Woman Leader of the Year 2025 and featured in the Power 100 List at the Global Business Conclave held at the UK House of Lords. Additionally, she has been acknowledged among the Top Arab Leaders in Professional Training and Workforce Development and named a Global 200 Women Power Leader.

Hayford Integrated Training Institute has been recognized as one of the 20 Most Promising Startups to Watch.

Social Impact & Humanitarian Engagement

Beyond business and education, Komal actively supports social and humanitarian initiatives. She contributed to community relief efforts during the COVID-19 crisis and collaborated with the Emirates Red Crescent in humanitarian activities.

She strongly believes that sustainable growth must be supported by responsibility and compassion.

Global Leadership Development

Komal completed the Executive Education Program in Crisis Leadership in Higher Education at Harvard Kennedy School in Cambridge, Massachusetts. This experience strengthened her global leadership perspective and her ability to lead effectively through complex and evolving environments.

Leadership Philosophy

At the core of her philosophy is a simple yet powerful belief:

Businesses grow when people grow.

She leads with trust, promotes continuous learning, and creates environments where individuals feel empowered to lead confidently and make meaningful impact.

Leadership Message

“True leadership is not about authority. It is about enabling others to discover their potential. When people are equipped with the right knowledge, values, and support, transformation becomes inevitable.”

Aruna Vaz | Advancing Risk Intelligence, ESG Governance, and Digital Trust

Aruna Vaz is a globally recognized leader in Risk Management and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategy whose career bridges enterprise resilience, regulatory intelligence, and inclusive leadership. With over 20 years of international experience spanning the UK, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East, she has built a distinguished path defined by strategic foresight, governance clarity, and transformative risk leadership.

Currently based in Dubai, Aruna serves as CEO of Tsaaro Consulting, a boutique Data Privacy, AI, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC), and Cyber Security advisory firm. In this role, she spearheads regional strategy, market expansion, and the delivery of forward-looking consulting services, positioning Tsaaro as a trusted partner for enterprises navigating the rapidly evolving regulatory and digital landscape across the Middle East.

Prior to Tsaaro, Aruna led the Operational Risk function at M2, a regulated digital asset exchange operating under the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) framework. There, she strengthened enterprise-wide risk governance within one of the region’s most dynamic financial innovation environments, reinforcing regulatory alignment in the digital assets ecosystem.

Her earlier leadership roles reflect both scale and complexity. At Aster DM Healthcare, Aruna oversaw risk and loss prevention strategies across a network of more than 350 hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies in seven countries. She also played a foundational role in crafting the group’s first ESG report, embedding sustainability, governance, and accountability into operational frameworks.

Before relocating to the Middle East, Aruna spent over a decade at M&G plc. There, she led initiatives across operational risk, compliance, internal controls, and Sarbanes-Oxley testing, working directly with Boards and Risk Committees to challenge risk posture and strengthen enterprise resilience. Beyond technical leadership, she founded the firm’s Diversity & Inclusion chapter and was honored with the Rising Star Award for her impact on workplace culture.

Aruna’s influence extends beyond corporate leadership into global thought forums. She has spoken at the Everywoman Global Summit, served as a juror for the UAE Privacy Awards, and was named among Asia’s Top 100 Women Power Leaders (2023). A finalist in the Chief Risk Officer category at the Women in GRC Awards, she is widely recognized for bridging strategic vision with regulatory precision in complex and evolving risk environments.

Her professional engagement continues through her role as Co-Chair of the UAE Data Protection Officers (DPO) Club, where she convenes legal, compliance, and cybersecurity professionals to elevate privacy and risk standards across the region.

A defining aspect of Aruna’s philosophy is the integration of governance with human accountability. As a trained mental health first aider, mentor, and advocate for inclusive leadership, she believes that risk management is not solely about controls and compliance, but about building cultures of trust, resilience, and ethical clarity. Her work reflects a commitment to transforming how organizations embed ESG principles and digital trust into core decision-making structures.

Aruna Vaz’s career is defined not merely by accolades or executive roles, but by a cohesive vision: to strengthen enterprise ecosystems through intelligent risk governance, sustainable strategy, and inclusive leadership. Her work demonstrates that in the era of AI, digital acceleration, and global regulatory change, effective risk leadership is both a strategic necessity and a moral responsibility.

International Women’s Day Message

On International Women’s Day, Aruna Vaz shares a message to women in risk, governance, and technology leadership:

“Leadership in risk and governance is not about avoiding uncertainty — it is about having the courage to confront it with clarity, integrity, and purpose. When women lead with confidence and accountability, organizations become stronger, more resilient, and more human.”

Through her continued dedication to ESG integration, regulatory excellence, and inclusive leadership, Aruna Vaz stands as a powerful example of how women are shaping the future of risk intelligence and digital trust.

Elizabeth Marston | Founder Bridging Technology, Insurance & Cultural Heritage

Elizabeth Marston is a founder operating at a rare intersection — fine art, insurance innovation, family enterprise, and cultural heritage preservation. With over two decades of experience managing a multi-generational Napa Valley wine business and building a venture-backed technology company based at Lloyd’s of London, she combines legacy stewardship with forward-thinking risk intelligence.

She is the Founder of Sotera and Proprietor of Marston Family Vineyard, bringing together deep operational leadership and cultural asset protection expertise.

Elizabeth began her professional journey in publishing in New York City before returning to her family’s winery in Napa Valley. Over the past 20 years, she has owned and managed the multi-generational estate, navigating growth, stewardship, and long-term brand preservation.

This experience in legacy business ownership shaped her perspective on risk, preservation, and generational continuity — themes that would later define her technology venture.

Elizabeth co-founded Sotera to address a critical gap in the insurance ecosystem: item-level risk analysis and contents modeling for Fine Art, Specie, and High-Net-Worth home collections.

Sotera was founded at Accelerate Cambridge, later accelerated at Lloyd’s Lab, and is now based within the Lloyd’s ecosystem in London.

Sotera leverages data modeling and risk analytics to help insurers, collectors, and institutions better understand and protect high-value assets. Their mission goes beyond underwriting efficiency. It extends into safeguarding cultural memory.

A defining element of Elizabeth’s work is her commitment to cultural heritage preservation.

She is developing Sotera’s nonprofit initiatives to bridge preservation and technology, enabling museums and institutions to manage collections with greater intelligence and resilience. Her work has included contributions connected to heritage initiatives at the British Museum and projects in Cairo focused on protecting cultural assets at risk.

Her approach reframes insurance technology not merely as a financial tool, but as infrastructure for cultural continuity.

Drawing on her own journey — from family enterprise leadership to venture-backed founder — Elizabeth actively supports founders and next-generation family business leaders.

She advises and mentors those stepping into leadership roles, helping them clarify purpose, define their “why,” and build businesses rooted in long-term impact rather than short-term valuation.

Her work emphasizes:

  • Purpose-driven entrepreneurship
  • Legacy stewardship
  • Sustainable growth
  • Cultural and social responsibility

Elizabeth’s academic background reflects her lifelong engagement with classical heritage and archaeology. She holds:

  • A BA in Classical Studies from the Claremont Colleges
  • An MA in Classical Archaeology
  • An MPhil in Egyptology from the University of Cambridge

This scholarly grounding in antiquity directly informs her modern mission: protecting cultural history through contemporary technology.

Leadership Philosophy

At the core of Elizabeth’s work is a belief that stewardship and innovation are not opposites. They are partners.

She advocates building businesses that balance:

  • Precision and empathy
  • Profitability and preservation
  • Technology and human legacy

Originally from California and now based in London, Elizabeth Marston operates at the convergence of technology, insurance, and cultural heritage — building systems designed not only to assess risk, but to safeguard history itself.

Karishma Mirchandani Sawlani | Education Leadership Strategist and Institutional Growth Architect

Karishma Mirchandani Sawlani is an international education leader and institutional growth strategist with more than 20 years of executive experience across education, EdTech, innovation ecosystems, luxury, and media in the United States, United Kingdom, the Caribbean, and Spain.

Her work focuses on institutional turnaround, enrollment acceleration, governance alignment, and culture transformation. Throughout her career, she has led multi-market expansion strategies, strengthened organizational performance, and rebuilt stakeholder trust during complex transition periods.

Across educational and innovation environments, Karishma has driven measurable growth outcomes, including significant enrollment increases, large-scale digital visibility expansion, improved retention metrics, and cross-border partnership development. She is particularly recognized for aligning strategic vision with disciplined execution and measurable institutional performance.

At IE Business School, she led the Startup Lab innovation program, incubating over 100 ventures and contributing to admissions growth through experiential positioning. As International Business Development Lead at Gamelearn, she expanded an EdTech platform across three continents, securing 30+ institutional partnerships and contributing to +40% revenue growth in the education sector.

Karishma integrates governance literacy with human-centered leadership. She is currently completing Harvard University’s Certificate in School Management and Leadership and holds an Executive Master’s in Positive Leadership, Strategy & Transformation from IE University.

Recognized in the WITH Guide of Women Leaders in the Business Ecosystem (2025), her areas of expertise include:

• Education leadership and school governance

• Institutional growth and enrollment strategy

• EdTech expansion and innovation ecosystems

• Culture transformation and stakeholder alignment

• Board advisory and strategic oversight

Reflecting on International Women’s Day, Karishma shares:

“Leadership is not only about representation. It is about influence in governance, capital allocation, and long-term institutional design. Sustainable impact requires both empathy and disciplined execution.”

Through strategic clarity, governance strength, and measurable performance outcomes, Karishma continues to support institutions navigating growth, complexity, and transformation.

Helga Dalla | Founder Advancing Health Naturally & Midlife Metabolic Resilience Advocate

Helga Dalla is a holistic wellness entrepreneur and Neuro Transformation Practitioner operating at a powerful intersection — metabolic science, nervous system regulation, and midlife women’s leadership. As the Founder of Advancing Health Naturally, she builds science-backed natural frameworks that help women 40+ restore vitality, reduce inflammation, and reclaim ownership of their health.

Her work bridges cellular biology and mindset transformation, translating complex health science into structured, accessible programs for sustainable change.

Before stepping into the wellness industry, Helga built an award-winning career as a photojournalist and author. She is the creator of A World of Twins — a nationally recognised Australian body of work documenting rare twin and triplet stories across the country. Her early professional life was defined by storytelling, perspective, and the ability to illuminate what others overlooked.

Then her own story shifted.

Diagnosed with Rheumatoid Arthritis during menopause, Helga faced a turning point that would redefine her path. Rather than accept chronic decline, she immersed herself in research around oxidative stress, cellular activation, autoimmune response, and nervous system dysregulation. What began as personal survival evolved into professional purpose.

Through years of study and application, she developed her signature CALM Framework™ — integrating strategic fasting protocols, cellular activation principles, and Neuro Transformation Therapy. The framework is designed to support autoimmune resilience, metabolic restoration, and hormonal balance, particularly for women navigating midlife transitions.

Today, Helga builds scalable digital programs and mentors women globally through structured health education, community support, and neuro-regulation methodologies. Her work extends beyond symptom management. It focuses on restoration, resilience, and long-term metabolic intelligence.

A defining element of Helga’s mission is empowering women to move from reactive health management to proactive self-leadership. She challenges outdated narratives around aging, advocating instead for regulated nervous systems, activated cells, and informed decision-making as foundations for vitality.

Her work emphasizes:

  • Nervous system regulation as the foundation of health
  • Cellular resilience and oxidative stress management
  • Science-backed natural frameworks
  • Midlife hormonal and metabolic restoration
  • Personal responsibility and empowered transformation

Through her community platforms and mentorship, Helga continues to cultivate a global network of women committed to reclaiming energy, clarity, and confidence in their second half of life.

Leadership Philosophy

At the core of Helga’s work is a belief that true transformation begins internally — biologically, neurologically, and emotionally.

She advocates building health from the inside out through:

  • Regulated nervous systems
  • Metabolic awareness
  • Structured behavioral change
  • Courage to evolve beyond diagnosis

For Helga, entrepreneurship is not simply about business growth. It is about becoming the architect of your own restoration.

Operating through Advancing Health Naturally and her growing global community, Helga Dalla is redefining what midlife health leadership looks like — grounded in science, resilience, and personal evolution.

Yeşim Taşöz | A Leader at the Intersection of Travel, Trust, and Borderless Living

A childhood dream can evolve into a lifelong mission, and for Yeşim Taşöz, that dream began as the daughter of immigrants who believed the world was bigger than the place she stood in. What started as a desire to explore oceans, cultures, and distant cities has become a career dedicated to helping others experience the beauty and diversity of the world with confidence and care.

Since entering the tourism industry in 1997, Yeşim has built nearly three decades of experience connecting people with meaningful travel experiences. With a background in business administration and a qualification as a certified business economist (FH), she combines entrepreneurial discipline with a deeply personal service philosophy.

In 2011, she became self-employed and established a traditional TUI travel center franchise in the city center. The business operated with fixed hours, a growing team, and the stability of a classic office structure. For years, it reflected the traditional model of travel consulting built on reliability and routine.

Then 2020 brought a turning point.

Rather than seeing the pandemic as an end, Yeşim saw it as a moment of reflection. She reexamined what travelers truly need in a digital and uncertain world. In one of the boldest decisions of her career, she closed her large downtown office and reimagined her business model. In its place, she created a hybrid travel boutique that blends a smaller office presence with a flexible digital workspace, operating by personal appointment and centered entirely around individualized care.

Today, her team works remotely from home offices, airports, and destinations worldwide. They do not simply organize travel. They experience it firsthand. Yeşim personally tests hotels and destinations before recommending them, ensuring that trust remains the foundation of every journey. Clients receive direct access to her before, during, and after travel, reinforcing a level of accessibility rarely found in modern tourism.

Her agency welcomes travelers from all nationalities and backgrounds, offering personalized service to anyone seeking trusted, high-quality travel planning, regardless of where they are based.

Beyond bookings and itineraries, Yeşim shares authentic travel insights with her community through social media, offering honest reflections and inspiration rooted in lived experience. Her approach reflects a belief that travel is not a transaction but a relationship built on transparency and connection.

Sharing her perspective on entrepreneurship, Yeşim emphasizes that in a fast-moving digital world, trust, care, and genuine human connection never lose their value.

Through resilience, reinvention, and unwavering authenticity, Yeşim Taşöz continues to transform travel consulting into a borderless, personalized experience, proving that a migrant child’s dream can become a life dedicated to helping others discover the world.
