Architecting the Ecosystems of Next-Generation Mobility | Dawlat H. Tarifi

Positioning the Middle East at the Forefront of the Global Sustainable Transport Transition

Across the world, the transition toward cleaner, smarter, and more connected transportation systems is accelerating. Governments, industries, and innovators are working to redefine how societies move, power their economies, and design the infrastructure of the future.

In this evolving landscape, the future of mobility is no longer defined by technology alone. It depends on the ability to align policy, infrastructure, capital, and innovation into ecosystems capable of delivering real-world transformation.

Tarifi entered the mobility sector at the early stages of this transformation in the region and continues to contribute to its evolution today.

Tarifi has built her career around a central principle: transformative industries are not built through isolated innovation, but through collaboration between governments, institutions, and companies willing to move forward together.

Across the Middle East’s rapidly evolving mobility landscape, Tarifi has focused on connecting the key actors shaping the sector: governments, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), infrastructure developers, investors, and emerging technology companies. Through these connections, she helps support the region’s transition toward next-generation transportation.

Her work sits at the intersection of partnerships, policy, and emerging technologies, where strategic alignment often determines whether innovation remains theoretical or becomes commercially viable.

This philosophy is reflected in a guiding principle that has come to define Tarifi’s approach to opportunity and leadership.

“We don’t wait for opportunity — we create it.”

From Strategy to Industry Impact

Before entering the mobility sector, Tarifi gained experience across several highly regulated industries, including legal, media, and pharmaceuticals.

Working within compliance-driven environments and complex stakeholder landscapes strengthened her ability to navigate regulatory frameworks, manage cross-functional collaboration, and operate within structured institutional systems.

These early experiences helped shape Tarifi’s understanding of the broader forces that govern large industries, a perspective that would later prove valuable as global transport systems began undergoing one of the most significant technological transformations in modern history.

Tarifi’s transition into the mobility sector marked a defining phase of her career.

She contributed to the development of one of the Middle East’s most influential mobility industry platforms, helping connect governments, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), infrastructure providers, and emerging technology companies within a shared ecosystem for collaboration and growth.

This experience reinforced a lesson that continues to guide Tarifi’s work today:

Industries do not scale through isolated innovation — they scale through ecosystems.

Positioning the Middle East as a Global Mobility Hub

Today, Tarifi leads business development initiatives within Abu Dhabi’s emerging advanced aerial mobility sector, supporting efforts to expand the ecosystem across the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia.

Her work focuses on structuring partnerships that connect international technology leaders with regional institutions, contributing to the development of an ecosystem that positions the Gulf as an emerging center for advanced mobility innovation.

With ambitious government visions, significant infrastructure investment, and strong institutional support, the Middle East is uniquely positioned to become one of the world’s most dynamic environments for testing and scaling next-generation transport solutions.

Tarifi’s role within this evolving landscape is both strategic and connective. She aligns stakeholders across continents and industries to support deployment, commercialization, and long-term market development.

In parallel, Tarifi advises enterprises, OEMs, smart mobility solution providers, and government entities navigating entry into the Middle East market.

She works with companies from the United States, Canada, Europe, China, Hong Kong, India, and South Korea, helping them translate global innovation into effective regional strategies.

Her advisory work focuses on regulatory navigation, stakeholder engagement, and long-term commercialization — key elements that often determine whether new technologies succeed when entering complex emerging markets.

Through this work, Tarifi continues to bridge continents, connecting global innovation with regional execution.

Leadership Through Trust and Human Connection

In sectors defined by rapid technological change, large-scale investment, and constant disruption, Tarifi advocates for a leadership model grounded in resilience, credibility, and relational intelligence.

While transactions may generate momentum, she believes trust is what ultimately builds industries.

“Building human connection is as important as generating sales. Transactions generate momentum. Trust builds industries. Ecosystems create legacy.”

Her strength lies not only in structuring partnerships and closing deals, but in aligning diverse stakeholders across cultures, institutions, and industries.

For Tarifi, sales may open doors — but human connection is what keeps them open.

Perspective on Leadership

Reflecting on leadership and progress, Tarifi emphasizes the importance of resilience, collaboration, and balance.

“To strive, to seek, to find – and not to yield. Tough times don’t last, but tough people do. Women and men each have equally important roles to play in society. Progress is built through balance, not competition. We are not here to compete against one another; we are here to complement one another. We balance each other out. We don’t compete – we complete. True leadership is measured not by dominance, but by resilience, collaboration, and the courage to keep moving forward despite uncertainty. Those who endure long enough are the ones who shape the future.”

As the global mobility transition accelerates, the future of transport will be shaped not only by technological breakthroughs, but by the ecosystems capable of supporting them.

Leaders who can connect innovation with institutions, infrastructure, and long-term strategy will play a defining role in shaping how that future unfolds.

Through her work building partnerships and aligning global innovation with regional execution, Tarifi continues to contribute to that evolving landscape — helping lay the foundations for the next generation of mobility.

Credentials

Tarifi holds a Master of Business Administration in International Business with a specialization in Green Energy from Regent’s University London — European Business School.

She also earned a double Bachelor of Arts from the American University of Beirut in Public Policy & Governance and English Creative Writing, a combination that reflects both her policy insight and her ability to communicate complex strategic ideas with clarity and impact.

Erica Antonietti | Leading Through People, Purpose, and Italian Tradition

Entrepreneurship rooted in heritage often creates businesses that blend authenticity with innovation. Erica Antonietti embodies this philosophy. As the Managing Director of FGC Food Industries LLC, she has built a company that brings authentic Italian culinary craftsmanship to the Middle East while maintaining a deep connection to her cultural roots.

Raised in an entrepreneurial Italian family of business owners, Erica grew up understanding that true quality is shaped by dedication, consistency, and respect for tradition. These early influences laid the foundation for her professional journey and continue to guide her leadership approach today.

Her connection with Dubai began in 2007 during a visit to GULFOOD, one of the world’s largest food and hospitality exhibitions. Inspired by the city’s dynamic energy and its openness to global business opportunities, she recognized the potential to introduce high-quality Italian food products to a rapidly expanding hospitality and aviation market.

This vision led to the creation of FGC Food Industries LLC, a company specializing in the production of fresh, authentic Italian products designed for hotels, airlines, and food service partners across the region. Under Erica’s leadership, the company has established itself as a trusted provider of premium Italian culinary solutions.

Drawing inspiration from her grandmother’s traditional recipes, Erica developed a production philosophy that combines Italian culinary heritage with modern standards of quality and efficiency. From freshly crafted pasta and sauces to artisanal pizzas, every product reflects a commitment to authenticity, responsibility, and meticulous attention to detail.

For Erica, leadership goes beyond managing operations. It is about creating a culture rooted in responsibility, respect, and shared purpose. She believes that professionalism, consistency, and an unwavering focus on quality are essential for building trust with both customers and teams.

The growth of FGC Food Industries, she emphasizes, is the result of people who share a dedication to excellence and a commitment to maintaining the highest standards. By nurturing strong relationships and empowering her team, Erica continues to strengthen the company’s presence while preserving the authenticity that defines its identity.

Through her vision and commitment to craftsmanship, Erica Antonietti continues to bring the flavors of Italy to international markets, demonstrating how tradition, leadership, and innovation can come together to build a brand rooted in quality and purpose.

Farah Al Hamra | Pharmaceutical Operations Leader & Strategic Business Transformation Expert

Farah Al Hamra is a distinguished pharmaceutical operations and business development leader whose career reflects strategic precision, operational excellence, and sustainable growth. With a Doctor of Pharmacy degree, an MBA in Business Administration, and a PMP (Project Management Professional) certification, she brings a rare blend of scientific depth and commercial intelligence to the healthcare industry.

Recognised for her ability to align business strategy with regulatory frameworks and market realities, Farah has built a reputation as a results-driven leader who transforms complexity into scalable growth.

Driving Pharmaceutical Excellence Across Markets

Throughout her career, Farah has played a pivotal role in strengthening pharmaceutical operations, optimizing compliance structures, and spearheading market-entry initiatives across multiple regions. Her expertise spans operational management, regulatory alignment, commercial expansion, and structured project execution.

She has successfully led cross-functional teams through complex operational landscapes, ensuring seamless coordination between compliance, sales, and supply chain functions. Her leadership has enabled organizations to enhance efficiency, improve market penetration, and deliver measurable revenue growth.

With deep insight into evolving healthcare regulations and market demands, Farah consistently bridges corporate objectives with sustainable execution strategies.

Operational Leadership with Strategic Vision

Farah’s leadership style is rooted in accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. She believes that operational excellence is achieved not only through systems and frameworks, but through empowered teams aligned with a clear strategic direction.

Her PMP certification strengthens her ability to manage high-impact projects with precision — optimizing resources, mitigating risks, and ensuring timely execution. By leveraging structured methodologies and data-driven decision-making, she has implemented transformation initiatives that enhance productivity while maintaining regulatory integrity.

Her approach combines:

  • Strategic growth planning
  • Process optimization
  • Market expansion frameworks
  • Cross-border partnership development
  • Performance-driven team leadership

Commitment to Sustainable Growth and Transformation

Beyond operational achievements, Farah is deeply committed to long-term business sustainability. She recognizes that success in the pharmaceutical industry requires more than financial performance — it demands resilience, adaptability, and a forward-looking vision.

Her work reflects a commitment to innovation, compliance excellence, and customer-centric solutions that strengthen competitive positioning. By aligning strategy with execution, she continues to drive business transformation in dynamic and highly regulated markets.

Leadership Philosophy

At the core of Farah’s professional journey is a belief in structured growth, strategic clarity, and empowered leadership. She champions disciplined execution, continuous learning, and proactive adaptation to change.

For Farah, impactful leadership means building systems that endure, teams that thrive, and businesses that grow responsibly.

With a steadfast focus on operational performance and scalable expansion, Farah Al Hamra continues to shape the pharmaceutical landscape through vision, expertise, and resilient leadership.

Ange Bakeba | From Satellite Communication to Strategic Authority

In today’s leadership landscape, influence is no longer defined solely by expertise or performance. It requires visibility, strategic positioning, and the confidence to lead with conviction. Ange Bakeba has built her mission around helping high-performing women unlock that authority.

As the Founder of the FIRE Leadership Institute, Ange equips faith-driven women leaders to transition from overlooked contributors to positioned authorities within their industries. Her work focuses on helping accomplished professionals align their identity, voice, and strategic leadership so they can step fully into their influence.

Before launching her leadership platform, Ange built her professional career in the satellite telecommunications industry, a highly technical and male-dominated global sector where precision, analytical thinking, and operational discipline are essential.

Working in this environment gave her a clear perspective on corporate leadership dynamics and performance expectations. While navigating complex technical projects and global teams, she began noticing a consistent pattern within many organizations.

Highly capable women were delivering strong results and demonstrating exceptional expertise, yet many remained under-recognized, under-promoted, and under-compensated.

These professionals possessed the knowledge and capability to lead. What they often lacked was the strategic positioning, negotiation confidence, and executive visibility required to command authority within competitive leadership environments.

This realization led Ange to develop the F.I.R.E.™ Leadership Framework, a transformational model designed to help women align identity, faith, voice, and executive strategy.

Find Your Value focuses on helping women clearly identify their leadership strengths, unique value, and professional influence. Many high-performing women underestimate the depth of their expertise and contribution. Through this stage, they move from self-doubt and underestimation to deep conviction about the value they bring to organizations, industries, and communities.

Ignite Your Faith emphasizes the importance of internal alignment in leadership. Sustainable leadership requires more than professional competence. It requires spiritual confidence and clarity of identity. Through faith-rooted mindset development, women shift from hesitation and the need for external validation toward purpose-driven leadership anchored in conviction.

Reclaim Your Voice addresses a challenge faced by many accomplished professionals who hesitate to advocate for themselves or speak with authority in high-level environments. In this stage, women develop executive presence, communication confidence, and negotiation capability. They learn to articulate their value clearly, influence strategic decisions, and participate in leadership conversations with confidence.

Expand Your Influence focuses on translating clarity and confidence into measurable results. Through guided action, strategic planning, and accountability, women working with Ange experience profound mindset transformation. Many rediscover their authentic leadership identity, step into visible leadership roles, and multiply both their impact and opportunities.

Beyond her leadership institute, Ange is also the author of Victory: A Daily Choice, a faith-centered book that encourages women to cultivate a victorious mindset. The book teaches readers how to silence internal narratives of defeat and intentionally choose courage, resilience, and spiritual alignment each day.

Through both her ministry and leadership work, Ange emphasizes a powerful principle. Victory is not determined by circumstances. It is an intentional choice.

When women align their faith, identity, and strategic leadership, they do more than achieve professional success. They become catalysts of transformation within every environment they enter.

As Ange explains, “Many women have mastered performance, but few have been trained in positioning. When a woman understands her value, aligns her faith, and speaks with authority, her leadership becomes undeniable.”

Through the FIRE Leadership Institute, Ange Bakeba continues to equip women around the world to lead with faith, strategic clarity, and the courage to steward their authority.

FIRE helps high-capacity women move from overlooked contributor to positioned authority.

Rita Singh | Coaching Business Leaders to Evolve and Manage Change

In an era where businesses must constantly adapt to disruption, leadership requires more than operational expertise. It demands resilience, strategic foresight, and the ability to guide organizations through change while empowering the people who drive them forward. Rita N. Singh has spent more than three decades helping leaders and organizations do exactly that.

With over thirty five years of progressive management experience, Rita Singh is widely recognized as a visionary executive leader, entrepreneur, and executive coach. Her career spans multiple industries including manufacturing, healthcare, automotive, construction, and the restaurant sector. Working with businesses ranging from closely held family enterprises to large organizations, she has consistently helped leaders strengthen strategy, build resilient teams, and position their organizations for sustainable growth.

Rita currently serves as the Chief Financial and Operations Officer of S&A Consulting Group LLP, a global resource management consulting firm headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio. Through her work with the firm, she advises CEOs, executives, entrepreneurs, and emerging leaders across corporate, nonprofit, and entrepreneurial environments.

Her approach to leadership development centers on cultivating entrepreneurial leadership skills that allow executives to navigate complex and evolving markets. Through S&A’s Entrepreneurship and Leadership Institute®, she provides a structured platform that includes executive coaching, workshops, seminars, lecture series, and leadership forums designed to strengthen decision making, strategic thinking, and organizational performance.

Over the course of her career, Rita has built expertise across organizational strategy, financial management, change management, client services, team leadership, and corporate communication. She is widely respected for her ability to rebuild organizations facing leadership gaps and transform them into productive, collaborative environments with strong corporate cultures.

Her work also reflects a deep commitment to education and mentorship. While teaching in the MBA program at the School of Graduate and Professional Studies, Rita played a key role in developing the Center of Excellence in Ethical and Entrepreneurial Leadership at Ursuline College. Through this initiative, she helped establish a platform dedicated to cultivating principled and innovative business leaders.

Beyond her corporate leadership, Rita is also the CEO and Founder of Elite Women Around The World®, operating as the Women’s Business and Leadership Development Center. This nonprofit organization works globally to strengthen the economic position of women by providing mentorship, resources, and leadership development opportunities that help women expand their influence and entrepreneurial impact.

Rita is also a best selling author. Her book Be a Warrior in Business | How to Develop Resilient Organizations and Teams, co authored with Nipendra Singh, presents a powerful framework for navigating uncertainty in today’s business environment.

Drawing from decades of entrepreneurial and executive experience, the book encourages leaders to adopt a warrior mindset that prioritizes preparation, resilience, and strategic discipline. It provides practical guidance for building strong organizational cultures, developing resilient teams, and leading confidently during times of disruption and rapid change.

Through real world insights and leadership principles, the book offers a blueprint for executives who want to lead organizations that are capable of adapting, evolving, and thriving even in unpredictable conditions.

As bestselling author and business strategist John R. DiJulius III writes, “Every leader needs to read Be a Warrior in Business. Rita and Nipendra have provided a blueprint for how to grow, sustain, and persevere in today’s unpredictable business climate. This book is a game changer.”

Throughout her career, Rita Singh has remained committed to helping leaders evolve alongside the changing demands of modern business. Her work continues to empower executives, entrepreneurs, and organizations to lead with confidence, resilience, and strategic clarity.

Women’s Day Message

“Leadership is not defined by titles or authority. It is defined by the courage to stand firm in the face of challenges, the wisdom to guide others forward, and the resilience to keep building even when the path is uncertain. When leaders embrace this mindset, they create organizations and communities that are stronger, more inclusive, and prepared for the future.”

LinkedIn | Website | Email: rsingh@sa-consultinggroup.com

Conclusion

The indomitable spirit of the trailblazers featured in this article has helped them rise to where they are today. With a passion and strong vision, these women leaders are not just setting new standards, they are the drivers of change and are shaping the next era.

content:
In current times, women leaders are reshaping business, innovation, and influence. Strong advocates of transformation, these trailblazers are influential voices in diverse fields, spanning from healthcare to technology. Reflecting qualities like transparency, integrity, and resilience, these women leaders are shifting from traditional leadership, into voices who can empower, foster growth, and drive impactful results. 

Guided by a passion to make a difference, these women leaders march forward in their fields, navigating through challenges of existing power structures. 

The Top Women Leaders Shaping Tomorrow

In the sections that follow, you will read about top women leaders, powerful voices in today’s world who are playing a crucial role in shaping the next era. Their inspirational journeys, visionary approach, milestones, setbacks, and every experience that has shaped their approach are mentioned in this article.

Layal Abou Ghanem | Architect of Human Potential and Organizational Transformation

Layal Abou Ghanem is a distinguished Human Resources Executive and entrepreneur recognized for shaping high-performing organizations through strategic human capital leadership. With more than 15 years of cross-industry experience spanning oil and gas, healthcare, and consultancy, she has built a career centered on transformation, leadership development, and succession architecture to enable businesses to thrive in complex, rapidly evolving environments.

Her professional journey reflects a deep understanding that organizations succeed when their people are empowered. Across senior leadership roles, Layal has led large-scale transformation initiatives, designing performance ecosystems, competency frameworks, and succession planning models that secure long term organizational continuity. She operates at the intersection of organizational psychology, business strategy, and leadership science, helping institutions build resilient cultures that sustain performance under pressure.

Driven by a vision to expand her impact beyond corporate structures, Layal co-founded Solutions for Training & Consultancy, also known as: STC Middle East. The firm has rapidly established itself as a trusted partner in healthcare consultancy, quality management, accreditation readiness, leadership development, and organizational excellence. Through strategic advisory and capability-building programs, STC Middle East supports institutions seeking structured growth and sustainable transformation across the region.

A defining feature of the organization is its commitment to women’s advancement. Nearly seventy percent of the firm’s contributors are women, a deliberate reflection of the company’s belief that inclusive leadership drives stronger outcomes. At STC, empowerment is translated into action through mentorship, leadership pathways, and an operational culture that fosters collaboration and professional growth.

Layal’s leadership philosophy is guided by a powerful conviction that sustainable success is built by empowering people and that women rise highest when they rise together. As she often shares:

“When a woman rises alone, it is an achievement.  When women rise together, it becomes a movement.”

Alongside her executive and entrepreneurial roles, Layal is currently finalizing her doctorate focused on AI enabled HR transformation. Her research explores how artificial intelligence, trust, and usability are reshaping employee experience and the future of work. By bridging academic insight with executive practice, she represents a rare scholar-practitioner equally comfortable in boardrooms and research forums. Her strategies are designed not only for today’s organizations but for the workforce of tomorrow.

Her journey has not been defined by ease, but by courage and deliberate perseverance. Layal believes leadership is less about authority and more about stewardship. It is about the doors one opens for others and the legacy one builds through people. Her work reflects the balance between ambition and empathy, proving that performance and humanity can coexist at the highest levels of leadership.

On International Women’s Day, Layal’s message to women navigating their professional paths is both clear and deeply personal:

“The road will not always be accommodating. There will be moments of doubt and voices that question your readiness. Walk anyway. Progress is built on small, courageous steps taken despite uncertainty. And as you rise, extend your hand to another woman. Shared success is the most powerful success of all.”

Through her continued commitment to transformation, inclusion, and innovation, Layal Abou Ghanem is shaping organizations that value capability, character, and collaboration. Her leadership stands as a reminder that when women empower one another, and institutions prioritize people, entire industries move forward.

Dr. Sonakshi Ruhela | Championing Mental Health and Education Across Borders

Some leaders shape institutions, while others shape people. Dr. Sonakshi Ruhela stands at the intersection of both. An accomplished educationalist, psychologist, and academic leader, she brings over 15 years of experience spanning higher education, mental health practice, research, and institutional development across India and the UAE. Her work reflects a deep commitment to inclusive education, evidence-based psychological practice, and community impact.

Dr. Ruhela holds a Harvard Certification in Higher Education and a PhD in psychology approved by the UAE Ministry of Education. According to Advance HE, she is a Senior Fellow of the Higher Education Academy (SFHEA), aligned with the UK Professional Standards Framework. In addition to making significant contributions to university administration, accreditation, quality assurance, and institutional effectiveness, she has taught, mentored, and trained undergraduate and postgraduate students from various countries and cultural backgrounds over the last 16 years. 

Dr. Ruhela is currently employed at Rochester Institute of Technology, Dubai, as an Assistant Professor of Psychology. Beyond academia, Dr. Ruhela is a Licensed Psychologist with the Community Development Authority (CDA Dubai) and has extensive experience in counselling, psychotherapy, behavioural lifestyle interventions, neuro-linguistic programming, and psychometric assessments. Her clinical work covers adolescent and adult counselling, couples and family therapy, and the management of depression, anxiety, and emotional-psychological distress. She currently consults at Dubai’s Open Minds Psychiatry, Counselling and Neuroscience Centre. She is also an active trainer in teaching and learning excellence and in diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) practices across UAE schools.

Dr. Ruhela has a global influence on both authorship and research. In 2020, Lambert Publications released her book ‘Counselling Interventions for Millennials’, which is now housed at the Mohammed Bin Rashid Library in the United Arab Emirates and has been translated into nine languages. In 2023, the work received the prestigious UAE Mastermind – Authors Award. Her research portfolio includes multidisciplinary papers indexed by Scopus and research projects related to the Al-Jalila Foundation in the United Arab Emirates, ICSSR, and AIIMS in India. She is a recognised professional member of the Middle East Psychological Association, the Indian Association of Clinical Psychologists, and the American Psychological Association. 

Recognised widely for her contributions, Dr. Ruhela was honoured as one of Asia’s 40 Under 40 by TradeFlock in 2025. Her accolades include the “Outstanding Positive Impact Speaker” award (UAE Next Mastermind, 2024), the “Educational Leadership” award (International Business Summit and Awards, 2023), and multiple international recognitions celebrating her leadership, academic excellence, and advocacy for mental health and wellness.

Sharing her perspective on leadership, resilience, and women’s growth, Dr. Sonakshi Ruhela reflects:

“My journey as a psychologist and an academician has helped me recognise the subtle yet powerful strength and impact that women hold across every industry and sphere of life. Over the years, I have learned that women’s growth is often shaped not only by ambition and talent but also by patience, resilience, and quiet perseverance. Behind every professional achievement lies a story of balancing responsibilities, managing expectations, and moving forward despite personal and social challenges. Women consistently show an extraordinary capacity to adapt, learn, and lead, often while nurturing families, communities, and workplaces with compassion and integrity.

What stands out most to me is the spirit of support and empathy that women extend to one another. Whether as colleagues, mentors, caregivers, or leaders, women uplift others even as they work toward their own goals. Their strength is reflected not only in milestones achieved but also in the sacrifices made, the values upheld, and the courage to remain authentic in demanding environments. As we celebrate women’s progress, it is important to honour both their visible successes and their unseen efforts. When women are encouraged, respected, and given equal opportunities, they do not merely succeed individually; they contribute to building stronger, more humane, and more balanced societies.”

Dr. Ruhela’s contributions to education, mental health, and community involvement continue to influence how organisations support students, how communities perceive wellbeing, and how leadership can be deeply human and powerful.

Anupriya Ramraj | Building Purpose-Driven Technology with AI and Empathy

Anupriya(Anu) Ramraj is a global technology leader, social-impact entrepreneur, and visionary builder working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, cloud, and human-centered innovation. With over two decades of experience, she has led large-scale digital transformations for Fortune 500 companies across industries, including healthcare and other highly regulated sectors. She has been recognized as a Top 25 Global Digital Transformation Leader and a Top 100 Influencer for Hybrid Cloud.

Anu has held senior global leadership roles at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, DXC, and Unisys, and was most recently a Partner at PwC US. In all of these positions, she assisted companies in adopting cutting-edge technologies, modernizing core processes, and navigating complex change with clarity and responsibility. Her leadership consistently balances people-first leadership with deep technical and strategy expertise.

Anu is the CEO and founder of Vaultzy (www.vaultzy.ai), a blockchain-powered secure digital vault. The platform is designed to secure and transform access to vital records, especially for marginalized groups such as foster children, seniors, and families affected by disasters. By combining advanced technology with empathy, Anu ensures that innovation truly serves human needs.

Anu is a member of the Forbes Technology Council with a master’s degree in Computer Science from California State University, Chico, and executive education from Stanford Graduate School of Business. She has co-authored the forthcoming book When AI Robots Knock, which explores how AI is reshaping work, opportunities, and leadership across industries and generations.

Beyond her career, Anu is deeply committed to giving back. She has held leadership roles and runs women’s and youth empowerment programs with Asian community organizations, actively supports women in technology, and serves on the board of IANGEL to advance women’s rights worldwide. Her work focuses on building long-term opportunity, representation, and access.

Anu Ramraj leads with purpose, honesty, and compassion—whether she is mentoring founders, driving innovation in public and private sectors, or guiding the next generation of leaders. This International Women’s Day, her journey is a reminder that technology, when guided by vision and care, can be a powerful force for equity and enduring change.

LinkedIn   Book

Anna Mazarsky | Rewriting the Rules of Venture Capital for Women Founders

Anna Mazarsky spent two decades in the global startup ecosystem watching a pattern she couldn’t ignore: brilliant women with stronger teams, better data, and more defensible business models walking out of pitch rooms with less capital, harder questions, and a gnawing doubt that whispered “maybe I’m not good enough.”

After working with over 500 startups and helping founders raise more than $60 million, Anna noticed something striking. Only a fraction of those founders were women. This discovery led her to uncover the widely cited 2.3% funding gap and identify the real issue: female founders don’t have a pipeline problem. They have a positioning problem.

The system asks women prevention questions while men get promotion questions. It holds women to traction standards while men raise on vision alone. Women are wasting time and energy trying to raise capital in a system built on men’s rules.

Anna’s response? “The system isn’t broken. It’s working exactly as designed. I’m not here to fix it. I’m here to arm female founders with the tools to beat it from the inside, at scale, and turn the 2.3% into 50%.”

Despite being non-technical, Anna taught herself to speak AI and built Pink X Power Core, the first hyper-personalized platform designed to flip the power balance. Instead of teaching women to play by broken rules, or to settle for limited “female-focused initiatives”, it arms them with proven frameworks like FLIP and CARVE to negotiate confidently, ask for what they truly need, and gain access to high-impact investor networks. The platform makes investor-readiness accessible at under $1,000, turning “investor-ready” into “inevitable.”

title: Why Did The President of Iran Issue an Apology?
author: editor
excerpt: In a statement given on Saturday morning as part of the country’s temporary administration, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian shocked many onlookers by expressing regret to his neighbors for recent attacks against them. States rarely apologize to one another, especially when there is an ongoing conflict, and the phrasing caught our attention. Leaders typically show “regret” or disassociate themselves with accountability. Instead, Pezeshkian openly admitted that neighboring nations had been targeted and stated that Iranian soldiers had now been directed to cease attacking them unless assaults on Iran came from their borders.I feel compelled to apologize to the neighboring nations who were targeted,” he stated. “We do not intend to invade neighbouring countries. That alone begs the first question: why now, and was this a sincere apology? The interim administration may be attempting to control the growing regional repercussions. Following strikes by Israel and the United States on Saturday, February 28, other nations in the region were caught in the crossfire. Following the initial wave of strikes that killed key Iranian commanders and crippled central command systems, Pezeshkian proposed that these operations were executed under “fire at will” orders. title: Following Maduro’s Detention, the US and Venezuela Decide to Restore Diplomatic Relations
author: editor
excerpt: Restoring diplomatic and consular ties between the US and Venezuela has been agreed upon. The two parties will work together to advance political reconciliation, support economic recovery, and foster stability, the agency said in a statement. The establishment of formal bilateral connections is a highly symbolic gesture, even if their diplomatic relations have been improving since the US military’s surprise incursion in January that resulted in the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. Maduro and his wife were taken into custody by forces under President Donald Trump’s orders, and they were brought before a Manhattan court to answer to accusations of drug and firearm offenses, which they deny. Washington has already named a new diplomat in Venezuela, and the US embassy in Caracas, which closed in 2019, has reopened. A “new stage of constructive dialogue, based on mutual respect” is what the Venezuelan administration declared on Thursday. It said that the “social and economic happiness of the Venezuelan people” must be the outcome of the partnership. However, unlike the US state department’s announcement, the Caracas statement did not mention a transition or upcoming elections. Maduro, who is scheduled to go on trial in the US this month, and other government officials have been charged by the US with running a criminal organization that engages in illicit mining and drug trafficking. More diplomatic personnel from the US embassy in Bogotá, Colombia, are anticipated to be sent to Caracas shortly, according to sources who spoke to the BBC. Officials will find it much simpler to conduct in-person negotiations and offer consular services as a result of the relocation. Helping the Venezuelan people progress through a “phased process that creates the conditions for a peaceful transition to a democratically elected government” was the stated goal of the US State Department’s engagement. On Thursday, as he was returning to the United States from a visit to Venezuela, U.S. Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum told reporters on the Caracas airport that it was a “brilliant strategic move” to act in Venezuela before Iran. title: Fuel and Remittances: The Domestic Impact of the Iran Conflict on India
author: editor
excerpt: India is starting to experience domestic unrest as the US and Israel fight Iran. A significant portion of India’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) shipments, as well as over half of its crude oil imports, typically go via the Strait of Hormuz, a small Gulf chokepoint that is currently essentially closed due to the fighting. Beyond oil, India has deeper ties to the area. A significant portion of India’s foreign accounts is financed by the record remittances that the 10 million Indians who live and work throughout the Gulf send home. In general, India has strong economic ties to the Middle East: according to brokerage company Jefferies, the region provides 55% of India’s crude oil, creates 38% of its remittances, and accounts for 17% of its exports. A widening war in the Gulf could therefore hit India on several fronts: energy supplies, remittance flows from the diaspora and Delhi’s delicate diplomatic balancing act between Washington, Tehran and the Arab Gulf states. Delhi is cautious for the time being. According to Harsh V. Pant of the think tank Observer Research Foundation, India is “waiting and watching” in the face of growing uncertainty. title: Regarding the Supply Chain Risk Label, Anthropic Promises to Sue the Pentagon
author: editor
excerpt: An unusual court battle has begun after the United States formally designated the artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic as a supply chain risk. The Pentagon has designated Anthropic as a supply chain risk for the first time, indicating that the agency does not believe Anthropic is safe enough to use. Anthropic has taken steps to challenge the ruling in court after refusing to grant defense agencies unrestricted access to its AI technologies due to worries about mass surveillance and autonomous weaponry. Chief executive Dario Amodei stated on Thursday night, “We do not think this action is legally sound, and we see no choice but to challenge it in court.” A senior Pentagon source stated earlier Thursday that the classification for supply chain risk was “effective immediately.” The defense department had sent Anthropic a letter the day before labeling it a danger, according to Amodei, who noted that the designation “has a narrow scope.”According to the law, the Secretary of War must employ the least restrictive methods to achieve the supply chain protection objective,” he added.The supply chain risk categorization does not (and cannot) restrict the use of Claude or business ties with Anthropic, even for Department of War contractors, provided those uses are not tied to their particular Department of War contracts. The Department of Defense had recently held discussions with the AI developer. According to a person with knowledge of Anthropic who wished to remain anonymous, those discussions were unsuccessful, partly due to the public criticism of the company by President Donald Trump and other members of his administration. After weeks of back and forth, Anthropic leadership believed last week that a resolution was imminent. According to the source familiar, Trump then announced on his Truth Social platform that he was ordering all federal departments to discontinue their use of Anthropic. title: Trump Administration Setback: US Trade Court Mandates Tariff Refunds
author: editor
excerpt: A federal magistrate has facilitated the refund of tariffs to thousands of businesses that were invalidated by the US Supreme Court last month. On Wednesday, the US Court of International Trade directed Customs and Border Protection to issue refunds for duties that US President Donald Trump implemented last year under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). Judge Richard Eaton stated that “all importers of record whose entries were subject to IEEPA duties are entitled to the benefit” of the high court’s ruling. It is still unclear how the payment procedure is conducted. However, the trade court’s decision represents a setback for Trump, who has expressed his dissatisfaction with the possibility of refunds and has endeavored to replace the import duties. The judge’s decision was explicitly related to a case brought by Atmus Filtration, a filtration company in Tennessee. However, the judge stated that he will be the sole individual to hear cases regarding refunds. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the United States was “likely” to implement a 15% global tariff this week, up from the previous 10% rate, in response to Trump’s conflicting statements about the new rate. It is intended to replace the IEEPA tariffs invalidated by the Supreme Court. Tariffs placed on the majority of commodities imported into the United States through the International Economic Partnership Agreement (IEEPA) generated an estimated $130 billion (£97 billion) in revenue for the Trump administration. title: China’s Goal for Economic Growth is the Lowest Since 1991
author: editor
excerpt: As it faces difficulties both domestically and internationally, China has lowered its yearly economic growth target to a range of 4.5%–5%, the lowest expansion aim since 1991. Since it was reduced to “around 5” in 2023, this is the first time the goal has been dropped. The pandemic prevented the establishment of an objective in 2020. The information was made public during the “two sessions,” China’s largest political assembly, which also included some specifics of the 15th Five Year Plan for the second-largest economy in the world. As it faces problems including low consumption, a declining population, an ongoing real estate crisis, tensions in international commerce, and an energy shortage stemming from the Iran War, Beijing seeks to rebuild its economy. According to a China analyst who spoke to the BBC, the reduced aim allows China “more room to manage the economy” without having to make significant financial commitments in order to achieve a specific goal. Although it’s not common, China has previously employed flexible targets, especially during the pandemic,” Jason Bedford of the East Asian Institute study group continued. The nation’s leaders gather for back-to-back meetings during the two sessions, which started on Wednesday and typically last for at least a week.Premier Li Qiang’s 46-page report, which the BBC saw, contained information about China’s GDP target as well as its goals under its most recent Five-Year Plan. title: TikTok Claims That Using Contentious Privacy Technology to Secure Direct Messages will Put at Risk Users
author: editor
excerpt: End-to-end encryption (E2EE), a contentious privacy feature used by almost all of its competitors, will not be implemented by TikTok, citing concerns about user security. The most secure communication method accessible to the general public is E2EE, which means only the sender and the recipient can see the contents of a direct message. It has been adopted by platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and X, which claim that protecting user privacy is their top priority. However, detractors argue that because E2EE prevents law enforcement and tech companies from seeing the content of direct messages, it becomes more difficult to stop dangerous content from spreading online. TikTok has long been accused of having ties to the Chinese government that could jeopardize user data, which complicates matters. Although TikTok has always denied this, US lawmakers ordered the separation of the social media company’s US operations from its international business earlier this year. TikTok has not previously provided an explanation for their decision to forego E2EE. However, the business has now told the BBC that it thinks the technology makes it impossible for safety and police teams to read direct conversations if necessary. title: Fears That the Iran War may Linger on Cause Asian Stock Markets to Plummet and Energy Prices to Surge
author: editor
excerpt: Wednesday saw a third day of declines in Asian stock markets and an increase in oil prices due to concerns that the US-Israel conflict with Iran would continue, creating an energy shock that could lead to inflation. The stock markets in Thailand and South Korea were obliged to temporarily suspend index trading after they fell more than 8%, setting off so-called circuit breakers, which are designed to prevent panic selling. At $83.96 a barrel, Brent crude increased 2.5 percent. Since the US and Israel started bombing Iran on Saturday and Tehran retaliated by striking neighboring Arab nations, it has increased by 15%. Following attacks on ships close to the vital Strait of Hormuz shipping channel, the price of gas and oil has skyrocketed this week. The Nikkei 225 in Japan fell 3.6%, while the benchmark Kospi index in South Korea closed 12% down. The mainland Chinese Shanghai Composite fell 0.8% in afternoon trading, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index fell 2.5%. “A growing probability of this conflict just taking longer to resolve” is what investors are looking at, according to Lindsay James, investment strategist at wealth management company Quilter, who spoke on the BBC’s Today program. The Strait of Hormuz, a narrow strait between Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), is typically the route taken by about 5% of the world’s oil and gas. But when Iran threatened to “set fire” to ships, commerce has virtually stopped. A ship was hit “by an unknown projectile” near the United Arab Emirates, according to a report released by the UK Maritime Trade Operations Centre on Wednesday. title: To Combat Drug Trafficking, US and Ecuadorian Forces Begin an Operation
author: editor
excerpt: The US military’s Southern Command announced on Tuesday that Ecuadorian and US forces had begun operations against what it claimed were terrorist groups in the South American nation. In a statement on X, the Southern Command stated that the action was intended to combat illegal narcotics trafficking but did not go into further detail. A day prior to the declaration, Ecuador’s president Daniel Noboa declared that the United States was one of the “regional allies” participating in a “new phase” of the country’s fight against drug gangs. According to Noboa, Ecuador’s massive ports now handle around 70% of the world’s cocaine, making it a profitable place for drug trafficking organizations. The two biggest producers of cocaine in the world, Colombia and Peru, are also its neighbors. The most recent activities take place four months after Ecuadorians voted against permitting the reintroduction of foreign military bases in the nation, shattering US plans to increase its presence in the eastern Pacific. Noboa, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, who is working to combat organized crime and lower rising levels of violence, was dealt a setback by the referendum outcome. The nation has emerged as one of the major hubs for drug trafficking worldwide in recent years. Francis Donovan, the head of US Southern Command, and Mark Schafer, the head of US Special Operations in Central and South America and the Caribbean, met with Noboa in Quito on Monday. According to a statement from Noboa’s office, plans for information exchange and operational coordination at seaports and airports were reviewed during the discussion.To combat narco-terrorists who have long terrorized, violently attacked, and corrupted people across the hemisphere, we are acting decisively together,” the US Southern Command announced Tuesday. The declaration was made three months after Washington declared that Air Force soldiers would be temporarily stationed at the former US outpost in the port city of Manta. title: Following Calls for an Iranian Regime Change, the European Parliament is Considering inviting Reza Pahlavi
author: editor
excerpt: One of the key figures in the opposition to the Tehran dictatorship and the son of the last Iranian Shah, Reza Pahlavi, may shortly speak to members of the European Parliament. The Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs has compiled a provisional list with his name on it in order to facilitate a discussion on the state of affairs in the nation. The list, which Euronews obtained, is tentative and will be verified on Wednesday afternoon. It includes seven individuals, including Shirin Ebadi, a lawyer and recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize, as well as leaders of other groups and parties that are hostile to the Islamic Republic of Iran, including the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan, the 7 Aban Front, and the communist Tudeh Party. In order to symbolically symbolize Iranian opposition leaders who are unable to participate in the discussion, one seat will be left vacant. title: A Few Aircraft Depart the UAE, but there is still Interruption Due to the Strikes in Iran
author: editor
excerpt: As the joint Israeli-US war on Iran continues to hamper departures around the Middle East, only a few flights have been able to depart the United Arab Emirates. According to flight tracking firm Flightradar24, hundreds of thousands of travelers are impacted by the more than 4,000 flights that are canceled daily throughout the region. The interruption “will only increase the longer the crisis continues” and “will have enormous repercussions for the industry,” according to Ian Petchenik, director of communications. Over 100,000 Britons have registered their presence in the Middle East with the UK government, which coincides with the continuous airline disruption. According to aviation analytics company Cirium, 79% of international flights to Qatar and 71% of flights to the United Arab Emirates were canceled Monday morning. Additionally, 81% of flights to Israel and 92% of flights to Bahrain were grounded. Etihad Airways, the official airline of the United Arab Emirates, halted operations until Wednesday at 14:00 local time (10:00 GMT). However, Monday saw a few ad hoc flights, such as an Etihad flight to London Heathrow (EY67), which is scheduled to arrive in the UK early in the evening. Flightradar 24, a flight-tracking website, reports that other Etihad flights have departed for Delhi, Paris, Cairo, Moscow, and Karachi. The carrier stated: “Some repositioning, cargo and repatriation flights may operate in coordination with UAE authorities and subject to strict operational and safety approvals” . Every regularly planned service is still canceled. Dubai International and Dubai World Central, the region’s two primary hubs, will see a “limited resumption of operations” starting Monday night, according to a social media announcement from Dubai Airports. title: As the Crisis Intensifies, Oil and Gas Costs Rise
author: editor
excerpt: As Iran continues to unleash strikes throughout the Middle East in retaliation for continued airstrikes by the US and Israel, oil and gas prices have skyrocketed. After QatarEnergy, one of the largest exporters in the world, suspended production due to “military attacks” on its facilities, natural gas prices jumped by almost 50% on Monday. Following the weekend attacks on at least three ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Brent crude, the world’s benchmark for oil prices, surged 10% to beyond $82 per barrel on Monday. About 20% of the world’s oil and gas are transported through the vital waterway in the country’s south, and Iran issued a warning to ships not to sail through it. The two main US stock market indexes began the day lower, but by the middle of the trading day, the Nasdaq and S&P 500 had recovered their losses and were slightly higher. The owner of British Airways had the largest decline in the index after the disruption to Middle Eastern airspace, and the FTSE 100 share index in London closed down 1.2%. Concerns that a persistent increase in energy prices could feed inflation, which could result in fewer interest rate reduction by central banks, caused banks including Barclays, Standard Chartered, and HSBC to have their share values decline. The largest increases on the FTSE 100 were companies in the oil and defense sectors. Germany’s Dax continued its previous drops to trade 2.6% lower, while France’s CAC-40 index closed down 2.2%. The state-owned company QatarEnergy announced that it has halted LNG production after the Ministry of Defense (MoD) of the nation claimed that a drone fired from Iran had targeted a facility in Ras Laffan Industrial City. A drone targeted a water tank at a power facility in Mesaieed, south of the capital Doha, according to Qatar’s Ministry of Defense. Aramco temporarily closed its large oil refinery at Ras Tanura on the coast in neighboring Saudi Arabia after it was struck by a drone. With analysts cautioning that a protracted battle could drive oil prices even higher, international shipping has all but stopped at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. title: ‘Landmark’ Nuclear Energy Pact Between Canada and India to Reastablish Relations
author: editor
excerpt: A 10-year nuclear energy pact is among the several agreements that India and Canada have announced since their prime leaders met in Delhi to mend strained diplomatic relations. In other sectors, including technology, vital minerals, space, defense, and education, Narendra Modi and Mark Carney reached a consensus. According to Carney, they decided to finalize a free trade agreement that had been brewing for years by the end of 2026. Reducing susceptibility to hefty US trade tariffs is a goal shared by both nations. After his predecessor accused Delhi of having a hand in the 2023 assassination of Sikh separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar on Canadian land, Carney’s administration is working to mend the tense relationship between the two countries. India vehemently denied Justin Trudeau’s accusation. As both sides canceled visa services and removed each other’s diplomats, trade and diplomatic relations nearly came to a halt. There is a sizable Indian expat population in Canada. However, since Carney entered office last year, the connection has been carefully restored, aided by his government’s declaration that it does not now believe India is connected to violent acts or threats on Canadian land. However, other Canadians have refuted that assertion, including members of the Sikh diaspora in Canada and a Liberal MP from Carney’s own party, who say they think India still targets them. Anita Anand, Canada’s foreign minister, disassociated herself from remarks made by a senior Canadian official claiming that India has stopped all foreign meddling in Canada after Carney’s meeting with Modi on Monday.”I personally wouldn’t use the senior official’s words,” she told reporters in Delhi. However, Anand said that “we need to have these diplomatic conversations in order to make progress” and supported Canada’s move to re-engage with India. Since the start of his trip, Carney has not yet talked to Canadian press. Citing his busy schedule, his administration canceled a scheduled news conference after the meeting with Modi. title: As the Cost of Commodities Increases, US Consumer Prices rise Sharply in January
author: editor
excerpt: As companies passed on import duties and hiked prices at the beginning of 2026, US producer prices surged in January, with the cost of products outside the volatile food and energy category rising by the greatest in almost three and a half years. Economists’ views that the Federal Reserve would not continue lowering interest rates prior to its June 16–17 meeting were strengthened by the Labour Department’s Friday release of a stronger-than-expected increase in the Producer Price Index. A broadening of margins, including for the wholesale and commercial equipment business as well as the retail sales of clothing, accessories, and footwear, helped the PPI. Last month, there was a strong increase in several components, including as domestic airfare and healthcare, that are used to calculate the Personal Consumption Expenditures price indexes, which are the inflation measures that the US central bank tracks for its 2% target. After rounding, economists calculated that the so-called core PCE inflation which does not include food and energy rose by as much as 0.5% per month in January. In December, that metric increased by 0.4%, the largest increase in ten months. “As businesses pass on higher costs for services, wider producer margins could add some upside for consumer costs in the coming months,” stated Ben Ayers, senior economist at Nationwide. “We expect the Fed to stay on pause at its upcoming March meeting, given still-buoyant core inflation and the recent firming of job gains. The strike was launched for a number of reasons, including regime change and the failure to come to an agreement to restrict Iran’s nuclear program, according to US President Donald Trump. International air traffic is avoiding the area, according to flight-tracking data, while Iranian airspace has been restricted.

British Airways has canceled its flights to Amman, Jordan, on Saturday, as well as to Tel Aviv and Bahrain until Wednesday. title: Dyson Accepts Forced Labor lawsuit in Landmark UK Case
author: editor
excerpt: Dyson, an electronics appliance manufacturer, has agreed to settle a lawsuit filed against it by 24 migrant workers who claimed they were exposed to coercive and harsh treatment in a Malaysian facility that produced the company’s parts. Workers from Nepal and Bangladesh sued the corporation in 2022, claiming they were subjected to modern-day slavery. Dyson has denied all culpability. When the action was filed, it stated that it was previously unaware of the alleged abuses and that the Malaysian supplier should be held accountable instead. The case is noteworthy because it establishes a precedent that accusations against foreign businesses who supply British manufacturers can be heard in English courts. The employees claimed being harassed and abused, having their passports confiscated, and being made to work long hours in filthy conditions. According to their lawyers, Leigh Day denied them toilet breaks and forced them to labor “upwards of 12 hours at a time without relieving themselves”. The terms of any compensation to the workers are not mentioned in the settlement agreement. Dyson and Leigh Day stated the conclusion was reached “in recognition of the expenses of litigation and the benefits of settlement” in separate but nearly identical comments posted on their websites. title: What Do a Broken AC, a Cobra Farm, and Human Nature Have in Common?
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Written By Hamzah Abu Zannad Imagine you’re a landlord. Not a bad one. Not greedy. Just practical. You’re tired of tenants calling about dripping taps, squeaky hinges, and AC filters that “feel weaker than last summer.” So you introduce a rule: “If a repair or maintenance bill is above AED 1,000, I’ll pay. If it’s below AED 1,000, you pay.” You lean back in your chair. You’ve just filtered out the nonsense. Except you haven’t. Three months later, something fascinating happens. Every repair bill is AED 1,450. Or AED 1,620. Or AED 1,300. Never AED 800. Never AED 950. Always comfortably north of your threshold. What changed? Nothing about the plumbing. Nothing about the AC. Nothing about the hinges. Only the incentive. The Small Leak That Became a Strategy The tenant isn’t immoral. He’s rational. If he calls the technician for a small AED 600 fix, he pays. If he waits, lets two or three minor issues accumulate, and the invoice becomes AED 1,200… You pay. So what does he do? He waits. And when the technician arrives, there’s a subtle suggestion: “While you’re here, maybe check the compressor.” A loose screw becomes a full assembly adjustment. A minor fix becomes a preventive overhaul. Not because the tenant is evil. Because he is optimizing. Enter the Cobras In colonial India, under the British Raj, officials faced a cobra problem in Delhi. So they did what any sensible administration would do: They paid people for dead cobras. Initially, it worked. Then something strange happened. People started breeding cobras. Why chase snakes when you can manufacture them? When the government canceled the program, breeders released the snakes. The cobra population increased. The solution created the problem. Economists later gave this phenomenon a name: The Cobra Effect. But it’s really just human nature responding to incentives. The Uncomfortable Truth Here’s the part that makes people uneasy: The tenant is not cheating you. He is responding perfectly to the system you built. And this is where the Freakonomics lens kicks in. When daycare centers introduced a small fine for late pickups, lateness increased. Why? Because the fine transformed guilt into a transaction. Parents were no longer “bad.” They were simply “buying extra time.” Your AED 1,000 repair threshold does the same thing. You transformed: “Be reasonable with maintenance.” Into: “Make sure it’s above the limit.” The Rule Beneath the Rule People do not respond to intentions. They respond to incentives. You didn’t design a maintenance policy. You designed a pricing game. And humans are excellent game players. Especially when someone else is paying. The Question That Matters Before introducing any rule — in real estate, policy, or corporate life — ask: “If someone wanted to game this, how would they?” If you can answer that question in under 30 seconds… They will too. And they’ll do it better. Now let me ask you something, because this matters: In your real case — Did repair approvals require landlord sign-off first? Or was the tenant free to call vendors and submit invoices? Because if the tenant controlled vendor selection, you didn’t just create a threshold incentive. You created a collaborative ecosystem. Which is even more interesting. About the Author Hamzah Abu Zannad is the Co-Founder and Managing Director of Axiom Prime Real Estate Development. With over two decades of experience in Dubai’s property market, he has contributed to projects shaped by long-term strategy, disciplined execution, and sustainable growth. At Axiom Prime, he focuses on low-density, community-centered luxury developments inspired by Dutch living principles — prioritizing walkability, natural light, and human-scale design. The company’s flagship projects in Jumeirah Village Triangle and Jumeirah Garden City reflect his belief that real estate should be intentional, functional, and enduring — not merely impressive. With a steady, forward-looking view of Dubai’s evolution, Hamzah continues to play a thoughtful role in shaping the city’s evolving urban fabric. content:
Written By Hamzah Abu Zannad

Imagine you’re a landlord.

Not a bad one. Not greedy. Just practical.

You’re tired of tenants calling about dripping taps, squeaky hinges, and AC filters that “feel weaker than last summer.”

So you introduce a rule:

“If a repair or maintenance bill is above AED 1,000, I’ll pay.
If it’s below AED 1,000, you pay.”

You lean back in your chair.

You’ve just filtered out the nonsense.

Except you haven’t.

Three months later, something fascinating happens.

Every repair bill is AED 1,450.

Or AED 1,620.
Or AED 1,300.

Never AED 800.
Never AED 950.

Always comfortably north of your threshold.

What changed?

Nothing about the plumbing.
Nothing about the AC.
Nothing about the hinges.

Only the incentive.

The Small Leak That Became a Strategy

The tenant isn’t immoral.

He’s rational.

If he calls the technician for a small AED 600 fix, he pays.

If he waits, lets two or three minor issues accumulate, and the invoice becomes AED 1,200…

You pay.

So what does he do?

He waits.

And when the technician arrives, there’s a subtle suggestion:

“While you’re here, maybe check the compressor.”

A loose screw becomes a full assembly adjustment.

A minor fix becomes a preventive overhaul.

Not because the tenant is evil.

Because he is optimizing.

Enter the Cobras

In colonial India, under the British Raj, officials faced a cobra problem in Delhi.

So they did what any sensible administration would do:

They paid people for dead cobras.

Initially, it worked.

Then something strange happened.

People started breeding cobras.

Why chase snakes when you can manufacture them?

When the government canceled the program, breeders released the snakes.

The cobra population increased.

The solution created the problem.

Economists later gave this phenomenon a name:

The Cobra Effect.

But it’s really just human nature responding to incentives.

The Uncomfortable Truth

Here’s the part that makes people uneasy:

The tenant is not cheating you.

He is responding perfectly to the system you built.

And this is where the Freakonomics lens kicks in.

When daycare centers introduced a small fine for late pickups, lateness increased.

Why?

Because the fine transformed guilt into a transaction.

Parents were no longer “bad.”
They were simply “buying extra time.”

Your AED 1,000 repair threshold does the same thing.

You transformed:

“Be reasonable with maintenance.”

Into:

“Make sure it’s above the limit.”

The Rule Beneath the Rule

People do not respond to intentions.

They respond to incentives.

You didn’t design a maintenance policy.

You designed a pricing game.

And humans are excellent game players.

Especially when someone else is paying.

The Question That Matters

Before introducing any rule — in real estate, policy, or corporate life — ask:

“If someone wanted to game this, how would they?”

If you can answer that question in under 30 seconds…

They will too.

And they’ll do it better.

Now let me ask you something, because this matters:

In your real case —
Did repair approvals require landlord sign-off first?
Or was the tenant free to call vendors and submit invoices?

Because if the tenant controlled vendor selection, you didn’t just create a threshold incentive.

You created a collaborative ecosystem.

Which is even more interesting.

About the Author

Hamzah Abu Zannad is the Co-Founder and Managing Director of Axiom Prime Real Estate Development. With over two decades of experience in Dubai’s property market, he has contributed to projects shaped by long-term strategy, disciplined execution, and sustainable growth.

At Axiom Prime, he focuses on low-density, community-centered luxury developments inspired by Dutch living principles — prioritizing walkability, natural light, and human-scale design. The company’s flagship projects in Jumeirah Village Triangle and Jumeirah Garden City reflect his belief that real estate should be intentional, functional, and enduring — not merely impressive.

With a steady, forward-looking view of Dubai’s evolution, Hamzah continues to play a thoughtful role in shaping the city’s evolving urban fabric.

Naturally, resistance emerges. Humans are not wired for sudden change. The key is empathetic leadership. You must communicate clearly, create understanding, and build energy around the desired outcome. Emotional intelligence plays a bigger role than pure technical intelligence in these situations. During transformation programs involving more than 450 professionals in the UK Government, success was built on trust first and execution second. When people feel included and validated, progress accelerates.” He concluded that ignoring the human element multiplies difficulty unnecessarily. The AI Inflection Point: “What Trends Will Define the Next Five Years?” When we asked about the future, Anthony spoke with conviction about Artificial Intelligence. “AI adoption is accelerating across every sector. This transformation is already underway.” He noted that early adopters will gain disproportionate advantage. Build the product thoughtfully. Recruit individuals based on personality, emotional intelligence, and cultural alignment. Skills can be taught. Character is foundational.” He described this vision as his long-term north star. Every initiative must create value, align with strategic goals, and deliver against clear KPIs. However, execution matters equally. I prioritize empathy, transparency, and structured governance. In complex environments such as government or large-scale smart city initiatives, clear accountability builds credibility. I also believe leaders must model the behavior they expect. Throughout our conversation, one theme remained consistent. Technology may enable progress, but people determine its success.

Here is what he shared with Entrepreneur Mirror.

From Uniform to Innovation: “What Sparked the Shift?”

When asked about the origins of his journey, Anthony reflected thoughtfully on the unexpected beginnings of his career.

“I actually began my career in the Police Force. At that time, I was seeking stability after facing some challenges as a late teenager. It felt like a secure and structured path.

However, I quickly realized that while I valued helping people, I was more fascinated by the technology and systems that enabled operations behind the scenes. A senior leader noticed that I had strengths in both people engagement and technology. He told me that technology would shape the future and that I should consider moving in that direction.

I took that advice seriously. I invested the savings I had into professional IT qualifications. That decision shaped everything that followed. Over the last 22 years, combining technical expertise with people skills has allowed me to lead programs from UK Government to global enterprises and now NEOM.”

He acknowledged that sometimes a single piece of advice can redefine an entire trajectory.

The Human Equation of Change: “What Has Been Your Toughest Challenge?”

As our discussion turned toward transformation at scale, Anthony emphasized that complexity rarely lies in code or systems.

“Every major challenge I have faced ultimately comes back to people. If you do not get people alignment right, nothing else works.

Large transformation programs require organizations to change direction. They must adopt new operating models and new ways of working. Naturally, resistance emerges. Humans are not wired for sudden change.

The key is empathetic leadership. You must communicate clearly, create understanding, and build energy around the desired outcome. Emotional intelligence plays a bigger role than pure technical intelligence in these situations.

During transformation programs involving more than 450 professionals in the UK Government, success was built on trust first and execution second. When people feel included and validated, progress accelerates.”

He concluded that ignoring the human element multiplies difficulty unnecessarily.

The AI Inflection Point: “What Trends Will Define the Next Five Years?”

When we asked about the future, Anthony spoke with conviction about Artificial Intelligence.

“AI adoption is accelerating across every sector. That is not a future trend. It is already happening.

The real challenge will not be capability. It will be how organizations manage the human side of AI integration. Many people are genuinely concerned about job displacement. Governance frameworks are still evolving. Ethical considerations are still being defined.

The leaders who succeed will be those who understand both the technology and the change management required to implement it responsibly. That is one reason I am currently completing an MBA in Artificial Intelligence alongside my executive role. Understanding both architecture and psychology will define the next generation of leadership.”

Reinventing Traditional Industries: “How Will Emerging Technologies Reshape Your Domain?”

Discussing industries such as construction, Anthony highlighted the scale of opportunity ahead.
