AI and emerging technologies can enable real-time traceability, smarter workflows, and contextual decision-making. Delivering the right knowledge to the right individual at the right time changes outcomes dramatically.

Business models will shift. Workflows will become fully digitized ecosystems rather than fragmented processes. Productivity levels will increase significantly within the next 12 to 24 months. This transformation is already underway.”

He noted that early adopters will gain disproportionate advantage.

Beyond Enterprise:” What Is Your Long-Term Vision?”

When asked about his personal aspirations, Anthony shared his entrepreneurial ambition.

“I genuinely enjoy leading within large organizations and intend to continue doing so effectively. However, I also aspire to build something independently.

I am currently at the pre-seed stage with a validated product ideology. My ambition is to create a culturally strong company where people feel intrinsically motivated. A company is nothing without its people.

The strategy is clear. Secure the right investment. Build the product thoughtfully. Recruit individuals based on personality, emotional intelligence, and cultural alignment. Skills can be taught. Character is foundational.”

He described this vision as his long-term north star.

Principles Over Profit: “What Guides Your Decisions?”

As our conversation deepened, Anthony explained how he balances commercial clarity with human awareness.

“In commercial business, revenue and measurable outcomes are essential. Every initiative must create value, align with strategic goals, and deliver against clear KPIs.

However, execution matters equally. I prioritize empathy, transparency, and structured governance. In complex environments such as government or large-scale smart city initiatives, clear accountability builds credibility.

I also believe leaders must model the behavior they expect. I stay present with my teams and remain approachable. When leaders build a strong foundation of support, teams respond with commitment when it matters most.”

He stressed that credibility is earned through consistency.

Innovation as an Ecosystem: “What Strategy Delivered Breakthrough Results?”

When discussing innovation, Anthony shared a structured framework rather than a single moment.

“Innovation requires an ecosystem. It begins with properly defining business problems rather than jumping to predefined solutions.

Next, build a supply ecosystem that includes accelerators, institutes, venture capital networks, and suppliers. Every promising concept should go through proof-of-concept testing in a controlled environment.

The most overlooked element is commercial structure. Traditional enterprise procurement processes can suffocate startups. Flexible sourcing models and supportive commercial terms are essential if you truly want innovation to flourish.”

He emphasized that innovation must be nurtured intentionally.

Leadership as Reciprocity: “How Has Your Style Evolved?”

As our interview concluded, Anthony reflected on his leadership journey.

“Empathy has always been my foundation. What has evolved is my understanding of different frames of reference. People come from diverse cultures, backgrounds, and capabilities. Understanding that diversity strengthens teams.

Leadership is an energy exchange. When you invest in people, they reciprocate during critical moments. Once that empathetic foundation is built, task-oriented execution becomes far easier.

I continue to invest heavily in self-development, both technically and psychologically. Understanding systems is important. Understanding people is essential.”

He ended our conversation by reaffirming that sustainable transformation begins with trust.”

Anthony Penwright’s journey is a powerful reminder that in a world driven by automation and digital acceleration, empathy remains a competitive advantage. Technology may enable transformation, but leadership rooted in human understanding ultimately determines its success.

By combining tradition with advanced methodologies and strategic thinking with technical rigor, we aim to deliver projects that outlast trends. Our ambition is to create architecture that contributes to the city, communicates values, and actively participates in shaping collective memory and future urban identity.” A Global Collaboration That Defined a Philosophy Entrepreneur MirrorBureau Cube Partners has collaborated with globally recognized firms. Can you highlight a project that best represents your design philosophy and share the key lessons from it? Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s replied: “One of the projects that most clearly reflects our design philosophy is our collaboration with Zaha Hadid Architects on the Nikola Tesla Museum in Belgrade, developed through an international competition. This project represents more than an architectural proposal; it demonstrates how we approach architecture as dialogue between history and future ambition, between local identity and universal values, and between conceptual vision and technical precision. content:
Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s Interview

Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s is the founder and principal architect of Bureau Cube Partners, an architectural practice established in 2009 and recognized for its multidisciplinary structure, contextual intelligence, and strong design authorship. From the very beginning, his approach has positioned architecture not simply as the creation of buildings, but as a cultural act and civic responsibility, one that must respond thoughtfully to history, urban complexity, and contemporary social needs.

Under his leadership, Bureau Cube Partners has developed into a highly skilled team of licensed architects and engineers capable of delivering projects across diverse typologies, from cultural institutions and public buildings to residential developments and large-scale urban strategies. Rašković’s work is defined by conceptual precision, innovation under real-world constraints, and rigorous technical execution. The ambition is clear: to create architecture that shapes identity, preserves collective memory, and contributes meaningfully to the evolving life of cities.

Architecture as Cultural Strategy

We began the conversation by asking: “You’ve led Bureau Cube Partners since its founding in 2009. How has your vision shaped the firm’s evolution, and what core principles define your architectural approach?”

Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s responded: “Since founding Bureau Cube Partners in 2009, my intention has been to frame architecture as both cultural responsibility and strategic practice. From the outset, the studio was conceived not merely as a design office, but as an integrated platform where concept, urban narrative, engineering logic, and construction precision develop together. Architecture, in our view, must operate as a meaningful civic artifact, not as a purely formal exercise.

Over time, this philosophy shaped the firm into a research-oriented and context-sensitive practice. Every project is understood as part of a broader spatial and historical continuum. Whether we are designing housing, public institutions, or cultural buildings, the goal is never to erase what exists, but to reinterpret identity through a contemporary architectural language. Respect for place, clarity of concept, and intelligent problem-solving under real constraints remain the foundation of our work.

This approach has allowed Bureau Cube Partners to grow into a professional team capable of operating both locally and internationally while maintaining strong authorship and professional integrity. By combining tradition with advanced methodologies and strategic thinking with technical rigor, we aim to deliver projects that outlast trends. Our ambition is to create architecture that contributes to the city, communicates values, and actively participates in shaping collective memory and future urban identity.”

A Global Collaboration That Defined a Philosophy

Entrepreneur MirrorBureau Cube Partners has collaborated with globally recognized firms. Can you highlight a project that best represents your design philosophy and share the key lessons from it?

Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s replied: “One of the projects that most clearly reflects our design philosophy is our collaboration with Zaha Hadid Architects on the Nikola Tesla Museum in Belgrade, developed through an international competition. This project represents more than an architectural proposal; it demonstrates how we approach architecture as dialogue between history and future ambition, between local identity and universal values, and between conceptual vision and technical precision.

The project required architecture to function simultaneously as a space of memory, an educational platform, and a forward-looking cultural landmark. The collaboration itself was based on genuine intellectual exchange. It showed how contemporary design language can reinterpret industrial heritage without diminishing its identity, transforming it into a new spatial narrative aligned with Tesla’s visionary spirit.

The same principles apply to projects of a more intimate scale. The Kings Villa residential development reflects our approach to careful mediation between landscape, historical context, and contemporary living standards. Rather than imposing form, the design emerges from topography, views, and the character of the surrounding neighborhood. Sustainability here is achieved through proportion, material integrity, and long-term livability rather than technological spectacle.

The most important lesson from these experiences was the value of dialogue between local expertise and global perspective, between ambition and constraint, and between different professional cultures. The strongest architecture emerges when local specificity and international discourse are not treated as opposites, but as complementary forces.”

Urban Habitat and Global Standards

Entrepreneur MirrorYou were selected as a juror for the CTBUH Annual Awards in the Urban Habitat category. How do global standards for urbanism and tall buildings influence your work?

Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s responded: “Serving as a juror for the CTBUH Annual Awards in the Urban Habitat category offered valuable insight into how global standards for dense cities and tall buildings are evolving. Today, urban quality is no longer defined solely by height or iconic presence. It is defined by how architecture contributes to human experience through social connectivity, environmental responsibility, inclusivity, and long-term adaptability.

This perspective reinforces our belief that architecture must be understood as part of a larger urban ecosystem. Global principles such as mixed-use integration, climate-responsive design, public realm activation, and ecological balance inform our evaluation of every project, regardless of scale.

At Bureau Cube Partners, even when working on complex urban developments or high-density structures, the central question remains the same: How does this project support everyday life? How does it strengthen the relationship between the built environment and its social and natural context?

Engaging with global urban discourse sharpens our ability to translate international benchmarks into locally grounded solutions. Standards should function as frameworks, not formulas. Architecture must remain contextual, responsible, and human-centered.”

Innovation and Sustainability in Heritage Architecture

Entrepreneur MirrorArchitecture today faces growing challenges, from sustainability to complex urban dynamics. How do you integrate innovation and sustainability into your practice, especially in public or heritage projects?

Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s replied: “Innovation and sustainability are not additions introduced at the end of the design process. They are foundational principles embedded from the first sketch. Every project begins with rigorous contextual research including climate, urban morphology, cultural layers, construction logic, and patterns of long-term use. Sustainable strategies must grow from place rather than be imposed through standard solutions.

Heritage and public projects are particularly demanding because they operate simultaneously within history, present-day functionality, and future resilience. In the restoration and adaptive reuse of the Palace of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, the process required close collaboration between architects, engineers, conservators, and public institutions. The goal was not simply preservation, but reinterpretation, ensuring that historical architecture remains relevant through technical upgrades and environmental improvements.

Similarly, the revitalization of the historic Hotel Bristol in Belgrade required balancing strict conservation principles with contemporary hospitality standards. Adaptive reuse became the primary sustainable strategy. Structural rehabilitation, energy performance improvement, and careful integration of modern systems allowed the building to evolve while preserving its identity and collective memory.

In projects located within sensitive historical contexts, innovation often lies in restraint. A residential and commercial building in Cara Dušana Street demonstrates how contextual integration through proportion, material articulation, and mixed-use programming can strengthen urban vitality without competing with history.

For us, sustainability extends beyond environmental metrics. It includes cultural continuity, urban regeneration, and long-term adaptability. True sustainability means creating architecture capable of enduring socially, culturally, and technologically over time.”

The Future of Bureau Cube Partners

Entrepreneur MirrorLooking ahead, what goals and trends are shaping your architectural journey and the future of Bureau Cube Partners?

Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s replied: “Looking forward, my work continues to explore how architecture can operate meaningfully within layered and often challenging contexts where innovation, sustainability, and social responsibility must be addressed simultaneously. My academic research and professional practice remain closely connected, allowing theoretical investigations to inform built outcomes, particularly in cities undergoing rapid transformation.

For Bureau Cube Partners, the future lies in strengthening international collaborations while expanding our engagement in urban regeneration, infrastructure-related architecture, and climate-responsive design. These fields demand integrated thinking and recognize cities as interconnected social and environmental systems.

At the same time, we remain committed to working across scales from strategic urban frameworks to highly detailed architectural interventions. Our ambition is to create architecture that is resilient and forward-looking, yet firmly rooted in cultural identity.

Ultimately, we aim to contribute projects that foster human connection, support environmental responsibility, and uphold architectural integrity. Architecture should not merely respond to present demands; it should help shape more inclusive, thoughtful, and sustainable urban futures.”

Conclusion

With a strong commitment to cultural continuity, technical excellence, and responsible urban innovation, Milan RAŠKOVIĆ’s continues to position Bureau Cube Partners as a practice where architecture becomes more than design, it becomes strategy, memory, and vision. From heritage restorations to global collaborations, his work reflects the conviction that architecture must not only serve functional needs, but also elevate the civic and emotional experience of the city.

title: Chip Titan Nvidia Makes Record $215 Billion in Sales Despite AI Worries
author: editor
excerpt: Nvidia, the chip giant, has posted a record annual revenue of $215.9 billion (£159.1 billion), despite investor concerns over the vast amounts of money being spent on artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. Sales increased by 73% in the last three months of the company’s fiscal year compared to the previous year, above analyst expectations.”Computing demand is increasing exponentially,” CEO Jensen Huang stated. “Our customers are racing to invest in AI compute – the factories powering the AI industrial revolution and their future growth.” While Nvidia provides chips to companies in the AI field, it has also announced intentions in recent weeks to drive demand with new technologies of its own. Nvidia is the world’s most valuable publicly traded business, with a market capitalization of over $4.8 trillion. It has become a key actor in the development of AI infrastructure, delivering advanced chips to top AI model developers such as OpenAI and Meta. According to Gene Munster, management partner at Deepwater Asset Management, the buildout is expected to last for a long period.”AI is accelerating faster than people who aren’t using these tools can understand,” Munster said on the social media platform X on Wednesday. Nvidia has been scrutinized by investors concerned about its ever-expanding network of partnerships with other companies. Critics have suggested the possibility of “circular financing” transactions, in which Nvidia’s investments in other startups may obscure perceptions of how strong AI demand truly is. title: The Canadian Finance Minister Doesn’t Think the US will Raise Tariffs
author: editor
excerpt: Canada’s finance minister stated that a baseline tariff may be the “price” it must pay to continue shipping goods to the United States. François-Philippe Champagne’s words came following Donald Trump’s State of the Union address, in which the US president stated that tariffs should eventually replace income taxes as America’s primary revenue source. Champagne’s comments come after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that Canada must accept “some level of higher tariff” if it wants to do business with the United States. Following the US Supreme Court’s rejection of his prior expansive tariff program, Trump implemented a global 10% duty last week using a never-used law known as Section 122. Champagne told reporters in Ottawa that the American administration believes there will be a cost for accessing the American market. He was asked if the president’s remarks in his speech hindered Canada’s hopes for tariff relief.”Every country in the world that I know of is paying a price,” he continued. “What I’m saying is that Canada is paying the lowest price.” Canada enjoys tariff exclusions in accordance with the USMCA, a continental free trade agreement. It also faces higher levies on steel, aluminum, and softwood lumber.If Canada agrees to a higher tax on us in exchange for opening up their market to us in areas such as dairy and other goods, that would be a beneficial talk,” Greer told CBC on Tuesday. Following the trade tensions, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that he aims to quadruple Canada’s non-US exports over the next decade, particularly in industries such as metals and automobiles. The United States is by far Canada’s largest customer, accounting for around 75% of Canadian exports. The Canadians’ new tone on US tariffs follows a 6-3 US Supreme Court judgment on Friday that determined Trump’s comprehensive tariff strategy, adopted in April, was illegal and that the president had overstepped his authority. title: The US Federal Department is Accused of Concealing Trump-Related Epstein Material
author: editor
excerpt: The chief Democrat on the congressional committee investigating Jeffrey Epstein has accused the US Justice Department of suppressing documents including allegations of sexual abuse of a minor leveled against President Donald Trump. Robert Garcia, a member of the House Oversight Committee, said he personally seen documents containing the allegation that had not been made public. In response, the Justice Department stated that “NOTHING has been deleted” and that documents were withheld only if they were “duplicates, privileged, or part of an ongoing federal investigation”. Trump has continually denied any wrongdoing in the Epstein case and recently stated that he had been “totally exonerated”. The Justice Department has previously stated that some of the papers contain “untrue and sensationalist claims against President Trump”. Abigail Jackson, a spokeswoman for the White House, “by releasing thousands of pages of documents, cooperating with the House Oversight Committee’s subpoena request, signing the Epstein Files Transparency Act, and calling for more investigations into Epstein’s Democrat friends, President Trump has done more for Epstein’s victims than anyone before him.” Epstein, the late convicted sex offender, appears to have been pals with Trump for several years. According to Trump, they had a falling out in the early 2000s, two years before Epstein was jailed. The Justice Department has released millions of files detailing what the government investigations against Epstein revealed. The staged releases were sparked by an act approved by the president, who had previously opposed the distribution of the material. title: Hillary Clinton appears before a US House Committee Examining Epstein
author: editor
excerpt: Hillary Clinton is testifying before a panel of the US House of Representatives examining the crimes of late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The former Democratic Secretary of State and presidential candidate recently consented to testify before the House Oversight Committee, alongside her husband, former President Bill Clinton. Both have previously rejected requests to appear, claiming they were politically motivated. Their willingness to testify averted potential contempt of Congress actions against them. Hillary Clinton has stated that she does not recall meeting or conversing with Epstein. Her spouse, who knew Epstein, has denied any culpability or knowledge of his misdeeds. Bill Clinton has stated that he severed relations with Epstein two decades ago and expressed remorse that he was ever acquainted with the financier, who died in 2019. He is due to give his own evidence on Friday. In a recent BBC interview in Berlin, Germany, Hillary Clinton stated that the deposition was a Republican ploy to distract attention from Trump’s relationship with Epstein.”We have nothing to hide,” she explained. “We have continuously requested the complete release of these files. We believe sunlight is the finest disinfectant. She claimed she never saw Epstein, although she did meet his guilty associate, Ghislaine Maxwell, “on a few occasions”. In 2010, Maxwell attended the wedding of the couple’s daughter, Chelsea Clinton, in New York. The couple’s recent decision that they would submit testimony after all was a change of their combative stance, and it came as a potential contempt vote loomed in the House. title: Tony Wu-Pasomthong | Driving the Future of Electric Mobility Through Intelligent Battery Infrastructure
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Building sustainable mobility systems requires more than technology. It requires foresight, operational discipline, and deep understanding of consumer behavior. Tony Wu-Pasomthong brings over 20 years of experience in the technology sector, positioning himself at the forefront of electric mobility innovation in Southeast Asia. As the founder of SWITCH, he is redefining how battery-swapping ecosystems function by combining IoT intelligence, flexible payment models, and scalable infrastructure designed for real-world urban mobility. The Early Foundations We began by asking, “Could you share a bit about your early background, education, and the key experiences that shaped your career journey?” “My educational background is in Technology Management, and I have spent more than two decades in the technology sector. In 2006, I founded a company focused on LED innovation, electronics, and smart lighting solutions. I spent ten years in Shenzhen during China’s technology boom, which gave me direct exposure to rapid industrial growth, manufacturing scale, and product development speed. After China, I served as COO of a European smart city technology company for five years, managing projects across multiple cities. Europe taught me stability, large-scale project management, and financial modeling for technology systems. However, I always felt drawn back to Asia, where the pace of change allows ideas to be implemented and scaled quickly.” The Evolution of SWITCH Continuing the discussion, we asked, “How has your company evolved since its inception?” “We operate with the mindset of a startup. In the early stages, we focused on tier two cities where we could test and refine our solutions in real conditions. The market responded quickly, and demand accelerated our growth. Today, SWITCH is scaling nationwide. What began as a focused pilot strategy is now evolving into a broader rollout, bringing intelligent battery-swapping infrastructure to a much wider audience and reshaping the electric mobility landscape across the country.” Contribution to the Regional Ecosystem Exploring the company’s broader impact, we asked, “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?” “Our focus has always been consumer convenience. That philosophy drove us to develop one of the most advanced IoT ecosystems in the battery swap sector. Our system integrates real-time monitoring, user-friendly access, and practical design to make electric mobility seamless. By improving reliability and accessibility, we are helping accelerate EV adoption while supporting delivery professionals and urban commuters who depend on efficiency for daily income.” Qualities for Success -Tony Wu-Pasomthong Shifting to leadership, we asked, “What three qualities do you believe are critical for success in your industry?” “In a highly competitive sector like ours, customer focus is essential. That includes vehicle performance, safety, and system reliability. Since we primarily serve professional delivery services, flexibility in financial models is also critical. We must adapt solutions to match customer realities. Ultimately, success comes from combining customer understanding with adaptability, innovation, and strong execution.” Innovation and Adaptation Turning to technology, we asked, “How has your organization adapted to technological changes? Could you share a key innovation you’ve implemented?” “In Southeast Asia, we are one of the few companies offering battery swaps charged only for the percentage of battery used. Consumers are accustomed to paying for fuel by volume, and we applied that logic to electric mobility. In addition, we designed our system to be extremely user-friendly. Accessibility is key. Technology must simplify life, not complicate it. These innovations allow us to remain competitive in a fast-evolving market while keeping customer experience at the center.” Navigating Industry Challenges As the conversation deepened, we asked, “How would you guide someone navigating the challenges of establishing themselves in this industry?” “You must always look two to three years ahead. In technology, time moves quickly, and anticipating trends is critical. Regulations can be challenging, but if managed wisely, they can become strategic advantages. It is not always about being the biggest or the most advanced. Practicality matters. Understanding consumer needs and applying survivability strategies in a fast-moving market is what ensures long-term success.” Final Reflection Before concluding, we asked Tony to share a final thought for emerging technology entrepreneurs. “The future belongs to those who combine vision with disciplined execution. Technology alone is not enough. You must understand markets, regulations, and human behavior. When those elements align, real transformation becomes possible.” Through SWITCH, Tony Wu-Pasomthong continues to build intelligent battery infrastructure designed not only for growth, but for practical, scalable impact in Southeast Asia’s evolving mobility ecosystem. title: The EU Commission is Telling MEPs to Vote for the EU-US Deal Even if Further Tariffs are Coming
author: editor
excerpt: On Tuesday, EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič told parliamentarians to continue forward with the EU-US trade deal, even though Washington is adding fresh tariffs and there is legal uncertainty over the deal’s terms. The pact was suddenly put on hold on Monday after the US Supreme Court ruled that most of the tariffs the White House imposed worldwide in 2025 were unlawful. Soon after the verdict, US President Donald Trump said that imports from US allies, like the EU, will have new 10% tariffs. Šefčovič reminded MEPs, “We must keep the process moving forward in fulfilling our promises.” “Getting a vote in plenary in March is still our goal, but only if we get more information from the US.” Šefčovič also added that his US counterparts had called him as of Saturday to “reassure” him that they will “stick” to the pact if the EU “respect the deal.” But the pact, which Trump and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen signed in July 2025 after weeks of trade brinkmanship, is now up in the air and requires the European Parliament’s approval to take effect. title: The UK Government Says That the Contract for the Chagos Islands is Not on Hold, even Though a Minister Said it Was
author: editor
excerpt: The government says there is “no pause” in its deal for the Chagos Islands. This is despite a minister informing MPs that the UK was “pausing” the process of adopting the law that would give Mauritius control of the island. A source in the administration said, “There is no pause; we have never set a deadline, and the usual way of announcing timings will be used. While answering questions from MPs, Foreign Office Minister Hamish Falconer said that the UK was “pausing” the process while “discussions” took place with the US. Last Monday, US President Donald Trump told Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer to cancel the accord, even though he had previously said he supported the treaty. Britain has been in control of the Chagos Islands in the Indian Ocean since the early 19th century. They are formally called the British Indian Ocean Territory. title: Apple Claims Some Mac Mini Production will Migrate to the United States
author: editor
excerpt: Apple has announced that it will manufacture some of its Mac Mini desktop computers in the United States for the first time, as the technology giant tries to increase domestic production in response to pressure from US President Donald Trump. On Tuesday, the iPhone maker announced plans for a “significant expansion” of its factory in Houston, Texas, to produce Mac Minis and AI servers. Apple’s latest move comes after the company committed last year to raise its investment in the United States by $600 billion (£445 billion). The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the expected volume of Mac Mini production in the United States. The niche tiny computers, currently manufactured in Asia, account for less than 5% of Mac sales. Apple is deeply committed to the future of American manufacturing, and we’re proud to significantly expand our footprint in Houston with Mac mini production beginning later this year,” CEO Tim Cook said in a statement. The company also announced plans for an advanced manufacturing training center at its Houston facility. title: Trump will Speak to a Transformed America at a Critical Juncture in his Presidency
author: editor
excerpt: Donald Trump’s State of the Union address, which he will give on Tuesday night, has more stakes in its outcome than most of his congressional remarks. Trump has expanded the scope of presidential authority in a number of ways during the past 12 months. He has made significant progress in both foreign and domestic affairs. However, not all of his accomplishments have been well received; in fact, some have caused great division. Trump will speak to an America that is very different from the one he returned to lead last year, regardless of how his policies have been received. He has accelerated the implementation of his expansive second-term agenda, which includes redefining the role of the presidency, upending foreign alliances, cracking down on illegal immigration and successfully sealing the border, and challenging the checks and balances that form the cornerstone of the American political system. However, he has encountered major challenges that have limited his goals, both from the general people and important organizations. Voters will evaluate Trump’s second term as president in November when the midterm elections are held in a little more than eight months. They could either give the Democrats control of Congress or maintain his Republican majority, guaranteeing two years of intense oversight and legislative deadlock that might, in his own words, result in his impeachment once more. title: Large French Investors no Longer pay Dividend Taxes in India
author: editor
excerpt: A three-decade-old tax pact between France and India has been updated, increasing Delhi’s authority to tax certain transactions but decreasing dividend levies for major French investors. Major corporations like Sanofi, Renault, and L’Oreal, who have increased their investments in India in recent years, may profit from the reforms. Additionally, the agreement grants Delhi the authority to tax capital gains from share sales, including those in which a French company controls less than 10% of an Indian business. A most-favoured-nation (MFN) clause that had permitted French firms to claim a reduced tax rate in India is also eliminated in the amended treaty. Once all procedures and legal clearances have been completed in both nations, it will take effect. Days after French President Emmanuel Macron’s visit to India, India’s finance ministry on Monday unveiled the specifics of the revised pact. The nations stated during the visit that they had elevated their relationship to a “Special Global Strategic Partnership” and strengthened their collaboration in sectors including space technology and defense. On February 17, they praised the bilateral tax treaty amendment in a joint statement. They said that it would “secure economic activity for French and Indian businesses and pave the way for greater investments and collaborations between the two countries” . According to data reported by the Reuters news agency, foreign portfolio investors headquartered in France had shares in Indian companies valued at $21 billion (£15.6 billion) as of January 2026. Last year, India and France’s bilateral commerce was $15 billion. The new regulations will reduce the dividend tax rate from 10% to 5% for French firms that possess at least 10% of an Indian company. For French investors who own less than 10% of an Indian company, the dividend tax would increase from 10% to 15%. title: Trump’s New Tariff is Implemented at a Slower Pace than Anticipated
author: editor
excerpt: Despite a promise to implement them at a greater rate, US President Donald Trump’s new global tariffs have already taken effect at a rate of 10%. The president announced he will implement a 10% global rate after the Supreme Court on Friday invalidated many of his broad import levies. The rate would be 15%, he added on Saturday. Official documents, however, state that the tariffs have been established at the lower amount as of Tuesday and that no direction to raise the rate has been issued. The White House has been approached by the BBC for a statement. A White House official told Reuters that the administration is working to revise the rate to 15% in light of Trump’s remarks, but they did not specify when the change may take effect. Investment bank ING analyst Carsten Brzeski stated, “I think it simply adds to the chaos and mess,” in reference to the rapidly shifting tariffs and how they affect companies.We’re back to where we were last year in terms of uncertainty,” he said on the BBC’s Today show, adding that there was now a greater chance of retaliation from the US’s trading partners.”Compared to last year, there is a much greater chance of a true, full-fledged tariff war, or trade war, escalation,” he stated. “Address fundamental international payments problems and continue the Administration’s work to rebalance our trade relationships to benefit American workers, farmers, and manufacturers” was the stated purpose of the temporary 10% import levy, which was signed by Trump on Friday. Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act, which permits the president to impose the tax for 150 days without congressional permission, is being used by the administration to implement the levy. title: When Remains are Discovered, Police Question how Sydney’s Grandfather was Abducted and Accidentally Killed
author: editor
excerpt: While searching for a Sydney grandpa who they suspect was accidentally abducted about two weeks ago, Australian police have discovered human remains. Just before dawn on February 13, widower Chris Baghsarian, 85, was seized by force from his North Ryde house. CCTV footage shows a group of masked men squeezing him into an SUV. According to local media, the intended target was a man who had ties to a well-known organized criminal family or his relatives, and police say the incident was most likely a case of mistaken identity. We’re all furious that an innocent individual might be the victim of this,” Det Acting Supt Andrew Marks stated on Tuesday. “I speak for not only the police but the public in general, we’re outraged by the recklessness of these people.” According to detectives, the next step in their investigation is to identify the remains and figure out how a regular granddad became the victim of a crime that might have been committed against a much younger gang member he didn’t even know. A dark SUV drew up on a residential street on a calm February morning, with sunrise more than an hour away and the skies still dark. CCTV showed multiple men exiting the vehicle and going into the residence, only to reappear moments later with a struggling man in their arms. Police issued the first of many frantic public pleas for Chris Baghsarian’s safe return about 36 hours after the kidnapping, revealing that he was the man who was taken. We’ll be adding to the market.”

Warner Bros agreed to Netflix’s bid to buy part of its properties last December, but Paramount has made a competing offer. Warner Bros. told Paramount last week that they had until the end of Monday to make their “best and final” bid before the shareholders vote on the Netflix acquisition next month.

Netflix has given Warner Bros. $27.75 per share, or $82.7 billion (£61.2 billion), for its studio and streaming networks, which include brands including HBO Max, Warner Bros., and New Line Cinema. The rest of the corporation will be spun off as a separate entity. Paramount’s $30 a share, or $108.4 billion, proposal is for the whole company, including its traditional pay-TV networks, which are thought to be a dying business.

Sarandos added that Paramount was “still trying to mess up” Netflix’s arrangement with Warner Bros.He added Netflix’s offer was better than Paramount’s because it would let them “buy assets we don’t have right now.

title: Wim Ouboter | Why Bigger Is Over and Smaller Wins the Future of Mobility
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In the late 1990s, long before micro-mobility became a global movement, Wim Ouboter was already imagining cities differently. Where others saw congestion and inefficiency as inevitable, he saw opportunity. Smaller vehicles. Shorter distances. Smarter design. Best known as the founder of Micro Mobility Systems, Ouboter sparked what many now call the micro revolution with the launch of the foldable scooter that became the Razor in the United States and the Micro Scooter across Europe and Asia. What began as a simple prototype tested on the streets of Zurich evolved into a worldwide phenomenon, transforming how people move through cities. Today, with the introduction of the Microlino, Ouboter is once again challenging conventional thinking. This time he is questioning why single-occupancy commuters need oversized SUVs for short urban trips. In this exclusive conversation, he reflects on his unconventional beginnings, breakthrough growth moments, and the mindset driving the next era of compact mobility. The Unconventional Beginning We began by asking, “Can you share your career journey and what led you to your current position?” “Having strong dyslexia, I was never a good student. But I had the vision to see things others could not see. My vision of urban mobility started in 1997 with a prototype that I was testing for several months. The outcome was a foldable mini scooter called RAZOR in the US and Micro Scooter in the rest of the world.” That early prototype did more than launch a product. It launched a movement and redefined short-distance transportation. Scaling a Global Revolution Continuing the discussion, we asked, “What was a key moment in your business journey that shaped your approach?” “In 1999 we went up from 500 workers to 15,000 workers in China to produce in three factories my idea of the Kickboard and the Micro Scooter. Seeing this volume with 80,000 Micro Scooters leaving every day the factory for the world was incredible.” This explosive growth marked a turning point. It proved global demand and reinforced his belief that bold ideas, when executed decisively, can scale at extraordinary speed. Strategy Over Routine Shifting focus to leadership, we asked, “How do you manage long-term goals while handling daily operations?” “I never focus on daily operations, only on strategic partnership with other companies.” For Ouboter, sustainable innovation depends less on micromanagement and more on alliances that amplify vision and accelerate execution. The Future of Urban Mobility Turning to the next five years, we asked, “What latest technologies or shifts do you think will change your industry?” “New mindset to think smaller. Microlino is the perfect product for downsizing and not using an SUV for every short trip with one person inside. We also call this the next ‘Tesla’ when it will come to disruption and market potential.” The philosophy is simple. Most urban journeys involve one person traveling a short distance. Designing vehicles accordingly is efficiency. Building a Culture of Momentum We then explored team leadership. “How do you encourage learning and growth within your team?” “Motivation, gratefulness, and a good salary beside a spirit that we can change the world to become a better place.” His leadership combines commercial realism with purpose, reinforcing the idea that innovation can create meaningful impact. A Defining Project When asked about a transformative initiative, he reflected on the evolution of his product ecosystem. “If you look into our Micro Brand Book, you will see our wide innovation for products. Now we concentrate on the Microlino in different varieties.” From scooters to kickboards to electric microcars, the trajectory reflects consistent commitment to compact mobility. Advice for Aspiring Entrepreneurs, we asked Wim Ouboter As the conversation concluded, we asked, “What advice would you give to aspiring entrepreneurs in your industry?” “Find strategic partners, go to market quick and include the media in your journey. Always have enough cash and take care of your liquidity as time can change.” It is pragmatic advice. Speed, visibility, and financial discipline form the foundation of sustainable innovation. Final Reflection Wim Ouboter’s journey demonstrates that transformative ideas often begin with simple observations. Most trips are short. Most cars are oversized. Most cities are overburdened. By thinking smaller, he built something bigger. A global micro-mobility movement that continues to reshape how the world navigates urban space. content:
In the late 1990s, long before micro-mobility became a global movement, Wim Ouboter was already imagining cities differently. Where others saw congestion and inefficiency as inevitable, he saw opportunity. Smaller vehicles. Shorter distances. Smarter design.

Best known as the founder of Micro Mobility Systems, Ouboter sparked what many now call the micro revolution with the launch of the foldable scooter that became the Razor in the United States and the Micro Scooter across Europe and Asia. What began as a simple prototype tested on the streets of Zurich evolved into a worldwide phenomenon, transforming how people move through cities.

Today, with the introduction of the Microlino, Ouboter is once again challenging conventional thinking. This time he is questioning why single-occupancy commuters need oversized SUVs for short urban trips. In this exclusive conversation, he reflects on his unconventional beginnings, breakthrough growth moments, and the mindset driving the next era of compact mobility.

The Unconventional Beginning

We began by asking, “Can you share your career journey and what led you to your current position?”

“Having strong dyslexia, I was never a good student. But I had the vision to see things others could not see. My vision of urban mobility started in 1997 with a prototype that I was testing for several months. The outcome was a foldable mini scooter called RAZOR in the US and Micro Scooter in the rest of the world.”

That early prototype did more than launch a product. It launched a movement and redefined short-distance transportation.

Scaling a Global Revolution

Continuing the discussion, we asked, “What was a key moment in your business journey that shaped your approach?”

“In 1999 we went up from 500 workers to 15,000 workers in China to produce in three factories my idea of the Kickboard and the Micro Scooter. Seeing this volume with 80,000 Micro Scooters leaving every day the factory for the world was incredible.”

This explosive growth marked a turning point. It proved global demand and reinforced his belief that bold ideas, when executed decisively, can scale at extraordinary speed.

Strategy Over Routine

Shifting focus to leadership, we asked, “How do you manage long-term goals while handling daily operations?”

“I never focus on daily operations, only on strategic partnership with other companies.”

For Ouboter, sustainable innovation depends less on micromanagement and more on alliances that amplify vision and accelerate execution.

The Future of Urban Mobility

Turning to the next five years, we asked, “What latest technologies or shifts do you think will change your industry?”

“New mindset to think smaller. Microlino is the perfect product for downsizing and not using an SUV for every short trip with one person inside. We also call this the next ‘Tesla’ when it will come to disruption and market potential.”

The philosophy is simple. Most urban journeys involve one person traveling a short distance. Designing vehicles accordingly is efficiency.

Building a Culture of Momentum

We then explored team leadership. “How do you encourage learning and growth within your team?”

“Motivation, gratefulness, and a good salary beside a spirit that we can change the world to become a better place.”

His leadership combines commercial realism with purpose, reinforcing the idea that innovation can create meaningful impact.

A Defining Project

When asked about a transformative initiative, he reflected on the evolution of his product ecosystem.

“If you look into our Micro Brand Book, you will see our wide innovation for products. Now we concentrate on the Microlino in different varieties.”

From scooters to kickboards to electric microcars, the trajectory reflects consistent commitment to compact mobility.

Advice for Aspiring Entrepreneurs, we asked Wim Ouboter

As the conversation concluded, we asked, “What advice would you give to aspiring entrepreneurs in your industry?”

“Find strategic partners, go to market quick and include the media in your journey. Always have enough cash and take care of your liquidity as time can change.”

It is pragmatic advice. Speed, visibility, and financial discipline form the foundation of sustainable innovation.

Final Reflection

Wim Ouboter’s journey demonstrates that transformative ideas often begin with simple observations. Most trips are short. Most cars are oversized. Most cities are overburdened.

By thinking smaller, he built something bigger. A global micro-mobility movement that continues to reshape how the world navigates urban space.

title: Willie Colón, a Trombone Who was a Pioneer in the Field of Salsa Music, Has Away at the Age of 75
author: editor
excerpt: Willie Colón, the trombonist and orchestra leader behind hits like El Malo, Oh, Qué Será, Talento de Televisión and Gitana died at the age of 75, according to US media. The Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter died peacefully on Saturday morning “surrounded by his loving family,” according to his family’s social media post. No cause of death was given. While we mourn his loss, we also celebrate the timeless gift of his music and the treasured memories he made, which will live on forever,” they wrote. Billboard magazine designated the Puerto Rican performer, who sung in Spanish and had a nearly 60-year career, as one of the most important Latino artists of all time. Colón’s death on Saturday was ascribed by US media to a Facebook statement shared by his family and a tribute written by his long-time manager, Pietro Carlos. Colón, an arranger and producer, addressed “the competing associations that Puerto Ricans have with their home and with the United States,” according to a biography provided on the Los Angeles Philharmonic website.He utilises his songs to represent and analyse the issues of living in the United States as a Puerto Rican, as well as to suggest the cultural contributions that Puerto Ricans have to offer. title: Trump Says he’ll Raise his New Worldwide Tariffs to 15%
author: editor
excerpt: US President Donald Trump has said that he will implement 15% global tariffs as he continues to criticise a Supreme Court decision that overturned his earlier import taxes. On Friday, Trump announced that he will replace the tariffs struck down by the court with a 10% duty on all goods entering the United States. However, on Saturday, he revealed on Truth Social that this would be extended to the maximum permitted by a never-used trade statute. The statute allows these new tariffs to remain in effect for around five months before the administration must seek congressional permission. The 10% tariffs were supposed to go into effect on Tuesday, February 24. It is uncertain whether the higher 15% would be enforced starting then. The BBC called the White House. The new 15% tax rate, a temporary remedy under Section 122 of the 1974 Trade Act, creates concerns for countries such as the United Kingdom and Australia, which had agreed to a 10% tariff accord with the US. title: As the Deadline Approaches, EU Countries Continue to Clash on Further Penalties Against Russia
author: editor
excerpt: Following a Friday meeting in which ambassadors failed to reach an agreement, the European Union’s next wave of sanctions against Russia remains uncertain. The clock is running out: the bloc has set the ratification deadline for February 24th, which is also the fourth anniversary of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The primary point of disagreement, according to officials with knowledge of the process, is a complete prohibition on Russian oil tanker maritime services, which, if implemented, would end the price cap set by the Group of Seven (G7) in late 2022. Brussels has determined that the cap, now set at $44.10 a barrel, is no longer meeting expectations and that further pressure is urgently needed to undermine the oil profits the Kremlin depends on to fund the war machine. EU businesses would be prohibited from offering any services, including banking, insurance, shipping, or catering, to ships transporting Russian petroleum under the proposed prohibition. The intention is to reduce earnings and raise transportation expenses. Greece and Malta, two nations with significant maritime industries, fear that enacting a complete ban would hurt their own economies, encourage competition from China and India, and strengthen Russia’s “shadow fleet,” which consists of deteriorating ships that Moscow uses to circumvent Western regulations. title: Is Manufacturing in the Eurozone at a Turning Point? PMI Reaches a 44-Month Peak
author: editor
excerpt: According to a widely followed business survey published on Friday, manufacturing in the Eurozone has returned to expansion territory for the first time in months, hitting its highest level since June 2022. According to statistics gathered by S&P Global and Hamburg Commercial Bank, the flash Eurozone Manufacturing PMI increased to 50.8 points in February from 49.5 points in January, marking a 44-month high. The result surpassed the 50-point barrier that distinguishes contraction from expansion and surpassed market expectations. The total private sector activity in the euro area is still growing at a moderate rate, as indicated by the rise in the broader composite index, which combines manufacturing and services, from 51.3 to 51.9. Due to tighter financial conditions, increased energy prices, and weak global demand, manufacturing has hampered eurozone growth for the most of the last two years. The recovery in February might signal a change. Given that the headline PMI rose to growth territory, this might mark a sea change for the manufacturing sector, according to Dr. Cyrus de la Rubia, chief economist at Hamburg Commercial Bank. Although the underlying fundamentals seem more stable than during past brief upturns, the economist cautioned that it might be too soon to declare a full recovery. content:
According to a widely followed business survey published on Friday, manufacturing in the Eurozone has returned to expansion territory for the first time in months, hitting its highest level since June 2022.

According to statistics gathered by S&P Global and Hamburg Commercial Bank, the flash Eurozone Manufacturing PMI increased to 50.8 points in February from 49.5 points in January, marking a 44-month high.

The result surpassed the 50-point barrier that distinguishes contraction from expansion and surpassed market expectations. The total private sector activity in the euro area is still growing at a moderate rate, as indicated by the rise in the broader composite index, which combines manufacturing and services, from 51.3 to 51.9.

Due to tighter financial conditions, increased energy prices, and weak global demand, manufacturing has hampered eurozone growth for the most of the last two years. The recovery in February might signal a change.

Given that the headline PMI rose to growth territory, this might mark a sea change for the manufacturing sector, according to Dr. Cyrus de la Rubia, chief economist at Hamburg Commercial Bank. Although the underlying fundamentals seem more stable than during past brief upturns, the economist cautioned that it might be too soon to declare a full recovery.

title: Hollywood is in a Panic Over the Chinese AI App
author: editor
excerpt: Hollywood was astonished this week by a new artificial intelligence (AI) model created by the Chinese company that created TikTok, not only because of its potential applications but also because of its potential implications for the creative industries. With just a few written instructions, Seedance 2.0, developed by IT behemoth ByteDance, can produce cinema-quality video with sound effects and dialogue. Numerous clips that featured well-known characters like Spider-Man and Deadpool and were allegedly created with Seedance went viral. ByteDance was swiftly accused of copyright infringement by major companies like Disney and Paramount, but worries about the technology go beyond simple legal considerations. Although Seedance was introduced in June 2025 with little notice, the second iteration, which was released eight months later, has generated a lot of controversy.I don’t think this is helpful for AI for the first time. Rather, this appears to be taken directly from an actual production process, according to Jan-Willem Blom of the creative firm Videostate. He continues by saying that while Western AI video models have advanced in processing user commands to create beautiful images, Seedance appears to have brought everything together. Seedance can produce films from brief text cues, just like Midjourney and OpenAI’s Sora. In certain instances, a single prompt appears to be creating excellent videos. According to AI ethics expert Margaret Mitchell, it is especially remarkable because it integrates text, images, and voice into a single system. title: Goar Sekhian Sanfilippo: The Sensory Visionary Behind Perfume Art Creation
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Redefining Contemporary Art Through Scent, Memory, and Human Experience In a contemporary art world dominated by visual immediacy, Goar Sekhian Sanfilippo introduces a concept that invites audiences to slow down and feel. As the founder of Perfume Art Creation, she has developed a multisensory artistic model that integrates fragrance into visual artworks, transforming observation into personal memory. With galleries in Zollikerberg, Venice, and Paris, Goar’s journey reflects the convergence of artistic intuition and international discipline. In this exclusive interview, she shares the origins of her concept, the evolution of her gallery, and the philosophy guiding her vision. The Early Influences We began the conversation by asking, “Could you share a bit about your early background, education, and the key experiences that shaped your career journey?” “My early background was shaped by two parallel influences: creativity and international exposure. From childhood, I was immersed in artistic expression and the sensory world of fragrance. Art was never something external to my life; it was a natural language of emotion and identity. Professionally, my path initially followed a different direction. For nearly two decades, I built my career in international trade. This experience profoundly shaped me. It taught me discipline, strategic thinking, negotiation, and the importance of cultural nuance. Working across borders refined my ability to connect different worlds — economically, culturally, and personally. Perfumed Art emerged at the intersection of these two dimensions. In many ways, it represents the convergence of analytical rigor and emotional depth.” The Evolution of the Gallery Continuing the discussion, we asked, “How has your company evolved since its inception?” “Since its inception, the gallery has evolved through both challenges and strong convictions. As a young gallery, we navigated limited recognition from critics and complex experiences within the art world. These challenges strengthened our commitment to integrity and long-term dedication to artists. From the beginning, we have been deeply selective, placing human values and artistic authenticity at the center of our development. We support artists not only for their talent, but also for their professionalism and personal integrity. In 2018, I founded Perfume Art Creation Gallery in Zollikerberg near Zurich. The gallery expanded to Venice in 2022 and Paris in 2023. Each expansion was intentional and reflective of the cultural identity of the region.” Contribution to Regional Ecosystems Exploring the gallery’s broader impact, we asked, “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?” “Our contribution is always shaped by the identity and environment of each location. In Zollikerberg, surrounded by protected green landscapes, we developed a palette of local olfactory identities inspired by the region — forest amber, tomato leaf, peony, fresh grass, and cut wood. These fragrances resonate with collective memory and strengthen cultural identity. In Venice, our artistic direction reflects the tonalities of the canals and the interplay of water and light. We operate primarily by appointment, limiting excessive visitor flow and supporting a respectful rhythm within the historic district. In Paris, located near the Eiffel Tower within Village Suisse, we are part of a cultural micro-ecosystem of contemporary and antique galleries. This environment fosters collaboration and reinforces artistic community. Across all locations, we integrate artistic excellence with environmental awareness and community engagement.” Qualities for Success Shifting the focus to leadership, we asked, “What three qualities do you believe are critical for success in your industry?” “In our industry, three qualities are essential: vision, discernment, and integrity. Vision is fundamental. Perfumed Art is an unconventional concept that required courage to develop beyond established formats. Discernment ensures excellence. The strength of a gallery depends on the authenticity and coherence of its artists. Integrity sustains credibility over time. Trust with artists and collectors is built through consistency, professionalism, and loyalty to one’s values.” Innovation and Adaptation Turning to innovation, we asked, “How has your organization adapted to technological changes? Could you share a key innovation you’ve implemented?” “Perfume Art Creation is primarily an intellectual and experiential innovation rather than a technological one. Our adaptation lies in integrating contemporary understanding of perception and olfaction into the artistic experience. Our key innovation is the development of perfumed art — artworks that combine visual expression with carefully composed fragrance. By engaging both sight and smell, we create a deeper interaction with the artwork. From a technical perspective, we research fabrics and materials compatible with fragrance diffusion to ensure aesthetic quality and durability. We also conduct fragrance creation workshops, allowing participants to design their own scents and transform from spectators into active creators.” Navigating Challenges As the interview drew deeper into the realities of the art world, we asked, “How would you guide someone to navigate the key challenges you faced when establishing yourself in this industry?” “I would emphasize originality, resilience, and collaboration. Innovation requires courage. One of the major challenges I faced was seeing original concepts imitated. Ideas can be copied, but vision cannot. A copied concept rarely evolves with the same coherence because it is not rooted in authentic identity. Resilience is essential. Behind elegant exhibitions lies a demanding reality that requires emotional strength and clarity. Trust can be fragile, and navigating artistic relationships requires maturity. Finally, I encourage collaboration over conflict. The public recognizes authenticity and consistency. In the long term, integrity and high standards always reinforce credibility.” Final Reflection Before concluding, we asked, “What final message would you like to share with emerging entrepreneurs and creatives?” “I would advise them to protect their vision and refine their quality continuously. True innovation grows from within and evolves over time. When your concept is deeply aligned with your identity, it cannot be equaled. Remain resilient, stay open to collaboration, and never compromise your integrity. Creativity flourishes where discipline and authenticity meet.” Connect with Goar Sekhian Sanfilippo on LinkedIn to explore her artistic vision and follow her journey in redefining contemporary art through scent and sensory experience. Visit Perfume Art Creation at https://www.perfumeart.ch/ to learn more about the gallery’s presence in Zollikerberg, Venice, and Paris, and discover the world of perfumed art. Also Read :- Human

In a contemporary art world dominated by visual immediacy, Goar Sekhian Sanfilippo introduces a concept that invites audiences to slow down and feel. As the founder of Perfume Art Creation, she has developed a multisensory artistic model that integrates fragrance into visual artworks, transforming observation into personal memory.

With galleries in Zollikerberg, Venice, and Paris, Goar’s journey reflects the convergence of artistic intuition and international discipline. In this exclusive interview, she shares the origins of her concept, the evolution of her gallery, and the philosophy guiding her vision.

The Early Influences

We began the conversation by asking, “Could you share a bit about your early background, education, and the key experiences that shaped your career journey?”

“My early background was shaped by two parallel influences: creativity and international exposure. From childhood, I was immersed in artistic expression and the sensory world of fragrance. Art was never something external to my life; it was a natural language of emotion and identity.

Professionally, my path initially followed a different direction. For nearly two decades, I built my career in international trade. This experience profoundly shaped me. It taught me discipline, strategic thinking, negotiation, and the importance of cultural nuance. Working across borders refined my ability to connect different worlds — economically, culturally, and personally.

Perfumed Art emerged at the intersection of these two dimensions. In many ways, it represents the convergence of analytical rigor and emotional depth.”

The Evolution of the Gallery

Continuing the discussion, we asked, “How has your company evolved since its inception?”

“Since its inception, the gallery has evolved through both challenges and strong convictions. As a young gallery, we navigated limited recognition from critics and complex experiences within the art world. These challenges strengthened our commitment to integrity and long-term dedication to artists.

From the beginning, we have been deeply selective, placing human values and artistic authenticity at the center of our development. We support artists not only for their talent, but also for their professionalism and personal integrity.

In 2018, I founded Perfume Art Creation Gallery in Zollikerberg near Zurich. The gallery expanded to Venice in 2022 and Paris in 2023. Each expansion was intentional and reflective of the cultural identity of the region.”

Contribution to Regional Ecosystems

Exploring the gallery’s broader impact, we asked, “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?”

“Our contribution is always shaped by the identity and environment of each location.

In Zollikerberg, surrounded by protected green landscapes, we developed a palette of local olfactory identities inspired by the region — forest amber, tomato leaf, peony, fresh grass, and cut wood. These fragrances resonate with collective memory and strengthen cultural identity.

In Venice, our artistic direction reflects the tonalities of the canals and the interplay of water and light. We operate primarily by appointment, limiting excessive visitor flow and supporting a respectful rhythm within the historic district.

In Paris, located near the Eiffel Tower within Village Suisse, we are part of a cultural micro-ecosystem of contemporary and antique galleries. This environment fosters collaboration and reinforces artistic community. Across all locations, we integrate artistic excellence with environmental awareness and community engagement.”

Qualities for Success

Shifting the focus to leadership, we asked, “What three qualities do you believe are critical for success in your industry?”

“In our industry, three qualities are essential: vision, discernment, and integrity.

Vision is fundamental. Perfumed Art is an unconventional concept that required courage to develop beyond established formats.

Discernment ensures excellence. The strength of a gallery depends on the authenticity and coherence of its artists.

Integrity sustains credibility over time. Trust with artists and collectors is built through consistency, professionalism, and loyalty to one’s values.”

Innovation and Adaptation

Turning to innovation, we asked, “How has your organization adapted to technological changes? Could you share a key innovation you’ve implemented?”

“Perfume Art Creation is primarily an intellectual and experiential innovation rather than a technological one. Our adaptation lies in integrating contemporary understanding of perception and olfaction into the artistic experience.

Our key innovation is the development of perfumed art — artworks that combine visual expression with carefully composed fragrance. By engaging both sight and smell, we create a deeper interaction with the artwork.

From a technical perspective, we research fabrics and materials compatible with fragrance diffusion to ensure aesthetic quality and durability. We also conduct fragrance creation workshops, allowing participants to design their own scents and transform from spectators into active creators.”

Navigating Challenges

As the interview drew deeper into the realities of the art world, we asked, “How would you guide someone to navigate the key challenges you faced when establishing yourself in this industry?”

“I would emphasize originality, resilience, and collaboration.

Innovation requires courage. One of the major challenges I faced was seeing original concepts imitated. Ideas can be copied, but vision cannot. A copied concept rarely evolves with the same coherence because it is not rooted in authentic identity.

Resilience is essential. Behind elegant exhibitions lies a demanding reality that requires emotional strength and clarity. Trust can be fragile, and navigating artistic relationships requires maturity.

Finally, I encourage collaboration over conflict. The public recognizes authenticity and consistency. In the long term, integrity and high standards always reinforce credibility.”

Final Reflection

Before concluding, we asked, “What final message would you like to share with emerging entrepreneurs and creatives?”

“I would advise them to protect their vision and refine their quality continuously. True innovation grows from within and evolves over time. When your concept is deeply aligned with your identity, it cannot be equaled.

Remain resilient, stay open to collaboration, and never compromise your integrity. Creativity flourishes where discipline and authenticity meet.”

title: Australian Host says Sorry for Drinking Before Giving a Garbled Report on the Olympics
author: editor
excerpt: After a video of an Australian sports presenter slurring her way through a live cross from the Winter Olympics in Italy went viral, even the prime minister of Australia spoke out. Danika Mason, a reporter for Channel Nine, said she had “misjudged the situation” by drinking before going on live TV. She also blamed the altitude, the cold, and not eating dinner.”I want to take full responsibility; it’s not the standard I set for myself,” she stated again the next day, adding that she was “embarrassed.” Anthony Albanese, the Prime Minister, claimed he was “pro-Danika” and that there was “nothing to see here,” which made it sound like she had jet lag. As she talked about the sports events of the day, Mason stumbled over her words and talked about iguanas and the cost of coffee.The price of coffee here is good; it’s the price of coffee in the US that we’ll have to get used to. “I’m not sure about the iguanas. Where are we going with that one?” she asked on her trip to the breakfast TV show Today on Wednesday, reportedly in response to comments from the studio hosts. author: editor
excerpt: Les Wexner, a billionaire from the US, has said that he was “naive, foolish, and gullible” for believing Jeffrey Epstein, who is said to have helped him build his wealth. title: Uzbekistan and the US Make their Joint Investment Plan Official in Washington
author: editor
excerpt: During meetings in Washington, US officials and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the start of a collaborative investment platform between Uzbekistan and the US. President Donald Trump invited Mirziyoyev to Washington, D.C. to attend the first meeting of the Board of Peace, which is Trump’s diplomatic effort to help Gaza. Earlier this year, Uzbekistan signed the body’s founding declaration at the World Economic Forum in Davos. In the last few years, the two countries have worked together more on economic issues. Last year, trade between the two countries was worth more than $1 billion (€850 million), and about 340 US companies do business in Uzbekistan. At the end of discussions with the heads of the Export-Import Bank of the United States and the US International Development Finance Corporation, the agreement that set up the Uzbekistan–US Investment Platform was officially signed. The framework is meant to give systemic support to important projects and improve communication between Uzbek officials, US development banks, and private investors. In the plan, Eximbank is supposed to give more money to big industrial and infrastructural projects, as well as help with exports of high-tech equipment. Talks with the DFC were mostly about strengthening investment collaboration and the company’s aspirations to take part in big national and regional initiatives, especially in developing the energy and financial markets. title: Things are Still Tense Toy Companies are Watching the US Supreme Court as Tariffs Hurt Profitability
author: editor
excerpt: Recently, the toy industry held its biggest annual convention in New York City. The head of a tiny company stood out from the crowd and was hailed by other business owners like a minor celebrity. Rick Woldenberg, the chief executive of Learning Resources, helped make headlines last year, when he took the White House to court, challenging Donald Trump’s sweeping global tariffs on imports from countries around the world. Many people in the US are expecting to move on from the effects of the tariffs, which have caused price increases and profit losses, as Trump’s quick-fire trade statements have slowed down this year. But the folks who stopped by Woldenberg’s booth showed how many businesses are still on edge because of uncertainties about trade policies. On Friday, the Supreme Court could make a decision about his case.”People have been coming to thank us for standing up,” Woldenberg added, pointing to a display of toy animals and building blocks. Last year, Trump’s messy rollout of tariffs turned the corporate world upside down. At one point, tariffs on Chinese imports reached 145%. The new import levies hit the toy business hard because it relies on China for a lot of its manufacturing. Many companies saw their expenses go up. Many companies hiked prices to help pay for the tariffs, which hurt their profitability. Woldenberg even embarked on a court battle, filing a lawsuit against the administration. But in several areas, the effects of the measures have been less severe than expected, notably for consumers. title: Looking on the Bright Side, a Latvian Minister Thinks the EU Ought to Advance Ukraine’s Defence and Assistance more Quickly
author: editor
excerpt: Latvia’s defence minister told Euronews that Europe’s reaction to Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has been uneven, and he urged the bloc to act more quickly on collective defence and sanctions as the invasion’s fourth anniversary approaches. “While there is broad principled agreement within the EU and NATO on the need to back Ukraine, delivery has not always matched ambition,” Andris Spruds told Euronews on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference, rejecting claims that Europe has failed Ukraine four years into the conflict. In terms of tenacity, motivation, common values and interests, and policy support for Ukraine, he stated, “The glass is half full.” “Where the glass might be a bit half empty, it is in the volumes and speed of the implementation.” Following Washington’s decision last year to halt all financial and military aid to the war-torn nation, Europe is by far the largest donor to Ukraine and is mostly anticipated to stay that way. Over the next two years, the group pledged to provide €90 billion for Ukraine’s needs. In addition, the EU is now debating its 20th set of sanctions on Russia, which it believes will be approved by February 24, the fourth anniversary of the conflict. The package’s primary component, which was proposed by the European Commission earlier this month, is a complete prohibition on maritime services with the goal of further undermining Russia’s energy earnings. In terms of tenacity, motivation, common values and interests, and policy support for Ukraine, he stated, “The glass is half full.” “Where the glass might be a bit half empty, it is in the volumes and speed of the implementation.” Following Washington’s decision last year to halt all financial and military aid to the war-torn nation, Europe is by far the largest donor to Ukraine and is mostly anticipated to stay that way. Over the next two years, the group pledged to provide €90 billion for Ukraine’s needs.

In addition, the EU is now debating its 20th set of sanctions on Russia, which it believes will be approved by February 24, the fourth anniversary of the conflict. The package’s primary component, which was proposed by the European Commission earlier this month, is a complete prohibition on maritime services with the goal of further undermining Russia’s energy earnings.

title: In 2028, Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte Plans to Run for President
author: editor
excerpt: Sara Duterte, the vice president of the Philippines, has announced her intention to run for president in the 2028 election. The declaration was made by the 47-year-old as she and incumbent President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. are engaged in a sour power battle. Candidates in the Philippines’ primarily personality-based elections are known to train for years before the presidential election, which is two years away. Marcos cannot run for reelection, and his supporters have not yet put up a candidate to fight Duterte, who is also the daughter of former President Rodrigo Duterte. The vice president declared, “I offer my life, my strength, and my future in the service of our nation.”My name is Sara Duterte. I’m going to run for Philippine president.” In the 2022 election, Marcos and Duterte ran on the same ticket and won handily. However, since they pursued different political objectives, the coalition quickly fell apart. When Marcos permitted the International Criminal Court to arrest Sara’s father in March 2025, the conflict erupted in a spectacular way. As he awaits prosecution for crimes against humanity related to his brutal war on drugs, the elder Duterte is currently being held in The Hague. Two months later, candidates backed by the Duterte family defeated those nominated by Marcos in a midterm legislative vote that was interpreted as a gauge of support for the current administration. A little more than a week ago, the vice president was the target of an impeachment complaint from Catholic clergy members for alleged corruption, which she denies.
