content:
A multilingual lawyer with extensive expertise in various fields of law, Dr. Csilla Rostas has built her career through a unique blend of international experience and a passion for helping others. With a rich background in the legal landscape, Dr. Csilla specializes in business immigration law and is a member of ITALAWYERS, the first association of Italian and Italian-speaking lawyers in the world.

Spark Behind The Journey

We started the interview by asking, “What inspired you to start your business, and what vision drives it this day?”

Dr. Csilla Rostas shared, “My inspiration to start my own business stems from my personal journey and experiences living in multiple countries. As someone who has lived in Italy, France, Belgium and now Germany, I’ve witnessed firsthand the challenges and complexities that come with moving abroad. These experiences sparked a deep passion in me to help individuals who are facing similar challenges, as well as companies expanding internationally.

My vision for my work has always been to create a space where expats can find not just legal expertise, but also a sense of support and understanding. I am driven by the idea of making the immigration process more accessible, transparent, and less daunting for people from all walks of life. In the international environments I’ve worked in, I’ve developed a strong appreciation for cultural diversity, and that fuels my dedication to assisting individuals who are building their lives in new countries.

Ultimately, I want my business to be more than just a legal service; I want it to be a trusted partner for people as they navigate new territories, ensuring that their legal matters are in good hands so they can focus on building a future in their new home.”

Adaptability To Tech-Driven Innovations

To learn more about the impact of technology in the business of Dr. Csilla Rostas, we asked, “How do you use technology to drive innovation and efficiency in your company?”

“In today’s digital age, technology plays a crucial role in enhancing both innovation and efficiency, especially in a field like immigration law, where timelines and documentation are key. I use a variety of tools to streamline the process, reduce paperwork, and improve communication with clients.  

Additionally, I use automated workflows and legal management software to help manage cases, ensuring that no deadlines are missed and that all documentation is up-to-date. This system allows me to focus on providing personalized advice rather than getting bogged down in administrative tasks. I also use video conferencing and digital communication tools to stay connected with clients across different time zones, making it easier for them to reach out, no matter where they are. 

With clients from various parts of the world, technology allows me to maintain an international reach while providing tailored, timely support. By integrating technology into every aspect of my work, I can deliver a more efficient and effective service to my clients, while also staying ahead of trends and continuously innovating in a fast-changing legal landscape.” She responded.

Empowering Growth Among The Team

Eager to understand Dr. Csilla Rostas’ view on the team’s growth, we asked her to share her strategies for fostering a culture of continuous learning and growth within the team.

Dr. Csilla Rostas explained, “Fostering a culture of continuous learning and growth is something I take very seriously, because the legal landscape, especially in immigration law, is constantly evolving. I encourage an open and collaborative environment where everyone feels empowered to share new insights, ask questions, and challenge conventional thinking. I prioritize regular training sessions on changes in immigration policies, and new technological tools that can improve our work. Whether it’s through webinars, conferences, or knowledge-sharing meetings, we ensure that our collaborators are always learning and staying updated.

I promote mentorship, where more experienced colleagues can guide junior colleagues. This creates a supportive learning environment where everyone has the opportunity to grow both professionally and personally. I aim to inspire a team that is agile, motivated, and always striving to deliver the best possible service to our clients.”

Staying Ahead Of  The Curve

We also asked, “What strategies help you stay competitive in a speedy-changing market?”

“Staying competitive in a fast-changing market, especially in immigration law, requires both adaptability and a proactive approach. One key strategy I focus on is staying ahead of legal and policy changes. Immigration law is constantly evolving, and I make it a priority to monitor new regulations, international agreements, and global trends that could affect my clients. This allows me to quickly adjust our strategies and provide up-to-date advice. Another crucial strategy is embracing technology.

By integrating the latest legal tech tools, I can increase efficiency and offer a more streamlined service. This not only improves the client experience but also allows us to scale our operations without sacrificing quality. I also keep a strong focus on building lasting relationships with clients. In a world full of options, personal connections and trust are irreplaceable. I ensure that I am accessible, responsive, and empathetic, which differentiates us from competitors who may not prioritize the human side of service.  

Finally, I invest in continuous professional development. Whether it’s attending global conferences or staying informed about industry best practices, I ensure that I am always at the cutting edge of legal knowledge and client service. By being adaptable, leveraging technology, building strong relationships, and committing to learning, I can stay competitive and provide exceptional value to my clients, even in a fast-paced, ever-changing market.” She replied.

An Impactful Project

We were interested to learn about a project that marked a turning point for Dr. Csilla Rostas and her business. So, we asked, “Can you highlight a project or initiative that made a significant impact on your company?”

“One of the most impactful initiatives has been the development of a strong, international network of legal professionals and collaborations with global companies. Over the years, I’ve built relationships with professionals around the world, allowing me to offer my clients not just expertise, but a truly international perspective. This network has been instrumental in providing comprehensive, cross-border solutions for my clients, especially in cases where they need guidance in multiple jurisdictions.  

Additionally, my involvement with the amazing Filipino community has played a key role in growing my reputation. Word of mouth within tight-knit communities like this has been invaluable in expanding my client base. By offering tailored services that speak to the unique needs of expats, particularly those facing complex immigration matters, I’ve been able to establish trust and become a go-to resource for many immigrants seeking legal support in Europe. These initiatives have significantly boosted my visibility, and the trust I’ve earned through personal connections and community engagement has had a ripple effect, leading to referrals and new business opportunities. It’s a reminder that building genuine relationships and offering tailored services is a powerful way to make a lasting impact.” She explained.

Adaptability Amidst A Dynamic Industry

We further asked, “How do you ensure your business remains agile and adaptable to industry changes?”

“Ensuring that my business remains agile and adaptable is a priority, especially in the ever-changing field of immigration law. One of the key ways I maintain this flexibility is by continuous learning. I actively stay updated on legal reforms, emerging trends, and evolving policies, which allows me to anticipate changes rather than react to them. This proactive approach ensures I’m always prepared to adapt my services to meet new challenges head-on. I also maintain flexibility in how I engage with clients.  

By creating customizable solutions based on each client’s unique needs, I can quickly pivot my approach when required. This has proven especially important when working with clients from various backgrounds, as immigration policies differ not only across countries but also within regions. Finally, I focus on strong relationships with both clients and professional partners. Staying connected with other legal professionals, businesses, and communities helps me understand shifting dynamics and opens doors to new opportunities. This constant feedback loop from clients and colleagues helps me identify early signs of change and respond effectively.” Dr. Csilla reflected.

Envisioning The Future

To learn more about her professional visions, we asked her to share her short-term and long-term goals, and how she plans to achieve them.

Dr. Csilla Rostas added, “In the short term, my goal is to further strengthen my global partnerships and expand my collaborations with other legal professionals, international companies, and organizations. By building a network of trusted partners across multiple regions, I want to ensure that I can offer even more comprehensive, seamless support for clients who have cross-border immigration needs. This means deeper relationships with other lawyers, consultants, and businesses in key markets, and continuing to build my firm as a reliable, international immigration law firm.

In the long term, I envision positioning my work as a go-to resource for expats and immigrants on a global scale. I want to make sure that no matter where my clients are coming from or where they are going, they can rely on our expertise to navigate the complexities of immigration law. A major part of this long-term vision is expanding my international presence and collaborating with legal professionals and organizations in emerging markets so that I can offer tailored services for a more diverse clientele. I also see the potential to develop educational resources and workshops to further empower expats with the knowledge they need to succeed in their new countries.

To achieve these goals, I will continue to make my services even more accessible across borders. I also participate in global conferences and forums to stay connected with industry leaders and stay ahead of market trends. By maintaining a strong focus on building meaningful relationships, staying adaptable, and investing in professional growth, I’m confident that both short-term and long-term objectives will be realized.”

Words Of Wisdom For Beginners

Addressing the beginners in her field, we posed the question, “What advice would you give to aspiring entrepreneurs looking to make an impact?”

Dr. Csilla Rostas responded, “My advice to aspiring entrepreneurs would be to focus on what truly drives you, find a cause or area where you can bring both passion and expertise. Building a business isn’t just about creating a product or service, it’s about making a difference in people’s lives. Whether you’re in a niche market or a more general one, aim to deliver real value to your customers and clients and the impact will follow. Another key piece of advice is to build strong relationships from the start. Surround yourself with people who believe in your vision, whether that’s mentors, peers, or collaborators.

As an entrepreneur, you won’t be able to succeed alone, so it’s important to build a network that supports, challenges, and inspires you. In my case, my international network of legal professionals has been crucial in helping me grow and stay adaptable in a fast-changing industry. Also, be prepared for the ups and downs. Entrepreneurship is rarely a straight path, and it’s easy to get discouraged. Resilience is key. Embrace failure as part of the learning process and keep an open mind to change and growth. Always stay grounded in your core values.

Finally, don’t underestimate the importance of technology and innovation. Even in a traditional field like law, embracing new tools can unlock efficiency, streamline operations, and make it easier to reach your audience. Always look for ways to improve your processes, keep learning, and stay curious about how to do things better. In short, be passionate, build relationships, embrace failure, and stay open to innovation. If you can do these things, you’ll be well on your way to making a meaningful impact.”

excerpt: This collection of insights highlights the journey from engineer to executive leader, emphasizing the importance of strategic growth, adaptability, and leadership in a dynamic world. It explores Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, showcasing the private sector’s role in economic diversification, sustainability, and long-term planning. Finally, it underscores how visionary leadership and resilience are key to thriving in an ever-changing global landscape. My Journey to the Executive Level My Perspective on Growing from Engineer to Executive Leader: I began my career as an electrical engineer, working hands-on in the field where I developed a strong technical foundation and a deep understanding of operational challenges. Early on, I realized the importance of aligning technical execution with business strategy, which sparked my interest in leadership and management. Over time, I took on roles with increasing responsibility—moving from engineering to service management, and then into broader operational leadership positions. Each role expanded my perspective, allowing me to lead diverse teams, manage P&Ls, and drive performance across multiple business units. I consistently focused on growth, innovation, and delivering value, which led to my progression into executive leadership. I now lead strategic direction, drive organizational development, and focus on long-term planning. My journey has been fueled by a passion for problem-solving, continuous learning, and empowering teams to achieve meaningful results. Driving Economic Growth The Role of Saudi Private Sector Companies in Vision 2030’s Economic Diversification’s Key Contributions of the Private Sector: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 emphasizes the pivotal role of the private sector in diversifying the nation’s economy and reducing its reliance on oil revenues. The plan aims to increase the private sector’s contribution to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) from 40% to 65%. Economic Diversification: Private enterprises are central to expanding non-oil sectors, with non-oil economic activities accounting for 52% of the total economy. Employment Generation: The private sector has significantly increased employment opportunities for Saudi nationals, contributing to a rise in women’s participation in the workforce to 35.8% in the second quarter of 2024. Support for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs): Recognizing the importance of SMEs, Vision 2030 aims to increase their contribution to GDP from 20% to 35%, facilitating entrepreneurship and innovation. Attracting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI): Private sector initiatives have led to increased FDI, with nearly 600 global companies choosing Saudi Arabia as their regional headquarters, reflecting growing investor confidence. Privatization Initiatives: Key sectors such as healthcare, education, transport, and municipal services are targeted for privatization, opening avenues for private investment and enhancing service quality. Infrastructure Development: The private sector is actively involved in infrastructure projects, with investments expected to reach approximately $1 trillion by 2030, supporting economic diversification and long-term objectives. Government Initiatives Supporting the Private Sector: Shareek Program: Launched in 2021, this program supports large Saudi companies by enabling private sector investments and contributing to economic development. Privatization Program: Initiated in 2018, this program focuses on identifying government assets for privatization to improve service quality and reduce costs. National Transformation Program: This program aims to create an inclusive private sector that prioritizes financial security and promotes digitization of government services. In summary, the active participation and investment of the private sector are crucial for achieving Vision 2030’s economic diversification goals, steering Saudi Arabia towards a more resilient and multifaceted economy. Future-Proofing Success The Importance of Long-Term Vision in Building Sustainable Businesses: In Saudi Arabia, several strategic initiatives reflect the importance of long-term vision. For example: NEOM, the $500 billion giga-project, is being developed as a smart, sustainable city that will rely entirely on renewable energy, aiming to attract global talent and industries of the future. The Saudi Green Initiative underscores environmental sustainability by targeting the planting of 10 billion trees and generating 50% of the country’s energy from renewables by 2030 — a shift that requires private sector alignment with long-term ESG strategies. The Public Investment Fund (PIF) has been expanding investments into sectors like tourism, logistics, and entertainment, aiming to increase non-oil revenues and create sustainable industries for generations to come. Sustainable business models also help companies weather market cycles, manage risks more effectively, and attract long-term investors and talent. In today’s rapidly changing global environment — where technology, regulation, and stakeholder expectations are evolving — short-term thinking can lead to missed opportunities or even business failure. Therefore, organizations that embed long-term vision into their operations, innovation, and governance structures are better positioned to drive consistent value, maintain stakeholder trust, and contribute to national development goals. Adaptive Leadership The Key to Leadership in a Rapidly Changing World: Leadership in today’s world demands far more than authority or experience — it requires agility, vision, and empathy. The pace of change driven by technology, globalization, and shifting societal expectations means that leaders must be proactive, adaptable, and continuously learning. It explores Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, showcasing the private sector’s role in economic diversification, sustainability, and long-term planning. Finally, it underscores how visionary leadership and resilience are key to thriving in an ever-changing global landscape.

My Journey to the Executive Level

My Perspective on Growing from Engineer to Executive Leader: I began my career as an electrical engineer, working hands-on in the field where I developed a strong technical foundation and a deep understanding of operational challenges. Early on, I realized the importance of aligning technical execution with business strategy, which sparked my interest in leadership and management.

Over time, I took on roles with increasing responsibility—moving from engineering to service management, and then into broader operational leadership positions. Each role expanded my perspective, allowing me to lead diverse teams, manage P&Ls, and drive performance across multiple business units. I consistently focused on growth, innovation, and delivering value, which led to my progression into executive leadership.

I now lead strategic direction, drive organizational development, and focus on long-term planning. My journey has been fueled by a passion for problem-solving, continuous learning, and empowering teams to achieve meaningful results.

Driving Economic Growth

The Role of Saudi Private Sector Companies in Vision 2030’s Economic Diversification’s Key Contributions of the Private Sector:

Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 emphasizes the pivotal role of the private sector in diversifying the nation’s economy and reducing its reliance on oil revenues. The plan aims to increase the private sector’s contribution to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) from 40% to 65%.

  1. Economic Diversification: Private enterprises are central to expanding non-oil sectors, with non-oil economic activities accounting for 52% of the total economy.
  2. Employment Generation: The private sector has significantly increased employment opportunities for Saudi nationals, contributing to a rise in women’s participation in the workforce to 35.8% in the second quarter of 2024.
  3. Support for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs): Recognizing the importance of SMEs, Vision 2030 aims to increase their contribution to GDP from 20% to 35%, facilitating entrepreneurship and innovation.
  4. Attracting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI): Private sector initiatives have led to increased FDI, with nearly 600 global companies choosing Saudi Arabia as their regional headquarters, reflecting growing investor confidence.
  5. Privatization Initiatives: Key sectors such as healthcare, education, transport, and municipal services are targeted for privatization, opening avenues for private investment and enhancing service quality.
  6. Infrastructure Development: The private sector is actively involved in infrastructure projects, with investments expected to reach approximately $1 trillion by 2030, supporting economic diversification and long-term objectives.

Government Initiatives Supporting the Private Sector:

  • Shareek Program: Launched in 2021, this program supports large Saudi companies by enabling private sector investments and contributing to economic development.
  • Privatization Program: Initiated in 2018, this program focuses on identifying government assets for privatization to improve service quality and reduce costs.
  • National Transformation Program: This program aims to create an inclusive private sector that prioritizes financial security and promotes digitization of government services.

In summary, the active participation and investment of the private sector are crucial for achieving Vision 2030’s economic diversification goals, steering Saudi Arabia towards a more resilient and multifaceted economy.

Future-Proofing Success

The Importance of Long-Term Vision in Building Sustainable Businesses: In Saudi Arabia, several strategic initiatives reflect the importance of long-term vision. For example:

  • NEOM, the $500 billion giga-project, is being developed as a smart, sustainable city that will rely entirely on renewable energy, aiming to attract global talent and industries of the future.
  • The Saudi Green Initiative underscores environmental sustainability by targeting the planting of 10 billion trees and generating 50% of the country’s energy from renewables by 2030 — a shift that requires private sector alignment with long-term ESG strategies.
  • The Public Investment Fund (PIF) has been expanding investments into sectors like tourism, logistics, and entertainment, aiming to increase non-oil revenues and create sustainable industries for generations to come.

Sustainable business models also help companies weather market cycles, manage risks more effectively, and attract long-term investors and talent. In today’s rapidly changing global environment — where technology, regulation, and stakeholder expectations are evolving — short-term thinking can lead to missed opportunities or even business failure.

Therefore, organizations that embed long-term vision into their operations, innovation, and governance structures are better positioned to drive consistent value, maintain stakeholder trust, and contribute to national development goals.

Adaptive Leadership

The Key to Leadership in a Rapidly Changing World: Leadership in today’s world demands far more than authority or experience — it requires agility, vision, and empathy. The pace of change driven by technology, globalization, and shifting societal expectations means that leaders must be proactive, adaptable, and continuously learning.

title: Indian Stock Markets Exhibit Resiliency Against Global Shock from Trump Tariffs
author: editor
excerpt: Dubai: Stock markets in the United States, Europe, and Asia have all crashed, but India’s Sensex appears to weather the storm, at least for now. The Sensex lost a little over 1,200 points in the two days after US President Donald Trump issued his tariff rate card, with a 930-point loss on Friday (April 4). The 930 points may appear harsh, but they represent a 1.22% drop, which compares favourably to the 2.75% decrease for the Nikkei, 1.52% for the Hang Seng, and 2.95% for the Singapore index. When markets start next week, investors will have to consider China’s 34% retaliatory tariffs, which were announced on Friday. According to a researcher, this could mean more pressure on Asian stock markets than India’s. So, in these two days, India has managed to survive the worst of the global selloff forces, while also seeing the rupee firm up little versus the dollar. (The INR rose to 23.20 to the dirham, or 855.22 to the dollar.) This is even after Trump imposed a 26% import charge on products and services. The fact that pharmaceuticals were exempt from the Trump tariffs contributed significantly to the resiliency of Indian stock markets this week. title: Trump’s Plan Deals with Political and Economic Reality
author: editor
excerpt: Donald Trump pledged that the history books would mark April 2 as America’s “liberation day” when he announced his broad new tariffs on US imports on Wednesday. After two days of stock market turbulence, this may be remembered as the week the president’s second-term agenda collided with economic and political realities. US equities have plummeted since Trump announced his tariffs at Wednesday afternoon’s White House Rose Garden ceremony, with hints that America’s trading partners – most notably Canada, the European Union, and China – are not backing down from a confrontation. On Thursday, the White House appeared to be bracing for a storm. Four large posters depicting America’s “reciprocal” tariffs on a long number of countries were prominently displayed in the press briefing room, but government officials who could answer media queries were few and far between. Workers unloaded pallets of metal fencing that will surround the White House grounds in preparation for what officials expect to be a big anti-Trump rally at the nearby Washington Monument on Saturday. title: Bill Gates Wishes Microsoft a Happy 50th Birthday and Thanks Them for the Awkward Photos
author: editor
excerpt: The birth of Microsoft was marked on April 4, 1975, when Bill Gates and Paul Allen formed Micro-Soft. The business signed an agreement with IBM to provide software for its first personal computer in 1980, just five years later. Bill Gates posted on Instagram on Saturday, “Happy 50th birthday, @microsoft. ” I appreciate the memories and the uncomfortable photo sessions. “Unfortunately, I’ll never feel cool again because this was me in the early Microsoft days,” he said in the reel. The code that Gates entered on a teletype machine earlier Friday may appear archaic in comparison to today’s sophisticated artificial intelligence systems, but it was essential to the establishment of Microsoft in April 1975, a milestone that the Redmond, Washington-based corporation will celebrate this Friday. According to AP, Gates, 69, wrote a blog entry in which he reflected on how, after finding an article on the Altair 8800 in the January 1975 issue of Popular Electronics, he and his late high school classmate, Paul Allen, rushed to create the first “software factory” in history. Their innovative endeavour began with this minicomputer, which was powered by a tiny chip from the then-unknown tech company, Intel. Gates, who was a freshman at Harvard at the time, and Allen got the idea from the article to contact Micro Instrumentation and Telemetry Systems, the company that made Altair. Ed Roberts, the company’s CEO, was reassured that they had created software to assist customers in using the hardware. The issue was that they still hadn’t written the code. title: Britain Authorises London Luton Airport’s Expansion
author: editor
excerpt: On Thursday, the British government authorised the construction of a new terminal at London’s Luton Airport, allowing the capital’s fourth busiest airport to handle about 80% more passengers. Accelerating the planning process to deliver new energy and transport projects is at the core of the growth strategy of the British Labour administration, which was elected in July. The government has already supported expansion at London’s larger Heathrow and Gatwick airports. Luton, 35 miles north of London, intends to increase its yearly passenger volume from the current 18 million to 32 million by 2043 by adding a terminal building, enlarging its current facilities, and constructing new taxiways. According to a government-published planning decision document, Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander believes there is a “compelling case” for authorising the project. EasyJet, Wizz Air, and Jet2 are among the airlines that use Luton, a leisure airport that transports vacationers to European locations. The airport welcomed Alexander’s decision, which said it would boost the British economy by an extra 1.5 billion pounds annually and create up to 11,000 jobs. Alexander disregarded the environmental concerns raised by planning officials, who suggested that she halt the development. title: Dr. Oz of TV has Been Confirmed as the Head of Medicare and Medicaid
author: editor

President Donald Trump appointed Oz, who has never served in public office, to head the Centres for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) last year. By a party-line vote of 53-45 on Thursday, the Republican-controlled US Senate approved him to the position. The 64-year-old, whose methods have drawn criticism, was a trained surgeon before becoming well-known on The Oprah Winfrey Show in the early 2000s. Health professionals have previously condemned Oz for promoting what they consider to be harmful health advice regarding “miracle cures” and weight-loss medications, as well as for implying that malaria medications could be used to treat COVID-19 at the beginning of the pandemic. Trump claimed in a statement after appointing Oz to head CMS that “no doctor may be more qualified and capable…to make America healthy again. Trump’s transition team announced ahead of his inauguration that Oz will “take on the illness industrial complex” by “working closely” with US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. About half of all Americans are covered by the major healthcare programs in the nation, which CMS manages. title: The UAE Passport is the Most Popular in The Middle East
author: editor
excerpt: According to a new index published by the tax and immigration consulting firm “Nomad Capitalist,” the UAE passport is the most powerful passport in the Middle East and ranks 10th globally for 2025. The passport received 106.50 points based on factors like travel flexibility, fiscal considerations, global perception, the possibility of dual citizenship, and personal liberties. The rating evaluated travel freedom using information from news sources, the Henley Passport Index, and the International Air Transport Association (IATA). The number of nations UAE passport holders can access without a visa, with a visa upon arrival, or through an electronic travel authorisation was used to determine the final score. According to the research, eight countries allow access with an electronic travel authorisation, 45 offer a visa on arrival, and 126 allow UAE passport holders to enter without a previous visa. As a result, holders of UAE passports can enter 179 countries without a previous visa, while 71 additional countries need a conventional or electronic visa. Since citizens are exempt from income tax, the United Arab Emirates received 40 points in the tax system ranking, which makes it a desirable location for investors and businesspeople looking for a flexible tax system. title: Buildings in Myanmar Are Still Crumble Days after the Tragic Earthquake
author: editor
excerpt: Five days after a huge earthquake struck Myanmar, buildings continue to crumble, creating risky conditions for rescuers attempting to pull survivors from the rubble. The 7.7-magnitude earthquake killed over 2,700 people and injured thousands more, according to Myanmar’s military government. Hundreds more are still missing, thus the death toll is likely certain to climb. The Myanmar Fire Services Department uploaded video on Wednesday of a moving scene in the military’s purpose-built capital, Naypyidaw, where workers rescued a man from the wreckage more than 100 hours after the quake, providing a rare glimpse of hope. The man appeared exhausted and dishevelled when he was dragged out of an air pocket between cracked concrete slabs, to a round of applause. A day earlier, a 62-year-old woman was rescued from fractured concrete slabs in Naypyidaw. According to human rights organisations, structurally unstable buildings in the country are still crumbling as earthquakes persist, emphasising the risks of the rescue operation. Two hotels fell Monday night near the epicentre in Mandalay, Myanmar’s second most populated city, as residents returned to the buildings days after the earthquake. title: Rescuers Search for Survivors after the Myanmar Earthquake toll Surpasses 1,000
author: editor
excerpt: As rescuers combed through the debris of collapsed buildings in a last-ditch effort to find survivors, the dead toll from the massive earthquake that struck Myanmar and Thailand on Saturday surpassed 1,000. A 6.7-magnitude aftershock occurred minutes after the shallow 7.7-magnitude earthquake that occurred early Friday afternoon northwest of the city of Sagaing in central Myanmar. Across large areas of Myanmar, the earthquake wrecked houses, collapsed bridges, and caused roads to bend. Mandalay, the nation’s second-largest city and home to almost 1.7 million people, saw the most severe damage. According to a statement from the junta, at least 1,007 people were killed, nearly 2,400 were injured, and 30 more were reported missing in Myanmar. There have been perhaps ten further verified deaths in Bangkok. However, the isolated military-ruled state is just now beginning to reveal the full extent of the disaster due to severely hampered communications, and the death toll is predicted to increase dramatically. In Sagaing, Myanmar, a car got trapped in a hole in the ground near veggies and watermelons that had spilt. AFP AFP reporters witnessed rescuers in Mandalay removing a woman alive from the wreckage of an apartment complex where a Red Cross representative claimed that over 90 people might be stranded. The Sky Villa Condominium had twelve stories, some of which were pancaked on top of one another. title: A State of Emergency was Proclaimed in Bangkok Following Myanmar’s 7.7-Magnitude Earthquake
author: editor
excerpt: In Bangkok, a state of emergency was imposed after scores of workers were trapped in a collapsed under-construction tower after a strong earthquake shook Myanmar and neighbouring Thailand on Friday. According to the US Geological Survey, on Friday afternoon, the 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck northwest of Sagaing at a shallow depth. Within minutes, the same region was struck by an aftershock with a magnitude of 6.4. According to police and medical officials, 43 construction workers were trapped when a 30-story building fell in the Thai capital. According to footage posted on social media, the enormous structure that was supposed to house government offices was quickly reduced to a mess of debris and twisted metal. Worapat Sukthai, Bang Sue district deputy police commander, told AFP, “I heard people calling for help, saying help me, when I arrived to inspect the site.” We are currently counting the number of casualties, but we think that hundreds of people are hurt,” he stated. A group of AFP reporters were in Myanmar, across the border, at the National Museum in Naypyidaw when the earthquake occurred. title: Emirates Will Start Operating a Second Daily Flight from Dubai to Beirut on April 1
author: editor
excerpt: The Dubai-based airline said on Friday that it will begin operating its second daily route between Dubai and Beirut on Tuesday, April 1. At 7.30 a.m. (UAE time), Emirates flight EK957 will depart Dubai and land in Beirut at 10.35 a.m. (Lebanon time). At 12:05 p.m. (Lebanon time), the return flight EK958 will leave Beirut and reach Dubai at 4:55 p.m. (UAE time). The Boeing 777-300ER-powered second service will increase weekly passenger capacity by over 5,000 seats in both directions, providing customers with flexibility and meeting the increasing demand, according to Emirates. Travellers from Beirut now have a second choice to visit friends and family in Dubai thanks to the additional daily flight. For passengers connecting and travelling outside of Dubai to Emirates’ destinations like Sydney, Melbourne, Montreal, Toronto, New York, Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, Mauritius, and other important locations throughout Asia and the Indian Ocean, this service is also a handy, seamless layover, the airline continued. Using a Boeing 777-300ER, the second route will increase weekly passenger capacity by almost 5,000 seats in both directions, according to the airline. title: Trump is Being sued by Democratic FTC Commissioners Who Were Fired
author: editor
excerpt: Two Federal Trade Commission members who were fired this month are suing the Trump administration. They said on Thursday that the decision went against a long-standing legal precedent that forbids political firings. The White House sent Democratic Commissioners Rebecca Kelly Slaughter and Alvaro Bedoya on March 18 to inform them that they were dismissed, effective immediately, and without cause. According to the lawsuit, President Donald Trump stated in the email that their “continued service on the FTC is inconsistent with my Administration’s priorities. Trump’s dismissal of the commissioners immediately raised concerns that the administration was weakening and undercutting independent regulators and watchdogs in Washington. “The president wants the FTC to be a lapdog for his golfing buddies,” Bedoya wrote in a harsh critique posted on X in March after the firings. Several independent organisations, including the Federal Reserve and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, offer removal protections. The lawsuit claims that President Franklin Roosevelt’s disputed message in the 1935 Humphrey’s Executor v. United States case was echoed “nearly word-for-word” in Trump’s email to the commissioners. title: South Korea Claims that North Korea Has Sent an Additional 3,000 Troops to Support Russia’s Attack on Ukraine
author: editor
excerpt: As world leaders work to settle the three-year conflict, South Korea’s military said Thursday that North Korea appears to have transferred at least 3,000 more troops to Russia early this year, indicating Pyongyang’s sustained backing for Moscow’s war on Ukraine. The news comes as state media TASS reports that Russia’s Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko stated preparations are underway for North Korean leader Kim Jong Un to visit Russia. According to South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff, the reinforcements, which were dispatched in January and February, are part of the approximately 11,000 personnel that North Korea has already sent to Russia. Seoul claims that almost 4,000 of them had been killed or wounded in battle. According to South Korea, Pyongyang has also deployed a “significant amount” of short-range ballistic missiles, roughly 220 pieces of 240-millimeter multiple rocket launchers, and 170-millimeter self-propelled howitzers. Contributions from the North are “expected to increase according to the situation,” it stated. Amid dubious efforts by the White House to broker a ceasefire, European leaders and allies are scheduled to gather in Paris Thursday to discuss aid for Ukraine and long-term security in the region, while North Korea seems to be increasing its support for Russia’s war. title: Trump Incites Trade War Concerns While Slapping Allies with Car Tariffs
author: editor
excerpt: Following US President Donald Trump’s announcement of a 25% tariff on imported cars on Thursday, governments from Ottawa to Paris warned reprisal, intensifying a global trade war, crushing stocks, and straining already strained relations with allies. The new taxes on cars and light trucks will go into effect on April 3, the day after Trump intends to declare reciprocal tariffs targeted at the nations he holds responsible for the majority of the US trade deficit. In 2024, the United States imported $474 billion worth of automotive goods, including $220 billion worth of passenger automobiles. The largest suppliers were close friends of the United States, including Mexico, Japan, South Korea, Canada, and Germany. The US is the ultimate guarantor of European security, and the tariffs are a sucker punch for Europe at a time when relations with Washington have deteriorated on problems like the crisis in Ukraine and the breaking of a decades-old transatlantic partnership. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the action as “bad for businesses, worse for consumers.” Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada convened a cabinet meeting to discuss possible retaliatory measures. title: UAE Introduces a New Dirham Emblem Based on the Flag of the Country
author: editor
excerpt: On Thursday, the UAE Central Bank presented the new digital and physical symbol for the country’s currency. The symbol was created to improve financial and monetary stability by taking the English name of the dirham and using it as a worldwide representation of the country’s currency. It features two horizontal lines that symbolise the stability of the UAE dirham and were inspired by the UAE flag. In contrast, the digital dirham sign uses the colours of the UAE flag to represent pride and national identity, with a circle encircling the physical currency symbol. The symbol’s selection demonstrates the national currency’s global reach, receptivity to a more prosperous future, and dedication to creating a cutting-edge, locally orientated financial ecosystem with an international viewpoint. This idea, which has its roots in the national identity of the United Arab Emirates, reimagines the flag’s lines and incorporates them into the design of the letter “D” for dirham. The pointed curves are modelled after the calligraphy of classical Arabic, where characters like Thuluth and Diwani frequently have sweeping, sharp ends that convey power and elegance. title: Patrick Mataix CEO and Founder of CEO Worldwide: Transforming Executive Recruitment with Speed, Flexibility, and Diversity
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: CEO Worldwide was founded by Patrick Mataix in 2001 to address the inefficiencies of traditional executive recruitment. Unlike conventional firms, it offers a fast, flexible, and cost-effective solution, providing vetted C-level executives within 10 days. The platform supports interim, contract, and permanent placements with a success-based fee model and a 6-month replacement guarantee. Additionally, CEO Worldwide promotes gender diversity through Female Executive Search, helping businesses connect with top female leaders. With a global network of 25,000+ executives across 183 countries, the company ensures quality leadership solutions for various industries and business challenges. Vision behind CEO Worldwide We started the interview by asking, “What inspired you to establish CEO Worldwide in 2001?” Patrick Mataix replied, “I founded CEO Worldwide after struggling to find the right executives quickly while expanding Vistaprint internationally. As an entrepreneur, I found traditional recruitment agencies slow, expensive, and often ineffective at addressing urgent leadership needs. I realized that businesses needed a faster, more flexible, and cost-effective way to hire top executives worldwide. This led to the creation of CEO Worldwide, a platform designed to connect businesses with vetted C-level executives within days rather than weeks or months. My vision was to provide companies with a seamless way to fill leadership gapswhether for interim, contract, or permanent positionswithout the usual frustrations of executive search. Since its launch, CEO Worldwide has become a go-to solution for businesses needing agile leadership solutions, offering expertise across multiple industries and global markets.” Fast, Flexible, Affordable How does CEO Worldwide differentiate itself from traditional executive search firms? Patrick Mataix replied, “Unlike traditional executive search firms, CEO Worldwide focuses on speed, flexibility, and transparency. Instead of taking months to fill leadership roles, the company delivers a selection of top candidates within just 10 days. We also offer flexible hiring options, including interim, contract, and permanent placements, ensuring businesses can find leadership solutions that fit their needs. Another key differentiator is oursuccess-based fee model, meaning clients only pay for resultsunlike conventional headhunters who charge high upfront fees. CEO Worldwide also provides a 6-month replacement guarantee, giving clients confidence in their hiring decisions. Additionally, the iCEO Investors on Demand service connects businesses with potential investors, making it a unique recruitment platform that goes beyond hiring. With over 25,000 vetted executives across 183 countries, CEO Worldwide offers a modern, efficient alternative to outdated, costly recruitment methods.” Empowering Women Leader What role does CEO Worldwide play in promoting gender diversity in leadership? Patrick Mataix replied, “CEO Worldwide is actively working to break gender barriers in executive leadership. Me and my team recognized that women are significantly underrepresented in C-level roles, with female executives making up less than 10% of their certified iCEO™ candidates and only 2% in CEO or board-level positions. To address this, we launched Female Executive Search, a platform dedicated to connecting highly qualified women leaders with global businesses that prioritize diversity. Patrick firmly believes that companies with greater gender diversity at senior levels are more profitable, innovative, and sustainable. By providing businesses with access to top-tier female executives, CEO Worldwide helps close the gender gap in leadership. The initiative aims to empower women in executive roles, create more inclusive corporate environments, and drive long-term business success through diverse leadership perspectives.” A Rigorous Vetting Process How does CEO Worldwide ensure quality in its executive recruitment process? Patrick Mataix replied, “Quality is at the heart of CEO Worldwide’s recruitment process. We have a rigorous vetting system, ensuring that only the best and most experienced executives make it into ouriCEO™ database. Our HR certification team has screened over 26,000 executives from nearly 160,000 applications, carefully evaluating each candidate’s skills, industry experience, leadership track record, and global adaptability. With executives from 183 countries who speak 84 different languages, CEO Worldwide ensures that businesses get leaders who fit not only the job requirements but also the company’s culture and international needs. Additionally, our6-month replacement guarantee gives clients peace of mind, ensuring that if a placement doesn’t work out, we have a fallback option. This commitment to quality and precision allows CEO Worldwide to provide top-tier executives who can make an immediate impact on business growth and transformation.” CEO World wide’s Industry Expertise Lastly we asked, “What are some key industries and situations where CEO Worldwide provides executive solutions?” “CEO Worldwide serves a wide range of industries, including technology, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, and energy. Our executive solutions are particularly valuable in situations requiring urgent leadership intervention, such as international expansion, turnaround management, crisis leadership, mergers and acquisitions, or sudden executive departures. Businesses facing market shifts, restructuring, or rapid growth often need experienced leaders who can step in quickly and navigate complex challenges. CEO Worldwide provides executives for both short-term interim roles and permanent placements, allowing companies to remain agile and competitive in fast-changing environments. Additionally, through ouriCEO Investors on Demand service, we help businesses secure funding when needed. With a global network of 25,000+ vetted executives, CEO Worldwide offers tailored leadership solutions that help businesses grow, restructure, or recover from crisis situations effectively.”Patrick Mataix Concluded Connect with Patrick Mataix on LinkedIn Also Read :- Matthew Smith, The Digital Marketing Executive That Values Authenticity Above All Redefining The Wearable Tech Landscape With SnapWatch: Vincent Douglas

title: UAE: Tax professionals’ and Chartered Accountants’ Salaries are Increasing by Up to 10% Annually
author: editor
excerpt: According to senior industry leaders, the demand for specialists has been extraordinarily high, particularly over the last three years, and as a result, the salaries of tax experts and chartered accountants (CAs) have been rising by up to 10% yearly. In an interview with Khaleej Times, Krishnan Narayanan Venkat, head of The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), Abu Dhabi Chapter, stated that the salaries of tax experts in the United Arab Emirates have been rising by 5 to 10% every year. According to Rohit Dayma, vice chairman of the ICAI, Abu Dhabi Chapter, the demand for tax specialists and chartered accountants has increased since the implementation of value-added tax (VAT), corporate tax, transfer pricing, and regularisation of the accounting profession as a whole. The total increase in pay is also supported by the growing demand for chartered accountants at all levels, he said. The Abu Dhabi Chapter now has over 1,500 members. In 2023 and 2024, it gained 200 new members annually. An estimated 12,000 to 15,000 ICAI chartered accounts are expected to operate in the United Arab Emirates. Over 700 members and delegates attended the ICAI Abu Dhabi Chapter’s 36th Annual Seminar, “Futuronomics: The Evolution of Opportunities,” which took place on February 22–23. This event was one of the area’s biggest meetings of financial professionals. content:
We recently had the privilege of interviewing Matthew Smith, Founder and Director of Steel Frame Socials, a digital marketing agency. With tailored strategies designed for their client’s business requirements, with his clientele ranging from bespoke furniture companies, luxury properties, and interior designers. After years of experience driving visibility for luxury properties and premium brands, Matthew founded the agency to deliver tailored digital marketing in SEO, social media, branding, and content creation. As a highly skilled social media and content executive getting millions of organic views for clients, Matthew is emerging as a key player in the digital marketing landscape.

The Beginning

We started by asking, “Can you walk us through your professional journey and how it led to where you are today?”

Matthew Smith shared, “My career began shortly after COVID-19 when a custom sneaker company wanted to interview me to be their social media manager as I had previously managed a few popular social media pages for personal interests. This business was Custom Crep City UK, and I owe them the beginning of my professional career. The skills I would use in my current executive role were developed in this job, which included managing social media content, planning photo shoots, creating email marketing campaigns, writing blogs, developing promotions, designing graphics, and coordinating influencer outreach. Following my departure from this position to pursue opportunities overseas, I strengthened my experience by earning the Hubspot Academy certifications in SEO, Digital Marketing, and Social Media Management.

Shortly after, I co-founded my first company, Optimisebnb, which was an Airbnb co-hosting company with a focus on digital marketing. I was in charge of 15 properties under this company. To increase cash flow, I began working as a social media and account manager for remote agencies, where I oversaw a greater number of clients from various industries. I planned and produced content every month, making sure it matched client specifications and brand objectives. Improved interaction via social media tactics and optimized posts. Worked together on blogs, ads, and SEO while keeping an eye on results and submitting weekly reports.”

Matthew Smith added, “After returning to the UK after a lengthy job search, I was able to secure a full-time position in digital marketing for a large business, leaving behind both these agencies and the company I founded. As of this interview, I am employed as a Social Media and Content Executive for a recruitment agency. In addition to managing every aspect of the company’s digital marketing, my responsibilities have broadened to include budget management, branded merchandise, and assigning tasks to a team. In addition to this position, I recently founded Steel Frame Socials, a digital marketing agency, where all of the abilities I’ve honed over the years have come together to create an accurate and effective lead generation strategy for clients.”

Adaptability Amidst Uncertainties

Interested to learn more about the challenges faced, we asked Matthew to share some of the significant challenges he faced in his career path and how he overcame them.

Matthew Smith explained, “One of the difficulties I faced in my career was starting my first company and collaborating with people without any immediate financial benefit. I discovered that even the most driven people can experience burnout, which is a real problem. Working in a team made me realize that everyone experiences ups and downs in motivation, and I found it difficult to balance this with other people’s expectations. To avoid overworking myself and becoming burned out for the coming weeks and months, I controlled the amount of work I would do in a single day.

Even though you might feel like working on your project for eight hours a day, I think it’s crucial to manage your time so you maintain the desire and hunger to keep creating something for yourself. Keeping up with the ever-changing trends and advancements of social media is currently the biggest challenge because the platforms themselves don’t specifically explain how to reach high numbers. The best strategy against this is to become deeply involved in the community where you are establishing your business, participate in forums, and pay attention to creators in the same market to stay ahead of industry and platform updates.”

The Art Of Balancing Vision And Requirements

We further asked, “How do you balance long-term vision with short-term operational needs?”

“Writing down a list of your long-term objectives and short-term tasks is what I find to be effective. In my opinion, the short-term task list is the most crucial since it is directly correlated to the growth of your business. There is no set time limit for this, but what I did to succeed in both my professional and personal endeavors in digital marketing is to make regular checklists of simple to medium-sized tasks that I can finish quickly to guarantee continuous progress free from difficult tasks. And when I reflect on these brief task lists, they all added up to an enormous amount of finished work that would have seemed too difficult to handle if given all at once.” Matthew added.

Current Offerings At Steel Frame Socials

We asked Matthew to share about his services and exciting additions coming up in the future in his company. 

“For bespoke furniture companies, interior designers, and other luxury brands in this industry, my company, Steel Frame Socials, offers an effective and efficient digital marketing strategy to generate leads. This involves transforming the client’s online presence across all channels and digital platforms, going beyond simple social media management and content production, which is what the majority of my competitors provide.” He mentioned.

Assessing Market Trends

To understand the strategies adopted by Matthew to stay ahead of the curve, we posed the question, “What methods do you use to analyze market trends, and how have these influenced your business decisions?”

“As previously stated, it is essential to become deeply involved in the communities to which I offer my services because, although anyone can read a blog post about a popular topic, these trends will shift in a month or two. I stay up to date with the biggest brands and creators in the field when it comes to popular subjects, so I’m always aware of what’s profitable for the biggest players in the market. However, I use the standard tools that most professionals use when it comes to data, such as Ahrefs, Google Trends, Google Keyword Planner, and all of the backend dashboards of the platforms that I use to market my clients.” He responded.

Impact Of Digital Transformation

We inquired about the effect of digital transformation on Matthew’s business model.

Matthew Smith explained, “The market for general digital marketing services is already fairly saturated, with an estimated $798.7 billion in market value as of this writing. As more businesses move to online platforms, the market will only grow. The business model is all about seeing what services my competitors aren’t offering and staying up to date with practices on digital platforms that drive the most reach. If I stay ahead of these things, I can maintain the basic business model while making minor adjustments to my strategies to stay ahead of the curve.”

Emerging Trends Of The Industry

We asked Matthew to share his perspective on emerging technologies that can leave a significant impact on your industry in the next five years.

“I think this is an obvious one. It’s AI; this technology is automating a lot of the processes digital marketers use for their services; however, it is not quite ahead of what humans can perform themselves; it’s just a lot more efficient at doing so. Google already has AI summaries on its first page, and from speaking to other industry professionals, I believe that the first page of Google will soon become a completely AI-generated response based on what would be the first page results for that search query. This is very dangerous for small businesses, as they are going to lose out on a lot of SERP traffic, so they will have to consider other mediums of traffic like social media to compete with the giants like Reddit and Forbes.”

Empowering Employee And A Positive Workspace

Ensuring employee satisfaction for a successful business is crucial. So, we asked, “What strategies do you implement to maintain high levels of employee engagement and satisfaction?”

Matthew Smith replied, “Positive reinforcement is a huge driving factor to make sure that the people I employ enjoy working for me, as I’ve seen a deeper level of commitment to my business from my employees who get a good sense of fulfillment in completing the tasks I set for them. From my experience of being an employee to now managing a team, having an overbearing, micromanaging boss can cause a negative atmosphere in the workplace and often drives a sense of resentment, which I try to avoid.  

Since the majority of my work is done remotely, I make it clear that we should maintain open lines of communication. I want my employees to feel comfortable approaching me with any questions or concerns regarding assigned tasks. My team feels more at ease approaching me with any problem at any time, which has resulted in a stronger working relationship.”

Crafting A Strong Legacy

We ended the interview by asking, “How do you want your business to be remembered, and what steps are you taking to secure that legacy?”

“I want my company to be known for staying on the cutting edge and providing genuine value to the digital marketing industry. What I value most is being a key player promoting authenticity and ethical practices because this is and always will be a constantly changing industry. I want Steel Frame Socials to add a personal touch to our clients’ brands and create vibrant communities around them, providing them with an audience that will remain dedicated to our client’s business growth.

 There are a lot of issues with the current digital landscape, which is becoming more automated and less personal. The primary factor that distinguishes me from most corporate marketing agencies is my continued involvement in my clients’ communities and industries, my understanding of popular subjects, and my understanding of what matters to people. With the rise of artificial intelligence, businesses and consumers are lacking a genuine human touch, which is what I offer.” Matthew concluded.

title: Elon Musk is Currently Being Practically Taunted by Tesla’s Top Competition
author: editor
excerpt: With the exception of the United States, where trade barriers on Chinese imports have long existed, the automaker is quickly gaining market share worldwide and eating everyone’s lunch in China, the largest auto market in the world. Even while demand in used EVs is growing, used Tesla prices are plummeting. title: The Next Jet will be “Evolutionary, not Revolutionary, According to Airbus
author: editor
excerpt: According to Airbus CEO Guillaume Faury, the company’s next single-aisle jet will be “evolutionary rather than revolutionary”. Still, it may have an open-rotor engine, like the one supplier CFM is currently researching. Following the company’s decision last month to postpone construction of a radical hydrogen-powered regional aircraft, the chairman of the largest planemaker in the world was speaking at the beginning of an event meant to draw attention to ongoing innovation. The next generation of aircraft will be a big step forward, and we’re looking at technologies that will make a big difference,” Faury stated at the Airbus Summit. As the engine industry waits for the next big step in fuel economy, which usually happens every 15 years or so, Airbus and Boeing are years away from starting new jet programs to replace their best-selling narrow-body planes. Among the concepts being considered is the RISE prototype, which is being developed by French-U.S. partnership CFM, the largest engine manufacturer in the world by units sold, and aims to save 20% on fuel by 2035. It is based on an efficient open fan, or visible rotor blades. title: Tech Stocks Rise as Tariff Optimism Pushes Wall Street to a Two-Week High
author: editor
excerpt: Due to technology stocks and indications that the Trump administration is implementing tariffs on its trading partners cautiously, Wall Street’s three major indexes reached two-week highs on Monday. According to media reports over the weekend, the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump is likely to exclude a set of sector-specific tariffs that are scheduled to be implemented on April 2. With Nvidia up 3.3% and Advanced Micro Devices adding 6.2%, investors snatched up bruised technology equities, sending the overall chip index up 3.1%. Amazon.com increased 2.8%, and Meta Platforms soared 3.2%, among other mega caps. Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer of Northlight Asset Management, discussed the effects of Trump’s shifting trade policy, saying, “We believe the biggest impact is that the uncertainty has at least slowed down or potentially frozen a lot of the business activity.” Additionally, there is a fear that this chilling effect would decrease profitability in the coming quarters. Over the past several weeks, financial markets have fluctuated as traders have faced concerns of a significant slowdown in the U.S. economy following Trump’s announcement last month of many tariffs on some of its major trading partners, including China, Mexico, and Canada. title: Banking in Britain: How the UK is Drawing in the Next wave of Financial Professionals
author: editor
excerpt: Being one of the few truly international financial centres, the UK’s dominance in this field is considered to be one of its strongest points. Edinburgh and Glasgow are presently two of the most competitive, globally important financial centres, whereas London has continuously placed second in the Global Financial Centres Index. The UK government is committed to ensuring the stability and predictability required for ten years of economic expansion and beyond. Given that the UK is currently ranked as the second most desirable country for investment in PwC’s most recent global CEO survey—its highest rating in 28 years—confidence in the UK as an investment destination is already strong. In the meantime, UK fintech companies raised more money in 2023 than the following 28 European nations put together, enhancing the UK’s standing as a reliable, investment-friendly location. The success of the UK is largely dependent on its global positioning. 41% of fintech companies headquartered in the UK have historically operated abroad, and this external orientation is still present today. There aren’t many organisations that better represent the outlook than JPMorgan Chase, which has over 22,000 employees nationwide and significant operations in London, Glasgow, and Bournemouth. The bank’s Glasgow Technology Centre is a prime example of the regional financial ecosystem in the UK, which is centred on technology and driven by local talent. title: A Syria Group Claims to Have gathered Numerous Testimonials regarding Sectarian Violence
author: editor
excerpt: The biggest violence since Bashar Al Assad’s overthrow has been documented by hundreds of reports, according to a committee looking into a wave of sectarian killings on Syria’s coast this month. The group stated Tuesday that investigations are still ongoing. According to spokesman Yasser Al Farhan, who spoke at a news conference in Damascus, the committee has recorded “more than 95 testimonies” and received “more than 30 oral and written reports through direct communication. ” However, some messages are still coming electronically. The committee was established following days of violence that started on March 6 and claimed the lives of about 1,600 civilians, primarily members of the Alawite minority, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights monitor. Security forces and affiliated organisations have been charged by the Observatory with taking part in “field executions, forced displacement, and burning of homes,” killing entire families, including women, children, and the elderly. The violence was allegedly initiated by armed Assad supporters who staged attacks on the newly established security forces, according to the Syrian government. Following that, military reinforcements were dispatched to the Alawite heartland, which is where the Assad family is from. title: Redefining The Wearable Tech Landscape With SnapWatch: Vincent Douglas
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: We recently had the privilege of having a conversation with Vincent Douglas, Founder of SnapWatch, a wearable display band. With truly flexible display technology, SnapWatch is the first wearable band that can be slapped around the wrist and viewed straight at the same time. Dreamt of this invention more than two decades back, Vincent eventually connected with the right people and with relentless efforts, made his dream come true. Unlike standard smartwatches, SnapWatch bands come with a flexible display platform, utilizing the entire surface of the band, with a more user-friendly viewing area and other exciting features. By leveraging cutting-edge flexible display technology, Vincent is not just enhancing usability, with SnapWatch he is redefining the wearable tech space. Spark Behind The Journey We started by asking, “What inspired you to start your business, and what vision drives it this day?” Vincent Douglas shared, “My journey began in the film industry, where I spent over 25 years immersed in creativity. Dyslexia has shaped the way I see the world – it gives me a unique perspective and a deep understanding of visual storytelling. I didn’t learn to read until I was 14, it never held me back – it only fuelled my ability to think outside the box. The idea for my business sparked 26 years ago when I came across a snap band advertising a local rugby club. It struck me – what if this simple, flexible design could be turned into a watch? Unlike conventional straps with clasps, a snap band is effortless to wear. However, I quickly realized the technology needed – flexible electronics and displays which didn’t exist at the time. When I first shared my vision, people assumed I was crazy. But being a firm believer in research and persistence, I eventually connected with a group of Cambridge University graduates developing electroluminescent displays flexible, not yet readable in daylight. Cambridge Display Technology built a prototype for me, which I still have today. This was the moment I knew the idea had real potential.” “Understanding innovation takes time, I pursued a patent – a complex and costly process if you’re not working with the right people. Once secured, I kept my eye on global research, waiting for technology to catch up. It took 15 years, but eventually, flexible display technology began to emerge. I attended countless seminars, watching as prototypes evolved, and with each step forward, I knew I was on the right path. Today, my vision continues to drive me. It’s about pushing boundaries, embracing new possibilities, and creating something which not only solves a problem but changes the way we interact with technology.” He added. Switching To Tech-Driven Innovations We were interested to learn more about Vincent’s take on tech-driven innovations. So, we asked him to share his views on utilizing the latest technology to drive innovation and efficiency in his company. Vincent Douglas explained, “With the commercialization of flexible display technology – seen in innovations like Samsung’s foldable phones – we are now at the forefront of a new era in wearable tech. While foldable phones remain a niche market, our wearable display platform offers something truly unique compared to traditional smartwatches. Unlike standard smartwatches with small, restrictive screens, our flexible display platform utilizes the entire surface of the band, providing a significantly larger and more user-friendly viewing area. Additionally, our design features a two-form factor mechanical process, allowing the band to remain rigid when needed without requiring a flat surface. This adaptability means the hardware can be seamlessly integrated around various parts of the body, offering greater versatility than existing smartwatch designs. By leveraging cutting-edge flexible display technology, we are not just enhancing usability – we are redefining what’s possible in the wearable tech space.
