The top 10 global women in business are shaping the future of industries in ways that were once unimaginable. Across sectors, they are leading companies, driving innovation, and creating opportunities that impact economies worldwide. From technology and finance to sustainability and healthcare, their work is transforming the way we live and do business.

As we celebrate Women’s Day, we take a moment to recognize ten women who are making a lasting impact in their fields. Each of them has built something remarkable—whether it’s a groundbreaking startup, a successful corporation, or a movement that challenges the status quo. Their journeys are different, but they all share a common thread: perseverance, vision, and a commitment to change. The top 10 global women in business are not just thriving in their respective fields; they are redefining leadership on a global scale.

Top 10 Global Women in Business Impacting the Business Landscape in 2025

This women’s day, let’s talk about the women leaders who are shaping the business landscape in their own unique ways. Let’s get to the top 10 global women in business below:

1. Dr. Tina D. Lewis | The BottomLine Queen – A Global Visionary Business Leader

Dr. Tina, affectionately known as “The BottomLine Queen,” is a visionary business leader with a network and meetings with global icons, including Richard Branson, Oprah Winfrey and Donald Trump, the President of the United States of America. As the driving force behind The 6-Figure Incubator, she empowers entrepreneurs to achieve financial freedom through dynamic coaching and mentorship. Dr. Tina’s dynamic coaching and mentorship empowers ambitious minds to break barriers and achieve financial freedom. Her journey from earning the first six figures in record-breaking time to receiving awards for top recruiting and income producing is a living testament to her extraordinary business insight and leadership.

As an International Certified Global Speaker, Dr. Tina captivates audiences worldwide with her powerful, transformational messages. Moreover, as the creator and host of GLOBALcon, an international conference designed to inspire and equip women leaders from all walks of life, her voice resonates with entrepreneurs, executives, and visionaries alike, making her a sought-after keynote speaker.

Driven by her passion for empowering women, Dr. Tina founded Global Women Speakers, a professional organization dedicated to positioning women on global stages, enabling them to share their message, sell their products worldwide, and travel internationally. Her leadership has catapulted countless women into influential roles, helping them amplify their voices and achieve global recognition. But Dr. Tina’s commitment to impact and women empowerment doesn’t stop there. As a teenage mom turned entrepreneurial icon, she often declares, “Entrepreneurship saved my life.” Her journey fuels her mission to uplift the next generation, leading to the creation of the Her Business Matters Foundation, a non-profit organization empowering young girls aged 9 -19 in mastering S.E.L.F – STEM/AI, Entrepreneurship, Leadership, and Financial Literacy.

Her mantra, “If it’s to be, it’s up to me—but not just for me,” reflects her belief in leadership through service and global impact. For Dr. Tina, entrepreneurship is more than a career—it’s a transformative journey of empowerment, influence and simply just in her DNA. This philosophy has earned her international acclaim in countries, including the United Arab Emirates. Dr. Tina was awarded the Middle East Summit of Excellence Award, and honored as “Woman of the Year!”

According to Dr. Tina, Women’s Month is a celebration of strength, resilience, and progress. It honors the trailblazers who paved the way and inspires future generations to dream without limits. Dr. Tina reflects, “To me, it’s a powerful reminder that we are the architects of change, united by purpose, and destined to redefine unlimited possibilities.”

As a strategic philanthropist, Dr. Tina continues to give back, contributing to educational initiatives, entrepreneurial training, and community development programs worldwide. She believes in creating a legacy of leadership, influence, and impact that inspires generations. Dr. Tina D. Lewis is not just a business leader—she is a global phenomenon. Her story of resilience, vision, and empowerment continues to inspire entrepreneurs, leaders, and change-makers worldwide. She is proof that with determination and purpose, greatness is achievable.

LinkedIn | Instagram

2. Dina Tahboub | Results-Driven Wealth  Management Professional

Dina Tahboub, a passionate Wealth Manager, specializes in managing the wealth and investment portfolios of high-net-worth individuals. Her commitment to excellence in this field has shaped her unique journey from Jordan in the Middle East to Switzerland. With more than two decades of extensive experience in private banking and investment across top global banks, she has earned recognition as a “strong and significant asset in the wealth management industry.”

Dina has always been passionate about wealth management, finance, entrepreneurship, business, and women’s leadership and empowerment. She began her professional journey at global banks in Jordan and steadily climbed the ranks in this field with passion and enthusiasm. She reflects, “Success doesn’t come from what you do occasionally; it comes from what you do consistently.”

In 2018, Dina moved to Geneva to join the Global Wealth Management division at UBS Bank; the largest asset manager in Switzerland. During her time at UBS, she was certified as a Wealth Management Advisor by the SAQ Swiss Association for Quality. She was also nominated by UBS Bank’s management as a financial ambassador to the Middle East, a role in which she led and empowered women in finance.

As a UBS Ambassador, Dina played a crucial role in women’s empowerment in finance, helping women enhance their financial confidence and decision-making. She also worked on educating women in the Middle East on managing their assets, investing wisely, diversifying their portfolios, and optimizing asset allocation to meet their financial needs.

After a successful and fulfilling tenure at UBS Switzerland, Dina transitioned into entrepreneurship, joining Woodman Asset Management as an external asset manager. Woodman is recognized as one of the top 50 wealth managers in Switzerland. As a wealth management entrepreneur, Dina continues to work with determination and dedication toward her clients’ and company’s goals.

As a visionary leader in the industry, Dina promotes portfolio diversity, sustainable investing, and strategic wealth planning. She also encourages the younger generation to take charge of their financial decisions. Additionally, she is an active member of the Women-to-Women International organization, where she finds inspiration in the stories and experiences of other women.

Beyond her professional pursuits, Dina enjoys reading, traveling, and has a deep passion for the arts, music, and education. She firmly believes that every young girl should dream big, have confidence in their abilities, and commit to lifelong learning. “Independent women know their own worth and pave their own path,” she adds. Committed to supporting women’s and children’s issues globally, Dina continues to pave a path of positive change, inspiring women everywhere to pursue their dreams.

LinkedIn | Instagram

3. Katrina Michelle | Curated Food Experience For Every Event

Katrina Michelle, the Founder of K Michelle’s Kitchen Catering, has over 29 years of experience in the hospitality sector and has been a seasoned independent business owner for the last 14 years. Driven by the encouragement of her friends and starting her culinary journey in childhood, Katrina started K Michelle’s Kitchen Catering back in 2020.

As a culinary professional, Katrina has an impressive 4-year track record, in catering to esteemed clients, including Soulja Boy, Offset, and Cardi B, along with renowned entities like Disney Pixar, LA Department of Mental Health, Arizona State University, LACC, and more. Well-known for specializing in weddings, student groups, and corporate events, K Michelle’s presence extends to major events with multi-year attendance in events like Taste of Soul, Rolling Loud, Taste of Inglewood, 1500 or nothin Day, Hot Water Cornbread, Black on the Block, South LA Pride, Frat Games, and beyond.

With K Michelle’s Kitchen Catering, Katrina offers the best catering services by creating unique menus to accommodate every special event with sustainably sourced ingredients. From casual in-home brunches and office lunches to elegant weddings and glamorous events, her catering services are perfect for any occasion and are customized to fit the client’s budget. As a testament to Katrina’s diverse and successful catering portfolio, she has been featured on KTLA morning news and Voyages LA. With an enduring passion and commitment to excellence for her services, Katrina navigates and thrives in the diverse landscape of the industry. “Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement. Nothing can be done without hope and confidence.” — Kartina Michelle quotes Helen Keller

Women’s Day celebrates the strength, resilience, and ambition of urban women, empowering them to thrive in business and leadership.

Website | Instagram

4. Patricia M. Montesinos | Fostering Gender-Diversity And Role Of Women Entrepreneurs

Patricia M. Montesinos is a serial entrepreneur, business angel, startup coach, and jury member in the Swiss startup ecosystem. She is the Founder and President of FE+MALE Think Tank, a non-profit international association dedicated to gender diversity in entrepreneurship. Her work focuses on addressing the challenges women face in business and creating initiatives that drive meaningful change.

She holds a professional degree in Social and Cultural Integration, an Executive Master’s in Commercial and Marketing Management, and an MBA in Entrepreneurship. Patricia started her career as a Sales Director in a women’s footwear company before moving into roles as Commercial Director in the publishing sector in Madrid and Chief Administrator Officer in an architecture firm in Copenhagen.

With women entrepreneurs navigating various challenges such as funding and business growth, FE+MALE Think Tank conducts research to develop initiatives that support female entrepreneurs. “The numbers don’t lie—despite progress, female entrepreneurs still receive only 2% of total funds raised in Europe, with all-women teams securing just 0.4% of venture capital. Yet, data shows that diverse teams drive higher returns and greater innovation. Investors who prioritize gender diversity are unlocking untapped potential and outperforming the market,” Patricia states.

Through initiatives like the Beat Funding Bias Initiative, supported by the Bern Economic Development Agency, Gebert Rüf Foundation, and Ernst Göhner Foundation, FE+MALE Think Tank equips investors and entrepreneurs with resources to close the gender funding gap. Patricia works to turn research into practical solutions that foster an environment where diversity is recognized and valued.

While FE+MALE Think Tank is her primary focus, Patricia is also the Founder of Women Change-makers, an initiative that provides support for women in entrepreneurship. Though less active, it remains part of her broader mission to create opportunities for women in business.

She is also committed to supporting young women through education, with 5% of Women Change-makers’ net income donated to initiatives that encourage entrepreneurship and career development.

LinkedIn | Website

5. Amy Koford | Transforming Lives Through Hypnosis

Amy Koford, The Happy Hypnotist, is a highly acclaimed clinical hypnotist, author, speaker, and performer who excels in empowering individuals to overcome depression and anxiety, heal from past traumas, conquer their fears, and unlock their fullest potential. She is also the Founder and a Certified Hypnotherapist at Results Hypnotherapy.

With accreditation from leading trainers and organizations worldwide, Amy has enriched her expertise by attending international hypnosis conferences and learning from the foremost hypnotists in the field. Her impactful work has garnered attention across various media platforms, including television shows, publications, and podcasts. Her book about how to rise to unnecessary fear so that it is no longer holding you back and causing you suffering is coming out in a few months.

Amy’s commitment to excellence has taken her around the globe to attend the top hypnosis conferences, receiving training from top experts in this field. Specializing in happiness and peace, Amy helps people with various techniques that are effective in resolving and letting go of the past and changing their center to become positive, confident, empowered individuals who know their amazing abilities to live their best lives.

As a top-rated specialist in hypnosis techniques, public speaker, author, and performer of comedy hypnosis shows, she is even a coach with guaranteed results. Amy reflects, “I am accredited by the leading trainers and organizations in the world today. Always professional, I am an exact fit for corporate-friendly presentations, events, training, and coaching!”

LinkedIn | Website

6. Dr. Gabi Kratochwil | Connecting People And Bridging Cultures

Dr. Gabi Kratochwil, Cultural Diversity Management Expert, Speaker, Networker, CEO of CrossCultures and Chairwoman of the German-Arab Women Business Leaders, brings over 25 years of experience in connecting people and empowering women globally. Dr. Kratochwil studied Middle Eastern Studies, Politics, and Public Law at the University of Bonn and at the American University in Cairo, Egypt, forming the base of her career path.

As a passionate high-profile change maker and multi-award winning female leader, she represents Germany at many international conferences and round tables as a keynote speaker, moderator, and facilitator and has been initiating and chairing many high-ranking events bringing together global excellence, including the German-Arab Women Business Leaders Summit (GAWBL-Summit), in 2018 in Munich, Germany.

Dr. Kratochwil is a renowned name in Cultural Diversity Management counting a large number of the world’s leading international enterprises and organizations on the client list. With her company CrossCultures, she provides workshops & events around the world supporting her customers to work better globally.

She mentions, “I firmly believe in the power of connecting people globally and growing together through exchange, networking, and partnerships. Let us be open to new ideas, be bold, and learn from each other. Because only together can we pave the way forward for future generations.”

Furthermore, Dr. Kratochwil is teaching at the University of Freiburg, mentors young female entrepreneurs and coaches individuals on career development, personal goal setting, and resilience.

Her intercultural business handbook on the Arab World has been listed as number 5 of the top management books by The Financial Times, her book on successful Arab women leaders was featured in FORBES.

As a member of the Board of Directors of the Arab-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (Ghorfa) since 2006, a member of the German Middle East Studies Association for Contemporary Research and Documentation (DAVO) and the Society for Intercultural Training and Research (SIETAR), she is strongly committed to contribute.

Dr. Kratochwil’s exceptional support and work have earned her several recognitions, including the Global Diversity Leadership Award, in 2017, and the World Women Leadership Achievement Award, in 2015.

LinkedIn | Website

7. Christina Ioannou | Driving PR And Brand Positioning For Growth

A Senior PR strategist with over a decade of experience in planning, leading, executing, and evaluating international communications and PR campaigns with great success, Christina Ioannou has a demonstrated history of delivering large and complex international PR campaigns. Being passionate about PR and communications, she has a proven track record in running and implementing communication strategies focusing on storytelling, branding, and profile raising. Currently, as the Director & Campaign Lead at CCIcomms, Christina looks after the communication services, strategic partnerships, and networking opportunities for the organization.

With a keen eye for detail and a solution-oriented approach, Christina follows a strong work ethic and stays updated with the latest developments in the PR sector, ensuring efficient solutions for clients. Over her career path, she has achieved more than 8K pieces of impactful press coverage for her clients and has helped numerous leaders and founders become authorities in their fields and get positioned in the press.

Christina is also a Member of the Board of Directors at Union Dance, advising on communication strategy and implementation, and a contributor to Entrepreneur Magazine. As a Goldsmiths University Graduate, she has also served as a student mentor for the ICCE department students, supporting them with their professional journey.

Regarding her upcoming plans, Christina reflects, “Supporting startups has been my focus lately, as I am keen to support young teams and their innovative solutions. The technology and AI space is fascinating for me and I look forward to seeing more startups flourish in Switzerland and beyond!” As a seasoned leader, Christina’s dedication to staying at the forefront of this industry and her commitment to excellence make her a perfect match for organizations seeking expert guidance on PR and communication strategies.

LinkedIn | CCIcomms | Instagram

8. Tlhonepo Modisane | A Seasoned Executive And Coach

Tlhonepo Modisane is a Senior HR Executive, currently a People & Communications Business Partner at KONE for the Africa Region where she is responsible for the development and implementation of Human Capital strategies in South Africa, Morocco, Tunisia, Kenya, and Uganda countries. She serves as an Executive Director for KONE South Africa and as the Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Lead for the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa Region. KONE is an innovative leader in the elevator and escalator industry with a footprint in more than 60 countries worldwide.

Tlhonepo holds an Honours Degree in Industrial & Organisational Psychology amongst other accolades. She transitioned from a finance background and moved into the Human Resources field and has spent the past 11 years in Senior HR roles in multiple organizations within the Elevator/Escalators, Mining Engineering, Manufacturing, and ICT industries within multinational organizations such as KONE and Metso as well as local South African private organizations.

Committed and passionate about driving positive organizational cultures, Tlhonepo empowers individuals within organizations, particularly in taking accountability, and ownership for their personal development and growth by creating and leveraging opportunities for self-improvement and growth. As a public speaker and coach, her passion for the empowerment of others is also seen in her involvement in non-profit organizations where she imparts her knowledge, skills, and time by coaching and empowering others through her involvement as a Board member and in other capacities in organizations that encompass servant leadership principles and focus on the upliftment of others.

Being a coach, Tlhonepo helps individuals and businesses develop strategies and structures for improvement, change and goal attainment. She assists individuals to set goals and aim to live the lives that they desire and assists businesses in strategic transformation. For those struggling to find their purpose in life, Tlhonepo is a beacon of hope, offering her guidance and assisting them to find their own solutions.

LinkedIn | Website

9. Deniz Erkuş | Conscious Leadership For Regenerative Living

Deniz Erkuş is an impact investing catalyst and change maker for holistic sustainability. She is the Managing Partner and Founder of Sidemi Business Consulting. As a former corporate warrior with over 28 years of solid international experience, she aims to build powerful bridges connecting finance and investment with a growth mindset, regeneration, and action. Regarding regeneration, Deniz shares, “Make a daily habit of doing one valuable action a day to positively impact the planet and people’s lives.”

With a vision to empower purpose-driven businesses to generate a net positive impact, Deniz is raising awareness among investors and stakeholders for a green circular economy that creates a carbon-neutral world. She believes in the principle of the Quadruple Bottom line and regenerative framework, for sustainable prosperity by involving future generations in addition to people, planet, and profits. Deniz is a C-level executive at HealthSum Holding AS, a pioneering Norwegian firm, with a vision to revolutionize the healthcare industry through innovative solutions and powerful partnerships.

Her vision is to mobilize and channel private and public capital towards impact investing while supporting innovation with disruptive business models and aims to support such businesses as an Impact Advisor/Board member with collaboration and partnerships, applying regenerative practices. To do this, Deniz organizes training sessions, workshops, and retreats to merge consciousness and regeneration with the investment and finance community, as the first step, to moving forward with collaboration, partnerships, and action-taking.

As an international speaker and a UNDP international consultant, she contributed and spoke at various events in Türkiye, Luxembourg, Switzerland (including the World Economic Forum in Davos), Azerbaijan, Tanzania, Uganda, the UAE, and Brazil, regarding climate financing, circular economy, AI and impact, Impact Measurement and Management, SDG-anchored investing, Innovative Finance, Conscious Leadership for Regenerative Living and Generating Change. As a passionate presenter, Deniz’s teaching sessions and workshops include sustainable and innovative finance to channel capital to global impact, ESG framework, and conscious leadership for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), inspiring her audience to generate change and propel transformation forward.

LinkedIn

10. Dr. Marika Crohns: Transforming Healthcare Through Leadership and Innovation

With over three decades in healthcare, Dr. Marika Crohns, MD, PhD, has built a career defined by leadership, expertise, and a drive for meaningful change. Her impact goes beyond medical practice, as she has played a key role in shaping healthcare policies and improving patient outcomes through strategic innovation.

Throughout her career, Dr. Crohns has focused on identifying inefficiencies in healthcare systems and implementing solutions that enhance both patient care and operational effectiveness. She has been instrumental in integrating emerging technologies like AI and telemedicine to make healthcare more accessible and efficient.

Beyond her professional achievements, Dr. Crohns is deeply committed to mentorship. She actively supports and guides future healthcare leaders, helping them develop the skills and confidence needed to navigate an evolving industry. Her approach ensures that innovation and leadership continue to thrive in the next generation of professionals.

Dr. Crohns also places strong emphasis on patient-centered care. She believes that while healthcare systems advance, they must always keep the patient experience at the core. Her dedication to balancing technological progress with compassionate care has earned her a reputation as a leader who drives meaningful, lasting improvements in the field.

LinkedIn

Conclusion

The women featured in this list represent just a fraction of the talent and leadership driving the business world forward. Their success is not just about personal achievement; it’s about paving the way for others and creating spaces where more women can thrive. The top 10 global women in business serve as an inspiration, demonstrating that success is not limited by background or industry.

As we move into 2025, their influence will continue to grow, inspiring the next generation of leaders to take bold steps and redefine what is possible. This Women’s Day, we celebrate their work, their impact, and the future they are helping to build.

excerpt: Although US President Donald Trump’s government worker reductions have begun to take effect, hiring was steady last month as growth in other industries made up for the losses. According to the Labour Department, federal employment fell by 10,000 in February. Employers created 151,000 new positions nationwide, while unemployment increased slightly from 4% in January to 4.1%. This month, with growing concerns about the economic disruption caused by Trump administration policy changes, the government’s monthly report a widely followed indicator of economic health was especially scrutinized. Analysts estimated that 170,000 additional jobs would be created. According to the Labor Department, February’s monthly gain was comparable to the average monthly increase of 168,000 during the previous 12 months. Financial and healthcare companies drove hiring. The Trump administration emphasized the roughly 10,000 new jobs created in the manufacturing sector. Analysts warned that the report did not yet fully represent the scope of the cuts that the White House has outlined, and government hiring fell precipitously. The news seemed “reassuringly in line with expectations, showing payrolls growth only modestly weaker than in recent months,” according to Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management. Yet, while the most dire fears were not met, the analysis does confirm that the labour market is cooling,” she stated. title: Trump Claims That Dealing with Ukraine is “More Difficult” Than Dealing With Russia
author: editor
excerpt: To mediate a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine, US President Donald Trump has stated that he is finding it “more difficult, frankly, to deal with Ukraine” than Russia. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Friday that the US is “doing very well with Russia” and that “it may be easier dealing with” Moscow than Kyiv. Trump had stated hours earlier that he was “strongly considering” imposing significant tariffs and penalties on Russia unless a ceasefire with Ukraine was achieved. After Trump halted military funding for Ukraine, space technology company Maxar informed BBC Verify that the US temporarily blocked Ukraine’s access to some satellite imagery. It occurred precisely one week after Trump chastised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for being “disrespectful” to the United States during a remarkable White House discussion. Following that public humiliation, Trump suspended all US military assistance and intelligence exchanges with Kyiv this week. Then, on Thursday evening, Russia launched a massive drone and missile assault on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. Trump reportedly responded to this attack by threatening to impose additional sanctions on Russia, which was already under a lot of them. He claimed that because “Russia is absolutely ‘pounding’ Ukraine on the battlefield right now, he was thinking about imposing fresh tariffs. title: Top 10 Businesswomen Redefining Success in 2025
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Success in business is constantly evolving, shaped by innovation, resilience, and leadership. As we enter 2025, women across industries are redefining what it means to succeed, breaking barriers, and creating lasting impact. From technology and finance to healthcare and sustainability, these leaders are transforming their fields with vision and determination. In honor of International Women’s Day, we highlight the top 10 businesswomen who are making a significant mark. Their journeys reflect not just personal achievement but also a shift in how leadership and success are perceived in today’s world. Top 10 Businesswomen – International Women’s Day Special Below is the list of the top 10 businesswomen in different industries and fields who are showcasing their innovations and ideas exceptionally. Let’s get to it. 1. Synneve Goode & Sensorial Dressing® – The Avant-Garde of Deep Innovation A visionary leader shaping the future of fashion, experience, and sustainable innovation, Synneve Goode stands at the convergence of art, wellness, and business transformation. As the founder of SYNNEVE GOODE ATELIER, she fuses avant-garde creativity with strategic vision, proving that innovation is not just about newness – but depth, feeling, and impact. From technology and finance to healthcare and sustainability, these leaders are transforming their fields with vision and determination.

In honor of International Women’s Day, we highlight the top 10 businesswomen who are making a significant mark. Their journeys reflect not just personal achievement but also a shift in how leadership and success are perceived in today’s world.

Top 10 Businesswomen – International Women’s Day Special

Below is the list of the top 10 businesswomen in different industries and fields who are showcasing their innovations and ideas exceptionally. Let’s get to it.

She is the co-founder of the renowned tailored clothing brand, Husbands Paris, pioneering new ways of thinking and creating. Now, through Sensorial Dressing®, she is introducing a radical shift – one that reimagines how we engage with clothing, brand experiences, and innovation itself.

“Sensorial Dressing® is not just an evolution in fashion—it’s an invitation to go deeper, to explore new dimensions within ourselves and our surroundings. It is about redefining our boundaries and how we experience creativity and innovation. The future belongs to those who dare to feel, think, and create differently. This is just the beginning.”

More than fashion, Sensorial Dressing® is a tool for transformation – a strategic approach that pushes boundaries, heightens emotional connection, and unlocks new innovation potential. Through immersive experiences, workshops, and made-to-order designs, Synneve enables both individuals and companies to engage the senses, break away from conventional models, and create something entirely new.

Recognized for her pioneering work, Synneve Goode continues to lead, inspire, and challenge industries to move beyond their own limits. Whether it’s a luxury brand redefining consumer engagement, a business seeking new creative methodologies, or an individual looking to feel truly fabulous, Sensorial Dressing® is a secret to deeper, more meaningful innovation.

Step into a new era of creativity – one where artistry, strategy, and transformation become one.

A trilingual leader fluent in French, English, and Spanish, Marie possesses extensive operational change management skills. Recognising the critical role clinic managers play in operational success, this programme offers an industry-first structured curriculum that combines leadership development, compliance training, financial acumen, and marketing strategy.

title: Bitcoin and Stocks are Falling as Markets are Roiled by Trump’s Policies
author: editor
excerpt: As traders awaited important US jobs data and uncertainty about US President Donald Trump’s trade policy shook markets, global stock markets fell and the currency declined on Friday. Following Trump’s executive order to create a “Strategic Bitcoin Reserve” without arranging for any public purchases of the cryptocurrency, the price of bitcoin fell as much as 5.7%. After a slight recovery, the unit traded about 1% lower. Despite Trump’s decision on Thursday to postpone duties on Canadian and Mexican goods covered by a North American trade pact until April 2, stocks in Europe and Asia were down. The pause provides automakers with short-term respite. However, Trump has stated that he will not change the general tariffs on steel and aluminum imports that are set to go into effect next week. Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, stated, “Investors are upset by Donald Trump’s constant tinkering, even though he has exempted more goods from tariffs on Canada and Mexico.” The fact that Trump constantly changes his mind makes things confusing because businesses don’t know what’s happening daily,” he continued. As expected, increases in Germany’s defence and infrastructure spending exacerbate inflation fears and encourage the European Central Bank to halt interest rate decreases, so the euro maintained its strong support. After a slight recovery, the unit traded about 1% lower. Despite Trump’s decision on Thursday to postpone duties on Canadian and Mexican goods covered by a North American trade pact until April 2, stocks in Europe and Asia were down.

The pause provides automakers with short-term respite. However, Trump has stated that he will not change the general tariffs on steel and aluminum imports that are set to go into effect next week.

Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, stated, “Investors are upset by Donald Trump’s constant tinkering, even though he has exempted more goods from tariffs on Canada and Mexico.” The fact that Trump constantly changes his mind makes things confusing because businesses don’t know what’s happening daily,” he continued.

As expected, increases in Germany’s defence and infrastructure spending exacerbate inflation fears and encourage the European Central Bank to halt interest rate decreases, so the euro maintained its strong support.

title: Is a US Cryptocurrency Reserve a Financial Time Bomb or the Next Fort Knox?
author: editor
excerpt: The cryptocurrency market has experienced a price boom due to US President Donald Trump’s full acceptance of digital assets, which has also increased dangers for businesses and investors while opening up new opportunities. On his Truth Social network, Mr. Trump stated last week that the United States was considering establishing a strategic reserve of digital assets, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and Cardano as possible core holdings. As traders rushed to realign their wagers, the move hurt Bitcoin through financial markets, rising as much as 11% to $95,000 on March 2 and then slightly down to $88,000 on March 6. A cryptocurrency reserve would legitimize the asset class by creating government-backed holdings, just like Fort Knox does for gold. The stockpile could serve as a buffer against inflation and help the US achieve its policy objectives. However, does this mean digital assets are becoming widely used, or are we just seeing another round of speculation? title: A Tectonic Movement Away From US Markets is Being Spotted by Investors
author: editor
excerpt: A prospective shift in investor capital away from the United States is being brought about by a historic global trade war, a proposed $1.2 trillion European fiscal bazooka, and China’s rise to prominence in the innovation race. China pledged to make more steps to mitigate the effects of a worsening U.S. trade conflict and unleashed more stimulus on Wednesday. The largest fiscal policy change since Germany’s reunification was agreed upon by the country’s probable next government just hours before. In reaction, 30-year rates jumped by a quarter of a percentage point on Wednesday, and the selloff continued into the second day on Thursday, sending German bonds plunging in the most spectacular selloff in decades. The trade war sparked by U.S. tariffs that went into effect this week is harming sentiment both inside and outside of the largest economy in the world, and U.S. economic data indicates a deterioration. The last three years have seen investors place bets on “U.S. exceptionalism,” since the nation has outperformed other nations in a number of categories, including artificial intelligence, stock prices, and economic development. Tim Graf, head of macro strategy for EMEA at State Street Global Markets, stated, “The world now sees the U.S. model is changing, and saying – we need to adapt to that, the U.S. is no longer as reliable as a trade partner, we have to take care of our own needs on defense.” A remarkable divergence in global stock markets has been fueled by the shift in mood. title: Ukraine’s Envoy to The UK Claims That The US is ‘Destroying’ The World Order
author: editor
excerpt: According to Ukraine’s ambassador to the UK, the US is “destroying” the current global order. The White House had “questioned the unity of the Western world” and was “taking more and more steps towards” Russia, which invaded Ukraine in 2022, according to Valerii Zaluzhnyi. The remarks follow a public altercation between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and his US counterpart Donald Trump, and as the US presses Ukraine to make compromises before any peace negotiations begin. Since then, Zelensky has declared that he is “ready to work” under Trump’s “strong leadership.” Trump has hailed the apparent easing of hostilities, which follows the US halting military assistance to Kyiv. However, Mr. Zaluzhnyi’s comments during a seminar held Thursday at London’s Chatham House imply that there is still dissatisfaction with US conduct. He spoke to a crowd: “We see that it is not only Russia and the axis of evil trying to destroy the world order, but the US is actually destroying it completely” . The Ukrainian ambassador went on to say that the White House was taking “steps towards the Kremlin regime, fully realizing that in this case Europe could be a new target for Russia” in negotiations with Russia, which were “headed by a war criminal” in President Vladimir Putin. title: Tesla Signs to Open its First Showroom in India to Sell Imported EVs
author: editor
excerpt: An electric vehicle manufacturer’s store in Beijing, China, gets passed by a Tesla automobile. The Reuters file. Images courtesy of Florence Lo After abandoning similar plans last year, US electric manufacturer Tesla has now inked a lease agreement to open its first showroom in Mumbai as part of its efforts to sell imported vehicles in India, according to registration documents. A request for comment from Tesla was not immediately answered. According to the documents, the business has agreed to a five-year lease beginning February 16, 2025, and will pay around $446,000 in rent for the first year of the contract, which covers 4,003 square feet (372 square meters), or nearly the size of a basketball court. According to the registered lease agreement that analytics firm CRE Matrix gave to Reuters, the rent will rise by 5% annually, totalling more than $2.5 million over five years. According to the documents, the shop would be located in the Maker Maxity building in the Bandra Kurla Complex, a commercial and retail district close to the city’s airport. Days after Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla, met Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the United States last month, Reuters reported that Tesla has chosen sites for two showrooms in New Delhi and Mumbai. Musk leads Donald Trump’s so-called Department of Government Efficiency and is a strong ally of the president. Since then, Tesla has listed around two dozen mid-level positions in India, including customer engagement, retail, and service managers. title: Apple Challenges a Ruling by the UK Government to Permit Access to Encrypted Data
author: editor
excerpt: Apple has filed a lawsuit to overturn a UK government ruling for it to set up a system that would allow law enforcement to access encrypted cloud data. According to the Financial Times and BBC News, the appeal was submitted to the Investigatory Powers Tribunal in response to a covert directive that the Home Office issued in January requiring Apple to give authorities access to iCloud backups in cases involving serious crime or national security. Apple removed its Advanced Data Protection (ADP) function from the UK last month in defiance of the directive. End-to-end encryption for cloud data is made possible by ADP, an optional security feature that prevents even Apple from accessing saved files, chats, and images. Apple has essentially guaranteed that it can access certain iCloud backups, including copies of iMessages, when legally required by taking this capability away from UK users. The action has rekindled discussions about encryption and government access to personal information around the world. While privacy activists caution that weakening encryption puts everyone’s security at risk, law enforcement agencies contend that encryption impedes investigations into major crimes like terrorism and child exploitation. title: Abu Dhabi is Offering Commuters Electric Buses
author: editor
excerpt: The Integrated Transport Centre (ITC), which is connected to the Department of Municipalities and Transport, started an electric bus service for public transportation on Zayed the First Street at the start of the Holy Month of Ramadan. Since then, demand for the service has grown. The new service uses a fleet of contemporary electric buses that are intended to offer a more comfortable and effective means of transportation. Four distinct varieties of electric buses are part of the fleet, including articulated buses with two or three compartments that can carry more people, cut down on wait times, and provide smooth movement. Three 30-meter-long, 44-seat articulated electric buses with a maximum capacity of 200 passengers each have been used on Zayed the First Street. title: Meta Targets Phony Celebrity Advertisements in South Korea and Europe
author: editor
excerpt: In a residential building in Guildford, south of London, an illustration snapshot taken on February 20, 2025, shows the Meta logo on a laptop screen next to social networking apps on a phone screen. A facial recognition technique is being introduced by Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, to identify fraudulent advertisements that use pictures of celebrities in South Korea, the UK, and the EU. The tool has already been tried in other nations, and Meta intends to add more superstars to the service. The “celeb-bait” defense tool using face recognition technology will be sent to public personalities in the UK and the EU in the upcoming weeks, according to David Agranovich, director of cyber threats at Meta. “Even if the advertisement uses generative artificial intelligence, we think this tool will help us identify misused images of public figures,” Agranovich told reporters. On social media, fake advertisements using altered photos of famous people are common and frequently trick consumers into giving money or divulging personal information When a public figure activates Meta’s new function, the tool will look at their profile photo and compare it with faces in suspected phony advertisements. If misuse is verified, the program will promptly stop the ad. Meta also declared that all users can use its account recovery tools with facial recognition. If an opt-in user’s account is locked, they can record a brief video to prove their identity. title: China is Struggling with Trump’s Tariffs and Aims for 5% Growth
author: editor
excerpt: China has committed to investing billions of dollars in its struggling economy, which is now embroiled in a trade war with the United States, and has set an economic growth target of “around 5%” for this year. As hundreds of delegates gather for the National People’s Congress, a rubber-stamp parliament that approves decisions already made behind closed doors, its leaders presented the plan. However, this year is more important than others, as the week-long event is widely scrutinized for hints about changes in Beijing’s policies. Before the implementation of Donald Trump’s new 10% tax on Chinese imports on Tuesday, President Xi Jinping was already struggling with unemployment, a property crisis, and consistently low spending. This raises the overall US levy to 20% after the 10% tax applied in early February. Additionally, it impacts exports, which have been a rare area of economic growth for China. Like last month, Beijing retaliated nearly instantly on Tuesday. It declared 10%–15% tariffs on specific US agricultural goods as part of its retaliation measures. This is crucial as China’s largest market for these products, including American corn, wheat, and soybeans. China pledged to make domestic demand the “main engine and anchor” of its economic growth at the start of this week’s meeting, which is referred to as the Two Sessions. For the past two years, Beijing has reached its 5% objective, but growth was fueled by robust exports, creating a record trade surplus of almost trillions of dollars. title: What is Known About Pope Francis’s Health Crisis at the Age of 88
author: editor
excerpt: Pope Francis, 88, had two episodes of “acute respiratory failure” on Monday and has been in the hospital in Rome since February 14. Here are our current understandings about the health of the Argentine pope, who has led the Catholic Church and its over 1.4 billion adherents since 2013. Initially diagnosed with bronchitis, Francis later developed pneumonia in both lungs, which led to his admission to the Gemelli hospital. The Vatican disclosed on February 22 that Francis had experienced a “prolonged asthmatic attack” that necessitated the use of a nasal cannula to administer “high-flow” oxygen. Due to thrombocytopenia, a blood disorder that can hinder clotting and result in ongoing bleeding, Francis also needed blood transfusions. The Vatican’s situation gradually improved over the next few days, but on February 28, another significant problem still appeared. The Holy See reported that the pope experienced “an episode of vomiting with inhalation” due to “an isolated crisis of bronchospasm,” which is a tightening of the muscles lining the lungs’ airways. He was reportedly “in good spirits” despite starting “non-invasive mechanical ventilation” a Vatican source claims he was receiving oxygen through a mask. author: editor
excerpt: According to emails obtained by Reuters, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services informed staff members on Monday that they could submit applications for early retirement within the next ten days and that they should reply to a request for details on their weekly successes. A historic attempt to reduce the federal bureaucracy is being driven by billionaire Elon Musk, who is in charge of the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, and Republican President Donald Trump. Workers were redirected to the OMP website, which states that among other qualifications, qualified personnel must be at least 50 years old and have served for the federal government for 20 years, or be of any age and have served for 25 years. According to the email, the deal is good until March 14 at 5:00 PM EST. The FBI, State Department, and several other U.S. agencies had similarly instructed staff not to immediately comply with DOGE’s request. However, in a Monday email obtained by Reuters, HHS instructed staff to reply to DOGE’s email by midnight without disclosing private information, such as the names of medications and equipment they are developing. title: Trump’s Cryptocurrency Reserve Appointment Ignites a Currency Rush and Surge
author: editor
excerpt: On Sunday, Donald Trump announced that five cryptocurrencies were being considered for a new US “strategic reserve,” which caused their valuations to soar and partially reverse a previous decline. The US president stated on his Truth Social network that a working group he established soon after assuming office is proceeding with the reserve, which would comprise three minor cryptocurrencies: Cardano, Solana, and XRP. When the news broke, the value of all three digital currencies skyrocketed, with XRP up over 34% at 1:00 pm local time in Washington (1800 GMT). Cardano increased by almost 63 percent, while Solana gained over 22 percent. Noting that other valuable cryptocurrencies, like as bitcoin and ether, would be at “the heart of the Reserve,” Trump commented again a few minutes later. This caused the price of the two main digital currencies to increase by more than 10 percent and 12 percent, respectively. Trump’s posts contributed to a widespread rally in cryptocurrencies, which had fallen precipitously in the previous days as investor confidence in the highly volatile assets was shaken by Trump’s tariff threats and fresh scandals involving the industry. Trump and people close to him have already expressed opinions about the cryptocurrency industry in posts published on Sunday. Recent claims that Trump and his wife Melania were trying to profit on his political achievements were sparked by the introduction of their own branded meme coins. title: The Jinxed T-Shirts and the Yellow Cars
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The other day, I did something completely out of character—I bought ridiculously expensive t-shirts. Now, I’m not the type to splurge on clothes, but I thought, what the hell, let me treat myself. Big mistake. Suddenly, I couldn’t eat like a normal human being. Every meal turned into a battlefield: oil splatters, sauce drops, even wine stains (and I wasn’t even drinking aggressively). It was as if the universe had activated some secret “Slob Mode” just to personally punish me for my fashion choices. At first, I thought these t-shirts were jinxed. Cursed. Fabric woven from the very threads of bad luck. But then it hit me—I’ve always dropped food on my clothes. The only difference? When it happened to my regular t-shirts, I never cared. What changed wasn’t my coordination. What changed was my perception. Welcome to the Yellow Car Experiment Have you ever played that game where someone punches you for every yellow car you see? content:
The other day, I did something completely out of character—I bought ridiculously expensive t-shirts. Now, I’m not the type to splurge on clothes, but I thought, what the hell, let me treat myself.

Big mistake.

Suddenly, I couldn’t eat like a normal human being. Every meal turned into a battlefield: oil splatters, sauce drops, even wine stains (and I wasn’t even drinking aggressively). It was as if the universe had activated some secret “Slob Mode” just to personally punish me for my fashion choices.

At first, I thought these t-shirts were jinxed. Cursed. Fabric woven from the very threads of bad luck. But then it hit me—I’ve always dropped food on my clothes. The only difference? When it happened to my regular t-shirts, I never cared.

What changed wasn’t my coordination. What changed was my perception.

Welcome to the Yellow Car Experiment

Have you ever played that game where someone punches you for every yellow car you see? Suddenly, yellow cars are everywhere. The streets are practically glowing with them. And of course, you can’t move your arm for a week.

Were they always there? Yes. But you weren’t paying attention before.

This is exactly how our brains work. What we focus on expands.

And this doesn’t just apply to expensive, doomed t-shirts—it applies to everything.

The Science of Your Brain Gaslighting You

Don’t believe me? Here are some of the most ridiculous, science-backed ways our brains completely mess with us.

1. The Placebo Effect: You Can Literally Heal Yourself with a Sugar Pill

Doctors have been baffled for years by the Placebo Effect, where people take completely fake medicine and still get better—simply because they believe they’re being treated.

Some surgeries have even been “faked” (yep, just an incision, no actual procedure), and yet patients report real pain relief.

The takeaway? Your brain is a liar. But in this case, it’s a helpful liar.

2. The Nocebo Effect: The Placebo’s Evil Twin

If belief alone can heal, guess what? It can also make you sick.

  • In one study, people were told they were being exposed to an allergen (but they weren’t), and guess what? They developed real allergy symptoms.
  • Some people took a harmless pill but were told it had side effects—and then they actually experienced them.
  • If enough people tell you, “You look tired today,” you’ll suddenly feel exhausted.

Moral of the story? If you expect bad things, your body will make sure you experience them.

3. The Invisible Gorilla Experiment: How You Can Literally Not See a Gorilla

In one of the most famous psychology experiments, people were asked to watch a video of a basketball game and count how many times players in white jerseys passed the ball.

Halfway through, a guy in a gorilla suit walked across the screen, stopped, beat his chest, and walked off.

Guess what? 50% of the people never saw the gorilla.

Why? Because their brains were too focused on counting to notice something blatantly obvious.

Lesson: You only see what you expect to see.

So if you expect bad luck, failure, or cursed t-shirts, guess what? That’s all you’ll see.

4. The Rubber Hand Illusion: Your Brain Will Believe Anything If You Convince It

In this experiment, scientists placed a fake rubber hand in front of participants and stroked it while simultaneously stroking their real hand (which was hidden).

After a few minutes, people started feeling sensations in the fake hand. Then, when researchers stabbed the rubber hand, people actually flinched and felt pain.

Their brains literally adopted a fake hand as their own.

The takeaway? Your brain is incredibly gullible.

5. The Pygmalion Effect: Expectations Shape Reality

In a classic study, teachers were told that certain students were “gifted” (they weren’t, this was random). But because teachers believed it, they treated those students differently, and by the end of the year, those students actually performed better.

What happened? Their belief changed their reality.

Flip side? If someone expects you to fail, it can impact your performance negatively—this is called the Golem Effect.

Moral? What people believe about you matters. But more importantly, what you believe about yourself matters even more.

6. The Stanford Prison Experiment: When People Actually Became Their Roles

In 1971, researchers divided normal students into “prisoners” and “guards” in a fake prison setting.

Within days, the “guards” became abusive, and the “prisoners” became helpless and psychologically broken. The experiment was supposed to last two weeks. They had to shut it down after six days.

The takeaway? People become what they believe they are.

If you see yourself as unlucky, cursed, or doomed to spill on every expensive shirt you own… your brain will make sure it happens.

Redefining the Law of Attraction: It’s All About What You Notice

People love talking about the Law of Attraction, the idea that “positive thinking attracts good things.” But that’s not quite how it works.

It’s not that thinking positively magically brings you money and happiness—it’s that your brain starts looking for opportunities instead of problems.

  • If you focus on failure, bad luck, and mistakes, your brain will highlight every single thing that goes wrong.
  • If you focus on success, opportunities, and positive outcomes, your brain will start filtering the world through that lens.

The truth is, life isn’t suddenly giving you more bad luck. You’re just noticing it more—just like my “jinxed” t-shirts.

The reality? I’ve always spilled things. I just never cared before.

  • If you start looking for opportunities, you’ll notice them.
  • If you start believing you’re capable and lucky, your actions will reflect that.
  • If you focus on the good in your life, your reality will shift accordingly.

So, are my expensive t-shirts actually cursed? Nope. My focus was.

And if your life feels full of bad luck, failure, or stress… maybe it’s time to change what you’re paying attention to.

Because trust me—there are a lot of yellow cars out there.

author: editor
excerpt: Following an astonishing dispute with US President Donald Trump in the Oval Office that left Western allies reeling and cast doubt on the future of the Russia-Ukraine war, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will meet European leaders at a crucial meeting in London on Sunday. In stark contrast to his reaction at the White House, Zelensky received a warm welcome from British Prime Minister Keir Starmer on Saturday. title: How to Kill Your Business: Take Your Customers for Fools
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: I had a contract with a telecom operator. I sold my unit, a new contract was created for the new owner, yet the telecom company kept charging me. When I investigated, I found out they had already suspended my services, but the fees kept accumulating. When I called to cancel, they hit me with four months of charges for nothing—plus a two-month early termination fee. It got me thinking—is this a sustainable business model? It left a bitter taste, much like those developers who once made more on late fees than actual sales. They milked customers dry—until customers left, and the businesses collapsed. Lesson? Don’t take customers for fools. If you do, your business won’t be around for long. And history proves it. The Business Failures Hall of Shame Blockbuster: Late Fees Were More Important Than Customers Blockbuster was once the king of movie rentals—until they got too greedy. Their massive late fees made them millions but also made customers hate them. Then came Netflix, which said, “No late fees, watch from home.” Blockbuster had the chance to buy Netflix for $50 million and laughed them off. A few years later, Blockbuster was bankrupt, and Netflix became a streaming empire. Motorola & BlackBerry BBM: Stubbornness Killed the Giants Motorola, BlackBerry, and Nokia were once the biggest names in mobile phones. Then Apple and Samsung introduced touchscreens, better software, and a focus on user experience. What did these giants do? They refused to change. Motorola stuck to flip phones like it was 2005 forever. BlackBerry clung to tiny keyboards while customers wanted sleek touchscreens. BlackBerry had BBM (BlackBerry Messenger), the world’s first great messaging app—but they refused to make it available outside BlackBerry devices. Meanwhile, WhatsApp and iMessage gave users free messaging across all phones. Customers moved on, and BlackBerry became a relic. Myspace: From King of Social Media to Irrelevance Before Facebook, Myspace ruled social media. Then it got greedy. Too many ads made it unbearable. Spam and poor security drove users away. A messy interface made Facebook’s clean design look like a dream. Facebook focused on user experience, while Myspace focused on squeezing every dollar out of customers. The result? Myspace is now a digital graveyard. Sears & Toys “R” Us: The Retail Dinosaurs That Refused to Evolve Sears and Toys “R” Us were once household names. But as Amazon and Walmart revolutionized retail, these companies thought they were too big to fail. Instead of adapting, they: Kept their outdated business models. Let stores become uninviting and overpriced. Ignored the rise of e-commerce. Customers wanted convenience, better pricing, and online shopping. Amazon delivered, and Sears and Toys “R” Us disappeared. MoviePass: A Brilliant Idea That Lied to Customers MoviePass offered unlimited movie tickets for $9.99/month. Sounds amazing, right? Too amazing. Once too many customers signed up, MoviePass panicked and changed the rules. Suddenly: Users couldn’t watch certain movies. Restrictions popped up without warning. Some accounts were randomly blocked from buying tickets. Customers felt scammed and left. By 2019, MoviePass was bankrupt. WeWork: The Billion-Dollar Fantasy That Crashed WeWork promised to revolutionize office spaces with trendy coworking environments. Instead, it turned into a cash-burning disaster thanks to: Overhyped promises and unrealistic valuations. Unfavorable lease agreements that locked in customers. A reckless CEO (Adam Neumann) who spent billions on nonsense. Investors lost faith, customers got stuck in bad contracts, and by 2023, WeWork was bankrupt. The Power Has Shifted: Customers Now Hold the Cards There was a time when businesses could get away with anything. Not anymore. TripAdvisor, Google Reviews, and social media have flipped the script. Now, if a hotel promises a sea-view room, it had better actually have a sea view—or customers will expose the lie online. Bad airline service? One viral post can destroy reputation and sales. A misleading product? Negative reviews will bury it. Hidden fees? Customers will warn each other instantly. Businesses that mistreat customers today don’t just lose a sale; they lose their entire reputation. Money follows happy customers. The companies that forget this end up like Blockbuster, Nokia, Myspace, and every other business that thought customers wouldn’t notice. So, to every telecom provider, developer, and business out there: Play the long game. Respect your customers. Or prepare to be the next cautionary tale. Lesson? Don’t take customers for fools. If you do, your business won’t be around for long. And history proves it.

The Business Failures Hall of Shame

Blockbuster: Late Fees Were More Important Than Customers

Blockbuster was once the king of movie rentals—until they got too greedy. Their massive late fees made them millions but also made customers hate them.

Then came Netflix, which said, “No late fees, watch from home.” Blockbuster had the chance to buy Netflix for $50 million and laughed them off. A few years later, Blockbuster was bankrupt, and Netflix became a streaming empire.

Motorola & BlackBerry BBM: Stubbornness Killed the Giants

Motorola, BlackBerry, and Nokia were once the biggest names in mobile phones. Then Apple and Samsung introduced touchscreens, better software, and a focus on user experience.

  • BlackBerry clung to tiny keyboards while customers wanted sleek touchscreens.
  • BlackBerry had BBM (BlackBerry Messenger), the world’s first great messaging app—but they refused to make it available outside BlackBerry devices.

  • Too many ads made it unbearable.
  • Spam and poor security drove users away.
  • A messy interface made Facebook’s clean design look like a dream.

Sears & Toys “R” Us: The Retail Dinosaurs That Refused to Evolve

Sears and Toys “R” Us were once household names. But as Amazon and Walmart revolutionized retail, these companies thought they were too big to fail.

Instead of adapting, they:

  • Kept their outdated business models.
  • Let stores become uninviting and overpriced.
  • Ignored the rise of e-commerce.

Customers wanted convenience, better pricing, and online shopping. Amazon delivered, and Sears and Toys “R” Us disappeared.

  • Overhyped promises and unrealistic valuations.

  • Bad airline service? One viral post can destroy reputation and sales.
  • A misleading product? Negative reviews will bury it.
  • Hidden fees? Customers will warn each other instantly.

Businesses that mistreat customers today don’t just lose a sale; they lose their entire reputation.

Money follows happy customers. The companies that forget this end up like Blockbuster, Nokia, Myspace, and every other business that thought customers wouldn’t notice.

So, to every telecom provider, developer, and business out there: Play the long game. Respect your customers. Or prepare to be the next cautionary tale.

title: Mass Firings of Some Government Employees are Probably illegal, According to a US Judge
author: editor
excerpt: According to a California judge, the Trump administration’s widespread terminations of probationary staff were probably illegal. US District Judge William Alsup concluded that the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) had informed thousands of workers in a few federal departments that they were fired using power that the agency lacked. Under no statute in the universe’s history does [OPM] have any authority whatsoever to hire and fire employees at another agency,” he stated. “They have the authority to hire and fire their staff. Additionally, they contended that only the best and most essential workers should be employed and that probationary staff are not assured jobs. The Trump administration’s efforts to downsize the federal workforce in the name of cost-cutting have targeted government employees. Many of the workers impacted by the layoffs are probationary workers, typically those in their first or second year of employment, though occasionally they are long-time workers who have just received a promotion. Judge Alsup mandated that OPM withdraw its orders to dismiss employees at several agencies, including the Defense Department, the National Park Service, and the Department of Veterans Affairs. title: Today, President Trump will sign an Executive Order Designating English as the United States’ Official Language
author: editor
excerpt: A historic executive order designating English as the official language of the United States is about to be signed by President Donald Trump. According to the Associated Press on Friday, this will be the first time a national language is formally recognized in the country’s history. title: How Everyday Gestures Reveal True Character: A New Way to Assess People
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: A few days ago, I was driving down Sheikh Zayed Road when a reckless driver caught my attention. He was tailgating, making sharp turns to catch an exit, and disrupting everyone around him. It got me thinking—this guy cannot be a good employee, a good husband, or even a good citizen. If someone is this impatient, inconsiderate, and reckless on the road, how can they be expected to act differently in the workplace or in life? That’s when I had a realization: people reveal their true character through small, everyday actions. In hiring, business, and even personal relationships, we often rely on interviews, resumes, and references—yet these are easily manipulated. Candidates rehearse their answers, polish their CVs, and say all the right things. But real character is exposed in the unnoticed moments. What if we had a way to weed out the incompetent, selfish, or impulsive individuals before they became problems in our companies or our lives? Here are some of the most revealing real-world tests used by sharp employers to identify the right people—and filter out the wrong ones. The Coffee Cup Test A CEO in Australia had a simple rule: after an interview, he watched whether the candidate returned their empty coffee cup to the kitchen or just left it on the table. Those who didn’t bother cleaning up after themselves were automatically disqualified. A small test, but a powerful filter. The Messy Reception Test Some hiring managers place a small piece of trash near the reception desk and watch if candidates pick it up or ignore it. Those who take the initiative to clean it, without being asked, demonstrate a strong work ethic and sense of responsibility. The Parking Lot Test A company CEO used to secretly observe how candidates parked when they arrived for interviews. If they parked in customer or handicapped spaces—even when other spots were available—they were instantly rejected. A person’s behavior in a parking lot, like their driving, tells you exactly how they operate in life. The Waiter Test Billionaire Warren Buffett famously said that a person’s true character is revealed by how they treat those who can do nothing for them. Some hiring managers take candidates out for a meal and observe how they treat waiters and service staff. If a candidate snaps at a waiter, they will snap at your customers and colleagues. The Rude Receptionist Test One company instructed its receptionist to act rude and impatient when greeting candidates. The hiring team observed how each person reacted—whether they stayed calm, were polite, or snapped back. You can train skills, but you can’t train decency. The Waiting Room Test Some companies deliberately make candidates wait in the reception area longer than expected. During this time, they secretly observe: Do they interact politely with the receptionist? Do they engage positively with others in the room? Do they complain or show frustration? If someone starts complaining before even getting the job, imagine what they’ll do once hired. The Real Indicator of Character The biggest mistakes in hiring and relationships come from trusting what people say instead of what they do. Anyone can say they are a team player—but will they treat a waiter with kindness? Anyone can claim they are detail-oriented—but will they notice a mess and clean it up? Anyone can promise they are calm under pressure—but will they snap at a rude receptionist? True character isn’t found in rehearsed answers. It’s revealed in unscripted moments. If someone fails these small tests, they will fail in the bigger moments of life too. The world doesn’t need more bad drivers, bad employees, or bad citizens. It’s time to weed them out. In hiring, business, and even personal relationships, we often rely on interviews, resumes, and references—yet these are easily manipulated. Candidates rehearse their answers, polish their CVs, and say all the right things. But real character is exposed in the unnoticed moments.

What if we had a way to weed out the incompetent, selfish, or impulsive individuals before they became problems in our companies or our lives?

Here are some of the most revealing real-world tests used by sharp employers to identify the right people—and filter out the wrong ones.

The Coffee Cup Test

A CEO in Australia had a simple rule: after an interview, he watched whether the candidate returned their empty coffee cup to the kitchen or just left it on the table. Those who didn’t bother cleaning up after themselves were automatically disqualified.

A small test, but a powerful filter.

The Messy Reception Test

Some hiring managers place a small piece of trash near the reception desk and watch if candidates pick it up or ignore it. Those who take the initiative to clean it, without being asked, demonstrate a strong work ethic and sense of responsibility.

The Parking Lot Test

A company CEO used to secretly observe how candidates parked when they arrived for interviews. If they parked in customer or handicapped spaces—even when other spots were available—they were instantly rejected.

A person’s behavior in a parking lot, like their driving, tells you exactly how they operate in life.

Billionaire Warren Buffett famously said that a person’s true character is revealed by how they treat those who can do nothing for them. Some hiring managers take candidates out for a meal and observe how they treat waiters and service staff.

If a candidate snaps at a waiter, they will snap at your customers and colleagues.

One company instructed its receptionist to act rude and impatient when greeting candidates. The hiring team observed how each person reacted—whether they stayed calm, were polite, or snapped back.

You can train skills, but you can’t train decency.

The Waiting Room Test

Some companies deliberately make candidates wait in the reception area longer than expected. During this time, they secretly observe:

  • Do they engage positively with others in the room?
  • Do they complain or show frustration?

If someone starts complaining before even getting the job, imagine what they’ll do once hired.

The Real Indicator of Character

The biggest mistakes in hiring and relationships come from trusting what people say instead of what they do.

  • Anyone can claim they are detail-oriented—but will they notice a mess and clean it up?
  • Anyone can promise they are calm under pressure—but will they snap at a rude receptionist?

True character isn’t found in rehearsed answers. It’s revealed in unscripted moments.

If someone fails these small tests, they will fail in the bigger moments of life too.

The world doesn’t need more bad drivers, bad employees, or bad citizens. It’s time to weed them out.

title: US Weekly Jobless Claims Show the Highest Jump in Five Months
author: editor
excerpt: Last week, the number of Americans filing new unemployment claims rose to its highest level in five months, although the underlying trend in claims remained consistent with a continuously deteriorating labor market. The larger-than-expected spike in initial claims published by the Labor Department on Thursday was most likely due to snowstorms in several portions of the Midwest and Northeast. The data also includes the Presidents’ Day holiday, which may have added some volatility. There were no signs that significant layoffs of federal government employees were increasing claims, although this could change as more workers are sacked in the coming weeks. The Labor Department reported that initial claims for state unemployment benefits increased by 22,000 to a seasonally adjusted 242,000 in the week ending February 22. This was the most significant gain since October of last year. Reuters polled economists, who expected 221,000 claims in the most recent week. Unadjusted claims dropped 2,997 to 220,541 last week. California, Kentucky, Texas, Washington state, and Tennessee all experienced severe reductions. They more than countered an increase of 3,731 filings in Massachusetts and 2,055 in Rhode Island. There was also a considerable increase in applications from Illinois. author: editor
excerpt: South Africa expressed disappointment on Thursday that the Summit Group of 20 talks it held on global economic concerns ended without agreement after top officials from several nations skipped them, and participants remained divided on matters such as climate funding. The two-day G20 summit of finance ministers and central bankers in Cape Town failed to produce a consensus communique. However, a “chair’s summary” provided by the host stated that participants “reiterated the commitment to resist protectionism.” The summary also stated that they “supported a rules-based, non-discriminatory, fair, open, inclusive, equitable, sustainable, and transparent multilateral trading system,” utilizing numerous terms that the Trump administration has previously firmly opposed. However, the meetings were overshadowed by the absence of several prominent finance chiefs, including those from the United States, China, India, and Japan, as well as foreign aid cuts by significant economies such as the United States and the United Kingdom, against the backdrop of escalating geopolitical tensions. South Africa’s Finance Minister, Enoch Godongwana, said he was “disappointed” that the G20 meeting could not release a joint communique. title: The peaceful Massachusetts Communities that Fueled the Revolution
author: editor
excerpt: On April 19, 2025, Lexington, Concord, and two other towns north-west of Boston will commemorate the 250th anniversary of the frigid spring day in 1775 when Massachusetts militias clashed with British forces in a battle that set the United States on the path to independence. The disastrous die was cast when Paul Revere rode on horseback in the little farming village of Lexington to warn leaders that British soldiers were marching from Boston to take colonial military supplies kept in Concord, just a few miles away. When the British came, they discovered a small band of local militiamen, Minutemen, waiting in the morning light. Nobody knows who fired the first shot, but eight Minutemen and one British soldier were killed by the end of the fight. The British marched on to Concord, where they encountered many Minutemen near the North Bridge. After intense battle and substantial losses on both sides, the British withdrew. Returning to Boston, British troops faced a running conflict as the towns of Lincoln, Lexington, and Menotomy (now Arlington) organized militias to resist. Every year on April 19, these little Massachusetts communities celebrate with historical reenactments and other special events. However, with additional celebrations planned in honour of the 250th anniversary, organizers expect this year’s festivities will lure more travellers than ever before to what many call “the birthplace of American liberty. title: Saudi Arabia Urges Muslims to Observe the Moon on February 28 During Ramadan in 2025
author: editor
excerpt: The Supreme Court of Saudi Arabia declared on Wednesday that all Muslims in the Kingdom are encouraged to observe the crescent during Ramadan on the evening of Friday, February 28. According to the Umm Al Qura calendar, which the nation created to calculate dates and months, the date is equivalent to 29 Shaban AD. “Anyone who witnesses the moon with their own eyes or through binoculars is asked by the Supreme Court to notify the closest court and provide their testimony, or contact the closest centre to help them get to the closest court,” the authorities stated. It said it “hopes that anyone who can see it will take notice of this issue, join the committees established in the regions for this purpose, and count the reward and recompense for participating. An “act of righteousness and piety” that “benefits all Muslims” is how the court described the Moon sighting. Ramadan will start on March 1 if the Moon is visible on Friday night following the Maghrib prayer. On the other hand, the holy month will start on March 2 if the crescent is not visible. According to the UAE’s International Astronomy Centre, Ramadan will probably start on March 1. Devotees all around the nation wait for the moon sighting, which marks the start of the holy month, each year. author: editor

Through a procedure called end-to-end encryption, Advanced Data Protection (ADP) ensures that only account users may read things like documents or images that they have stored online. However, early this month, the UK government requested access to the data, which is now unavailable to even Apple. Apple has continuously rejected opening a “backdoor” in its encryption service, claiming that if it did, it would only be a matter of time until malicious actors also managed to get in. The company did not respond at the time. It implies that not all UK consumer data kept on Apple’s cloud storage service, iCloud, will eventually be completely protected. Apple has access to data with standard encryption and can share it with law authorities with a warrant. The Home Office stated to the BBC: “We do not comment on operational matters, including for example confirming or denying the existence of any such notices.” Apple stated in a statement that it was “gravely disappointed” that British consumers will no longer be able to use the security feature.
