We recently had the pleasure of having a conversation with Christian Krauter, visionary entrepreneur and the Founder and Director of Datanova, a unique software development company focused on providing Enterprise Service Systems (ESS) for Australian Government Service Providers such as NDIS, Childcare, Aged Care and Community Services.

Christian’s inclination towards innovation and digital advancement has allowed him to successfully navigate the intersection of technology and social welfare. Under Christian’s management and leadership, the company has positioned itself as a good fit for organizations that seek effective and user-centric solutions. Additionally, Christian is popularly known to have a rather large following in the music industry and manages to delight more than 400,000 fans across music platforms.

In this insightful session, Christian shares his ideas on entrepreneurship, the role of technology in the modern world, and the prospects of service delivery based on his knowledge of the history of software development and business.

The Beginning

We started the interview by asking, “Can you walk us through your professional journey and how it led to where you are today?”​

Christian Krauter shared, “I began my early career with a deep interest in computer software and design, driven by the commercial opportunities emerging at the time. I didn’t finish university, as I was approached by friends to join a startup specializing in pre-print computing in the late ’80s. At that time, every publisher was transitioning from traditional methods to modern Apple-based systems.  

 

In my early 20’s, I established my first company, gaining valuable experience concerning the interpersonal dynamics of business. However, after 3 years, I exited that venture and spent 11 years traveling, where I undertook digital transformation-oriented ventures and other great projects, such as CD-ROM programming, and designing works in the USA, China, New Zealand, Germany, Greece, the UK, and Australia. This experience has deepened my understanding of different cultures, refined my business communication, project management, marketing, as well as client engagement abilities, and enabled me to lay out the groundwork for creating a viable software enterprise.”

Christian Krauter added, “The magic moment came with the dawn of the Internet. I realized this would be transformative, reshaping how we do business, exchange information, and pursue education. My focus shifted from single-user environments to networks of many users not confined to a single location, such as an intranet. I began building CRM applications accessible from anywhere, which was a game-changer in application development and delivery. 

Though my original plan was to return to Austria, I was captivated by Australia’s vast landscapes and beauty. And I decided to build my business here and so, I established my work in construction as a digital solution architect, focusing on business enhancement, database systems, and customer relationship management systems. Seventeen years ago, I founded Datanova, which developed software, in particular, for Australian Government Service Providers. 

Moreover, one of my proudest personal achievements has been mixing and producing music since 2017. Even starting from scratch with no background or experience in the industry, my music became such a hit that nearly 10 million impressions of my work were recorded on SoundCloud and other similar platforms, been listed in rank 100 several times, received many invitations to perform in Europe and the US, and now I have more than 400,000 online fans.”

Adaptability Amidst Challenges

Challenges are a part of every career path and Christian Krauter’s journey is not an exception. So, we asked, “Reflecting on your career, what have been some of the most significant challenges you’ve faced, and how did you overcome them?”

He responded, “Throughout my career, I’ve embraced challenges as stepping stones to innovation, especially in the fast-evolving tech landscape. One significant challenge has been staying ahead of rapid technological advancements while ensuring sustainable growth in project delivery. Each wave of new tech required agile adaptation—not just in terms of learning but in rethinking and reshaping solutions to meet emerging demands. Rather than seeing these shifts as setbacks, I saw them as openings to implement creative strategies, like adopting lean development processes and fostering cross-functional collaboration. This approach enabled me to deliver impactful, scalable solutions even amidst tight timelines and evolving requirements.  

Another pivotal challenge has been navigating complex integrations, particularly when aligning older systems with cutting-edge platforms. Such integrations often came with a host of technical obstacles and stakeholder expectations. However, I turned these complexities into opportunities by focusing on innovative problem-solving and proactive communication. I’d lead teams to break down these integrations into manageable phases, ensuring transparency with stakeholders at each stage. By turning challenges into structured pathways, I consistently delivered outcomes that met technical standards and exceeded client expectations, further solidifying trust and showcasing the power of resilience in tech.”

Balance For Sustainable Success

We further asked, “How do you balance long-term vision with short-term operational needs?​”​

Christian Krauter added, “Balancing long-term vision with immediate operational needs is essential for driving sustainable growth and delivering consistent results. I approach this by setting a clear roadmap that aligns both strategic goals and day-to-day actions, ensuring that short-term objectives actively contribute to our broader mission. This includes prioritizing initiatives that create quick wins while also laying the groundwork for future growth. For example, I focus on projects that improve operational efficiency—such as automating routine processes or investing in scalable technology—so we’re better positioned to take on larger strategic initiatives as we evolve.

At the same time, I place a strong emphasis on adaptability, recognizing that Government regulators, market conditions, and customer needs can shift quickly in a fast-moving world. By regularly revisiting our long-term strategy and remaining open to adjustment, I ensure that we’re not only keeping up with current demands but also building resilience for the future. This balance allows us to be responsive in the present without losing sight of our overarching goals, ultimately supporting both financial stability and continuous innovation in the business.”

Assessing The Right Trends

Understanding emerging trends and adapting to them is crucial for the success of a business. We asked, “What methods do you use to analyze market trends, and how have these influenced your business decisions?”

“As an innovator and visionary, I take a unique approach to analyzing market trends by focusing less on competitors’ specific software features and more on their social media presence and client feedback. This perspective offers invaluable insights into customer pain points and expectations, enabling me to gauge real-time client sentiment across the industry. While my team conducts detailed feature comparisons with competitors, I focus on how we can enhance and differentiate our software to stay ahead. My goal is not to follow industry trends but to anticipate them—constantly envisioning features that elevate our software’s value and utility before they become standard.

Additionally, I ensure to keep track of government compliance updates and general requirements so that the software is always adaptive and compliant. This allows for making rapid changes that help safeguard clients and keep them ready. I am at the forefront of product strategy and regulatory awareness, product evolution in this case, aimed at ensuring that we do not only meet but exceed the expectations of the markets, which is revealed through how we respond to new market trends and innovations from the competition.” Christian added.

Current Offerings At Datanova

We were interested in learning more about the services offered by Christian’s firm Datanova. So, we inquired, “Tell us more about your services and if you are planning to add something new in the future.”

Christian Krauter replied, “Our services are designed to provide comprehensive support through a platform that is both versatile and responsive to our clients’ needs. Currently, we offer a wide range of API integrations that connect seamlessly with Microsoft products, major financial software, government databases, and CRM systems, ensuring that our clients can leverage a cohesive, interconnected ecosystem. This year is especially focused on expanding our API capabilities, as we’re dedicated to enhancing the platform’s ability to communicate fluidly with even more systems. With additional APIs on the way, we’re continually refining how our clients access and utilize external data to streamline operations.​

Looking to the future, we’re excited about integrating AI into our platform. Rather than adopting out-of-the-box solutions, we are developing our own AI modules based on open-source models from Facebook, tailoring them to meet the unique demands of our clients. This AI integration will empower our platform to deliver smarter, more personalized insights, transforming how our clients interact with and benefit from their data. By combining robust API connectivity with advanced AI capabilities, we’re committed to pushing the boundaries of what our platform can achieve, enabling clients to navigate an increasingly digital landscape with ease and innovation.”

Emerging Trends Of Christian’s Industry

To learn Christian Krauter’s perspective on the emerging trends of the future, we asked, “What emerging technologies do you believe will have the most significant impact on your industry in the next five years?”

“In the next five years, I believe AI will profoundly impact the service industry by transforming how we engage with customers, automate tasks, and analyze data. As AI becomes increasingly sophisticated, its ability to personalize experiences at scale will be a game-changer, particularly in customer service, where predictive algorithms can anticipate needs, enabling faster and more tailored responses. Additionally, automation through AI-driven bots and workflows will streamline operations, freeing up resources to focus on complex, value-added tasks. This technology is already shifting our industry’s landscape, but its potential for refined customer insights and operational efficiency will redefine standards.

Moreover, the potential of new technologies such as Augmented Reality (AR) and Quantum Computing is enormous. In Health and Aged Care, AR can provide virtual experiences with products or services beforehand to raise customer interest and attachment to the brand. Finally, Quantum Computing that most likely facilitate fast decision-making and efficient management of resources in many quantitative heavy sectors, setting a new benchmark for efficiency across the service sector.” He mentioned.

Employee Empowerment And Growth

Employees are a crucial part of every business and ensuring their satisfaction is paramount for the success of the business. So, we asked, “What strategies do you implement to maintain high levels of employee engagement and satisfaction?”

Christian Krauter shared, “To maintain high levels of employee engagement and satisfaction, we focus on fostering a culture of support, collaboration, and continuous growth. For our clients, we provide a personalized service model, assigning a dedicated implementation team to each organization. This team not only manages the initial setup but also ensures a smooth transition into daily operations. Post-implementation, our clients continue to receive tailored support from a dedicated team of Data Captains who are committed to meeting their needs, offering reliable assistance, and strengthening client relationships over the long term. This commitment to quality service gives our team a clear purpose, driving engagement as they see the tangible impact of their work.  

Internally, we prioritize a positive workplace culture through group activities outside of work, fostering team spirit and camaraderie. To support personal and professional growth, we provide ongoing training opportunities, keeping our team equipped with the latest skills and industry knowledge. We also encourage open communication and actively listen to each employee, valuing their insights and addressing their individual needs. By creating a supportive environment where every team member feels heard and empowered, we’re able to maintain a high level of job satisfaction and engagement, which ultimately reflects in the quality of service we provide to our clients.”

Securing A Strong Legacy

We ended the session by asking, “How do you want your business to be remembered, and what steps are you taking to secure that legacy?”

“Simple is the best, ERP and ESS system for Australian Government Service Providers to manage their business. And for the music, I quote a friend ‘Your music sparks dreamy thoughts’ for this to continue. What are the steps I am taking; well I love what I do.” Christian concluded.

title: Boeing Notifies More than 400 Employees of Their Layoffs
author: editor
excerpt: As the corporation battles to recover from financial and regulatory issues as well as an eight-week strike by its machinists’ union, Boeing has sent layoff warnings to over 400 members of its professional aerospace labor union. According to The Seattle Times, the pink slips were distributed to members of the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace, or SPEEA, last week. title: Wall Street loses Ground as Powell Recommends Caution on interest-Rate Reduction
author: editor
excerpt: Wall Street’s main indexes fell on Friday after Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell indicated there was no need to hasten interest-rate decreases, raising US Treasury yields and weighing on stocks. In a speech on Thursday, Powell cited continuing economic expansion, a strong labor market, and inflation over the Fed’s 2% target as reasons the central bank can afford to be cautious about the speed and scope of future rate decreases. Powell’s remarks came after consumer and producer price data this week showed continuing inflation. On Friday, data indicated that US retail sales rose somewhat more than predicted in October, but the underlying momentum in consumer spending appeared to stall at the start of the fourth quarter. According to the CME FedWatch tool, traders upped their bets that the Fed will leave interest rates on hold at its December meeting, pricing in a 41.3% possibility, up from 14% the previous month. “Overall, retail sales were pretty excellent. That’s exactly what Powell was saying yesterday, that if the economy remains reasonably strong and inflation approaches our target, they can afford to be patient and cut rates more slowly than previously thought,” said Mike Dickson, head of research and quantitative strategies at Horizon Investments. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 149.62 points, or 0.34%, to 43,601.24, the S&P 500 dropped 40.21 points, or 0.68%, to 5,908.96, and the Nasdaq Composite plummeted 237.47 points, or 1.24%, to 18,870.18. title: Adnoc Gas and India’s GAIL Enter into a 10-year LNG Sales and Purchase Agreement
author: editor
excerpt: The largest natural gas company in India, GAIL India Limited, and Adnoc Gas have inked a 10-year Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) for the supply of up to 0.52 million metric tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) annually (mmtpa), beginning in 2026. The Heads of Agreement between ADNOC Gas and GAIL, which were previously announced in January, are now finalized by the SPA. The Das Island liquefaction facility of ADNOC Gas, which can produce 6.0 mmtpa of LNG, will provide the LNG. It is the third-oldest LNG plant in the world that is still operating. More than 3,500 LNG cargoes have been supplied to clients worldwide since operations started in 1977. “This agreement reflects our ambition to capture future growth opportunities in gas demand and strengthens ADNOC Gas’ role as a responsible and dependable global natural gas provider,” stated Rashid Khalfan Al Mazrouei, Senior Vice President, Marketing. Additionally, it strengthens our standing as India’s go-to partner for energy solutions. The industrial coal-to-gas conversion in China and the growing usage of LNG for power production throughout Southern and Southeast Asia are predicted to produce a 15% increase in global LNG demand over the next ten years. As part of our plan to increase our share of the expanding worldwide demand for lower carbon intensity products like ours, we are dedicated to more than tripling our capacity to produce LNG. title: Leaders Provide Conflicting Perspectives at the Baku Conference
author: editor
excerpt: At UN-led discussions on Wednesday, world leaders presented divergent ideas on how to address climate change, as a new report cautioned that the world needs to achieve carbon neutrality far sooner than anticipated. Preliminary findings from a global network of scientists at the Global Carbon Project show that this year saw record-high emissions of carbon dioxide, which warms the planet, from coal, gas, and oil. The research was released as world leaders convened in Azerbaijan for the COP29 climate talks, which intended to reach an agreement to increase assistance for developing countries to help them transition to cleaner energy and react to climate shocks. According to the study, the world must now achieve net-zero CO2 emissions by the late 2030s rather than 2050 in order to accomplish the ambitious goal of keeping warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius set forth in the Paris Agreement. Yalchin Rafiyev, Azerbaijan’s main negotiator for COP29, stated, “This is what the presidency has been promoting since the beginning of this year — the time window is narrowing, shrinking — and we need to act urgently.” Reaching an agreement on climate finance “will pave the way for us to realize this opportunity,” and “there are still possibilities for keeping 1.5C within reach. title: Drivers Need to follow these Six Safety Precautions in case their Car Breaks down While they are Driving
author: editor
excerpt: Six safety precautions have been developed by the Abu Dhabi Police that drivers must follow in case their car breaks down while they are driving. For the driver’s safety, these include pulling off the road and heading to the closest secure emergency parking space, as well as avoiding being inside a broken-down car or on the road. It is recommended that drivers only use the right-hand side of the road in an emergency if it is absolutely required. In order to warn other drivers, it is also advised that a reflective emergency triangle be positioned safely behind the car. It is also recommended that drivers activate their four-way warning signals and dial 999 for help. A video outlining the steps to be taken in the event of a vehicle breakdown was posted by the Abu Dhabi Police Department on social media. The “Safety Path 2” campaign included this activity. The campaign uses digital traffic awareness to encourage adherence to safety procedures in the event of a car breakdown. The significance of staying off the road, finding the closest safe parking space, and avoiding being inside a broken-down vehicle are all emphasized in the video. The chief executives of KESH and Masdar, Erald Elezi and Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi, respectively, inked the deal. Ideas are born all the time, and the main thing is a team that picks up and gets into all the processes and dives into the details with inspiration. CASPIT is a group of companies specializing in the trade of petroleum products, the production and trade of fertilizers, the construction and operation of solar power plants, grain trade and logistics operation.” CASPIT is a leading group of companies that has extensive experience in petrochemicals, energy, and fertilizers. title: After a Volcano erupts, international Airlines suspend Flights to Bali
author: editor
excerpt: After a neighboring volcano threw an ash tower miles into the sky on Wednesday, international airlines canceled flights to and from Bali, a vacation island in Indonesia, leaving travelers stranded. A day earlier, Mount Lewotobi Laki-Laki on Flores island erupted a nine-kilometer (5.6-mile) tower, disrupting at least 16 international routes, according to a statement from Bali’s international airport’s general manager. Ahmad Syaugi Shahab announced on Wednesday that all flights from Singapore, Hong Kong, Qatar, India, Australia, Malaysia, China’s Pudong, and South Korea’s Incheon were either delayed or grounded. According to an AFP journalist at Bali’s airport, Malaysia Airlines, AirAsia, India’s IndiGo, Singapore’s Scoot, and Australia’s Jetstar, Qantas, and Virgin Australia all listed flights as cancelled on Wednesday. “Volcanic ash poses a significant threat to safe operations of the aircraft in the vicinity of volcanic clouds,” AirAsia stated when it made a number of cancellation announcements. Cathay Pacific of Hong Kong also announced the cancellation of its flights and rescheduled its operations to and from Bali for Thursday. A visionary entrepreneur and change-maker, dedicated to driving transformative impact in Africa, Dr. Maureen Mandipaza is the Founder and CEO of Momentors Academy, an early pioneer in education and empowerment, and also the Founder of Dravens Healthcare, an innovative leader in healthcare solutions. Under the leadership of Dr. Maureen, the ventures undertaken have transformed numerous lives, especially concerning education, empowerment, community development, and healthcare.

Through uncompromising dedication to socio-economic inclusiveness and the growth of human potential, Dr Mandipaza has epitomized an exemplary legacy of innovation and leadership. She has empowered hundreds of women, youth, and marginalized communities through vocational training, mentorship, and access to health.

Vision Behind Building Dravens Healthcare

Dr Maureen Mandipaza founded Dravens Healthcare to provide compassionate, personalized care that goes beyond traditional standards. After losing her mother at a tender age, her topmost priority was to make a difference in other people’s lives through healthcare. Eventually, Dr. Maureen launched the company in my living room after seeing gaps in healthcare provision, particularly in how homecare services were managed.

Dr. Maureen Mandipaza shares, “My vision has always been to create a business model that prioritizes quality, dignity, and empowerment for both clients and employees building leaders through mentorship. Over the years, this vision expanded into empowering women through Momentors Academy, where we offer vocational training and entrepreneurship coaching, particularly in underserved communities in Zimbabwe. Our work is centered around creating sustainable, transformative opportunities that change lives across generations.”

Adaptability To The Latest Innovation

Fast-paced digital transformation has been transforming businesses. Dr. Maureen mentions that technology plays a pivotal role at Dravens Healthcare, particularly in care delivery and training. They use various digital platforms to manage care plans, track performance, and communicate with staff, which ensures that services are delivered efficiently and consistently.

“At Momentors Academy, we’re bridging the gap in education through digital learning platforms, expanding access to marginalized communities and remote students. Our focus is on process optimization, enhancing internal efficiency, and delivering exceptional experiences for clients and students alike.” She adds.

Redefining Businesses With AI

Dr. Maureen Mandipaza believes that AI is revolutionizing many industries, including healthcare, and it will be crucial in delivering personalized and predictive care. She further mentions that her company is looking into AI-driven solutions that can help with data analysis for better care outcomes, and even automating administrative tasks to allow their staff more time to focus on individualized care.

“At Momentors Academy, we’re also exploring AI in e-learning platforms to create personalized learning journeys for our students. We’re still in the early stages of adoption, but I’m excited about the potential AI offers in enhancing both care and education.” Dr. Maureen adds.

Staying Aligned With The Market Trends

Adaptability to the latest market trends ensures a strong position for the business. Dr. Maureen shares that the key to staying aligned with market changes is agility and a willingness to continuously learn. She further adds, “My company does ongoing market assessments, industry conferences, and all this with open communication channels with their stakeholders. We keep our finger on the pulse of healthcare trends and educational shifts, reviewing our strategies quarterly to ensure that it is relevant, adaptable, and responsive to changing regulations and markets.”

Career-Defining Moment

Every successful business leader has a certain defining moment in their entrepreneurial journey that shapes their business philosophy later. Likewise, Dr. Maureen had one of the most defining moments during the launch of Momentors Academy in Zimbabwe. She says, “Seeing the immense need for vocational skills and entrepreneurship coaching, especially for women, made me realize the power of education in transforming lives.”

She further let us know that her journey was never easy, as she had limited resources, but it taught her that true empowerment comes from providing people with tools for self-sufficiency at the same time. “This has deeply shaped my philosophy: empowerment must be sustainable, transferable, and transformative, which has been the driving force behind all my ventures.” Dr. Maureen adds.

Fostering Constant Improvement

At Dravens Healthcare and Momentors Academy, continuous learning is a cornerstone of their culture. Dr. Maureen Mandipaza shares, “We identify training gaps through regular spot checks and refresher sessions, while workshops, mentorship programs, and cutting-edge resources empower our staff and students to grow and improve constantly.”

Addressing The Challenges

Agility in business requires constant reassessment and an openness to change. “We have streamlined our decision-making processes, allowing for quicker responses to both opportunities and challenges.

For instance, during the pandemic, we had to shift many of our operations online almost overnight, and adaptability has remained a core strength. Regular team feedback sessions, market analysis, and close monitoring of industry trends help us pivot swiftly when needed.” She adds.

Impactful Projects By Dr. Maureen Mandipaza

Momentors Academy has been a game-changer for Dr. Maureen, empowering hundreds of women with vocational skills training and also addressing societal issues such as early child marriages, poverty, and substance abuse. “Being able to witness graduates starting up businesses and therefore changing their lives is highly rewarding. We have decided to extend our reach through franchising in Southern Africa.” She adds.

Aligning Visions And Business Requirements

Dr. Maureen Mandipaza shares with us that in the short term, she primarily focused on expanding Dravens Healthcare nationally through their franchise model, ensuring that the brand reaches more clients across the UK. She further adds, “For Momentors Academy, we’re working on securing additional resources and partnerships to scale our vocational training programs across Southern Africa. In the long term, I envision expanding our academy’s reach globally and launching more projects in Zimbabwe, creating employment and sustainable business opportunities for the community.”

Words Of Wisdom For Beginners

Addressing the beginners in her field, Dr. Maureen shares, “Be relentless in the pursuit of your vision but stay grounded in your purpose. It’s important to build a business with a solid foundation—whether that’s through education, mentorship, or partnerships. Also, don’t be afraid to adapt and innovate as the world around you changes. Most importantly, invest in people; your business is only as strong as the team and community that supports it. And remember, empowerment isn’t just about giving people opportunities; it’s about equipping them to create their own.”

content:
Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia, CEO of Higher Health, is leading a transformative mission to equip South African youth with Skills for Life and Soft Skills essential for personal and professional growth. Higher Health, operating under South Africa’s Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET), provides holistic health, wellness, and psychosocial services to over 2.5 million students across universities, TVET colleges, and CET colleges. Their Skills for Life and Soft Skills programme, accredited at NQF Level 5 through the Qualifications Certificate Trades Occupation (QCTO), teaches vital workplace competencies, including empathy, conflict resolution, digital literacy, teamwork, and time management, aiming to improve employability and life readiness. Prof. Ahluwalia’s vision emphasizes resilience, equality, and social responsibility, particularly through efforts to combat gender-based violence (GBV) and support mental health on campuses. With notable partnerships, such as with UNESCO, Higher Health is pioneering initiatives like the “Transforming MEN’talities” project, addressing GBV prevention and empowering students with essential Skills for Life and Soft Skills to thrive in diverse, challenging environments.

A Journey of Purpose

We started the interview by asking, “Can you tell us about your journey and what inspired you to focus on healthcare, particularly in South Africa?”

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “My journey in healthcare began in India, where I earned my medical degree, and later expanded globally with my work in countries like Germany and Mauritius. South Africa, however, provided a unique challenge and opportunity due to the magnitude of health and social issues here, particularly HIV, TB, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), teenage pregnancy, maternal death and mental health crises among others. I was inspired by the resilience of the people and the need to transform health systems to be more equitable and effective. My focus is on building a healthcare infrastructure that not only treats but also educates and empowers students and youth of South Africa.”

Positioning Higher Health

Entrepreneur Mirror: In your perspective, how would you describe Higher Health as an organisation, and where does it currently stand within its market?

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “Higher Health is a national agency of the Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) in South Africa. Its primary mission is to inspire success and promote holistic health, well-being and psychosocial support services in 2.5 million students across 26 universities, 50 public Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges, and 9 Community Education and Training (CET) colleges.

Higher Health has established the Skills for Life and Soft Skills online programme accredited at NQF Level5 by theQCTOin South Africa and also in partnership with the Health and Welfare SETA (HWSETA). The accredited programme offers the Top 10 Soft Skills of the workplace while building resilience amongst our young people at early stages of development.

Top 10 Soft Skills of the workplace, such as:

  1. Empathy, Listening and Counselling;
  2. Civic Responsibility and Peer Education;
  3. Conflict Resolution;
  4. Creativity, Critical Thinking and Problem Solving;
  5. Decision Making;
  6. Digital Literacy;
  7. Presentation Skills, Public Speaking and Communication;
  8. Resilience, Confidence and Self-Motivation;
  9. Teamwork, Organizational Skills and Leadership Skills; and
  10. Time-Management and Goal-Setting

As a bridging or exit course across our sector it  aims towards building Skills for Life and Soft Skills for better employability and complementing every hard skills offered by Universities and Colleges that will help better economic productivity. This unique first of its kind – NQF Level5 programme is built in all South African major languages including now the sign language.

Soft skills are needed in bridging our skills gap – an attempt to build a nation that has gone through a lot!”

Empowering Youth Globally

Entrepreneur Mirror: Can you tell us about your vision and impact of the Skills for Life and Soft Skills online programme? How is Higher Health working to ensure that young people around the world gain access to essential skills that not only improve employability but also contribute to their overall growth and well-being?

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “My passion is in empowering every young person with the skills they need for life – skills that go beyond academics or vocational training. I’m honoured to say that Higher Health is now acknowledged globally as a key partner of UNESCO, making us Africa’s second leading nonprofit partner for UNESCO. My vision is that the United Nations’ 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), also known as the Global Goals, shouldn’t just stay at the policy level among decision-makers. They need to reach every young person directly, in ways they can relate to and understand, ideally in their language of choice.

So, we’re working to make the Skills for Life and Soft Skills online programme accessible at a basic literacy level to bring these Goals to life for youth. We believe that every life matters, every young person matters. Skills for Life are the future of employability, the future of being a parent, and the cornerstone for the next generation. This generation needs to adapt to welcome and mentor the new generation, and we can only achieve that through a transformative approach.

Through this programme, we’re providing certificates, quality-assured and UNESCO-endorsed systems, all in their chosen language. But we’re also addressing critical issues that affect their lives – gender awareness from early ages, mental health, resilience, prevention of substance abuse, climate change consciousness, civic responsibility, protecting our democracy, digital and AI literacy, ethics, financial literacy, and support for disability inclusion. Higher Health specializes in teaching soft skills to help them thrive.

Our students are learning conflict management, time management, goal setting, empathy, critical thinking, and problem-solving. These are the skills today’s workforce needs, to be balanced and adaptable. Hard skills alone are no longer enough; they must be complemented by these soft skills. With each of these competencies, we’re building resilience in young people. As a result, we’re making their CVs stand out to employers by adding micro-credentials, credits, and certificates, all easily accessible on mobile devices and applications. This is the revolution we’re championing – empowering youth, strengthening employability, and shaping tomorrow’s leaders.”

Structure of the Skills Qualification

Entrepreneur Mirror: Can you explain the structure of the Skills for Life and Soft Skills online qualification?

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “The qualification is divided into eight comprehensive modules, each designed to address different challenges that youth face today. These modules include Civic Education, Gender Education, Mental Health, Disability, Sexuality Education, Substance Abuse and Resilience, Climate Change, and Financial Literacy. Each module is credit-bearing. After the successful completion of each module, a student receives a Certificate which can be added to their Curriculum Vitae (CV) and also shared on their professional and social networks such as LinkedIn.”

Transforming Student Health

Entrepreneur Mirror: Higher Health has become a leader in addressing student health, wellness and psychosocial support in South Africa. What do you consider the organization’s most significant achievement so far?

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “One of our most significant achievements has been the successful integration of holistic health, well-being and psychosocial support services into the Post-School Education and Training (PSET) sector. Our programmes reach over 2.5 million students annually in 26 public Universities, 50 Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Colleges and 9 Community Education and Training (CET) Colleges across South Africa, providing crucial services like primary healthcare, HIV testing, mental health support, and gender-based violence (GBV) interventions among others.

Our partnership with UNESCO, as we have become an implementing partner towards the Transforming MEN’talitiesinitiative and Soft Skills programme through our innovative Skills for Life and Soft Skills qualification and modules, is a groundbreaking movement led by South Africa, with the world looking on as this pivotal moment unfolded.

The partnership with UNESCO has launched successfully with over 88 Ambassadors and permanent delegates of UNESCO from different countries, all in support of South Africa’s efforts in transforming gender equality. South Africa is showing the world how it’s done – a way to do it, with 88 countries rallying behind the Transforming MEN’talities initiative. Together, we are making global strides and pioneering a movement for gender equality andlasting change!”

Tackling Gender-Based Violence

Entrepreneur Mirror: What is the most pressing challenge that Higher Health faces today, and how are you tackling it?

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “The most pressing challenge we face today is gender-based violence. The Post-School Education and Training (PSET) sector is home to over 2.5 million youth, including more than 51% adolescent girls and young women, and faces a serious GBV crisis. The statistics are alarming, with South African women experiencing a lifetime risk of 45.6% for GBVF, well above the global average. Furthermore, 10% of all reported rape cases in the country occur within the higher education sector, underscoring the urgent need for intervention.

Higher Health’s presence across all campuses in TVET Colleges, Universities and CET Colleges in South Africa ensures our commitment in tackling this pandemic. Over the past two years, more than 350,000 students have participated in the Higher Health Transforming MENtalities& Soft skills curriculum. In 2022-2023 period over 316,048 students engaged in Transforming MENtalities dialogues with over 219,316 young people voluntarily undergoing a Gender and Intimate partner Violence risk assessments tool kit with Higher Health And with 18,994 young people identifying themselves at high-risk for GBV. Over 12,682 young lives reported GBV and are linked to psychosocial counselling and where necessary legal and judicial support through this programme. Higher Health’s efforts aim to prevent toxic relationships and save lives through early identification and support. Early intervention Saves lives!”

Key Milestones & Transformative Experiences

Entrepreneur Mirror: Can you share the key milestones and experiences that have shaped your successful career over the past two decades?

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “My journey has been a tapestry woven with significant milestones and meaningful experiences. At its core, I began as a medical doctor, a role that not only bestowed upon me the knowledge of healing but also instilled a profound sense of humility and a human-centric approach in my leadership style. Writing the inaugural chapter for the BRICS academic forum, launched by former President Zuma, marked a pivotal moment, opening doors to cross-border collaboration and my involvement in ministerial task teams in South Africa. My close association with esteemed United Nations (UN) agencies like World Health Organisation (WHO) and UNESCO allowed me to champion transformative girl education and gender equality, speaking at global forums such as the Global Citizen Forum and the UN CSW.”

Leadership Lessons

Entrepreneur Mirror: What advice would you, as an established leader in the industry, offer to emerging leaders who are looking to make their mark and succeed in their respective fields?

Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia replied, “The advice I would like to impart to emerging leaders is to embody humility, embrace patience, and be perpetual learners. Remember, as a leader, your role is to uplift and empower those around you, and to truly understand them, you must learn from them and be the people you aim to lead.”

Vision for the Future

Lastly we asked, “Looking ahead, what are your long-term goals for Higher Health, and how do you see it evolving in the next 5-10 years?”

“In the next 5-10 years, I see Higher Health expanding its reach and impact, not just in Africa but across the globe. We aim to continue growing our holistic health, well-being and psychosocial support services and educational programs, with a focus on integrating digital health solutions and making healthcare more accessible. We also want to further develop our partnerships with international organizations like UNESCO to ensure that our programs are globally recognized and continue to set new standards in student health, well-being and psychosocial support services. My ultimate goal is to create a generation of young people who are not only academically and professionally prepared but also healthy, resilient, and socially responsible.” Dr. Ramneek Ahluwalia Concluded

title: DLD to Improve Sustainability and Innovation in the Real Estate Industry
author: editor
excerpt: The occasion is in line with DLD’s dedication to accomplishing the lofty objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and the Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033. The Real Estate Policy Lab was organized by the Dubai Land Department (DLD) as part of its continuous efforts to encourage innovation in the real estate industry and create laws that support expansion and sustainability. The Real Estate Alliances Policy, the Resilience and Sustainability Policy, the Real Estate Reputation Policy, and the Data Sharing and Publication Policy are the four main sector policies this project is discussing and improving. These regulations align with DLD’s goal of achieving the lofty goals of the Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033 and the Dubai Economic Agenda D33. Eng Marwan Ahmed bin Ghalita, Director General of DLD, attended the event, which took place at the company’s headquarters. He thanked everyone who attended and emphasized the significance of these kinds of initiatives in laying out a plan for sustainable development and governance in Dubai’s real estate industry. Dr. Mahmoud Al Burai, Director of the Real Estate Policies and Innovation Department, introduced the event, outlining the four policies. title: Masdar is Planning to build a 1 GW Wind Farm in Kazakhstan
author: editor
excerpt: With the signature of the project’s Investment Agreement, Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC—Masdar, the clean energy giant of the United Arab Emirates—and its partners have accomplished a major milestone in the construction of their 1GW windfarm in Kazakhstan. Nurlan Zhakupov, Chairman of the Board of Samruk-Kazyna, Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi, Chief Executive Officer of Masdar, and Nurlan Baibazarov, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy of the Republic of Kazakhstan, observed the signing of the agreement on the sidelines of COP29 in Baku. Almassadam Satkaliyev, Kazakhstan’s Energy Minister, and Abdulla Zayed, Masdar’s Director of Business and Project Development, inked the deal. Masdar is the principal developer of the 1GW wind project, which is being co-developed by W Solar, Qazaq Green Power (a company of the Samruk-Kazyna Group), and the Kazakhstan Investment Development Fund. It is expected to be one of the biggest wind farms in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) region and marks a substantial investment in the nation’s potential as a major clean energy generator. Construction of the wind farm is anticipated to start in Q1 2026. When finished, it will supply electricity to about 300,000 houses in southern Kazakhstan, preventing 2 million tonnes of CO2 emissions annually. author: editor
excerpt: The Al Ain Court of First Instance dismissed a lawsuit against another person. The lawsuit demanded Dhs35,000 in debt repayment, Dhs10,000 in material and moral compensation, a 12% delay interest on the amount owed from the date of the judicial claim until full payment, and fees, expenses, and legal fees. According to the appellant, he transferred Dhs141,000 from his account to the appellee’s, who paid off a portion but refused to pay the remaining amount. In addition to requiring him to pay, the appellee filed a memorandum asking that the plaintiff be given the decisive oath and that the case be assigned for inquiry. The plaintiff also produced a copy of the bank transfers. In addition, the appellee claimed that he had borrowed any money from the plaintiff, claiming that the sums they had exchanged were for modest business ventures and that he owed him nothing. The court ordered the appellee to take the definitive oath through one of the audio-visual connection channels. He swore that he had not borrowed Dhs141,000 from the plaintiff and that no amount was owed on his loan. The plaintiff requested that the appellee take the decisive oath, and the appellee did, the court explained. This resolved the dispute and confirmed that his debt was not outstanding for the sum claimed. Consequently, the court dismissed the lawsuit. title: The COP29 Summit is Clouded by Trump’s Concerns and the Leaders’ Absence
author: editor
excerpt: In a significant step toward enabling nations to sell credits to satisfy their climate commitments, governments at the COP29 negotiations agreed new UN criteria for international carbon markets on Monday. After nearly ten years of intricate negotiations, over 200 countries agreed on many key ground conditions for launching a market on the first day of the UN climate conference in Azerbaijan. Mukhtar Babayev, the president of COP29, praised the “breakthrough” but stated that further effort was required. Experts stated that although the decision moves closer to a long-sought UN-backed market trading in high-quality credits, other crucial elements of the broader framework still require negotiation. Simon Stiell, the UN climate chief, stated at Baku Stadium, “Let’s get rid of the notion that climate finance is charity.” “Every country, even the biggest and wealthiest, has a vested interest in achieving a bold new climate finance goal.” However, economic issues, the wars in Gaza and Ukraine, and the election of climate change denier Donald Trump for a second term as president of the United States, the largest economy in the world—are vying for attention with the financial aim. US President Joe Biden, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen are among the political figures who are anticipated to abstain. title: In Dubai, Flexible Work Schedules and Remote work Guidelines Reduce Morning rush Hour Commute Time by 30%
author: editor
excerpt: Dubai is taking steps to improve traffic efficiency and facilitate mobility after Sheikh Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defense, and Chairman of the Executive Council, approved the city’s traffic flow plan. The initiative intends to increase the use of remote work rules and flexible working hours throughout the emirate in order to strike a balance between corporate productivity and quality of life. To lessen traffic congestion, both the public and private sectors are urged to implement these strategies. The first survey included 644 businesses with more than 320,000 workers, and the second included 12,000 private sector workers. According to research, 32% of private businesses presently have policies allowing remote work, while 58% of businesses say they are prepared to increase remote employment. Furthermore, 31% of businesses have adopted flexible work schedules, and 66% of those that do not already have the policy in place may do so in the future. According to the study, allowing employees in the public and private sectors to work remotely four or five days a month and instituting flexible working hours with a two-hour start window can reduce morning peak travel times in Dubai by 30%. A draft resolution for the summit emphasizes the Palestinian people’s “national rights,” “foremost among which is their right to freedom and to an independent, sovereign state. ” Prince Mohammed also emphasized the growing relationship between Saudi Arabia and Iran and urged Israel to refrain from attacking Iran. title: The Federal Decree Creating the UAE Aid Agency is Issued by the UAE President
author: editor
excerpt: His Highness the President In order to create the UAE Aid Agency, which is connected to the International Humanitarian and Philanthropic Council, Sheikh Mohamed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan issued Federal Decree No. 27 of 2024. The agency will possess complete legal power to act and an autonomous juridical entity. Implementing foreign aid programs in accordance with the overarching international humanitarian affairs policy is the agency’s responsibility. content:
Recently, we had the chance to interview Balaji Anbil. He is a visionary Founder and Managing Director of Tenacium, a leader in technology, AI-driven solutions, and innovation. With his proven track record of innovation, strategic leadership, and entrepreneurial spirit, Balaji has become a respected voice in the industry.

With deep expertise in the realm of AI, cybersecurity, digital transformation, and strategic consulting, Balaji navigated the complex landscape of the dynamic and ever-evolving technology domain with expertise. His forward-thinking strategy for Tenacium has positioned it right at the cutting edge. Cutting-edge solutions delivered to the business through this solution can help businesses thrive. In this session, Balaji shares his inspiring journey – from conceptualizing Tenacium to growing into a leader in the technology space.

The Beginning

We started the interview by asking, “Can you walk us through your professional journey and how it led to where you are today?​”

Balaji Anbil shared, “I had the opportunity to work globally across Asia, the US, Europe, the Middle East, and across multiple sectors, including IT, investment banking, energy trading, professional services, public sector, and cybersecurity. The journey has been diverse, but the common thread has been a focus on using data and technology to solve complex problems.  

In between, I did my exec-MBA from Warwick Business School. Before jumping onto the entrepreneurial bandwagon, I learned a few things while running similar-sized models at bigger businesses. All these collectively have helped me to build Tenacium DC and to focus on providing cutting-edge data capabilities and cybersecurity services.”

Overcoming Major Adversities

Challenging phases are a part of every career path. To learn how Balaji Anbil overcame the same, we asked, “Reflecting on your career, what have been some of the most significant challenges you’ve faced, and how did you overcome them?”​

Balaji Anbil shared, “To give a size of magnitude of my career opportunities, before Tenacium, I led the Digital, Data & Cyber security aspects of a £1.2B Judicial reform program. However, this has been my biggest challenge till date. I bootstrapped and built Tenacium; part of this, I had to manage consulting work while simultaneously developing Tenacium – the fundamental reason for Tenacium is the JEDAI platform idea, that I strongly believe will transform the cybersecurity environment.” 

“Balancing multiple projects was tough. But I overcame this by embracing our company ethos, trusting and empowering my team, and coaching them when needed, resulting in a successful, collaborative outcome.”

Striking A Perfect Balance

We further asked, “How do you balance long-term vision with short-term operational needs?”

“At Tenacium, we are taking a radical shift to cybersecurity. Our JEDAI Platform is our long-term focus, and it is a mission that our customers can achieve resilience as an outcome.    

Having operated globally, I have been building a proprietary consulting methodology – JEEA (Just Enough Enterprise Architecture) which enables us to adapt quickly to customer needs while ensuring long-term goals, such as digital transformation, are met. This flexible yet focused approach has been internalized within our business, which allows us to cater to the immediate needs of our clients without losing sight of our broader vision​.” Balaji replied.

Current Offerings

We were intrigued to learn more about the services offered by Balaji Anbil’s organization. So, we asked, “Tell us more about your services and if you are planning to add something new in the future.”

Balaji Anbil shared, “We focus on three main service lines: Innovation Labs, Advisory & Consulting, and Professional Services, solely within the data and cybersecurity domains. 

Our customer promise is that we provide tested advice fueled by our Innovation service line. Looking ahead, we’ll launch Experimentation as a Service in 2025, offering clients the chance to test strategies in our Innovation Labs. Under our Professional Services line, as ISO27001-2022 is gaining traction, we have built a comprehensive T5 cybersecurity framework that gives a unique approach to not only ISO compliance but a continuous assessment across multiple cyber frameworks.  

AI is the new buzzword, but long before the ChatGPT sensation, I had spotted an opportunity as early as 2020 and started planning to build a platform that becomes a backbone for the industry to use AI safely and most importantly within their corporate perimeters. Currently, our JEEA consulting methodology empowers flexible, rapid client support. With recent expansion into India, we’re set to further grow into the Middle East and beyond.”

Assessing The Right Trends For Tenacium

Eager to learn more about the approaches adopted by Balaji Anbil to assess the right move at the right trend, we inquired, “What methods do you use to analyze market trends, and how have these influenced your business decisions?”

Balaji Anbil said, “We leverage data analytics and our global network to stay ahead of trends in the cybersecurity and data domains. By maintaining close connections with clients across different regions, we tailor our services to their evolving needs. This global approach has allowed us to make informed decisions on product offerings and consulting advice.   

The good thing about this global approach is the talent pool that comes with it. They also get to learn from other engagements which keeps them strongly engaged as well as pick up more ideas and fuel our innovation.”

Embracing Digital Transformation

The fast-paced digital revolution is redefining the way businesses perform. We asked, “How has digital transformation affected your business model?​”

“Digital transformation has been a catalyst for our business, driving demand for both data and cybersecurity services. Digital transformation is essentially Data transformation and securing that Data. Our JEDAI platform and T5 Cybersecurity Framework are designed to help organizations achieve resilience in a rapidly evolving digital landscape. By focusing on these transformations, we can support businesses in becoming more secure and adaptable​.” He replied.

Potential Trends Of The Industry

To get a glimpse of Balaji Anbil’s view on potential technological advancements in his industry, we inquired, “What emerging technologies do you believe will have the most significant impact on your industry in the next five years?”

Balaji Anbil mentioned, “Applied AI (Human-Machine Combo), Circular Energy (reuse & recycle), and Autonomous & Connected Vehicles will have a profound impact on cybersecurity over the next five years, particularly in terms of new job families, proactive, and predictive technologies. At Tenacium, we focus on helping our clients establish the foundations for AI-driven capabilities, rather than rushing into ChatGPT style adoption. 

Our emphasis is on data quality because data, not AI alone, is the cornerstone of success. Businesses often face significant challenges in obtaining good quality, structured, and usable data, and this will be crucial to harnessing the full potential of AI to keep their competitive edge.”

Empowering Employees In Tenacium

Ensuring employee satisfaction is paramount for the success of any business. We asked, “What strategies do you implement to maintain high levels of employee engagement and satisfaction?”​

Balaji Anbil added, “I have always been a people person, and that has helped shape our ethos – implicit trust, ensuring transparency as a business and practicing openness in an individual context, that then fosters respect for each other and that then leads to sharing gratitude. 

We refer to our team as ‘colleagues’ rather than employees, and we don’t have a traditional HR department —our people managers ensure that this mindset is molded into everything we do. This approach helps create a collaborative and engaged workforce.”

Crafting A Strong Legacy

We ended the session by asking, “How do you want your business to be remembered, and what steps are you taking to secure that legacy?​”

“I want Tenacium to be remembered for its tenacity and for delivering digital resilience to businesses worldwide. By focusing on continuous innovation, global expansion, and a commitment to our client’s success, we’re ensuring our legacy will be one of integrity, adaptability, and industry leadership in data and cybersecurity.” Balaji concluded.

title: By capturing Arizona, Trump Completes his swing State Sweep
author: editor
excerpt: US TV networks predicted on Saturday that Donald Trump had won Arizona in this week’s US presidential election, completing the Republican’s sweep of all seven swing states. CNN and NBC predicted that Trump had won 11 electoral votes after four days of counting in the heavily Hispanic southwest state, defeating Vice President Kamala Harris. In 2020, outgoing President Joe Biden defeated Trump in Arizona with a close but significant victory, ending Trump’s first term in power. The defeated Democratic Party has been rocked by the scope and intensity of Trump’s comeback, which also saw the real estate magnate win the popular vote by a margin of about four million votes. Thanks to the backing of white working-class voters and a sizable portion of Hispanic voters, the Republicans have already taken back control of the Senate and appear poised to maintain a majority in the House of Representatives. With 218 votes required for a majority in the lower house, CNN has predicted Republican victory for 213 House seats. According to the networks, Democrats own 205 seats, but top party officials are still hoping for a narrow win that would drastically limit Trump’s authority. title: Dozens are Killed in Lebanon by Israeli Airstrikes
author: editor
excerpt: According to the regional governor, Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed at least 30 people on Wednesday in the Bekaa Valley, near the eastern city of Baalbek. At sunset, more missiles struck the southern suburbs of Beirut. The conflict between Israel and Hizbollah has been going on for more than a year, coinciding with the war in Gaza, but since late September, Israeli troops have been bombing large areas of the south and east of Lebanon more frequently and invading border villages on foot. Bachir Khodr, the governor of the Baalbek-Hermel governorate, reported on X that about 20 Israeli attacks had killed 30 people and injured 35 more. Following the Israeli military’s order for people to leave multiple areas, the region was the target of at least four strikes on Wednesday. Details about what was struck and the number of casualties were not immediately available. The assault occurred soon after Naim Qassem, the secretary general of Hizbollah, stated that he did not think “political action” would stop the fighting. If Israel ceased its attacks, he argued, there might be a path to indirect talks. title: Trump Wins over Muslim Voters with his Promise of Peace in the Middle East
author: editor
excerpt: Late in the 2024 campaign, Donald Trump, the next US president, accomplished an unexpected achievement by winning over large numbers of Muslim voters by promising to put an end to the violence in the Middle East. As Israel continues its 13-month siege of Gaza and bombardment of nearby Lebanon, his new supporters are now rejoicing in his triumph and are sure he will deliver. According to early data, Trump barely won first place in Dearborn, the largest Arab-American enclave in America. This is a sharp contrast to 2020, when departing President Joe Biden won by a wide margin. This time, Vice President Kamala Harris and Jill Stein of the Green Party split the left-leaning vote. Bazzi denied that the media had misrepresented Trump’s earlier “Muslim ban,” stating that it was just a question of more stringent screening of some unstable nations to keep Daesh extremists out of the US. title: For Taxpayers Who are Overdue on Updating Their Tax Registration, the FTA Provides a Grace Period
author: editor
excerpt: In order to assist businesses in effectively fulfilling their tax duties, the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) released a new decision that grants tax registrants that have fallen behind on updating their tax records a grace period from January 1, 2024, until March 31, 2025. By taking this effort, violators can make the required corrections and avoid the administrative penalties that come with not notifying the FTA of any situations in which their tax records need to be modified. In accordance with the Penalty Refund Procedures described in Cabinet Decision No. (105) of 2021 on Controls and Procedures for Paying Administrative Penalties by Instalments, and Waiving and Refunding Administrative Penalties, the Cabinet decided to grant a grace period for administrative penalties for registrants who have neglected to update their tax record information. This decision states that if registrants were penalized for failing to update their records on time and they have already paid the penalties between January 1, 2024, and the grace period deadline, the penalties will be reimbursed. According to Cabinet Decision No. (74) of 2023 on the Executive Regulation of Federal Decree-Law No. (28) of 2022 on Tax Procedures, registered taxpayers must notify the authority using its approved form and procedure within 20 working days of any change in the information registered in the FTA systems. The FTA stated that the initiative aims to encourage registrants to update their tax records. This comprises the registrant’s name, address, email, and activities as stated in their articles of organization, legal form, partnership agreement for joint ventures, and commercial license. It also includes any modifications to the type of business they operate or the address from which they do so. According to Cabinet Decision No. (74) of 2023 on the Executive Regulation of Federal Decree-Law No. (28) of 2022 on Tax Procedures, registered taxpayers must notify the authority using its approved form and procedure within 20 working days of any change in the information registered in the FTA systems. The FTA stated that the initiative aims to encourage registrants to update their tax records. This comprises the registrant’s name, address, email, and activities as stated in their articles of organization, legal form, partnership agreement for joint ventures, and commercial license. It also includes any modifications to the type of business they operate or the address from which they do so.

title: A Corporation that makes Unapproved and Deceptive Financial Promotions is Fined by the DFSA
author: editor
excerpt: A Decision Notice against Vedas International Marketing Management (Vedas Marketing) for unapproved and misleading financial promotions pertaining to the Multibank Group was released today by the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA). The DFSA announced in a press release on Tuesday that Vedas Marketing had been fined US$100,000 (Dhs367,000) for promoting the Multibank Group to people in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) without authorisation. Additionally, for acting dishonestly and deceptively by claiming that some Multibank Group companies were subject to DFSA regulation while, in reality, none of the touted companies were. The Multibank Group provides trading platforms, and in the Decision Notice, the DFSA made no accusations of misconduct against the Multibank Group. Vedas Marketing appealed the DFSA’s Decision Notice’s findings to the Financial Markets Tribunal (FMT) on June 2, 2024. On July 22, 2024, however, the FMT ordered that the reference be stricken out since Vedas Marketing had neglected to pay the necessary filing fee. “Maintaining the integrity and reputation of the DIFC is one of our top priorities,” stated Ian Johnston, DFSA Chief Executive. The DFSA will take the required actions to discourage companies from misleading the public about their location or regulatory status. title: The Capital and Reserves of the UAE Banking Sector reach an all-Time High of Dhs502.6 Billion
author: editor
excerpt: The banking industry in the United Arab Emirates has reached a noteworthy milestone. For the first time, as of July 2024, the total capital and reserves of banks doing business in the United Arab Emirates surpassed Dhs500 billion. The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) recently revealed data showing that the sector’s capital and reserves increased by 10.5% year over year, from Dhs454.9 billion in July 2023 to Dhs502.6 billion in July 2024. Additionally, from Dhs489.3 billion at the end of 2023 to Dhs13.3 billion during the first seven months of 2024, the sector’s capital and reserves saw a significant boost. The apex bank claims that these numbers reflect current year profits but do not include subordinated borrowings or deposits. The majority, or 86.3%, of the total capital and reserves are held by national banks, which will have grown by 10.4% annually to Dhs433.7 billion by July 2024. Foreign banks also played an important role, contributing 13.7% of the total capital and reserves by the end of July, or Dhs68.9 billion, an increase of 11.1% from the previous year. This outstanding accomplishment demonstrates the durability and power of the UAE banking industry, reaffirming its role as a major force behind the country’s stability and economic prosperity. As the Founder and Principal Consultant of ACE Consulting Group, he leverages his extensive expertise to guide gaming executives, founders, and managers in crafting winning strategies that drive growth and operational excellence. His unique approach combines a deep passion for gaming with a sharp focus on business structure, resource optimization, and leadership development.

Throughout his career, Alexis has worked with leading studios, helping them enhance decision-making processes, optimize budgets, and build sustainable growth strategies. His expertise spans strategic planning, business structure setup, and operational efficiency, making him a go-to consultant for companies looking to scale in the highly competitive gaming industry. His passion for the gaming world goes beyond the love of the product itself—Alexis is inspired by the collaborative talent behind these creations, working with teams of diverse skills and perspectives to bring joy to players worldwide.

“With the right vision, structure, and management principles, game studios can not only survive but excel in this dynamic industry,” Alexis emphasizes. “My mission is to make that happen.”

With his 25+ years of experience, Alexis Gresoviac continues to shape the gaming industry by empowering leaders to make smarter decisions, optimize their operations, and thrive in an ever-evolving market. 6. Søren L. Nielsen | Building a Workplace of the Future at yellow3.io

Søren L. Nielsen is very busy these days with building a future workplace that everyone would want to join: yellow3.io, where he is CTO and Co-Founder.

yellow3.io will be a tech powerhouse built for the future based on Web3 technology—the first product will be Digital Product Passports, the EU’s new tool of choice to ensure circularity and transparency for all physical goods. This is a market set to explode when legislation comes into force by 2027. Building upon Søren’s extensive blockchain knowledge, the platform will leverage this technology to provide tamperproof data traces within the Passport data to protect against fraud.

Søren comes from a tech engineering background and has worked as a tech lead, which eventually led him into various C-level positions. Along the way, he also acquired a business degree. His latest role was CEO at Bitcoin Suisse’s Danish development company, making him a blockchain specialist, a tech expert, an organizer, a top manager, and a visionary leader.

“One great way to build a great organization is to have leadership that knows the core business of the company,” Søren believes. A CEO who is also excellent at coding makes it much easier to inspire the tech people (and everyone else). Although he doesn’t necessarily do the coding himself, his technical understanding enables him to make and drive strategic decisions much more efficiently. Over the years, one of the challenges has been the demand from various bosses to choose between being managerial or technical. Søren refuses to choose, explaining that he “has instead worked in companies where this dual role is appreciated and has created a lot of value.” Now, he is building a future organization based on his experience and values: trust, competency, transparency, equality, and fun.

It’ll be a partially remote company with a strong culture, with the hub centered around Copenhagen, but employees will work from wherever they want. “Why shouldn’t you be able to go to Bali to work for 3 months while you and your better half are on parental leave?” Søren suggested.

“The newest hire fresh out of university should be able to tell the CEO/CTO, ‘That’s not going to work because…’ and then we can have an honest discussion about that, and the final outcome will be better for it,” Søren stated. “We require, and only hire, excellent competent people. However, we also only want to work with nice people, and therefore the ‘no asshole policy’ also applies.”

As a partner with SCAVAI and through her collaboration with the Federation of World Cultural and Arts Society (FOWCAS), Deeya has extended her influence globally, promoting cultural exchange and artistic development. Her initiatives redefine the therapeutic capacity of creative expression, positioning art as a bridge to emotional well-being and innovation.

An advocate for embracing one’s unique identity, Deeya also shares her expertise through public speaking engagements, mentorship of emerging artists, and her writings. With her trailblazing approach, Deeya continues to inspire countless others, leading the way in reshaping art as both a path to healing and a force for innovation.

LinkedIn

With a degree from EHL, Lausanne’s acclaimed hospitality business school, Mettler began his career immersing himself in the art and science of food and hospitality. This rich foundation soon sparked an ambition that led him into the world of premium chocolate.

Driven by a vision to create something remarkable, Mettler launched Attimo, a luxury chocolate brand that quickly rose to global prominence. Under his leadership, Attimo set a Guinness World Record for the most valuable chocolate in the world—an achievement that underscores his relentless dedication to quality and innovation. For Mettler, it wasn’t just about creating a premium product; it was about pushing boundaries and delivering a truly memorable experience.

Following Attimo’s success, Mettler brought his talents to Nestlé, where he took on leadership roles, driving impactful food and coffee initiatives across Switzerland. From high-profile projects for Nescafé to Starbucks, he helped shape the Swiss coffee landscape and proved his ability to make a meaningful mark in the corporate world.

Today, Mettler heads up the Coffee Business Unit at Coca-Cola, steering the national vision for Costa Coffee and Caffè Vergnano. Entrusted with full strategic responsibility, he continues to push forward in the coffee space, blending visionary thinking with his deep industry knowledge. This role allows Mettler to bring his unique touch to the world of coffee, reshaping it for a global audience.

Tatjana Markovic redefines what it means to be an entrepreneur in today’s world, viewing success not only by profit, but by the legacy of empathy and resilience she leaves behind. Based in Dubai, Tatjana’s journey is a testament to the power of purpose. “For me, business isn’t just about growth,” she explains. “It’s about inspiring real, lasting change.”

One of her defining projects, Kiko & Friends, is dedicated to nurturing empathy in children, helping them discover their own “inner magic” and fostering connections that can span generations. Her upcoming book, Embracing the Inner Child: Nurturing the Magic Within, invites adults on a poetic journey back to their own resilience and wonder, bridging the values we often lose touch with.

Her work embodies the UAE’s commitment to purpose and unity, leading the way toward a future where the true impact of success is measured by the lives touched and communities uplifted.

For those who seek a deeper meaning in business and beyond, Tatjana’s story is a powerful reminder: our legacy is built not only through what we achieve, but through the compassion and purpose we inspire in others.

His comprehensive skill set includes strategic product launches, online reputation management, and impactful PPC, SEO/SEM, and email marketing campaigns, positioning him as a go-to expert for transforming marketing challenges into growth opportunities.

Hamza’s current academic pursuits in Germany represent more than a quest for knowledge; they’re a commitment to enhancing his skills and broadening his global market understanding. “This academic journey is about expanding my capacity to deliver innovative and impactful marketing solutions,” he shares, underscoring his dedication to continuous improvement.

Since beginning his career in 2013 as a junior SEO specialist, Hamza has achieved impressive milestones in SaaS product marketing. In his words, “I have helped over 200 product owners successfully launch on Product Hunt, achieving a 90% success rate.” Hamza has also managed the online reputation of more than 30 companies, boosting their visibility across essential digital platforms.

Beyond Product Hunt, Hamza has successfully launched over 10 products on marketplaces like AppSumo, delivering essential support in branding and revenue generation for product owners. His SEO efforts have driven lead generation for over 50 companies, and his social media management services have helped more than 50 clients enhance brand awareness and engagement.

Conclusion

This group of Top 10 Leaders showcases a remarkable shift in how we measure business success in 2024. Their influence goes beyond short-term gains, focusing instead on creating lasting value that benefits both people and the planet. title: Israel Terminates Pact with UN aid Organisation in Gaza
author: editor
excerpt: In what seemed to be an attempt to put into effect legislation passed last month that would cut off ties with the UN agency for Palestinian refugees and prohibit it from operating in Israel, Israel announced Monday that it had ended the agreement that allowed the agency to carry out its work. The agency is the primary aid provider in Gaza. Israel claims that Hamas has infiltrated the organisation, which is called UNRWA. UNRWA says it takes precautions to maintain its neutrality and refutes the accusations. Israel said on Sunday that its forces had invaded Syria on foot to capture a Syrian it believes is collaborating with Iran. Israel declared that its troops had entered Syrian soil for the first time in the ongoing conflict. Increased Israeli assaults against the Hezbollah organisation are spreading outside of Lebanon’s border regions, despite mounting pressure from the US and other international players for a cease-fire in Gaza and Lebanon. Additionally, Israel and Hamas are engaged in a never-ending conflict in northern Gaza. The Health Ministry said that, excluding Friday’s death toll, at least 2,900 people have been killed and 13,150 wounded in Lebanon since the war between Israel and Hezbollah broke out last year. According to health officials, women and children accounted for 25% of the fatalities. title: China-made EV Sales for Tesla in October Drop 5.3%
author: editor
excerpt: According to figures released Monday by the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA), US automaker Tesla sold 68,280 electric cars built in China in October, a 5.3% decrease from the previous month. Model 3 and Model Y car deliveries from China decreased 22.7% from the prior month. With its Dynasty and Ocean series of electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, Chinese rival BYD set another monthly record last month, increasing passenger car sales by 66.2% year over year to 500,526 units. In a BYD filing, overseas shipments accounted for 6% of overall sales. After one-time layoffs in the previous quarter, the US EV company’s third-quarter earnings above forecasts, and it reported the first yearly increase in deliveries this year due to sales. Tesla extended a zero-interest financing plan for certain Model 3 and Model Y vehicles, which it had first announced in China in July, by one month until the end of November in late October. Model 3 and Model Y car deliveries from China fell 22.7% from the prior month. With its Dynasty and Ocean series of electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, Chinese rival BYD set yet another monthly record last month, increasing passenger car sales by 66.2% year over year to 500,526 units. title: Sheikh Mansour Begins ADIPEC’s 40th Edition
author: editor
