title: Review of the Vehicle: The 2024 Maserati GranTurismo Trofeo is an Elegant Supercar
author: editor
excerpt: Maserati’s romance with grand tourers started 80 years ago. The affair that began with the A6 1500 in 1947 continued with iconic models like the 3500 GT, 5000 GT, Sebring, Mistral, Ghibli, Bora, Khamsin, and 3200 GT and finally, the first generation GranTurismo. What we have here is the second generation, the 2024 Maserati GranTurismo Trofeo, the top dog of the petrol-engine line-up. The new GranTurismo maintains classic proportions, featuring a long bonnet and short boot deck with a swoopy roofline connecting them. It shares the ground-hugging silhouette with its predecessor, but its stylistic details have been tweaked to give it a fresh identity. It now features new vertical headlights (reminiscent of the MC20 halo car) and slimmed-down tail lamps. But the iconic trident logo on the grille and pillar, along with the trio of side fender vents remain, paying homage to the models of the past and present. Beyond aesthetics, Maserati has also focused on the engineering aspects. Over 65 percent of the car is made from aluminum, and it threw in some magnesium as well. The sum of these shapes is a dream machine that appeals to both the child’s imagination and the adult’s desires. title: Asia’s Developing Economies are expected to Expand by 5% a Year
author: editor
excerpt: The Asian Development Bank stated in a report on Wednesday that developing countries in Asia are expected to grow economies at a 5.0% annual pace this year, aided by the robust US economy and the rising demand for computer chips that underpin artificial intelligence. The 4.9% growth projection from the ADB in April was slightly revised upward in the forecast. However, the regional lender did issue a warning that, depending on the results of the US presidential election, additional protectionist measures, such as greater taxes on Chinese goods, may be threatened The report identified a number of encouraging indicators, such as the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence this year leading to a resurgence in computer chip and other advanced electronics exports from Asia. It also mentioned that while food and energy costs are declining, inflation is still excruciatingly high in places like Pakistan, Laos, and Myanmar. Stronger growth in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and South Korea, and to a lesser extent, the Philippines and Thailand, has been fuelled by the recovery in the worldwide demand for semiconductors and related electronics materials and components. This trend is anticipated to continue. According to data referenced in the paper, the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics predicts that this year’s spending on memory chips essential for AI applications will increase by 77%. title: Selling Sand to an Arab: Dubai’s Genius in Turning the Impossible into the Inevitable
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Imagine selling snow to an Eskimo. Now, imagine selling sand to an Arab. In a city where sand surrounds every corner, Dubai has turned even this seemingly limitless resource into a valuable commodity. Here, all the sand belongs to the government, and you can’t touch a grain of it without their consent. Just like swans belong to the Queen of England and pandas are the sole property of the Chinese government, Dubai’s sand is not free for the taking. Not all sand is created equal in this dazzling desert metropolis. There are two distinct types of sand in Dubai, and each is treated very differently. First, there’s the ubiquitous desert sand—rough, gritty, and golden. This sand is used for construction projects, either dumped after excavation or refilled to level out the land. Even this common desert sand is heavily regulated. You can’t move or use it without paying the government, making it a clear example of “selling sand to an Arab.” Every truckload is accounted for, and every movement of sand comes with a price tag. Image Credit Then, there’s the real treasure—Dubai’s white beach sand. Soft, luxurious, and as valuable as gold, this premium sand lines the shores of the city’s world-famous beaches and high-end resorts. This isn’t just any sand; it’s a symbol of the city’s opulence and exclusivity. Reserved for the most luxurious properties, Dubai’s white sand is treated like a rare treasure, reinforcing the city’s image as a place where even the simplest things are elevated to extraordinary heights. Dubai’s ability to transform sand into a valuable resource mirrors a global trend where seemingly common commodities are turned into luxurious, highly regulated assets. Consider Venice, a city built on water, yet fresh water is a rare commodity. The Venetians rely on water piped in from the mainland, despite being surrounded by the very element they need. In a city where water is everywhere, they’ve managed to “sell water to Venetians,” proving that scarcity can be created where none seems to exist. Image Credit In Switzerland, the country’s famed mountain air has been transformed into a luxury product. Visitors from polluted cities can purchase bottled Swiss air to take home, a literal example of “selling air to the world.” The Swiss have mastered the art of turning their natural environment into a valuable commodity, much like Dubai has with its sand. Image Credit The Dutch have done something similar with tulips, flowers that are as common in the Netherlands as sand is in Dubai. Yet, the Netherlands has managed to create an entire economy around these vibrant blooms, with tourists and locals alike paying premium prices for tulips. It’s another case of turning something abundant into a luxury—“selling tulips to the Dutch” in a land full of flowers. Image Credit Canada’s maple syrup industry operates in much the same way. Despite producing 70% of the world’s supply, the syrup is tightly controlled and sold at high prices, even to Canadians themselves. The government ensures that the syrup, much like Dubai’s sand, is a valuable commodity by managing its production and pricing. It’s a sweet example of “selling syrup to Canadians,” even in a land where maple trees are everywhere. Image Credit In Colombia, some of the world’s best coffee beans are grown, but most of the premium product is exported to other countries. Locals often drink lower-grade coffee, as the finest beans are reserved for international markets. It’s a perfect example of “selling coffee to Colombians,” where the very people who grow the product don’t always get to enjoy the best of it. Image Credit Japan takes the concept even further by turning something as simple as a watermelon into a luxury item. Square watermelons, meticulously grown and sold for hundreds of dollars, are often given as gifts, proving that even the most ordinary things can be transformed into high-end commodities. In Japan, they’ve managed to “sell watermelons to the Japanese” by reimagining an everyday fruit as a status symbol. Image Credit France’s Brittany region is home to another example of turning the ordinary into the extraordinary. Salt harvested from the Atlantic coast, known as “white gold,” is sold at premium prices around the world, despite being as abundant as the sea itself. This artisanal salt has been elevated to a luxury good, showing that even the simplest resources can be turned into treasures with the right narrative. Image Credit In Greece, olive oil, a staple of the Mediterranean diet, has become a prized export. The finest olive oil is often reserved for international markets, while locals consume lower-grade versions. It’s yet another example of “selling olive oil to Greeks,” where a common resource is transformed into a valuable product for those who can afford it. In every one of these examples, from Venice’s water to Canada’s syrup, the story is the same: abundant resources turned into precious commodities. And Dubai, with its mastery of sand, leads the way. By transforming both desert and beach sand into valuable resources, the city has proven that even the most ordinary materials can be reimagined into something extraordinary. Whether it’s “selling sand to an Arab” or creating value out of air, the future belongs to those who can turn the ordinary into the extraordinary. And in Dubai, even sand—whether it’s the rough desert variety or the silky white beach sand—is priceless. With over two decades of experience in the dynamic Dubai real estate market, Hamzah has played a pivotal role in introducing forward-thinking and sustainable living solutions to the region. Axiom Prime Real Estate Development, renowned for its Dutch-inspired, luxurious developments, focuses on community-driven designs and cutting-edge technology. Their flagship projects in Jumeirah Village Triangle and Jumeirah Garden City (Satwa) exemplify their vision of creating spaces that promote a sense of belonging while unlocking growth potential. content:
Imagine selling snow to an Eskimo. Now, imagine selling sand to an Arab. In a city where sand surrounds every corner, Dubai has turned even this seemingly limitless resource into a valuable commodity. Here, all the sand belongs to the government, and you can’t touch a grain of it without their consent. Just like swans belong to the Queen of England and pandas are the sole property of the Chinese government, Dubai’s sand is not free for the taking.

Not all sand is created equal in this dazzling desert metropolis. There are two distinct types of sand in Dubai, and each is treated very differently. First, there’s the ubiquitous desert sand—rough, gritty, and golden. This sand is used for construction projects, either dumped after excavation or refilled to level out the land. Even this common desert sand is heavily regulated. You can’t move or use it without paying the government, making it a clear example of “selling sand to an Arab.” Every truckload is accounted for, and every movement of sand comes with a price tag.

Image Credit

Then, there’s the real treasure—Dubai’s white beach sand. Soft, luxurious, and as valuable as gold, this premium sand lines the shores of the city’s world-famous beaches and high-end resorts. This isn’t just any sand; it’s a symbol of the city’s opulence and exclusivity. Reserved for the most luxurious properties, Dubai’s white sand is treated like a rare treasure, reinforcing the city’s image as a place where even the simplest things are elevated to extraordinary heights.

Dubai’s ability to transform sand into a valuable resource mirrors a global trend where seemingly common commodities are turned into luxurious, highly regulated assets. Consider Venice, a city built on water, yet fresh water is a rare commodity. The Venetians rely on water piped in from the mainland, despite being surrounded by the very element they need. In a city where water is everywhere, they’ve managed to “sell water to Venetians,” proving that scarcity can be created where none seems to exist.

Image Credit

In Switzerland, the country’s famed mountain air has been transformed into a luxury product. Visitors from polluted cities can purchase bottled Swiss air to take home, a literal example of “selling air to the world.” The Swiss have mastered the art of turning their natural environment into a valuable commodity, much like Dubai has with its sand.

Image Credit

The Dutch have done something similar with tulips, flowers that are as common in the Netherlands as sand is in Dubai. Yet, the Netherlands has managed to create an entire economy around these vibrant blooms, with tourists and locals alike paying premium prices for tulips. It’s another case of turning something abundant into a luxury—“selling tulips to the Dutch” in a land full of flowers.

Image Credit

Canada’s maple syrup industry operates in much the same way. Despite producing 70% of the world’s supply, the syrup is tightly controlled and sold at high prices, even to Canadians themselves. The government ensures that the syrup, much like Dubai’s sand, is a valuable commodity by managing its production and pricing. It’s a sweet example of “selling syrup to Canadians,” even in a land where maple trees are everywhere.

Image Credit

In Colombia, some of the world’s best coffee beans are grown, but most of the premium product is exported to other countries. Locals often drink lower-grade coffee, as the finest beans are reserved for international markets. It’s a perfect example of “selling coffee to Colombians,” where the very people who grow the product don’t always get to enjoy the best of it.

Image Credit

Japan takes the concept even further by turning something as simple as a watermelon into a luxury item. Square watermelons, meticulously grown and sold for hundreds of dollars, are often given as gifts, proving that even the most ordinary things can be transformed into high-end commodities. In Japan, they’ve managed to “sell watermelons to the Japanese” by reimagining an everyday fruit as a status symbol.

Image Credit

France’s Brittany region is home to another example of turning the ordinary into the extraordinary. Salt harvested from the Atlantic coast, known as “white gold,” is sold at premium prices around the world, despite being as abundant as the sea itself. This artisanal salt has been elevated to a luxury good, showing that even the simplest resources can be turned into treasures with the right narrative.

Image Credit

In Greece, olive oil, a staple of the Mediterranean diet, has become a prized export. The finest olive oil is often reserved for international markets, while locals consume lower-grade versions. It’s yet another example of “selling olive oil to Greeks,” where a common resource is transformed into a valuable product for those who can afford it.

In every one of these examples, from Venice’s water to Canada’s syrup, the story is the same: abundant resources turned into precious commodities. And Dubai, with its mastery of sand, leads the way. By transforming both desert and beach sand into valuable resources, the city has proven that even the most ordinary materials can be reimagined into something extraordinary. Whether it’s “selling sand to an Arab” or creating value out of air, the future belongs to those who can turn the ordinary into the extraordinary.

And in Dubai, even sand—whether it’s the rough desert variety or the silky white beach sand—is priceless.

title: 2030 Renewable Energy Targets Appear Feasible
author: editor
excerpt: In a report published on Tuesday, the International Energy Agency (IEA) stated that it is feasible to meet the targets established during the Conference of Parties 28 (COP28) in Dubai last November, which is also referred to as “the UAE Consensus,” which calls for tripling renewable energy to 1500 GW and doubling energy efficiency by 2030. This will allow many of the 200 countries to reach their agreed-upon goal of having a net-zero economy by 2050. China and India are expected to reach net-zero by 2060 and 2070, respectively. But if member nations can maintain the policy focus at the top of the agenda, the green energy transition can be accomplished. Secondly, in order to double the energy efficiency target, it would also be necessary to design energy-efficient buildings and install more efficient air conditioners. According to the analysis, concentrating solely on renewable energy sources will not suffice. The transition away from fossil fuels, such as coal-fired power plants, must be deliberate. Although it may sound like a tall order, the paper claims that if the implementation is done throughout the nations and in all economic sectors, it is possible to meet the green energy objective. “The goal set by nearly 200 countries at COP28 can be transformative for the global energy sector, putting it on a fast track towards a more secure, affordable, and sustainable future,” stated Fatih Birol, Executive Director of the International Energy Agency. title: Etihad Cargo Commemorates 20 years of Prosperous Business in India
author: editor
excerpt: The cargo and logistics division of Etihad Airways, Etihad Cargo, is commemorating 20 years of business in India. This milestone shows the airline’s continued dedication to the Indian market since its inaugural flight to Mumbai on September 26, 2004. With intentions to continue growing, Etihad Cargo has increased its footprint in India over time and is currently providing belly hold capacity via nonstop flights between Abu Dhabi and twelve important Indian locations. Etihad Cargo transports approximately 46,000 tonnes of cargo yearly ex India, linking the country to over 100 global destinations via its Abu Dhabi hub with 588 widebody and narrowbody rotations each month. Etihad Cargo has expanded its product line, introducing new items and adding new features to suit the demands of particular industries better. The carrier’s IATA CEIV Pharma-certified PharmaLife product offers precise temperature control, ideal for the safe transportation of expensive pharmaceuticals—a sector that is expanding in India. Etihad Cargo has implemented strict cargo screening for shipments from major Indian hubs, such as Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, and Hyderabad, to the United States. The company is also exploring establishing new authorised pharma trade routes with important airline partners. By enhancing connections and frequencies, Etihad Cargo’s Pharma roadshows in India, which were introduced in 2023, have assisted in doubling PharmaLife volumes. Furthermore, the expansion of electronics exports has been aided by the launch in 2024 of Etihad Cargo’s IATA CEIV Li-batt certified SecureTech solution. title: Instead of Six Months, the Minimum Validity term for Passports will be one month, allowing violators to Change the status of their Visa in the UAE.
author: editor
excerpt: The passport validity time that is necessary to approve a request to change the status of overstayers from six months to just one month during the amnesty period has been modified by the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Ports Security (ICP). Major General Suhail Saeed Al Khaili, Director General of ICP, has stated that the six-month passport validity period previously applicable to residents, visa violators, foreign nationals born in the nation, and individuals on administrative lists has been reduced to one month. According to him, the goal of the ruling is to give overstayers the option to change their status without having to renew their passports if they will be staying longer than six months, as was the case previously. Al Khaili emphasised that the ruling would allow overstayers to benefit from the unique chance presented by the amnesty, and that this exception would only be in effect from September 1 through October 31, 2024, when the amnesty is in effect. He emphasised that the move shows the ICP’s desire to find practical answers to the problems that the amnesty’s recipients confront and urged overstayers to get in touch with the organization’s call centre to discuss their concerns and issues. title: Due to Israeli Bombings, UAE Airlines Cancel their Flights to and from Lebanon
author: editor
excerpt: In response to the current regional developments, a number of flights to and from Beirut were cancelled by airlines on Tuesday and Wednesday. On September 24 and 25, Emirates Airlines cancelled its scheduled flights from Dubai to Beirut. According to data provided by Emirates, this was caused by events that followed a string of Israeli attacks that targeted several Lebanese provinces, leaving tens of thousands of people displaced and over 500 casualties. Etihad Airways has said that, due to the current security situation in the area, it will discontinue its planned services to and from Beirut on Tuesday, September 24. The impacted flights are EY535, which takes off from Abu Dhabi and lands in Beirut, and EY538, which takes off from Beirut and lands in Abu Dhabi. Assistance in arranging alternate travel arrangements is offered to those visitors who have reserved these services. Etihad Airways is actively monitoring the situation across the region and maintaining tight interaction with the necessary authorities. According to a Flydubai representative, the 24th and 25th of September flights between Dubai International Airport and Beirut International Airport have been cancelled. Given the current situation, this decision has been made. The spokesman said that travellers with confirmed reservations had received information on refund or rebooking choices. title: Mohammed Controls the Appointment of Officials from the Dubai Government to the Judicial Authority in Dubai
author: editor
excerpt: His Highness Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates, issued Decree No. (49) of 2024 governing the nomination of Dubai Government employees as members of the judicial authority in Dubai while serving as the Ruler of Dubai. The Decree protects employees’ legal status, rights, and financial benefits while they are receiving training at the Dubai Judicial Institute in an effort to draw top talent from within the country for positions in Dubai’s judicial authorities. The Judicial and Legal Studies Programme for judges and the Diploma in Legal and Judicial Sciences for Public Prosecutors are two of the programs offered by the Institute. The Decree also guarantees that staff members can continue to work for their respective government agencies while receiving training at the school. This Decree’s provisions apply to qualified civilian and military workers employed by government organisations subject to human resources laws, such as Law No. (6) of 2012, which handles local military personnel’s HR management, and Law No. (8) of 2018, which handles Dubai Government’s HR management. The terms of this Decree do not apply to CEOs, who Law No covers. (8) of 2021, or Directors General, governed by Law No. (8) of 2013. According to the human resources norms of their government agency, the Decree specifies the rights of employees throughout their training time. These rights include earning their entire monthly income, exclusive of any allowances or other bonuses. title: Taxable Persons are Advised by FTA to Follow the Deadlines
author: editor
excerpt: To avoid administrative penalties, the Federal Tax Authority (FTA) is urging resident juridical persons holding licenses issued in July, regardless of the year of issuance, to file their corporate tax registration application as soon as possible by September 30, 2024. For the purposes of Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 on the Taxation of Corporations and Businesses and its amendments, which went into effect on March 1, 2024, the FTA advised Taxable Persons to follow the deadlines specified in FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024 on the Timeline specified for Registration of Taxable Persons for Corporate Tax, according to a press release released on Monday. The FTA Decision stipulates when each type of taxable person subject to corporate tax must submit their application for corporate tax registration. The FTA stated that Taxable Persons who do not comply with submitting their Corporate Tax registration application within the time periods specified in the FTA Decision will be subject to an Administrative Penalty under Cabinet Decision No. 75 of 2023 on the Administrative Penalties for Violations Related to the Application of Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 on the Taxation of Corporations and Businesses, and its amendments. title: Speaking with Biden, the President of the UAE Reiterates his “Unwavering Commitment” to the US Cooperation.
author: editor
excerpt: The President, His Excellency Sheikh Mohamed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan discussed the “power of partnerships” on Monday in the White House with US President Joe Biden. He praised the ability to forge connections with countries that have similar ideals and aspirations for a better future and reiterated the UAE’s steadfast dedication to the US alliance. President Biden and Sheikh Mohamed Bin Zayed spoke about the depth of the strategic alliance between the US and the UAE and their shared desire to fortify it further. The presidents discussed a range of topics related to their long-standing bilateral ties, including trade and investment, the economy, space exploration, advanced technology, renewable energy, combating climate change, sustainability, and food security. They expressed a strong desire to increase cooperation in these areas in order to further the goals of global stability and prosperity that both nations share. His Highness cited a 1974 meeting between Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the founding father of the United Arab Emirates, and a NASA team that provided a briefing on the Apollo program as an example of how the two nations’ relations have blossomed. He clarified that, fifty years later, the UAE and NASA are currently working together to construct the Gateway mission, which aims to build the first space station for humankind around the moon. title: Profits are Declining for Global Refiners as new Facilities come Online
author: editor
excerpt: The profitability of oil refiners in Asia, Europe, and the US is falling to multi-year lows, signalling a slump for a sector Global that had seen explosive returns during the epidemic and highlighting the severity of the present dip in demand around the world. The weakness is an additional indicator of weak industrial and consumer demand, particularly in China where economic growth is slowing and the number of electric vehicles on the road is increasing. The pressure has decreased due to the addition of new refineries in Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. Refiners like TotalEnergies and traders like Glencore made enormous profits in 2022 and 2023 by profiting from supply bottlenecks brought on by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Houthi insurgents’ obstruction of Red Sea navigation, and a significant uptick in demand after the COVID-19 epidemic. “It’s certainly looking like the refining supercycle that we’ve experienced over the past few years may now be coming to an end, with supply from newly inaugurated refineries finally catching up with slower-growing fuel demand,” Rory Johnston, an analyst at Commodity Context, stated. title: Residents of the UAE are Moving to the Schengen Region as Rates rise in the Caribbean
author: editor
excerpt: Following the Caribbean countries’ surge in citizenship by investment program rates, individuals in the UAE and elsewhere who are seeking for a second passport are choosing to switch to Schengen countries. However, business leaders claim that Caribbean passports continue to be a popular choice because of their easy application, affordable price, and low restrictions. Four Caribbean nations—Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, and St. Kitts and Nevis—signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) in March 2024 to harmonise their policies, including the cost of their Citizenship by Investment (CBI) programs, according to advisory firm Citizenship Invest. This June, St. Lucia became a part of the accord. Since July 1, 2024, all five Caribbean countries have imposed new minimum cost thresholds. According to Urusa Imran, director of business development management at Samana Group, the cost of citizenship by investment programs has increased by over 100% in several Caribbean nations. The lack of a visa was the main motivator for many to want a second passport. People want a Caribbean passport since it allowed them to visit all of Europe and the Schengen nations without a visa; these passports may be obtained in six months. People waited five to seven years and paid large sums for European passports. title: Marxist Leader of Sri Lanka Dissanayaka Proclaimed the next President
author: editor
excerpt: A former fringe Marxist politician was proclaimed the nation’s president-elect by Sri Lanka’s electoral commission on Sunday, following a vote tainted by dissatisfaction over the island nation’s handling of an unparalleled financial crisis. The People’s Liberation Front’s 55-year-old leader, Anura Kumara Dissanayaka, emerged victorious in the presidential race on Saturday, garnering 42.31% of the total vote, according to the commission. Sajith Premadasa, the head of the opposition, came in second with 32.76%. Outgoing President Ranil Wickremesinghe, who took office at the height of the economic crisis in 2022 and implemented strict austerity measures in accordance with the terms of an IMF bailout, finished in a distant third place with 17.27%. title: Dubai’s Evolving Skyline: A Guide to Urban Growth
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Dubai, like any major city, is constantly evolving. Many end users and investors often find that the views they were promised with their properties are disrupted by new developments. My response to this is simple: if your view is that important to you, do your homework. Get the master plan for your community or, at the very least, review the block around your future property. If the plots around you are undeveloped, it’s only a matter of time before something will be built. Take, for example, the residents of Palma Villas who are upset about Como Tower. Did they really think that the empty plot next door would stay vacant forever for them to use as a litter box for their pets? And then there are the people in JBR, who assumed that the first-row waterfront plots, temporarily used as parking lots, would remain open spaces for their cars to bask in the sun. Unfortunately, that’s not how urban development works. A perfect illustration of Dubai’s dynamic nature is the case of Cayan Tower, formerly known as Infinity Tower. When the RTA moved the bridge connecting to the marina island, a new premium plot of land was freed up. And what came next? The world’s tallest hotel, Ciel Tower, was built right there. It’s a prime example of how, in Dubai, undeveloped land doesn’t stay that way for long—and when it’s used, it’s often for something remarkable. This isn’t unique to Dubai. Major cities worldwide face similar situations. In New York, for example, the construction of 432 Park Avenue—one of the tallest residential buildings in the world—disrupted the iconic views for many residents in Midtown Manhattan and the Upper East Side. People who had long enjoyed unobstructed views of Central Park suddenly found themselves looking at a new luxury tower instead. Billionaire’s Row along 57th Street in New York saw the rise of towers like One57, Central Park Tower, and 111 West 57th Street, forever changing the skyline and blocking the park views for many older buildings in the area. In cities like New York, rapid development is just part of life. London has seen its fair share of skyline changes too. The Shard, the tallest building in the UK, transformed the city’s skyline and altered views across Southwark and central London. Many properties that once had panoramic views of Tower Bridge now see a very different landscape with the completion of The Shard. Back in Dubai, the same applies to residents on The Palm, who once had clear views of the Marina and the Al-Sufouh skyscraper block, but are now facing the new Dubai Harbour community. While the Marina skyline was impressive, the Dubai Harbour development offers something equally appealing, with the bonus of cruise ships docking nearby. It may not be what they originally expected, but it’s still a world-class view, enhanced if anything. At least in Dubai, the process is handled with vision and purpose. Other cities, like Hong Kong, have faced similar disruptions. In the West Kowloon Cultural District, new developments have impacted the views of residents in Yau Ma Tei and Tsim Sha Tsui, who previously enjoyed sweeping vistas across the harbor toward Hong Kong Island. These new high-rise developments have completely altered the cityscape. Ultimately, whether it’s Dubai, New York, London, or Hong Kong, rapid urban growth and changing skylines are inevitable in world-class cities. In Dubai, these changes come with a certain agility, often transforming the city for the better. It’s all part of the evolving landscape of major cities worldwide. title: First Early Ballots in the Tight US Presidential Contest Cast
author: editor
excerpt: On Friday, the first early voters in the tight US presidential race in November cast their votes, with Democratic nominee Kamala Harris on her way to a campaign rally centred on the divisive topic of abortion. Early voting was underway in three US states: Virginia, Minnesota, and South Dakota. Republican nominee Donald Trump has previously questioned the procedure, claiming to have won the 2020 election erroneously. AFP journalists observed throngs of people waiting at an early voting polling place in the heart of Arlington, Virginia, which is located just outside of the nation’s capital, Washington. The majority of US states allow mail-in or in-person voting for those with scheduling issues or who cannot cast a ballot on election day, November 5. Former President Trump has consistently attacked any voting method other than on-the-day voting, blaming mail-in votes for Joe Biden’s victory over him in 2020. title: Abu Dhabi Closes shop Due to Food Safety Infractions
author: editor
excerpt: Itiyadi Foodstuff Trading LLC, located in Musaffah, Abu Dhabi, and holding trade licence number CN-4761612, was administratively shut down by the Abu Dhabi Agriculture & Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA) for violating Law No. 2 for 2008 regarding food in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and the legislation issued thereunder, as well as for posing a health risk to the public. The ADAFSA clarified that the food control report indicated that the facility’s failure to meet food safety standards was the reason for the administrative closure decision. This included the recurrence of high-risk items that directly affected food safety, inadequate hygiene, and the discovery of insects within the facility. The administrative closure order will be in place until the institution fixes the violations and complies with all standards, according to the ADAFSA. The ADAFSA stated that all facilities, regardless of their nature and food products, are subject to routine inspection by the ADAFSA’s inspectors. The administrative closure decision and the discovery of violations came as part of the inspection efforts aimed at strengthening the food safety system in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and ensuring that all facilities meet food safety requirements. title: The CB of Indonesia Announces its First Rate Reduction in over Three Years
author: editor
excerpt: Just hours before the US Federal Reserve’s widely anticipated start of its easing cycle, Indonesia’s central bank announced its first rate cut in over three years on Wednesday in an effort to support growth in Southeast Asia’s largest economy. For the first time since February 2021, Bank Indonesia (BI) abruptly lowered the benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 6.00 percent.Of the 33 economists surveyed by Reuters, only three had anticipated the move, with the remaining analysts expecting no change. According to BI governor Perry Warjiyo, the decision aligns with BI’s prediction that inflation will stay low in 2024 and 2025 and that the rupiah will remain stable. He continued, “It also fits in with BI’s efforts to support economic growth. Due to shifting risk appetite in international financial markets, the rupiah saw pressure earlier in the year. However, it has since reversed those losses versus the US dollar and is currently trading marginally stronger than it was at year’s end. This year, the main stock index has also increased by 7.8%, indicating that capital inflows are returning. According to DBS Bank economist Radhika Rao, “recent rupiah gains and markets pricing in a near certain cut by the US Fed, likely offered BI the headroom to kick-start the easing cycle earlier.” “At this time, we anticipate one more rate reduction by year’s end.” Following BI’s announcement, the currency experienced a brief decline, but it recovered its losses and closed the market at 15,330 per dollar. title: In Eight Months, Etihad Transports 12 Million Passengers
author: editor
excerpt: Etihad Airways declared that it had carried 12 million passengers, a 36% rise from the year before. According to the airline’s traffic statistics, the rolling 12-month passenger count for August 2024 exceeded 17 million, nearly 70% more than for the entire year 2022. With 1.7 million passengers carried and an average passenger load factor of 89% in August, the airline demonstrated exceptional performance during the summer travel season. “Our passenger numbers in August increased significantly compared to the same period last year, demonstrating our continued growth momentum,” stated Antonoaldo Neves, CEO of Etihad Airways. For August 2024, we increased our capacity relative to 2023 while still maintaining a strong passenger load factor of 89%. This strong showing highlights how Etihad is becoming more and more popular among travellers, especially during the holidays. Compared to 79 aircraft during the same period last year, Etihad’s operating fleet has increased to 95, he continued. In addition to continuously delivering a load factor above 86%, the company’s ambition and dedication have resulted in the increase of 16 new aircraft over the last 12 months. Two of the six A321neos anticipated to be delivered in 2024 were put into service in August. Compared to the same period last year, we are currently flying to ten more passenger destinations. title: Land is Scarce, Repurpose: Unlocking Dubai’s Urban Potential
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: As Dubai continues to grow and evolve, the strategic utilization of its scarce land resources within prime areas has become more crucial than ever. The city has undergone transformative projects where underutilized or misaligned plots of land were repurposed to unlock their highest potential. These efforts reflect the visionary approach of the government and master developers, driven by the understanding that certain plots are too valuable to remain in their current state. One such project exemplifying this forward-thinking strategy is the reshaping of the Safa Park area. The government strategically acquired surrounding villas and properties, even repurposing part of the park itself, to carve out a new channel for the Dubai Canal. This move transformed the connectivity of the city, linking the Arabian Gulf from Ras Al Khor through Business Bay and Safa Park, effectively turning key parts of Deira and Bur Dubai into an island. This monumental infrastructure project not only elevated the city’s landscape but also unleashed untapped value from previously static land, making way for super high-end projects on the canal. A similar initiative is the Jumeirah Garden City. In this case, Meraas undertook the ambitious task of acquiring and demolishing old villas in the Satwa area, clearing the way for a new community that serves as a vibrant bridge between City Walk, Sheikh Zayed Road, and Downtown Dubai. By reclaiming and revitalizing the area, Meraas created a dynamic, modern development that complements the surrounding regions and adds immense value to the overall urban fabric. These examples of bold interventions in urban planning and development are models that must continue to be replicated. There are many areas, particularly along Sheikh Zayed Road, that are grossly underutilized despite their prime locations. For instance, several villa communities along this major artery of the city occupy massive, strategically important plots that remain dormant or misaligned with the city’s broader vision. To fully capitalize on the value of these plots, they either need to be reclaimed by the government or rezoned to serve more fitting purposes, unlocking their potential as commercial, residential, or mixed-use developments. Al Quoz is another critical area that demands reevaluation. Currently, it houses a mix of residential, commercial, and industrial zones that are out of sync with its true potential. Relocating the industrial component of Al Quoz to specialized zones such as Dubai Industrial City (DIC), Dubai Investments Park (DIP), or IMPZ, would free up substantial land, which could then be repurposed for more valuable, community-oriented uses. This move could reinvigorate the area, bringing new life and economic activity while allowing industrial operations to thrive in dedicated hubs. Similarly, the Dubai World Trade Centre (DWTC) should be reconsidered. Moving it to Expo City, with its expansive infrastructure and post-Expo legacy, provides a ready-made destination for events and trade shows, allowing DWTC to be relocated and freeing up valuable central land. Repurposing this area into a large-scale, vibrant community would not only create significant land availability but also drive further traffic and energy toward Expo City, fulfilling its potential as a long-term commercial and residential hub. One of the more glaring misuses of land lies in the Jumeirah Lakes Towers (JLT) area. A notable portion of JLT includes labor accommodations and industrial zones that are no longer the highest and best use for such prime real estate. Reclaiming this land under the authority of the Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC) would allow it to be integrated into the broader JLT community. These plots could be transformed into valuable residential, commercial, or retail spaces that would significantly enhance the area’s vibrancy and utility. With that brief in mind, perhaps the most absurd example of wasted land is on Palm Jumeirah. The spectacle of Palm West and Palm East—two low-rise, low-density studio buildings sitting on the most prime waterfront plots of the “eighth wonder of the world.” Taking some of the most coveted land on the planet and turning it into a suburban-style parking lot. Instead of incorporating parking into the building’s structure, the developer graciously sacrificed two more invaluable plots to create open-air parking bays. So now, studio tenants park their cars on these super premium dirt patches—where the land alone is worth a huge fortune. In fact, those parking bays are likely worth more than the entire studio building as a whole. It’s almost unimaginable to be pulling into what could easily be the most expensive piece of land your car will ever touch. Image credit These buildings and their open-air parking lots are sitting on some of the most coveted waterfront land in Dubai, falling short of the grandeur that should define this location. It’s not just a missed opportunity, it’s a downright lost treasure and misuse of ultra-prime real estate. These plots should be repurchased at any cost and repurposed into something that actually deserves to stand on Palm Jumeirah—developments that make full use of the unparalleled views and prestige that come with this world-famous destination. In conclusion, the development strategies employed in Dubai must continue to focus on maximizing the value of scarce land resources. Whether through government intervention or private enterprise, every underutilized plot represents an opportunity to recapture its value. With smart zoning, repurchasing, and repurposing strategies, Dubai can continue its trajectory as one of the world’s most innovative and forward-thinking cities. About the Author: Hamzah Abu Zannad is an industry veteran and the co-founder and managing director of Axiom Prime Real Estate Development. With over two decades of experience in the dynamic Dubai real estate market, Hamzah has played a pivotal role in introducing forward-thinking and sustainable living solutions to the region. Axiom Prime Real Estate Development, renowned for its Dutch-inspired, luxurious developments, focuses on community-driven designs and cutting-edge technology. Their flagship projects in Jumeirah Village Triangle and Jumeirah Garden City (Satwa) exemplify their vision of creating spaces that promote a sense of belonging while unlocking growth potential. title: A Dubai Company is Offering Half-Priced Petrol-to-Electric Vehicles
author: editor
excerpt: Deliveries are scheduled to start by the second quarter of 2025. A Dubai-based start-up company is offering to produce electric vehicles (EVs) made from repurposed cars at prices 50% less than newly manufactured EVs. The starting price of an EV is Dh70,000. A prototype of ReCar.03, an electric vehicle (EV) sedan that was formerly a gasoline-powered Toyota Camry, is on display at the five-day Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) World Congress and Exhibition being held at the Dubai World Trade Centre. The vehicle was designed and engineered by Peec Mobility. Our most recent version of the ReCar has been in development for a while. Zach Faizal, the founder of Peec Mobility, who was born in the United Arab Emirates, said, “We’re close to production with orders due to be delivered in Q2 2025. This is a big step in the future of mobility. ReCar is constructed from a vehicle with an internal combustion engine, either petrol or diesel. Because the technology used to repurpose retired petrol vehicles requires keeping their body and chassis before transforming them into electric vehicles, it is less expensive than a newly-manufactured EV, which can cost upwards of Dh100,000. Compared to new versions, this results in an 80% reduction in manufacturing time and a 30% reduction in manufacturing costs. title: Early in 2024, Sharjah Police Assisted in the Peaceful Settlement of Financial Disputes Totalling Dhs20 Million
author: editor
excerpt: The Sharjah Police’s ‘Reconciliation is Good’ initiative, which aims to settle financial disputes and reconcile parties, achieved notable success, reaching 385 reconciliation cases during the first half of this year (2024). Through the initiative, more than Dhs20.160 million have been successfully returned to their rightful owners, avoiding the need to use the legal system. excerpt: We recently had the privilege of interviewing Nikos Migdalis, Co-founder and CEO of International Media Ideas (IMI), an exhibition and events agency in Dubai. As a seasoned serial entrepreneur, Nikos is driving growth and success through his strategic vision, inspirational leadership, and operational expertise.

With a proven track record of identifying market opportunities, he crafts and executes plans that propel businesses forward. With IMI, Nikos offers top-notch event solutions, with a constant aim for success. In this insightful session, the CEO shares his career highlights, achievements of IMI, and his leadership style.

First steps

We started the interview by asking, “Can you tell us about your professional journey and what led you to your current role?”

Nikos Migdalis  shared, “I started my career back in Greece through internships and quite soon I jumped into entrepreneurship in the UAE back in 2007, following my studies in Greece & U.K. Everything was a mix of actions, ideas, and of being in the correct place at the correct time. Back in those years, Dubai was developing into an international business hub which was enhancing and leading the whole dynamic of the region.

I established IMI which gradually turned into a full-scale exhibition agency, offering turnkey solutions to both local and international companies that were and are participating in various trade fairs that are taking place in the country. Step by step the company grew and as of today, is a leading recognizable entity within its industry. I will always be grateful to the UAE which I call first home for opening its arms.”

Setting A Unique Approach

We were curious to learn more about the approaches adopted by Nikos to ensure his company has a unique position in the market. We asked, “What sets your business apart from competitors in the industry?”

Nikos Migdalis  shared, “I am not fond of talking about competition, but I strongly believe that in IMI we offer a Unique Value Proposition which makes our businesses and services unique to the customers and this is why we achieve high percentage retainers of projects. In terms of customer experience as well, we emphasize any unique approaches towards the client such as personalized support and exceptional responsiveness which stands out.  

In addition, the quality and innovation that we try to implement in the projects that we offer play a significant role as well. Our brand story and values also include a special commitment to sustainability and community involvement.”

Triumphs Of IMI

Eager to learn more about the triumphs at Nikos Migdalis’s business, we asked, “What has been your business’s biggest achievement to date?”

“The biggest achievement so far I believe is our distinctive company culture that resonates with our customers. Good players win the games but a good team can win the championship, and I am proud of my team.” He said.

Leading By Doing

Regarding the leadership approach followed by Nikos, we asked, “How would you describe your leadership style?”

Nikos Migdalis  responded, “I would describe it as a ‘Leadership by Example’ which is a powerful approach to guiding and influencing others. It always involves demonstrating the values, behaviors, and work ethics you expect from your Team. Consistency, integrity, accountability, and respect for others, along with mentoring are aspects that a leader shall demonstrate towards the greater success of all.”

Empowering Employees

We further asked, “What strategies do you use to motivate and develop talent in your organization?”

“Motivating and developing talent is crucial for any company’s success. Having a clear vision and goals along with recognition and rewards are part of that. Furthermore, offering professional development along with career growth opportunities enhances that. Lastly,

an inclusive culture with diverse teams and parallel good team building is always leading to multiple positive effects.” Nikos added.

Embracing Digital Transformation

To stay competitive in the dynamic business landscape, businesses need to keep pace with technological advancements. We asked, “What role do you see artificial intelligence or technology playing in this industry?”

Nikos Migdalis  shared, “Undoubtedly, we live in the AI era with its impact on our daily lives has never been more significant than today. It is transforming the way we interact with technology and the world around us. Integration of AI into trade fairs enhances efficiency, personalization, and the whole attendee experience and will move the industry into more dynamic and data-driven events.  

It is something already happening and it will accelerate very shortly, and undoubtedly, we are experiencing a very interesting era.”

Envisioning The Future

To get a glimpse of Nikos Migdalis’ perspective on the growth of his industry in the upcoming years, we asked, “How do you envision the future of your industry?”

Nikos Migdalis  replied, “The future of trade fairs is most likely to be shaped by several emerging trends and technological  advancements such as sustainability, personalization and AI, enhanced engagement technologies along with data-driven insights.”

Adaptability Amidst Challenges

Adversities are an inevitable part of every business. To learn how Nikos overcame similar phases, we asked, “What have been some of the most significant hurdles you’ve encountered in your business, and how did you address them?”

Nikos shared, “There have always been several hurdles and challenges so I wouldn’t like to identify one or two specifically only. Each of these challenges though requires careful planning and adaptability to ensure a successful trade fair experience. Every day is a new adventure as I keep saying to my team.”

A Customer-Centric Approach

We asked, “What is an excellent piece of business advice you have ever received?”

Nikos Migdalis  shared, “I have received a lot but I would say – Focus on the customer value, not just a business transaction.”

Striking A Balance

To stay ahead, businesses need to constantly invest in fresh ideas, ensuring their existing operations remain efficient. So, we asked, “How do you balance investing in up-to-date ideas with ensuring ongoing operations remain successful?”

“Balancing investment in new ideas with maintaining successful ongoing operations is a critical challenge for any company. Strategic alignment, resource allocation along with regular review and adjustments are some ways to achieve that. We live in a fast-moving train and any action shall be done with prior detailed market research and a great plan while at the same time, too much analysis leads to paralysis.” Nikos concluded.

title: CBUAE Declares the M-Bills Sale
author: editor
excerpt: The Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates (CBUAE) announced Monday’s monetary bill (M-Bill) auction. Four M-Bills Treasury bond issues are up for auction. The first issue will be up to Dhs1,500 million for 28 days, the second for 84 days, the third for 112 days, and the fourth for 280 days, all based on CBUAE data. The fourth issue will be up to Dhs4,000 million. The first issue is due on October 16, 2024; the second issue is due on December 11, 2024; the third issue is due on January 8, 2025; and the fourth issue is due on June 25, 2025. The issue date is September 18, 2024. According to data released by the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), the total gross banks’ assets, including bankers’ acceptances, increased by 0.5% from Dhs4,287.0 billion at the end of May 2024 to Dhs4,310.2 billion at the end of June 2024. In its Monetary and Banking Developments for June 2024 report, the Central Bank stated that gross credit increased by 1.1% from Dhs2,077.7 billion at the end of May 2024 to Dhs2,100.9 billion at the end of June 2024. Gross credit increased as a result of 2.9% growth in foreign credit and 0.8% increase in domestic credit. Over 80 eminent speakers from around the globe will lead two days of in-depth discussions. title: In Dubai, Yango Launches Corporate Rides Service
author: editor
excerpt: A new business-to-business (B2B) service called Yango Rides for Business was introduced by international ride-hailing company Yango, a part of the global tech company Yango Group, during the ITS World Congress 2024, the premier international gathering for smart mobility and transport innovation in Dubai. This new service aims to make corporate transportation management easier and better. With a single, centralised platform, Yango Rides for Business provides businesses with a seamless way to handle all employee transportation needs. Businesses can use the service to combine their ride-hailing costs, doing away with the need for upfront payments or staff reimbursements. Every ride is charged to a corporate account every month, and all costs are easily traceable and fully tax deductible. One of the service’s key features is its advanced customisation, which enables businesses to limit ride access and set spending caps for clients or employees based on their individual requirements. Teams and departments can customise transport options for specialised travel or everyday commuting thanks to this flexibility. Businesses can efficiently monitor ride access, usage limits, and expenses with a dedicated account management system, which guarantees effective cost reduction and budget management. title: Dubai Hosts the Opening of the 30th Intelligent Transport Systems World Congress and Exhibition
author: editor
excerpt: The 30th Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) World Congress and Exhibition was opened on Monday by Sheikh Ahmed Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Second Deputy Ruler of Dubai, under the patronage of Sheikh Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai. The Congress is anticipated to draw approximately 20,000 attendees from 100 different countries, which will be the largest turnout in the Congress’s history. Mattar Al Tayer, Director General and Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA), and Dr. Angelos Amditis, Director General of ERTICO (Europe), greeted Sheikh Ahmed Bin Mohammed. LinkedIn | Website

3. Helen Zeitoun | Championing Human-Centric AI and Strategic Innovation

Helen Zeitoun, the trailblazing CEO of DATAE HUMANUM, has spent over 30 years at the forefront of global market research and data insights. Her career is marked by a relentless drive to create value by harmonizing technological innovation with human-centric strategies, by thought leadership namely as author of an awarded book on AI-human transformation, making her a key figure in the transformation of business models towards data-driven and ethical practices.

Throughout her career, Helen has encountered CEOs and technology leaders grappling with the complexities of AI integration. She observes, “I keep meeting CEOs ‘lost in translation’ with AI, stretched between the hyper opportunity and the potential risk, confused about the true ROI, and often uninspired by the over-functional and mechanistic recommendations of traditional consultants on AI.” Her insights into these challenges have driven her to develop a unique approach capitalizing on her own CEO experience and on academic work, that prioritizes the articulation between human and business aspects of AI adoption, aligned with the firm’s raison d’être.

Helen’s influence extends far beyond traditional business practices. She has pioneered the development of innovation labs in collaboration with institutions like MIT Sloan, the Sorbonne Neuroscience Centre and Boston University, reinforcing her commitment to advancing ethical, data-driven leadership for more sustainable value. Her work building up the Ipsos Global Science Organization has been lauded as a game-changer in the industry, promoting responsible and impactful use of data.

She further notes, “AI is such an extraordinary opportunity but is also full of fears, can create silos, can kill energy by forced processes, and is often too disconnected from the firm’s core strategy, including from the sustainability strategy.” With this understanding, Helen has crafted a customized “external eye” approach designed to help CEOs, Boards and Chief Data Officers (CDOs) navigate strategic renewal with AI. “My passion is to help large groups as well as SMEs in a completely customized 360 ‘external eye’ approach to orchestrate much more than ROI from AI, rather their strategic renewal with AI, leveraging people, planet, and consequently profit. And it works—smoothly, simply, efficiently, with respect, dignity, and a smile on all faces.”

Helen’s vision is not just about technology; it’s about fighting the over-processed and mechanistic approach to AI adoption (leading to slow adoption, leaving aside women, non-tech and older people); it’s about encouraging “living” organizations where AI is seamlessly and responsibly integrated into the fabric of the company, enhancing its strategy and aligning with people, augmenting their dignity and true re-excitement at work. Her mantra, “See, Be, Own the future with AI,” is a call for a responsible new leadership of the CEO and the Board — embracing the future of business where technology serves societies and humanity, not the other way around.

LinkedIn | DATAE HUMANUM

4. Dr. Desziree Richardson | Elevating Women’s Voices Globally

Dr. Desziree Richardson is a celebrated leader in global women’s empowerment, whose visionary efforts span across public speaking, media, fashion, and beauty. As the founder of the innovative platform, Face of Woha, Dr. Richardson has created a dynamic space that not only showcases women’s talents and stories but also empowers them to take center stage regardless of their background. Face of Woha is known for its public speaking events, TV productions, and a variety of products that reinforce women’s inherent power and potential.

Her commitment to women’s empowerment is deeply integrated into every facet of her work, including her role as an international speaker and branding expert. Dr. Richardson utilizes these platforms to motivate women globally, encouraging them to break barriers and pursue their dreams. Her initiatives are designed not just to celebrate achievements but to provide practical tools and a supportive community for women navigating various challenges.

One of Dr. Richardson’s notable quotes encapsulates her mission: “A man, woman, a nation, village or city unafraid to empower and uplift women and girls is among the most admired in the world.” This statement reflects her belief in the transformative power of uplifting women, which she actively promotes through her various roles and initiatives.

Dr. Richardson’s extensive work and dedication have not only earned her numerous accolades but have also made her a beacon of hope and a source of inspiration for many. Her efforts to foster a world where empowerment and equality are accessible to all women are a testament to her unwavering dedication to societal progress and gender equality.

LinkedIn

5. Dr. Cristina Lunghi | Pioneer in Professional Equality and Inclusive AI

Dr. Cristina Lunghi, the Founder and Managing Director of Arborus, is an internationally recognized expert on professional equality and inclusion, as well as a leading advocate for inclusive Artificial Intelligence (AI). With a PhD in Law from France, she has been at the forefront of promoting equality in employment and equal opportunities across Europe and beyond since establishing Arborus in 1995.

Her long-standing commitment to gender equality is reflected in her founding of CEPD (Conseil en Egalité Professionnelle et Diversité) in 2007, an organization specializing in gender and diversity training, consultancy, and studies. In 2010, she expanded her efforts by establishing the Endowment Fund Arborus, the first European fund for professional gender equality, with international reach, certified by Bureau Veritas Certification.

Dr. Lunghi’s work has earned her key roles on various international platforms, including her role as an expert for the European Commission on equality issues and her contribution as an international expert at UN Women since 2016. She has also authored several books and guides on professional equality, notably Et si les femmes réinventaient le travail, L’égalité professionnelle en pratique, and Bleu Blanc Rose.

As co-director of the Charter for Inclusive AI, Dr. Lunghi is at the forefront of addressing the challenges posed by AI. She strongly advocates for combating biased and sexist algorithms in technology. She asserts, “The potential of artificial intelligence is immense! However, it comes with biased and highly sexist algorithms. This calls for new forms of mobilization, activism, and perhaps even a new wave of feminism.” To tackle these societal challenges, she has proposed the International Charter for Inclusive AI and the GEEIS AI Certification, which aim to implement inclusive coding principles to create fair and unbiased AI systems.

Dr. Cristina Lunghi’s career is a testament to her tireless dedication to advancing gender equality in the workplace and ensuring that emerging technologies like AI are designed to be inclusive and equitable for all.

LinkedIn | Arborus | Charter for Inclusive AI

6. Akinwole II Omoboriowo: Illuminating Africa’s Energy Future

Akinwole II Omoboriowo (AOII) stands as a pivotal figure in Africa’s oil, gas, and power sectors, leading transformative initiatives as the Chairman and CEO of Genesis Energy Group. With over two decades of experience, he has been instrumental in actualizing Genesis’ mission of “Lighting up Africa, One community at a time,” overseeing the company’s expansion to over 100MW of operational assets and more than $150 million in energy sector investments.

Akinwole’s academic credentials are as distinguished as his professional achievements. He holds a degree in Economics from the University of Jos, with further specialization in Electricity Pricing & Modeling from the London Business School. In 2011, he earned a Post-Graduate Diploma in Strategy & Innovation from Oxford’s Saïd Business School, where he now shares his expertise as a lecturer, particularly in the context of African markets and infrastructure development.

His career has been marked by leadership in pioneering Independent Power Producing companies and thriving utility companies across Africa. In addition to his role at Genesis, he has served as Chairman of Bissau Electricidade de Agua in Guinea-Bissau and CEO of Petroleum Projects International, solidifying his influence in the continent’s energy sector.

Under Akinwole’s leadership, Genesis Energy Group now operates in nine African countries, with plans to extend its reach to 20 countries by the end of the decade. The company has a robust pipeline of energy projects totaling over 4GW, including 500MW contracted and 58MW under construction. His strategic vision has earned him recognition as one of “The Most Influential Figures across Africa in Power.”

Reflecting on his mission, Akinwole has said, “Innovation is the engine that drives progress, and strategic thinking is the fuel that powers it. Africa’s future lies in our ability to harness these forces to transform our continent.” His unwavering commitment to Africa’s development continues to drive the growth of sustainable energy solutions across the continent.

LinkedIn | Genesis Energy | Website

7. Liesa Euton | Leadership Development Expert | Women’s Empowerment Advocate

Leadership and professional development are crucial fields we should focus on in the current business world. In this regard, Liesa Euton is leading, particularly when we talk about empowering women in this field globally. Liesa Euton is the Director for the MENA & Caribbean regions at EHP International and has pioneered innovative Women’s Leadership workshops focused on empowering women and providing them with critical leadership skills. Her professional roles also extend to being an international speaker, and radio & TV presenter.

Liesa Euton is deeply committed to nurturing female leadership, a commitment that is reflected in her workshops and training solutions. These programs are designed to support women at various levels, from C-suite executives to small business owners, helping them advance in their careers and enhance their organizations’ success. Under her guidance, EHP International has become a beacon for female empowerment, breaking traditional barriers and fostering an environment where women can thrive in leadership roles. “We believe in equipping women with the tools they need to shatter the proverbial glass ceiling and take charge of their futures,” Liesa states. Through her efforts, Liesa continues to inspire a new generation of women to rise to leadership positions and drive meaningful change in their communities and beyond.

In addition to women’s empowerment, Liesa also focuses on bridging the gap between leadership and corporate sustainability. Through EHP International’s Corporate Sustainability Mindset Training, she helps organizations instill eco-friendly workplace practices. EHP has been a key player in providing sustainability training for businesses across various industries, empowering employees to incorporate green practices into their daily operations. These training programs are tailored to align with a company’s ESG goals and vision, promoting not just a “change” mindset but also a shift in workplace behaviours toward sustainability.

Founded in 1995, EHP International offers customizable training solutions for companies of all sizes and industries, ranging from hotels and banking to logistics and garment merchandising. EHP has a team of  International Trainers in Asia, the Middle East, Africa and the Caribbean.

Under the leadership of Raju and Liesa, EHP’s corporate training programs ensure employees are actively engaged, fostering a culture of sustainability that is integrated into both professional and personal spaces. The organization also offers its training services in multiple languages, ensuring global reach and impact.

Through the EHP Team of International trainers’ dedication to leadership development and sustainable business practices, EHP International has become a trusted partner for companies seeking to empower their workforce and adopt environmentally responsible operations.

LinkedIn | EHP International | Company LinkedIn.

8. Roula El Hachem | A Visionary Entrepreneur in the Hospitality Industry

At just 23, Roula El Hachem founded Dumont International for Business and Trading, a consultancy specializing in hotel furnishings. What started as a small business quickly expanded across Lebanon and the Gulf region, becoming a trusted partner for hospitality brands seeking a perfect blend of aesthetic design and functionality. Roula’s hands-on approach ensures that each project, from luxurious fabrics to bespoke furnishings, reflects the unique vision and brand identity of her clients

Dumont International is known for more than just hotel furnishings. Roula has cultivated a holistic consultancy, offering a comprehensive interior design service that elevates guest experiences while maximizing operational efficiency. Her team works closely with clients to craft personalized design plans, ensuring every detail enhances the atmosphere and functionality of each space. Through her factory, she produces high-quality fabrics, clothing, and textiles, guaranteeing that curtains, bed linens, and upholstery meet the highest standards.

In response to the growing needs of her clients, Roula expanded her offerings to include renovation and construction services. By managing projects from concept to completion, she is able to deliver full-spectrum solutions, covering everything from initial design to large-scale project execution. This move has further cemented her leadership in the hospitality sector, showcasing her ability to integrate multiple facets of the industry under one umbrella.

Recently, Roula launched an amenities and personal care product line, adding yet another layer to her diverse range of services. Dumont International can now furnish a hotel from A to Z, offering custom linens, mattresses, sanitary products, and luxury toiletries. This seamless integration of services demonstrates Roula’s visionary leadership and deep understanding of the hospitality industry’s needs.

Roula El Hachem’s journey is a testament to the power of innovation, hard work, and leadership. Her ability to grow a business that delivers unparalleled quality and service has made her a trailblazer in her field, proving that success knows no age limit. Today, Dumont International stands as a dynamic force in the industry, and Roula continues to inspire with her forward-thinking approach and unwavering commitment to excellence.

LinkedIn 

9. Dr. Marika Crohns: A Beacon of Leadership and Innovation in Healthcare

Dr. Marika Crohns, MD, PhD, stands as a towering figure in the global healthcare landscape, with a career that spans over three decades. Her journey is not just one of professional success but one of relentless dedication to transforming healthcare. Dr. Crohns is celebrated for her extraordinary blend of medical expertise and extensive commercial acumen, a combination that has enabled her to lead with both vision and empathy.

From the early stages of her career, Dr. Crohns demonstrated a unique ability to see beyond the status quo, identifying gaps in healthcare delivery and innovating solutions that prioritize patient outcomes. Her leadership has been instrumental in driving forward healthcare initiatives that have had a profound impact on both clinical practice and healthcare policy.

One of the hallmarks of Dr. Crohns’ leadership is her commitment to mentorship. Recognizing that the future of healthcare depends on the next generation of leaders, she has dedicated significant effort to nurturing talent within her teams. Her approach to mentorship goes beyond mere guidance; she actively invests in the personal and professional growth of her colleagues, empowering them to take on leadership roles with confidence and competence.

In addition to her mentorship, Dr. Crohns is known for her visionary approach to integrating technology into healthcare. She has been at the forefront of adopting cutting-edge technologies, such as AI and telemedicine, to enhance patient care and streamline healthcare operations. Her strategic foresight has positioned her organizations at the leading edge of healthcare innovation, setting new standards for others to follow.

Dr. Crohns’ leadership is also deeply rooted in empathy. She understands that at the heart of healthcare are the patients, and she has consistently advocated for patient-centered care. Her ability to balance the demands of a rapidly evolving healthcare industry with the need for compassionate care has earned her immense respect from her peers and those she serves.

As a C-suite executive, Dr. Crohns has not only led her organizations to commercial success but has also championed initiatives that have improved healthcare access and equity. Her influence extends beyond the boardroom, as she actively participates in shaping healthcare policy, ensuring that the systems in place serve the best interests of patients and healthcare providers alike.

Dr. Marika Crohns is more than a leader; she is an inspiration. Her career is a testament to the power of visionary leadership, where innovation, empathy, and mentorship converge to create a lasting impact. Her work continues to inspire healthcare professionals worldwide, proving that true leadership in healthcare is about making a difference that transcends the boundaries of the industry.

LinkedIn 

10. Joseph Frankie III | Elevating Careers through LinkedIn Strategy and Leadership

Joseph Frankie III, a retired U.S. Army Colonel and founder of JFIII Associates LLC, brings over 30 years of leadership and strategic experience from his military service to the private sector. His distinguished career has taken him across the globe, where he developed a deep understanding of leadership, team dynamics, and effective communication—skills he now channels into career coaching. Through JFIII Associates, Joseph specializes in guiding professionals on how to leverage LinkedIn for career growth and personal branding.

Joseph’s coaching style is unique, having successfully coached more than 700 executives, veterans, and students to elevate their professional presence. He firmly believes that a well-curated LinkedIn profile is a critical tool for success, once famously stating, “If it’s not on your LinkedIn profile, it never happened.” Inspired by the legendary baseball player Dizzy Dean’s philosophy, Joseph emphasizes the importance of owning your achievements and showcasing them authentically to make a lasting impact.

Beyond optimizing profiles, Joseph’s expertise lies in helping professionals at various career stages, from new graduates seeking their first role to seasoned veterans eyeing their next move. His deep sector knowledge allows him to guide clients through complex transitions, whether they’re switching industries, seeking promotion, or pivoting to new fields entirely. His coaching is personalized, offering strategies tailored to each client’s unique goals.

As the leader of JFIII Associates, Joseph continues to empower individuals to achieve their full potential through networking and personal branding, particularly via LinkedIn. His insights and strategies underscore the importance of building a strong digital footprint in today’s competitive job market, helping professionals stand out and reach their goals.

Website | LinkedIn | JFIII Associates | Twitter | Facebook

Conclusion

In 2024, the top 10 inspiring leaders to watch are not only shaping the present but also building the future. Their stories serve as a reminder that true leadership is about vision, perseverance, and the ability to inspire others to reach new heights. As these trailblazers continue to innovate and break barriers, they will leave a lasting legacy, not just in their industries, but in the broader world of business. Watching their journeys unfold will undoubtedly inspire others to follow in their footsteps, embracing bold ideas and driving meaningful change.

title: Arab League Commends UAE for Halting the Proliferation of Illegal Small Arms
author: editor
excerpt: The UAE was recognised by the League of Arab States for its contributions to the program that the League, in collaboration with the European Union, organised to stop the illegal spread of light and small arms throughout Arab nations. The UAE’s participation in the “Conference on Combating the Illicit Trade in, and Proliferation of Small Arms and Light Weapons,” which was held at the Arab League headquarters in Cairo, came to an end with this recognition. Mohamed Suhail Al Neyadi, head of the UAE delegation and Director-General of the Weapons and Hazardous Substances Office of the Supreme Council for National Security, accepted the award. The conference covered several topics, including the assessment of the second phase of the EU and Arab League program aimed at preventing the proliferation and illicit trafficking of light and small arms, the difficulties encountered in this phase, the project’s prospects going forward, and international controls on the transfer of small arms, such as border control and measures to stop the flow of illegal weapons by locating and obstructing their sources. title: Suhail Al Mazrouei: The UAE has Invested More than Dhs45 Billion in Clean Energy
author: editor
excerpt: The UAE has significantly increased the share of clean energy production in the overall energy mix, with Suhail Bin Mohammed Al Mazrouei, Minister of Energy and Infrastructure, stating that the country reached 27.83 percent in 2023, falling short of the target of 32 percent by 2030. Al Mazrouei stated, “From 2019 to 2022, the UAE has succeeded in doubling its renewable energy capacity as part of the UAE Energy Strategy to triple the installed capacity by 2030, towards our commitment to achieve the energy transition targets as per the UAE Consensus at COP28,” in an interview with the Emirates News Agency (WAM) in advance of the World Utilities Congress 2024, which gets underway in Abu Dhabi tomorrow. He continued that the UAE made significant progress in renewable energy competitive indicators in 2023, “achieving a quantum leap from sixth to second place in the indicator of per capita energy consumption from renewable energy sources in the latest Statistical Review of World Energy prepared by the Energy Institute.” Installed renewable energy capacity reached 6.1 GW, a remarkable 70% growth. Regarding the UAE’s dedication to encouraging investment in clean and renewable energy, Al Mazrouei said: Our finished new and renewable energy projects are estimated to be worth over Dhs45 billion in total. The value of the most recent projects currently operational is not even included in this figure.
