title: UAE: Free Parking is Offered in Sharjah on the Prophet’s Birthday
author: editor
excerpt: The public parking lot in Sharjah will be free on Sunday, September 15, in honor of Prophet Muhammad’s birthday. The seven-day paid public parking zones, which are marked by blue parking information signs and open Monday through Friday and on official holidays, are not covered by this exemption, according to Sharjah Municipality. The third month of the Islamic calendar, Rabi’ Al-Awwal 1444, is the Prophet’s birthday in most Islamic nations, including those in the Gulf. Residents of the UAE will have a long December holiday following this one, as it is National Day. Monday and Tuesday are the dates of December 2 and 3, respectively. When combined with the Saturday-Sunday weekend, that makes for a four-day holiday. In order to control the high demand for parking spaces in this important residential and commercial district, the Municipality of Sharjah announced on September 2 that all public parking around the Muwaileh commercial area would now be subject to charges throughout the week, including public holidays. The Public Parking Management of Sharjah Municipality has put up blue directional signs all over the place to let drivers know about the new hours and costs. title: Capital and Reserves of UAE Banks Reached Dhs495.2 Billion
author: editor
excerpt: According to the most recent data from the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), the total capital and reserves of banks operating in the UAE reached Dhs 495.2 billion at the end of June 2024, a year-over-year (YoY) increase of 10.6% from Dhs 447.8 billion in June 2023. According to data released today by the apex bank, the capital and reserves of banks in the nation increased by 1.5 percent monthly and 1.2 percent in the first half of the year. The CBUAE clarified that current-year profits are included in banks’ capital and reserves, but subordinated borrowings and deposits are not. In June 2023, national banks made up 86.3 percent of all the capital and reserves held by banks in the nation. As of the end of June, their value had increased to Dhs427.5 billion, a YoY increase of 10.6 percent, from Dhs386.6 billion. Foreign banks now account for 13.7 percent of all capital and reserves held by banks that operate in the United Arab Emirates. As of the end of June, their value was Dhs67.7 billion, up 10.6 percent year over year from Dhs61.2 billion in June 2023. According to the US Labour Department, initial claims for state unemployment benefits increased by 2,000 to a seasonally adjusted 230,000. title: Sheikh Mohammed Establishes a New Media Company to Oversee Dubai’s Advertising Sites
author: editor
excerpt: Enacted by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the Vice President and Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates, in his capacity as the Ruler of Dubai, law No. (20) of 2024 relates to the establishment of Mada Media Company, a private joint-stock company (PJSC) with the purpose of managing and running advertising sites in Dubai. As per the legal regulations, the recently established organisation is assigned the responsibility of overseeing, creating, and running advertising websites, as well as investing in advertising technologies and carrying out relevant research, all while maintaining regulatory compliance. It also permits the business to establish alliances, acquire property, and enter into agreements with other parties to accomplish its goals both inside and outside the emirate. The Articles of Association specify the duties and authority of the Commissioner General for the Infrastructure, Urban Planning, and Well-Being Pillar, who is designated by law to supervise the organization’s activities and guarantee that its goals are met. Moreover, Decision No. (79) of 2024 approving the “Articles of Association of Mada Media (PJSC),” including its rules and provisions, was issued by Sheikh Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai. content:
Happy Joe’s Pizza & Ice Cream Parlors, founded in 1972, quickly gained popularity for its innovative menu. The Taco Joe Pizza, the world’s first taco pizza, was born out of a challenge to compete with a local taco shop. Founder Joe Whitty turned the idea into a game-changing pizza that combined taco ingredients with a pizza base, creating a culinary sensation. Despite initial challenges, the Taco Joe Pizza became the brand’s signature item, contributing to Happy Joe’s success and cult-like following. Today, the company continues to innovate while maintaining the consistency and quality that customers love.

A Happy Joe’s Origin Story

We started the interview by asking, “Can you share the story behind the creation of the Taco Joe Pizza? What inspired Happy Joe’s to create the first taco pizza in the world?”

Thomas Sacco replied, “The Birth of the Taco Joe Pizza: A Happy Joe’s Original!  Happy Joe’s Pizza & Ice Cream Parlors was founded on November 12th, 1972. From the start, Happy Joe’s was a success. Unlike many businesses that struggle in their early years, Happy Joe’s took off immediately, with lines out the door and rave reviews spreading fast. One couple, Max and Betty Brewer from Muscatine, Iowa, were particularly smitten. Every weekend, they traveled 45 minutes just to enjoy Joe’s famous pizzas and ice cream specialties. Over time, they became friends with Joe and watched as his business flourished.

One day, Max and Betty threw out the idea of opening a Happy Joe’s franchise in Muscatine. They believed Joe’s concept would be a hit in their community and wanted to be the first franchisees. Joe, thinking they were joking, laughed and said, “Well, bring me a check for $5,000, and we’ll talk.” To his surprise, the next weekend, Max and Betty did just that.

A few years into their business, Max and Betty came to Joe with a concern. Although their Happy Joe’s locations were thriving, a new taco shop had opened nearby, drawing customers away. They asked Joe if they could add tacos to their menu to compete. While Joe found the idea interesting, he wasn’t keen on getting into the taco business. Still, he told the Brewers he would think about it.

Joe went to the local grocery store and bought all the ingredients for what he envisioned to be the best taco he could make. But there was one twist—there was no plan of making any tacos in Happy Joe’s location. He was going to invent an amazing taco experience on a pizza!

Joe had a way of rallying people around an idea, and this was no exception. Soon, all Happy Joe’s locations were serving Taco Joe Pizzas, and it was a hit everywhere. It quickly became a newsworthy sensation, further cementing Happy Joe’s reputation for innovation.

Little did Joe know at the time that this creation would cement his name in history as the first entrepreneur to create a taco pizza?”

Joe’s Secret Ingredient

Entrepreneur Mirror: What do you believe sets Joe’s Signature Taco Joe Pizza apart from other taco pizzas on the market?

Thomas Sacco replied, “Joe created a taco pizza that tasted incredible, and topped the pizza with fresh lettuce, bright red tomatoes, and seasoned taco chips. This elevated both the look and the taste profile of the pizza to another level. The result was not only delicious but also visually stunning.  From that point forward, the Taco Joe Pizza became a sensation.”

A Cult Classic in the Making

Entrepreneur Mirror: How has the Taco Joe Pizza contributed to the overall success and cult-like following of Happy Joe’s?

Thomas Sacco replied, “Since then, many restaurants have tried to replicate Joe’s recipe, but nothing can match the original Taco Joe Pizza. Joe later expanded his Mexican-style pizza offerings to include a Taco Supreme Pizza, Nacho Joe, and the Matador. Additionally, Happy Joe’s now sells its own branded taco sauce and specially seasoned chips in grocery stores.

Fast forward to today, and Happy Joe’s boasts over 50 locations, with new ones on the horizon, both domestically and abroad. The Taco Joe Pizza remains the company’s number one seller and has made the Happy Joe’s brand a household name in the areas where they reside.”

Introducing a Unique Pizza

Entrepreneur Mirror: Can you discuss any challenges Happy Joe’s faced when initially introducing the Taco Joe Pizza and how those were overcome?

Thomas Sacco replied, “However, the process wasn’t without its challenges. Franchisees had to order new ingredients, and the taco chips and lettuce created quite a mess in the kitchens. Some franchisees were hesitant, citing the extra work and mess.  Joe stood firm. He knew this pizza had the potential to be a game-changer for Happy Joe’s.”

Ensuring Consistent Taste

Entrepreneur Mirror: How does Happy Joe’s ensure the consistency and quality of the Taco Joe Pizza across all its locations, including franchisees?

Thomas Sacco replied, “As we have grown across the US and around the globe, our recipes, ingredients, and procedures for all core menu items have been memorialized with the advent of the digital world we all conduct business in.  Our Franchise Business Coaches (FBC) are in every Happy Joe’s locations, everywhere we have locations, at least four times a year checking, coaching, critiquing, counseling, and complimenting each Head Coach (General Manager) at our Happy Joe’s.”

The Next Big Thing?

Entrepreneur Mirror: Can you describe any upcoming innovations or new menu items that might join the ranks of the Taco Joe Pizza in popularity?

Thomas Sacco replied, “Another real winner that we rolled out in 2023 was our Sloppy Joe Pizza.  We are becoming very well known for taking our favorite, comfort food, regardless of genealogy, and recreating it in a pizza format.  Our Sloppy Joe Pizza was one of the few pizzas that have ever out sold a Taco Joe Pizza.

The Secret Sauce

Lastly we asked, “How does Happy Joe’s engage with its loyal customer base and cultivate the cult-like following for the Taco Joe Pizza, especially in the age of social media?”

“As the Chief Happiness Officer, I have my personal cell phone and email address on everything so our guests can share ALL their feedback, good, bad, creative, or silly with me.

This communication link has helped create a consistent flowing pipeline of ideas, coupled with the continued input from our Franchisee owners in the US and across the globe, to our Director of Culinary Services, Ashley Balluff and I, to work on all menu ideations.  If we look at 10 ideas, we present 1 to our Product Innovation Committee (PIC) for their signoff and approval.  Whenever we get that far, we go into a live test mode in our company Happy Joe’s locations to gauge how well or not so well, our guests enjoy the new menu offering, to assess and determine the ease of preparation, or lack thereof, that our team members go through to make a great Happy Joe’s pizza.” Thomas Sacco Concluded

author: editor
excerpt: Emirates is scheduled to take delivery of its first Airbus A350 in October. By the end of the year, the airline expects to have five Airbus aircraft delivered. We had to extend the service of some of our current aircraft due to delays in aircraft deliveries,” he continued. Alredha also brought up the company’s aircraft modernisation program and Emirates’ dedication to offering the greatest customer experience. Alredha clarified that the delivery issues have been there for years because the COVID-19 pandemic forced many aircraft manufacturing companies to reduce production or lay off a portion of their workforce. Consequently, he went on, these companies were unable to effectively reorganise their operations and meet the high demand for air travel that followed the end of the pandemic. title: By the End of June, gross Banks Assets will Surpass Dhs4.3 Trillion. CBUAE
author: editor
excerpt: According to data released by the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), the gross assets of all banks, including bankers’ acceptances, increased by 0.5% from Dhs4,287.0 billion at the end of May 2024 to Dhs4,310.2 billion at the end of June 2024. In its Monetary and Banking Developments for June 2024 report, the Central Bank stated that gross credit increased by 1.1% from Dhs2,077.7 billion at the end of May 2024 to Dhs2,100.9 billion at the end of June 2024. Gross credit increased due to 2.9% growth in foreign credit and 0.8% increase in domestic credit. The bank claimed that the increase in domestic credit was caused by increases in credit to the private and public sectors (government-related entities) of 1.4% and 1.0%, respectively, offsetting decreases in credit to non-banking financial institutions and the government sector of 1.1% and 0.6%, respectively. By the end of June 2024, bank deposits had increased by 0.5 percent, from Dhs2,678.2 billion at the end of May 2024 to Dhs2,692.5 billion. The increase in non-resident deposits, which accounted for 8.4% of the total bank deposit growth, outweighed the 0.1% decline in resident deposits. title: As of October 1, Abu Dhabi Offers Genetic Testing as Part of Premarital Examinations for Emiratis
author: editor
excerpt: According to the Department of Health—Abu Dhabi, genetic testing will be a mandatory component of the pre-marital screening program for Emiratis in the emirate beginning on October 1. The action is motivated by a desire to enable people to make the healthiest decisions for their families and themselves. The inclusion came about due to the successful pilot program, which was started in 2022 in collaboration with the Abu Dhabi Public Health Centre. During that time, about 800 couples underwent genetic testing in Abu Dhabi and received the support they needed to make decisions regarding the health of their future children. According to the program’s data, 86% of couples were able to confirm their genetic compatibility, and only 14% of them required further assistance in order to create a suitable family plan based on their genetic results. The test improves the capacity to identify genetic risks or possible hereditary conditions by including 570 genes for over 840 medical conditions. The test, which is the most crucial preventive measure when preparing to start a family, involves speaking with genetic counsellors and medical professionals to gain a thorough understanding of potential risks and available treatments. title: A Woman in Dubai was Fined Dhs 1,000 for Verbally Abusing her Boss and Accusing him of Drug Trafficking and Human Trafficking
author: editor
excerpt: An Arab woman who verbally abused her employer after a disagreement between them was fined Dhs1,000 by the Dubai Misdemeanours Court. Her accusations against him allegedly included drug sales, human trafficking, and indecent behaviour. The case’s details date back to April of last year, when the employer reported that one of his workers had insulted him. Despite his attempts to calm her down and ask her to stop shouting in the workplace, the latter suddenly made up a problem at work and began to shout at him and loudly insult him, according to what the employer told the police. He went on to say that the accused did not quit and persisted in abusing him in front of other workers, claiming that he engages in immoral activities and trades in drugs and flesh. Even when her coworkers tried to calm her down and asked her to stop, she ignored their requests. A female employee of the same company claimed she had tried to step in and console the defendant, but she had been rejected. title: An Interline Agreement is Announced by Flydubai and SriLankan Airlines
author: editor
excerpt: A new interline agreement between SriLankan Airlines and flydubai, the airline based in Dubai, will go into effect on September 9, 2024. It will provide more travel options on specific routes within the carriers’ networks between the UAE and Sri Lanka. With this agreement, flydubai customers will have access to 16 Sri Lankan destinations in Australia, the Middle East, Southern and East Asia, and Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, and Melbourne. Thanks to the interline, passengers flying on Sri Lankan Airlines will also be able to effortlessly connect through Dubai’s aviation hub to over 30 destinations in Africa, Central Asia, Central and Southeast Europe, and the Middle East. These include well-known vacation destinations like Mombasa, Naples, Tashkent, Krakow, Bucharest, and Zanzibar. We are thrilled to collaborate with Flydubai to offer our customers smoother connections and more convenience. This collaboration bolsters our plan to broaden our network and reach internationally while providing clients with increased flexibility and travel options. Richard Nuttall, the CEO of Sri Lankan Airlines, stated, We are excited to work with flydubai and welcome their guests on board to experience an authentic Sri Lankan journey. Under the new agreement, passengers are provided with convenient single-ticket itineraries, through-checked baggage, and coordinated flight schedules. title: Fewer Rates Provide Protection from the Storm of Property
author: editor
excerpt: There is little chance that the free money that fuelled a boom will return, and the global property markets, rattled by the sharpest increase in interest rates in a generation, will benefit much from the gradual easing of borrowing costs. The multitrillion-dollar industry has suffered greatly as central banks have raised borrowing costs. This industry flourished in the decade following the global financial crisis when the cost of money was lowered to zero. Currently, interest rates are being lowered by central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, the European Central Bank, the Bank of England, Switzerland, and Sweden. According to consultants Falkensteg, the number of property insolvencies in Germany has been increasing since early 2022 and surpassed 1,100 in the first half of this year. Over the 12 months ending June 2024, the construction industry in Britain saw approximately 4,300 insolvencies, more than any other industry for the previous two years. Rising borrowing costs and remote work are causing severe pain for offices, but the effects are also being felt in the large housing market, which has collapsed in Germany and faltered in Britain. title: GCC Propels Sukuk Issuances to Almost all-Time Highs
author: editor
excerpt: Sovereign solid issuance in the GCC and Southeast Asia is expected to boost this year’s global sukuk issuance to $200 billion to $210 billion, surpassing the slightly under $200 billion total from 2023, according to Moody’s Ratings. According to Moody’s analysts, the sukuk market has significant growth potential in the upcoming years, helped along by the entry of new issuers who will cater to the growing demand for sukuk assets. Since the governments in the region are still working to diversify their economies away from the oil industry, we anticipate that GCC issuance will continue to be robust. According to them, GCC issuance increased 138% in the first half of the year to $69.2 billion. Although sukuk activity in the UAE doubled to $8.6 billion annually due to higher overall volumes, the GCC’s robust first-half issuance was primarily driven by Saudi Arabia, which accounted for 37% of all issuance, and Malaysia, which issued close to 30% of all sukuk. The GCC countries’ issuance will continue to be robust despite a slowdown in the second half of the year to approximately $80 to $90 billion, as their governments continue to seek ways to diversify their economies away from the oil industry. According to Abdulla AlHammadi, assistant vice president and analyst at Moody’s Ratings, “those looking to issue sustainable sukuk, those looking to diversify funding sources and investors, or those returning to the market after delaying issuance will drive issuance by companies and financial institutions. title: The First Week of Amnesty sees Close to 20,000 Applications for Dubai
author: editor
excerpt: The UAE began offering an amnesty on September 1, 2024, to settle the status of overstayers. As the seventh day of the amnesty approaches, the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in Dubai (GDRFA) reports a notable turnout. The enormous turnout is proof of the UAE’s dedication to upholding its humanitarian role, encouraging community safety, and enhancing living standards. The high degree of participation and productive partnership between partners and government agencies support these claims. During the first seven days of operation, the GDRFA received 19,784 applications in total. A 48-hour turnaround time of 98.96% for these demonstrates the effectiveness of the work teams and digital services used. Over 2,393 individuals visited the settlement centre in Al Aweer, Dubai during the first seven days of operation, accounting for 10.15% of all applications received in the Emirate of Dubai. This was a remarkable influx of customers. title: The Non-Oil Economy of Saudi Arabia Expanded by 4.9% in Q2: GASTAT
author: editor
excerpt: According to official data, Saudi Arabia’s non-oil activities grew 4.9% year over year in the second quarter of 2024, led by improvements in the insurance and financial industries. In comparison to the same period last year, the financial, insurance, and business services sectors saw a 7.1% increase in second-quarter revenue, according to data released by Arab News and sourced from the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT). The report also showed that, in comparison to the first quarter, Saudi Arabia’s seasonally adjusted gross domestic product grew by 1.4% in the second quarter. The Kingdom’s decision to reduce crude output under OPEC+ agreements resulted in an 8.9% decline in oil activities during the same period, which contributed to the GDP’s slight year-over-year decline of 0.3%. In April 2023, Saudi Arabia lowered its oil production by 500,000 barrels per day in an effort to stabilise the market. This reduction has been maintained through December 2024. Additionally, according to GASTAT, the Kingdom’s GDP for the second quarter came to SR1.02 trillion ($270 billion) at current prices. According to GASTAT, “activities related to crude oil and natural gas achieved the highest contribution to the GDP, at 23.2%. title: Korea Reports a 19.9% Increase in Foreign travellers Between July and August
author: editor
excerpt: Data released on Sunday showed that during the summer vacation, the Republic of Korea saw a 19.9% YoY increase in the number of international flight passengers, fully recovering to the pre-pandemic level. Yonhap News Agency reported that in July and August, 15.69 million people used international flights at Korean airports, up nearly 20 percent from the same period last year. The Korea Airports Corp. and the Incheon International Airport Corp provided the data. The amount for this year was roughly 97% of the total recorded in 2019. The highest number of travellers for a single country was 4.17 million, who used flights connecting Korea and Japan as their destination during the period under review. The number represented a growth of 25% from the 2019 level and an increase of 18.5 percent year over year. In the summer, 2.79 million passengers took flights to and from China, representing a 58.9 percent year-over-year increase. According to the data, demand for flights connecting Europe edged down 0.2 percent to 879,000, while the number of passengers travelling to and from America increased 16.3 percent to 1.23 million. title: Egypt and the UAE Deepen Economic Ties in Important Areas
author: editor
excerpt: The Egyptian Minister of Economy, Abdullah Bin Touq Al Marri, met one-on-one with Dr Rania Al Mashat, the country’s Minister of Planning, Economic Development, and International Cooperation, and Lieutenant General Kamel El Wazir, the country’s Deputy Prime Minister for Industrial Development and Minister of Industry and Transport. The goal of the conversation was to improve the UAE and Egypt’s economic cooperation in several areas, such as infrastructure, entrepreneurship, the new economy, transportation, the circular economy, agriculture, and industry. The meeting happened concurrently with Bin Touq’s attendance at the 114th Arab Economic and Social Council session. The UAE presided over the council meeting, which was held at the General Secretariat of the League of Arab States’ Cairo headquarters. The Minister of Economy emphasised the solid strategic ties and close kinship between Egypt and the United Arab Emirates, which are characterised by thriving partnerships and collaborations across a range of industries. Both countries possess significant economic resources and potential, as well as advantageous geographic locations that enable easy access to multiple important markets,” stated Bin Touq. title: The Hidden Potential of Abandoned Projects: From Failure to World-Class Triumphs
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Is there a sight more depressing than an abandoned project in the heart of a bustling city? Standing as a testament to failure, a silent witness to the unrealized dreams and aspirations it was meant to embody. However, there are times when such a depressing sight is, in fact, a blessing in disguise. Across the globe, and particularly in Dubai, there are countless examples of abandoned or stalled developments that have been revived, repurposed, and transformed into iconic landmarks—sometimes even breaking world records in the process. Dubai, known for its resilience and creativity, has seen several such transformations. One notable example is the Marina Yacht Club. Initially a two-story building that was underperforming on a rare and valuable plot, it was redeveloped into a towering skyscraper by Vida Emaar, along with a massive new yacht club. This redevelopment has made it one of the most sought-after residential locations in Dubai Marina, where finding new plots is nearly impossible. Another example is the Meydan Beach Club on Jumeirah Beach Residence (JBR), one of the best beach plots in JBR. It was repurposed into the gigantic, luxurious Five Hotel and Residences. Building on this success, Sensoria at Five, another luxury skyscraper, is currently under construction on the same plot, further cementing the value of once-failed projects. Among Dubai’s most iconic unfinished developments is the Dubai Pearl, a massive 7-million-square-foot plot at the base of Palm Jumeirah. Although it remains incomplete, its sheer size and iconic location make it an incredibly valuable asset. Once revived, it would be nearly impossible to put a price tag on such prime real estate, and it will potentially redefine the city’s skyline. One of the most remarkable revivals in recent times is the Pentominium Tower by Trident, once an abandoned vision. It is now being transformed into the Six Senses Tower, which will claim the title of the world’s tallest residential building. With lush, super high-end finishes and unparalleled designs, this project is set to redefine luxury living. Similarly, just a few plots down, Al Qabda Holding’s stalled project was picked up by London Gate in collaboration with the renowned watchmaker Franck Muller. The development will feature a state-of-the-art mechanical clock, set to be the tallest in the world, adding a new landmark to Dubai’s list of record-breaking achievements. These projects highlight the resilience and innovation that characterize Dubai’s approach to development. What were once considered failures or eyesores are now setting new global standards, proving that with the right vision, any project can be transformed into a world-class success. Globally, similar success stories can be found. In New York, the Hudson Yards development transformed an underutilized industrial area into one of the largest and most expensive private real estate projects in U.S. history. In London, the Battersea Power Station, long abandoned, has been revitalized into a thriving hub of residential, retail, and office spaces, with major companies like Apple choosing it as their headquarters. Both in Dubai and across the world, these examples show that even the most challenging projects can become iconic successes. What might appear as setbacks are often just opportunities waiting to be realized, proving that vision and determination can turn failure into a record-breaking triumph. About Author: Hamzah Abu Zannad is an industry expert and the co-founder and managing director of Axiom Prime Real Estate Development. With over 20 years of experience in the Dubai real estate market, Hamzah has played a pivotal role in introducing innovative and sustainable living concepts to the region. Under his leadership, Axiom Prime has gained recognition for its Dutch-inspired, cozy, and luxurious developments that emphasize community-centric design and cutting-edge technology. Their notable projects in Jumeirah Village Triangle and Jumeirah Garden City “Satwa” reflect their dedication to creating spaces that promote a sense of belonging and offer unique opportunities for growth. For more information, visit Axiom Prime Real Estate Development. 4. Jennifer Smith | A Leader in Media Innovation and Inclusion

Jennifer Smith has transformed the media landscape by combining impactful storytelling with a passion for social change. As the Founder and CEO of Everything Podcasts, she has built a platform that gives a voice to brands and stories that need to be heard. Jennifer’s work has long been driven by her advocacy for LGBTQIA+ and BIPOC communities, ensuring representation and inclusion at every step. Her career is a testament to the power of purpose-driven storytelling, where creativity and social responsibility come together to create meaningful change.

Breaking through countless barriers, Jennifer has consistently paved the way for women in the media. She was the first woman to serve on the British Columbia Association of Broadcasters and the first female Vice President in Western Canada’s radio industry. She also co-founded OutTV, the world’s first gay and lesbian television network, which was a groundbreaking achievement in media. Her contributions didn’t stop there—Jennifer’s entrepreneurial spirit led her to develop six startups, including the successful sale of Rainbow Connections to Headline Media Group, which linked business and charitable giving in a revolutionary way.

Jennifer’s innovative leadership at Everything Podcasts has earned widespread recognition. The company won multiple accolades at the 2023 and 2024 Quill Podcast Awards, including Best Podcast Agency and Most Creative Brand Podcast of the Year for “Ideas of Order,” created with California Closets and Netflix’s Tan France. In 2023, they received the Best B2B Branded Podcast of the Year for their series “Beyond” with KPMG, further solidifying Jennifer’s reputation for blending creative excellence with strategic business growth.

Jennifer’s individual achievements have also been recognized with several prestigious awards. In 2024, she was the Finalist for BC Business’s Women of the Year Award in the Diversity and Inclusion category. Her work in the podcast industry earned her the YWCA Women of Distinction Award for Entrepreneur and Innovation in 2023, as well as a finalist spot for the Quill Podcast Awards’ Innovator of the Year. These accolades highlight not only her business acumen but also her commitment to uplifting marginalized voices and creating a more inclusive world.

Beyond her professional endeavors, Jennifer is dedicated to mentorship and giving back to her community. She annually takes on pro-bono clients to raise awareness for important causes, using her platform to shine a light on issues that matter. Her leadership and generosity continue to inspire the next generation, as she mentors future leaders to embrace innovation, inclusion, and social impact. For Jennifer Smith, the future of media is about more than profit—it’s about creating a world where every voice is heard.

5. Ihab Hallab | Innovating Public Interests through Social Impact Technology

Ihab Hallab stands out as a visionary social impact entrepreneur whose transformative work in technology, public policy, and impact investments has positioned him as a leader in his field, despite his young age. As the co-founder and CEO of SmartGov, Ihab has been at the forefront of revolutionizing public governance through tech-driven innovation. Since its founding in 2020, SmartGov has become a pivotal force in public reform, developing solutions to some of the most pressing challenges faced by governments today. Under Ihab’s leadership, SmartGov has been involved in projects worth over $2.2 million, including both consortium and organizational initiatives, helping to reshape government operations to better serve citizens.

Before SmartGov, Ihab was already making a global impact through his consultancy work with renowned organizations such as the OECD and SALAR International, and his contributions to R&D projects with universities in Lebanon. His research and initiatives have been crucial in areas like E-government, Digital Transformation, Public Policy, and Civic Technologies, bridging the gap between social sciences and technology.

Ihab’s influence extends to the global social impact community, highlighted by his selection as a social impact fellow at Halcyon House in Washington, D.C., where he joins a network that has collectively raised $350 million and positively impacted over 2.7 million lives. His dedication to public reform has earned him accolades, including being named one of the ‘Most Influential Young Arab Pioneers’ at the age of 19 by the UAE government’s Arab Youth Center.

As a speaker at international summits like the World Government Summit in Dubai and the Middle East & Mediterranean Summit in Switzerland, Ihab continues to advocate for interdisciplinary collaboration and the integration of technology in public governance. His work not only transforms how governments operate but also inspires a new generation of entrepreneurs and leaders to pursue innovation for the betterment of society.

Through his unwavering commitment to societal progress and his innovative approach to governance, Ihab Hallab is shaping a future where technology and public policy work hand in hand to create more efficient, responsive, and equitable governments. His journey is a testament to the power of youth-driven change and the potential for a better, more connected world.

6. Deb Farnworth-Wood: Redefining Skincare with ISSADA Cosmetics

Deb Farnworth-Wood, the Owner and Managing Director of ISSADA Cosmetics, is a powerhouse in the skincare industry, known for her innovative approach and visionary leadership. With a career that began in hospitality and retail, Deb quickly transitioned into a role with the UK National Health Service, where she honed her leadership skills over 18 years. Her move to Australia marked a new chapter, where she founded Australian Skin Clinics, transforming it into a $70 million international franchise.

In 2020, Deb took the helm of ISSADA Cosmetics, a brand she had long admired. Under her leadership, ISSADA has introduced the ISSADA Clinical Formula skincare range, reflecting her commitment to clean cosmeceuticals and holistic skincare. Deb’s ability to balance visionary thinking with operational excellence has driven the brand’s success, launching innovative products like the Synbiotic Moisturizer, which utilizes live probiotics to restore the skin microbiome.

Deb’s leadership is marked by her emphasis on adaptability and employee well-being. She has implemented a four-day workweek in ISSADA’s factory, fostering a better work-life balance while maintaining productivity. Her forward-thinking approach also includes leveraging digital tools to enhance customer engagement and streamline operations.

Beyond her achievements with ISSADA, Deb is passionate about mentoring the next generation of female entrepreneurs. She is actively involved in supporting women in business through board memberships and sponsorship of the Women in Business Awards Australia, further solidifying her impact on the industry.

Deb Farnworth-Wood’s dedication to innovation and excellence ensures that ISSADA Cosmetics remains a leader in the skincare industry, setting new standards for quality and efficacy.

LinkedIn | ISSADA | Website | Instagram | TikTok | Pinterest | Facebook

7. Juan José Thuemme | A Visionary Flavorist Reviving Mexico’s Culinary Heritage

Juan José Thuemme is not just a flavorist; he is a cultural ambassador, weaving the rich tapestry of Mexico’s culinary heritage into the global palate. As the Global Flavorist and Creative Center Leader at Etadar by Deiman, Thuemme’s innovative approach is revolutionizing the flavor industry, particularly through his groundbreaking work on “Native Flavors.” This unique flavor class celebrates the traditional pre-Hispanic Mexican ingredients and customs that have faded from contemporary cuisine. By resurrecting these ancient flavors, Thuemme ensures that the world can once again taste the essence of Mexico’s past.

Since joining Deiman in 2014 after a distinguished tenure with international flavor houses, Thuemme has been instrumental in transforming Deiman into a global leader in flavor innovation. His expertise, honed over the creation of more than 50,000 flavors, has positioned the company as a competitive force in the international market. Thuemme’s dedication to flavor research is unparalleled; he is currently developing a Flavorists School in Mexico to train future professionals, passing on his extensive knowledge and passion for the craft.

One of Thuemme’s most remarkable contributions is the creation of flavors that embody the spirit of Mexican independence, celebrated each September. Among his notable creations are the Tres Leches flavor, a tequila with citrus undertones enhanced by exotic fruits like cactus and nanches, and a tepache flavor that brings a traditional fermented pineapple beverage to the global stage. He has also innovated by reclaiming the residues of vanilla beans through reactions with amino acids, reviving the authentic aroma of vanilla and creating derivative flavors that pay homage to Mexico’s rich culinary history.

Thuemme’s work goes beyond mere flavor creation; it is a deep exploration of Mexico’s cultural identity. His chocolate taco flavors, cappuccino with chipotle pepper, and cacao-chile mixes are a testament to his ability to blend ancient Aztec traditions with modern tastes. His efforts to preserve and share these flavors with the world are not just about innovation—they are about cultural preservation and pride.

Reflecting on his journey, Thuemme often says, “Dreams are made of a subtle, immaterial essence from which the impulse to create, to shape, and to transform emanates. That essence is what motivates us, what ignites our passion and creativity.” This philosophy underpins his work at Deiman, where he continues to craft flavors that are not only delicious but are also imbued with history and tradition.

LinkedIn | Etadar by Deiman | Website

8. Oscar Bellina Lishner | A Visionary Leader Redefining Social Impact

Oscar Bellina Lishner’s journey is a testament to the power of versatility and resilience. From humble beginnings at Xerox in Peru to becoming a renowned geopolitical analyst and advisor, Bellina Lishner has consistently shown an ability to adapt, innovate, and inspire. Specializing in pre-seed project development, he dedicates his expertise to solving complex social issues, driving change through innovative approaches.

title: According to Sources, OPEC+ is Close to Reaching a Deal to Postpone Increasing Oil Output
author: editor
excerpt: Following the lowest point in nine months for crude prices, OPEC+ is getting close to reaching a decision to postpone an increase in oil output scheduled for October, two sources within the producers group told Reuters on Thursday. Due to concerns about a faltering global economy and soft data from China, the largest oil importer in the world, oil prices have been declining along with those of other asset classes. According to one of the sources, “it is likely that the countries will take action to balance the market by delaying the increase.” According to the second source, OPEC+ was “almost there” in reaching a consensus. Due to the potential delay, oil prices increased. On Thursday, benchmark Brent crude reached $73 per barrel, although it is still near its lowest point since December. Increasing production would cause a significant surplus in the market starting in the first quarter of 2025. However, delaying could be seen as OPEC’s tardy acknowledgement of the weak oil demand. Helima Croft, an analyst at RBC Capital, suggested in a note that it might be wise for OPEC+ to hold off on returning more barrels until December. title: UAE Provides a Comprehensive List of Steps Needed to Modify an Overstayer’s Visa Status
author: editor
excerpt: Residents and visa violators can modify their status by remaining and working in the United Arab Emirates in accordance with the regulation option during the amnesty period, which runs until October 30, 2024. The Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Ports Security (ICP) has identified all the specific procedures required. According to the ICP, a person whose residency has expired and who does not have a work permit issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization (MoHRE) but who still wants to remain in the nation by the regulations is considered a residency violator. Violators in this category must follow two processes. They are free to join another company, but in order to comply with this process, the new employer must apply for a new work permit issued by the MoHRE or the ICP, depending on the type of his establishment. The ICP stated that in the event that a worker who has violated the law wants to start working for a new employer, the latter must apply for the issuance of a work permit. If the worker wants to leave the country, he must apply for an exit permit through the ICP systems. Residency violators with expired residency must follow one of two procedures, a work permit issued by the MoHRE, and a work interruption complaint filed against them. title: Black Point Reduction Services are Available from Abu Dhabi Police Through September 8

excerpt: As part of its participation in the 21st Abu Dhabi International Hunting and Equestrian Exhibition, the Police Follow-up and Aftercare Department of Abu Dhabi Police launched an initiative to recover suspended driving licenses (for drivers with 24 black points) and reduce black points. Drivers with 24 black points may find retrieving suspended licenses to be of interest, according to Lieutenant Colonel Nahyan Mohammed Bin Zaytoun Al Muhairi, Head of the Black Points Programs Section. title: The World’s Largest Low-Carbon Hydrogen Facility will be Constructed by Adnoc and ExxonMobil
author: editor
excerpt: The Honourable Sheikh Khaled Bin Mohamed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi and Chairman of the Abu Dhabi Executive Council, witnessed the signing of a strategic partnership between Adnoc and ExxonMobil Corporation. Under the agreement, Adnoc will purchase a 35% equity stake in ExxonMobil’s proposed low-carbon hydrogen and ammonia production facility in Baytown, Texas, US. Sheikh Khaled Bin Mohamed bin Zayed emphasised the value of cooperation to support the UAE’s efforts to guarantee the security and sustainability of the global energy sector and to bolster its standing as a major producer and supplier of low-carbon hydrogen worldwide. He reiterated that the facility’s development is in line with the leadership’s plan to fund and promote clean energy initiatives in the United Arab Emirates. The strategic agreement represents a sizable investment in US energy production and the global energy transition, aiming to meet the growing demand for lower-carbon fuels, reduce greenhouse gas emissions in hard-to-decarbonize sectors like industry, energy, and transportation, and expedite the transition to a net-zero future. The facility is anticipated to be the largest of its kind in the world when it opens, assuming favourable government policy and the required regulatory permits. It will be able to produce more than 1 million tonnes of low-carbon ammonia annually and up to 1 billion cubic feet of daily low-carbon hydrogen, which is almost carbon-free due to the removal of about 98% of carbon dioxide. title: A Company’s Dissolution and Liquidation are Ordered by a Dubai Court due to Financial Losses Exceeding Dhs344 Million
author: editor
excerpt: The Dubai Commercial Court of First Instance ordered a contracting company that suffered losses exceeding Dhs344 million to be dissolved and liquidated. A specialist accountant was also assigned to inventory the company’s assets and list its rights and obligations. The liquidator will be tasked with selling the company’s assets at public auction, putting the sale proceeds in a bank account designated for the company under liquidation, informing the company’s creditors as a result, paying off the company’s outstanding debts, and dividing the remaining assets among the partners in accordance with their respective shares. The official documents state that the limited liability contracting company that the court ordered to be liquidated is owned by another company, which owns 49 per cent of the shares and a businessman who owns the remaining 51 per cent of the shares. According to the case file, the company, which holds almost half of the shares, asked for the contracting company to be liquidated because it was losing money on operations and could not continue as a business due to a lack of funding, ongoing projects, and means to carry out its operations. Since 2016 until now, its losses have mounted, and there has been no way for it to get funding to keep going. title: A Car Fire is Put out in Two Minutes by a Sharjah Civil Defence Team
author: editor
excerpt: A car fire that broke out on a major road in the Industrial Area on Monday was effectively put out by the firefighting units of the Sharjah Civil Defence Authority, sparing no lives. At around 7:30 a.m. on Monday, the operations room of the Sharjah Police General Command received a report that a small vehicle had caught fire in the middle of the main road in the Industrial Area. The National Ambulance, police patrols, and civil defence vehicles were sent to the scene in response. Within two minutes of arriving on the scene, the Civil Defence team successfully put out the fire by implementing rapid fire suppression measures. After that, they cooled the fire scene to stop the fire from starting again and made it easier for the car to be removed, protecting the nearby traffic. The Civil Defence Authority urges Sharjah residents to perform routine auto maintenance, especially during the summer months. The appeal also exhorts car owners to ensure that fire extinguishers are easily accessible and that their vehicles undergo the necessary inspections. title: African Leaders in Beijing Want Greater Investment and Large Loans
author: editor
excerpt: This week, African leaders will converge on China’s capital to raise capital for expensive infrastructure projects as they watch the growing rivalry between great powers for resources and influence on the continent. Over the past ten years, China has deepened its connections with African countries, lending them billions of dollars to help with infrastructure development, but at times, this has sparked controversy by burdening these nations with massive debt. China has utilised Africa’s abundant natural resources, such as copper, gold, lithium, and rare earth minerals, while also sending hundreds of thousands of labourers there to complete its massive projects. Leaders of South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, and other countries have confirmed their attendance at this week’s China-Africa forum. Beijing claims it will be its biggest diplomatic gathering since the COVID-19 pandemic, and dozens of delegations are anticipated. According to Ovigwe Eguegu, a policy analyst at Development Reimagined, African nations were “looking to tap the opportunities in China for growth.” This was stated to AFP. According to Chinese state media, bilateral trade between China and Africa reached $167.8 billion in the first half of this year, making China the continent’s largest trading partner and the second-largest economy globally. According to data compiled by the Chinese Loans to Africa Database, Beijing’s loans to African countries reached their highest level in five years last year. The top five borrowers were Angola, Ethiopia, Egypt, Nigeria, and Kenya. title: According to IATA, the Demand for Air Cargo Increased by 13.6% Overall in July
author: editor
excerpt: Data for the global air cargo markets for July 2024 has been made public by the International Air Transport Association (IATA), and it continues to demonstrate strong annual demand growth. Comparing July 2023 to July 2024, the total demand, expressed in cargo tonne-kilometers (CTKs), climbed by 13.6% (or 14.3% for international traffic). title: The Rise of Private Master Developers in Dubai: A Developer’s Perspective
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: As a Dubai-based developer, I’ve witnessed firsthand the challenges and disappointments that come with investing in numerous promising communities. Time and again, master developers have promised the moon but ended up delivering a terrain that resembles it instead. It has become clear that investing and developing within certain master developments is akin to tossing the dice at a casino. However, private master developers have stepped in and delivered truly exceptional communities. Majid Al Futtaim’s Tilal Al Ghaf, for instance, stands out as perhaps the most astounding community delivered in Dubai at its price point. The quality of materials and craftsmanship surpasses most others. Had they been granted the luxury of choosing the most prime locations, they would have undoubtedly topped any other community by far. Reflecting on this, it’s evident that private master developers are outperforming their semi-government counterparts—though Emaar remains a notable exception. Emaar has consistently demonstrated that they operate more like a private entity, without relying on government grants or favors. This sets them apart from others who, despite having vast land banks and the ability to pick prime spots, have left them severely underdeveloped. Examples include Dubai Science Park, Studio City, Healthcare City 2, and many others. Looking back, when District One was managed by Sobha, it was a trailblazing community, the first of its kind. However, after Meydan took over the remaining development, we struggled to achieve any solid profits. We were among just 5 of 50 plots that were actually built. Delving deeper, the entire Dubai-land area, initially managed by Dubai Properties, was eventually sold to private master developers like Damac, who transformed it into the successful Damac Hills community. Similarly, what was once Golf City, another project by Dubai Properties, was reimagined as Damac Lagoons by Damac. Tilal Al Ghaf, another example, was picked up from Dubai Properties and developed into a paradise community. It overlooks a shadow of what was supposed to be a thriving community, Sports City—once envisioned as the beacon of sports entertainment. Culture Village (now Jaddaf Waterfront) is another example where grand promises were made. It was the only freehold community on the creek, featuring landmarks like the opera house, the glamorous Versace hotel, and D1 Tower, one of the tallest structures in the city, along with the Jameel Museum. Despite all these attractions, we failed to recoup our investment there because the community was not developed as promised. The point here is that only Emaar has consistently managed to fulfill its grand promises as a semi-government entity. The rest have struggled to deliver. Emaar’s takeover of what was once The Lagoons by Sama Dubai—a failed attempt by Dubai Properties—now rebranded as Creek Harbour, is another testament to their capability. It’s yet another fantastic achievement by Mohamed Alabbar. If it’s not Emaar, these new communities must be developed in collaboration with the private sector. Many have proven themselves worthy of such tasks, including Majid Al Futtaim, Hussain Sajwani, Memon of Sobha, MAG Group, and others. The Dubai brand cannot afford to lose any of its glamour to broken promises. About the Author: Hamzah Abu Zannad is the Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Axiom Prime Real Estate Development, a leader in luxury real estate development. With a rich background in marketing management, business planning, and customer retention, Hamzah has successfully led his team in creating refined residential communities across the globe. Drawing on decades of experience in both the Dutch and Dubai markets, he is committed to delivering boutique, low-density living spaces that blend modern refinement with a personal touch. Hamzah is passionate about integrating smart technologies into his projects and fostering a culture of innovation and collaboration within his organization. title: July Sees a Slowdown in Australia’s Inflation, but Progress is still Slow
author: editor
excerpt: Sydney: Because of government rebates on electricity bills, Australian inflation slowed to a four-month low in July. However, the lack of progress in curbing price increases abroad dampened market expectations of a near-term interest rate cut. The annual growth rate of the consumer price index (CPI) decreased to 3.5% in July from 3.8% in June, according to data released on Wednesday by the Australian Bureau of Statistics. Because the number was marginally higher than expected (3.4%), markets extended the odds of the Reserve Bank of Australia’s first easing to 48.4% in November from the previous 58%. The Australian dollar reached its highest point of the year, $0.6803, up 0.1%, and $0.6803, about the highest this year. The inflation estimate for July is deceptive and full of smoke. According to Moody’s Analytics economist Harry Murphy Cruise, “at face value, the fight against inflation looks to have made significant progress, but some of that improvement came from rebates that artificially lowered the cost of electricity.” Prices remain the same in the end, even though that greatly improves the headline inflation figure. The CPI excluding volatile items and holiday travel dipped to 3.7 per cent, the lowest reading since early 2022, compared with 4.0 per cent. title: A New Government Policy will see $300 Billion in the bio Economy of India by 2030
author: editor
excerpt: As per Jitendra Singh, the Minister for Science and Technology, India’s bio economy has grown 13 times in the last ten years and is predicted to double by 2030. According to Singh, who briefed the media on the introduction of the Biotechnology for Economy, Employment and Environment (BioE3) policy by the Indian Cabinet, India’s bio-economy has grown significantly, from $10 billion in 2014 to over $130 billion in 2024, and is expected to reach $300 billion by 2030. According to him, the BioE3 policy will spur economic expansion and establish India as a possible front-runner in the event of the next industrial revolution. Critical global issues like climate change and the depletion of non-renewable resources are the focus of the new policy. The BioE3 initiative aims to address these issues by creating a circular bioeconomy, supporting net-zero carbon emissions, easing the transition from chemical-based to sustainable bio-based business models, and stimulating the creation of bio-based products. title: Spain Rejects a Hungarian Attempt to Acquire Train Manufacturer Talgo
author: editor
excerpt: The leftist government of Spain denied a Hungarian consortium’s takeover bid for the Spanish train manufacturer Talgo on Tuesday, citing threats to public order and national security. According to the ministry of economy, the cabinet resolved “to not authorise direct foreign investment” in Talgo by Ganz Mavag Europe, a company based in Hungary, “for reasons linked to protecting Spain’s national security and strategic interests.” According to the statement, Talgo is a strategic enterprise in an industry important to Spain’s industrial development, territorial cohesion, and economic security. Although it did not explicitly state this in its statement, the government has made it plain that it is worried about the close ties that the Hungarian businesses have with Prime Minister Viktor Orban, who is seen as Putin’s ally. Just two days before Russian missiles blowing up a children’s hospital in Kyiv, on July 5, Orban—whose nation currently holds the rotating presidency of the European Union—met with Putin in Moscow, setting off a chain reaction of intense resentment throughout the 27-nation bloc. title: Egypt’s Economy Appears to be Improving, According to the IMF
author: editor
excerpt: RIYADH: The International Monetary Fund says Egypt’s economy is beginning to show signs of recovery as a consequence of the government’s recent efforts to re-establish macroeconomic stability. According to the IMF’s most recent review report, Egypt’s inflation rate is still high but is starting to decline. The North African nation has been implementing various economic reforms to preserve fiscal stability. One such reform was the unification of the official and parallel exchange rates in March. Since then, the nation’s economy has greatly improved; the market now determines the Egyptian pound, bank foreign exchange backlogs have been cleared, and daily interbank global exchange turnover has increased. The monetary policy tightening that accompanied the unification of the exchange rate reduced speculation, attracted foreign investment, and slowed the price growth rate. Given the indications of improving sentiment, private sector growth should be ready for a surge, according to IMF deputy managing director and acting chair Antoinette Sayeh. She went on, saying that “continuing to implement a tight monetary policy stance, continuing to shift towards a flexible exchange rate regime and a liberalised foreign exchange system, and further fiscal consolidation along with appropriate implementation of the framework to monitor and control public investment should support internal and external balance. title: Amidst robust non-oil growth, Jadwa Investment Reduces its Forecast for Saudi Inflation to 1.7%
author: editor
excerpt: RIYADH: According to Jadwa Investment, robust growth in the non-oil sector and lower prices in key sectors are expected to drive Saudi Arabia’s inflation down to 1.7 percent in 2024, from a previous estimate of 2 percent. The Riyadh-based investment management and advisory firm ascribed this revision to steady growth in consumer prices, given that inflation increased just 1.6% in the first half of the year. Jadwa said that lower clothing, footwear, and transportation prices have mitigated inflationary pressures from the housing market. This trend aligns with global patterns, where easing demand and improved supply chains reduce price pressures. Despite the overall moderation in inflation, housing costs remain a significant driver, particularly in the ‘rentals for housing’ segment. Prices in this category have stayed high due to elevated demand and a tight rental market, exacerbated by high interest rates prompting more Saudis to rent rather than buy homes. The report said that this trend is expected to persist, maintaining pressure on prices within the housing and utilities segment, which constitutes 25 percent of the Consumer Price Index. Alongside my husband and co-founder, Tyreeq Thomas, whose background in sales, with a passion for art and history complemented mine, we founded Tykorchélli in October 2022. Moreover, we take pride in paying special attention to cultural traditions when designing, ensuring that our creations respect and reflect the diverse backgrounds of our clients. We recently had the privilege of interviewing Corie Anziano, Founder and CEO of Tykorchélli. Corie is the visionary behind Tykorchélli, a luxury couture brand that embodies the celebration of individuality, craftsmanship, and the art of storytelling through fashion. With each collection, the CEO strives to inspire confidence, empower self-expression, and redefine the boundaries of luxury fashion.

In this insightful interview, Corie Anziano shares her professional journey in the creative field, her career highlights, and the services offered by Tykorchélli.

The Beginning

We started the interview by asking, “Can you walk us through your professional journey and how it led to where you are today?”

Corie Anziano shared, “My professional journey began in the creative realms with over two decades of experience in business management, finance, and art. These disciplines provided me with a deep understanding of how to balance creativity with strategic planning, which naturally transitioned into the world of fashion. Alongside my husband and co-founder, Tyreeq Thomas, whose background in sales, with a passion for art and history complemented mine, we founded Tykorchélli in October 2022.

Our goal was to create a brand that merges historical grandeur with modern elegance, offering wearable masterpieces that tell a story. This vision, coupled with years of learning and studying business and human experiences, brought Tykorchélli to life and has guided us to where we are today.”

Adaptability Amidst Challenges

Challenges are a part of every professional path. To learn how Corie Anziano overcame the same, we asked, “Reflecting on your career, what have been some of the most significant challenges you’ve faced, and how did you overcome them?”

Corie Anziano shared, “Launching a luxury couture brand in a fast fashion-dominated industry required us to stand out through exceptional quality, compelling storytelling, and distinctive designs to gain global recognition. We overcame this by staying true to our vision – creating one-of-a-kind pieces that merge historical influences with modern interpretations.

Moreover, we take pride in paying special attention to cultural traditions when designing, ensuring that our creations respect and reflect the diverse backgrounds of our clients. The press coverage and recognition we’ve received, including features in Harper’s Bazaar, Elle, and Vogue Weekly, as well as making the best-dressed list at Cannes dressing Miss Universe, Sheynnis Palacios, have been affirmations of our perseverance and commitment.”

Aligning Vision With Operation

We further asked, “How do you balance long-term vision with short-term operational needs?”

“Balancing long-term vision with short-term operational needs requires a strategic approach. We have a clear vision of what we want Tykorchélli to become—a globally recognized brand known for its distinctive Renaissance designs, intricate detailing, and craftsmanship.

To achieve this, we ensure that our daily operations, from design to production and marketing, align with this overarching goal. We remain flexible in our approach, allowing for adjustments as necessary, while keeping our long-term vision at the forefront of every decision.” She replied.

Current Offerings At Tykorchélli

Eager to learn about the services and products offered by Corie Anziano’s company and its upcoming events, we asked, “Tell us more about your services and if you are planning to add something new in the future.”

Corie Anziano  said, “Tykorchélli offers a wide range of services, including exclusive one-of-a-kind couture, red carpet and special occasion wear, Sarees, Abayas, and even film costuming. Each piece is designed with meticulous attention to detail and storytelling. Looking to the future, we plan to expand into Tykorchélli Kids, bringing our unique blend of luxury and artistry to children’s fashion as well as launching our streetwear brand, Chélli.

Additionally, we are continuously exploring new ways to innovate within the industry, ensuring our offerings remain fresh and aligned with our brand’s ethos.”

Blend Of Research And Feedback

Staying ahead of the market demands top-notch market analysis. So, we asked, “What methods do you use to analyze market trends, and how have these influenced your business decisions?”

“We analyze market trends through a combination of research, customer feedback, and staying attuned to shifts in the fashion industry. We look at what is resonating with consumers, both in terms of aesthetics and values and incorporate those insights into our designs.

For instance, the increasing demand for sustainability and ethical production has influenced us to be more mindful of our sourcing and production processes, ensuring that our products are not only beautiful but also responsible.” She added.

Redefining Businesses

The digital landscape is changing at a faster rate, transforming the way businesses perform, interact with customers, and drive growth. We also Corie, “How has digital transformation affected your business model?”

Corie Anziano responded, “Digital transformation has played a crucial role in expanding our reach and enhancing our customer experience. From online shopping platforms to social media marketing, digital tools have allowed us to connect with a global audience, showcase our collections in innovative ways, and provide personalized services through virtual consultations. It has also streamlined our operations, making it easier to manage everything from design to distribution more efficiently.”

Potential Trends Of The Industry

To gather Corie’s perspective on the potential trends of her industry, we asked, “What emerging technologies do you believe will have the most significant impact on your industry in the next five years?”

Corie Anziano replied, “I believe that advancements in 3D printing, AI-driven design tools, and sustainable textile innovations will have a profound impact on the fashion industry. 3D printing will revolutionize the way we create intricate designs, allowing for more customization and reducing waste. AI will enhance our ability to predict trends and create personalized experiences for our clients. Sustainable textiles will be crucial as the industry moves towards more eco-friendly practices, aligning with the growing demand for ethical fashion.”

Empowering Employees

Addressing the employees, we asked Corie Anziano, “What strategies do you implement to maintain high levels of employee engagement and satisfaction?”:

“We prioritize creating a positive and collaborative work environment where every team member feels valued and heard. We encourage creativity and innovation, giving our team the freedom to experiment and contribute their ideas to our collections.  

Regular team meetings, recognition of achievements, and opportunities for professional growth are also key strategies we use to maintain high levels of engagement and satisfaction. We believe that when our team is inspired and motivated, it reflects in the quality of our work and the success of our brand.” She shared.

Crafting Timeless Works Of Art

Lastly, we ended the interview by asking, “How do you want your business to be remembered, and what steps are you taking to secure that legacy?”

Corie Anziano said, “We want Tykorchélli to be remembered as a brand that transcended fashion, creating timeless works of art that told stories and evoked emotions. Our goal is to be recognized for our distinctive designs, our commitment to quality, and our ability to merge historical influences with modern elegance.

To secure this legacy, we are focused on maintaining the highest standards in every aspect of our work, from design to customer experience, while staying true to our vision. We are also actively building partnerships and expanding our reach, ensuring that Tykorchélli continues to inspire and captivate audiences for generations to come.”

title: India’s Reduction in gold Duties is Anticipated to cause a Shopping Frenzy During the Holidays
author: editor
excerpt: Industry officials stated that the significant decrease in import duties has made gold prices attractive, comforting retail consumers and stimulating purchases. As a result, demand for the metal is expected to remain strong in India during the forthcoming festive season. The second-largest gold consumer in the world may see increased demand, which could fuel a rise in prices that culminated last week in a record high. However, a rise in the demand for gold imports might worsen India’s trade imbalance and weaken the rupee. According to Sachin Jain, CEO of the World Gold Council’s Indian operations, retail customers will primarily benefit from the lower duty cut. To combat smuggling, India reduced import duties on gold in July from 15% to 6%. On the fringes of the India Gold Conference, Jain told Reuters there will be a huge demand during the festival season. The end of the year, when bullion purchases are regarded as auspicious, coincides with the traditional wedding season and important festivals like Diwali and Dusherra, which typically increase the demand for gold in India. title: US Companies’ Equipment Spending Begins the Third Quarter Slowly
author: editor
excerpt: The unexpected decline in new orders for important capital goods manufactured in the United States in July and the revision of lower data for the previous month suggested a loss of momentum in business spending on equipment. This decline continued into the early part of the third quarter. In addition, the Commerce Department’s report from Monday showed that the manufacturing sector remained stagnant despite rising interest rates. Aircraft made up the majority of the sharp increase in orders for durable manufactured goods last month. Even so, the increase in corporate equipment spending is probably enough to keep the economy growing. Chief economist at FWDBONDS Christopher Rupkey stated, “The economy hasn’t hit the skids yet.” “Although business investment in long-term core capital goods orders has somewhat slowed at the beginning of the third quarter, new orders are far from signalling the beginning of a recession in the overall economy.”The Census Bureau of the Commerce Department reported that non-defence capital goods orders, which do not include aircraft and are a closely watched indicator of business spending plans, decreased by 0.1% in June following a downwardly revised 0.5% increase. title: ExxonMobil Projects that by 2050, Global Oil Demand will be Roughly Where it is Now
author: editor
excerpt: The US oil and gas giant ExxonMobil stated on Monday that despite advancements in renewable energy, global oil demand will unlikely decline by 2050 due to the growing population and energy consumption worldwide. According to a recent ExxonMobil study, “oil demand is expected to plateau beyond 2030, staying above 100 million barrels per day through 2050. This number is much higher than what rival BP projected earlier this year, indicating that if current trends continue, oil demand will drop to about 75 million barrels per day by 2050. ExxonMobil estimated in its report that four billion people worldwide do not have access to the energy they require. According to the company, supplying the world’s basic energy needs “will drive a projected 15% increase in total energy use worldwide between now and 2050,” as the world’s population is predicted to rise from eight billion to nearly ten billion people. According to the company, the vast majority of oil produced worldwide is and will be used in heavy-duty transportation like shipping, trucking, and aviation, as well as industrial processes like manufacturing and chemical production. Despite this, ExxonMobil continues to project that increased renewable energy, improved energy efficiency, and introducing new “lower-emission technologies” like carbon capture and storage will reduce global carbon emissions by about 25% by the middle of the century. title: Canada Levies a 100% Tariff on EV Imports Manufactured in China
author: editor
excerpt: On Monday, the Canadian government declared it would levy a 100% tariff on Chinese-made electric vehicle imports, matching US tariffs and adopting policies akin to those proclaimed by the European Commission. US national security advisor Jake Sullivan encouraged the announcement during a Sunday meeting with Canadian cabinet ministers and Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. On Tuesday, Sullivan will travel to Beijing for the first time. According to Trudeau, Canada will levy a 25% tariff on steel and aluminium imports from China. China and other actors have decided to give themselves an unfair edge in the international market,” he said. As Beijing works to revive its economy following the COVID-19 pandemic, Chinese officials will probably raise concerns regarding US tariffs with Sullivan. In May, US President Joe Biden imposed major new tariffs on Chinese electric cars, solar cells, advanced batteries, steel, aluminium, and medical equipment. Sullivan told reporters on Sunday, “The US does believe that a united front, a coordinated approach on these issues benefits all of us. Chinese companies can sell EVs for as little as $12,000. The capacity of China’s steel, aluminium, and solar cell factories is sufficient to meet most of the global demand. Chinese officials contend that their production helps facilitate the shift to a green economy and keeps prices low. title: RTA adds Four New Metro link Bus Routes and Improves Existing Ones, Including an Intercity Route
author: editor
excerpt: The Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) of Dubai intends to begin operating four new metro link bus routes on August 30, 2024, and to improve the offerings of multiple other routes, including one intercity route. By making these changes, travellers should have a better everyday commute and easily travel across the Emirate. The two new routes, F39 and F40, will replace Route 31 among the four new routes. With a 30-minute frequency, the first new route, F39, will travel from Etisalat Bus Station to Oud Al Muteena Roundabout Bus Stop 1 and back. The second new route, F40, will run from Etisalat Bus Station to Mirdif, Street 78, and back. Due to the cancellation of the sector from Al Ghubaiba Station to Oud Metha, Route 6 will now only travel from the Bus Stop at Oud Metha Metro Station to Dubai Healthcare City. Bus 95A’s route will be rerouted to begin at Veneto, Jebel Ali Waterfront and travel through the Jebel Ali Industrial Area before ending at Parco Hypermarket. JAFZA One will be covered by Route 99, and The Greens will see new stops added to Route F31. Route F45 will also see new stops added in Al Furjan, and Route F54 will see the removal of the JAFZA One stop. Furthermore, intercity Route E700 to Fujairah will now originate from Etisalat Bus Station rather than Union Bus Station.
